message:
[XLA:GPU] Check unnormalized dot shapes in `upcaster_filter`

After `DotDimensionSorter` and `DotDecomposer` were removed from the early part of `GpuCompiler::OptimizeHloModule` in favor of running `DotDimensionNormalizer` later in the pipeline, `ResultCaster` and `OperandUpcaster` now inspect `dot` instructions before their contracting/non-contracting dimensions are flattened and before `GpuLayoutAssignment` assigns physical layouts.

Because `IsCublasSupportedMatMul` assumed normalized dot dimensions (`Rank(kContracting) == 1`, `Rank(kNonContracting) <= 1`, and non-minor batch dimensions), `upcaster_filter` falsely treated multi-dimensional mixed-precision dots (such as `f16 x f16 -> f32` attention einsums with multiple contracting or non-contracting dimensions) as unsupported by cuBLAS and upcasted their `f16` operands to `f32`.

Add `bool is_normalized = true` to `IsCublasSupportedMatMul` and pass `/*is_normalized=*/false` from `upcaster_filter` so that dots that will be normalized into valid 2D/batched GEMMs by `DotDimensionNormalizer` and `GpuLayoutAssignment` retain their mixed-precision operands.

author: A. Unique TensorFlower

message:
Eliminate redundant copies in DecodeCompressed.

`DecodeCompressed` runs on high-throughput input pipelines, where copying tensor payloads across ops wastes CPU cycles and allocator bandwidth on every batch.

For uncompressed inputs, the op now forwards the input tensor directly to the output instead of allocating a new tensor and deep-copying each string. This turns passthrough into a constant-time zero-copy handoff, cutting 16 MiB batch CPU time from 2.39 ms to ~63 ns (a 51% to 99.997% reduction across payload sizes).

For ZLIB and GZIP streams, chunk reads now yield unowned string views directly into the input tensor rather than staging bytes in temporary strings, speeding up multi-chunk decompression by up to 22.6% (and throughput by up to 29.1%).

PiperOrigin-RevId: 1009219101
author: Larry Lansing

message:
Use BlasLtMatmulAlgorithm descriptors in CublasLtMatmulThunk

`CublasLtMatmulThunk` previously selected its cuBLASLt algorithm at runtime using an integer index into the list returned by `cublasLtMatmulAlgoGetHeuristic`. Because that heuristic order depends on device properties (like SM count) and the cuBLASLt version, two GPUs of the same compute capability (for example, A100 and PG199) can order the heuristic list differently and end up running a different kernel than the one chosen during autotuning.

Since `GemmBackendConfig` now records the full `BlasLtMatmulAlgorithmProto` descriptor, this change passes the descriptor to `CublasLtMatmulThunk` (and serializes it in `CublasLtMatmulThunkProto` for AOT executables). At runtime, `CublasLtMatmulThunk` reconstructs and validates the exact algorithm from the descriptor instead of querying the heuristic list by index.

When the descriptor is missing (for example, in older serialized executables or autotune caches) or is rejected by cuBLASLt on the target device, the thunk logs a warning and falls back to the heuristic index. Setting `--xla_gpu_require_exact_blas_lt_algorithm` (either at compile time or at runtime when deserializing an AOT executable) disables that fallback and returns an error instead.

message:
Grow global SharedBatchScheduler thread pools to the maximum requested.

When `SharedBatchScheduler::Create()` is called with `use_global_scheduler = true`, all callers in the process share a single `SharedBatchScheduler` instance. Previously, only the `Options` from the first `Create()` call initialized `batch_threads_` and `warmup_threads_`, ignoring larger thread counts requested by subsequent callers. If an initial caller created the global scheduler with fewer batch threads or zero warmup threads, later models requesting higher concurrency or dedicated warmup threads remained constrained to the initial pool sizes.

Add `MaybeGrowThreads()` and invoke it on each `Create()` call when `use_global_scheduler = true` so `batch_threads_` and `warmup_threads_` grow monotonically to the largest `num_batch_threads` and `num_warmup_batch_threads` requested. When `warmup_threads_` transitions from empty to non-empty, enable the warmup queue on all existing queues via `Queue::EnableWarmupQueue()`. Guard `batch_threads_`, `warmup_threads_`, and `enable_warmup_queue_` with `mu_`, and move thread vectors into local variables under `mu_` before joining in `~SharedBatchScheduler()`.

message:
[XLA:GPU] Scale intermediate tile sizes by byte width in EstimateNumWarps.

`EstimateNumWarps` previously computed `largest_live_tile_size` using raw padded element counts across all instructions in the tiled computation. For fusions with broadcasted inputs, `iota`, or sub-32-bit intermediate tiles (such as `pred` comparisons feeding a reduction), this inflated `largest_live_tile_size` by 4x or more and selected 4-8 warps where 2-4 warps are faster.

Introduce `GetLiveTileSizeForNumWarps`:

- Keep full padded element counts for operands and roots so global memory vectorization is unchanged.
- Ignore non-root `broadcast` and `constant` tiles, which do not materialize a separate register array beyond their operands, and size non-root `iota` by its 1D range along `iota_dimension`.
- Scale other intermediate array tiles by `min(element_bytes, 4) / 4` (32-bit register words).

Also account for multi-block SM residency (`blocks_per_core`) when computing `active_threads_per_core` in `EstimateRunTimeForTiledHloComputationImpl` so that 1-warp and 2-warp candidates on multi-wave grids are not penalized as if only a single block could reside on each SM.

message:
Constant-fold `BROADCAST_TO`.

`tfl.broadcast_to` had no folder, so broadcasting a constant survived
conversion as a runtime op. GPU delegates that require a runtime data input
reject such a node (ML Drift: `inputs[0] should not be a constant tensor`),
leaving a CPU island in an otherwise delegable graph.

Add a `FoldConstantBroadcastTo` canonicalization pattern that replaces a
BROADCAST_TO of a constant with the right-aligned broadcast constant. It is a
pattern rather than a folder so it can look at the users: if every user
broadcasts implicitly (`ResultsBroadcastableShape` ops within the rank limits
of optimize_broadcast_like, or `BATCH_MATMUL`), the BROADCAST_TO is left for
optimize_broadcast_like to drop, which keeps the constant small and lets
patterns that look at the unbroadcast operand still match (e.g. `EQUAL`
against a 0..N-1 sequence becoming `ONE_HOT`). The result is also limited to
at most 1 MiB, splats included (the flatbuffer exporter writes splats out in
full), so it cannot grow a model by more than that per op. Non-int/float
element types are left alone.

Every <=8-bit integer value (`S1`, `U1`, `S2`, `U2`, `S4`, `U4`, `S8`, `U8`) is
losslessly representable in `BF16` (which has 8 significand bits). Previously,
`DotOperandConverter` upcasted the integer operand of a mixed `(int<=8, f32)`
`dot` to `F32`, forcing the `dot` onto the TF32 Tensor Core path
(`dot(f32, f32) -> f32`) even when `PrecisionConfig` had default precision
(`ALG_UNSET` and `DEFAULT` operand precision).

Update `DotOperandConverter` so that when a `dot` with `F32` or `BF16` output
and default precision multiplies an <=8-bit integer operand by an `F32` operand
on a target that supports both fast `BF16` GEMMs and `TF32` (Ampere+ on CUDA,
or MI300 series with hipBLASLt on ROCm) and `tensor_float_32_execution_enabled()` is
true, both operands are converted to `BF16` (`dot(bf16, bf16) -> f32`/`bf16`).
Explicit higher precision requests (`HIGH`, `HIGHEST`, explicit `DotAlgorithm`s,
or disabled TF32 execution) and targets without `BF16` GEMM support continue to
upcast to `F32`.

message:
Fix base dilation overlap in SpaceToBatchConverter

When inherent_low_padding equals base_dilation_factor, SpaceToBatchConverter prepends one undilated element to each split and sets low_padding_for_conv to 0.

For each split of S undilated elements to produce S * base_dilation_factor outputs, the high-side overlap must be kernel_spatial_dim_size + base_dilation_factor - 2 rather than kernel_spatial_dim_size (which only matched for base_dilation_factor == 2). Therefore this change updates last_overlap in GetConvolutionDetails accordingly.

Also update the split-size loop in PropagateOnConv for base-dilated convolutions so it uses the actual low padding passed to HaloDuplicateWithSlice and does not count halo_size as available spatial size (since ChangeSpatialSizeOnSpaceToBatchedShape slices the collapsed spatial dimension to spatial_split_size * num_splits).

Fixes <url>

message:
[XLA] Use typed LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T> in HandleAllReduceOrReduceScatter.

In `AlgebraicSimplifierVisitor::HandleAllReduceOrReduceScatter` (`xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers/algebraic_simplifier.cc`), the `ReductionKind::SUM` constant-folding branch is already inside a `primitive_util::ArrayTypeSwitch` over `element_type` where `using T = primitive_util::NativeTypeOf<type_constant>` is the native C++ type corresponding to `element_type`. Calling the 2-argument `LiteralUtil::CreateR0(element_type, result)` instead of the 1-argument `LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T>(result)` caused `CreateR0(PrimitiveType, T)` to instantiate a nested 29-way `ArrayTypeSwitch` for each of the 27 integral and floating-point types `T` (`27 × 29 = 783` cross-type `static_cast<NativeT>(result)` branches), adding 151.6 KB to `algebraic_simplifier.pic.o`.

Call `LiteralUtil::CreateR0<T>(result)` directly, matching `MakeScalarInstruction` in the same file.

Runtime and memory performance impact: Zero memory overhead and slightly faster constant folding for `AllReduce`/`ReduceScatter` of a scalar constant by avoiding a redundant runtime `ArrayTypeSwitch` dispatch.

PR #51563: [ROCm] Support contiguous sub-communicators in the MORI collectives backend

Imported from GitHub PR <url>

## Summary

The MORI backend used to accept only the full global clique with an identity
rank-to-PE mapping. Any collective over a subset of devices was rejected, for
example `replica_groups={{0,1},{2,3}}` or a collective-permute whose connected
components form smaller cliques.

This PR adds support for sub-communicators whose ranks map to a **contiguous**
PE range (`rank i -> PE base + i`), such as `{3,4,5}`. Arbitrary mappings such
as `{0,2,7}` are still rejected with a clear error.

It also repins MORI to `xla-pin-20261024`, which provides the matching
facade-side support.

## Changes

### `xla/backends/gpu/collectives/mori_communicator.{h,cc}`

- Each `MoriCommunicator` now owns its own `CollectivesFacade` instance, created
  through `CollectivesFacade::Get(rank, num_ranks, rank_to_pe)`. Previously it
  held a non-owning pointer to the per-device singleton.
- `CollectivesFacade::Get` validates the mapping. It requires the PEs to be
  contiguous, to fit within the node's LSA team, and to match this device's PE.
  If any of these fail, `Create` returns `InvalidArgument` with the rank and the
  full `rank_to_pe` mapping.
- The old full-world/identity-mapping checks and the cached `rank_` and
  `num_ranks_` are gone. `NumRanks()`, `CurrentRank()`, `ToString()` and the
  all-to-all buffer-count check now read the communicator-local rank and size
  from the facade.
- The unused `MoriCollectives*` back-pointer and the `friend` declaration are
  removed, and `Create` no longer takes the parent collectives.

### `xla/backends/gpu/collectives/mori_collectives.cc`

- Updated to the new MORI API: `CollectivesFacade::Create(comm, pool_size,
  max_staging)` no longer takes `rank`/`nranks`, and
  `MoriCommunicator::Create` no longer takes the parent collectives.
- `rank_to_pe` is still built from the clique key's global device ids. A

description: 🤗 Transformers: the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning models in text, vision, audio, and
content:
English | 简体中文 | 繁體中文 | 한국어 | Español | 日本語 | हिन्दी | मराठी | Русский | Português | తెలుగు | Français | Deutsch | Italiano | Tiếng Việt | العربية | اردو | বাংলা | فارسی | Română | Türkçe

State-of-the-art pretrained models for inference and training

Transformers acts as the model-definition framework for state-of-the-art machine learning with text, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal models, for both inference and training. It centralizes the model definition so that this definition is agreed upon across the ecosystem. `transformers` is the pivot across frameworks: if a model definition is supported, it will be compatible with the majority of training frameworks (Axolotl, Unsloth, DeepSpeed, FSDP, PyTorch-Lightning, ...), inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TGI, ...), and adjacent modeling libraries (llama.cpp, mlx, ...) which leverage the model definition from `transformers`. We pledge to help support new state-of-the-art models and democratize their usage by having their model definition be simple, customizable, and efficient. There are over 1M+ Transformers [model checkpoints]() on the [Hugging Face Hub]() you can use. Explore the [Hub]() today to find a model and use Transformers to help you get started right away. ## Installation Transformers works with Python 3.11+, and [PyTorch]() 2.6+. Create and activate a virtual environment with [venv]() or [uv](), a fast Rust-based Python package and project manager. ```py # venv python -m venv .my-env source .my-env/bin/activate # uv uv venv .my-env source .my-env/bin/activate ``` Install Transformers in your virtual environment. ```py # pip pip install "transformers[torch]" # uv uv pip install "transformers[torch]" ``` Install Transformers from source if you want the latest changes in the library or are interested in contributing. However, the *latest* version may not be stable. Feel free to open an [issue]() if you encounter an error. ```shell git clone cd transformers # pip pip install '.[torch]' # uv uv pip install '.[torch]' ``` ## Quickstart Get started with Transformers right away with the [Pipeline]() API. The `Pipeline` is a high-level inference class that supports text, audio, vision, and multimodal tasks. It handles preprocessing the input and returns the appropriate output. Instantiate a pipeline and specify model to use for text generation. The model is downloaded and cached so you can easily reuse it again. Finally, pass some text to prompt the model. ```py from transformers import pipeline pipeline = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B") pipeline("the secret to baking a really good cake is ") [{'generated_text': 'the secret to baking a really good cake is 1) to use the right ingredients and 2) to follow the recipe exactly. the recipe for the cake is as follows: 1 cup of sugar, 1 cup of flour, 1 cup of milk, 1 cup of butter, 1 cup of eggs, 1 cup of chocolate chips. if you want to make 2 cakes, how much sugar do you need? To make 2 cakes, you will need 2 cups of sugar.'}] ``` To chat with a model, the usage pattern is the same. The only difference is you need to construct a chat history (the input to `Pipeline`) between you and the system. > [!TIP] > You can also chat with a model directly from the command line, as long as [`transformers serve` is running](). > ```shell > transformers chat Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct > ``` ```py import torch from transformers import pipeline chat = [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are a sassy, wise-cracking robot as imagined by Hollywood circa 1986."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Hey, can you tell me any fun things to do in New York?"} ] pipeline = pipeline(task="text-generation", model="meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct", dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map="auto") response = pipeline(chat, max_new_tokens=512) print(response[0]["generated_text"][-1]["content"]) ``` Expand the examples below to see how `Pipeline` works for different modalities and tasks.
Automatic speech recognition ```py from transformers import pipeline pipeline = pipeline(task="automatic-speech-recognition", model="openai/whisper-large-v3") pipeline("") {'text': ' I have a dream that one day this nation will rise up and live out the true meaning of its creed.'} ```
Image classification

```py from transformers import pipeline pipeline = pipeline(task="image-classification", model="facebook/dinov2-small-imagenet1k-1-layer") pipeline("") [{'label': 'macaw', 'score': 0.997848391532898}, {'label': 'sulphur-crested cockatoo, Kakatoe galerita, Cacatua galerita', 'score': 0.0016551691805943847}, {'label': 'lorikeet', 'score': 0.00018523589824326336}, {'label': 'African grey, African gray, Psittacus erithacus', 'score': 7.85409429227002e-05}, {'label': 'quail', 'score': 5.502637941390276e-05}] ```
Visual question answering

```py from transformers import pipeline pipeline = pipeline(task="visual-question-answering", model="Salesforce/blip-vqa-base") pipeline( image="", question="What is in the image?", ) [{'answer': 'statue of liberty'}] ```
## Why should I use Transformers? 1. Easy-to-use state-of-the-art models: - High performance on natural language understanding & generation, computer vision, audio, video, and multimodal tasks. - Low barrier to entry for researchers, engineers, and developers. - Few user-facing abstractions with just three classes to learn. - A unified API for using all our pretrained models. 1. Lower compute costs, smaller carbon footprint: - Share trained models instead of training from scratch. - Reduce compute time and production costs. - Hundreds of model architectures with 1M+ pretrained checkpoints across all modalities. 1. Choose the right framework for every part of a model's lifetime: - Train state-of-the-art models in 3 lines of code. - Move a single model between PyTorch/JAX/TF2.0 frameworks at will. - Pick the right framework for training, evaluation, and production. 1. Easily customize a model or an example to your needs: - We provide examples for each architecture to reproduce the results published by its original authors. - Model internals are exposed as consistently as possible. - Model files can be used independently of the library for quick experiments.
## When shouldn't I use Transformers? - This library is not a modular toolbox of building blocks for neural nets. The code in the model files is not refactored with additional abstractions on purpose, so that researchers can quickly iterate on each of the models without diving into additional abstractions/files. - The training API is optimized to work with PyTorch models provided by Transformers. For generic machine learning loops, you should use another library like [Accelerate](). ## 100 projects using Transformers Transformers is more than a toolkit to use pretrained models, it's a community of projects built around it and the Hugging Face Hub. We want Transformers to enable developers, researchers, students, professors, engineers, and anyone else to build their dream projects. In order to celebrate Transformers 100,000 stars, we wanted to put the spotlight on the community with the [awesome-transformers](./awesome-transformers.md) page which lists 100 incredible projects built with Transformers. If you own or use a project that you believe should be part of the list, please open a PR to add it! ## Example models You can test most of our models directly on their [Hub model pages](). Expand each modality below to see a few example models for various use cases.
Audio - Audio classification with [CLAP]() - Automatic speech recognition with [Parakeet](), [Whisper](), [GLM-ASR]() and [Moonshine-Streaming]() - Keyword spotting with [Wav2Vec2]() - Speech to speech generation with [Moshi]() - Text to audio with [MusicGen]() - Text to speech with [CSM]()

NLP - Masked word completion with [ModernBERT]() - Named entity recognition with [Gemma]() - Question answering with [Mixtral]() - Summarization with [BART]() - Translation with [T5]() - Text generation with [Llama]() - Text classification with [Qwen]()

title: 5.21.0 regression: end-anchored `WeightRenaming` rules save corrupted keys (`mask_embedding$`) that silently fail to reload
body:
### System Info

- **Broken**: `transformers` 5.21.0 (also reproduced on 5.22.0, and still present on `main` as of 2026-10-31)
- **Working**: `transformers` 5.18.0, 5.19.0, 5.20.0
- Python 3.12, Linux

The regression window is exactly 5.20.0 → 5.21.0.

### Who can help?

Not sure who maintains `core_model_loading` / the checkpoint conversion mappings — whoever does, pointers appreciated.

### Information

- [x] The official example scripts
- [ ] My own modified scripts

**Tasks:**

- [ ] An officially supported task in the `examples` folder
- [x] My own task or dataset (custom model with `register_checkpoint_conversion_mapping`)

**Reproduction (bug)**

- [x] I have tried to reproduce the issue with the latest `main` version
- [x] I have tried to reproduce the issue with the latest released version

### Reproduction

A `WeightRenaming` rule whose **source pattern is end-anchored** produces a corrupted key when the mapping is reversed at `save_pretrained` time. This is exactly the rule shipped by `LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B` (`modeling_lfm3_audio.py`):

```python
from transformers.core_model_loading import WeightRenaming

t = WeightRenaming(source_patterns=r"^mask_embedding$", target_patterns="model.depth_decoder.mask_embedding")
rev = t.reverse_transform()
print(rev.rename_source_key("model.depth_decoder.mask_embedding"))
```

Output:

```text
5.20.0: ('mask_embedding', '^model.depth_decoder.mask_embedding$')
5.21.0: ('mask_embedding$', '^model.depth_decoder.mask_embedding')
```

End-to-end with a real checkpoint: load `LiquidAI/LFM3-Audio-2B` and `save_pretrained()` it. With 5.21.0 the saved safetensors contains the tensor under the key **`mask_embedding$`** instead of `mask_embedding`. That key no longer matches the forward renaming rule `^mask_embedding$` nor any parameter path, so reloading the exported checkpoint **silently** leaves `model.depth_decoder.mask_embedding` randomly initialized (`init.normal_(std=0.02)` in that model) — no warning is raised anywhere. We hit this in practice with an exported copy of that model; its `mask_embedding` tensor was present but unreachable, i.e. speech generation was broken with no error message.

The end result is that `save_pretrained` produces a checkpoint that `from_pretrained` cannot load back losslessly, which defeats the purpose of the reverse mapping.

### Root cause

`process_target_pattern()` in `src/transformers/core_model_loading.py` strips only the leading `^` from the pattern that becomes the replacement string in the reverse transform — not the trailing `$`. 5.20.0 and earlier had:

```python
  # Some mapping contains `$` to notify end of string when matching -> remove it during reverse mapping
  pattern = pattern.removesuffix("$")
```

This line (and the corresponding docstring text *"Removes `^` prefix and `$` suffix"*) was dropped in 5.21.0. The sibling `process_source_pattern()` also lost its `$` handling (`if target_pattern.endswith("$"): ...`), which is why the reverse transform in 5.21.0 also reports the source pattern without its end anchor (see the second element of the 5.21.0 tuple above).

Suggested fix: restore the `$` handling in both `process_target_pattern()` and `process_source_pattern()`.

### Expected behavior

`save_pretrained()` on a model whose checkpoint conversion mapping contains end-anchored `WeightRenaming` rules must round-trip: saved keys match the forward source patterns (here `mask_embedding`), so `from_pretrained()` reloads every weight. This is the behavior of 5.20.0 and earlier.

title: TIPSv2: bfloat16 forward fails, text pooling returns float32 (`expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype`)
body:
### System info

- transformers main @ `0460c6d977` (5.22.0.dev0), torch 2.14.1
- CPU (also on CUDA A10G)

### Who can help?

@vasqu @molbap (reviewed and merged #46347), @Ternura143 (added TIPSv2 in #46347)

### Reproduction

A `Tipsv2Model` loaded in bfloat16 cannot run a forward pass with both text and images:

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
from transformers import AutoProcessor, Tipsv2Model

model_id = "google/tipsv2-b14"
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = Tipsv2Model.from_pretrained(model_id, dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
images = [np.full((224, 224, 3), c, np.uint8) for c in ((200, 30, 30), (30, 30, 200))]
inputs = processor(text=["a red square", "a blue square"], images=images, return_tensors="pt", padding=True)
inputs = inputs.to(dtype=torch.bfloat16)

with torch.no_grad():
  model(**inputs)
```

```
  File ".../models/tipsv2/modeling_tipsv2.py", line 1114, in forward
  logits_per_text = torch.matmul(text_embeds, image_embeds.t().to(text_embeds.device))
RuntimeError: expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16
```

The same failure through the model integration contract (MIC) for TIPSv2, on its 40 MB slim fixture (CPU, about 3 s). The contract is published as [`huggingface-mic/tipsv2-b14-mic`](<url>) and pinned in the `prototypes` fleet. Its bfloat16 variant is declared unmeasured until this is fixed; `--run-declared` runs it anyway:

```bash
git clone <url> && cd transformers-mic
pip install -e . && pip install -e /path/to/transformers
LOCK=$(python -c "from transformers_mic import fleet; print(fleet.download('prototypes', 'main')[0])")
python example/run.py --framework transformers --lock "$LOCK" --contract TIPSv2 \
  --variant bfloat16 --run-declared --fixtures-only --no-baseline
# {"target": "tipsv2-b14-mic", "status": "error", ... "RuntimeError: expected m1 and m2 to have the same dtype, but got: float != c10::BFloat16"}
```

### Cause

`Tipsv2TextModel` mean-pools with the integer attention mask (`modular_tipsv2.py:673`, `modeling_tipsv2.py:925`):

```python
pooling_mask = pooling_mask.to(last_hidden_state.device)
masked_hidden_state = last_hidden_state * pooling_mask[..., None]
pooled_output = masked_hidden_state.sum(dim=1) / (
  pooling_mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) + self.config.pooling_epsilon
)
```

`pooling_mask.sum(...) + pooling_epsilon` is an int64 tensor plus a Python float, so a float32 tensor; dividing the bfloat16 sum by it promotes `pooler_output` (and `text_embeds`) to float32, while `image_embeds` stay bfloat16.

### Suggested fix

Cast the mask to the hidden states' dtype in `modular_tipsv2.py` (then `make fix-copies`):

```diff
-  pooling_mask = pooling_mask.to(last_hidden_state.device)
+  pooling_mask = pooling_mask.to(device=last_hidden_state.device, dtype=last_hidden_state.dtype)
```

Verified locally: `text_model(...).pooler_output` is then bfloat16 and the full forward above succeeds. A bfloat16 test for `Tipsv2Model` with text and images would have caught it.

### Expected behavior

`Tipsv2Model` runs in bfloat16 with text and images, returning bfloat16 `text_embeds` like `image_embeds`.

title: Qwen4Exp QSA indexer: data-dependent k_layernorm calls deadlock ZeRO-3 training
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.23.0.dev0 (main @ 0460c6d977); also 5.17.0
- Platform: Linux-6.8.0-147-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.33.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.14.0
- DeepSpeed version: 0.19.7
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA)
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: yes, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, 2 ranks
- Using GPU in script?: yes
- GPU type: 2x NVIDIA H100 80GB (NVLink)

### Who can help?

@ArthurZucker @Cyrilvallez

### Reproduction

`Qwen4ExpTextQSAIndexer.forward` loops over batch x query and calls `self.k_layernorm` once per query that
has a complete key block. Under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 every module call fetches its parameters through hooks, so
ranks whose rows differ in length/padding issue different numbers of all-gathers and hang.

<details><summary>repro script</summary>

```python
# Needs 2 GPUs. Qwen4Exp's QSA indexer calls k_layernorm a data-dependent number of times, so under
# DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 two ranks with different row lengths issue different numbers of parameter all-gathers and hang.
#  TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 timeout 300 torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 qwen4exp_zero3_deadlock_sketch.py  # expect a hang / NCCL timeout
#  TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 timeout 300 torchrun --nproc_per_node 2 qwen4exp_zero3_deadlock_sketch.py leaf  # expect 3 clean steps
# The tiny config is the one our unit tests use (indexer_budget=8, so the indexer selects blocks at these lengths).
import datetime
import sys
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import deepspeed
from deepspeed.utils import set_z3_leaf_modules
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
from transformers.integrations import HfDeepSpeedConfig
from transformers.models.qwen4_exp.modeling_qwen4_exp import Qwen4ExpTextAttention, Qwen4ExpTextConfig

deepspeed.init_distributed(timeout=datetime.timedelta(seconds=120))
rank = dist.get_rank()
torch.cuda.set_device(rank)
ds = {"train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 1, "gradient_accumulation_steps": 1, "bf16": {"enabled": True},
  "zero_optimization": {"stage": 3, "stage3_param_persistence_threshold": 0},
  "optimizer": {"type": "AdamW", "params": {"lr": 1e-4}}}
keep = HfDeepSpeedConfig(ds)
cfg = Qwen4ExpTextConfig(
  vocab_size=256, hidden_size=64, intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=4,
  num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=16, full_attention_interval=4,
  num_experts=4, num_experts_per_tok=2, moe_intermediate_size=32,
  shared_expert_intermediate_size=32, ngram_vocab_size_base=512, ngram_size=3,
  heads_per_ngram=2, ple_layer_ids=[2], ple_embed_dim=64, split_ngram_parts=4,
  make_ngram_vocab_size_divisible_by=8, linear_num_key_heads=2, linear_num_value_heads=4,
  linear_key_head_dim=16, linear_value_head_dim=16, linear_conv_kernel_dim=4,
  indexer_n_heads=2, indexer_kv_heads=1, indexer_head_dim=16, indexer_budget=8,
  indexer_compress_ratio=4, hc_count=2, hc_lowrank=16, max_position_embeddings=128,
  mtp_num_hidden_layers=1, attn_implementation="sdpa", eos_token_id=0, bos_token_id=0,
)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
if "leaf" in sys.argv[1:]:
  set_z3_leaf_modules(model, [Qwen4ExpTextAttention])
engine, *_ = deepspeed.initialize(model=model, model_parameters=model.parameters(), config=ds)
for step in range(3):
  length = 48 if rank == 0 else 96  # different row lengths: different numbers of complete key blocks
  ids = torch.randint(1, 256, (1, length), device=engine.device)
  loss = engine(input_ids=ids, labels=ids).loss
  engine.backward(loss)
  engine.step()
  print(f"rank {rank} step {step} loss {loss.item():.4f}", flush=True)
print(f"rank {rank} OK", flush=True)
```

</details>

Output, same on 5.17.0 and main:
- without `leaf`: both ranks hang, then NCCL's watchdog fires after 120 s. The ranks are one all-gather apart: `[Rank 0] Watchdog caught collective operation timeout: WorkNCCL(SeqNum=563, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=4096, NumelOut=8192, ...)` vs `[Rank 1] ... WorkNCCL(SeqNum=564, OpType=_ALLGATHER_BASE, NumelIn=8, NumelOut=16, ...)`.
- with `leaf` (`set_z3_leaf_modules(model, [Qwen4ExpTextAttention])`): 3 clean steps on both ranks.


### Expected behavior

Training under ZeRO-3 should not depend on every rank calling submodules the same number of times.

#50169 (the vectorized indexer) should fix this for causal and right-padded masks, i.e. training: it calls `k_layernorm` once per forward on all pooled blocks instead of once per query. Counting every module call of one forward + backward of the config above at 48 and 96 tokens (CPU):

| | modules whose call count depends on the length |
|---|---|
| main | 1: `model.layers.3.self_attn.indexer.k_layernorm`, 45 vs 93 calls |
| #50169 | none |

I haven't re-run the 2-GPU repro on #50169 yet. Masks the vectorized path doesn't take (left padding) still go through the loop, so `set_z3_leaf_modules(model, [Qwen4ExpTextAttention])` stays the workaround there.

(Related: in training the indexed layers also get a dense [B,1,S,S] causal mask plus a scattered [B,S,S+1]
pick mask, ~38 GiB in one allocation at 141k tokens; happy to open that separately.)

title: apply_chat_template sanitize_control_tokens silently fails when a template prints a dict or list
body:
`sanitize_control_tokens=True` wraps control tokens found in user-supplied text in private-use markers (U+F0000 / U+F0001). Any chat template that prints a whole dict or list — `{{ tool | string }}`, `{{ tools[0] }}` — writes those strings with `repr()`, which escapes the markers into the literal text `\U000f0000`. The unescape step (`_get_control_token_patterns` in `src/transformers/utils/chat_template_utils.py:439-440`) only matches the raw marker characters, so it no longer finds them.

Two consequences:

- the injected control token stays a real control token, so sanitization silently fails;
- the escape junk is left in the prompt.

This hits Hugging Face's own SmolLM3-3B template (`(tool | string)`) and has been released since v5.20.0.

Repro: a tool whose description contains `<|im_end|>`, rendered with SmolLM3's template. On main the prompt has 3 `<|im_end|>` token ids instead of 2, plus literal `\U000f0000<|im_end|>\U000f0001` text in the rendered string.

Suggested fix: build `markers_re` so it also matches each marker's `repr()` form (`re.escape(ascii(marker)[1:-1])`); local change is +6/-2 in `chat_template_utils.py` plus a test case (`test_apply_chat_template_sanitize_control_tokens_tools_and_documents`), which fails on main (`2 != 1`) and passes with the fix. Three test files give 139 passed; ruff clean.

Trade-off: a string that already contains the literal text `\U000f0000` loses it. That stays safe: nothing becomes a control token.

Related gaps worth a sentence, not part of the proposed fix: tools passed through template kwargs (SmolLM3's `xml_tools` / `python_tools`) are never sanitized, and `tojson(ensure_ascii=True)` would escape the markers to surrogate-pair escapes (no template seen uses it).

cc @Rocketknight1 (author of the feature, #47386) @ArthurZucker

title: [distributed] Save/load benchmark on 8x B200: gathered save, DCP save and consolidation bottlenecks
body:
This issue tracks a benchmark of the current weight save/load paths in `transformers.distributed` on one 8x B200 node, and the bottlenecks it found. No code was changed; all numbers are for the current `main` (`144ecf007b`).

Date: 2026-10-30. Node: one 8x B200 node (183 GB per GPU, 224 CPUs, 2 TB RAM).
Software: torch 2.15.0+cu132, transformers `144ecf007b` (5.22.0.dev0), accelerate 1.15.0.
Scope: model weights only, current code, no code changes. Every run checked that the weights loaded
from the DCP checkpoint are bit-identical to the weights from the Hub-format load (0 mismatches in all runs).

## Method
- One `torchrun` launch per case: Hub-format load (`from_pretrained` on the downloaded Hub safetensors, sharded on read by
  `DtensorShardOperation`) -> gathered save (`save_pretrained()`) -> DCP save
  (`save_pretrained(..., distributed_checkpoint=True)`) -> DCP load (`from_pretrained(dcp_dir)`) -> weight check.
- Times are wall time of the slowest rank. Save times include `fsync`. All `/raid` loads are cold: the files are
  evicted from the page cache with `posix_fadvise(DONTNEED)` and `mincore` confirms 0 bytes are cached.
- Step times come from wrapping library functions in the script (`bench.py`), not from editing `src/`.
- Raw disk speed (`dd`): `/raid` (RAID0 of 8 NVMe, direct I/O) 1 stream: write 11 / read 16 GB/s,
  8 streams: write 38 / read 77 GB/s.

## Results

| Model | GB | Layout | Storage | Hub-format load (DtensorShardOperation) | Gathered save | DCP save | DCP load |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.5 | FSDP8 | `/raid` | 8.5 s (0.2 GB/s) | 2.4 s (0.6 GB/s) | 3.1 s (0.5 GB/s) | 8.9 s (0.2 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.5 | TP8 | `/raid` | 9.2 s (0.2 GB/s) | 3.5 s (0.4 GB/s) | 2.8 s (0.5 GB/s) | 8.9 s (0.2 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.5 | FSDP2×TP4 | `/raid` | 11 s (0.1 GB/s) | 4.8 s (0.3 GB/s) | 7.0 s (0.2 GB/s) | 11 s (0.1 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-0.6B | 1.5 | FSDP4×TP2 | `/raid` | 10 s (0.2 GB/s) | 4.6 s (0.3 GB/s) | 6.4 s (0.2 GB/s) | 10 s (0.1 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | 61 | TP8 | `/raid` | 46 s (1.3 GB/s) | 103 s (0.6 GB/s) | 25 s (2.5 GB/s) | 14 s (4.4 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B (MoE) | 61 | FSDP2×TP4 | `/raid` | 32 s (1.9 GB/s) | 92 s (0.7 GB/s) | 28 s (2.2 GB/s) | 16 s (3.9 GB/s) |
| Qwen2.5-72B (median of 3) | 145 | FSDP8 | `/raid` | 36 s (4.1 GB/s) | 158 s (0.9 GB/s) | 52 s (2.8 GB/s) | 18 s (8.2 GB/s) |
| Qwen2.5-72B | 145 | FSDP4×TP2 | `/raid` | 42 s (3.5 GB/s) | 160 s (0.9 GB/s) | 55 s (2.7 GB/s) | 21 s (6.9 GB/s) |
| Qwen2.5-72B | 145 | FSDP2×TP4 | `/raid` | 46 s (3.2 GB/s) | 158 s (0.9 GB/s) | 53 s (2.7 GB/s) | 19 s (7.5 GB/s) |
| Qwen3-235B-A22B (MoE) | 470 | FSDP8 | `/raid` | 44 s (10.6 GB/s) | 772 s (0.6 GB/s) | 219 s (2.1 GB/s) | 41 s (11.4 GB/s) |

Consolidation of the 72B DCP checkpoint (`consolidate_distributed_checkpoint`, one process):
202 s (0.72 GB/s), output = 1 safetensors file of 145 GB.

Run-to-run noise (72B, FSDP8, `/raid`, 3 runs): gathered save ±5%, DCP save ±3%, DCP load ±6%,
Hub-format load ±20% (24-39 s). Differences below these numbers are not meaningful.

## Plots

![Wall time per path](<url>)

![Throughput vs raw disk speed](<url>)

![Gathered save breakdown and host RAM](<url>)

![2D layouts on 72B: DCP step breakdown and peak GPU memory](<url>)

## Findings, ranked by cost

1. **Gathered save (`save_pretrained()` default) is the slowest path: 0.6-1.1 GB/s.** 72B takes ~2.6 min, 235B takes
  13 min. Rank 0 does all the work while the other 7 ranks wait in a barrier (536 s for 235B).
  Time on rank 0 for 235B: gather to CPU 236 s, `revert_weight_conversion` 172 s (MoE experts are split back into
  per-expert tensors), `safe_save_file` 335 s (1.4 GB/s from one thread).
  It is not limited by the disk: the single writer reaches ~1.9 GB/s (72B) while one disk stream can do 11 GB/s.
  Host RAM: rank 0 holds the full model on CPU. For 235B, rank 0 peaks at 775 GB RSS (1.65x the model size).

2. **Gathered save with TP keeps a full CPU copy of the model on every rank.** 30B-A3B TP8 used 490 GB of node RAM
  (8x 61 GB). By the same rule, 72B would need ~1.2 TB and 235B ~3.8 TB, more than the node has (2 TB).
  (`gather_state_dict_for_save` calls `full_tensor().cpu()` on every rank and only rank 0 keeps the result.)
  2D layouts do not have this problem (finding 7).

3. **DCP save uses only ~7% of the disk bandwidth: 2.1-2.8 GB/s** (8 writers, disk can do 38 GB/s).
  `dcp.save` is ~100% of the time.
  DCP save also needs ~2.35x the local shard size in host RAM per rank: 139 GB per rank for 235B, 1.1 TB for the node.
  Transformers creates `HuggingFaceStorageWriter` with the default `thread_count` (1). That is a likely knob (not tested).

4. **Consolidation is single-process (0.72 GB/s) and writes one file.** `consolidate_distributed_checkpoint` maps every
  tensor to file index 1, so the 72B output is a single 145 GB file. The Hub rejects files above 50 GB, so
  `save_pretrained(..., distributed_checkpoint=True, push_to_hub=True)` will likely fail for models above ~50 GB
  (not tested).

5. **Every `from_pretrained` with `distributed_config` pays ~6-8 s to create the device mesh**
  (`prepare_distribute_model`, mostly `split_group`). This does not depend on model size. It is ~40% of the 72B DCP
  load and ~90% of the 0.6B loads. It grows with each call in the same process (7.6 -> 8.2 -> 8.8 s over 3 calls)
  and is 13 s on the first call when the process group does not exist yet (separate test, `mesh_test.py`).

6. **Loads are fast at large scale.** DCP load: 18 s for 72B (8.2 GB/s), 41 s for 235B (11.4 GB/s). Hub-format
  load (`DtensorShardOperation`): 44 s for 235B (10.6 GB/s). At 235B the DCP format is not much faster to load (41 s vs 44 s).
  For 30B-A3B with TP8, the Hub-format load is slower (46 s, 1.3 GB/s) than DCP (14 s); it also fuses the experts while loading, which DCP does not need.

7. **2D layouts (FSDP x TP) cost about the same time as FSDP8, but DCP needs more GPU memory.**
  For 72B, FSDP4×TP2 and FSDP2×TP4 match FSDP8 on gathered save (158-160 s) and are close on DCP save (53-55 s vs 52 s)
  and DCP load (19-21 s vs 18 s). The Hub-format load is a bit slower (42-46 s vs 36 s, just above its ±20% noise).
  The gathered save takes the FSDP branch, so only rank 0 keeps a CPU copy: 30B-A3B with FSDP2×TP4 used 100 GB of
  node RAM, against 490 GB with TP8.
  The `_StridedShard` redistribute (`_redistribute_state_dict`) is the main extra cost: ~4 s on DCP save and ~2 s on
  DCP load for 72B (8-10% of those phases). It is partly a fixed cost: it still takes 3-4 s for the 0.6B model.
  It also raises peak GPU memory: DCP save peaks at 31.8 GB per GPU vs 18.2 GB for FSDP8 (+75% of the local shard),
  and DCP load at 62 GB vs 36.5 GB with both models resident (+140% of the local shard). 30B-A3B TP8 shows the same
  pattern (DCP save 14.0 GB vs 7.8 GB) because its fused experts are also `_StridedShard`.
  Hub-format load host RAM grows with the TP degree: 72B peaks at 20 / 26 / 38 GB RSS per rank for FSDP8 / FSDP4×TP2 /
  FSDP2×TP4.

## What was not measured
Optimizer state, resharding (save with one layout, load with another), EP, TP8 on 72B/235B
(host RAM, see finding 2), 2D layouts on 235B, multi-node. Each case ran once, except 72B FSDP8 on `/raid` (3 runs).

## Reproduce
`torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 bench.py run --model-dir <model> --layout {fsdp8,tp8,fsdp2tp4,fsdp4tp2} --out-dir <dir> --results <file>.json`, then
`python bench.py consolidate --dcp-dir <dir>/dcp --out-dir <out> --results <file>.json` for consolidation (run with `--keep-dcp` first).

<details>
<summary>bench.py</summary>

```python
"""Measure the current transformers.distributed weight save/load paths.

8 ranks: torchrun --nproc-per-node 8 bench.py run --model-dir SRC --layout {fsdp8,tp8,fsdp2tp4,fsdp4tp2} \\
  --out-dir OUT --results RESULTS.json [--keep-dcp] [--no-evict] [--tag TEXT]
1 process: python bench.py consolidate --dcp-dir OUT/dcp --out-dir COND --results RESULTS.json [--delete]

Phases, each bracketed by a device sync + barrier: load_hub (from_pretrained(SRC) -> model_a),
save_gathered, save_dcp, load_dcp (from_pretrained(OUT/dcp) -> model_b), check (tensor comparison).
torch.distributed is initialized here with the same 2h timeout transformers uses. Labels may nest
(e.g. get_model_state_dict inside gather_full_state_dict), so label times are not disjoint.
"""

import argparse
import cProfile
import ctypes
import functools
import importlib
import inspect
import json
import mmap
import os
import pstats
import shutil
import socket
import subprocess
import sys
import threading
import time
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed.checkpoint as dcp
from torch.distributed.tensor import DTensor

import transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, PreTrainedConfig, PreTrainedModel
from transformers.distributed import DistributedConfig
from transformers.distributed.checkpoint import consolidate_distributed_checkpoint

dist_mixin = importlib.import_module("transformers.distributed.mixin")
dist_checkpoint = importlib.import_module("transformers.distributed.checkpoint")
modeling_utils = importlib.import_module("transformers.modeling_utils")
dcp_state_dict = importlib.import_module("torch.distributed.checkpoint.state_dict")

GIB = 1024**3
LAYOUTS = {"fsdp8": (8, 1), "tp8": (1, 8), "fsdp2tp4": (2, 4), "fsdp4tp2": (4, 2)}  # name -> (fsdp_size, tp_size)
PHASES = ["load_hub", "save_gathered", "save_dcp", "load_dcp", "check"]
BASE_KEYS = {"wall", "peak_gpu_bytes", "peak_rss_bytes", "node_mem_available_drop", "bytes", "files", "steps"}
PAGE_SIZE = os.sysconf("SC_PAGE_SIZE")
PHASE = {"name": None}  # current phase; step timers only record while it is set
STEPS = {}  # (phase, label) -> [seconds, calls]


def _timed(function, label):
  @functools.wraps(function)
  def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
  if PHASE["name"] is None:
  return function(*args, **kwargs)
  started = time.perf_counter()
  try:
  return function(*args, **kwargs)
  finally:
  torch.cuda.synchronize()  # a step must not absorb work launched by an earlier one
  step = STEPS.setdefault((PHASE["name"], label), [0.0, 0])
  step[0] += time.perf_counter() - started
  step[1] += 1

  return wrapper


def add_step(label, seconds):
  step = STEPS.setdefault((PHASE["name"], label), [0.0, 0])
  step[0] += seconds
  step[1] += 1


def patch(target, name, label):
  """Patch a module attribute or a class method; transformers looks these up at call time."""
  raw = inspect.getattr_static(target, name)
  function = raw.__func__ if isinstance(raw, (staticmethod, classmethod)) else raw
  wrapped = _timed(function, label)
  setattr(target, name, type(raw)(wrapped) if isinstance(raw, (staticmethod, classmethod)) else wrapped)


def instrument():
  patch(dist_mixin, "gather_full_state_dict", "gather_full_state_dict")
  patch(dist_mixin, "gather_state_dict_for_save", "gather_state_dict_for_save")
  patch(modeling_utils, "safe_save_file", "safe_save_file")
  patch(modeling_utils, "revert_weight_conversion", "revert_weight_conversion")
  patch(modeling_utils, "remove_tied_weights_from_state_dict", "remove_tied_weights_from_state_dict")
  patch(dist_mixin, "_distributed_barrier", "mixin._distributed_barrier")
  patch(dist_checkpoint, "_distributed_barrier", "checkpoint._distributed_barrier")
  patch(dist_checkpoint, "_redistribute_state_dict", "_redistribute_state_dict")
  patch(dist_mixin, "_load_model_checkpoint_distributed", "_load_model_checkpoint_distributed")
  patch(dcp, "save", "dcp.save")
  patch(dcp, "load", "dcp.load")
  patch(dcp_state_dict, "get_model_state_dict", "get_model_state_dict")
  patch(dcp_state_dict, "set_model_state_dict", "set_model_state_dict")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "_load_pretrained_model", "_load_pretrained_model")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "_move_missing_keys_from_meta_to_device", "_move_missing_keys_from_meta_to_device")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "initialize_weights", "initialize_weights")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "prepare_distribute_model", "prepare_distribute_model")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "maybe_distribute_model", "maybe_distribute_model")
  patch(PreTrainedModel, "_finalize_model_loading", "_finalize_model_loading")
  patch(modeling_utils, "_get_resolved_checkpoint_files", "_get_resolved_checkpoint_files")
  patch(PreTrainedConfig, "from_pretrained", "config.from_pretrained")


def rss_bytes():
  with open("/proc/self/statm") as handle:
  return int(handle.read().split()[1]) * PAGE_SIZE


def mem_available():
  info = dict(line.split(": ", 1) for line in Path("/proc/meminfo").read_text().splitlines())
  return int(info["MemAvailable"].split()[0]) * 1024


def start_sampler():
  samples = {"stop": False, "rss": rss_bytes(), "mem_start": mem_available(), "mem_min": mem_available()}

  def loop():
  while not samples["stop"]:
  samples["rss"] = max(samples["rss"], rss_bytes())
  samples["mem_min"] = min(samples["mem_min"], mem_available())
  time.sleep(0.05)

  samples["thread"] = threading.Thread(target=loop, daemon=True)
  samples["thread"].start()
  return samples


def stop_sampler(samples):
  samples["stop"] = True
  samples["thread"].join()


def sync():
  torch.cuda.synchronize()
  if dist.is_initialized():
  dist.barrier()


def all_ranks_min(ok):
  flag = torch.tensor([int(ok)], device="cuda")
  dist.all_reduce(flag, op=dist.ReduceOp.MIN)
  return bool(flag.item())


def all_ranks_sum(value):
  total = torch.tensor([value], device="cuda")
  dist.all_reduce(total, op=dist.ReduceOp.SUM)
  return int(total.item())


def require(ok, message, rank):
  if ok:
  return
  if rank == 0:
  print(f"[bench] ABORT: {message}", flush=True)
  else:
  time.sleep(2.0)
  sys.exit(1)


def free_space_ok(path, model_bytes):
  return shutil.disk_usage(path).free >= model_bytes + 200 * GIB


def dir_stats(path):
  files = [file for file in Path(path).rglob("*") if file.is_file()]
  return len(files), sum(file.stat().st_size for file in files)


def fsync_tree(path):
  for root, _, names in os.walk(path):
  for entry in [os.path.join(root, name) for name in names] + [root]:
  fd = os.open(entry, os.O_RDONLY)
  try:
  os.fsync(fd)
  finally:
  os.close(fd)


def finish_save(directory, rank):
  """Rank 0 records the written file count/bytes and fsyncs them (the `fsync` step)."""
  if rank != 0:
  return {}
  files, nbytes = dir_stats(directory)
  started = time.perf_counter()
  fsync_tree(directory)
  add_step("fsync", time.perf_counter() - started)
  return {"bytes": nbytes, "files": files}


LIBC = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6", use_errno=True)
LIBC.mmap.restype = ctypes.c_void_p
LIBC.mmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_long]
LIBC.mincore.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t, ctypes.c_void_p]
LIBC.munmap.argtypes = [ctypes.c_void_p, ctypes.c_size_t]


def cached_bytes(path):
  """Page-cache resident bytes of the files under `path`, via mincore(2)."""
  total = 0
  for file in Path(path).rglob("*"):
  size = file.stat().st_size if file.is_file() else 0
  if size == 0:
  continue
  fd = os.open(file, os.O_RDONLY)
  try:
  address = LIBC.mmap(None, size, mmap.PROT_READ, mmap.MAP_SHARED, fd, 0)
  pages = (size + PAGE_SIZE - 1) // PAGE_SIZE
  vector = (ctypes.c_ubyte * pages)()
  if LIBC.mincore(address, size, vector) != 0:
  raise OSError(ctypes.get_errno(), "mincore failed")
  LIBC.munmap(address, size)
  finally:
  os.close(fd)
  total += sum(byte & 1 for byte in vector) * PAGE_SIZE
  return total


def evict(path, rank):
  """Drop `path`'s files from the page cache on rank 0, then wait for every rank."""
  record = {}
  if rank == 0:
  started = time.perf_counter()
  for file in Path(path).rglob("*"):
  if file.is_file():
  fd = os.open(file, os.O_RDONLY)
  try:
  os.posix_fadvise(fd, 0, 0, os.POSIX_FADV_DONTNEED)
  finally:
  os.close(fd)
  record = {"evict_s": round(time.perf_counter() - started, 3), "cached_bytes_after_evict": cached_bytes(path)}
  dist.barrier()
  return record


def tensor_equal(a, b):
  if isinstance(a, DTensor) != isinstance(b, DTensor):
  return False
  if isinstance(a, DTensor):
  if a.placements != b.placements:
  return False
  a, b = a.to_local(), b.to_local()
  if a.is_meta or b.is_meta or a.shape != b.shape or a.dtype != b.dtype:
  return False
  if a.device != b.device:
  a, b = a.cpu(), b.cpu()
  return bool(torch.equal(a, b))


def transformers_commit():
  root = Path(transformers.__file__).resolve().parents[1]
  try:
  result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(root), "rev-parse", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, text=True)
  except (OSError, subprocess.SubprocessError):
  return None
  if result.returncode != 0:
  return None
  return result.stdout.strip() or None


def env_info():
  gpu = torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if torch.cuda.is_available() else None
  return {
  "hostname": socket.gethostname(), "torch": torch.__version__, "torch_cuda": torch.version.cuda,
  "gpu_count": torch.cuda.device_count(), "gpu": gpu,
  "transformers": transformers.__version__, "transformers_commit": transformers_commit(),
  }


def write_results(path, results):
  target = Path(path)
  target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  target.write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2) + "\n")


def run_phase(name, body, records, rank):
  sync()
  torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
  samples = start_sampler()
  PHASE["name"] = name
  profiler = cProfile.Profile() if rank == 0 and os.environ.get("BENCH_PROFILE") == name else None

  profiler.enable()
  extra = body() or {}
  sync()
  wall = time.perf_counter() - started
  if profiler:
  profiler.disable()
  pstats.Stats(profiler).sort_stats("cumulative").print_stats(40)

  record = {
  "wall": wall,
  "peak_gpu_bytes": torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated(),
  "peak_rss_bytes": samples["rss"],
  "node_mem_available_drop": samples["mem_start"] - samples["mem_min"],
  "bytes": 0,
  "files": 0,
  "steps": {
  label: {"s": round(seconds, 4), "n": calls}
  for (phase, label), (seconds, calls) in STEPS.items()
  if phase == name
  },
  }
  record.update(extra)
  records[name] = record
  print(f"[bench] rank {rank} {name}: wall={wall:.2f}s", flush=True)


def merge_phase(records):

  "peak_gpu_bytes_max": max(record["peak_gpu_bytes"] for record in records),

  "files": max(record["files"] for record in records),

  merged["gb_per_s"] = merged["bytes"] / wall_max / 1e9 if wall_max and merged["bytes"] else None

title: RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor penalizes masked padding tokens, causing batch-dependent EOS scores and generation
body:
### System Info

Transformers: 5.16.1
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu128
Environment: Kaggle notebook
Models tested: distilbert/distilgpt2, Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
Inference: single-process, greedy decoding
Repetition penalty: 2.0
Padding: left, with pad_token_id == eos_token_id

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction


While comparing single-prompt and mixed-length batched generation noticed that left-padding changes EOS scores even when the padding is excluded by the attention mask. With `repetition_penalty=2.0` and `pad_token_id == eos_token_id`, `RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor` treats masked padding tokens as previously seen tokens, incorrectly penalizing EOS.

###  Reproduction

```python
import torch
from transformers.generation.logits_process import RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor

processor = RepetitionPenaltyLogitsProcessor(penalty=2.0)

# EOS = PAD = 0; valid prompt = [1, 2]
solo = torch.tensor([[1, 2]])
padded = torch.tensor([[0, 1, 2]])  # attention_mask = [0, 1, 1]
scores = torch.tensor([[3.0, -2.0, -2.0, 2.5]])

a = processor(solo, scores.clone())
b = processor(padded, scores.clone())

print("EOS:", a[0, 0].item(), b[0, 0].item())
print("Next token:", a.argmax(-1).item(), b.argmax(-1).item())
```

Output:

```text
EOS: 3.0 1.5
Next token: 0 3
```

The processor does not receive an attention mask, so it cannot distinguish valid tokens from padding.

### Pretrained-model validation

Reproduced using `distilbert/distilgpt2` through `model.generate()`, comparing `"The capital of France is"` alone versus in a mixed-length batch with 13 masked padding tokens.

| Measurement | Individual | Batched |
|---|---:|---:|
| Raw EOS logit | -68.7572 | -68.7572 |
| Processed EOS logit | -68.7572 | -137.5144 |

Maximum first-step raw-logit difference: `3.81e-05`.

With the same controlled EOS sequence bias applied to both inputs, actual generation also diverged:

| Measurement | Individual | Batched |
|---|---|---|
| Processed EOS score | -43.0366 | -86.0732 |
| Next token | 50256 (EOS) | 262 |
| Continuation | `<|endoftext|>` | ` the largest city in Europe, with a` |

The bias was introduced specifically to expose output divergence; ordinary generation produced identical continuations.

### Boundary tests

Tested padding lengths of 1, 13, and 32:

- EOS only in masked padding: incorrectly penalized in 3/3 cases.
- Genuine EOS in valid prompt: correctly penalized in 3/3 cases.

With `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, all 8 tested cases showed different processed EOS scores, although generated outputs remained identical.

### Expected behavior / possible fix

Repetition penalties should ignore attention-masked padding while preserving penalties for genuine prompt tokens and newly generated tokens. The fix should also account for beam expansion, multiple return sequences, and backward compatibility.


### Expected behavior

Adding attention-masked padding to a prompt should not affect the repetition penalty when the valid token history and underlying model logits are unchanged.

Specifically:

- Tokens with `attention_mask=0` should not contribute to repetition penalties.
- Genuine prompt tokens, including a real EOS token, should still be penalized normally.
- Newly generated tokens should continue to contribute to repetition history.
- A prompt generated individually or as part of a mixed-length batch should receive equivalent processed scores when its underlying model logits are equivalent.

The expected behavior should hold even when `pad_token_id == eos_token_id`.

Ideally, the fix would preserve existing behavior for unpadded inputs and for users calling the logits processor directly.

I'd be happy to work on a PR with regression tests if this approach makes sense.

title: fsdp_config["ignored_modules"] is silently ignored by TrainingArguments
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.22.0.dev0
- Platform: Linux-6.8.0-147-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.33.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.14.0
- DeepSpeed version: 0.19.7
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA)
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: no (TrainingArguments only)
- Using GPU in script?: no
- GPU type: NVIDIA H200 (not used though)
(main @ 9c64f0c; the repro below also ran on CPU, macOS, transformers 5.22.0.dev0: prints `None`)

### Who can help?

@SunMarc

### Reproduction

  args = TrainingArguments("out", fsdp=True, fsdp_config={"version": 2, "ignored_modules": "lm_head"})
  print(args.fsdp_plugin_args.get("ignored_modules"))  # None

`_process_fsdp_args` copies a fixed set of keys into the FSDP plugin kwargs and `ignored_modules` is not
among them, although accelerate's `FullyShardedDataParallelPlugin` supports it (regex fullmatch; FSDP2
turns the matches into ignored params). Unknown keys aren't validated, so this fails silently and the module
gets sharded. Setting `FSDP_IGNORED_MODULES` in the environment works, because accelerate falls back to it.

Use case: keeping a frozen `lm_head` unsharded under FSDP2 so a fused linear-cross-entropy kernel gets a
plain tensor instead of a DTensor.

### Expected behavior

`ignored_modules` in `fsdp_config` reaches the plugin (or unknown keys raise/warn).
i can open a small pr with in tests/trainer/test_training_args.py

  def test_fsdp_config_ignored_modules(self):
  """`ignored_modules` in `fsdp_config` reaches the accelerate FSDP plugin args."""
  with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp_dir:
  args = TrainingArguments(output_dir=tmp_dir, fsdp=True, fsdp_config={"ignored_modules": "lm_head"})
  self.assertEqual(args.fsdp_plugin_args["ignored_modules"], "lm_head")

  args = TrainingArguments(output_dir=tmp_dir, fsdp=True)
  self.assertNotIn("ignored_modules", args.fsdp_plugin_args)

title: glm5_next / qwen4_exp: hyper-connection mapping keeps full-width fp32 activations for backward
body:
### Feature request

Since the mapping is per-token and cheap, recomputing it in backward (e.g. checkpointing it in token chunks)
removes this with no change to results. Would a checkpointed mapping be welcome in the modeling code, or is
this better left to training frameworks?

### Motivation

ML Team Lead using transformers/huggingface ecosystem to train LoRAs. (and vLLM as well, send my best regards to Harry)

practical motivation:

`Glm5NextTextHyperConnection` flattens the 4 residual streams to [S, 4*hidden] and runs RMSNorm + linear in
fp32 (modeling_glm5_next.py:300-303); `Qwen4ExpTextGatedResidual` does the same in fp32 for 4 x 2560 streams.
Autograd keeps those fp32 tensors for backward at both mapping sites of every layer:

| model | tokens / GPU | saved by the mapping, one layer |
|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.3-Flash | 56k | ~13.6 GiB |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next | 125k | ~35 GB |

Measured on transformers main, one GLM-5.3 mapping (`layers[0].attn_hc`), what autograd keeps after the forward:

| tokens | held after forward | of which outputs | saved for backward |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8,192 | 1.12 GiB | 0.06 GiB | 138.7 KB / token |
| 16,384 | 2.21 GiB | 0.13 GiB | 136.5 KB / token |
| 32,768 | 4.39 GiB | 0.25 GiB | 135.5 KB / token |

That is ~136 KB per token per mapping against 32 KB for the bf16 streams themselves, two mappings per layer. (Our training code recomputes the mapping in 4,096-token chunks; I haven't benchmarked a recompute version against the stock modeling code here.)

### Your contribution

I have chunked-recompute mapping ready as a PR when needed

title: RoPE inv_freq is initialized in bf16 under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 again (regression of #28760 from #47598)
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.17.0 (reproduced on main 5.22.0.dev0)
- Platform: Linux-6.8.0-147-generic-x86_64-with-glibc2.39
- Python version: 3.12.3
- Huggingface_hub version: 1.33.0
- Safetensors version: 0.8.0
- Accelerate version: 1.14.0
- DeepSpeed version: 0.19.7 (reproduced on on 0.19.8 and master)
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.13.0+cu130 (CUDA)
- Using distributed or parallel set-up in script?: yes, DeepSpeed ZeRO-3 (1 rank is enough)
- Using GPU in script?: yes
- GPU type: NVIDIA H200
Also reproduced on main 5.22.0.dev0 (9c64f0c); deepspeed 0.19.7, 0.19.8 and master (1bdaaf73); 1× H200, driver 595.91.07.

### Who can help?

@Cyrilvallez (author of #47598)

### Reproduction

Under ZeRO-3, `from_pretrained` runs inside `deepspeed.zero.Init`, which wraps tensor constructors such as
`torch.arange` and casts floating results to the training dtype. #28760 worked around this by building RoPE
frequencies from an int64 arange. #47598 ("Simplify all Rotary modules") moved the default init into each
model as `torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.float)`, so under ZeRO-3 `inv_freq` is bf16 again
(177 modeling files on main). `_init_weights` copies fresh values into the existing bf16 buffer, so it stays bf16.

<details><summary>repro script (rope_zero3.py)</summary>

```python
# Under DeepSpeed ZeRO-3, does zero.Init leave RoPE inv_freq in bf16, and how far off are the angles?
import os, sys, torch, deepspeed, transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, LlamaConfig
from transformers.integrations import HfDeepSpeedConfig
deepspeed.init_distributed()
stage = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 3
ds = {"train_micro_batch_size_per_gpu": 1, "zero_optimization": {"stage": stage}, "bf16": {"enabled": True}}
if os.environ.get("KEEP"):  # DeepSpeed >= 0.19.8: keep these buffers in fp32, e.g. KEEP=rotary_emb
  ds["data_types"] = {"keep_in_fp32_modules": [os.environ["KEEP"]]}
keep = HfDeepSpeedConfig(ds)  # must stay alive: makes from_config use zero.Init for stage 3
if os.environ.get("STRICT"):  # list rotary_emb in _keep_in_fp32_modules_strict, for DeepSpeed's "auto" mode
  import transformers.models.llama.modeling_llama as ml, transformers.models.qwen3_5.modeling_qwen3_5 as mq
  for cls in (ml.LlamaPreTrainedModel, mq.Qwen3_5PreTrainedModel):
  cls._keep_in_fp32_modules_strict = list(getattr(cls, "_keep_in_fp32_modules_strict", None) or []) + ["rotary_emb"]
theta, dim = 10_000_000.0, 256
cfgs = {"llama": LlamaConfig(hidden_size=512, intermediate_size=1024, num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=2,
  num_key_value_heads=1, head_dim=dim, rope_parameters={"rope_type": "default", "rope_theta": theta},
  vocab_size=1000),
  "llama_yarn": LlamaConfig(hidden_size=512, intermediate_size=1024, num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=2,
  num_key_value_heads=1, head_dim=dim, vocab_size=1000, max_position_embeddings=1048576,
  rope_parameters={"rope_type": "yarn", "rope_theta": theta, "factor": 4.0,
  "original_max_position_embeddings": 262144})}
try:
  from transformers import Qwen3_5TextConfig
  cfgs["qwen3_5_text"] = Qwen3_5TextConfig(hidden_size=512, intermediate_size=1024, num_hidden_layers=4,
  num_attention_heads=2, num_key_value_heads=1, head_dim=dim, vocab_size=1000,
  linear_num_key_heads=2, linear_num_value_heads=2, linear_key_head_dim=64, linear_value_head_dim=64)
except Exception as e:
  print("no qwen3_5:", e)
print(f"transformers {transformers.__version__}, deepspeed {deepspeed.__version__}, torch {torch.__version__}, ZeRO stage {stage}")
for name, cfg in cfgs.items():
  model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_config(cfg, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
  rot = model.model.rotary_emb
  inv = rot.inv_freq.detach().float().cpu()
  d = inv.numel() * 2
  th = getattr(cfg, "rope_parameters", {}).get("rope_theta", theta) if isinstance(getattr(cfg, "rope_parameters", None), dict) else theta
  if name == "llama_yarn":  # reference: the same model built without ZeRO-3, in fp32
  from transformers.modeling_rope_utils import ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS
  ref = ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS["yarn"](cfg, "cpu")[0].double()
  else:
  ref = 1.0 / (th ** (torch.arange(0, d, 2, dtype=torch.int64).double() / d))
  rel = ((inv.double() - ref).abs() / ref).max().item()
  for pos in (4096, 65536, 262144):
  ang = (pos * (inv.double() - ref)).abs().max().item()
  print(f"{name:13s} inv_freq dtype={rot.inv_freq.dtype} max_rel_err={rel:.2e} pos={pos:>6d} max_angle_err={ang:.3f} rad")
```

</details>

`torchrun --nproc_per_node 1 rope_zero3.py 3` (ZeRO-3) / `... 0` (ZeRO-0). head_dim 256, rope_theta 1e7, against an fp64 reference:

| transformers | ZeRO | `inv_freq` dtype | max rel. error | max angle error at pos 65,536 |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|
| 5.17.0 | 0 | float32 | 8.5e-8 | 0.003 rad |
| 5.17.0 | 3 | bfloat16 | 3.7e-3 | 117.7 rad (llama), 28.6 rad (qwen3_5_text) |
| main 9c64f0c | 3 | bfloat16 | 3.7e-3 | 117.7 rad |
| 5.12.1 | 3 | float32 | 8.5e-8 | 0.003 rad |
| d24918c442 (parent of #47598) | 3 | float32 | 8.5e-8 | 0.003 rad |
| 6034e90c7d (#47598) | 3 | bfloat16 | 3.7e-3 | 117.7 rad |

YaRN (`modeling_rope_utils`, int64 arange) is unaffected. On main, changing llama's arange back to `torch.arange(0, dim, 2, dtype=torch.int64).float()` restores fp32 (8.5e-8).

Impact (Qwen3.8-27B, LoRA, one 65k-token row): grad norm 0.78 under ZeRO-3 vs 7.91 on one GPU; ZeRO-0/2
bit-identical to one GPU; rebuilding the rotary module in fp32 after load makes ZeRO-3 bit-identical too.

This is not the `.to(bf16)` case from #49288: it's the documented `from_pretrained(dtype=...)` path.

### Expected behavior

`inv_freq` stays fp32 under ZeRO-3, as with every other loading path (e.g. restore the int64 arange, or
re-create the buffers in fp32 in `_init_weights` rather than copying into them).

title: PaliGemma 2 ignores final_logit_softcapping
body:
### System Info

- `transformers` version: 5.21.1 (also checked main)
- Platform: Windows-11-10.0.26200-SP0
- Python version: 3.14.6
- PyTorch version (accelerator?): 2.15.0+cpu (NA)

### Who can help?

@zucchini-nlp

### Reproduction

PaliGemma 2 checkpoints use a Gemma 2 text config with `final_logit_softcapping=30.0`, but `PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration.forward` never applies it. It just does `logits = self.lm_head(hidden_states)`.

Up to v4.51 the language model was built with `AutoModelForCausalLM`, so `Gemma2ForCausalLM` applied the cap. Since v4.52 it's `AutoModel` plus a separate `lm_head`, and the cap got lost. Gemma3n and T5Gemma apply it after `lm_head`, PaliGemma doesn't.

Tiny repro on CPU, comparing against `Gemma2ForCausalLM` with the same weights:

```python
import torch
from transformers import Gemma2Config, Gemma2ForCausalLM, PaliGemmaConfig, PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration, SiglipVisionConfig

torch.manual_seed(0)
text_config = Gemma2Config(
  vocab_size=1000, hidden_size=64, intermediate_size=128, num_hidden_layers=2,
  num_attention_heads=4, num_key_value_heads=2, head_dim=16, final_logit_softcapping=30.0,
)
vision_config = SiglipVisionConfig(
  hidden_size=32, intermediate_size=64, num_hidden_layers=1, num_attention_heads=2, image_size=28, patch_size=14
)
config = PaliGemmaConfig(
  text_config=text_config.to_dict(), vision_config=vision_config.to_dict(), projection_dim=64, image_token_index=999
)
config._attn_implementation = "eager"
text_config._attn_implementation = "eager"

pali = PaliGemmaForConditionalGeneration(config).eval()
gemma2 = Gemma2ForCausalLM(text_config).eval()
gemma2.model.load_state_dict(pali.model.language_model.state_dict())
gemma2.lm_head.load_state_dict(pali.lm_head.state_dict())
with torch.no_grad():  # make the logits large enough for the cap to matter
  pali.lm_head.weight.mul_(50)
  gemma2.lm_head.weight.mul_(50)

input_ids = torch.randint(0, 900, (1, 8))
with torch.no_grad():
  a = pali(input_ids=input_ids, labels=input_ids)
  b = gemma2(input_ids=input_ids, labels=input_ids)

print(a.logits.abs().max(), b.logits.abs().max())  # 72.03 vs 29.51
print(torch.allclose(torch.tanh(a.logits / 30) * 30, b.logits, atol=1e-4))  # True
print(a.loss, b.loss)  # 65.31 vs 31.77
```

Greedy decoding doesn't change since tanh is monotonic, which is probably why the integration tests didn't catch it. Sampling with temperature, beam scores, returned logprobs and the training loss all differ from the original model.

### Expected behavior

PaliGemma should apply `final_logit_softcapping` from the text config after `lm_head`, like Gemma3n does. PaliGemma 1 uses `GemmaConfig`, which doesn't have that field, so it would need a `getattr`. I can open a PR with the fix and a test comparing against `Gemma2ForCausalLM` if that sounds right.

title: WatermarkDetector p-values are wrong for large z-scores (exactly 0 above z ≈ 7.7)
body:
### System Info

- transformers version: 5.20.1
- Platform: Linux-6.12.107+deb13-amd64-x86_64-with-glibc2.41
- Python version: 3.12.12
- NumPy version: 2.5.4

### Who can help?

_No response_

### Reproduction

`WatermarkDetector._compute_pval` in `src/transformers/generation/watermarking.py` approximates the normal tail as

```python
return 1 - (0.5 * (1 + np.sign(z) * (1 - np.exp(-2 * z**2 / np.pi))))
```

```python
import math, numpy as np
from transformers.generation.watermarking import WatermarkDetector
for z in [4, 6, 8]:
  print(z, WatermarkDetector._compute_pval(None, np.array([z]))[0], 0.5 * math.erfc(z / math.sqrt(2)))
# 4  1.9e-05  3.2e-05
# 6  5.6e-11  9.9e-10
# 8  0.0  6.2e-16
```

This issue was found and reported by Claude Opus 5.5.

### Expected behavior

The returned p_value should match the exact normal tail, 0.5 * erfc(z / sqrt(2)). Currently it is too small for z > 3.5 (about 18x at z = 6) and exactly 0 for z ≳ 7.7. `prediction` uses `z_threshold` and is not affected.

Suggested fix: `return 0.5 * erfc(z / sqrt(2))` (or `scipy.special.ndtr(-z)`).

title: Image preprocessing ~20% slower on Linux since v5.18.0: in-place normalize (#48897) causes extra page faults
body:
### System Info

- transformers 5.18.0 and 5.19.0 (regression); 5.17.0 is fine. `main` still has the change.
- Linux x86_64 (glibc), Intel Xeon Platinum 8488C, Python 3.14
- torch 2.13.0+cpu, torchvision 0.28.0+cpu, Pillow 12.3.0
- 8 torch threads

### Who can help?

@jzakrzew @Rocketknight1 (author and co-author of #48897)

### Reproduction

Since v5.18.0, the Qwen3-VL image processor (`Qwen2VLImageProcessor`, torchvision backend) is ~20% slower on CPU for a multi-image request. The output is identical, so this is perf only.

I bisected the 300 commits between the v5.17.0 and v5.19.0 merge-bases on `main`. The first bad commit is 207fca7b5b, #48897 "Skip an unnecessary image copy in the torchvision image normalization path". Reverting only its change to `image_processing_backends.py` on top of v5.19.0 restores the old latency.

```python
import resource, statistics, time
import numpy as np, torch
from PIL import Image
from transformers import AutoImageProcessor

torch.set_num_threads(8)
proc = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct")
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
batch = lambda: [Image.fromarray(rng.integers(0, 256, (512, 512, 3), dtype=np.uint8)) for _ in range(30)]

for _ in range(3):
  proc(images=batch(), return_tensors="pt")
ts, fl = [], []
for _ in range(40):
  imgs = batch()
  f0 = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_minflt
  t = time.perf_counter()
  out = proc(images=imgs, return_tensors="pt")
  ts.append((time.perf_counter() - t) * 1e3)
  fl.append(resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_minflt - f0)
  del out
print(f"median {statistics.median(ts):.1f} ms, min {min(ts):.1f} ms, minor faults/call {statistics.median(fl):.0f}")
```

Results (30 x 512x512 images per call, `pixel_values` shape `(30720, 1536)` in every case):

| transformers | min ms | median ms | minor page faults / call |
|---|---|---|---|
| main @ c210bb3966 (parent of #48897) | 37.8 - 39.9 | 49 - 55 | 87k - 92k |
| main @ 207fca7b5b (#48897) | 50.1 - 51.8 | 59 - 61 | 106k |
| v5.19.0 base | 49.6 - 50.2 | 55 - 56 | 95k |
| v5.19.0 base + revert of #48897 | 38.2 - 41.2 | 45 - 52 | 66k - 93k |

We first saw this in vLLM. vLLM's multimodal processor timing (`apply_hf_processor`, Qwen3-VL, 30 images/request) goes from 84.9 ms (5.17.0) to 104.4 ms (5.19.0), and back to 86.1 ms with only #48897 reverted.

**Analysis.** The extra time is page faults, not compute:
- In the vLLM path, minor page faults per request rise in exact steps of 23,040. That is 30 images x 768 pages, i.e. one extra freshly mapped 3 MB float32 image buffer per image (sometimes two).
- The slower ops are memory-bound copies on fresh memory: `Tensor.to(float32)`, the patchify `reshape`, and `np.array(PIL)`.
- Setting `MALLOC_MMAP_THRESHOLD_=268435456 MALLOC_TRIM_THRESHOLD_=1073741824` (glibc) removes the faults. Both versions then run at the same speed, ~53 ms in the vLLM path.

So with glibc malloc, the in-place normalize changes the allocation/free pattern. Before #48897, the extra temporary from out-of-place `normalize` was freed early, and later ~3 MB buffers reused that memory. Now more of them come from new mmaps and fault on first touch. I have not traced the exact malloc sequence. The effect is likely allocator-specific, so it may not show on macOS.

`BaseVideoProcessor` and the other `TorchvisionBackend` image processors call the same `rescale_and_normalize`, so other models may be affected too. The size of the effect depends on image size and count.

### Expected behavior

No slowdown: #48897 was intended as a speedup. Possible fixes: revert #48897, or make the in-place normalize opt-in.

title: ClapFeatureExtractor forces is_longer=True in fusion mode when every clip is ≤10 s
body:
## Reproduction

```python
import numpy as np
from transformers import ClapFeatureExtractor

fe = ClapFeatureExtractor()  # 48 kHz, max_length_s=10
sr = fe.sampling_rate

def flags(n, secs=10):
  audio = [np.zeros(secs * sr, dtype=np.float32) for _ in range(n)]
  out = fe(audio, sampling_rate=sr, truncation="fusion", return_tensors="pt")
  return out["is_longer"].ravel().tolist()

flags(1)  # [True]  every call
flags(8)  # [False, False, True, False, False, False, False, False]  random position
```

At batch 1, `is_longer` is always `[True]`, so the clip is routed through the fusion
branch even though it is not longer than the window. At batch 8 exactly one index is
`True`, and which one changes between calls because the choice is `np.random.randint` and
nothing seeds it.

Environment: `transformers` 5.21.0, torch 2.8.0+cu128, Python 3.12. The block is
unchanged on `main` today (the `truncation == "fusion" and sum(is_longer) == 0` branch),
and the same behaviour reproduces on 5.17.0.dev0, so it is not specific to one release. My run's
environment block does not record numpy; the reproduction itself needs only
`np.random.randint` and `np.zeros`.

Source, `src/transformers/models/clap/feature_extraction_clap.py`:

```python
if truncation == "fusion" and sum(is_longer) == 0:
  # if no audio is longer than 10s, then randomly select one audio to be longer
  rand_idx = np.random.randint(0, len(input_mel))
  is_longer[rand_idx] = True
```

## Expected behaviour

Clips at or under the window should get `is_longer=False`.

`laion_clap`'s inference API does exactly that. `CLAP_Module.get_audio_embedding_from_data`
in `hook.py` calls `get_audio_features` from `training.data` once per clip with
`data_truncating='fusion'`; in that function the short-audio branch pads, stacks four
identical mels, and sets `longer = torch.tensor([False])`. The flag is randomised only in
`ToyDataset.__getitem__`, a training dataset, as `longer = random.choice([True, False])`,
where it plausibly exists so the fusion module sees both branches during training.

So the inference processor appears to have inherited a training-time behaviour, and the
reference implementation never takes the branch it forces.

## Impact on retrieval

Fused `laion/clap-htsat-fused` on AudioCaps, 957 clips, 10 s trim, cosine, R@1
text-to-audio:

| audio batch | clips forced onto the fusion branch | T2A R@1 |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 100% | 0.232 |
| 2 | 50% (random which) | 0.241 / 0.238 / 0.258 |
| 4 | 25% (single run) | 0.296 |
| 8 | 12.5% | 0.315 to 0.322 |
| 1, `is_longer` forced False | 0% | 0.349 |

Two consequences worth flagging:

- Seeding the processor makes repeats bit-identical. Two seeded batch-8 runs both give
  0.321839 with identical per-query ranks; the unseeded pair differed in 478 of 957
  ranks. The observed "nondeterminism" is this RNG, not the model.
- Forcing `is_longer=False` puts the HF path at 0.349, against 0.342 for the `laion_clap`
  package on the same fixture and trim, a 0.7 point gap, so the corrected path now matches
  the reference. On the fusion-forced path it is 0.232, an 11.0 point gap from that
  reference. On this fixture the branch routing, not the checkpoint, drives that
  difference.

Full protocol, per-query arrays and the pre-registered analysis:
<url>

## Downstream evidence

`mlboydaisuke/CLAP-HTSAT-fused-ExecuTorch` documents this same block, observes that
`is_longer` is always True at batch 1, and therefore builds the fusion branch into the
exported graph unconditionally. The quirk is already determining the behaviour of a
published export.

## Backward compatibility

Fixing this changes outputs for anyone currently running fused CLAP through this
processor, so I want to be explicit about it. At batch 1 the current behaviour is
deterministic but routes every short clip through the long-audio branch, which the
reference implementation never does. At batch above 1 it is not stable: the same clip gets
different embeddings depending on the batch size it is processed with, and on an unseeded
RNG. Anyone who wants the present behaviour for training can keep it behind a flag.

## Proposed change

Remove the random assignment from the inference processor, or gate it behind an opt-in
flag defaulting to off, so `is_longer` follows clip length. I am happy to open the PR with
the reproduction above turned into a test.

Related: #23648 (open, `ClapFeatureExtractor` padding behaviour), #30795 (closed, mentions
`is_longer` in a fine-tuning context), and PR #21931, which added batched input support
and the list-shaped `is_longer` handling.
