title: Agents window: sessions from worktrees of a bare repository are grouped under the bare git directory
body:
- VS Code Version: 1.144.0 (2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf); also reproduces on 1.145.0-insider (206844b5537c1b7582f6e81b41e1c5402c7e7fbc)
- OS Version: Windows x64

## Setup

A common way to work with many worktrees in parallel is a **bare repository plus linked worktrees**. The repository is cloned as bare, so it has no main working tree. Every branch you work on is checked out as a linked worktree, and all worktrees have equal status.

Usually the bare git directory and the worktrees share a container folder:

```
my-repo/  <- plain container folder (not a working tree)
├─ .bare/  <- bare repository (git common dir)
├─ .git  <- file: "gitdir: ./.bare"
├─ main/  <- linked worktree (branch: main)
├─ feature-a/  <- linked worktree (branch: feature-a)
└─ feature-b/  <- linked worktree (branch: feature-b)
```

The bare directory can have any name (`.bare`, `repo.git`, and so on), and the worktrees can be anywhere on disk. In every case:

- all worktrees share one git common dir, the bare repository
- there is **no main working tree**
- `git worktree list --porcelain` lists the bare repository **first**, marked `bare`, followed by the linked worktrees:

```
worktree /path/to/my-repo/.bare
bare

worktree /path/to/my-repo/main
HEAD ...
branch refs/heads/main

worktree /path/to/my-repo/feature-a
HEAD ...
branch refs/heads/feature-a
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set up the layout above: `git clone --bare <url> my-repo/.bare`, write `gitdir: ./.bare` to `my-repo/.git`, then `git worktree add main main` and `git worktree add feature-a -b feature-a` from inside `my-repo`.
2. Open `my-repo/feature-a` in a VS Code window and start a chat session. Do the same for `my-repo/main`.
3. Open the Agents window and group the sessions list by repository or workspace.

## Expected

Sessions from all worktrees of the repository are grouped under a meaningful repository name (for example `my-repo`), the same way sessions from linked worktrees of a non-bare repository are grouped under that repository.

## Actual

Sessions from all worktrees are grouped under the **bare git directory's name** (here `.bare`, or `repo.git` for a `repo.git` bare clone). Worktree sessions from every repository set up this way get a meaningless label, and repositories that use the same bare-directory naming convention can end up in a single shared group.

## Likely cause

#328374 derives the "primary repository root" from the first entry of `git worktree list --porcelain` and assumes that entry is the main working tree. In a non-bare repository it is. In a bare repository the first entry is the git common dir, which isn't a working tree, so the project label (and possibly the persisted repository root, worktree placement, and other metadata) comes from the git data directory instead of from a checkout.

## Suggested fix

When the first `git worktree list --porcelain` entry is marked `bare`, don't treat it as a working-tree root. Possible ways to derive the repository identity:

- the `origin` remote's repository name
- the bare directory's name without a `.git` suffix
- the bare directory's parent folder when the bare directory is a hidden dot-directory inside a container folder (for example `.bare` or `.git`)

Grouping should also be keyed on a URI rather than the label (#334397), so that unrelated repositories with the same label don't merge.

Related: #267606, #328374, #306592, #312770, #334397

title: MCP Apps in Copilot SDK (agent host) sessions: tool result _meta is dropped before reaching the app
body:
Version: VS Code 1.144.0 (commit 2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf), Windows

Summary
In a chat session using the Copilot: SDK Agent Host harness, the CallToolResult that an MCP App receives (ui/notifications/tool-result) contains only content, structuredContent and isError. The result's _meta is dropped. The same tool and the same app in a Local chat session receive the result unchanged, including _meta.

Apps that put viewer-only data in _meta, to keep it out of the model's context, therefore can't render in agent host sessions.

Steps to reproduce

1. Configure an HTTP MCP server with a tool whose result has a ui:// resource (an MCP App) and whose CallToolResult includes _meta, for example: `{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "short summary for the model" }],
  "isError": false,
  "_meta": { "example.com/viewerData": { "foo": "bar" } }
}`
2. In the app, log the result it receives in ontoolresult.
3. Call the tool from a Copilot: SDK Agent Host chat, then from a Local chat.

Expected: both sessions deliver the result with _meta intact.
Actual: Local delivers _meta; the agent host session delivers { content, isError } (plus structuredContent if present) with no _meta.

Evidence
For a single tool call, identified by a unique id in the payload, I captured both ends:

- On the wire (an HTTP proxy between VS Code and the MCP server): the server's response contains content, isError and _meta.
- In the workbench, immediately before the result is posted to the app (ChatMcpAppModel._sendToolResult): content and isError only, with _meta empty.

Where it's lost (source at the commit above)

The agent host path rebuilds the result from a reduced protocol type that has no field for the server's _meta:

- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts: the live ChatToolCallComplete.result copies content and structuredContent but not the MCP result's _meta. The nearby _meta: toToolCallMeta(...) is VS Code's own tool-call metadata, not the server's.
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts: the same omission when rebuilding from history.
- src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts: ToolCallResult has content and structuredContent, with no field for the raw MCP _meta.
- <blob>.ts: toMcpCallToolResult returns only content, structuredContent and isError.
- <blob>.ts: forwards resultDetails.mcpOutput unchanged, so the loss happens upstream.

For comparison, the Local path (<blob>.ts) sets details.mcpOutput = callResult, keeping _meta.

History

- #321016 ("Wire up MCP App support for agent-host sessions") deliberately built a minimal result, noting that the raw MCP result never passes through the agent host protocol.

- #340375 (for #340165) added structuredContent to that path, but not _meta.

Suggested fix
Carry the server's CallToolResult._meta through ToolCallResult (live and history) and include it in toMcpCallToolResult, so agent host sessions deliver the same result to the app as Local sessions.

Related: using structuredContent instead isn't a workaround
The MCP Apps spec presents structuredContent as data for the UI that isn't added to model context. VS Code's Local path, however, serializes structuredContent into the content the model sees (mcpLanguageModelToolContribution.ts). So apps that need to keep large viewer data out of model context have only _meta, which is why forwarding it matters. If that difference from the MCP Apps spec is unintended, it may deserve its own issue. See also #290063

title: Copilot working-set filename click uses a local file: URI for WSL files; diff button works — VS Code 1.144.0
body:
### Description

Environment

VS Code: 1.144.0

Client OS: Windows

Workspace: WSL, repository under /mnt/x/

Feature: GitHub Copilot Chat changed-files working set

Description

After Copilot modifies files, clicking a filename in its changed-files list sometimes fails with:

The editor could not be opened because the file was not found.

The file exists and opens normally through VS Code Explorer. The adjacent Show Changes in Diff Editor button also works correctly.

The displayed file path matches the actual WSL path.

Steps to reproduce

Open a repository under /mnt/x/ in a WSL-connected VS Code window.

Ask Copilot to modify an existing file.

Click the filename in Copilot’s changed-files working set.

When the error occurs, click the adjacent Show Changes in Diff Editor button for the same file.

The issue is intermittent; I have not identified the exact trigger.

Expected behavior

Clicking the filename opens the existing file in the WSL workspace.

Actual behavior

Clicking the filename produces “file was not found,” while opening it through Explorer or the diff button succeeds.

Debugging evidence

I set a breakpoint at chatSessionWorkingSet.ts:348 inside _openFile() and inspected the resource passed to openEditor.

The captured URI had these values (directory names anonymized):

scheme:  "file"
authority: ""
path:  "/mnt/x/Work/project/README.md"
query:  ""
fragment:  ""

_formatted:
file:///mnt/x/Work/project/README.md

fsPath:
\mnt\x\Work\project\README.md

The resource is a local file: URI with an empty authority, even though the file belongs to the WSL workspace. Its fsPath is consequently interpreted as a Windows path.

This appears to indicate missing WSL URI mapping in the working-set filename-opening flow. The breakpoint establishes the incorrect resource passed to the editor, but I have not determined where that resource originates.

Stack trace

ERR ya: The editor could not be opened because the file was not found.

Workaround

Use Show Changes in Diff Editor, or open the file through Explorer.

### Description With `"telemetry.telemetryLevel": "off"`, the built-in GitHub Copilot Chat extension still sends `GET about 20 seconds after VS Code starts and then every 15 minutes, apparently from the bundled Application Insights SDK's Azure VM detection (`AzureVirtualMachine`, 2500 ms timeout). Because VS Code routes extension traffic through the configured HTTP proxy, these link-local requests also go to the proxy, which cannot reach them and logs a failed request each time. title: Agent host tunnel gateway deadlocks when the client sends requests while a large response is being written ("Connection appears dead ... 25000ms")
body:
**Version:** observed with host tunnel CLI `code-insiders 1.142.0` (commit `e9eaf94e8bb`). The code paths below are unchanged in `1.145.0-insider` (commit `cd2259bdf72`), which still pins russh `vscode-russh@fd4f608` and dev-tunnels `b73b0eb`. Host: Linux (WSL). Client: VS Code Insiders Agents window on Windows over Remote Tunnel.

Related: #339997 (same symptom, different cause: frames over 16 MiB).

### Symptom

The Agents window frequently reports `Liveness: no data from tunnel:<id> for 25xxxms; forcing close to trigger reconnect.` Over one week the client logged 10 such stalls against one host. In 8 of 10, the last message received was a large JSON-RPC response (160 KB to 1.8 MB, an `ahp-chat` snapshot), followed by no bytes at all, including no pong. Responses over 150 KB end in silence about 100 times more often than small ones.

This is different from #339997: the gateway never logs `MessageTooLong`, and the payloads are well under 16 MiB.

### Host-side evidence

- The per-client forwarding stops in both directions at the same moment, while the relay connection stays healthy (the host's own relay liveness pings succeed during the stall).
- `window_adjusted` stops being logged for the client session at the moment of the stall.
- The stalled connections never get cleaned up. One hour and twelve hours after two stalls, the tunnel CLI still holds both loopback connections to the agent host, with 4.0 MB and 2.2 MB unread in the CLI's receive queue. All tokio worker threads are idle, so this is an async deadlock, not a blocked thread.

### Root cause

There is a cycle between the gateway proxy task and the russh server session loop for the client's forwarded channel:

1. `proxy_gateway_frames` ([cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs#L2268](<url>)) is a single `select!` loop. While it forwards a target frame with `client.send(m).await` ([L2300](<url>)), it does not poll `client.next()`.
2. `client` is a WebSocket over `ForwardedPortRW` ([control_server.rs#L304](<url>)). Its writer calls `russh::server::Handle::data`, which sends into the session loop's bounded queue (`event_buffer_size: 10`).
3. Inbound client data is delivered by the dev-tunnels server handler, which awaits a bounded `mpsc::channel(10)` inside the russh session loop ([relay_tunnel_host.rs#L894](<url>), [#L939](<url>)).

When more than 10 inbound packets arrive while the proxy writes a large frame, the session loop blocks in `Handler::data` waiting for the proxy to read. It then stops draining its handle queue, so the proxy's `Handle::data` never completes and the proxy never reads. The session loop also stops processing `WINDOW_ADJUST` and channel close, which explains the frozen window and the leaked connections.

The probability grows with response size (a longer write) multiplied by the client request rate. Opening a session does both: it returns large chat snapshots and the client sends a burst of `subscribe`, `resourceResolve` and `createResourceWatch` requests. That matches the observed correlation.

A longer liveness timeout would not help, because the deadlock is permanent.

### Suggested fixes

1. **CLI:** split `proxy_gateway_frames` into two independent directions (split the WebSocket streams and run client→target and target→client as separate tasks or futures), so reading from the client never waits on writing to the client. The same pattern should be checked in other tunnel forwarders.
2. **dev-tunnels:** avoid awaiting a bounded send inside the russh session loop in `Handler::data`. Use the SSH channel window for backpressure instead, so a slow consumer cannot stop window adjust and close processing for the whole session.
3. Add a regression test: through a forwarded channel, have the target send a multi-MB frame while the client concurrently sends more than 10 small frames, and assert that both complete.

title: "Reply immediately" after the agent has finished its reply cancels its running background subagents
body:
### Description

**Version:** VS Code 1.144.0 stable (2c33b50b16), Copilot CLI agent host (runtime 1.0.103-unstable), Windows 11.
**Models:** Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Opus 5.5, with the same result. The cancellation happens before the
message is sent to the model, so it does not depend on the model.

## Steps

1. Open a new chat with the Copilot harness. Send:
  ```
  Start a background agent with the task tool: agent_type "task", mode "background", prompt: "Run Start-Sleep -Seconds 600 in powershell, then reply: awake." Do not wait for it. Reply only with its agent_id.
  ```
2. Wait until the agent has replied with the id. Its turn is complete, but the chat still counts as busy
  while the background agent runs, so the send button offers Steer, Reply immediately and Queue.
  Send `Reply OK.` with **Reply immediately**.
3. Send: `Call list_agents and report each agent's status.`

**Actual:** the background agent is reported as `cancelled` after a few seconds; it never finishes its
sleep. Pressing Stop instead of step 2 has the same effect.

**Expected:** the background agent keeps running. The agent's turn was already complete, so there is
nothing to interrupt; at most, Reply immediately should interrupt the main agent's own turn, never its
background subagents. (Sending a message with Steer in step 2 does not cancel it; neither does a
follow-up message in the Copilot CLI terminal UI.)

Reproduced in 2 of 2 runs.

## Evidence (one run)

```
11:12:27.949  events.jsonl  assistant.message "a2b12bc0-…"  (the agent's turn is complete)
11:12:33.423  renderer.log  [AgentHost] Cancellation requested for ahp-session:/ff055d78-…, dispatching turnCancelled
11:12:33.427  agenthost.log  [Copilot:75e42905-…] Aborting session...
11:12:33.440  events.jsonl  abort {reason: user_initiated}
11:12:33.446  events.jsonl  subagent.completed sleeper, cancelled: true
```

The message itself is only sent afterwards. In the agent host, `abort()` completes the turns of all
active subagents and aborts the SDK session, which cancels the background agents for good: later
`read_agent` and `write_agent` calls return `Agent is cancelled` or `Agent not found`.

Related:
- github/copilot-cli#4555 (in ACP mode, every `session/prompt` aborts the session and its background
  agents).
- #342375 is different: there, steering only makes background agents look cancelled and they keep
  running. Here, the agents are actually aborted.

title: Codex extension stalling repeatedly
body:
### Environment

- Windows 11 x64, build 10.0.26300
- VS Code 1.144.0; also observed on 1.143.1
- OpenAI Codex extension: 26.1021.22027, win32-x64
- Intel Core Ultra 7 155U, 32 GB RAM
- Existing Arduino/PlatformIO workspace

### Problem

When reopening my workspace with Codex views open, Codex can remain stuck
on its loading screen in both the sidebar and editor panels. VS Code
becomes unresponsive and displays “The window is not responding.”

Reloading or reopening the window has not reliably resolved the problem.

### Steps associated with the failure

1. Open a workspace and use Codex in the sidebar and an editor panel.
2. Close VS Code with those editor tabs open.
3. Reopen the workspace and allow VS Code to restore the previous session.
4. Codex views may remain loading while the extension host repeatedly
  becomes unresponsive. The entire window can freeze.

The exact trigger is not yet isolated; the issue is intermittent.

### Expected behavior

VS Code should remain responsive while Codex initializes. Restoring Codex
panels should not cause a prolonged window freeze.

### Observed logs

The logs repeatedly report:

  Extension host (...) is unresponsive.
  CodeWindow: detected unresponsive

Codex reports:

  Webview renderer did not become ready
  reason=renderer_ready_timeout
  receivedWebviewMessage=false
  stage=renderer

Failures were recorded for both sidebar and editor-panel views.

Main-window unresponsive samples included MessagePort handlers and
file-decoration processing, including notifyFileDecorationsChanges.

### Investigation and workarounds

- The original Codex webview startup timeout was 30 seconds.
- For diagnosis, the installed extension was locally modified to increase
  that timeout to 120 seconds and log startup phases. This was not an
  official extension update.
- The problem recurred with that modification still intact: views timed
  out after approximately 121–123 seconds.
- A clean profile containing only Codex and Codex Audio also encountered
  the original 30-second webview timeout. The full-window freeze was
  observed in the normal workspace.
- Setting `"workbench.editor.restoreEditors": false` prevented editor-tab
  restoration. Two subsequent normal-profile restarts loaded Codex
  successfully without a Codex timeout or window-unresponsive event.
- Codex frontend route mounting still took approximately 30–42 seconds
  in those successful runs. Account lookup succeeded once the UI loaded.

Disabling editor restoration is a mitigation with a usability tradeoff,
not a confirmed fix. The underlying cause remains unconfirmed.

### Description **Environment:** VS Code 1.144.0 (x64), Windows, Copilot Chat agent mode. - Parent agent model: Claude Opus - Subagent model: GPT-5.6 Luna ## Steps 1. Create `.github/agents/luna-write-test.agent.md`: ```markdown --- name: Luna Write Test description: 'Test agent restricted to read, edit, and search tools.' tools: [read, edit, search] agents: [] model: GPT-5.6 Luna (copilot) user-invocable: false --- Perform the requested file operation, then report the tools you used and any errors verbatim. ``` 2. Run Developer: Reload Window. 3. With Claude Opus selected as the chat model, call the `Luna Write Test` subagent: "Create `tmp-luna-write-test.md` in the workspace root, append `Edit step - OK`, read it back." 4. Create `tmp-luna-write-test.md` yourself, then call the subagent again: "List the exact names of every tool available to you, then append `Edit step - OK` to `tmp-luna-write-test.md`." ## Expected `edit` gives the subagent the edit tools for its own model (Luna). The file is created (step 3) and edited (step 4). ## Actual - The subagent only has `view`, `rg`, `glob`, and `multi_tool_use.parallel`. - Step 3: the file isn't created. The read-back fails with `Path ...\tmp-luna-write-test.md does not exist.` - Step 4: the file is unchanged. The subagent reports that no edit/write tool is available. - `read` and `search` work. Only `edit` gives no tools. - The bug only happens when the parent and subagent models have different edit tool sets. title: Codex Agent Host on macOS: vscode-workspace blocks pinned pyenv runtime; need supported read-only path configuration
body:
### Description

Environment:
- macOS
- VS Code 1.144.0
- Built-in Codex Agent Host integration
- Effective permission profile: vscode-workspace
- Command network access disabled

A project-authorized launcher uses a pinned Python installation under:
~/.pyenv/versions/3.13.1

The command fails before the launcher starts:
libpython3.13.dylib: blocked by sandbox
Exit code: 134

Inspection of the installed Agent Host code indicates that the generated
vscode-workspace profile grants minimal system reads and workspace access,
but does not include this Python runtime.

The project guard permits the specific launcher inside the sandbox and
deliberately rejects permission escalation. We need the launcher to run
within the existing sandbox.

codex.additionalDirectories was inspected locally and appears to grant
write access, which exceeds the required read-only access.

Please provide the supported mechanism to grant read-only access to this
specific runtime for this workspace, preserving:
- the project hooks and guard;
- existing protected paths;
- disabled command network access;
- the restriction against runtime writes.

The grant must survive Agent Host startup, thread resume and subsequent turns.

No supported user setting for this grant has been established.

title: Source Control Graph: add an automatic current-branch-only mode
body:
Type: Feature Request

With the Source Control Graph filter set to Auto, newer commits from the base branch can appear above the checked-out branch's latest commit. This makes it look as though the wrong branch is selected or the current branch's commits are missing.

In the case investigated, the checked-out branch's latest commit appeared 20th, below 19 commits included from origin/master. Git and VS Code both correctly recognized the checked-out branch.

Please provide a persistent "Follow current branch only" option that:
- Automatically follows the checked-out branch when switching branches.
- Shows commits reachable from that branch, including its ancestors.
- Excludes commits from the base branch that are not reachable from the checked-out branch.

Selecting a specific branch manually narrows the graph, but does not provide the same automatic following behavior. A clearer explanation that Auto includes the base branch would also help prevent confusion.

The requested behavior should retain shared ancestral history; the concern is the additional base-branch commits outside the checked-out branch's history.

Codex could not start
The extension could not start its user interface.

The Codex user interface fails to initialize, making the extension completely unusable.

The issue began approximately one week ago, although Codex had been working correctly in my development environment before that.

I have attempted several troubleshooting procedures without obtaining a permanent solution.

First, I signed out of my Codex/OpenAI account and signed back in, but the problem remained unchanged.

Next, I updated Visual Studio Code and the Codex extension to their latest available versions. Unfortunately, this did not resolve the issue.

After these unsuccessful attempts, I downgraded the Codex extension to an older version released approximately three weeks earlier.

Interestingly, the older version initially worked correctly, and I was able to use Codex again.

However, I later received another update notification or request from Codex. Following this, the same startup error returned.

More importantly, the older extension version that had previously restored functionality has now also stopped working.

title: bug: TreeView selection becomes corrupted when children of parents of selected items change
body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes/No - VS Code Version: 1.144.0 (user setup) - OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26300
When a TreeView has multiple selected items, changing the children of a parent whose children are included in the selection corrupts the selection of children belonging to other parents. Also, when the selection becomes corrupted, it cannot be cleared normally: clicking elsewhere in the tree or pressing Esc does not clear the selection. The affected items can only be deselected by clicking them individually. Example tree structure: ``` Parent A Child A 1 Child A 2 Parent B Child B 1 Child B 2 ``` If the children of Parent A change while the selection includes children of both Parent A and Parent B, the selection of children belonging to Parent B becomes corrupted. title: Allow inlay hint providers to opt out of temporary truncation while typing
body:
## Problem

Inlay hints on the cursor line can be temporarily truncated to an ellipsis while typing, even with `editor.inlayHints.maximumLength` set to `0`. This makes inline deleted-text previews difficult to read during editing. In my case, the full text returns after editing pauses.

## Steps to reproduce

Observed with an extension that supplies deleted-text previews as inlay hints:

1. Enable inlay hints, set `"editor.inlayHints.maximumLength": 0`, and enable word wrap.
2. Open a document with a long line. Render multiple inlay hints containing deleted text on that line; update their labels as the document changes.
3. Type or delete text later on the same line, after the hints.
4. During editing, hints before the cursor can change from their full labels to shortened labels ending in `…`. They return to full length after the editor refreshes following a pause.

I observed this with Typst text and Chinese deletion labels. The screenshot contains private document text, so I have not attached it. I have not yet prepared a minimal standalone extension reproducer.

## Why this matters

This limitation is important for Word-style track changes: deleted text must remain visible in full while the user continues editing. Truncating it to an ellipsis hides the content being reviewed, so a user cannot reliably read the revision inline during editing. Inlay hints participate in word wrapping, but their temporary truncation makes this approach unsuitable for a complete track-changes experience. Alternatives such as decoration attachments do not participate in wrap-width calculation and can push line endings outside the viewport.

This request addresses the truncation part of the problem; a complete Word-style experience may also require additional APIs, including text styling.

## Expected

Provide a way for an inlay hint provider to opt out of temporary fixed-width truncation when complete labels are important. Reflow and cursor movement may be acceptable for these hints.

## Investigation

The current `InlayHintsController._updateHintsDecorators` appears to collect existing hint lengths before the cursor and apply `itemFixedLengths` to updated hints, replacing excess text with `…`. This is separate from the `editor.inlayHints.maximumLength` setting. The width lock appears intended to avoid cursor jumping; an opt-out would preserve that behavior by default.

### Possible solution

Allow providers to opt out of fixed-length rendering, for example via an `InlayHint` property. When opted out, skip the fixed-length constraint for that item; continue to apply `editor.inlayHints.maximumLength` independently. The default should retain existing behavior for compatibility.

As a local experiment, I patched the VS Code 1.141.0 workbench bundle to select certain hints by their tooltip and set their `itemFixedLength` to `undefined` before rendering:

```ts
// Conceptual equivalent of the local bundle patch, not a proposed API.
const itemFixedLength = isSelectedHint(item.hint) ? undefined : itemFixedLengths.get(item);
```

This bypasses both fixed-length truncation and fixed-length padding for the selected hints, while leaving other hints and the separate `maximumLength` handling unchanged. Tooltip matching is only a local workaround; an explicit provider opt-out would be preferable. The patch has passed code-level tests but has **not yet been verified interactively**. The observed issue occurred before patching.

## Environment

- VS Code 1.141.0, commit `2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c`, arm64
- macOS 27.0.1
- Inlay hints supplied through `InlayHintsProvider`

title: Chat view "New Chat" always opens a read-only Claude session when the Claude agent is disabled by org policy
body:
Environment
- VS Code 1.144.0 (macOS)
- GitHub Copilot Business; Claude agent disabled by account policy (Claude3PIntegration)
- Policy Diagnostics: no managed settings, chat harness enforcement "Not enforced"

Steps
1. Open the Chat view (secondary side bar)
2. Click "New Chat" (+)

Actual
- No chat input appears. The view only shows:
  "Your organization has disabled this agent. This conversation is read-only.
  Continue in Copilot to copy the conversation and keep the original."
- "Continue in Copilot" does nothing (the conversation appears empty).
- Same result with "New Chat Editor", a new window, and a new profile.
- Setting chat.editor.localAgent.enabled: true / chat.defaultToCopilotHarness: false did not help.

Expected
- New chats fall back to an allowed harness (Copilot/Local) with a working chat input.

Workaround
- Starting a session in the Agents window and opening it from the Chat view's
  session list works. New chats via "+" still fail.

title: Git extension can exhaust disk when sorting refs in a large partial clone
body:
## Reproduction

1. Open a large partial clone configured with `remote.origin.partialclonefilter=blob:none` and many refs (~17,000 in the reproduced repository):
  ```bash
  code /path/to/partial-clone
  ```
2. Leave the window open and monitor `.git/objects/pack`.

**Expected:** Opening the repository does not download large amounts of Git history.

**Actual:** The Git extension immediately runs:
```text
git for-each-ref --sort -committerdate --format %(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(*objectname)
```

Git then repeatedly performs lazy filtered fetches and creates ~40–50 MB promisor packs every 15–20 seconds. If the extension host exits, the Git process can remain orphaned and continue consuming disk. This exhausted approximately 150 GB during the observed incident.

**Workaround:** Set `\"git.branchSortOrder\": \"alphabetically\"`.

<details>
<summary>Environment and investigation details</summary>

- VS Code: 1.144.0 (`2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf`, arm64)
- macOS: 26.7.1 (25G241)
- Git: 2.56.0
- Repository: `blob:none` partial clone, 17,071 refs, including 16,129 remote refs
- Reproduced by launching VS Code while monitoring Git processes and pack creation
- The scan called `promisor_remote_get_direct` and repeatedly spawned:
  ```text
  git -c fetch.negotiationAlgorithm=noop fetch origin --no-tags --no-write-fetch-head --recurse-submodules=no --filter=blob:none --stdin
  ```
- Source path:
  - `extensions/git/src/repository.ts`: model refresh calls `getRefs({})`
  - `extensions/git/src/git.ts`: `getRefs` adds `--sort -committerdate`
  - `extensions/git/package.json`: `git.branchSortOrder` defaults to `committerdate`
- A clean reproduction created another promisor pack before the window and fetch process were stopped.

Potential mitigations include avoiding unrestricted commit-date sorting for large partial clones, bounding the queried refs, and ensuring child Git processes are cancelled when the extension host exits.

</details>

*🤖 Written by GitHub Copilot on behalf of @jruales.*

title: Expose an update-aware “Restart Extensions” command for programmatic VSIX updates
body:
## Current gap

VS Code [documents installing a VSIX programmatically](<url>), but there appears to be no exposed command to apply a pending extension update using the Extensions editor’s **Restart Extensions** operation. The generic `workbench.action.restartExtensionHost` command restarts the hosts without applying the updated extension version.

This leaves a self-updating extension unable to offer the equivalent restart action in its own notification without requiring navigation to the Extensions editor or a full window reload.

## Observed behavior

**Environment:** Windows, VS Code 1.144.0.

1. Start with version A of an extension running.
2. Install version B of the same extension using `workbench.extensions.installExtension`, passing the local VSIX URI, and await completion.
3. Execute `workbench.action.restartExtensionHost`.
4. The extension host restarts, but the extension activates with **version A**.
5. Open the extension’s page in the Extensions editor. Its **Restart Extensions** button is still present.
6. Click that button. The extension activates with **version B**.

The installation succeeded; the difference is which restart operation applies it.

## Source-level distinction

The two actions use different paths:

- [`RestartExtensionHostAction`](<url>) stops the extension hosts, then calls `startExtensionHosts()` without supplying extension replacements.
- [`ExtensionRuntimeStateAction`](<url>), used by the Extensions editor’s **Restart Extensions** button, calls `extensionsWorkbenchService.updateRunningExtensions()`.
- [`updateRunningExtensions()`](<url>) collects pending extension changes and starts the hosts with `{ toAdd, toRemove }`.

This appears to explain why the generic restart preserves the old version while the Extensions editor action applies the update.

## Requested enhancement

Expose a supported command equivalent to the Extensions editor’s **Restart Extensions** action, so extension-authored notifications can apply pending updates without reloading the entire window.

If preserving the existing running extension list is intentional for `workbench.action.restartExtensionHost`, please also document that distinction alongside the programmatic installation guidance.

A separate update-aware command would avoid changing the semantics of the existing developer command.

---

Drafted by copilot, reviewed before posting by me.

title: Claude harness can freeze during agent plugin synchronization
body:
## Bug

Selecting the Claude agent harness can freeze and crash the editor during agent plugin synchronization, before a prompt is sent.

Suspected triggering agent plugin: [Mobile Canvas (Redth/mobile-canvas-ghcp)](<url>). Disabling all agent plugins avoided the failure; this plugin has not been isolated in a single-plugin test.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Have an agent plugin whose cached directory contains large Git metadata.
2. Open Chat and select the Claude harness.
3. The editor may become unresponsive during plugin synchronization.

**Expected:** Plugin synchronization does not freeze or crash the editor.

**Actual:** The renderer can run out of JavaScript heap memory.

## Suspected Cause

The plugin copy path may include `.git` metadata and transfer large files through whole-file base64/JSON serialization. Excluding VCS metadata and bounding large resource transfers may prevent this. The exact triggering resource has not been confirmed.

## Workaround

Disabling agent plugins with `"chat.plugins.enabled": false` avoids the observed startup failure.

title: Editing the built-in "Ask" agent permanently breaks built-in agent resolution (Ask/Plan/Explore) for a profile, surviving extension reinstall and full app restart
body:
**Environment:**
- VS Code version: 1.144.0
- OS: macOS
- GitHub Copilot Chat extension (agent-host-copilotcli)

**Summary:**
Directly editing the built-in `Ask` agent's definition file (via the in-app "customize agent" flow, which writes to `~/Library/Application Support/Code/User/globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/ask-agent/Ask.agent.md`) corrupts built-in agent resolution for the "Agents" window/hub permanently. Even after the edited file's content is reverted to the exact shipped default, the Agents window's built-in agent list (Ask/Plan/Explore) stays broken — showing 0–2 of the 3 built-ins, with "Ask" appearing misclassified as a "User" agent instead of "Built-in." The misclassified entry cannot be removed via the UI's delete action.

**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Open the Agents window / Agent Customizations panel. Confirm Built-in shows Ask, Plan, Explore (3 agents).
2. Use the in-app flow to "customize" the built-in Ask agent (adds tool entries to its `tools:` array, e.g. from an MCP server like `azure-devops`). Save.
3. Revert the edit (or let it auto-revert) so the file's content is byte-identical to the original shipped default.
4. Reopen the Agent Customizations panel.

**Expected:** Built-in shows Ask, Plan, Explore again (3 agents), since the underlying `.agent.md` files are confirmed unmodified.

**Actual:** The panel shows an incomplete/incorrect list (e.g., Agents: 2, with Ask listed under "User" instead of "Built-in"; Plan and Explore missing entirely). The "Ask" entry's reported source path is the virtual built-in URI itself — `vscode-agent-host://local/agents/ask.agent.md?_ah=eyJzY2hlbWUiOiJjb3BpbG90LWJ1aWx0aW4ifQ` (base64-decodes to `{"scheme":"copilot-builtin"}`) — not a real editable file path, yet it's rendered/tracked as a deletable "User" item. Attempting to delete it from the User agents list does nothing (no error, no removal, no effect on subsequent panel loads).

**What I verified while investigating (confirms this is a backend state bug, not a display glitch):**
- The three built-in files in `globalStorage/github.copilot-chat/{ask,plan,explore}-agent/*.agent.md` are confirmed byte-identical to their pristine shipped defaults (verified via content diff and VS Code Local History).
- The standalone customization scanner (`customizationsDebug.log`) sometimes correctly finds all 4 agents (3 built-in + 1 user custom) and sometimes only finds 1–2, inconsistently, across repeated scans in the same window session — suggesting a race condition in built-in agent discovery that produces non-deterministic, and sometimes permanently cached, incomplete results.
- A specific per-"workspace" cache key, `chat.customModes.agent-host-copilotcli`, stored in `workspaceStorage/<hash for agent-sessions.code-workspace>/state.vscdb`, persistently holds only the broken subset of agents, with the "Ask" entry's `id`/`uri` correctly pointing at `copilot-builtin:/agents/ask.agent.md` / `vscode-agent-host://local/agents/ask.agent.md?...` (i.e., the backend *does* know it's a builtin resource) yet the UI still renders/treats it as User-sourced and non-deletable.
- Disabling/re-enabling the GitHub Copilot Chat extension did not fix it.
- A full quit (Cmd+Q, confirmed via `pgrep` that no VS Code processes remained) and relaunch did not fix it.
- Manually patching `chat.customModes.agent-host-copilotcli` in the SQLite `state.vscdb` (while VS Code was fully closed) to the correct 4-entry value was silently reverted back to the broken value the next time VS Code loaded the Agents window — i.e., VS Code actively recomputes this value on load and recomputes it incorrectly, rather than reading a stale cache.
- The issue is tied to the `agent-sessions.code-workspace` backing store specifically; the same built-in agents resolve correctly when accessed from an unrelated, never-touched project workspace in a separate window.

**Workaround used:** Copied the three built-in `.agent.md` files verbatim into `~/.copilot/agents/` so they register as user-level custom agents (discovery of user/local agents works correctly). This restores functional parity but loses "Built-in" classification and risks duplicate entries if/when the underlying bug is fixed.

**Impact:** Any user who uses the in-app "customize a built-in agent" feature on Ask (and likely Plan/Explore) risks permanently losing access to all three built-in agents in the Agents window for that profile, with no in-app recovery path (reload, restart, extension disable/re-enable, direct state edits, and the delete action all failed to resolve it).

Observed on October 29, 2026. A deterministic reproduction has not yet been established.

The agent has no WorkIQ tools and asks for the transcript to be pasted manually, even though WorkIQ is enabled and reaches `ready` in other sessions in the same window.

The session has access to the enabled WorkIQ connector, or exposes a session-specific failure explaining why it is unavailable.

- **15:54:09:** The captured model response lists 196 available tools, with no WorkIQ tools and no `tool_search` tool. The agent then asks for the transcript.

title: Agent Host chat: restored empty chat shows "Agent" in mode picker but first request is sent with the built-in Ask agent (read-only)
body:
### Description

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not tested

VS Code Version: 1.144.0 (commit 2c33b50b16c472efe58357d1d2a8a5414bc23fbf), stable
Copilot CLI runtime: 1.0.103
OS Version: Windows 11
Chat: Agent Host (Copilot CLI) sessions, model Copilot Fusion (auto), Interactive permissions
Steps to Reproduce
Open a folder workspace. In the Chat view, start a new Agent Host chat.
In the empty chat, switch the mode picker to Ask and leave it there; do not send anything.
Run Developer: Reload Window.
In the restored empty chat, observe the mode picker shows Agent. Do not touch it.
Send: create a file C:\Repos\askprobe.txt containing hi
Expected: The request runs in Agent mode (matching the picker) and creates the file.

Actual: The request runs as the built-in Ask agent and the model refuses because it only has read-only tools. Sending a second message in the same chat runs as Agent.

Evidence
Agent Host protocol log (chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled): the first client chat/turnStarted carries "agent":{"uri":"copilot-builtin:/agents/ask.agent.md"} while the picker shows Agent. Later turns in the same chat omit agent.
Copilot session events: subagent.selected {agentName:"vscode-ask"} is emitted at session start, before the first user.message.
Workspace storage chat.untitledInputState holds mode: {"id":"copilot-builtin:/agents/ask.agent.md","kind":"ask"}.
Debug renderer log: the restored untitled chat receives setting empty model state but no setChatMode2 to Ask. The picker remains Agent.
In normal use after updating to 1.144.0, 18 of 20 new chats started in Ask while the picker showed Agent. None did on the prior version; 0 of 29 in the preceding days.
Suspected cause
_syncFromModel calls setChatMode(e.mode.id, false) with the persisted Ask id. copilot-builtin:/agents/ask.agent.md is an Agent Host-provided agent that may not be registered yet for a new (deferred-backing) session. In that case setChatMode falls back to agent for the picker, while the input model state keeps mode=ask and is used to build turnStarted.agent. The picker and the sent request disagree.

A related symptom: after the user switches the agent mid-chat, persisted session metadata copilot.agent stays ask.agent.md, because _changeAgentOnce does not call _storeSessionAgentMetadata.

Workaround
In an empty chat, explicitly switch the picker to Agent before sending; it then persists Agent for new chats.

Run “Chat: Install Dictation Model from Local Package…” and select the Nemotron model package. 2. Observe the success notification: “Installed nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b version 3.” 3. Click the microphone in Copilot Chat. 4. Observe the download error below. 5. Reload the window or fully quit and reopen VS Code, then retry. The error persists. ### Actual Result “Could not download the nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b speech-to-text model, which can happen on networks that block the model registry. title: Keep idle sash gripper styling from restyling the whole workbench
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #341282

## Problem

Since sash grippers started hiding while the mouse is idle (#343441), two moments make Chromium recompute the style of every element in the window: the first mouse movement after 2 seconds without movement (the grippers appear), and 2 seconds after the mouse stops (they hide again). With a large chat open, each of these takes about 0.4 s, and the window does not respond in the meantime. This happens in every window with the default settings, not only in the Agents window.

Switching sessions in the Agents window runs into both: moving the mouse to the Sessions list shows the grippers, and they hide again while the next chat is still rendering. In a dev build, switching between two sessions with large responses took **2,739 ms on `main` and 1,903 ms with this change (−836 ms, −31%)**, median of 3 runs × 4 switches each. Switching is still slower than it should be, so this does not close #341282; the remaining costs are listed at the end.

## Root cause

`SashGrippersController` toggles the `sash-grippers-hidden` class on the workbench container ([sash.ts#L103-L110](<url>)). The rule for that class ([style.css#L69-L72](<url>)) sets `--sash-grip-opacity` and `--sash-grip-transition-duration` on `.monaco-workbench` itself. Custom properties are inherited, so every time the class changes, every element in the workbench gets a new computed style and Chromium has to recalculate all of them, even though only the sash grip dots read these properties.

In a trace of one session switch on `main`, these two toggles show up as the two largest style recalculations, each covering about 34,300 elements:

- **393 ms** when the mouse moves onto the session row. Chromium applies it while processing the click, before any of the switch code runs. A trace with style invalidation tracking attributes it to `showGrippers` removing the class from the workbench root.
- **400 ms** about 2 s after the mouse stopped, which matches the hide timer adding the class back while the incoming chat is being rendered. It runs inside whichever code reads layout next: `ChatBackgroundRenderer` reading `clientWidth` in one recording, the measurement script's visibility check in another. It is gone with this change.

## Fix

Set the two custom properties on the `.monaco-sash` elements inside a workbench with hidden grippers, instead of on the workbench element. The grip dots are `::after` pseudo-elements of the sashes, so they inherit the same values and fade exactly as before. When the class changes, Chromium now only restyles the sashes. The controller, the settings and the timing are unchanged, and no TypeScript changed.

The new unit test reads `--sash-grip-opacity` on a plain element inside the workbench while the grippers are hidden. On `main` it is `0` (inherited from the workbench); with this change it is empty, and the sash itself still gets `0`. Existing tests for gripper opacity, hover and drag feedback, fade durations, reduced motion and the Agents window sashes pass unchanged.

## Before / after

No recordings: the change is only a difference in timing, so it is documented with the measurements and profiles below rather than GIFs.

## How it was measured

- **Input:** a dev build of the Agents window with `VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1`, connected to the scripted mock agent host (`agentHostServerMain --enable-mock-agent`, added through `chat.remoteAgentHosts`). The host lists two completed sessions, each with one response of about 115 KB: 50 or 51 sections, each with a list, a 20-line TypeScript code block and a table. Two tiny sessions are the control. The window is signed out and its sign-in dialog is closed. Default settings, so `workbench.sash.autoHideGrippers` is on with a 2 s delay.
- **Builds:** one compiled build of `main` at `c8a3f81`. Because the change touches no TypeScript, the `main` runs used that build with `main`'s `style.css` copied into `out/`, and the runs for this change used this change's `style.css`. The two batches ran back to back on the same Windows machine.
- **Run:** open each large session once to warm up, then switch between them 4 times. 3 runs per build, each in a fresh window. Switch time is the time from the click on the session row until the incoming chat's request and response text are both visible.

| Switching between the two large sessions | `main` | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Median of the 3 per-run medians | **2,739 ms** | **1,903 ms** |
| Per-run medians | 2,878 / 2,739 / 2,731 ms | 2,018 / 1,842 / 1,903 ms |
| Every switch, run 1 | 2,833, 2,922, 3,628, 2,775 ms | 1,889, 2,147, 2,781, 1,878 ms |
| Every switch, run 2 | 2,668, 2,797, 2,681, 2,871 ms | 1,844, 2,887, 1,809, 1,840 ms |
| Every switch, run 3 | 2,766, 2,695, 2,669, 2,803 ms | 1,851, 1,954, 2,633, 1,842 ms |
| Tiny sessions (control), per-run medians | 206 / 203 / 181 ms | 375 / 205 / 184 ms |

An earlier batch on `main` before the change was made (same input, 3 runs) measured 2,792 / 2,714 / 2,687 ms. In each run with this change, one of the four switches still took 2.6 to 2.9 s; `main` also has an occasional slow switch (3,628 ms in run 1). That variation was not investigated here. The tiny-session control was slower in the first run with this change (375 ms) than in all other runs (181 to 206 ms); those switches have very little to restyle either way, so this is treated as noise.

**Profile of one switch**, recorded after the scenario runs in the same windows. Each recording starts after the previous switch has settled, with the mouse not moved for more than 2 seconds, and ends 0.8 s after the response is visible:

| Per switch | `main` | This change |
|---|---:|---:|
| Style recalculations covering the whole window (about 34,300 elements) | 2 (393 ms + 400 ms) | none |
| Total time in style recalculation (trace) | 1,752 ms | 961 ms |
| CPU profile, `(program)` self time, where the click's hit test does the style work (2 switches) | 650 / 887 ms | 216 / 218 ms |
| CPU profile, self time of the layout read that applied the hide toggle (2 switches) | 460 ms (measurement script) / 472 ms (`ChatBackgroundRenderer`) | 3.0 / 3.7 ms (measurement script; `ChatBackgroundRenderer` under 1 ms) |
| CPU profile, busy time (not idle) of the whole recording (2 switches) | 3,110 / 3,512 ms | 2,566 / 2,498 ms |

Time per switch in the CPU profile is higher than in the table above because the profiler adds overhead.

## What remains

With this change, the remaining time in one switch is mostly:

- About 450 ms of script to render the incoming chat: markdown, 50 code-block editors and tables.
- A 344 ms style recalculation plus 47 ms layout of the **outgoing** transcript. It is forced by `ChatListWidget.updateScrollDownButtonPosition`, reached from `ChatWidget.setTranscriptProgress` early in `ChatView.setChat`, before the previous transcript is released.
- About 370 ms of style and 120 ms of layout the first time the incoming chat is measured, forced by the code-block editors' first render.

These are separate changes.

## How to test

1. Open a window with a long chat (or the Agents window with a session that has a long response with code blocks and tables).
2. Keep the mouse still for more than 2 seconds, then move it. In **Developer: Toggle Developer Tools** > Performance, record this. On `main`, a "Recalculate style" covering the whole document appears at the first movement, and again 2 seconds after the mouse stops. With this change those recalculations only cover the sashes.
3. Check the grippers still behave the same, in the editor window with Modern UI and in the Agents window: the dots between parts fade out after 2 seconds idle and fade back in on mouse movement, hovering or dragging a sash still shows the full highlight, and with reduced motion they change without a fade.
4. In the Agents window, switch between two sessions with long responses and compare with `main`.

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| New test fails with `main`'s stylesheet | Built this change, copied `main`'s `style.css` into `out/`, then `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sash/test/browser/sash.test.ts` | ❌ as expected: 15 passing, 1 failing. The plain element inherits `--sash-grip-opacity: 0`. |
| Sash gripper and Agents window grid tests with this change | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/sash/test/browser/sash.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/sessionGridLayout.test.ts` | ✅ all 16 sash gripper tests pass, including the existing checks of gripper opacity, hover and drag feedback, fades and reduced motion, and the Agents window test "idle grippers recede across session, side-pane and panel sashes". 2 grid layout tests fail, and the same 2 fail with `main`'s stylesheet: they check pixel geometry that differs on this 125% scaled display (0.8 px instead of 1 px borders, 396 px instead of 397 px). |
| Type check | `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ passed |
| Formatting and lint | `node build/hygiene.ts <2 changed files>`, `npm run eslint -- <changed test file>`, `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/media/style.css` | ✅ passed. Stylelint only lists existing design-token suggestions for other lines in the file. |
| Switch timing | Measurement above, 3 runs per build | `main` 2,739 ms, this change 1,903 ms |

---
<sub>Found and fixed with automated exploratory testing. Draft until reviewed by a human.</sub>

title: Offer Compare when saving a notebook that changed on disk
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #344849

## Problem

When a notebook has unsaved changes and its file changes on disk (an agent, git, a script), saving shows "Failed to save 'analysis.ipynb': The content of the file is newer. Do you want to overwrite the file with your changes?" with only **Overwrite** and **Revert**. A dirty notebook never shows the change on disk, so the user cannot see what **Overwrite** throws away, and Overwrite looks like the right choice. Text files in the same situation get a **Compare** action that opens a diff of the file on disk against the editor.

## Root cause

Notebooks are backed by stored file working copies, and the stored file working copy builds its own save error notification. For a save conflict (`FILE_MODIFIED_SINCE`) it only adds Overwrite and Revert:
<url>

Text files go through `TextFileSaveErrorHandler`, which adds Compare and opens the disk side through a text content provider for the `conflictResolution` scheme:
<url>
<url>

That provider only produces text models, so it can't feed the notebook diff editor, which resolves both sides as notebooks through the file service.

## Fix

- The stored file working copy save conflict notification now offers **Compare**, **Overwrite**, and **Revert**. Compare opens a diff with the file as it is on disk on the left and the working copy on the right, titled "analysis.ipynb (in file) ↔ analysis.ipynb - Resolve save conflict". It uses the editor that shows the working copy (for notebooks, the notebook diff editor of the same notebook type), so the right side is the unsaved notebook.
- The disk side comes from a new readonly file system provider (`vscode-file-on-disk` scheme, `FileOnDiskFileSystemProvider`) that reads the resource through the file service. This follows the guidance on #194917 that comparisons for custom editors need a file system provider rather than a text content provider. The files contribution registers it, and Compare is only offered when it is registered.
- Text files have toolbar actions in their conflict diff to accept or revert. The notebook diff has none, so after Compare opens the diff, the conflict notification is shown again and Overwrite and Revert stay one click away. Overwrite, Revert, and the message are unchanged.

#282368 (draft) proposes a similar readonly provider to fix **Compare with Saved** for notebooks and custom editors. This PR doesn't depend on it and doesn't change Compare with Saved. If both move forward, they can share one provider.

### Other gaps found, not changed here

- A dirty notebook never shows that its file changed on disk. Dirty working copies are not reloaded, so the editor keeps the old cells with no indication until the save fails:
  <url>
  <url>
- An external edit that keeps the file the same size is not detected at all, so saving silently overwrites it. The dirty-write check compares an etag built from the old mtime and the new size, so it only reports a conflict when the size changed. This affects text files too:
  <url>
- With a screen reader active, or with `notebook.diff.enablePreview` turned off, notebooks don't use the notebook diff editor. From reading the editor resolver, Compare then falls back to a text diff of the notebook JSON, and the right side would be the file on disk rather than the unsaved notebook, so it would show no changes. I didn't verify this in the UI.

## Before / after

### Before

The notebook has an unsaved edit and a cell was added to the file on disk. Saving shows the conflict with only Overwrite and Revert.

![Before: the notebook save conflict notification offers only Overwrite and Revert](<url>)

### After

Same steps. The notification offers Compare, and Compare opens the notebook diff: the cell added on disk on the left (red, what Overwrite would discard) and the unsaved edit on the right. The notification stays available with Overwrite and Revert.

![After: Compare opens the notebook diff showing the cell added on disk and the unsaved edit](<url>)

## How to test

1. Open a `.ipynb` in a dev build and type into a cell so the notebook is dirty. Don't save.
2. From outside VS Code, add a cell to the file on disk (for example with a small script that appends to `cells` and rewrites the JSON).
3. Save the notebook. The error notification offers **Compare**, **Overwrite**, and **Revert**.
4. Select **Compare**. The notebook diff opens with the added cell on the left and your edit on the right. The notification is shown again, and **Overwrite** or **Revert** resolves the conflict.

<details><summary>Automated repro scenario</summary>

Save as `repro.cjs`, then run `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev repro.cjs` from the repo root
(fails on main, passes with this PR). The scenario runner disables notification toasts, so the scenario reads the notification in the Notifications Center.

```js
// Save conflict on a notebook: the notification should offer Compare, and Compare
// should open the notebook diff of the file on disk against the unsaved notebook.
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');
const fs = require('fs');

const workspacePath = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'nb-save-conflict-'));
const notebookPath = path.join(workspacePath, 'analysis.ipynb');

const ADDED_ON_DISK = 'added_on_disk = True';
const TYPED_IN_EDITOR = 'typed_in_editor = 1';

function cell(id, cellType, source) {
	return cellType === 'code'
		? { cell_type: 'code', execution_count: null, id, metadata: {}, outputs: [], source: [source] }
		: { cell_type: 'markdown', id, metadata: {}, source: [source] };
}

const notebook = {
	cells: [
		cell('c1', 'markdown', '# Sales analysis'),
		cell('c2', 'code', 'total = 40 + 2')
	],
	metadata: { language_info: { name: 'python' } },
	nbformat: 4,
	nbformat_minor: 5
};
fs.writeFileSync(notebookPath, JSON.stringify(notebook, null, 1) + '\n');

const CELL_ROWS = '.notebook-editor .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row';
// The scenario runner disables notification toasts, so read notifications in the Notifications Center.
const NOTIFICATION = '.notifications-center .notification-list-item';

async function conflictToast(context) {
	const { page, workbench } = context;
	if (!(await page.locator('.notifications-center').isVisible())) {
		await workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('notifications.showList');
	}
	const toast = page.locator(NOTIFICATION, { hasText: 'The content of the file is newer' }).first();
	await toast.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
	return toast;
}

async function toastButtons(toast) {
	return (await toast.locator('.monaco-button').allInnerTexts()).map(label => label.trim()).filter(Boolean);
}

module.exports = {
	id: 'notebook-save-conflict-compare',
	title: 'Notebook save conflict offers Compare with the file on disk',
	source: '<url>',
	workspacePath,
	stepPauseMs: 1500,
	userSettings: {
		'files.autoSave': 'off',
		'workbench.startupEditor': 'none',
		'workbench.editor.enablePreview': false,
		'notebook.experimental.enableNewDiffEditor': false,
		'workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibility': 'hidden',
		'chat.disableAIFeatures': true
	},
	steps: [
		{
  id: 'S1',
  title: 'Open a notebook with two cells',
  async run(context) {
  const { page, workbench } = context;
  await workbench.quickaccess.openFileQuickAccessAndWait(notebookPath, 'analysis.ipynb');
  await workbench.quickinput.selectQuickInputElement(0);
  await page.waitForFunction(selector => document.querySelectorAll(selector).length === 2, CELL_ROWS, { timeout: 60000 });
  await page.locator(CELL_ROWS).nth(1).locator('.view-lines').waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
  return 'The notebook editor shows the two cells from disk.';
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'S2',
  title: 'Edit a cell so the notebook has unsaved changes',
  async run(context) {
  const { page } = context;
  const codeCell = page.locator(CELL_ROWS).nth(1);
  await codeCell.locator('.view-lines').click();
  await page.keyboard.press('End');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await page.keyboard.type(TYPED_IN_EDITOR);
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await page.waitForSelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty', { timeout: 10000 });
  return `Typed "${TYPED_IN_EDITOR}"; the tab shows unsaved changes.`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'S3',
  title: 'Another tool adds a cell to the file on disk',
  async run(context) {
  const onDisk = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8'));
  onDisk.cells.push(cell('c3', 'code', ADDED_ON_DISK));
  fs.writeFileSync(notebookPath, JSON.stringify(onDisk, null, 1) + '\n');
  await context.page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  const rows = await context.page.locator(CELL_ROWS).count();
  return `The file on disk now has 3 cells; the dirty editor still shows ${rows}.`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'S4',
  title: 'Save: the conflict notification offers Compare',
  async run(context) {
  const { page } = context;
  await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.files.save');
  const toast = await conflictToast(context);
  const buttons = await toastButtons(toast);
  if (!buttons.includes('Compare')) {
  throw new Error(`The save conflict notification offers only [${buttons.join(', ')}], no Compare.`);
  }
  for (const expected of ['Overwrite', 'Revert']) {
  if (!buttons.includes(expected)) {
  throw new Error(`The save conflict notification lost ${expected}: [${buttons.join(', ')}].`);
  }
  }
  return `The notification offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'S5',
  title: 'Compare opens the notebook diff of the file on disk and the unsaved notebook',
  async run(context) {
  const { page } = context;
  const toast = await conflictToast(context);
  await toast.locator('.monaco-button', { hasText: 'Compare' }).first().click();
  const diff = page.locator('.notebook-text-diff-editor').first();
  await diff.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
  await page.waitForFunction(([added, typed]) => {
  const editor = document.querySelector('.notebook-text-diff-editor');
  const text = (editor?.textContent ?? '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ');
  return text.includes(added) && text.includes(typed);
  }, [ADDED_ON_DISK, TYPED_IN_EDITOR], { timeout: 20000 });
  const title = (await page.locator('.tabs-container .tab.active').first().innerText()).trim();
  return `The notebook diff editor "${title}" shows the cell added on disk and the unsaved edit.`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'S6',
  title: 'Overwrite and Revert stay available next to the diff',
  async run(context) {
  const { page } = context;
  const toast = await conflictToast(context);
  const buttons = await toastButtons(toast);
  if (!buttons.includes('Overwrite') || !buttons.includes('Revert')) {
  throw new Error(`After Compare the notification offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`);
  }
  const onDisk = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebookPath, 'utf8'));
  if (onDisk.cells.length !== 3) {
  throw new Error(`Compare changed the file on disk: it has ${onDisk.cells.length} cells.`);
  }
  return `The file on disk is untouched; the notification still offers [${buttons.join(', ')}].`;
  }
		}
	]
};
```

</details>

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Repro on `main` @ `c8a3f819b4a` | `node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js --dev repro.cjs` (3 runs) | ❌ fails 3/3 as expected: the save conflict notification offers only [Overwrite, Revert], no Compare |
| Repro with this PR | same (3 runs) | ✅ passes 3/3: the notification offers [Compare, Overwrite, Revert]; Compare opens the notebook diff "analysis.ipynb (in file) ↔ analysis.ipynb - Resolve save conflict" showing the cell added on disk and the unsaved edit; the file on disk keeps its 3 cells, and Overwrite and Revert are still offered |
| Unit tests | `scripts\test.bat --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts` | ✅ 37 passing, including the new save conflict Compare test and the new readonly provider test |
| Type check | `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ no errors |
| Lint | `npx eslint <changed files>` | ✅ no problems |
| Formatting | `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>` | ✅ passed |

title: Fix Remove Keybinding for the chat steer and queue Enter bindings
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #338834

## Problem

In the Keyboard Shortcuts editor, **Remove Keybinding** on the default <kbd>Enter</kbd> binding of **Chat: Steer with Message** or **Chat: Add to Queue** adds a removal rule to `keybindings.json`, but the binding stays active: pressing Enter in the chat input during a running request still steers or queues the message. A removal rule without a `when` clause does work, which is the only workaround today.

## Root cause

"Remove Keybinding" writes the default's `when`, serialized ([keybindingEditing.ts#L157](<url>)), and that string is parsed again when `keybindings.json` is read. `KeybindingResolver._isTargetedForRemoval` removes the default only if the default's `when` implies the rule's `when` ([keybindingResolver.ts#L91-L116](<url>)). `implies` compares OR terms and AND terms one by one and assumes both sides are normalized the same way ([contextkey.ts#L2115-L2177](<url>)).

They are not. The steer and queue Enter bindings combine nested ORs ([chatQueueActions.ts#L25-L47](<url>)) with the action precondition ([actions.ts#L770](<url>)). `ContextKeyAndExpr._normalizeArr` distributes each OR over its neighbouring term. Some of the resulting branches are contradictions such as `chatEditingSentRequest == 'st' && chatEditingSentRequest != 'st'`, which become `false`, so the OR collapses into a single AND. That AND is pushed back into the outer AND as one term instead of being flattened ([contextkey.ts#L1715-L1741](<url>)). The default `when` then holds terms like `chatInputHasText && inChatInput && … && (chatEditingSentRequest == 'st' && chatEditingSentRequest != 's')`. The serialized string has no parentheses, so the parsed rule is flat, `implies` finds different OR terms, and the default is kept.

Making ANDs flat exposes two related gaps in the same loop, so this PR fixes them too:

- The loop distributes an OR only when it is the last term after sorting, but `in`, `not in` and comparison terms (`>`, `<=`, …) sort after ORs. `ContextKeyExpr.and(a || b, c > 1)` stays undistributed and serializes as `a || b && c > 1`, which parses to a different expression. On `main`, the nested AND sometimes hid such terms and let the OR be distributed. With flat ANDs it no longer does, so the loop now picks the last OR wherever it sorts.
- When every branch of a distributed OR is `false`, the result was kept as `false && …` instead of `false`.

Distributed ORs started collapsing like this when #163841 (85f62d7aca6, 2022) made `A && !A` normalize to `false`; the loop that pushes the result back without flattening is older.

## Fix

`ContextKeyAndExpr._normalizeArr` now:

1. distributes the last OR term wherever it sorts, not only when it is the last term;
2. returns `false` as soon as a distributed OR collapses to `false`;
3. flattens an AND left behind by a collapsed OR into the outer AND and drops duplicate terms.

Every AND it produces is flat, so the default `when` equals the rule parsed from its own serialization, and `KeybindingResolver` needs no change.

`serialize()` output is persisted in user `keybindings.json`, so I checked what changes. It only changes for expressions that, on `main`, held a nested AND, an undistributed OR before an `in` or comparison term, or a `false && …` AND. For the first two, the old string never parsed back to the same expression, so removal rules generated from them never matched. A `false && …` AND already parsed back to `false`. All other expressions serialize exactly as before (see the randomized check below).

Not changed: #337659 (1.140) added `!chatInputBlocked` to both preconditions. Removal rules saved before 1.140, including the two in the issue, describe the old defaults, so they still won't match the new ones. Removing the binding again from the Keyboard Shortcuts editor writes a rule that works. Making old rules follow later changes to a default `when` is out of scope here.

## Before / after

No recordings; the effect was checked by hand in a Code OSS dev build of this branch, signed in, with the default `"chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction": "steer"`:

- In Keyboard Shortcuts, **Remove Keybinding** on the Enter row of `workbench.action.chat.steerWithMessage` removed the row; only the Alt+Enter row was left. On `main`, the removal rule is ignored and the Enter binding stays in effect (unit test below).
- While a chat request was running (Stop button shown), typing a message and pressing Enter added a new line to the input and sent nothing.
- After deleting the removal rule from `keybindings.json`, pressing Enter in the same running request sent the message as steering again.

## How to test

1. In a dev build, open **Preferences: Open Keyboard Shortcuts** and search for `workbench.action.chat.steerWithMessage`.
2. Right-click the row bound to <kbd>Enter</kbd> and choose **Remove Keybinding**. The Enter row disappears. On `main` it stays, and the `-workbench.action.chat.steerWithMessage` rule is ignored.
3. Start a long chat request, type a message in the chat input, and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The message is no longer sent as steering.
4. Repeat with `workbench.action.chat.queueMessage` and `"chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction": "queue"`.

## Validation

|-------|---------|--------|
| New tests on `main` @ `c8a3f81` | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/platform/contextkey/test/common/contextkey.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/keybinding/test/common/keybindingResolver.test.ts --grep 338834` | ❌ fails as expected: both Enter defaults survive their removal rules, and the collapsed AND serializes as `a && a && b && c` and does not equal its parsed form. The `in` and comparison test was added later; with `main`'s `contextkey.ts`, its three expressions serialize as `a \|\| b && c > 1`, `a \|\| b && c in 'd'` and `false && a` instead of the expected values |
| Same tests with this PR | same | ✅ pass |
| Context key, parser, keybinding resolver, keybinding editing and Keyboard Shortcuts model suites | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/platform/contextkey/test/common/contextkey.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/contextkey/test/common/parser.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/contextkey/test/browser/contextkey.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/keybinding/test/common/keybindingResolver.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts` | ✅ 181 passing |
| Wider unit tests: all of `vs/platform`, `vs/workbench/services` and `vs/sessions`, plus the preferences, keybindings, canvases and multi-diff editor contributions and the chat tests that serialize context keys | `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "{vs/platform/**/test/**/*.test.js,vs/workbench/services/**/test/**/*.test.js,vs/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js,…}"` | ✅ no new failures: 34,491 passing, 204 pending. 64 layout tests fail on this machine, which runs at 125% display scaling (for example a 1px border measures 0.8px). The same 64 tests fail with `main`'s `contextkey.ts` |
| Chat queue and steer action tests | `scripts\test.bat --run <blob>.test.ts` | ✅ 10 passing |
| Randomized normalization check (scratch script, not committed) | 24,000 random expressions over 4 keys built from `has`, `!`, `==`, `!=` and `>` terms with AND, OR and NOT up to 3 levels deep, built once with `main`'s `contextkey.ts` and once with this PR's, and evaluated on all 625 combinations of the values `0`, `1`, `2`, `'1'` and `'2'` for the 4 keys | ✅ The two builds evaluate identically for every expression. Fixes #339698.

An unavailable GitHub reference could announce its URL in the References list, then repeat the same URL in a details dialog with no additional information.

title: sessions: expand the Pinned section when the first session is pinned
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Found by an automated Agents window QA run.

Related: <url> That issue is about the Pinned section missing until reload, which is a different symptom. This PR does not claim to fix it.

## Repro

1. Have no pinned sessions and at least one session in the Agents window sessions list.
2. Right-click a session row and choose **Pin**.

**Expected:** an expanded **Pinned** group appears, showing the session.
**Actual:** a collapsed **Pinned** header appears at the top, and the session you just pinned is hidden until you expand it.

## Root cause

<url> made the Pinned section default to `PreserveOrCollapsed` when there is no saved collapse state. At that time Pinned was always visible, even with no pins. Later, <url> hid Pinned while it is empty. Together, these mean the first pin always creates a new Pinned tree node with no saved state, so it renders collapsed and hides the session.

## Fix

`SessionsList` now handles `SessionListModelChangeKind.Pinned` changes from `ISessionsListModelService`. When a session becomes pinned and the user has **no saved collapse state** for `pinned`, it saves the section as expanded. Then the rerender shows the section open. A collapse the user chose (`pinned: true` in `sessionsListControl.sectionCollapseState`) is kept as is. Unpinning does nothing.

The test harness gets an opt-in `livePins` option, so `pinSession` updates pin state and fires change events like the real service. Existing `liveListModel` tests keep their current behavior.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/browser/sessionsList.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: **passed** (437 passing).
- New tests `first pin shows an expanded Pinned section` and `first pin keeps a user-collapsed Pinned section`: **passed**. With the production change reverted, the first test **failed** (`pinnedExpanded: 'false'`), as expected.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: **passed**.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: **passed**.
- **End to end:** Validated live on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 with Code OSS built from `809053d4c7a`. The build ran inside the desktop container, signed in as the GitHub test account. Before and after media are below.

### End-to-end: before and after

| Before (Insiders 1.145.0, `cd2259bd`) | After (Code OSS from `809053d4c7a`) |
| --- | --- |
| ![First pin: collapsed Pinned header, session hidden](<url>) | ![First pin: Pinned expanded, pinned session visible](<url>) |

After you collapse Pinned yourself, pinning a second session keeps it collapsed:

![Pinned stays collapsed after the user collapsed it and pinned another session](<url>)

Recording, before (Insiders): right-click a session, **Pin**, and the session disappears under a collapsed Pinned header.

<url>

Recording, after (Code OSS from this branch): right-click a session, **Pin**, and Pinned appears expanded with the session.

<url>

Not verified live: unpin and re-pin across a reload. The unit tests cover the saved-state logic.

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What and why

Keep missing engine input/output pairing IDs missing, rather than replacing them with an unrelated SDK model-call ID.

The restricted router previously fell back from `properties.modelCallId` to the top-level `model_call_id` for every target event. Engine snapshots mint their own input/output pairing UUID, so that fallback can manufacture an invalid correlation key. This change excludes `engine.messages` and `engine.messages.length` from the fallback.

For example, an engine snapshot with no pairing UUID and SDK ID `sdk-call-A` previously acquired `modelCallId: sdk-call-A`. It now remains unpaired instead of presenting that unrelated ID as an engine pairing key.

Related: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9195.

This is the narrow namespace-safety part of the continuation work, not the complete conversation-ownership solution. It does not add ownership emission or repair downstream ingestion, sharing, or curation.
