title: agentHost: Use the client's proxy and Kerberos tickets for WSL and local containers
body:
Related to #342540.

An Agent Host in WSL or a local Dev Container now uses the client's proxy configuration and falls back to the client's Kerberos tickets, the same way a remote extension host with `useHostProxy` does (`proxyResolver.ts`). This covers the Agents window's WSL and Dev Container connections and editor windows connected to WSL or Dev Containers.

## Changes

- **Which connections.** WSL always counts. A Dev Container counts only when the existing certificate-forwarding detection (#343431) finds a local Docker endpoint: `DOCKER_HOST`, then the active context, must be `unix://` or `npipe://`. The flag is renamed from `forwardClientCertificates` to `sharesClientNetwork`, since certificates, proxy and Kerberos now all depend on it. Editor-window remotes use the same `useHostProxy` gate as certificates.
- **Proxy resolution.** Such clients advertise `vscode.clientProxy` and serve `vscode/resolveProxy`. While one is connected, the Agent Host resolves proxies through it after `http.proxy` and the proxy environment variables. PAC and system proxies resolved on the client therefore apply to the Agent Host's own requests and to the Copilot runtime's `HTTPS_PROXY`. As for a remote extension host, `http.useLocalProxyConfiguration: false` turns this off.
- **Kerberos.** The Agent Host and the Copilot runtime use their own tickets first and fall back to `vscode/lookupProxyKerberosAuthorization`. The client answers through `IRequestService.lookupKerberosAuthorization`, which uses the platform's principal syntax (`HTTP@host` on macOS and Linux) and honors `http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal`. It only issues tickets for proxies it points the Agent Host at: its `http.proxy` setting, proxies it resolved for that Agent Host, or its system proxy for GitHub Copilot. With a principal override configured, tickets are only for that principal.
- **Copilot runtime.** The runtime's fallback uses the new SDK `kerberosAuth` option from github/copilot-agent-runtime#30203 (`mode: 'fallback'`, `scope: 'runtime'`). The option is declared locally and intersected with `CopilotClientOptions`. The currently pinned SDK compiles and ignores it, and an SDK release that includes the option registers the callback without code changes. The local declaration can be removed after that update.

Until VS Code moves to an SDK with the callback, everything above works except the Copilot runtime's own Kerberos fallback.

## How to test

1. On Windows, behind a proxy that requires Kerberos (Negotiate), open the Agents window and connect to a WSL distro without its own Kerberos tickets.
2. Start a Copilot session. The Agent Host log shows the proxy resolved through the client, and Agent Host requests through the proxy succeed with the Windows user's tickets.
3. Repeat with a Dev Container on local Docker Desktop, and with an editor window connected to WSL.
4. Set `http.useLocalProxyConfiguration` to `false`: the Agent Host no longer resolves proxies through the client.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed.

title: animations: allow WebKit's microsecond duration rounding in the confetti timing test
body:
Main CI [491287](<url>) failed on macOS ARM64 `Run unit tests (Browser, Webkit)` with `Animations › creates consecutive pixelated rainbow confetti animations`, where `allParticlesUseBalancedTiming` was `false`. The same commit passed in the previous main CI.

## Cause

`triggerConfettiAnimation` computes each keyframe offset as `time / duration`, using the full-precision random duration (for example `1490.6732…`). The test multiplies the offset step by `effect.getTiming().duration` and requires the result to be `<= 40 + 1e-10`. **WebKit reports that duration rounded to whole microseconds** (`1490.673`). Whenever the rounding goes up, each 40 ms step reads as up to about `1e-5` ms longer, which fails the `1e-10` tolerance. The duration is random, so the test fails about half the time on WebKit. Chromium and Electron report the exact value.

I confirmed this in local WebKit with a temporary probe over 40 animations. Every failing case had `d` with exactly 3 decimals and `maxGap − 40` between `5e-6` and `1.3e-5`, while easing, keyframe counts and duration bounds were all fine.

## Change (test only)

The tolerance goes from `1e-10` to `1e-3` ms, which covers microsecond rounding, and a comment says why. That's still 4 orders of magnitude tighter than anything visible, so the test still checks that the steps are 40 ms. The product is unchanged.

## Validation (local, `--run animations.test.ts`)

- **Before**, WebKit: 5 of 10 runs failed.
- **After:**
  - WebKit: 0 of 20 runs failed.
  - Chromium: 0 of 20 runs failed.
  - Electron: 9 passing.
- eslint is clean.

> Authored with Copilot

title: chat: reduce cloud sandbox discovery load on the task list
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What this changes

Part of #345234. Fixes problems 1, 2, 3 and 5 described there; problem 4 (re-reading every sandbox task on reload) stays open as a follow-up.

VS Code's cloud sandbox feature asks the Copilot API for your task list so it knows which cloud sessions to show. Today it asks far more often than it needs to, every open window asks the same way at the same time, and a single bad moment at startup can leave a window on the expensive path for good. This PR changes *when* and *how* the client asks, one change per commit, so the service sees a fraction of the traffic and users don't notice a difference.

## Problems and fixes

Numbered as in #345234.

### 1. It turned pages the wrong way

**Problem.** Long task lists come back in pages, and the server says where the next page is. VS Code ignored that and guessed: "page 2, now page 3…". If the server ever stopped treating those numbers as page numbers, VS Code would ask for the same page over and over until the scan was cancelled.

**Fix** (`1c1305ea120`, `cloudSandboxApiService.ts`). Follow the server's `Link: rel="next"` header, using the parser the rest of VS Code's GitHub integration already uses. Only the query part of the link is adopted, so requests stay on the same API host and keep the filters a link might leave out. A repeated, foreign, or unreadable link ends that scan and reports it as incomplete (keeping the sessions we already had) instead of looping or quietly pretending it finished.

### 2. It asked "anything new?" every minute, even while it was being told

**Problem.** VS Code learns about changed sessions two ways: a live push connection (the server tells us) or asking on a timer. It asked on the timer regardless — every 5 minutes with the push connection, every 60 seconds without it. Each ask is really four requests (repo vs. no repo, archived vs. not), more if the list spans pages, and every open window asked on the same minute, so the server saw the load in bursts.

**Fix** (`61e80da2e98` and `c42273c66ba`, `cloudSandboxSessionContribution.ts`). Don't poll at all while the push connection is working — it already reports changes, and reconnecting after a gap catches up anything missed. The timer keeps running so polling resumes within one interval if the connection drops. Without a push connection, poll every 5 minutes, with each window adding up to a minute of random delay (measured from its own last pass) so windows spread out. If polls keep failing, back off up to 15 minutes. Switching back to VS Code or changing the selected host still refreshes right away if the list is stale.

### 3. Accounts with no sandboxes were polled just as hard

**Problem.** If you have never created a sandbox, there is nothing for those requests to find — but they ran at the same rate anyway.

**Fix** (`0dd73e6dd62` and `0f8bb05e241`, same file). Accounts with no known sandbox only check every 15 minutes. The first sandbox to appear — created here, found by a scan, or announced by the push connection — brings back the 5-minute rhythm, and the timer is re-armed immediately so a changed interval takes effect on the next tick rather than one interval late.

### 5. One bad moment knocked a window off the push connection for good

**Problem.** Setting up the push connection takes one request. If that request failed for any reason other than "not available for this account" — a momentary server error, a network blip, a timeout — VS Code gave up on it for the rest of the window's life and polled instead. A failed renewal of a working connection did the same. A local window log showed exactly this: one transient error at startup, then polling until the next reload. Nothing in telemetry showed it either.

**Fix** (`633e294aa8d`, `cloudSandboxSessionFeed.ts` and `cloudSandboxTelemetry.ts`). Keep trying, slowly. Only "not available for this account" or a corrupt message from the server stops attempts for good. Anything else retries after about a minute, doubling each time up to 30 minutes, with a random spread so windows don't retry together, and never sooner than the server's `Retry-After` if it sends one. Polling continues until the connection is back, then stops again. A connection that drops after it was working keeps its existing, faster reconnect. A new `cloudSandboxSessionFeed` telemetry event records each connection, failure, retry delay and give-up, so we can see how many windows are on the push connection versus polling.

## What changes for users

- **With a working push connection:** nothing visible. Changes still arrive as they happen; background list requests go from 4 every 5 minutes to **0**.
- **Without one:** a sandbox created from another client shows up within about 5–6 minutes instead of 1–2, or within about 15 minutes if the account had no sandboxes before. Background requests go from 4 per minute to 4 per 5 minutes (or 4 per 15 minutes).
- **After a transient error at startup:** the window gets back on the push connection within the backoff instead of polling until reload.
- Sessions created in the window, manual refresh, and push notifications behave as before.

Supersedes #344841, which also rewrote the shared `Link` parser; that part is dropped here in favor of the unchanged platform parser.

## How to check

Count `GET /agents/tasks*` requests from one focused window (Output → Telemetry channel, or a local proxy):

| Situation | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Push connection working, window in the background | 4 requests every 5 min | 0 |
| No push connection, account has sandboxes | 4 requests every minute | 4 every 5 min, plus up to 1 min random delay |
| No push connection, account has no sandboxes | 4 requests every minute | 4 every 15 min |
| Push connection setup fails once (transient server error) | polling for the rest of the window's life | retries after ~1 min, doubling to 30 min; back on the push connection as soon as one succeeds |

Whether a window is on the push connection or polling is visible in the `[CloudSandboxSessionFeed]` lines of the window log and in the `cloudSandboxSessionFeed` telemetry event (`outcome` is `connected`, `unavailable`, `negotiationFailed`, `socketFailed`, `disconnected`, or `invalidMessage`, with the consecutive failure count and the next retry delay).

## Validation

macOS, Node.js 24.22.1, after `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`:

- `npm run test-browser-no-install -- --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --browser chromium --reporter dot` — passed, **830 tests**. These cover the page-following rules (repeated, foreign and unreadable links), the poll gating, jitter, backoff and idle intervals, and the feed retry pacing, `Retry-After` handling and telemetry, all with virtual time.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>` — passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.

Not run: verification against the live service. The exact `Link` format the service emits for the next page was not inspected, which is why the client adopts whatever query the server advertises rather than assuming a parameter name.

title: sessions: search the Sessions list for every word, in any order
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Searching the Agents window Sessions list used the tree's fuzzy find. It matched any letters in typed order (`hlow` matched "hello world"), searched only titles, pull request numbers and section labels, and left matches hidden inside collapsed sections such as Pinned and Archived. This makes the list own its search, so that results are predictable and explain themselves.

## Before / after

<!-- Drop the before/after video here -->


<url>


## What changes

- **Matching:** every word of the query must appear, in any order, ignoring case and accents. `hlow` no longer matches "hello world", and `macos terminal` finds "Fix flaky terminal tests on macOS".
- **What is searched:** title, nested chat titles, folder or repository, custom group or comparison name, branch, pull request number and title, and remote host. A section header no longer matches on its own; its sessions match through their folder or group, so searching a folder name shows that folder's sessions instead of an empty header.
- **Nested chats** show under their session only when their own title contains a word.
- **Collapsed sections:** a search expands Pinned, Archived/Done, Older and collapsed sessions to show its results without persisting that. Closing the search restores the previous collapse state.
- **Why a row matched:** words are highlighted in titles and chat titles. When a session matched only through a branch, pull request or host that its row doesn't show, the row's details line shows that field with the words highlighted, and its ARIA label says "matches branch …".
- **Accessibility:** the result count is announced politely ("3 sessions found"), and "No sessions found" shows under the input.
- **Telemetry:** a new `agents/sessionsListSearch` event reports word count, result count, results matched beyond their title, query changes, opens and duration per search. The query text is not collected.

## Implementation notes

- The tree's built-in find (`FindFilter`/`FindController`) only supports fuzzy or contiguous matching of row labels. The list now turns it off and uses `SessionsListFindController`, built on the base `AbstractFindController` (same input, history, close button and messages), with a list-owned tree filter. Nothing changes in `vs/base`.
- Turning off the built-in find also turns off `list.find` and `list.closeFind` for this tree, so `sessionsViewPane.find` now has their keybindings (Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+F or F3), and a new `sessionsViewPane.closeFind` handles Escape in the list (`sessionsListSearchOpen` context key).
- Agent names (Copilot, Claude, Codex) and "This Computer"/"Cloud" are deliberately not searched: they would match most sessions, and the Filter menu already covers them.
- `SESSIONS_LIST.md`: updated the one sentence describing find, which said it matches section labels.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open the search from the Sessions header (or press Cmd/Ctrl+Alt+F or F3 in the list).
2. Type a few scattered letters, e.g. `hlow`: unrelated sessions no longer match.
3. Type two words of a title in a different order: the session is found.
4. Type a folder name: its sessions show, not an empty header.
5. Type a word from a pinned or archived session: the section opens. Close the search: it collapses again, also after a reload.
6. Type part of a branch name or pull request title: the row shows the branch or pull request with the word highlighted.
7. Press Escape in the list: the search closes.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/contrib/sessions/test/**/*.test.js"`: 1132 passing, including the new `sessionsListSearch.test.ts` and the new `search` suite in `sessionsList.test.ts`

- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed
- `@vscode/telemetry-extractor` on `src/vs/sessions/contrib/sessions/browser/views`: `agents/sessionsListSearch` resolves with owner `alexdima` and all six fields as `SystemMetaData` measurements

There is no tracking issue; this comes from an audit of the Sessions list search.

title: chat: don't start new chats with a harness disabled by policy
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

When org policy disables the Claude agent (`Claude3PIntegration`, e.g. via the account's preview-features setting), users who had previously chosen Claude could not start a usable chat. Chat view **New Chat** (+), **New Chat Editor**, a new window and the restored Chat view all opened an empty Claude chat that only showed:

> Your organization has disabled this agent. This conversation is read-only. Continue in Copilot to copy the conversation and keep the original.

There was no chat input, and **Continue in Copilot** did nothing because the conversation was empty.

The new-chat harness resolver treated every Agent Host session type as usable when the Agent Host was enabled. A remembered (`chat.userSelectedSessionType`), current or explicit Claude/Codex type therefore kept winning even after policy disabled that provider. The resulting chat was immediately marked read-only.

## Fix

- `isNewChatSessionTypeUsable` now treats a local Agent Host provider that policy disables (Claude or Codex) as unusable, so remembered and current choices fall back to the regular default (Local or Copilot).
- An explicit request for a policy-disabled harness falls through to the regular resolution instead of opening an unusable chat.
- The remembered choice is not cleared, so it applies again if the policy is lifted.
- Empty untitled drafts of a disabled harness, persisted before the fix, are replaced on restore in the Chat view and in chat editors. Saved Claude chats with history stay readable as before.
- Unsent prompts: the replacement chat gets the chat input's saved empty-chat draft. If the policy arrives while VS Code is open, the read-only draft is replaced with a Local chat that keeps the prompt. With several drafts across a restart, the replacement shows the most recently typed one (existing draft-memory behavior). No step waits on account policy or the network before you can type.

## How to test

1. Set the `Claude3PIntegration` policy to `false` (Linux: `/etc/vscode/policy.json`; macOS dev build: a `defaults` value for the product's `darwinBundleIdentifier`).
2. Have `chat.userSelectedSessionType` remembered as `agent-host-claude` (for example, Claude was picked before the policy applied).
3. Start VS Code, open the Chat view, click **New Chat** (+), and run **Chat: New Chat Editor**. Each should open a usable chat with an input, not the read-only banner.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

title: chat: render the model picker label once per model configuration burst
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Switching to an agent host session re-renders the model picker's label once for every model the session reports a configuration for. In a trace from an Insiders Agents window that's 23 to 45 renders per switch, and each one re-measures the label, forcing style and layout passes. This PR renders the label once per burst, and stops the input part from re-syncing its draft for models other than the selected one.

## Why it happens

Agent host sessions carry a model configuration report from the host, covering every model the session offers. When the chat input binds a session, `ChatInputPart` hands that report to its `ChatModelConfigurationStore` (`setSessionModelConfiguration`), which fires `onDidChange(modelId)` once per model. `notifyConversationChanged` also fires once for every model the store holds. Two listeners ignored which model changed:

- `ModelPickerWidget` called `_renderLabel()` for every event. Each render rebuilds the label, then measures the name (`_getNameMinimumWidth`) and the configuration readout (`_updateMinimumWidth`), which forces style and layout passes.
- `ChatInputPart` called `_syncInputStateToModel()` for every event, which writes the draft state and queues a toolbar relayout.

## Fix

- `ModelPickerWidget` coalesces the store's events with `Event.debounce(…, MicrotaskDelay)`, so a burst renders the label once, with the final configuration. The microtask runs before the next paint, so the outdated label is never shown. Every other trigger still renders synchronously.
- `ChatInputPart` syncs the draft only when the selected model's configuration changes. The draft holds only that model's configuration (see `getCurrentInputState`), and the `onDidSelectConfiguration` listener next to it already makes the same check. Both listeners move into `registerModelConfigurationListeners()`, like `registerChatSessionPickerListeners()`, so a test can drive them.

The toolbar still re-evaluates its overflow after the label changes: `ChatInputPickerResponsiveLayout` observes the toolbar's DOM and relays it out at the next animation frame, before paint. That also covers a model shown in place of the selected one (Fusion for a HydraFusion model), whose changes no longer go through the input part's sync.

## Measurements

### Trace from the real window

A performance trace of three session switches in an Insiders Agents window (`ea8056df`), symbolicated. Work triggered by the store's notifications, per click:

| | click 1 | click 2 | click 3 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| model picker label renders | 23 | 45 | 45 |
| CPU in those renders | 8.1 ms | 45.2 ms | 23.1 ms |
| input part re-syncs, and the relayouts they queue | 1.7 ms | 2.2 ms | 1.1 ms |

The picker was compact on clicks 1 and 3, so those renders only measured the readout. With this PR, each burst renders once.

### Benchmark

The real Agents window (Code OSS dev build, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 26.7), connected to the scripted mock agent host, switching between four sessions of 16 turns. To reproduce the burst, the mock offered 25 models and each session reported a configuration for them. That is a benchmark-only change, not part of this PR.

Per switch, from traces and CPU profiles (8 switches each):

| | `main` | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| forced style and layout passes in the model picker | 102 (25–26 renders), 10.1 ms | 3, 0.45 ms |
| all forced style and layout passes | 164 | 71 |
| `_renderLabel` CPU, profiled | 14.0 ms | 2.1 ms |
| `setSessionModelConfiguration` CPU including its listeners, profiled | 13.2 ms | 0.1 ms |

Timing, three interleaved rounds of 24 switches without profiling (72 switches each):

| | `main` median (p90) | this PR median (p90) | Δ median | Mann-Whitney p |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| event processing | 90.3 ms (117.2) | 85.0 ms (114.0) | −5.3 ms (−6%) | 0.002 |
| long animation frames | 104.9 ms (135.1) | 100.7 ms (131.9) | −4.2 ms (−4%) | 0.02 |

Click to paint isn't significantly different in the benchmark (p = 0.33; mean 152.8 → 150.3 ms). Its distribution has two modes, about 136 ms for the sessions without editors and 168 ms for those with the details pane, so its median flips between them. The mean for each of the four sessions is the same or lower. A render costs less in the benchmark's small window than in the real one, where the renders this removes took 8 to 45 ms per click.

The benchmark's screenshots after each switch match `main` pixel for pixel in the chat input. They differ only in a few small spots (the title bar, the chat header and the grip on the divider next to the session list), which also differ between two runs of `main`.

## Tests

- New `ModelPickerActionItem` test, *renders the label once for a burst of model configuration changes*. It reports a configuration change for three models at once. With this PR the label renders once, a microtask later, showing the final configuration ("Medium · 256K"). On `main` it renders three times.
- New `ChatInputPart` test, *syncs the draft only for configuration changes to the selected model*. On `main` the draft syncs for all three models.

Validation:
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/workbench/contrib/chat/test/**/*.test.js"`: 16,156 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js"`: 9,456 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client`: clean
- `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open two agent host sessions that use different models or model settings, for example a different thinking effort.
2. Switch between them.
3. The model picker should show each session's model and settings, as before.
4. Optionally, record a performance trace of a switch. `setSessionModelConfiguration` should no longer call `_renderLabel`; the label renders once, in the microtask that follows.

- Acquire Sessions-pane suppression only when Inbox is focused, not on unfocused restoration. Opt only Inbox into restoring focus lost to canvas detachment, without overriding another focused control.

- Keep quick-chat navigation preservation separate from explicit focus preservation. Only Inbox's embedded composer opts into preserving focus; ordinary automatic quick chats retain their original behavior.
- Reseed workspace and quick-chat drafts after background comparisons, without discarding the draft prematurely or replacing a newer user-selected draft.
- Prefer the full-session widget over Inbox's input-only widget only when routing question and confirmation controls; preserve default widget lookup for the submitting input's references and tool selections.

Failed/cancelled actions remain pending, and an older background action must not clear a newer selection.
- Update accessibility help and add regression coverage.
- Render multiple PRs as a quiet list; groups larger than three collapse behind a count disclosure. Move merged-card cleanup, Open Session, and Done actions into a wrapping bottom row, with long PR labels ellipsized and available through hover.
- Collapse evidence-pane PR and artifact/reference collections past three entries, without repeating PR artifacts already shown with their observed states. Preserve all sources in Accessible View and keep Agent interpretation directly visible above the disclosures.

title: Browser: Tighten remote canvas networking
body:
Follow-up to #345102 and #345149:
- Offer canvases on remote agent hosts only while browser remote proxying is enabled and the host can forward TCP; an unknown host, such as a disconnected one, keeps its canvases.
- Require an embedded view's owner network whenever an owner is given, instead of a separate flag.
- Remove the WebSocket upgrade handler from the tunnel proxy: Chromium always tunnels WebSockets, including ws://, through CONNECT.
- Replace the extension test commands with unit coverage for failing closed, gating, and large and WebSocket traffic over agent host streams.

## Summary

Fixes #345200.

Fixes the reported no-op when choosing **Work in Repository** after selecting a GitHub Environment in the Agents window.

- Route repository cloning through the selected remote provider using the host's advertised project-management capability and existing repository-preparation helper.
- Wait for a ready checkout, reuse existing host projects, and select the returned directory on the correct remote host.
- Show cancellable progress and actionable errors for unsupported hosts or clone failures. Cancellation and superseded selections retain the current workspace; cancelling the client wait does not delete or cancel the host's checkout.

title: sessions: offer Open Pull Request Changes for GitHub pull request references
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

GitHub pull requests that an agent records as **references** stay in the References pill, and their rows only offered **Copy Pull Request Link**. Pull requests recorded as **artifacts** go to the Pull Requests pill, where each row also has **Open Pull Request Changes** to open the PR's changed files in a multi-file diff editor.

This PR gives referenced pull requests the same action:

- `createOpenPullRequestChangesAction` is a new shared helper in `sessionArtifacts.ts`. Both the Pull Requests pill and recorded PR rows use it, so the label, icon, hover label ("Open Changes"), and action id stay the same in both places.
- Recorded PR rows get the action when their link is a canonical `github.com` pull request URL, which is the same rule `parseGitHubArtifactLink` uses to promote PR artifacts. Enterprise-host PRs and issues are unchanged.
- `ISessionArtifactActions` has a new `openPullRequestChanges` member. `SessionArtifacts` implements it the same way as the Pull Requests pill: it activates the row's session, then runs `OPEN_PULL_REQUEST_CHANGES_ACTION_ID` with the pull request ref.
- Integration decoration keeps a row's toolbar actions, so integrated references keep the new action too.
- The accessibility help now says the row action is also available for pull requests in the References pill.

## How to test

1. In an Agents window session, have the agent record a GitHub PR with `add_artifact_or_reference` and `isArtifact: false`.
2. Open the References pill. The PR row now shows **Open Pull Request Changes** (diff icon) before **Copy Pull Request Link**.
3. Run it. The PR's changes open in the multi-file diff editor, the same as from the Pull Requests pill.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionArtifacts.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: passed (200 tests, including the new test `offers Open Pull Request Changes for GitHub pull request references, like the pull requests pill`)

title: editor: improve minimap search highlight visibility
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #319262

## Summary

- Make minimap search markers follow the overview ruler's search colour at a consistent 80% opacity, instead of inheriting faint inline editor fills. The existing full-line renderer then paints their backing at 40% opacity, rather than approximately 17% in Dark Modern or 5% in Light 2026.
- Restore high-contrast search markers using the editor's match-border colour. Explicit minimap customizations, including translucent and transparent colours, still take precedence.
- Add an absolute-opacity colour transform and regression coverage. Other minimap markers, inline editor highlights and search/navigation behaviour are unchanged.

## Issues addressed

| Severity | Issue | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| Medium | Full-line minimap search markers became difficult to distinguish after inheriting translucent editor search fills. | Reuse the theme-aware overview ruler hue with a dedicated minimap opacity. |
| Medium | High-contrast default markers disappeared because the inherited editor fill is unset. | Derive their colour from the editor match border instead. |

## Validation

Validated in isolated checkouts without unrelated local edits. Successful build/type-check validation was reused while its relevant client inputs remained unchanged; focused tests and current ESLint rules were rerun before publication.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast` | Passed: complete client, built-in extensions and Copilot build. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast -- --client-only` | Passed: fresh incremental output for the final test selection. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/theme/test/common/colorUtils.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/theme/test/common/chartsColors.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/themes/test/common/colorThemeData.test.ts` | Passed: 17 tests. All three added bundled-theme regressions failed before the production fix. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run typecheck-client` | Passed. |
| `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/theme/common/colorUtils.ts src/vs/platform/theme/common/colors/minimapColors.ts src/vs/platform/theme/test/common/colorUtils.test.ts <blob>.test.ts` | Passed. |
| `git diff --cached --check` | Passed. |
| `gh pr checks 345195 --repo microsoft/vscode` | 41 passed, 13 skipped, no failures. One pending check: **VS Code PR Check**, awaiting one collaborator approval (0/1). |

Native Code OSS validation exercised Dark Modern, Dark 2026, Light 2026, High Contrast Dark and High Contrast Light. Each retained 96 search matches and rendered 18,810 full-line canvas pixels at the expected hue/opacity. Tests also cover theme references, nested transforms, missing colours, alpha bounds, and explicit minimap colour overrides.

To test manually: enable the minimap, use Find on a file with repeated matches, and inspect its full-line markers in normal and high-contrast themes. Customize `minimap.findMatchHighlight` to verify explicit overrides are retained.

## Visual evidence

### Dark Modern and Light 2026

Single combined image: before on the left, after on the right, with one row per theme. The baseline runs unmodified main in a separate detached worktree. Both builds use identical text in Plain Text mode to isolate minimap rendering from syntax providers, the first of 96 matches, a 1200x800 CSS viewport and DPR 2. Source text, fonts, geometry and controls match; the captured crops have zero changed pixels outside the minimap. Captures are colour-normalized to sRGB. The hosted upload was verified pixel-identical to the final image.

![Minimap search markers before and after in Dark Modern and Light 2026](<url>)

## Review status

- Unresolved actionable findings: None in the final local review.
- Residual risks: Third-party themes were not exercised end-to-end; custom colour precedence is covered by tests. The visual attachment is verified and all build/test checks passed. The remaining merge-policy check requires one collaborator approval (0/1); it is not a code or test failure.

title: copilot: remove workspace-snapshot simulation support and the Log Workbench State command
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #345173.

That PR removed the simulator's external chat scenarios, which were the only source of workspace-snapshot scenarios. This one removes the rest of that pipeline: the simulator code that replayed snapshots, the `Developer: Log Workbench State` command that wrote them, and a few unrelated unused test helpers. Simulation results don't change: the CI suite still replays the same 130 scenarios with an unchanged score.

**21 files changed (39 insertions, 738 deletions).** About 81% of the deleted lines date from the June 2025 import and 16% is `endpointTestFixtures.ts`, which has never been imported. The rest are ripple edits from formatting and API changes.

## Why this is dead
- A snapshot scenario was a folder with a `*.conversation.json` and a `*.state.json` file. Only the external scenario loader removed in #345173 read them, and the repository contains no such files.
- `github.copilot.debug.workbenchState` (`Developer: Log Workbench State`) asked for symbol queries and a file name, then saved a snapshot as `<name>.state.json` in the workspace root. Only that removed loader ever read the format.

## What's removed
**Commit 1: the simulator's snapshot loading**
- `SimulationWorkspace.resetFromDeserializedWorkspaceState`, its 11 snapshot getters and the `IDeserializedWorkspaceState` type (`src/platform/test/node/promptContextModel.ts`).
- `mapLocation`, which redirected the simulated workspace path to the scenario folder on disk, and the path rewriting built on it in the simulated file system, workspace and terminal services. Without a snapshot it already returned its input unchanged.
- The snapshot branches in the simulated git, terminal, debug-output and language services. They now return the defaults they already returned.
- The snapshot scenario type, the `conversationPath`, `scenarioFolderPath` and `stateFile` test options that nothing sets, and the JSON schema and file association for `*.conversation.json`.

**Commit 2: the `Developer: Log Workbench State` command**
- The command, its contribution and registration, its two `package.json` entries, its title in `package.nls.json`, and the JSON schema for `*.state.json`.
- `WorkspaceStateSnapshotHelper` stays, because internal feedback reports (behind the team-internal `DebugReportFeedback` setting) include its output. It loses the symbol queries that only the command supplied, and the snapshot type loses the fields that nothing writes or reads any more: `workspaceFolderFilePath`, `symbols`, `lsifIndex`, `changeFiles` and `testFailures`.

**Commit 3: unused helpers**
- `src/platform/test/common/endpointTestFixtures.ts` and its lint exemption.
- `isQualifiedFile`, `isRelativeFile`, `logComments`, `IInlineEditTest`, `IInlineEditTestDocument` and `NextCursorPosition`.
- The `tiktoken` and `rich` Python test requirements, which no code or fixture imports.

## Behavior changes
- `Developer: Log Workbench State` no longer appears in the Command Palette.
- The WORKSPACE STATE section of internal feedback reports no longer has the `symbols` list, which was always empty there.

## Open PRs
52 of the 3,062 open PRs touch files changed here, mostly `package.json` and `eslint.config.js`. I simulated merging each of them into this branch, and none picks up a new conflict.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` (all 4 projects) passes at each commit. `npm run eslint` on the 13 touched source files and `git diff --check` are clean, and `package.json` and `package.nls.json` still parse.
- A scan of every export against `origin/main` finds nothing newly unreferenced.
- With the simulator built, `node dist/simulationMain.js --ci --require-cache` reports "Score unchanged in 130 scenarios" (overall score 90.25%).
- External NES scenarios (`--external-scenarios=test/simulation/fixtures/inlineEdits --nes=external --require-cache --n=1`) build the same model request as before this change: the run stops at the same test with the same request hash.
- `npx vitest run --changed origin/main`: 463 test files passed (10,141 tests), 5 skipped.
- Not run: the simulation workbench, whose code didn't change, and the extension's integration tests.

title: agentHost: route Auto to the on-device model when the cloud fallback serves only /responses
body:
Fixes #344974

## What

When Auto (or Copilot Fusion) picks the on-device model, CAPI's `/auto` answer includes a `cloud_fallback_model` for the case where the local model fails before its first output. The local model bridge only accepted a fallback that lists `/chat/completions` in `supported_endpoints`. Current Auto fallbacks, such as GPT-6 Luna, list only `/responses`. So every local pick was rejected with `fallbackNotChat`, `/auto` was sent again cloud-only, and the on-device model was never used.

- `readFallbackModel` accepts a fallback that supports `/chat/completions` (preferred, unchanged path) or `/responses`, and records which one on the route.
- For a Responses-only fallback, `buildFallbackResponsesRequest` translates the runtime's chat completions request into a non-streaming `/responses` request with the route's `Copilot-Session-Token`. It covers messages, images, tool calls and results, function tools, `tool_choice`, `max_output_tokens` (clamped to the fallback's limit), the mapped reasoning effort and `store: false`.
- `toChatCompletionFromResponses` turns the answer back into a `chat.completion`. If the runtime asked for a stream, it gets the whole answer as one chunk followed by `[DONE]`. CAPI errors such as a 401 still reach the runtime unchanged, and a response that did not complete returns a 502.
- `fallbackNotChat` now applies only when the fallback supports neither endpoint.

## Notes for reviewers

- The translation runs only on the fallback path: the local model failing before output, ancillary work, image requests, full slots and so on. A healthy on-device turn is unchanged.
- Earlier reasoning is not sent to a Responses fallback, because the history doesn't record which model produced it.
- The fallback is deliberately non-streaming and minimal. The bundled runtime sends its `-local` chat requests without streaming today. It does not request reasoning summaries and does not pass on `response_format`, a `tool_choice` naming one function, or images inside tool results.
- Longer term, the runtime has its own on-device Auto routing (`session.autoLocalModels.set`, behind `AUTO_LOCAL_ROUTING`) that builds the fallback through its normal Responses path. The SDK doesn't expose that method yet. Once it does, this translation and most of the `/auto` patching could be removed.

## How to test

Automated:

- `npm run test-node -- --runGlob "**/agentHost/test/node/localModelBridge/*.test.js"`: passed (280 passing). Includes new tests for the request translation, the answer translation and an end-to-end handler run (streamed, JSON and 401).
- `npm run test-node -- --run <blob>.integrationTest.ts`: passed (10 passing). The new case runs the bundled Copilot runtime against loopback fakes with a `/responses`-only fallback. Without this change it fails with `cloudOnlyReissue:fallbackNotChat`; with it, the local model is tried first and the turn completes through `/responses`.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: passed.

Manual (verified end to end in a local build):

1. Set `chat.copilot.localModel.enabled`, `chat.copilot.localModel.useInAuto` and `chat.copilot.localModel.llamaServerPath`. To match the issue, also set `chat.copilot.dynamicAutoTiers.enabled` to `false`.
2. Start the on-device MAI model and wait for `Ready ... Auto eligible` in `agenthost.log`.
3. In a Copilot harness chat, pick Auto and send a trivial prompt.
4. `agenthost.log` shows `/auto: local pick routed`, not `local pick without a usable fallback (fallbackNotChat)`, and the response shows as on-device.

Fixes the worktree cleanup issues reported in the attached screenshot and follow-up error report.

## Changes

- Track cleanups already pending or running when the editor opens, so the persistent results counter updates as removal is verified without reopening the editor.
- Keep polling with bounded backoff after a refresh request throws, instead of leaving scheduled rows stale indefinitely. Errors remain explicitly reported.
- Hide the eligibility summary, Select All, and cleanup action when every matching row is in Progress and results. Restore the controls when selectable worktrees appear.
- Remove the checkbox widget margin that compounded the Select All group gap. Do not automatically move focus or reveal results when cleanup starts.
- Exclude all cleanup failures reporting exit code 128, regardless of command or reason, including scheduling-time failures. Other exit codes and locks without that error remain visible; this does not unlock or delete worktrees.
- Update accessibility help and add regression coverage. Confirmed removals remain visible as results until the editor is reopened; disappearance alone is not treated as proof of removal.

title: editor: support mixed tab/space indentation (GNU style)
body:
Fixes #5394, #42740, #275754

Includes #300059 (slightly updated and improved)

Detect an independent indent size when a file uses mixed tabs and spaces for indentation (e.g. tab size 8, indent size 2, where 12 columns of indent are encoded as `\t  `). Use the detected indent size for normalization (shift/unshift, auto indent, typing) and show it in the status bar indentation indicator. When inserting tabs, normalize against the render tab size instead of the indent size.

Code generated with a local GLM5.3 model.

Several tests have been added to catch future regressions. You can also test it manually by opening any file that contains code that uses GNU style indentation, and seeing that it renders tabs properly, and that indent and unindent actions work properly.

title: Agent host gateway: accept frames up to 100 MiB and close peers on errors
body:
Refs #339997

The protocol-v6 selection gateway in `cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs` opens its WebSocket streams with tungstenite's default limits. The 16 MiB frame limit rejects chat snapshots that the agent host sends as a single frame:

```text
Gateway proxy: target connection error: Capacity(MessageTooLong { size: 17128534, max_size: 16777216 })
```

When that happens, `proxy_gateway_frames` returns without closing the client. The client notices only after its 25 s liveness timeout, reconnects, subscribes to the same chat, and fails again about every 30 s.

## Changes

- Configure the client-facing gateway socket and both target dial paths (TCP and socket) with a 100 MiB frame and message limit. This matches `defaultMaxPayloadLength` in `webSocketOverDuplex.ts`, so the gateway accepts every frame the client accepts.
- When either side of the proxy fails, send a Close frame to the other side: 1009 for size errors, 1011 for other errors. A 5 s timeout bounds the close so a stalled peer cannot hold the streams open. The client sees the failure right away.

## Tests

Two new tests drive the real `/agent-host/select` route:

- `gateway_proxies_frames_larger_than_16_mib` echoes a 17 MiB frame through the gateway.
- `gateway_closes_client_when_target_frame_exceeds_limit` has the target announce a frame above the limit and expects the client to receive Close 1009 within 5 s.

Both fail without the change. `cargo test gateway_` passes (18 tests).

## Out of scope

Snapshots keep growing, and the issue reports chats estimated at 60 to 80 MiB, so the higher limit gives headroom for most sessions. Long-lived sessions still need the protocol changes discussed in the issue: honouring `view.turns` in `subscribe`, paging in `fetchTurns`, and sending large tool results and images by reference.

body:

title: chat: restore a scrolled-up transcript by the row at the top of the viewport
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

When you switch away from a chat that is scrolled up, then switch back, it should reopen on the same content. Today that only works reliably near the start of the transcript. Further in, it can reopen an exchange or more away from where you were reading. This PR remembers the row at the top of the viewport and the offset into it, so the chat reopens exactly where you left it.

It came out of the review of #345136, which found that restoring a scrolled-up position depends on which rows happen to be measured when it's restored. #345136 builds on this PR, so this one lands first.

## Why it happens

The hosts (the Agents window, the Chat view and the chat editor) save `ChatWidget.getViewState()` when you switch away, and call `restoreViewState` right after binding the chat again. The saved state is an absolute `scrollTop`. Rows that haven't rendered yet have estimated heights (200 px by default), and every bind creates new view model items, so no measured heights carry over. An absolute offset only lands on the same content if the rows above it have the same heights as when it was saved. So it lands somewhere else whenever the rows you scrolled past are taller or shorter than their estimates, which chat responses usually are.

## Fix

- When the transcript isn't at its bottom, `getViewState` also saves a scroll anchor: the row at the top of the viewport, and how far the viewport is scrolled past its top.
  - A row is identified by its request ID, and whether it is the request or its response. Agent host sessions come back with the same request IDs but new response IDs (I saw this in the real window), so response IDs can't be used.
- `restoreViewState` first scrolls that row to the top of the viewport. Rendering it there measures it without moving it, because the list keeps the first visible row in place while it measures rows. Then it scrolls past the row's top by the saved offset, which is now exact.
- If the row is gone (for example, its request was removed), or the state was saved without an anchor, it restores `scrollTop` as before. A chat that was saved at its bottom still opens at its bottom.

`getScrollAnchor` finds the row with a binary search over row tops, and only runs when the transcript is scrolled up.

## Measurements

In the real Agents window, connected to the scripted mock agent host (Code OSS dev build, Apple M5 Pro, macOS 26.7): scroll a session to a position, switch to another session and back, then compare the row at the top of the viewport and the offset into it.

| Saved at (top of viewport) | `main` restores to | this PR restores to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| request 1, +150 px | same place | same place |
| response 1, +6 px | response 1, +10 px | same place |
| request 2, +46 px | request 2, +50 px | same place |
| request 4, +38 px | request 4, +72 px | same place |
| request 9, +99 px | request 8, +30 px | same place |
| the bottom | the bottom | the bottom |

#345136 builds on this PR: it makes switching faster by rendering only the last rows of a transcript, so fewer rows have been measured when a chat is restored. With it on top, this PR also restored all five positions I tried exactly, in a separate set of sessions.

## Tests

- New `ChatListWidget` test: *restores the row at the top of the viewport after switching to another chat and back*. It reads down to the fourth response, switches to another chat, then back to a copy of the chat whose responses have new IDs, and restores through `ChatWidget`. On `main` it reopens two exchanges lower (row 11, +756 px, instead of row 7, +150 px). With this PR it lands exactly.
- Extended `ChatWidget` › *captures and restores transcript scroll state*: the anchor is only saved when scrolled up, restoring uses it, and a missing row or a state without an anchor falls back to `scrollTop`.

Validation:
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: 308 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 15,049 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js"`: 9,370 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean

## How to test

1. Open a long chat in the Agents window, the Chat view or a chat editor.
2. Scroll up into the middle of the transcript.
3. Switch to another chat or session, then back.
4. The transcript should reopen at exactly the same place.

title: copilot: remove the simulator's external chat scenario and in-extension-host modes
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Follow-up to #344959, #345067 and #345137.

This removes two Copilot simulator run modes that nothing uses anymore, everything only they reached, and a few independently dead flags and scripts. No product code, simulation tests, cache recordings or CI gates change: the CI suite still replays the same 130 scenarios with an unchanged score.

**47 files changed (53 insertions, 3,500 deletions).** All 53 insertions are existing lines rewritten without the removed parts, plus one new JSDoc line.

## Why these modes are dead
- **External chat scenarios** (`--external-scenarios` with `--inline` or `--sidebar`) ran chat scenarios and recorded workspace snapshots from a folder outside the repository. No such scenario folders exist here, and CI doesn't run them. The only external caller I found in the microsoft org is a script that nothing invokes, and it targets the archived `microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat` repository.
- **`--in-extension-host`** re-ran the simulator inside a real VS Code extension host through a bootstrap extension and an RPC bridge. Its only caller was that same script.
- Apart from `analyzeEdits.ts`, every change to the deleted files since the June 2025 import was a ripple edit from work elsewhere: interface and API updates, lint and build migrations, and one re-indent.

## What's removed
**Commit 1: the two modes and everything only they reached**
- The external scenario loader and scenario test runner (`test/e2e/scenarioLoader.ts`, `scenarioTest.ts`), the panel code-mapper simulator, and the chat parts of `externalScenarios.ts`. Only `ExternalSimulationTestRuntime` remains, for NES.
- The LSIF language feature service, and the clang, eslint, roslyn, ruff and pylint diagnostic providers, with their cache salts, cache scopes and the pylint/ruff entries in `test/requirements.txt`. The remaining suites only use `tsc` and `pyright`.
- The extension-host harness (`testExecutionInExtension.ts`, `test/simulationExtension/`, `test/base/extHostContext/`), its RPC proxies for outcomes, endpoint health and JSON output, the `COPILOT_SIMULATION_VSCODE` hook in the esbuild VS Code shim, and the ESLint and allowed-JavaScript exceptions that existed only for it.
- Helpers left without callers: `deserializeWorkbenchState`, `waitForListenerOnPort` (`src/util/node/ports.ts`), `SimulationTestProvider`, `findIfInstalled`, `parseQueryForScenarioTest`, and the suite factory's input-path parameter.
- Flags: `--inline`, `--sidebar`, `--apply-chat-code-blocks`, `--in-extension-host`, `--install-extension`, `--headless`, `--run-number` and `--scenario-workspace-folder`.

**Commit 2: dead flags and scripts**
- `--swebench-prompt` and `--cache-location` were parsed but never read.
- `--regenerate-cache` was listed in the help text but never parsed. The workbench's matching cache mode wasn't offered in its UI, and a persisted value already behaved like the default mode.
- `script/analyzeEdits.ts` (`npm run analyze-edits`) reads MSBench output from a hard-coded personal path, so it only works on one machine.
- A `docs/tools.md` checklist item about swebench simulator scenarios, which this repository doesn't have.

## Behavior changes
- `--external-scenarios` now requires `--nes`. Old `--inline` or `--sidebar` invocations exit with a usage error instead of running anything.
- `--external-scenarios` combined with `--scenario-test` used to skip NES discovery and pass the folder to scenario-test suites. Those suites are gone, so the folder is now always treated as NES scenarios.

## What's deliberately kept
- NES external scenarios: `--nes=external` (also the default for a bare `--nes`) and `--nes=coffe`.
- The **STest Runner** workspace extension (`.vscode/extensions/test-extension`), the test visualization runner, `editFromPatchTests.ts` and `script/compareStestAlternativeRuns.ts`.
- Vendored `src/util/vs` files that lost their last user (`EditOperation`, `raceCancellablePromises`). That folder is regenerated by `script/setup/copySources.ts`.

## Open PRs that will conflict
I simulated merging each of the 53 open PRs that touch these files (out of 3,060 open PRs) into this branch. Only two pick up new conflicts, and both are trivial:
- #341819 (draft): it edits `script/analyzeEdits.ts`, which this PR deletes, and the `setupTools` lines in `inlineChatSimulator.ts`. Keep its removal of the edit-tool override along with this PR's `as TestToolsService` cast.
- #336441: drop its spelling fixes in `lsifLanguageFeatureService.ts`, which this PR deletes.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck` (all 4 projects) passes at both commits. `npm run eslint` on the 24 modified source files and `git diff --check` are clean.
- A scan of every export against `origin/main` finds nothing newly unreferenced, apart from the vendored files above and symbols still used inside their own file.
- With the simulator built, `node dist/simulationMain.js --ci --require-cache` reports "Score unchanged in 130 scenarios".
- CLI: `--external-scenarios` without `--nes`, and the old `--sidebar` form, print the usage error and exit 1. `--nes=external` and a bare `--nes` list the 4 NES recordings in `src/extension/inlineEdits/test/node/recordings`. `--list-tests` lists 130 tests, and `--help` mentions none of the removed flags.
- `npx vitest run --changed HEAD`: 437 files passed. The other 26 failed only because this worktree had no built workers or tree-sitter wasm in `dist/`, and all of them pass once those are staged (879 tests passed, 4 skipped).
- Simulation workbench, driven through Electron with Playwright: Local mode lists 130 tests, and the cache picker offers Use Cache, No Cache and Require Cache. Running one codeMapper test from the UI with Require Cache passes 10 of 10 runs with no cache misses. NES External and Adhoc Request switch without errors. The only console error came from the workbench reading `baseline.old.json.txt` at the start of a run, before the simulator writes it. That code isn't changed here.

## Possible follow-up (not in this PR)
The removed external scenarios were the only source of workspace-snapshot scenarios. Nothing calls `SimulationWorkspace.resetFromDeserializedWorkspaceState` any more, so its 11 state getters are always `undefined`, and the snapshot branches in the simulated git, terminal, debug-output and language services that read them never run. Those services are shared by every simulation test, so that's better as its own PR. The `github.copilot.debug.workbenchState` command, which writes snapshots, stays: it's a contributed Developer command, and the feedback reporter uses the same snapshot helper.

title: build: clear package feed credentials in the remaining jobs
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Follow-up to #345143, which clears package feed credentials once dependencies are installed in the jobs that run tests.

Six more jobs still keep a feed access token in their environment after `Install dependencies`. They run no tests, so this change is defense in depth: later steps could still write the token to logs.

| Job | Template | Variable cleared |
|---|---|---|
| Alpine | `alpine/product-build-alpine.yml` | `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` |
| Alpine node_modules | `alpine/product-build-alpine-node-modules.yml` | `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` |
| Web | `web/product-build-web.yml` | `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` |
| Web node_modules | `web/product-build-web-node-modules.yml` | `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` |
| macOS node_modules | `darwin/product-build-darwin-node-modules.yml` | `PIP_INDEX_URL` |
| Windows API scan | `win32/sdl-scan-win32.yml` | `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` |

Each new step works like the steps that #345143 added. It runs right after `Install dependencies` with `condition: always()`, is named `Clear package feed credentials`, and empties the variable with `##vso[task.setvariable variable=…]`.

- In these jobs, only the install step uses the token, for the Foundry Local NuGet download or pip on macOS.
- The Windows API scan job signs in to NuGet twice, both times before its install, so one clear step covers both.
- The Linux and Windows node_modules jobs don't sign in to NuGet or pip, so they're unchanged.

With this change, every `NuGetAuthenticate@1` and `PipAuthenticate@1` step under `build/azure-pipelines/` is followed by a step that clears its variable.

## How to test

- `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts <the six changed files>`: passed. It also passed as the pre-commit hook.
- Parsing the six changed files with `js-yaml`: passed.
- A static check of all 88 YAML files under `build/azure-pipelines/`: passed. Each of the 14 `NuGetAuthenticate@1` and `PipAuthenticate@1` steps is followed by a step that clears its variable.
- Not run yet: a pipeline build of this branch. A Product build runs the Alpine, Web and Windows API scan jobs, and a CI build runs the node_modules jobs. In each job, the `Clear package feed credentials` step should succeed and the later steps should behave as before.

title: sessions: Keep archived Dev Container sessions restorable
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #338449

## Problem

Marking the last session in a Dev Container as **Done** ran `docker rm --force` on the container. The container's writable layer holds the session's only Agent Host data (user data dir) and Copilot state (`~/.copilot/session-state`). **Restore** then started a replacement container whose empty host listed no sessions, and the authoritative-list eviction dropped the session from **Done** and from the persisted cache, so reloading did not bring it back.

Live testing against local Docker found a second issue on the restore path. The provider subscribed to the session and dispatched `SessionIsArchivedChanged` immediately. A restarted host only delivers action envelopes to *active* subscribers, which it becomes after loading the session (~2.5s here). The confirmation was therefore missed, the 5s timeout rolled the local state back and stopped the container, even though the host had applied the change. The same applies to marking a session done after an idle stop.

## Changes

- **Archive the last active session:** stop the container instead of removing it, so restore restarts the same container with its state.
- **Failed unarchive:** stop rather than remove, which would destroy the archived session's state.
- **Delete:** remove the container only once no sessions remain; when only archived sessions remain, stop it.
- **Archive toggles:** wait for the session subscription's first snapshot (new 30s `DEV_CONTAINER_SESSION_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`) before dispatching; the 5s confirmation timeout is unchanged. A subscription error now fails immediately with the host's reason instead of after a silent timeout.
- Updated `REMOTE_AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md`.

Trade-off: archived sessions keep a stopped container (and, with New Worktree, its worktree) until the last session is deleted.

Note for testplan #338262: step 2.3 should now expect the container to be **stopped**, not removed, after marking the last session done.

## How to test

1. Enable `chat.agentHost.devContainer.enabled`, set `chat.agentHost.devContainer.idleTimeout` to `0`.
2. In the Agents window, pick a Dev Container workspace (e.g. vscode-remote-try-node), choose the **Dev Container** environment, and send: "Remember this code word for later: PELICAN-42. Do not use any tools. Reply with just OK."
3. **Mark as Done** → `docker ps -a` shows the container `Exited`, not removed.
4. Show Done → **Restore** → the same container starts and the session leaves Done and stays there.
5. Ask "What code word did I ask you to remember?" → `PELICAN-42`.

## Validation

- Manual end-to-end test with a Code OSS Agents window against local Docker on Windows (Docker 29.9): steps 1–5 above passed, including a follow-up after the cold restore (answered `24-NACILEP` when asked to reverse the word) on the same container ID. Before the second fix, restore timed out and stopped the container again. Deleting the last session was not exercised live.
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts` — passed (382 passing).
- `npx tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` — passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>` — passed.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

The host silently drops passive `SessionIsArchivedChanged` actions for sessions it has not surfaced yet (`_applyPassiveSessionMetadata` returns `undefined`, with no envelope or rejection). Rejecting instead would surface such failures to clients.

title: sessions: let artifact integrations opt into their own pills with a group ID
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Previously, every artifact or reference with an artifact integration left the Artifacts and References pills for a pill of its own, and artifacts were grouped by their main integration. This PR lets each integration decide, per artifact, whether it gets its own pill. Extensions can make the same choice.

### What changed

- **New optional `groupId` on the contribution view.** It's added to `ArtifactContributionView` and validated as a non-empty string on the wire. Extensions set it through `ChatArtifactIntegrationState.groupId` in the proposed `chatArtifactIntegrations` API.
- **With a `groupId`:** the artifact gets a dedicated pill. Artifacts sharing a `groupId` collapse into one group pill, even across integrations or extensions. The pill is named by the first artifact's `groupLabel`, and icon priorities are compared across the whole group. Pinning, unpinning and alias collapsing work as before. References never join a group.
- **Without a `groupId`:** the artifact is listed in the normal pill for its kind (Artifacts, References, Pull Requests or Issues), with the integration's icon and label.
  - Selecting the row opens the artifact's details (status, actions, Autopilot), and a new **Open** row action opens the resource.
  - If it's the pill's only entry, the pill renders as the full integration pill.
  - Several records of the same resource still show once.
- **GitHub pull requests are unchanged.** The built-in integration sets `groupId: 'github.pullRequest'`, so PR pills look and behave as before.
- **Details host:** `IArtifactDetailsHost.toggle` now accepts an optional target. When none is given, focus returns to the control that opened the details.
- **Docs:** the accessibility help and the grouping section of `ARTIFACT_INTEGRATIONS_PROPOSAL.md` describe the new behavior.

### Notes for reviewers

- **Behavior change for existing extension integrations:** integrations that don't set `groupId` (for example Commit, ExP and Test Plan Item) will move into the standard pills until they adopt it.
- **Details from a dropdown row can close on their own:** they're tied to the pill that opened them, so if that pill changes shape while they're open (for example, the list drops to one entry), the details close. Group pills already behave this way.

### How to test

1. Enable `chat.artifactIntegrations.enabled` and open a session in the Agents window.
2. Record a GitHub pull request artifact. It should get its own PR pill, as before.
3. Record artifacts handled by an extension integration that does not set `groupId`. They should appear in the **Artifacts** pill with the integration's icon. Selecting a row opens its details, and **Open** opens the link. If it's the only artifact, the Artifacts pill shows the integration's sections directly.
4. Have two integrations return the same `groupId`. Their artifacts should share one group pill.

### Validation

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed, no errors |
| `npm run eslint -- <changed files>` | Passed, 19 files |
| `./scripts/test.sh --run …/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/{artifactIntegrationGroup,sessionArtifacts,sessionChatInputToolbar,artifactIntegrationPresentation,sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp}.test.ts --run …/platform/artifactIntegrations/test/common/{artifactIntegrationProtocol,artifactIntegrations}.test.ts --run …/<blob>.test.ts` | Passed, 431 tests |
| `npm run test-node -- --run …/agentHost/test/node/githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration.test.ts --run …/agentHost/test/node/clientArtifactIntegrationEndpoint.test.ts` | Passed, 99 tests |

I didn't run integration, smoke or screenshot tests, and I didn't do a manual check in a running build.

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Fix sidepane visibility in the Agents window's `chat` layout mode:

- Wait for the incoming editor working set before restoring visibility. Opening an existing chat must not automatically reveal an empty or docked-only sidepane.
- Preserve the current pane composition when the active new session or nested session is submitted, without preserving that exception on a later visit.
- Respect explicit pane opens during restoration. Explicitly reopening a submitted chat's docked-only composition shows both Editor and Details; unsubmitted drafts retain docked-only reopening.

title: sessions: group integrated references with their integration's artifacts
body:
When an artifact integration presents both artifacts and references, only the artifacts joined its group pill. A chat with two ExP experiments recorded as artifacts and three scorecards of one step recorded as references showed **2 Experiments** in a dropdown, plus the scorecards in a pill of their own. The scorecards already collapse into one pill because they bind to the same step.

## What changed

- **Grouping key**: integrated records now group by their main integration alone, whether they are artifacts or references. The `[pill kind, integration]` key and the "references never group" rule are gone. In the example above, all three appear in one **3 Experiments** dropdown.
- **Hidden pill kinds**: a group can now mix the Artifacts and References kinds. Records of a hidden kind (for example after **Hide References**) are left out before grouping, rather than hiding the whole group pill. They keep a hidden source, so their kind's options stay reachable from the row.
- **Group pill kind**: the group pill takes its first artifact's kind, falling back to the first member. Other member kinds keep a hidden source so the row still counts them as shown in the visibility menu.
- **Pinning**: unchanged. A reference can now be pinned out of a group the same way an artifact can, using its own kind's pin storage.
- **Docs**: updated the grouping paragraph in `ARTIFACT_INTEGRATIONS_PROPOSAL.md` and the Agents window accessibility help.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.
- `artifactIntegrationGroup.test.ts`, `sessionChatInputToolbar.test.ts` and `sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts` pass (155 tests).
- Updated tests:
  - The "never group references" and scorecard-alias tests now expect references inside the group.
  - New coverage for mixed kinds, hidden kinds and pinning a reference.
  - The toolbar test keeps a reference from a different integration as a lone pill, so removal scoping is still covered.

title: Don't reuse a remembered remote agent host session type when this window lacks the host
body:
`chat.userSelectedSessionType` is stored per profile, so a session type for a remote agent host (`remote-*`) chosen in one window carries over to windows that don't have that host. In those windows **Chat: New Chat Editor** reuses it and opens a broken `untitled-<uuid>` editor: no chat editor is registered for that scheme, so the text model resolver fails with `Unable to resolve resource`.

### Changes

- **`isNewChatSessionTypeUsable`** (`chat/common/constants.ts`): a `remote-*` type now also requires a registered chat session contribution in this window. Remote hosts register one per connected agent. If it's missing, the remembered selection falls back to the computed default.
  ```ts
  if (isAgentHostTarget(sessionType)) {
  return agentHostEnabled && (!isRemoteAgentHostTarget(sessionType) || !!chatSessionsService.getChatSessionContribution(sessionType));
  }
  ```
  Local agent host types (`agent-host-*`) are unchanged and stay usable before their contribution registers.
- **Test** (`constants.test.ts`): covers a remembered remote type both without and with a registered contribution.

### Note for review

A remote type is now unusable until its host connects and registers, even in a window that does have the host. A New Chat Editor opened before that point uses the computed default instead of the remembered remote type.

title: sessions: retain shared PR models across presentation updates
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fix unnecessary teardown and recreation of shared pull-request presentation models. Recent Insiders logs showed a single burst disposing and recreating 312 PR models.

Reactive presentation previously released its references before recomputing, allowing the last reference to destroy a model immediately before the same model was acquired again. Use the reader's delayed store to acquire replacement PR, CI, and review-thread references before releasing the previous references. This preserves existing models without suppressing listener diagnostics or retaining obsolete models.

Regression tests cover both provider and pill presentation: repeated updates reuse models, a head change replaces only the CI model, and removal or loss of observers releases all references. Both new regressions failed before the fix (60 unnecessary recreations per model).

No separately filed issue; discovered during local log triage. Rebased onto current main, preserving upstream tests.
