title: sessions: pin chat canvases to the Agents window sidebar
body:
## TL;DR In the Agents window, a user can now **pin a chat's canvas to the sidebar**. A pinned canvas stays live while the user works in other chats, and clicking its sidebar row shows it on a full page of its own, without switching to its chat. The canvas stays owned by its chat, whose agent keeps updating it. No issue was filed. The series is rebased on `main` (`3ee7c48cab0`), is split into 11 commits that each build and pass tests, and is meant to be reviewed commit by commit (see the [review guide](#review-guide-commit-by-commit)). ## Background (no prior context needed) - **Canvas:** a live web page that a chat's agent opens and keeps updating, such as a plan, a preview, or a dashboard. It is served by a canvas extension that runs in the agent host, and the window renders it in a native web contents view. Each canvas is owned by one chat: `ICanvasOwner = { providerId, session, chat }`. - **How canvases are shown today:** `CanvasService` (`vs/workbench/contrib/canvases`) shows a canvas only while its owning chat is visible, as an editor tab beside that chat (`isOwnerPresentable`). In the Agents window, `SessionCanvasContextService` reports only the active session's active chat as visible, and the Agent Host provider subscribes to a chat's canvases only while its session is active. - **The problem:** as soon as the user switches chats, a canvas disappears, and its updates are no longer observed. Users want to keep a canvas at hand, for example a plan they check between turns. - **Why it can stay live:** holding a subscription to a canvas channel keeps the owning agent-host session resident. A pinned canvas only needs the client to keep that subscription; no host or protocol change is needed. ## What changes for users All of this is gated on `ChatContextKeys.enabled`, the Agents window (not auxiliary windows), and `chat.canvases.enabled`. - **Pinning:** - An **Add to Sidebar / Remove from Sidebar** toggle (pin / unpin icons) in the title of an active canvas editor. - The same choice in a canvas tab's context menu. - **Agents: Add Canvas to Sidebar...** in the Command Palette, which picks among the shown chat's live canvases. - It is deliberately not labeled "Pin", which would clash with Pin Tab and the sessions **Pinned** section. - **Sidebar rows:** - Placement: in the default layout, pinned canvases are rows directly below **Automations**. With `sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation`, they come last in the navigation shortcuts. There are no rows when nothing is pinned. - Content: each row shows the canvas title, its chat as secondary text, and its state (live, not connected, or unavailable), and is highlighted while its page is shown. - Actions: hovering or keyboard focus reveals a **Remove from Sidebar** button. The context menu offers **Go to Chat**, **Remove from Sidebar** and **Close Canvas**. - **Canvas page:** - Clicking a row shows the canvas full-page, replacing the sessions grid like Automations does. It never switches to the owning chat. - Its icon-only header offers the same three actions. - Back/Forward return to the canvas each opening showed. - **Lifecycle:** - Up to 5 pins, with a notification when full. - Pins persist per workspace and reconnect after a reload. - A pin is removed automatically when its session or chat is deleted or archived, or when its canvas is closed through Close Canvas (from the page, the row, or the chat). - Closing a canvas's editor tab does not unpin it. - A pin whose canvas is gone shows as unavailable with **Remove from Sidebar**. ## How it works ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph WB["vs/workbench/contrib/canvases (shared)"] CE["CanvasEditor (editor tab)"] --> CV["CanvasView"] CV --> CS["CanvasService
isOwnerPresentable: may open as an editor
isPresentable: may attach in a view"] CS --> CCS["ICanvasContextService
+ optional getTrackedCanvas, isCanvasTracked, isPresentedElsewhere"] end subgraph SW["vs/sessions (Agents window)"] PAGE["Canvas page (custom view)"] --> CV PAGE --> PCS["IPinnedCanvasService
pins, storage, lifecycle"] ROWS["Sidebar rows and actions"] --> PCS SCCS["SessionCanvasContextService"] -. implements .-> CCS SCCS --> PCS PCS --> SMS["ISessionsManagementService
observeCanvas, observeChatCanvases"] SMS --> PROV["ISessionsProvider optional hooks
Agent Host: no active-session gate"] end ``` - **Shared canvas layer (`vs/workbench/contrib/canvases`):** - The rendering moves out of `CanvasEditor` into a reusable `CanvasView`. - `ICanvasService` gains `isPresentable`, separate from `isOwnerPresentable`. - `ICanvasContextService` gains three optional members, so a host can keep canvases live outside their owner's visibility without ever opening them as editors. - **Provider-neutral liveness (`vs/sessions`):** two optional `ISessionsProvider` hooks, `observeCanvas` and `observeChatCanvases`, are routed through `ISessionsManagementService`. Shared sessions code never imports provider code. The Agent Host provider implements them without the active-session gate. - **Pins:** - `IPinnedCanvasService` keeps pins and their storage, and holds one `observeCanvas` reference per pin. - `SessionCanvasContextService` reports pins to `CanvasService`. - The page is a custom view (`sessions.customView.canvas`). A custom view opening can now carry a `state` (the pin) for history. - **Specs:** `SESSIONS.md` (the pin contract), `SESSIONS_LIST.md` (row placement and ownership) and `LAYOUT.md` (custom view history state) are updated concisely. ## Key decisions | Decision | Why | |---|---| | A pinned canvas stays owned by its chat | Its agent keeps driving it. Pinning only keeps it live and gives it a second place to be shown. | | `isPresentable` is separate from `isOwnerPresentable` | Editors keep their current rule (beside the visible owner only), so a pinned canvas can never auto-open as an editor in another chat's working set. Only views, such as the page, use the wider rule. | | Persist identity only (provider, session, chat, extension, canvas type, instance ID, last title), never the URL | Canvas URLs carry access tokens and change whenever the canvas restarts. A pin rebinds to the live canvas with the same instance ID. | | Clicking a pin always shows its page, never its chat | It keeps the user where they are. A pin that isn't connected after a reload reconnects through `observeChatCanvases` without showing the chat. | | One browser model per canvas, attached to one view at a time | The same canvas can be in an editor and on the page. A hidden view never takes the model from a visible one, and takes it back once it is visible again. | | At most 5 pins | Each pin keeps its session resident in the agent host. | ## Review guide (commit by commit) Each commit builds and passes the affected test suites on its own. | # | Commit | What to review | Size | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `canvases: extract CanvasView from CanvasEditor` | Mostly moved code. New logic: one view at a time owns a browser model (claim, yield, reclaim). It also includes main's corner-radius forwarding (#344727), which moved into `CanvasView._measure` during the rebase. | +667 / −383 | | 2 | `canvases: let other surfaces track and present a canvas` | `isPresentable` versus `isOwnerPresentable`. External presentations: their models are retained and then released. Closing a tab while the page shows its canvas keeps the model. A request ahead of reconciliation waits for the update to settle. | +130 / −23 | | 3 | `sessions: observe chat canvases outside the active session` | The optional provider hooks, routing through the management service, the Agent Host implementation, and `onDidCloseCanvas`. | +178 / −5 | | 4 | `sessions: return custom views to the item each opening showed` | Custom view `state` and `acceptsState`, and Back/Forward history. | +102 / −13 | | 5 | `sessions: add a service for canvases pinned to the sidebar` | `IPinnedCanvasService`: storage (identity only), the cap, rebinding after a reload, and automatic removal. Most of the size is tests. | +1317 | | 6 | `sessions: present pinned canvases outside their chat` | `SessionCanvasContextService` wiring. A pinned canvas is presentable only on the page, never as an editor in another chat. | +194 / −5 | | 7 | `sessions: add a full-page view for pinned canvases` | The canvas page custom view and its states (live, reconnecting, unavailable). | +206 | | 8 | `sessions: add actions to pin canvases to the sidebar` | Actions, menus, context keys and gating. | +422 | | 9 | `sessions: list pinned canvases in the sidebar` | Rows in both sidebar layouts, accessibility labels, the hover toolbar, and the context menu. | +426 / −8 | | 10 | `canvases: hold the last frame while a canvas view switches canvases` | Polish: no empty flash when switching pins. `WebContentsViewHost.setVisible(visible, immediate)`. | +232 / −7 | | 11 | `sessions: keep shortcut rows highlighted without a pointer focus ring` | Polish: no stale focus outline under pointer focus, and the active row keeps its highlight. | +111 / −2 | ## Review so far An automated AI review of the full series (GPT-6 Astra; architecture, decisions, correctness, security, engineering, implementation) judged the architecture sound. It reported 4 high and 2 medium findings, and all are fixed in the commits above. Each fix has a regression test that fails without it. | Finding | Fix | In commit | |---|---|---| | High: the canvas page could stay on "Loading canvas…" after a canvas restarted with a new URL | Model resolution lets the update settle before judging the source | 2 | | High: closing a canvas tab while its page showed it reloaded the page and leaked the new model | The editor input is released first, and the presentation is kept as external while the page shows it | 2 | | High: Close Canvas from the chat left an "Unavailable" pin | Close events match the last canvas the pin was bound to | 5 | | High: deleting a session from another client left its pins | Sessions reported as `removed` drop their pins (catalog-hidden sessions report no removal) | 5 | | Medium: pins of owners archived while the window was closed stayed | Archived owners are pruned on load and on every catalog change | 5 | | Medium: a slow close could unpin a reopened canvas | Only the close event of the bound canvas removes a pin | 5 | ## Interactions with `main` and other PRs - **Rebase onto `main`:** - On `main`, `SessionCanvasContextService.isOwnerVisible` is false while any custom view is open. The canvas page is a custom view, so a pinned canvas is admitted there only through `isPresentedElsewhere`. The pinned-canvas tests now open the page as a custom view. - Main's Inbox sidebar row is kept, and pins still follow Automations. - **#345093 (draft):** - It also changes `CanvasEditor`'s load state machine and `CanvasService`'s source handling (it keeps the view while a provider reconnects). - This PR moves that `CanvasEditor` logic into `CanvasView`, so whichever lands second must port the other's changes. - **#345102:** it also touches `canvasService.ts`. ## Out of scope / follow-ups - **Chat-input pill:** a pin entry in the chat-input canvases pill (`IChatPillEntry` has only one promoted action). - **Agent host restarts:** by host design, canvases are not restored after an agent host *process* restart (`AGENT_HOST_SESSIONS_PROVIDER.md`), so pins then show as unavailable. A follow-up could reopen the instance with the pin's stored identity. - **Residency cost:** each pin keeps its session resident. The cap bounds this. - **Validation gaps:** - **Agents: Add Canvas to Sidebar...** has no automated test and was not exercised manually. - Two unit tests are still missing: - resolving a pinned canvas through the tracked-canvas fallback for another session with unknown membership; - releasing bound pin subscriptions when canvases or AI are disabled, on service disposal, and on provider reconnection. ## How to test 1. Set `"chat.canvases.enabled": true` and open the Agents window. Start a Copilot CLI session and ask the agent to open a canvas. 2. In the canvas editor's title, select **Add to Sidebar** (pin icon). A row appears below **Automations**, showing the canvas title, the chat, and the live state. 3. Switch to another chat or session, then select the row. The canvas shows full-page and live, without switching chats. Back returns. 4. Hover the row to see **Remove from Sidebar**. Right-click it for **Go to Chat**, **Remove from Sidebar** and **Close Canvas**. 5. Reload the window and select the row. It reconnects without showing its chat. 6. Close the canvas from the page or the chat: the row disappears. Archive or delete the chat: its rows disappear. Close only the editor tab: the row stays. 7. Pin a sixth canvas: a notification explains the limit of 5. 8. Toggle `"sessions.sidebar.separateNavigation"` to check the other sidebar layout. ## Validation All of the following ran on the rebased branch (`main` at `3ee7c48cab0`): | Command | Result | |---|---| | `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed | | `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/{sessions/contrib/canvases,workbench/contrib/canvases,workbench/contrib/browserView,sessions/contrib/sessions,sessions/services/sessions,sessions/services/customView,sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost}/test/**/*.test.js"` | 3297 passing, 19 pending, 0 failing | | Per commit: `tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` and the same test glob, on each of the 11 commits | All passed (3263 to 3297 passing, 0 failing) | | `npm run eslint -- <40 changed .ts files>` | Passed | | `node build/hygiene.ts ` | Passed | | `npm run stylelint -- <3 changed .css files>` | Passed. Its 3 design-token suggestions are on lines this PR doesn't touch. | | `npm run valid-layers-check` | Passed | | `git diff --check` | Clean | The regression tests for the six review findings were also run against the unfixed sources, before the rebase. All six failed there and pass with the fixes. Manual testing in Code OSS, before the rebase, covered: - pinning from the editor title; - both sidebar layouts; - switching chats and opening pins from the sidebar; - the hover button and the context menu; - the page's icon-only header; - the held frame when switching pins; - the shortcut-row focus ring. It has not been repeated after the rebase yet.

title: Browser: harden remote unlisted view networking
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

This closes two generic network-containment gaps for unlisted BrowserViews using a remote Agent Host network:

1. Forward authenticated plain-HTTP WebSocket Upgrade traffic (`ws://`) through `TunnelProxy`, including IPv6 literals and client cancellation while the upstream dial is pending.
2. Prevent traffic from escaping the selected remote network through non-proxied WebRTC UDP or system-browser popup handling.

The changes are independent of canvas enablement and apply to any remote unlisted BrowserView.

## How to review

Review the two commits independently:

### 1. `browser: proxy authenticated WebSocket upgrades`

- [`TunnelProxy._onUpgrade`](src/vs/platform/tunnel/node/tunnelProxy.ts) authenticates the proxy request, validates an absolute HTTP URL, normalizes IPv6 literals, forwards the origin-form request, and bridges the established stream.
- Client closure is observed while connecting; a late upstream stream is destroyed before forwarding.
- [`tunnelProxy.test.ts`](src/vs/platform/tunnel/test/node/tunnelProxy.test.ts) covers successful Upgrade forwarding, IPv6 normalization, and abandoned connections.

### 2. `browser: contain remote unlisted views`

- [`BrowserView`](src/vs/platform/browserView/electron-main/browserView.ts) applies `disable_non_proxied_udp` when its browser session has a remote network.
- [`getBrowserViewPopupAction`](src/vs/platform/browserView/common/browserView.ts) denies external popup escape for unlisted remote views while preserving listed browser-tab behavior and consuming the initiating gesture.

## Security properties

- Proxy authentication remains mandatory for Upgrade requests.
- The destination host/port comes only from a valid absolute `http:` request target.
- Proxy credentials and hop-by-hop proxy headers are not forwarded upstream.
- WebRTC can use only proxied routes.
- An unlisted remote BrowserView cannot open its URL in the client system browser.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/tunnel/test/node/tunnelProxy.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/browserView/test/common/browserView.test.ts` — 42 passed
- Changed TypeScript ESLint — passed for 5 files
- `git diff origin/main..HEAD --check` — passed

Other theme palettes and status-bar behaviour are unchanged. ## Issues addressed | Severity | Issue | Resolution | |---|---|---| | P2 | Hovering an error status item erased its error colour. | Define `statusBarItem.errorHoverBackground` in Dark 2026. | | P2 | Using the resting red for hover removed the interaction cue. | Use a darker shade with the same hue and enforce a distinct state in regression coverage. | ## Validation Commands ran with Node 24.22.1 in a detached worktree containing only the intended patch, independently of unrelated local edits. | Command | Result | |---|---| | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast` | Passed: complete candidate build, including built-in extensions. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast -- --client-only` | Passed: candidate client output. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run typecheck-client` | Passed. | | `PATH=/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin:/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH fnm exec --using=24.22.1 bash scripts/test.sh --run .test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/services/themes/test/common/colorThemeData.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarItem.test.ts --run .test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/statusbar/statusbarPart.test.ts --reporter dot` | Passed: 38 tests. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run eslint -- .test.ts` | Passed. | | `git diff --check` | Passed. | | Commit hooks | Passed: staged-file hygiene. | The regression rejects both the original grey fallback and an identical resting/hover red. title: cli: decode large msgpack messages in linear time, retry initial resolve
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #337090

Two independent fixes found while investigating why **Open in VS Code** for a Dev Container session on a tunnel host hangs at "Installing server".

### cli: decode large msgpack messages in linear time

Dev Containers installs the VS Code server (currently ~220 MB) by piping the downloaded tarball through the Remote - Tunnels exec server as a single `stream_data` message on the control connection. `MsgPackCodec` re-ran `rmp_serde::from_read` from the start of the buffer on every socket read; `from_read` copies the partial binary payload before hitting EOF, so decoding one large message is O(n²). Reads from a forwarded port are at most one SSH packet (~32 KB), and no other RPC on the connection (e.g. `ping`, `spawn`) is processed until the message completes.

The codec now finds the end of each message with a resumable scanner over msgpack headers, skipping string/binary/ext payloads by their declared lengths, and deserializes only complete messages with `rmp_serde::from_slice`. Nesting deeper than 1024 and the reserved `0xc1` marker are rejected as invalid data.

Measured with a ~218 MiB `stream_data` message decoded as `PartialIncoming`, fed in 32 KB chunks:

| Decoder | Time |
|---|---|
| Before (release build) | 384 s |
| After (debug build) | 0.14 s |

### extensions: retry initial remote authority resolution

`_resolveAuthorityInitial` did `return this._resolveAuthorityWithLogging(...)` inside `try` without `await`, so rejections escaped the `catch` and the retry loop added in #156444 has not retried anything since 06b97f6be73 (January 2023). It now awaits, restoring up to 5 attempts for errors other than `NotAvailable` and `NoResolverFound`.

### Notes for reviewers

- The retry fix is a behavior change: resolvers that throw `TemporarilyNotAvailable` or a plain `Error` during the initial resolve will now be re-run (immediately, up to 5 times), as originally designed.
- The CLI fix does **not** by itself prevent #337090: a `ping` sent after the large message is still queued behind it until it has fully crossed the relay, so Remote - Tunnels' 5 s `isStreamValid` ping can still time out and dispose the shared connection. Avoiding that needs Dev Containers to not upload the server through the tunnel (or to chunk with backpressure) and/or Remote - Tunnels to not dispose a busy connection.

### Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --reporter dot --run <blob>.test.ts` — passed (15 tests, 3 new)
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- `npm run eslint -- <blob>.ts <blob>.test.ts` — passed
- `cargo test --lib` (in `cli/`) — passed (187 tests, 3 new in `msgpack_rpc`)
- `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check src/msgpack_rpc.rs` — passed
- `cargo clippy --bin=code` — no warnings in `msgpack_rpc.rs` (11 existing warnings elsewhere)
- Not run: an end-to-end Dev Container install over a real tunnel.

title: Agent Host: preserve MCP decisions and provenance during late plugin discovery
body:
Closes #345015

### What was wrong

Following the review on merged #344961 and Copilot code review on #345144, several runtime-first MCP edge cases needed correction during late plugin discovery and ownership adoption:

1. **Scoped host decision preservation & write normalization**:
  - Adopting a confirmed late plugin owner changed the persistence key from `mcpServers#<name>` to `<pluginUri>#mcp=<name>`. While the runtime session ID was preserved, prior explicit host disable decisions recorded at Global or Workspace scope stopped applying, causing SDK-enabled servers to be erroneously published as enabled.
  - Furthermore, after an unowned Global or Workspace disable was adopted/preserved, enabling the owned server at that scope could have no effect if write normalization (`_setGlobalEnablement` / `_setWorkspace` / `_removeRedundantWorkspaceDecisions`) deleted the requested owned `true` as redundant with defaults or Global values, erroneously restoring the unowned `false`.
2. **Provenance-aware server matching & metadata merge**:
  - `findDiscoveredPluginMcpServer` matched only on `serverName` and `source === 'plugin'`, ignoring known runtime `sourcePlugin`. If runtime and discovery snapshots disagreed, a live server from plugin A could mistakenly match an SDK-discovered child belonging to plugin B.
  - When provenance changed from plugin A to plugin B and B already had a matching discovered child, stripping A's discovery metadata without merging B's metadata discarded B's discovery metadata (e.g. `defaultEnabled: false`) and source range.
3. **Clean transition when moving away from adopted plugin / stale configuration URIs**:
  - If a runtime server previously adopted late plugin discovery metadata and a subsequent inventory identified it as `user`, `workspace`, or `builtin`, the controller rejected `native` but fell back to `existing`. This retained the unrelated plugin's discovery metadata, inherited defaults, and configuration URI/range.
  - Retaining `existing?.uri` for runtime-only entries without discovery metadata caused servers whose provenance changed to `builtin` or `workspace` without a `sourceUri` to retain stale user configuration URIs.

### What changed

1. **Enablement resolution & write normalization**:
  - In `AgentHostCustomizationEnablementService._setGlobalEnablement` and `_setWorkspace`, account for same-scope unowned persistent fallbacks (`unownedGlobal` / `unownedWorkspace`) during write normalization so that an explicit owned enablement is retained when an opposing unowned disable exists at the same scope.
  - Updated `_removeRedundantWorkspaceDecisions` to prevent deletion of owned workspace decisions when opposing unowned decisions exist.
  - Directory isolation is preserved: `adoptMcpServerOwnership` migrates decisions for adopted working directories without leaking unowned keys across unadopted workspaces.
2. **Provenance-aware matcher & metadata adoption**:
  - Updated `findDiscoveredPluginMcpServer` and its call sites in `mcpCustomizationController.ts` and `copilotAgent.ts` to accept `sourcePlugin?: string` and reject declarations where `sourcePlugin` conflicts with the plugin identity or child metadata.
  - In `McpCustomizationController._buildTopLevel`, when incompatible plugin discovery metadata is present, it is stripped first via `withCustomizationDiscoveryMeta(existing?._meta, undefined)`, and any newly matched child declaration metadata from the new plugin is cleanly merged on top (`baseMeta = discovered ? { ...existingMeta, ...discovered._meta } : existingMeta`).
  - The newly matched declaration's source range is adopted without being blocked by prior incompatibility.
3. **Stale configuration URI prevention**:
  - Avoided falling back to `existing?.uri` when provenance changes; configuration URIs fall back directly to `this._mintTopLevelId(serverName)` unless an explicit `provenance.sourceUri` or compatible `discovered?.uri` is provided.
4. **Customization discovery meta helper**:
  - Extended `withCustomizationDiscoveryMeta` with overloads supporting `discovery: undefined` to cleanly strip the discovery metadata key while preserving unrelated metadata entries.

### How it was tested

- Added unit regression tests in `<blob>.test.ts`:
  - `late SDK plugin discovery rejects a different-plugin runtime server`
  - `transitioning provenance from plugin to user/workspace/builtin discards adopted plugin discovery without losing unrelated metadata`
  - `transitioning provenance from plugin A to plugin B merges B discovery metadata and range`
  - `transitioning runtime-only user server to builtin without sourceUri resets uri to minted id`
- Added unit regression tests in `<blob>.test.ts`:
  - `preserves owned enablement after adopting unowned disable at global scope`
  - `preserves owned enablement after adopting unowned disable at workspace scope`
- Added integration regression test in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`:
  - `preserves scoped host disable across late plugin discovery and ownership adoption with real enablement service` (covering disable -> adopt -> enable)
- Verified all 52 tests in `mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` pass cleanly (0 failures).
- Verified all 50 tests in `agentHostCustomizationEnablementService.test.ts` pass cleanly (0 failures).
- Verified all 16 tests in `copilotAgent.test.ts` discovered SDK customizations pass cleanly (0 failures).
- Verified full TypeScript compilation (`npm run compile-client`) passes with 0 errors.
- Verified ESLint clean on all touched files with 0 errors and 0 warnings.

### Risks

Low. The changes strictly target MCP servers whose provenance transitions or whose ownership is reconciled late from SDK plugin discovery. Write normalization only checks same-scope unowned fallbacks to ensure user-directed re-enablement is not pruned as a duplicate of default values.

title: build: clear package feed credentials once dependencies are installed
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

`NuGetAuthenticate@1` sets `VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN` as a regular, non-secret pipeline variable, so every later step in the job gets its access token in its environment. On macOS, `PipAuthenticate@1` does the same with the token inside `PIP_INDEX_URL`. Our tests write their environment into log files, crash dumps capture it too, and we publish both as pipeline artifacts.

Only a few steps need the token, so this clears the variables right after them:

- **Linux, macOS and Windows setup templates** (compile, test and sign jobs): after `Install dependencies`, which installs Foundry Local from the NuGet feed and, on macOS, `setuptools` from the Python feed. The macOS step clears both variables. These steps run in every build, so they can't fall out of sync with the conditions of the sign-in steps.
- **Dictation runtime** (publish runs only): after `Dictation runtime: build + upload`, which signs in to NuGet again for its ONNX downloads.
- **Quality checks**: after `Install dependencies`.
- **Sanity tests on Windows arm64**: after `Install SignTool (Windows ARM64)`.

Each new step uses `condition: always()`, so it also runs when an earlier step failed and later `succeededOrFailed()` steps still run.

The Alpine, Web, Windows API scan and node_modules jobs also sign in to a feed, but they run no tests, so this PR leaves them unchanged.

### Validation

- Every changed file parses with `js-yaml`, and the pre-commit hygiene check passed.
- Azure DevOps pipeline preview, which expands all templates without running anything, for `main` and this branch, with `VSCODE_BUILD_TYPE` set to `Product` and to `CI`:

  ```sh
  curl -X POST "<url>" \
  -d '{"previewRun":true,"resources":{"repositories":{"self":{"refName":"refs/heads/alexdima/clear-nuget-token-before-tests"}}},"templateParameters":{"VSCODE_BUILD_TYPE":"CI"}}'
  ```

  All four expand. A step counts as cleared only when its script resets the variable. Counting statically, without runtime conditions, these are the steps whose names mention tests (test, smoke, integration, sanity) that run while a token is set:

  | `VSCODE_BUILD_TYPE` | `main` | This branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Product` | 170, 50 of them with `PIP_INDEX_URL` | 0 |
  | `CI` | 168, 50 of them with `PIP_INDEX_URL` | 0 |

  After setup, only the jobs without tests listed above still hold a token.

Not run yet: a real product build. To test it, queue definition 111 on this branch with `VSCODE_PUBLISH=false`. Then check that the clear steps succeed, that installs still work, and that searching the log and crash-dump artifacts for `eyJ`, which is how these tokens start, finds nothing.

Follow-up to #344959 and #345067.

This removes the **AML** (Azure ML) results mode from the Copilot simulation workbench, plus everything only that mode used. No product code, simulation tests, cache recordings or CI gates change.

**25 files changed (20 insertions, 1,309 deletions).** All 20 insertions are existing lines rewritten without their AML part.

## Why AML is dead here
- The mode only displayed results that a separate download step placed in `extensions/copilot/test/aml/out`. Nothing in this repository produces that folder.
- The AML jobs and their tooling moved out of the extension before it was open-sourced. They clone the archived `microsoft/vscode-copilot-chat` repository, not this one, and their schedule still lists test configurations that were deleted when those tests moved to MSBench in October 2025.
- The five AML-only workbench files haven't changed since the June 2025 import, apart from the repo-wide lint rule rollout.
- No open PR touches the removed code: I checked all 3,060 open PRs, plus the recently pushed branches of this year's workbench contributors. Two open PRs edit config files changed here, #214051 (`.eslint-ignore`) and #336098 (`.esbuild.mts`), but on lines that aren't adjacent to these edits.

## What's removed
- **The mode itself:** the AML run provider, results parser and run resolver (`stores/amlSimulations.ts`, `amlResults.ts`, `resolvedAMLRun.ts`), the mode toolbar and run picker, and the "AML" entry in the mode picker.
- **UI only the AML results could populate:**
  - the scorecards (`scorecard.tsx`, `scorecardByLanguage.tsx`) and their CSS
  - the error comparison view and its CSS, plus its diagnostics fallback in `testRun.tsx`
  - the language line in `testView.tsx`
  - the "Open In VS Code Insiders" button. Its input path was never set, so it couldn't render even in AML mode.
- **Plumbing only those used:**

  - the `allLanguageIds` getter
  - the three filters only the AML toolbar used

- **Config:** the `test/aml/out` entries in `.gitignore`, `tsconfig.json`, `.eslint-ignore` and the esbuild watcher, and the `AML_OUTPUT_PATH` constant.

## Behavior
- The mode picker now offers Local, NES External and Adhoc Request.
- A stored AML selection from an older build falls back to Local, through the existing sanitization in `simulationWorkbench.tsx`. `TestSource.NesExternal` keeps its stored value (`3`).

## Deliberately kept
- The notebook scenarios named after the AML runs that found them (for example `(AML-10-35) can not access member`) are live CI scenarios, so they keep their names.
- `script/analyzeEdits.ts` analyzes MSBench output and only has a leftover `amlOutPath` parameter name. #341819 also edits it.

## Validation

  - switching between the three modes works

  - there were no page or console errors

title: list: render bottom-anchored content that replaces every row only at its final position
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Switching between sessions in the Agents window renders, measures and throws away a full screen of chat rows on every click. This PR removes that work: across the measurement sessions below, **session switch click → next paint drops by 88–112 ms (22–27%)**.

**Builds on #345176 (merged)**, which restores a scrolled-up chat by row. This PR relies on it; see *Restoring a scrolled-up position* below.

There is no issue for this yet. It came out of profiling session switching in Insiders (`ea8056df`), where each click was a single 390–510 ms task. Most of that task was rendering the chat transcript.

## Why it happens

When a session is opened, `ChatView._loadChat` clears the widget (`ChatWidget.setModel(undefined)`), then binds the new model in the same task. Clearing the list happens while it's anchored at the bottom, and applying the empty list's scroll height scrolls it to the top. Binding the new model calls `ChatListWidget.refresh()`, which runs `setChildren` inside `withScrollAnchorAtBottom` again. Then:

1. `ListView._splice` renders the new rows at the current position, the top: the **oldest** messages of the transcript.
2. `_rerender` measures them, re-anchors to the bottom, renders the **newest** messages as measurement rows and promotes them, and discards the rows it rendered first.

Chat rows are expensive: markdown, DOMPurify, code block editors, tool and terminal parts. Instrumenting `ListView` during a switch in the benchmark below shows `main` rendering 9 transcript rows per switch, 4 of which are thrown away within the same task. With this change, it renders the 5 rows that are shown.

## Fix

These changes apply only to lists with dynamic heights that are anchored at the bottom. Today the chat transcript is the only one.

- **`ListView._splice`**: when the splice replaces every row, there are no rows to keep in place, so it renders directly at the bottom position computed from the new content.
- **`ListView.onScroll`**: while anchored, it renders at the bottom. `_rerender` ends with `setScrollTop(bottom)`, which first applies the deferred scroll height. That emits a scroll event that still carries the stale position, and rendering it would re-render the top rows. Lists with dynamic heights re-anchor right after rendering anyway (`_rerender`), so the final state is the same as before; only the throwaway intermediate render is skipped.
- **`ListView._rerender`**: when it converges on the bottom while anchored, it moves the rows container there itself before setting the scroll position. A replacement that measures to the previous content height leaves the scroll position unchanged, so setting it emits no scroll event that would move the rows from their estimated offset (found in review).

Partial splices, such as follow-up requests and streaming, still render at the current position and keep their existing rows. Lists without dynamic heights are unchanged.

## Restoring a scrolled-up position (found in review)

Review found one regression. Scroll up near the start of a session, switch to a session that is at its bottom, then switch back: the first session reopened about a screen lower than where you left it.

Hosts restore a saved `scrollTop` right after binding the chat again, and rows that haven't rendered yet have estimated heights. On `main`, the throwaway render of the oldest rows happened to measure them before the restore, so a position near the start landed where it was saved. With this change, those rows are still estimates.

#345176 restores a scrolled-up chat by the row at the top of the viewport and the offset into it, so a restore no longer depends on which rows have been measured. Measured in the real Agents window: scroll a session to a position, switch to another session and back, then compare the row at the top of the viewport and the offset into it.

| Scrolled down from the top | `main` | this PR alone | this PR on top of #345176 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 150 px | same place | 229 px lower | same place |
| 400 px | 4 px lower | request 2 instead of request 1 | same place |
| 800 px | 8 px lower | request 3 instead of response 1 | same place |
| 1,500 px | 38 px lower | response 4 instead of response 3 | same place |
| 3,000 px | request 8 instead of request 9 | 52 px higher | same place |

Review also suggested making the fast path opt-in, for hosts that know a chat opens at its bottom. With #345176, restores are exact either way, so the fast path stays on for every bind.

## Measurements

Environment and method:
- Code OSS dev build with Electron 43.8.3, on an Apple M5 Pro (macOS 26.7).
- The real desktop Agents window, connected to the scripted mock agent host (`agentHostServerMain.js --enable-mock-agent`).
- 4 sessions with 16 turns each: code blocks, terminal commands, tool calls, subagents, reasoning, lists and tables.
- Each run relaunches the window, opens every session once, then clicks through the session list 24 times.
- `main` runs and runs with this change are interleaved: 3 + 3 runs, 72 switches each.
- Timings come from Event Timing (`click` duration, i.e. until the next paint) and Long Animation Frames.

Final code (this PR on top of #345176), compared with #345176 alone:

| Per session switch | #345176 alone, median (p90) | this PR on top, median (p90) | Δ median |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Click → next paint | 392 ms (408) | **288 ms** (304) | **−104 ms (−27%)** |
| Click event processing | 347 ms (365) | 250 ms (262) | −97 ms (−28%) |
| Long animation frame duration | 365 ms (392) | 268 ms (285) | −97 ms (−27%) |
| Transcript rows / DOM nodes added | 10 / 1,259 | 7 / 1,141 | −3 / −118 |

#345176 doesn't change switching to a chat that opens at its bottom: it only saves a scroll anchor when the transcript is scrolled up, and alone it adds the same rows and nodes per switch, in the same time, as `main` did in the earlier sessions.

Earlier sessions measured the same `ListView` change against `main`: 392 → 304 ms (−22%) based on `ce233327`, and 408 → 296 ms (−27%) based on `e219e7c0`. Every timing difference is significant in every session (Mann–Whitney U, p < 0.0001). A CPU profile of 8 switches puts transcript rendering inside `ChatWidget.setModel` at **238 ms → 126 ms** per switch. In a narrower chat column, where 5 rows fill the screen instead of 7–10, an earlier comparison gave 336 → 208 ms (−38%).

Correctness checks, in every session:
- After every switch (288 in total), the transcript ends at its last row with the same 28 px bottom gap as `main`, and there are no gaps between rows.
- Screenshots of the transcript are pixel-identical between `main` and this PR.
- While follow-ups stream (a long-running response, a tool call, a subagent and reasoning), the transcript stayed pinned to its last row in every sample taken every 100 ms, exactly as on `main`.

## Tests

- New `ListView` test: content that replaces every row while anchored renders only its final rows. A partial append keeps the rows already in view.
- New `ListView` test: a list without dynamic heights keeps its rendered rows at its own scroll position while anchored. This is a regression guard for the gating.
- New `ListView` test (from review): an anchored replacement whose rows are estimated at half their measured height, and that ends at the previous content height, still shows its bottom. It fails without the `_rerender` change and passes on `main`.
- Adjusted `ChatListWidget` › *keeps one-line and two-line sticky requests stable through push-out*. The test read `getElementTop(secondRequest)` right after the initial `refresh()`. That only worked because `main` incidentally rendered, and therefore measured, the oldest rows in that refresh. With this change, rows above the viewport keep their estimated height until they render, just as rows in the middle of a long transcript already do on `main`. The test now renders the first exchange before reading the position. It passes on both `main` and this branch.
- Restoring scrolled-up positions is covered by #345176's `ChatListWidget` test, which also passes on top of this PR.

Validation (re-run on the current head, on top of #345176):
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/base/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 767 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/browser/**/*.test.js"`: 15,049 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/sessions/**/test/**/*.test.js"`: 9,370 passing
- `npm run typecheck-client` and `npm run eslint` on the changed files: clean

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window with a few long sessions.
2. Click between the sessions. Switching should be noticeably quicker.
3. Each transcript should still open scrolled to its last message.
4. Send a follow-up in a session and confirm the transcript stays pinned to the bottom while the response streams.
5. Scroll up anywhere in a session, switch to another session and back. It should reopen exactly where you left it.

title: Git: avoid promisor ref sorting fetches and orphan processes in partial clones
body:
Fixes #345108

### Summary of Changes

1. **Model Refresh Ref Sorting**:
  In `Repository._updateModelState()`, explicitly query refs with `{ sort: 'alphabetically' }` instead of inheriting `branchSortOrder` (`committerdate`). Internal model state `this._refs` only serves `historyProvider` (which sorts alphabetically anyway) and deprecated `api.state.refs`, so peeling commit dates was never needed during background status refreshes.

2. **Partial Clone Detection & Sorting Guard**:
  - Added `initIsPartialClone()` and `isPartialClone` on `Repository` (inspecting local configs `extensions.partialclone`, `remote.*.promisor`, and `remote.*.partialclonefilter`).
  - In `Repository.getRefs()`, if `isPartialClone` is active, date-based sort orders (`committerdate` / `creatordate`) are automatically downgraded to `'alphabetically'` when querying unrestricted refs (e.g. without pattern or when including remote refs). Queries specifically bounded to local heads (`refs/heads`) continue to sort by date.

3. **Child Process Tracking & Cleanup**:
  - Added child process tracking to `Git` class so running child processes are killed on `Git.dispose()` and extension deactivation, preventing orphaned background Git processes when the extension host exits.
  - Cancel and dispose `updateModelStateCancellationTokenSource` in `Repository.dispose()`.

4. **Tests**:
  - Added unit test suite for `isPatternRestrictedToLocalHeads` in `extensions/git/src/test/git.test.ts`.

title: chat: add M365 rollout setting and Agent Host plumbing
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

## Summary

Tracks microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10447, part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10422.

- Register `chat.agentHost.copilot.m365.enabled` as an application-scoped, default-off, advanced/experimental setting with startup ExP metadata and restart-required wording.
- Mirror the requested value into the typed, default-off Copilot Agent Host root key `m365Enabled` using the existing configuration transport.
- Cover registration, host schema and typed reads, default/explicit/invalid values, target scopes, and reconnect forwarding.

## Stack and scope

This is the foundational `copilot-m365/rollout` layer of a `gh stack` stack rooted on `main`. Credential integration and subsequent account-choice work will build on top of it.

The first layer is tracked locally by `gh stack`; GitHub requires at least two PRs to create the stack object. Submitting the next layer will link the PRs into that GitHub stack.

The host value is **requested configuration**, which is mirrored live and refreshed on reconnect. It is not the startup-effective runtime mode. The first consumer must implement shared startup-effective capture before using the flag. This PR adds no credential acquisition, SDK update, account switching, inference behavior, or experiment rollout.

title: Fix authentication provider cleanup when an extension host stops
body:
Related to #343316.

Authentication providers can remain in `AuthenticationService` after their owning `MainThreadAuthentication` customer is disposed, leaving discovery to reuse a provider backed by the old RPC proxy. The customer already is disposed when its extension host stops; the missing cleanup is the service's independent provider registration.

Tie provider cleanup to customer disposal, preserve same-ID replacements owned by another host, and suppress unregister notifications back to the stopping host. Persisted OAuth registrations and sessions are left intact.

Regression coverage includes host replacement, cross-host isolation, late unregister calls, and registration/session event behavior. The new production `RPCProtocol` test models the manager's RPC-then-customer teardown order, verifies actual cancellation through the old proxy, and registers a replacement host against the same authentication service. It does not start a real extension-host process.

Validation for `ecaef8a5b708092acb0dff35fc8ea3323aa81d5f` passed in [this isolated fork run](<url>): changed-file hygiene and ESLint, full client typecheck/transpilation, and the official Electron suites (12 `MainThreadAuthentication` tests and 24 `AuthenticationService` tests, plus one clean-state harness check per invocation; JUnit totals 13 and 25, no failures/errors/skips).

The same RPC regression was then run with only the production `mainThreadAuthentication.ts` replaced by its unpatched version from `cd2259bdf72ec7421e70ae80999ceb46f8bd86fe`. It failed at provider discovery: actual `dynamic-provider`, expected `undefined`, after the real cancellation assertion had passed. [Logs and JUnit artifact](<url>). The validation workflow stays on a separate fork branch, not in this PR.

This establishes the component-level lifecycle defect, not the original live Datadog OAuth/Add Folder to Workspace scenario. I have not reproduced that end-to-end flow or confirmed this resolves all of #343316.

title: Avoid reading large agent host files when opening Changes
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #343103

## Problem

With a remote agent host, opening **Changes** in the Agents window for a repository with large untracked files (packet captures in the report) makes the agent host read each of those files in full and send it to the window as Base64. Its memory climbs by gigabytes until V8 runs out of heap and the process aborts, and reconnecting reopens Changes and crashes it again.

Reproduced locally with two 150 MiB and one 30 MiB untracked binary file: on `main` the agent host received a whole-file read request for all three files (330 MiB) as soon as Changes opened, its working set grew from about 164 MB to about 2.5 GB, and it crashed with `JavaScript heap out of memory` in 3 of 3 runs. With this change it reads none of them, peaks at about 208 MB, and does not crash (3 of 3 runs).

## Root cause

Opening Changes opens the session's Changes editor, a multi diff editor that resolves a text model for every changed file up front:

1. `SessionChangesEditor` resolves the input's view model when it is shown ([sessionChangesEditor.ts#L385-L386](<url>)), and `MultiDiffEditorInput._createModel` calls `ITextModelService.createModelReference` for both sides of every item ([multiDiffEditorInput.ts#L225-L230](<url>)).
2. For a file-backed resource that resolves a text file model ([textModelResolverService.ts#L75-L77](<url>)). The text file service finds out that a file is binary from its first bytes and then cancels the read ([textFileService.ts#L224-L244](<url>)), but that only saves work when the file system can stream: for a provider without `FileReadStream` or `FileOpenReadWriteClose` the file service reads the whole file first ([fileService.ts#L624-L630](<url>), [#L713](<url>)).
3. The agent host file system (`vscode-agent-host` URIs) only has `FileReadWrite` ([agentHostFileSystemProvider.ts#L173-L177](<url>)), and `readFile` asks the host for the whole file with `resourceRead`, Base64-encoded ([#L493-L496](<url>)). So detecting that an untracked capture is binary costs the host a full read, a Base64 string of the whole file and a message carrying it, for every such file at once.

The text and diff editors avoid this with a large file limit checked against a stat before reading ([resourceEditorInput.ts#L190-L209](<url>)), but the multi diff editor doesn't apply it, and `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit` gives agent host files the local limit of 1024 MB ([files.ts#L1632-L1659](<url>)) although they are transferred like remote files.

## Fix

- `MultiDiffEditorInput`: for each side that comes from a file system that can only read whole files, stat it first (one `resourceResolve` round trip for the agent host) and compare the size with the large file limit that text editors use (`workbench.editorLargeFileConfirmation` when set, otherwise `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit`). When a side is above it, neither side is loaded and the item shows the existing binary placeholder with the label **File is too large to show**. File systems that stream reads (local disk, `vscode-remote`) are unchanged, since binary detection already stops after the first bytes there.
  - A side that already has a resolved text file model, such as a file that is open and dirty in an editor, is not checked: loading it reuses that model without reading the file, so it is shown, saved and reverted as before. If the other side of the item is too large, the item still shows the placeholder, and saving or reverting the multi diff editor still saves or reverts the item's dirty sides.
  - The check activates the file system provider first, as loading the model does, so a file system that an extension registers when it activates (for example when a multi diff editor is restored) is checked on the first load too. Untitled, in-memory and content provider resources are not read from a file system and are not checked.
- `getLargeFileConfirmationLimit`: agent host files (new `Schemas.vscodeAgentHost`, which `AGENT_HOST_SCHEME` now uses) get the remote limit of 10 MB. This also means a text editor opened on an agent host file over 10 MB asks before loading it, as for Remote-SSH files.

Deliberately unchanged:

- Files under the limit are still read in full to detect that they are binary (in the report, four captures between 1.9 and 5.4 MB, 12.8 MB together). The Base64 encoder's memory amplification for those reads is addressed separately by #339434, which complements this change.
- The original side of a modified tracked file is a git blob content reference without a size, so it is still loaded unless the working tree side is too large.
- No protocol, agent host or Changes view changes.

## Before / after

Both recordings: an Agents window connected through `chat.remoteAgentHosts` to a local agent host on a 2 GiB V8 heap, serving a repository with two 150 MiB and one 30 MiB untracked binary file and one edited README. The session is opened with Changes closed, then Changes is opened. The readout in the bottom-left corner is the scenario's own instrument: the agent host's working set, sampled from outside the process, and how many of the three large files the host was asked to read.

### Before

![Before: opening Changes leaves the Changes editor loading while the agent host's memory climbs past 1.7 GB, then the host process exits out of memory and the window shows Reconnecting](<url>)

### After

![After: opening Changes lists the three captures as "File is too large to show" next to the README diff, and the agent host stays at about 160 MB with no large file read](<url>)

## Measurements

What opening Changes costs the agent host, from a fresh agent host and a fresh Agents window per run. Reads were counted by wrapping `AgentService.resourceRead` in the agent host process. The working set was sampled every 200 ms from outside the process (Windows `Get-Process`; the peak is `PeakWorkingSet64`), because the host's event loop is blocked while it encodes a large file. Windows, Node.js 24.22.1, Code - OSS dev build with `VSCODE_DEV_DISABLE_DISPOSABLE_TRACKING=1`; the agent host is this build's `agentHostServerMain` with the scripted mock agent and `--max-old-space-size=2048` (a 2,240 MB V8 heap limit, close to the ~2 GiB limit in the report).

Two 150 MiB `.pcapng` files and one 30 MiB `.qmdl` file of random bytes, untracked, plus one edited README:

| | `main` @ `cd2259b` (3 runs) | This PR (3 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Whole-file reads of the three large files requested by opening Changes | 3 per run (330 MiB) | none |
| Agent host working set with the session open and Changes closed | 163–164 MB | 164 MB |
| Agent host peak working set after opening Changes | 2,490–2,523 MB | 207–208 MB (the process's lifetime peak) |
| Agent host process crashed (`JavaScript heap out of memory`) | 3 of 3 | 0 of 3 |

The eight untracked files from the report, with the same sizes (358 MB in total, from 1.9 MB to 146 MB), one run each:

| | `main` @ `cd2259b` | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Untracked files read in full when Changes opens | all 8 (358 MB requested) | the 4 under 10 MB (12.8 MB); the 4 over 10 MB are not read |
| Agent host peak working set | 2,490 MB | 723 MB |
| Agent host process crashed | yes | no (V8 heap peak 373 MB of 2,240 MB) |

These numbers are from the first version of this change, on `main` @ `cd2259b`, which is still its base. The later review fixes only change what happens for files that are already open in an editor and for file systems registered on demand; neither applies to these untracked files on the already-connected agent host, so the numbers were not measured again.

## How to test

1. Run a dev build of this branch and an agent host on a machine that has a git repository with a few large untracked binary files (for example `node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync('capture.pcapng', require('crypto').randomBytes(150*1024*1024))"` twice with different names) and one small edited file.
2. Connect the Agents window to that agent host (Remote-SSH, or `chat.remoteAgentHosts` pointing at a local agent host server), and open a session whose working directory is that repository, with Changes closed.
3. Open **Changes**. The large files appear with **File is too large to show**, the small file's diff appears, and the agent host's memory stays flat. On `main`, the agent host's memory climbs by several times the files' size and, with a 2 GiB heap, the agent host crashes.

<details><summary>Automated repro scenario</summary>

Start the instrumented agent host from the repository root with `node --max-old-space-size=2048 mockhost.mjs` (keep its stdin open; env `BS_STATUS` sets where it writes its read log and memory samples), create a session in the test repository with `node seed.mjs 8996 <repo>`, open an Agents window with `chat.remoteAgentHosts` set to `ws://127.0.0.1:8996` and `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable` enabled, then run the scenario over CDP: `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>`. It fails on `main` and passes with this PR.

```js
// Repro: opening Changes in the Agents window must not make the agent host read large untracked files in full.
// Runs over CDP against an Agents window connected (chat.remoteAgentHosts) to the instrumented agent host in
// mockhost.mjs, which serves a git repository with three large untracked binaries (two 150 MiB .pcapng files and a
// 30 MiB .qmdl file) and one small tracked change (README.md). The host records every resourceRead and samples its
// own memory into BS_STATUS; a small overlay in the window shows the host's memory while the scenario runs.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');

const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-changes-oom-status.json');
const LARGE_FILES = ['capture-1.pcapng', 'capture-2.pcapng', 'modem.qmdl'];
const ALL_FILES = ['README.md', ...LARGE_FILES];
const MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB = 256;
const MiB = 1024 * 1024;

const readStatusOnce = () => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(STATUS, 'utf8')); } catch { return undefined; } };
// The host rewrites the status file every 100 ms, so a read can see a partial file: retry briefly.
const readStatus = () => {
	for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
		const s = readStatusOnce();
		if (s) { return s; }
		const until = Date.now() + 25;
		while (Date.now() < until) { /* wait */ }
	}
	return undefined;
};
const isAlive = pid => { try { process.kill(pid, 0); return true; } catch { return false; } };
const largeReads = s => (s?.reads ?? []).filter(r => r.uri.startsWith('file:') && LARGE_FILES.some(f => r.uri.endsWith('/' + f)));
const mb = n => `${Math.round(n)} MB`;

let baseline;
let overlayTimer;

async function waitFor(fn, timeoutMs, intervalMs = 200) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	let value;
	while (Date.now() < end) {
		value = await fn();
		if (value) { return value; }
		await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
	}
	return value;
}

// This repro needs no Copilot account: dismiss the sign-in prompt, which can open a few seconds after the window starts.
async function dismissSignIn(page) {
	for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
		const cont = page.getByText('Continue Without Signing In');
		if (await cont.count()) { await cont.first().click(); await page.waitForTimeout(800); continue; }
		if (!await page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-dialog-box, .monaco-dialog-modal-block, .sessions-signing-in-dialog-modal-block'))) { break; }
		await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
		await page.waitForTimeout(800);
	}
}

// Small read-only readout of the agent host's memory in the bottom-left corner (the scenario's own instrument). It
// prefers BS_MEM, the working set sampled from outside the host, which keeps updating while the host's event loop is busy.
function startOverlay(page) {
	const update = async () => {
		const s = readStatusOnce();
		if (!s) { return; }
		let memMB = s.current.rssMB;
		try { memMB = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.BS_MEM, 'utf8')).samples.at(-1).wsMB; } catch { }
		const alive = isAlive(s.pid) && !s.exitedAt;
		const reads = largeReads(s);
		const text = alive
  ? `Agent host memory: ${mb(memMB)} \u00b7 large files read: ${reads.length}`
  : `Agent host process exited (out of memory) \u00b7 large files read: ${reads.length}`;
		await page.evaluate(t => {
  let el = document.getElementById('bs-host-readout');
  if (!el) {
  el = document.createElement('div');
  el.id = 'bs-host-readout';
  el.style.cssText = 'position:fixed;left:12px;bottom:10px;z-index:100000;padding:4px 10px;border-radius:4px;font:12px var(--monaco-monospace-font, monospace);background:rgba(0,0,0,.75);color:#fff;pointer-events:none';
  document.body.appendChild(el);
  }
  el.textContent = t;
		}, text).catch(() => { });
	};
	overlayTimer = setInterval(update, 250);
	overlayTimer.unref?.();
	return update();
}

const changesEntries = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.multiDiffEntry')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent)
	.map(e => ({
		// The title also holds the +added/-removed stats; keep only the file label.
		name: (e.querySelector('.title.modified .label-name')?.textContent ?? e.querySelector('.title.modified')?.textContent ?? '').trim(),
		placeholder: (() => { const p = e.querySelector('.binary-file-placeholder'); return p && getComputedStyle(p).display !== 'none' ? p.querySelector('span')?.textContent.trim() : undefined; })(),
	})));

module.exports = {
	id: 'changes-large-untracked-files',
	title: 'Opening Changes does not read large untracked files on the agent host',
	source: '<url>',
	stepPauseMs: 1200,
	steps: [
		{
  id: 'open-session', title: 'Open the session with Changes closed', async run({ page }) {
  const s = readStatus();
  if (!s || !isAlive(s.pid)) { throw new Error(`The agent host is not running (status ${STATUS})`); }
  await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].some(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('hello')), null, { timeout: 60000 });
  await dismissSignIn(page);
  await page.locator('.monaco-list-row', { hasText: 'hello' }).first().click();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-response')].some(e => e.textContent.includes('Hello, world!')), null, { timeout: 30000 });
  await dismissSignIn(page);
  await startOverlay(page);
  if ((await changesEntries(page)).length) { throw new Error('The Changes editor is already open'); }
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  const now = readStatus();
  if (largeReads(now).length) { throw new Error(`The large files were read before Changes was opened: ${largeReads(now).length}`); }
  baseline = { rssMB: now.current.rssMB, heapUsedMB: now.current.heapUsedMB, reads: now.reads.length };
  return `Session open, Changes closed; agent host RSS ${mb(baseline.rssMB)}, V8 heap ${mb(baseline.heapUsedMB)}, no large file read yet`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'open-changes', title: 'Open Changes', async run({ page }) {
  fs.writeFileSync(STATUS + '.mark', JSON.stringify({ mark: 'open-changes' }));
  await page.waitForTimeout(300);
  await page.locator('a.codicon-diff-multiple').first().click();
  // Wait until every changed file is listed, or the agent host is gone.
  const outcome = await waitFor(async () => {
  const s = readStatus();
  if (s && (!isAlive(s.pid) || s.exitedAt)) { return 'host-exited'; }
  const names = (await changesEntries(page)).map(e => e.name);
  return ALL_FILES.every(f => names.some(n => n.startsWith(f))) ? 'listed' : undefined;
  }, 60000, 250);
  // Keep watching for a few seconds so late reads and the memory peak are captured.
  await page.waitForTimeout(4000);
  const entries = await changesEntries(page);
  return `After opening Changes: ${outcome ?? 'timed out'}; entries ${JSON.stringify(entries)}`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'check-host', title: 'The agent host read no large file and stayed within its memory budget', async run({ page }) {
  const s = readStatus();
  const reads = largeReads(s);
  const readBytes = reads.reduce((sum, r) => sum + (r.bytes ?? 0), 0);
  const alive = isAlive(s.pid) && !s.exitedAt;
  const peak = s.mark?.label === 'open-changes' ? s.peak : undefined;
  const summary = `large-file reads ${reads.length} (${reads.map(r => r.uri.split('/').pop()).join(', ') || 'none'}; ${Math.round(readBytes / MiB)} MiB returned), `
  + `host RSS ${mb(baseline.rssMB)} -> peak ${peak ? mb(peak.rssMB) : '?'}, V8 heap peak ${peak ? mb(peak.heapUsedMB) : '?'} (limit ${s.heapLimitMB} MB), host ${alive ? 'alive' : 'EXITED'}`;
  clearInterval(overlayTimer);
  const problems = [];
  if (!alive) { problems.push('the agent host process exited'); }
  if (reads.length) { problems.push(`${reads.length} large untracked files were read in full`); }
  if (peak && peak.rssMB - baseline.rssMB > MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB) { problems.push(`agent host RSS grew by ${mb(peak.rssMB - baseline.rssMB)} (budget ${MAX_RSS_GROWTH_MB} MB)`); }
  const entries = await changesEntries(page);
  const missing = ALL_FILES.filter(f => !entries.some(e => e.name.startsWith(f)));
  if (missing.length) { problems.push(`Changes does not list ${missing.join(', ')}`); }
  const notPlaceholder = LARGE_FILES.filter(f => !entries.find(e => e.name.startsWith(f))?.placeholder);
  if (!missing.length && notPlaceholder.length) { problems.push(`no placeholder for ${notPlaceholder.join(', ')}`); }
  if (problems.length) { throw new Error(`${problems.join('; ')}. ${summary}`); }
  return `${summary}; entries ${JSON.stringify(entries)}`;
  }
		},
	]
};
```

</details>

<details><summary>Instrumented agent host (mockhost.mjs)</summary>

```js
// Standalone Agent Host server (from a built VS Code checkout's out/) with the scripted mock agent, instrumented to
// show what opening Changes in the Agents window costs the host.
// - Wraps AgentService.resourceRead: records every read (uri, encoding, bytes returned, duration) in BS_STATUS.
// - Samples process.memoryUsage() every 100 ms and records the peak RSS and V8 heap since the last mark.
