title: Apply agent notebook edits to the open notebook instead of failing
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #343214
Refs #344849

## Problem

When an agent host session (Copilot SDK / agent host) asks to change a Jupyter notebook, the Copilot notebook edit tool always fails with `Invalid input, no stream`. The agent then falls back to rewriting the `.ipynb` file on disk. If the notebook is open with unsaved changes (for example after the user typed in a cell, or after running cells, which changes outputs), the editor never shows the agent's change, and saving the notebook removes it again: either through the "content of the file is newer" prompt, where **Overwrite** looks like the right answer because the editor never showed the change, or silently when the file size didn't change. That is the "edits disappear after initially appearing on disk" behavior in #344849.

## Root cause

- The tool only works with a chat response stream. It reads it from `promptContext`, which is only set by [`resolveInput`](<url>), and it [throws `Invalid input, no stream`](<url>) without one. Only Copilot Chat's own tool loops call `resolveInput`.
- Agent host sessions run client tools through [`ILanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool`](<url>), which ends in the tool's `invoke` without `resolveInput`, so there is never a stream. `editNotebook` is offered to those sessions through the [Jupyter Notebooks client tool set](<url>), next to `runNotebookCell` and `getNotebookSummary`, which don't need a stream. So the agent can run cells (making the notebook dirty) and read the in-memory notebook, but can't edit it.
- When the agent writes the file instead, a dirty notebook is [never reloaded](<url>), and the save conflict only offers [Overwrite or Revert](<url>) (no Compare, unlike text files). The agent host review that reconciles text files after agent writes [skips notebooks](<url>).

## Fix

In `editNotebookTool.tsx`, when there is no chat response stream, the tool now collects the same notebook edits (insert or delete cells) and cell text edits it would have sent to the stream into a `WorkspaceEdit` and applies it with `IWorkspaceService.applyEdit`. The edit lands in the open notebook model, next to any unsaved changes, so the editor shows it right away and a normal save keeps it. If the edit can't be applied, the tool fails with a clear error instead of reporting success. The result also tells the model that the edit is in the open notebook and may not be saved yet, so it shouldn't rewrite the `.ipynb` on disk.

Local Copilot Chat is unchanged: when `resolveInput` provided a stream for this request, the edits still go through it (chat editing session, Keep/Undo). The no-stream path follows the same pattern as the built-in rename tool, which applies its edits with the bulk edit service when there is no chat context.

The tool also no longer reuses a prompt context from another request. There is a single `EditNotebookTool` instance ([created once](<url>) and [registered once](<url>)), and `resolveInput` stores the prompt context, including its stream, on it until the next local tool call. Without a check, an agent session call after an earlier Copilot Chat request would use that request's finished stream and fail with `Response stream has been closed` (the new unit tests reproduce this on `main`). The tool now uses the stored context only when its `requestId` matches the invocation's `chatRequestId`. The Copilot Chat tool loop passes the same value to both: it calls [`resolveInput` with the prompt context](<url>) whose [`requestId`](<url>) it also passes as [`chatRequestId`](<url>) (the turn id, [always set](<url>)), and VS Code carries `chatRequestId` [to the main thread](<url>) and [back to the tool](<url>). Agent sessions don't set `chatRequestId`, and other chat requests have their own, so they get the workspace edit path. Inline chat never offers this tool, so requiring a request id doesn't change it.

Not changed, possible follow-ups:
- Edits applied this way are not part of the agent session's edit review or checkpoints and are left unsaved, like the rename tool's fallback.
- Dirty notebooks still don't reload or merge external changes, and the notebook save conflict still has no Compare action. The file service's same-size check is unchanged.

## Before / after

Both recordings use a small test extension that calls the notebook edit tool the way agent sessions do (`vscode.lm.invokeTool('copilot_editNotebook', …)` with no chat stream) and, like the agent, writes the cell into the `.ipynb` on disk if the tool fails. The notebook has an unsaved edit (` # checked`) when the agent adds its cell.

### Before

![Before: the notebook edit tool fails with "Invalid input, no stream", the cell is written to disk but never shows in the editor, saving reports that the file is newer, and after Overwrite the agent's cell is gone](<url>)

### After

![After: the agent's cell appears in the open notebook right away, the save completes without a conflict, and both the agent's cell and the user's edit are kept](<url>)

## How to test

1. In a dev build of this branch, signed in to Copilot (or with a BYOK model, so Copilot's tools are registered), open a folder with a Python `.ipynb` and open it in the notebook editor.
2. Type in a cell so the notebook has unsaved changes.
3. From an agent host session, ask the agent to add a cell to the notebook. Or call the tool directly from an extension: `vscode.lm.invokeTool('copilot_editNotebook', { input: { filePath, editType: 'insert', cellId: 'BOTTOM', newCode: 'print(1)', language: 'python' }, toolInvocationToken: undefined })`.
4. The new cell appears in the open notebook. Save: there's no conflict, and the file on disk has the new cell and your edit.
5. On `main`, step 3 fails with `Invalid input, no stream`.

<details><summary>Automated repro: test extension, workspace and scenario</summary>

Create the workspace with `node reset-ws.cjs <tmp>/nb-edit-proof/ws`, launch Code OSS signed in on that folder with `--extensionDevelopmentPath=<probe-ext folder>`, then run `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>`. It fails on `main` and passes with this PR.

`probe-ext/package.json`

```json
{
	"name": "notebook-edit-tool-probe",
	"displayName": "Notebook edit tool probe",
	"publisher": "bugswarm",
	"version": "0.0.1",
	"engines": { "vscode": "^1.90.0" },
	"main": "./extension.js",
	"activationEvents": ["onStartupFinished"],
	"contributes": {
		"commands": [
  { "command": "notebookEditToolProbe.addCell", "title": "Agent: Add a Cell to the Open Notebook" }
		]
	}
}
```

`probe-ext/extension.js`

```js
// Calls the Copilot notebook edit tool the way agent sessions do: through the tools service,
// without a chat response stream. When the tool fails, it falls back to writing the cell into the
// .ipynb on disk, which is what the agent does in that case.
const vscode = require('vscode');
const fs = require('fs');

const TOOL = 'copilot_editNotebook';
const CODE = 'print("cell added by the agent")';

exports.activate = context => {
	context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand('notebookEditToolProbe.addCell', async () => {
		const notebook = vscode.window.activeNotebookEditor?.notebook;
		if (!notebook) {
  vscode.window.showErrorMessage('Open a notebook first.');
  return;
		}
		try {
  await vscode.lm.invokeTool(TOOL, {
  input: { filePath: notebook.uri.fsPath, editType: 'insert', cellId: 'BOTTOM', newCode: CODE, language: 'python', explanation: 'Add a cell at the end' },
  toolInvocationToken: undefined,
  });
  vscode.window.showInformationMessage('Agent: the notebook edit tool added the cell.');
		} catch (error) {
  const json = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(notebook.uri.fsPath, 'utf8'));
  json.cells.push({ cell_type: 'code', execution_count: null, metadata: {}, outputs: [], source: [CODE] });
  fs.writeFileSync(notebook.uri.fsPath, JSON.stringify(json, null, 1) + '\n');
  vscode.window.showErrorMessage(`Agent: the notebook edit tool failed (${error.message}), so the agent wrote the cell to the file on disk.`);
		}
	}));
};
```

`reset-ws.cjs`

```js
// Writes a fresh two-cell Python notebook into the workspace folder given as the first argument.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const dir = process.argv[2];
fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true });
const notebook = {
	cells: [
		{ cell_type: 'markdown', metadata: {}, source: ['# Sales report'] },
		{ cell_type: 'code', execution_count: null, metadata: {}, outputs: [], source: ['total = 40 + 2\n', 'print(total)'] },
	],
	metadata: {
		kernelspec: { display_name: 'Python 3', language: 'python', name: 'python3' },
		language_info: { name: 'python' },
	},
	nbformat: 4,
	nbformat_minor: 5,
};
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, 'report.ipynb'), JSON.stringify(notebook, null, 1) + '\n');
fs.mkdirSync(path.join(dir, '.vscode'), { recursive: true });
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, '.vscode', 'settings.json'), JSON.stringify({ 'files.autoSave': 'off', 'workbench.activityBar.location': 'hidden', 'workbench.startupEditor': 'none', 'workbench.secondarySideBar.defaultVisibility': 'hidden' }, null, '\t'));
console.log(path.join(dir, 'report.ipynb'));
```

`repro.cjs`

```js
// Agent edits to an open, unsaved notebook land in the editor and survive saving.
//
// Run against a Code OSS window that is signed in to Copilot, opened on the workspace written by
// reset-ws.cjs (os.tmpdir()/nb-edit-proof/ws), with the probe extension in ./probe-ext loaded via
// --extensionDevelopmentPath. The probe's command calls the Copilot notebook edit tool through
// vscode.lm.invokeTool without a chat response stream, which is how agent sessions call it, and, like
// the agent, writes the cell to the .ipynb on disk if the tool fails.
const fs = require('fs');
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');

const NOTEBOOK_FILE = path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'nb-edit-proof', 'ws', 'report.ipynb');
const AGENT_CODE = 'print("cell added by the agent")';
const USER_TEXT = '# checked';

const normalize = text => (text || '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ');

async function notebookCells(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => {
		return [...document.querySelectorAll('.notebookOverlay .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row')]
  .map(row => [...row.querySelectorAll('.view-line')].map(line => line.textContent).join('\n'));
	}).then(cells => cells.map(normalize));
}

async function activeTabIsDirty(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty'));
}

async function waitFor(ctx, predicate, timeoutMs, what) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	for (; ;) {
		const value = await predicate();
		if (value) {
  return value;
		}
		if (Date.now() > end) {
  throw new Error(`Timed out after ${timeoutMs} ms waiting for ${what}`);
		}
		await ctx.sleep(200);
	}
}

module.exports = {
	id: 'agent-notebook-edit-open-dirty',
	title: 'Agent edits to an open, unsaved notebook land in the editor and survive saving',
	source: '<url>',
	stepPauseMs: 1200,
	steps: [
		{
  id: 'S1',
  title: 'The notebook is open with two cells',
  async run(ctx) {
  await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-workbench .part.editor')), 30000, 'the workbench');
  if (!(await ctx.page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.notebookOverlay .cell-list-container .monaco-list-row')))) {
  await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+P');
  await ctx.page.locator('.quick-input-widget input').waitFor();
  await ctx.page.keyboard.type('report.ipynb', { delay: 30 });
  await ctx.page.locator('.quick-input-widget .monaco-list-row', { hasText: 'report.ipynb' }).first().waitFor();
  await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  }
  const cells = await waitFor(ctx, async () => {
  const c = await notebookCells(ctx.page);
  return c.length === 2 && c.some(text => text.includes('total = 40 + 2')) ? c : undefined;
  }, 30000, 'the notebook editor to show both cells');
  if (!fs.readFileSync(NOTEBOOK_FILE, 'utf8').includes('total = 40 + 2')) {
  throw new Error('The notebook file on disk is not the expected fixture');
  }
  return `Notebook editor shows ${cells.length} cells`;
  },
		},
		{
  id: 'S2',
  title: 'The user edits the code cell without saving',
  async run(ctx) {
  const line = ctx.page.locator('.notebookOverlay .monaco-list-row .view-line', { hasText: 'print(total)' }).first();
  await line.click();
  await ctx.page.keyboard.press('End');
  await ctx.page.keyboard.type(`  ${USER_TEXT}`, { delay: 40 });
  await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await waitFor(ctx, () => activeTabIsDirty(ctx.page), 5000, 'the notebook to become dirty');
  return 'The notebook has unsaved changes';
  },
		},
		{
  id: 'S3',
  title: 'The agent adds a cell with the notebook edit tool',
  async run(ctx) {
  await ctx.runCommand('Agent: Add a Cell to the Open Notebook');
  const toast = await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => {
  const messages = [...document.querySelectorAll('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast .notification-list-item-message')];
  return messages.map(t => t.textContent || '').find(t => t.includes('Agent:'));
  }), 30000, 'the agent to report back');
  await ctx.sleep(1500);
  return `Agent reported: ${toast.trim().slice(0, 160)}`;
  },
		},
		{
  id: 'S4',
  title: 'The user saves the notebook',
  async run(ctx) {
  await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+S');
  const outcome = await waitFor(ctx, () => ctx.page.evaluate(() => {
  const conflict = [...document.querySelectorAll('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast')]
  .find(t => (t.textContent || '').includes('content of the file is newer'));
  if (conflict) {
  return 'conflict';
  }
  return document.querySelector('.tabs-container .tab.active.dirty') ? undefined : 'saved';
  }), 10000, 'the save to finish');
  if (outcome === 'conflict') {
  // The editor never showed the agent's cell, so overwriting looks like the right choice.
  await ctx.sleep(1500);
  await ctx.page.locator('.notifications-toasts .notification-toast', { hasText: 'content of the file is newer' })
  .locator('.monaco-button', { hasText: 'Overwrite' }).first().click();
  await waitFor(ctx, async () => !(await activeTabIsDirty(ctx.page)), 10000, 'the overwrite to finish');
  return 'Save reported that the file on disk is newer; the user chose Overwrite';
  }
  return 'Saved without a conflict';
  },
		},
		{
  id: 'S5',
  title: "The agent's cell is in the editor and in the saved file",
  async run(ctx) {
  await ctx.sleep(1000);
  const cells = await notebookCells(ctx.page);
  const disk = fs.readFileSync(NOTEBOOK_FILE, 'utf8');
  const inEditor = cells.some(text => text.includes(AGENT_CODE));
  const onDisk = disk.includes(AGENT_CODE.replace(/"/g, '\\"'));
  const userEditKept = disk.includes(USER_TEXT);
  if (!inEditor || !onDisk || !userEditKept) {
  throw new Error(`Agent cell in editor: ${inEditor}, agent cell on disk: ${onDisk}, user edit on disk: ${userEditKept} (editor shows ${cells.length} cells)`);
  }
  return `Editor shows ${cells.length} cells including the agent's; the saved file has the agent's cell and the user's edit`;
  },
		},
	],
};
```

</details>

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|
| New unit tests on `main` @ `cd2259b` | `npx vitest --run src/extension/tools/node/test/editNotebookTool.spec.tsx` (in `extensions/copilot`) | ❌ fails as expected: 6 of the new tests fail. Insert, edit and delete without a stream, and the failed-apply test, throw `Invalid input, no stream`. The 2 tests with a prompt context left over from an earlier request (then invoked from an agent session, or from another request) use that request's closed stream and throw `Response stream has been closed`. The 13 existing tests pass |
| Unit tests with this PR | same | ✅ 19/19 passed. The existing tests now pass the same request id to `resolveInput` and `invoke`, as the Copilot Chat tool loop does, and still go through the stream |
| Agent-style edit on an open, unsaved notebook, `main` @ `cd2259b` | `cdp-scenario.mjs --scenario repro.cjs` (3 runs, fresh window each) | ❌ 3/3 as expected: the tool fails with `Invalid input, no stream`, the cell is written to disk only, save reports the file is newer, and after Overwrite the agent's cell is gone from the editor and the file |

One earlier run on the current head was cut short when the Copilot sign-in dialog (the test profile's token had expired) opened mid-run and took the Ctrl+S; the agent's cell had already been added. The setup now dismisses that dialog before recording, and all 3 reruns passed |
| Copilot extension typecheck | `npx tsc --noEmit --project tsconfig.json` (in `extensions/copilot`) | ✅ no errors |

title: Chat: reopen slash command completions when editing the command word again
body:
## Problem

In the chat input, slash command completions (`/` → prompts, skills, commands) only open on the `/` trigger character, because the chat input editor sets `quickSuggestions` to `false` (`chatInputPart.ts`).

If the suggest session gets cancelled, it never comes back while the user keeps editing the command word. For example:

1. Type `/delete` → completions are shown and filtered ✅
2. Accidentally type a space (or click, or use the arrow keys) → suggest session is cancelled (`SuggestModel._onCursorChange` / `_onNewContext`)
3. Backspace the space and continue typing `-merged…` → **no completions anymore** ❌ (only Ctrl+Space brings them back)

## Fix

Add a small chat widget contribution, `ChatSlashCommandSuggestRetrigger`. On `onDidType`, if suggest is idle, the selection is empty, and the text from the start of the input up to the cursor is a leading slash command word (`^\s*/[\p{L}0-9_.:-]+$`, same character set as `SlashCommandWord`), it calls `SuggestController.triggerSuggest(undefined, true)`.

Quick suggestions stay disabled for regular text, so the change only affects editing a leading `/command` word.

## Tests

Added unit tests for `shouldRetriggerSlashCommandSuggest` and for registering the contribution in `chatInputEditorContrib.test.ts`.

title: chat: persist timing for contiguous reasoning runs
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Persist the duration of each **contiguous thinking run**, not a total for an assistant message or a UI group.

```text
tool -> thinking (5s) -> markdown -> thinking (12s) -> tool
```

This retains two independent durations, `5000` and `12000`, including after database restart and UI reload. A run starts at its first nonempty reasoning text and ends at the next markdown/tool part or turn termination. SDK reasoning IDs, reasoning-complete events, full-message boundaries, and sideband notifications do not split it.

- Measure each run with a monotonic clock and stable reasoning-part ID. A run spanning multiple SDK messages keeps one clock and one final duration.
- Persist ordered reasoning/markdown pieces and tool references in `assistant_response_parts`, keyed by durable assistant-message IDs. Final timing updates earlier fragments of an unfinished run.
- Restore the observed boundaries and retain canonical provider tool results. Merge fragments by run identity without adding their repeated duration; use recorded projections only when their text still matches the native transcript.
- Carry timing through AHP updates, reconnects, local imports, and chat serialization. Single-run fallback headers show "Thought for 5s"; expanded conversation groups expose each run's own duration without a group-wide sum. Generated titles and conversation grouping remain available.
- Keep turn remapping/pruning behavior and migrate without treating the earlier draft's aggregate `reasoning_timing` rows as individual run timings. Unknown or unfinished history stays untimed.
- Preserve imported reasoning projections against synthesized SDK event IDs before resume; refresh finalized visible/ARIA labels when timing arrives late; and mark all AHP reasoning as provider-owned independently of optional timing values so reconnect tails never fabricate totals.

Companion protocol PR: microsoft/agent-host-protocol#552 is merged. The generated protocol source is pinned to merge commit `d7a5579b`; the protocol dependency is satisfied.

Scope: producer-side capture is implemented for Copilot. Other conforming hosts can supply the optional timing fields; this does not add capture to other providers, estimate older history, or change tool timing. Local, non-AHP providers retain their existing client-side reasoning measurement.

No issue was supplied for this feature request.

- Repository hygiene — passed, using this command before committing:


- `npm run stylelint -- <blob>.css` — passed, with 15 pre-existing design-token suggestions. CSS is unchanged by the review follow-up.
- Initial contiguous-run implementation validation, before the review follow-up below — **3,378 passed; 2 existing pending**:

The tests cover separate 5s/12s markdown/tool boundaries through real SQLite close/reopen and UI reload in Compact, Verbose, and Conversation modes; a single run spanning SDK messages; partial/mismatched recordings; parent/child isolation; legacy aggregate migration; and accessible labels.

title: Keep the chat's custom agent when a queued message starts
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #341837

## Problem

In an Agent Host chat with a custom agent selected, a message you queue while a turn is running starts without that agent. The agent picker still shows the custom agent, but the queued turn runs with the default agent, and the provider drops its custom agent selection until the next direct send. Messages another session sends with `send_message` have the same problem. The issue's comment reports this ("agent definition should be loaded in queue also").

## Root cause

Model and agent selection travel on each turn's message. Before a turn is sent, the host applies the message's agent with `changeAgent(chat, message.agent)` ([agentSideEffects.ts](<url>)). The protocol defines a message without `agent` as "no custom agent, the provider's default behavior applies" ([state.ts](<url>)). The Copilot, Claude and Codex providers all clear their custom agent when they get `undefined`.

Direct sends set `agent` from the selected mode ([agentHostSessionHandler.ts](<url>)), but the pending messages the workbench publishes for queued and steering requests never did ([agentHostSessionHandler.ts](<url>)). The `send_message` tool builds its queued, steering and started messages without an agent too ([sessionServerTools.ts](<url>), [agentService.ts](<url>)). So when such a message started a turn, the host switched the chat to the default agent. A side effect in the workbench: the next local change to the queue re-published a message queued elsewhere without its agent.

## Fix

The messages now say which agent they run with, as the protocol expects, and the host's `changeAgent` handling is unchanged:

- **Workbench:** a pending message carries the custom agent that was selected when it was queued, read from the request's mode the same way a direct send does (shared helper `getRequestedAgentUri`). A pending message that came from the host has no local mode, so it keeps the agent it already has instead of being re-published without one.
- **Host, `send_message`:** queued, steering and directly started messages carry the target chat's current agent, which is the agent of its latest turn (new helper `getLatestTurnAgent`). New chats have no turns, so `create_session` and `create_chat` prompts are unchanged.
- **Host, steering:** steering joins the turn that is already running, so the agent selected for it is not applied, yet Copilot and Codex show consumed steering as a turn of its own. When a provider starts a turn from steering it consumed, the host now records the agent of the turn it steered on that turn's message (`withSteeredTurnAgent` in `agentSideEffects.ts`). So if Reviewer is running and you pick Coder before steering, later `send_message` messages keep Reviewer, the agent actually running. Steering the provider hands back unsent (the turn ended first) starts a fresh turn through the queue, so it still runs with, and records, the agent you selected.

A host-side "skip `changeAgent` when the message has no agent" guard would be wrong: a direct send without an agent is how you switch back to the default agent. That still works, and a unit test now covers it. Other turns the host writes itself, such as agent merge prompts, still carry no agent; they are left for a separate change.

## Before / after

Agents window connected to a mock agent host that offers a "Reviewer" custom agent. Every reply starts with the agent the host selected for that turn. Reviewer is selected, "Review the parser" keeps running, and "Then summarize the changes" is queued.

### Before

![Before: the queued message replies "Agent: default" while the picker still shows Reviewer](<url>)

### After

![After: the queued message replies "Agent: Reviewer"](<url>)

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open a Copilot chat on the Agent Host and pick a custom agent in the agent picker.
2. Send a prompt that takes a while, then type a second message and add it to the queue (set `chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction` to `queue` to make Enter queue).
3. When the first turn ends and the queued message starts, it runs with the custom agent. The automated repro below shows this with a mock agent that reports which agent the host selected for each turn.
4. Pick the built-in Agent mode and send: the chat switches back to the default agent.

<details><summary>Automated repro (mock agent host + Agents window)</summary>

The repro uses the scripted mock agent from `out/`, so it needs no account. Save the three files next to each other, build (`npm run transpile-client`), then:

1. `node runHost.cjs` with `BS_VSCODE` set to the checkout root (starts the host on `ws://127.0.0.1:8985`).
2. Launch the Agents window (`.agents/skills/launch`) with `--agents --disable-extension GitHub.copilot-chat`, and set `chat.remoteAgentHosts` to `[{ "address": "ws://127.0.0.1:8985", "name": "Mock Host" }]`, `chat.agentHost.allowSignedOutWhenUsable: true` and `chat.requestQueuing.defaultAction: "queue"`.
3. `node <bug-swarm skill>/scripts/cdp-scenario.mjs --cdp <port> --scenario repro.cjs --out <dir>` (fails on main, passes with this PR).

`repro.cjs`:

```js
// Repro: a message queued while a turn runs must start with the custom agent the chat had selected.
// Runs over CDP against an Agents window connected to the mock Agent Host in mockhost.mjs (chat.remoteAgentHosts).
// The mock agent starts every reply with "Agent: <name>", the agent the host selected for that turn, and writes the
// host's agent changes to BS_STATUS, which is reported as an independent check.
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');

const PROMPT = 'Review the parser';
const QUEUED = 'Then summarize the changes';
const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-host-status.json');
const readStatus = () => { try { return JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(STATUS, 'utf8')); } catch { return { agentChanges: [], turns: [] }; } };

let turnCount = 0;

async function waitFor(fn, timeoutMs, intervalMs = 100) {
	const end = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
	let value;
	while (Date.now() < end) {
		value = await fn();
		if (value) { return value; }
		await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, intervalMs));
	}
	return value;
}

// This repro needs no Copilot account: dismiss the sign-in prompt, which can open a few seconds after the window starts.
async function dismissSignIn(page) {
	for (let i = 0; i < 6; i++) {
		const cont = page.getByText('Continue Without Signing In');
		if (await cont.count()) { await cont.first().click(); await page.waitForTimeout(800); continue; }
		if (!await page.evaluate(() => !!document.querySelector('.monaco-dialog-box, .monaco-dialog-modal-block, .sessions-signing-in-dialog-modal-block'))) { break; }
		await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
		await page.waitForTimeout(800);
	}
}

const replies = page => page.evaluate(() => {
	const down = [...document.querySelectorAll('.chat-scroll-down')].find(e => e.offsetParent);
	down?.click();
	return [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-response')].filter(e => e.offsetParent).map(e => [...e.querySelectorAll('.rendered-markdown')].map(m => m.textContent).join(' ').trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' '));
});
const pendingRows = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-item-container.pending-request')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent)
	.map(e => (e.querySelector('.value')?.textContent ?? e.textContent).trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ')));
const pickerLabel = page => page.evaluate(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-input-part .action-label')]
	.filter(e => e.offsetParent && (e.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Pick Mode')).at(-1)?.textContent.trim());

module.exports = {
	id: 'queued-message-keeps-custom-agent',
	title: 'A queued message starts with the chat\'s custom agent',
	source: '<url>',
	stepPauseMs: 1500,
	steps: [
		{
  id: 'open', title: 'Open a session on the mock agent host', async run({ page }) {
  await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].some(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Agent mock')), null, { timeout: 60000 });
  await dismissSignIn(page);
  const rowId = await page.evaluate(() => {
  const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-list-row')].filter(r => r.offsetParent);
  const header = rows.findIndex(r => (r.getAttribute('aria-label') || '').startsWith('Agent mock'));
  return rows.slice(header + 1).find(r => /^(Parser review|Session),/.test(r.getAttribute('aria-label') || ''))?.id;
  });
  if (!rowId) { throw new Error('The mock host session is not in the sessions list'); }
  await page.locator(`[id="${rowId}"]`).click();
  await page.waitForFunction(() => [...document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-request')].some(e => e.textContent.includes('Look at the parser module') || e.textContent.includes('Review the parser')), null, { timeout: 30000 });
  return 'The session transcript is visible';
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'pick', title: 'Select the Reviewer custom agent', async run({ page }) {
  await dismissSignIn(page);
  await page.locator('.interactive-input-part .action-label[aria-label^="Pick Mode"]:visible').last().click();
  await page.getByRole('option', { name: 'Reviewer', exact: true }).click();
  const label = await waitFor(async () => (await pickerLabel(page)) === 'Reviewer' && 'Reviewer', 5000);
  if (!label) { throw new Error(`The agent picker shows "${await pickerLabel(page)}"`); }
  return 'The agent picker shows Reviewer';
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'send', title: `Send "${PROMPT}"; the turn keeps running`, async run({ page }) {
  turnCount = readStatus().turns.length;
  const input = page.locator('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor:visible').last();
  await input.click();
  await page.keyboard.type(PROMPT, { delay: 15 });
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const reply = await waitFor(async () => readStatus().turns.length > turnCount && (await replies(page)).at(-1)?.includes('Reviewing the parser') && (await replies(page)).at(-1), 30000);
  if (!reply) { throw new Error('The turn did not start'); }
  return `Reply so far: "${reply}"`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'queue', title: `Queue "${QUEUED}" while the turn runs`, async run({ page }) {
  const input = page.locator('.interactive-input-part .monaco-editor:visible').last();
  await input.click();
  await page.keyboard.type(QUEUED, { delay: 15 });
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const rows = await waitFor(async () => { const r = await pendingRows(page); return r.some(t => t.includes(QUEUED)) && r; }, 10000);
  if (!rows) { throw new Error(`The message was not queued; pending rows: ${JSON.stringify(await pendingRows(page))}`); }
  return `Queued: ${JSON.stringify(rows)}`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'drain', title: 'The first turn ends and the queued message starts', async run({ page }) {
  const reply = await waitFor(async () => readStatus().turns.slice(turnCount).some(t => t.prompt === QUEUED) && (await replies(page)).at(-1)?.includes('Summary:') && (await replies(page)).at(-1), 40000);
  if (!reply) { throw new Error('The queued message did not start'); }
  return `Queued message reply: "${reply}"`;
  }
		},
		{
  id: 'check', title: 'The queued message ran with the Reviewer agent', async run({ page }) {
  const reply = (await replies(page)).findLast(t => t.includes('Summary:'));
  const hostTurn = readStatus().turns.slice(turnCount).find(t => t.prompt === QUEUED);
  const picker = await pickerLabel(page);
  const agent = /Agent: (\w+)\./.exec(reply)?.[1];
  if (agent !== 'Reviewer') {
  throw new Error(`The queued message ran with the ${agent} agent instead of Reviewer. Reply: "${reply}"; host selected: ${hostTurn?.agent}; picker shows: ${picker}`);
  }
  return `Reply: "${reply}"; host selected: ${hostTurn?.agent}; picker shows: ${picker}`;
  }
		},
	]
};
```

`mockhost.mjs`:

```js
// Standalone Agent Host (from a built VS Code checkout's out/) with the ScriptedMockAgent, used to show which custom
// agent a queued message runs with.
// - Seeds one session mock:/bs-agent titled "Parser review" with a one-turn history.
// - Publishes one custom agent, "Reviewer", in the session's customizations so the chat's agent picker offers it.
// - Records every changeAgent call the host makes and writes it to BS_STATUS (JSON).
// - Every reply starts with "Agent: <name>", the agent the host selected for that turn ("Reviewer" or "default").
// - A prompt starting with "Review the parser" keeps its turn running for BS_HOLD_MS (default 15000 ms).
// Usage (from an interactive terminal: the server exits when stdin closes): node runHost.cjs
//  env BS_VSCODE = checkout root, BS_PORT, BS_UDD, BS_STATUS, BS_HOLD_MS
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import path from 'node:path';
import fs from 'node:fs';
import os from 'node:os';

const VSCODE = process.env.BS_VSCODE || process.cwd();
const out = p => pathToFileURL(path.join(VSCODE, 'out', p)).href;
const HOLD_MS = Number(process.env.BS_HOLD_MS || 15000);
const STATUS = process.env.BS_STATUS || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-host-status.json');
const SESSION = 'mock:/bs-agent';
const TITLE = 'Parser review';
const REVIEWER_URI = 'file:///bs-agents/reviewer.agent.md';
process.env.VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_MOCK_SEED_SESSIONS = SESSION;

const mock = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mockAgent.js'));
const fx = await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/historyRecordFixtures.js'));
const { URI } = await import(out('vs/base/common/uri.js'));

const status = { pid: process.pid, agentChanges: [], turns: [] };
const writeStatus = () => fs.writeFileSync(STATUS, JSON.stringify(status, null, 1));
writeStatus();
const logLine = s => process.stderr.write(`[bs-agent] ${s}\n`);

let currentAgentUri;
const agentName = () => currentAgentUri === REVIEWER_URI ? 'Reviewer' : currentAgentUri ? currentAgentUri : 'default';

const P = mock.ScriptedMockAgent.prototype;
P.getChatCustomizations = async function () {
	return [{
		type: 'directory', id: 'bs-agents', uri: 'file:///bs-agents', name: 'Agents',
		enabled: true, contents: 'agent', writable: false,
		children: [{ type: 'agent', id: 'reviewer', uri: REVIEWER_URI, name: 'Reviewer', description: 'Reviews code changes' }],
	}];
};

let history;
const origGet = P.getSessionMessages;
P.getSessionMessages = async function (session) {
	const s = decodeURIComponent(session.toString());
	if (s.includes('bs-agent') && !s.includes('subagent')) {
		history ??= fx.buildTurnsFromHistory([
  { type: 'message', role: 'user', session: URI.parse(SESSION), messageId: 'u-0', content: 'Look at the parser module.' },
  { type: 'message', role: 'assistant', session: URI.parse(SESSION), messageId: 'a-0', content: 'Ready. The parser lives in src/parser.ts.' },
		]);
		return history;
	}
	return origGet.call(this, session);
};
const label = s => String(s).includes('bs-agent') ? TITLE : undefined;
const origFireDisc = P.fireDiscoveredChats;
P.fireDiscoveredChats = function (chats) {
	return origFireDisc.call(this, chats.map(m => ({ ...m, external: false, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })));
};
for (const k of ['listExternalChats', 'listSessions']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { return (await o.apply(this, a)).map(m => ({ ...m, summary: label(m.session) ?? m.summary })); };
}
for (const k of ['getSessionMetadata', 'getChatMetadata']) {
	const o = P[k];
	P[k] = async function (...a) { const r = await o.apply(this, a); const l = label(String(a[1]?.toString?.() ?? '') + String(a[0])); return r && l ? { ...r, summary: l } : r; };
}
const origDesc = P.getDescriptor;
P.getDescriptor = function () {
	if (!this.__bsInit) {
		this.__bsInit = true;
		const origChange = this.chats.changeAgent;
		this.chats.changeAgent = (chat, agent, context) => {
  currentAgentUri = agent?.uri;
  status.agentChanges.push({ at: Date.now(), chat: chat.toString(), agent: agent?.uri ?? null });
  writeStatus();
  logLine(`changeAgent ${agent?.uri ?? '(default)'}`);
  return origChange(chat, agent, context);
		};
		for (const ms of [1500, 5000]) {
  setTimeout(() => {
  void this.listExternalChats().then(chats => { this.fireDiscoveredChats(chats); });
  }, ms);
		}
		for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) {
  setTimeout(() => {
  try {
  this._onDidChatProgress.fire({ kind: 'action', resource: URI.parse(SESSION), action: { type: 'session/titleChanged', title: TITLE } });
  } catch (e) { logLine(`title failed: ${e}`); }
  }, 2000 + i * 3000);
		}
	}
	return origDesc.call(this);
};

const origFire = P._fireSequence;
P._fireSequence = function (signals) {
	const first = signals[0];
	const content = first?.action?.part && typeof first.action.part.content === 'string' ? first.action.part.content : '';
	const match = /^Unknown prompt: (.*)$/s.exec(content);
	if (!match) {
		return origFire.call(this, signals);
	}
	const prompt = match[1];
	const agent = agentName();
	const turn = { turnId: first.action.turnId, prompt, agent, startedAt: Date.now() };
	status.turns.push(turn);
	writeStatus();
	logLine(`turn "${prompt}" agent=${agent}`);
	const hold = /^Review the parser/.test(prompt);
	const text = `Agent: ${agent}. ${hold ? 'Reviewing the parser, this takes a while…' : 'Summary: the parser changes look good.'}`;
	const reply = { ...first, action: { ...first.action, part: { ...first.action.part, content: text } } };
	if (!hold) {
		return origFire.call(this, [reply, ...signals.slice(1)]);
	}
	this._onDidChatProgress.fire(reply);
	setTimeout(() => {
		turn.completedAt = Date.now();
		writeStatus();
		this._onDidChatProgress.fire(signals[signals.length - 1]);
	}, HOLD_MS);
};

process.argv = [process.argv[0], process.argv[1], '--enable-mock-agent', '--port', process.env.BS_PORT || '8985', '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--without-connection-token', '--quiet', '--user-data-dir', process.env.BS_UDD || path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'bs-agent-ahost-udd')];
await import(out('vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostServerMain.js'));
setInterval(() => { }, 1 << 30);
```

`runHost.cjs`:

```js
// Keeps the mock Agent Host's stdin open (the server shuts down when stdin ends) and forwards its output.
const { spawn } = require('child_process');
const path = require('path');
const child = spawn(process.execPath, [path.join(__dirname, 'mockhost.mjs')], { stdio: ['pipe', 'pipe', 'pipe'], env: { BS_VSCODE: 'Q:\\GIT\\vscode.worktrees\\bug-swarm-fix-retry', ...process.env } });
child.stdout.on('data', d => process.stdout.write(d));
child.stderr.on('data', d => process.stderr.write(d));
console.log(`[runHost] child pid ${child.pid}`);
child.on('exit', (code, sig) => { console.log(`[runHost] child exit ${code} ${sig}`); process.exit(0); });
process.on('SIGTERM', () => child.kill());
setInterval(() => { }, 1 << 30);
```

</details>

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|
| Repro on `main` @ `cd2259b` | `cdp-scenario.mjs --scenario repro.cjs` (3 runs, fresh mock host and window) | ❌ fails 3/3 as expected: the queued message replied "Agent: default", the host recorded a switch to the default agent for that turn, and the picker still showed Reviewer |
| Repro with this PR | same | ✅ passes 3/3: the queued message replied "Agent: Reviewer" and the host kept Reviewer |
| New unit tests on `main` | `scripts\test.bat --run <the 3 test files> --grep "send_message keeps the custom agent\|switches the chat back to the default agent\|pending messages carry the custom agent"` | ❌ 2 fail as expected (`send_message` turns ran with `[Reviewer, default, default]`; queued messages published no agent and a host message lost its agent); the default-agent guard passes |

title: sessions: fix cloud composer pickers after window reload
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Fix the Agents window composer getting stuck with unresponsive "Session Controls" and "Model" buttons after reloading with Cloud selected.

The toolbar can render before its custom action-view factories register. It then uses the placeholder actions, whose handlers do nothing. Registering a factory later does not refresh an existing toolbar.

- Register the shared composer controls, model picker, and cloud mode/approval picker factories at `BlockRestore` instead of `AfterRestored`.
- Keep picker construction lazy and leave cloud connections, model selection, permission rules, and menu visibility unchanged.
- Add a regression test that reads the production lifecycle registrations and checks that all seven required menu factories are available before UI restoration.

## Validation

Commands ran with Node 24.22.1, as specified by the repository.

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- The regression test failed before the production fix: the factory list was empty instead of containing the seven required registrations.
- Focused unit tests: **146 passed**.

```sh
./scripts/test.sh \
  --run <blob>.test.ts \
  --run <blob>.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/modelPicker.test.ts \
  --run <blob>.test.ts \
  --run <blob>.test.ts \
  --run <blob>.test.ts \
  --reporter dot
```

- Targeted lint: **passed**.

```sh
npm run eslint -- \
  src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/modelPicker.ts \
  <blob>.contribution.ts \
  <blob>.ts \
  <blob>.test.ts
```

## Review path

Illustrative scenario, not live-tested: select Cloud in the new-session composer and reload the window. The first rendered toolbar should contain working model and permission controls, not placeholder command labels. Allow about three minutes for this review.

1. **Registration, one minute.** The important ordering change is below. The same phase is used for the model picker and the nested cloud controls. Check that these constructors only register factories rather than constructing pickers or starting a cloud connection.

  [sharedChatInputComposer.contribution.ts](<url>)

  ```ts
  // Register before restoration: adding a factory later does not refresh existing toolbars.
  registerWorkbenchContribution2(SharedChatInputComposerContribution.ID, SharedChatInputComposerContribution, WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore);
  ```

2. **First toolbar render, one minute.** Follow [MenuWorkbenchToolBar](<url>): it looks up the registered factory before falling back to a generic action. The early registrations let the existing picker widgets own rendering and clicks.

3. **Regression guard, one minute.** Check [the new test](<url>). It uses the real registration phases, not a phase hard-coded by the test, and leaves the global contribution registry untouched.

### Decisions and limits

- The fix changes three lightweight UI contribution phases rather than changing global action-view registration notifications.
- The test deliberately inspects private registration metadata to avoid starting unrelated workbench contributions or adding a test-only production API.
- No live cloud reload or full end-to-end test was run. For manual verification, reload with Cloud selected and open both the model and permission menus; also check a local composer and the existing cloud conversation UI.

title: agentHost: add scoped permission rules and smart approvals
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Replaces the tool-wide "Allow in this Session" approval for shell, URL, and file
tools in the agent host. The old approval allowed every later call of the tool. Now
the host offers scoped grants. The grants use permission rules in the format of
Claude Code. The local VS Code client keeps these rules in sync with its settings.

- Adds a permission rule parser and matcher for `Shell(...)`, `WebFetch(...)`,
  `Read(...)`, `Edit(...)`, and bare tool names. Shell rules support wildcard,
  `/regex/`, and `commandLine:` forms. WebFetch rules use VS Code URL patterns with
  https as the default scheme.
- Adds `permissions.ask` next to `allow` and `deny`. A deny rule rejects the call,
  also when Allow All is set. An ask rule always prompts. Rules from the chat, the
  session, and the host are combined.
- Changes the shell and URL confirmations. "Allow Once" is the default. The options
  are "Allow `cmd …` in this Session", "Allow Exact Command in this Session", "Always
  Allow …", "Allow Fetching <host> in this Session", and "Always Allow Fetching
  <host>". Read and write confirmations offer grants for the file and for the
  nearest git root folder. The option ID contains the grant rules, so a client
  cannot forge a grant.
- Moves the default terminal auto-approve rules to a shared platform module. VS Code
  and the agent host use the same rules. The host applies them only where no
  explicit rule matches.
- Syncs `chat.tools.urls.autoApprove`, `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove`, and
  `chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules` from user settings to the
  local agent host at start and when they change. "Always Allow" grants on the local
  host are written back to user settings. Remote agent hosts do not sync.
- Removes the client-generated terminal actions for agent host sessions and the
  `terminalAutoApproveRules` and `urlAutoApproveRules` root config keys.
- Adds an `AgentPermissionKind` const enum. Claude shell requests now use bash.
- Writes the host config to a temporary file and renames it. This prevents a host
  that starts at the same time from reading a partial file and losing values.

Fixes <url>

## Validation

Commands run on the merged branch:

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run eslint -- <54 changed files>`: passed
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: passed

title: markdown: stop snapping the editor back to the preview scroll position
body:
Fixes #317033

## Motivation

After the Markdown preview of a file has been scrolled once, every later switch back to that file's text editor scrolls the editor to the preview's last position. Wherever the user had scrolled in the editor is lost on each tab switch, until the window is reloaded.

`MarkdownPreviewManager` scrolls a markdown text editor to `TopmostLineMonitor.getPreviousStaticEditorLineByUri` whenever it becomes active. That line is set by `StaticMarkdownPreview` on every preview scroll, but unlike `getPreviousTextEditorLineByUri` (the other direction), the getter never removes it. So the handoff meant for "preview → editor" is replayed on every later activation.

## Changes made

- `getPreviousStaticEditorLineByUri` now removes the entry it returns, the same way `getPreviousTextEditorLineByUri` does. Opening the text editor from a scrolled preview still lands on the preview's position once. Later tab switches keep the editor's own position.

This is the editor-side half. #342822 addresses the preview-side scroll position (#147718) in `preview-src/index.ts` and does not touch this code.

**Known limit:** with a static preview open beside the text editor, the stored line is still applied once. For example, you scroll the preview without focusing it, then scroll the editor elsewhere, switch tabs and come back: the editor jumps to the preview's position one time instead of on every switch. Fully fixing that needs the stored line cleared when the user scrolls the text editor. That depends on the order of the active-editor and visible-range events when an editor opens, which I couldn't check outside the extension host, so I left it out of this PR. I can follow up with it if you want that behaviour.

## How to test

1. Open a long markdown file in the preview (`Open With... > Markdown Preview`) and scroll down.
2. Reopen it in the text editor. It opens at the preview's position.
3. Scroll the text editor somewhere else, switch to another tab, then back.
4. The editor stays where you scrolled it. Before this change it jumped back to the preview's position.

## Validation

- New test `src/test/topmostLineMonitor.test.ts`: the stored preview line is returned once, then `undefined`. It fails with the change reverted (the second read returns `10`).
- The extension's `tsconfig.json` typechecks with no errors, and eslint passes on both files.
- I ran the new test locally with mocha against a minimal `vscode` stub, not in the extension host.

title: terminal: fall back to DOM renderer when sticky scroll loses its WebGL context
body:
Fixes #344170

When the sticky scroll overlay's WebGL context is lost, the overlay keeps the dead canvas (a white bar with the sad-face placeholder) until the window is reloaded. The terminal itself falls back to the DOM renderer in the same situation.

### Changes

- Subscribe to `WebglAddon.onContextLoss` in `TerminalStickyScrollOverlay._refreshGpuAcceleration` and dispose of the addon, the same way `XtermTerminal._enableWebglRenderer` does.
- Remember the loss until the next `terminal.integrated` configuration change. `_syncOptions` calls `_refreshGpuAcceleration` on every resize, theme change and terminal configuration change, so without this the addon was recreated right away on the lost context. Retrying on configuration changes matches the terminal, which re-enables WebGL in `updateConfig`.
- Take the same fallback when `loadAddon` throws. This covers loads after the overlay is opened, for example the retry above while WebGL2 is still unavailable. The first load happens before `open()`, where the addon defers activation, so that case is unchanged.
- Re-check `_shouldLoadWebgl()` after the addon import resolves, so a refresh that was waiting on the import doesn't recreate the addon after a fallback.

### How to test

1. Set `"terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration": "on"`, open a terminal with shell integration and run `seq 1 200` so that sticky scroll shows the command.
2. In Developer Tools, run:
  ```js
  document.querySelector('.terminal-sticky-scroll .xterm-screen canvas:not([class])').getContext('webgl2').getExtension('WEBGL_lose_context').loseContext()
  ```
3. Wait more than 3 seconds, then run `seq 1 100`. The overlay now renders `seq 1 100` with the DOM renderer instead of the white bar.
4. Change a `terminal.integrated` setting. The overlay goes back to WebGL.

### Tests

- Context loss: the addon is disposed, a resize does not recreate it, and a configuration change does. Fails with the source change reverted.
- Load failure: a throwing addon leaves the overlay on the DOM renderer until a configuration change. Fails with the try/catch removed.
- `terminalStickyScrollOverlay.test.ts` and `xtermTerminal.test.ts` pass in Chromium (56 tests).

title: Canvases: enable remote Agent Host presentation
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Prerequisite

[microsoft/vscode#345149](<url>) merged into `main` and provides the generic WebSocket/WebRTC/popup hardening used here. This branch is rebased directly onto the merged commits.

## Deep architecture explainer

[Remote canvases from the ground up](<url>) explains the protocol state, ownership model, BrowserView network routing, authenticated proxy and Agent Host TCP flow, lifecycle, security boundaries, validation, and debugging path without assuming prior context.

## Summary

This enables desktop canvases published by a remote Agent Host to render in the existing native BrowserView canvas editor.

Remote canvas URLs retain their original URL, including `127.0.0.1`, while the BrowserView resolves the network from the exact owning session/chat. The canvas requires that network, preventing a disconnected, unsupported, or disabled remote from falling back to the client or an unrelated workspace remote.

## Architecture

```text
Remote Agent Host publishes CanvasState.url
  │
  ▼
AgentHostCanvasCollection projects the exact chat-owned canvas
  │
  ▼
CanvasService creates an unlisted BrowserView for the owning chat
  │
  ▼
SessionBrowserNetworkContribution resolves chat → session → host authority
  │
  ▼
BrowserViewWorkbenchService requires that resolved network
  │
  ▼
Existing authenticated Agent Host BrowserView proxy
  │
  ▼
Remote Agent Host network, including its loopback canvas server
```

### Fail-closed behavior

- `CanvasService` supplies the exact chat owner and requests strict network resolution.
- `BrowserViewWorkbenchService` resolves the owner even when remote proxying is disabled, then rejects if that network cannot be used.
- Ambient remote Editor windows delegate TCP to their Agent Host connection.
- Non-ambient remote hosts present canvases only in the Agents window, where owning-session resolution exists.
- Local canvases retain their current behavior.

## How to review

Review the two commits independently:

### 1. `canvases: enable remote Agent Host presentation`

1. Provider policy:
  - [`RemoteAgentHostSessionsProvider`](<blob>.ts)
  - [`AgentHostChatContribution`](<blob>.ts)
  - [`RemoteAgentHostContribution`](<blob>.ts)
2. Exact network requirement:
  - [`CanvasService.resolveCanvasModel`](src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/electron-browser/canvasService.ts)
  - [`BrowserViewWorkbenchService.createExternalBrowserView`](src/vs/workbench/contrib/browserView/electron-browser/browserViewWorkbenchService.ts)
  - focused test: `does not fall back when an external view requires its resolved network`
3. Ambient remote Editor TCP:
  - [`EditorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient`](<blob>.ts)

Canvas enablement and strict routing intentionally remain in the same commit: enabling presentation without fail-closed ownership would create an unsafe intermediate state.

### 2. `canvases: add native remote network coverage`

- [`browser.test.ts`](extensions/vscode-api-tests/src/singlefolder-tests/browser.test.ts) drives a real Electron BrowserView through redirect, SSE, `ws://`, an 8 MiB response, and WebRTC gathering.
- It first disables remote proxying and verifies zero HTTP/WebSocket/UDP traffic.
- It then enables proxying and verifies all browser protocols succeed with zero UDP/STUN leakage.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed
- Provider, canvas, chat contribution, and ambient remote client suites — 1,824 passed
- Changed TypeScript ESLint — passed for 13 files
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed
- `npm run gulp compile-extension:vscode-api-tests` — passed with 0 errors
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite api-folder --grep "remote Agent Host network loads native Chromium protocols and fails closed"` — 1 passed
- `git diff origin/main..HEAD --check` — passed

## Manual dogfood

Verified against a Windows `devbox2` Remote Agent Host through an authenticated dev tunnel:

- the remote agent discovered and opened the Session timeline canvas;
- the BrowserView rendered while retaining its remote loopback URL;
- that port had no listener on the Mac and direct local `curl` failed, confirming traffic crossed the Agent Host proxy;
- closing, reopening, and interacting with the canvas succeeded.

## Scope and limitations

- Desktop native BrowserViews only.
- Copilot Agent Host canvas channels only.
- No public extension API changes.
- No relay transport support without negotiated TCP forwarding.
- Non-ambient remote hosts present canvases only in the Agents window.

Main CI [491042](<url>) and [491050](<url>) fail on macOS ARM64 smoke in `Integrated Browser › allows agents to use shared pages and blocks unshared pages`, which times out clicking `.browser-share-toggle[aria-label="Stop Sharing with Agent"]`.

Since #344900, attachments can show as inline pills in the chat input, and clicking a pill opens its attachment in an editor. title: Copilot CLI: Stop large session stores exhausting file handles
body:
Fixes #344829. Related: #327021.

## Problem

`_getAllSessions` called `sessionManager.listSessions()` with no options. For every directory in `~/.copilot/session-state`, the SDK then opened `events.jsonl` (twice) and `workspace.yaml`, all at the same time. Only after that did we throw away every session VS Code didn't create. With a large store (42k sessions from `copilot -p` in the report), each window's extension host held 10k–20k open files during startup. On macOS that breaks child-process spawning (`spawn EBADF` for ESLint, ripgrep and git), and several windows together fill the system file table (ENFILE).

Passing only `metadataLimit` is not enough. While detached sessions are included (the default), the SDK still opens every `events.jsonl` at once to detect them.

## Solution
The listing in copilot CLI provider now fetches only session IDs, skips sessions the agent host already lists and sessions VS Code didn't create, and reads details just for the rest, at most 10 at a time and cached until their files change

## Changes

- **Listing** (`copilotcliSessionService.ts`)
  - Call `listSessions({ metadataLimit: 0, includeDetached: false })`, which returns only IDs and times and opens no `events.jsonl` or `workspace.yaml`.
  - Drop agent-host-owned IDs (`agentSessionData/<id>`) and sessions VS Code didn't create *before* any SDK read.
  - Read details (summary, name, `clientName`, context) with `enrichSessionMetadata`, 10 at a time, only for the remaining sessions. Output is identical to a full listing, including the SDK's pruning of empty sessions.
  - The `clientName === vscode-agent-host` filter now runs after the details read; agent-host ownership is re-read on every listing and checked first, so an adopted legacy session still drops out on the next refresh.
- **Cache:** details are reused while both the SDK's `modifiedTime` (`events.jsonl`) and the `workspace.yaml` modification time are unchanged. A rename that only rewrites `workspace.yaml` doesn't change `modifiedTime`, so both are needed. Also cleared on delete, rename and summary updates. Repeated refreshes become nearly free (#327021).
- **Item building:** both session item providers build list items at most 32 at a time instead of all at once.
- **`getSessionWorkingDirectory` is now async.** The listing only records working directories for VS Code-created sessions, so for any other session (e.g. a legacy session opened after declined adoption, or one restored at startup) it reads that one session from the SDK on demand.
- **Logging:** a trace line reports listed / agent-host-owned / external / read / cached / shown counts.
- **Docs:** `copilotcli/AGENTS.md` documents the listing contract.

No change to which sessions are shown, their titles, timing or order, or to legacy → agent-host migration, remote (WSL/SSH) or the Agents window. None of those paths call this listing differently.

## How to test

Automated:
- `npx vitest run src/extension/chatSessions` (in `extensions/copilot`): 1335 passed, 1 failed. The failure ("preserves order of edit toolCallIds and permissions…" in `copilotcliSession.spec.ts`) also fails on `main` without this change.
  - New tests: external sessions are never read; at most 10 reads run at once; the cache is reused, and refreshed when either file changes; an adopted session disappears even with cached details; agent-host `clientName` and empty sessions are filtered; the working directory resolves for a session that was never listed.
- `copilotCLISDKUpgrade.spec.ts`: 4/4 passed. A new test runs the real SDK and fails if a future SDK version changes what `metadataLimit: 0` does, or if `enrichSessionMetadata` stops matching a full listing.
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` and `eslint --max-warnings=0` on the changed files: clean.

Manual end to end (Windows, generated store of 20,000 external + 100 VS Code-created sessions):
- Real SDK, old vs new: peak extra handles about 8,700 → about 30; time about 4.1 s → about 2.2 s; the same 100 sessions.
- Code OSS signed in, cold start: log shows `Listed 20100 sessions: … 20000 external, 100 read … 100 shown`, and the refresh shows `100 cached` (about 1 s). No Code OSS process went above about 1,700 handles. No EMFILE, ENFILE or EBADF in any log. The Sessions view shows only the VS Code-created sessions.
- WSL remote sessions

To reproduce: generate many session directories under a temporary `COPILOT_HOME` (script in the issue), launch Code OSS with `--log GitHub.copilot-chat:trace`, and check the `Listed … sessions` line in the Copilot Chat log.

Not covered: the macOS-specific `spawn EBADF` itself (only Windows was tested, though the fix removes its cause).

Follow-ups, out of scope:
- Limit parallelism inside the SDK's `listSessions` (github/copilot-cli#5282).

title: canvases: keep the last frame while the provider reconnects
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

In the Agents window, sending a chat message could make an open canvas show "The canvas provider is temporarily unavailable." for several seconds, after which the page reloaded from scratch. No issue was filed for this.

When the agent host relaunches the Copilot runtime on send (`Session configuration changed, refreshing session: operation=sendMessage … reason=clientPluginsChanged`), the canvas handoff withdraws every canvas URL until the replacement runtime republishes it. The client disposed the canvas browser view as soon as its URL disappeared. In Insiders agent host and AHP transport logs, the URL went missing at the exact moment of each restart and returned 3–15 seconds later.

## Change

- **`CanvasService`** keeps the browser view of a canvas whose source disappears, and loads the returning URL into that view in place (`loadURL`) instead of creating a new view. A changed live URL is also loaded in place. Canvases that the agent host removes still close and dispose their view.
- **`CanvasEditor`** hides the native view behind its last frame while the provider is away. The frame is dimmed and shows a "Reconnecting to the canvas provider…" status (`role="status"`), so the dead page can't be used or mistaken for a live one. The editor keeps its own copy of that frame and ignores the retained page's loading events while frozen, so a page that reloads or fails in the background can't clear the frame or replace the status. The page is revealed again only after the fresh URL has loaded. If no provider returns within 30 seconds, the status changes to "The canvas provider is unavailable." and the frame stays. This follows the SDK guidance for `session.canvas.unavailable`: keep the panel mounted and show a reconnecting affordance until `session.canvas.opened` arrives.

When the provider doesn't come back:

| Case | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Runtime restart throws | The host publishes no canvases, so the tab closes (unchanged) |
| Runtime restarts but the provider fails to start | Handoff reconciliation drops the canvas, so the tab closes (unchanged; verified live, 0.6 seconds) |
| Provider drops mid-session and never returns | Frozen frame, then "unavailable" after 30 seconds (previously "temporarily unavailable" indefinitely) |

Out of scope: avoiding the runtime restart itself when the client plugin set changes. That relaunch is what withdraws the URL; this PR only handles the client side.

## How to test

1. Set `chat.canvases.enabled` to `true`, start a Copilot CLI session in the Agents window, and open a canvas.
2. Add a file under `.github/agents/` in the session's workspace, then send any message. The agent host relaunches the runtime: the canvas shows its dimmed last frame with "Reconnecting to the canvas provider…", and the same tab then shows the fresh page.
3. To see the unavailable state, make the canvas extension exit on start, then ask the agent to call `extensions_reload`. After 30 seconds the status reads "The canvas provider is unavailable." and the frame stays.

## Validation

All commands were run after rebasing on `origin/main` (`2ca5edc0cd3`):

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/canvasEditor.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/canvasEditorTelemetry.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/canvasService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/test/common/canvas.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasService.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasWorkingSet.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/canvases/test/electron-browser/sessionCanvasRegistryService.test.ts`: **passed** (115 tests, including the two A → B → A regression tests and the frozen-frame/loading-events test; each fails without its fix)
- `npm run typecheck-client`: **passed**
- `npm run eslint -- <changed .ts files>`: **passed**
- `node build/stylelint.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/canvases/electron-browser/media/sessionCanvas.css`: **passed**
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts --grep "<handoff failure tests>"` (unchanged host tests covering restart failures; run before the rebase): **passed**

Live validation in a Code OSS dev build on macOS: Agents window, signed-in Copilot CLI session, and a demo canvas extension that displays its provider port and page load time. Results come from workbench DOM sampling (every 25 ms), Chrome DevTools targets, and the agent host log. A captioned recording is available.

- **Before this change:** "The canvas provider is temporarily unavailable." and then "Loading canvas…"; the page was replaced by a new browser view.
- **With this change, provider returns:** the dimmed last frame with "Reconnecting…" showed for 0.9 seconds. The same browser view (unchanged DevTools target) loaded the new port and was revealed.
- **With this change, provider fails on restart:** the tab closed after 0.6 seconds.
- **With this change, mid-session drop that never returns:** "The canvas provider is unavailable." appeared after 30.0 seconds and the frame stayed.
- **Same drop, with the dead page reloading itself into an error page while frozen:** the host cleared its own screenshot 0.6 seconds into the outage, but the frozen frame and "Reconnecting…" status stayed, followed by "unavailable" after 30.0 seconds. "The canvas page failed to load." never appeared.

## Review follow-up

Two automated reviews (design and code) found one race introduced by in-place navigation: if a source changes A → B → A before B finishes loading, the editor and the service both still treated A as loaded, so the canvas stayed on B. The second commit makes an in-place load invalidate both, and adds a regression test for each.

The reviews also found that loading or error events from the retained page could overwrite the reconnect status, and that an error load cleared the host's screenshot, removing the frozen frame. The third commit gives the editor its own frozen-frame layer and ignores loading events while reconnecting.

Known follow-ups, not addressed here:
- Reconnect state lives in the editor pane, so switching away during an outage and back shows the text-only "temporarily unavailable" message instead of the frozen frame.
- In-place navigation does not wait for a replacement network proxy that is still starting; this only affects canvases routed through a remote proxy.

Stacked on #345083, continuing the bounded callback-rule adoption from #345081 and #345049. This layer contains three commits:

title: agentHost: exclude unchanged text from edit ARC
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#10461.

## What and why

Agent Host `editTelemetry.reportEditArc` should not attribute unchanged text between separated changes to the agent. A full-file write that changes two characters around 10,000 unchanged characters should report two original characters, not 10,002. Broad string replacements can have the same problem.

ARC currently prefers tool-input replacement ranges over the character diff already computed for the file edit. This change uses that diff for every tool and removes the tool-range extraction path. Original and retained character/line measures therefore follow the changed ranges, including in the Copilot GitHub mirror.

When the initial diff fails, times out, or does not reconstruct the captured result, ARC is skipped with a warning rather than falling back to whole-file attribution. File-edit persistence and the other edit telemetry paths continue. This deliberately trades incomplete ARC coverage in those cases for avoiding misleading counts.

This corrects replacement geometry, not the separate local batching versus Agent Host per-file observation-count difference. It does not establish which downstream GitHub Copilot Metrics aggregates consume these measures.

## How to test

```powershell
fnm exec --using 24.22.1 -- .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\fileEditTracker.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\shared\arcToolEdit.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\shared\editArcReporter.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\diffWorkerMain.test.ts --reporter dot
```

**Passed: 60 tests.** Regression coverage includes broad write/string tools, LF/CRLF, unchanged interior lines, creation/deletion/no-op edits, and invalid or timed-out diffs. The reporter test verifies both telemetry destinations at 0/60/300 seconds: two changed characters initially, then one retained after overwriting one change.

A separate diagnostic using the compiled real diff and ARC tracker confirmed that the 10,000-character single-line example reports `originalCharCount: 2`.

title: build: capture Windows network failure diagnostics
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Related to [microsoft/vscode-engineering#3684](<url>).

## What changes

Build maintainers get a bounded snapshot of the Windows agent's network state when client packaging, or an earlier step in the shared compile workflow, fails. Capture happens before 1ES stops Network Isolation, so the next rare DNS failure can be investigated using evidence from the affected agent rather than depending on a reproduction.

For example, `az artifacts universal` can exhaust its retries because `vsblob.dev.azure.com` cannot be resolved. Previously, maintainers had the command error and cleanup messages but little structured evidence about the listener or resolver state. With this change, the failed run also provides:

- Listener PIDs/start times, configured DNS servers, and local port-53 ownership.
- Available recent crash records for the listener and DNS Client events for the affected hostname.
- Explicit `unavailable`/`notCollected` states, bounded reason codes, and a completion marker, distinguishing missing evidence from an empty successful query or interrupted capture.

CI and flaky-build jobs include the snapshot under `.build/logs/network` in their existing logs artifact. Product compile jobs publish a dedicated `network-diagnostics-windows-<arch>-compile-<attempt>` artifact when capture has initialized.

## Scope and safeguards

Collection is failure-only, with a 45-second process-tree deadline, at most 64 records and 64 KiB per JSON section, and a one-hour event lookback. It projects selected fields rather than retaining command lines, event messages, credentials, or environment/state files. Listener log files are inventoried by name, size, and modification time only; their raw contents have not been reviewed for retention and are not copied.

This improves diagnosis, not DNS reliability by itself: it does not establish a listener root cause or resolve the linked umbrella issue. Collection is after the existing download retries and cannot recover events that were never logged. The operational guide documents evidence interpretation and a deliberate-failure validation procedure.

## How to test

- `node --test build\lib\test\windowsNetworkDiagnostics.test.ts` — **passed: 9 tests on Windows**, including isolated PowerShell tests for evidence projection, excluded sensitive content, empty versus unavailable sources, record/byte limits, interrupted captures, and YAML wiring.
- A live, read-only Windows capture completed and explicitly reported the disabled DNS operational channel and missing 1ES log directory as unavailable; other sections were written. This did not alter DNS or isolation settings.
- Azure Pipelines **preview-only** expansion using the actual collector step and artifact definition succeeded: capture precedes Stop Network Isolation, and artifact publication follows it. No pipeline was queued for this check.

**Before rollout:** hosted-pool permissions, event availability, and actual artifact publication still need validation. Use a non-publishing validation run with a harmless injected failure before the collector; confirm evidence is retained and the original failure remains visible. No hosted-agent execution or actual artifact upload was performed for this change.

title: Resolve Codex binaries from the selected main package
body:
## Summary

Fixes #342628.

The Agent Host previously looked for the Codex platform package directly under `<sdkRoot>/node_modules`. While this works for flat structures (like npm), package managers like **pnpm** (with isolated mode) or **Yarn** (with the pnpm linker) may keep platform dependencies within the main package's private dependency tree or behind symlinks. 

Although the configured `sdkRoot` contained the documented `node_modules/@openai/codex` and the Codex CLI ran successfully, Agent Host could not locate the native binary and failed to start a Codex session.

### Solution
- **Real-Path Resolution**: Resolve the selected main package's manifest (`package.json`) to its real path, then use `createRequire()` anchored there to locate the platform package. This accurately follows the installed dependency tree (including symlinks) without hardcoding a specific package manager's physical layout.
- **Vendor Fallback**: If platform-package resolution returns `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`, fall back to checking the main package's `vendor` directory (matching Codex CLI behavior).
- **Error Handling**: Malformed platform manifests and missing or non-executable binaries are reported as errors; these failures do not trigger the vendor fallback.

---

## Package-Manager Compatibility

| Tool | Mode / Layout | Behavior After This Change |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **npm** | Standard `node_modules` | Resolves the platform package relative to the selected main package. |
| **pnpm** | `isolated` | Follows the main package's real path to resolve its private platform dependency. |
| **pnpm** | `hoisted` | Resolves the platform package relative to the selected main package. |
| **Yarn** | Classic / `node-modules` | Resolves the platform package relative to the selected main package. |
| **Yarn** | `pnpm` linker | Follows symlinks to resolve the main package's platform dependency. |
| **Yarn** | PnP | Still requires `node_modules/@openai/codex` (PnP-only SDK roots are currently not supported). |

---

## Validation & Testing

Validated on **Linux x64** with **Node 24.22.1** and **Codex 0.163.0**:

- [x] Ran `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` successfully.
- [x] Passed targeted ESLint and hygiene checks for the 3 modified files.
- [x] Unit Tests: `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/codex/codexPackagePaths.test.ts --grep 'codex package paths'` (**20 tests passing**).
- [x] Integration / Fixture Testing:
  - Tested with real standalone Agent Host and Codex subprocesses across **npm**, **pnpm v10.34.5** (`isolated`), and **Yarn Classic v1.22.22**.
  - Verified nested dependency and main-package `vendor` layout fixtures (using the Codex 0.163.0 binary).
  - Confirmed that each server exited normally and completed cleanup successfully.

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
