* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

The new-session composer in the Agents window shows banners below its input: a getting-started tip, the customization migration notice, and the experimental worktree suggestion hint (#344870, #344956). They used to stack on top of each other. This adds `NewSessionBanners`, which makes them show one at a time:

- Each banner registers with a numeric priority and an observable of its own conditions, and renders only while it is the banner that shows: the one with the highest priority of those that want to show. The priorities are worktree suggestion 300, migration notice 200 and tip 100 (`NewSessionBannerPriority`). Ties go to the banner registered first, and the gaps leave room for future banners.
- No banner shows until the user created 3 sessions in the Agents window (`NEW_SESSION_BANNERS_MIN_CREATED_SESSIONS`). The arbiter enforces this for every banner. The only exception is a developer preview of the worktree suggestion (**Developer: Preview Worktree Suggestion...**), which promises to work with too few sessions.
- A banner that makes way while it has keyboard focus returns focus to the input.

title: Engineering - generate the CG NOTICE before compiling in the Quality job
body:
Every platform's Compile job blocks in **Apply CG NOTICE** until the Quality job uploads the `notice_output` artifact. `notice@0` often times out against the NOTICE API after a fixed ~241 s and is retried, so the artifact can arrive minutes after the compile jobs need it.

Across 42 scheduled insiders from Oct 14 to 29:
- **15 builds hit at least one timeout**, with 28 failed calls in total. The retry usually succeeds in about 30 s.
- In those builds the macOS Compile jobs waited up to **11.7 min**. On macOS that wait is on the release path (Compile, then Sign, then Publish).
- Linux and Windows waited up to 10.3 min.

## Change

This moves the NOTICE steps of the Quality job to right after dependency install, ahead of `Compile & Hygiene` (~3.3 min). The moved steps are:
- built-in extension CG details
- Component Detection
- `notice@0`
- the cache fallback
- the merged NOTICE upload

`notice_output` is ready about 3.3 min earlier. That absorbs a single NOTICE API timeout entirely. The Quality job isn't on the critical path; it finishes 10–20 min in, long before Publish. No step changed, and the YAML still holds the same set of steps. A new `Remove NOTICE intermediates` step deletes `.oss-build-out` and `ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt` before the lint checks. ESLint and hygiene would otherwise reject them, and the outputs are already staged.

**Why scanning before compile is safe:** Component Detection reads manifests and lockfiles. Its debug log on 490496 shows that the only files compile adds to the scan are 6 `out-build/**/cgmanifest.json` copies of the `src/**/cgmanifest.json` files it already reads, so the detected components are the same. `notice@0` still runs after Component Detection, so the NOTICE comes from this build's snapshot.

`notice@0` has no request-timeout or retry input (only `outputfile`, `outputformat` and `additionaldata`), so the 240 s wait can't be shortened from the pipeline. A step `timeoutInMinutes` cancel wouldn't be retried.

## Validation

- Official-parameter def 111 run [490960](<url>), on insider 490752's commit with Publish off. It failed in `Compile & Hygiene` on the intermediates, which is now fixed. The `notice_output` it uploaded is byte-identical to 490752's: `ThirdPartyNotices.new.txt`, `.extensions.txt` and `.generated.txt`. Only `notice-meta.txt` differs, in its build and branch fields.
- Rerun with the fix: [491073](<url>), using the same parameters. I'll check that Apply CG NOTICE is green on every platform and that the NOTICE is unchanged.
- YAML parses. The job has the same steps as before plus the cleanup step.

> Authored with Copilot

title: authentication: add default scopes request for GitHub sessions
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Why

First-party GitHub consumers each hardcode their own scope list for `authentication.getSession('github', [...])`. When the lists drift, users end up with several GitHub tokens and extra consent prompts. This adds a single, explicit way to ask for "the default GitHub scopes", with `product.json` as the only source of truth.

## What changed

**New proposed API: `authDefaultScopes`**
- Callers pass `{ defaultScopes: true }` in place of the scope list in `vscode.authentication.getSession` (same three overloads). A caller that needs more than the defaults lists every scope explicitly, the normal way.
- Gated with `checkProposedApiEnabled(extension, 'authDefaultScopes')`.
- `[]` / `undefined` are deliberately not reused, because they already mean "any session" in core and in the GitHub provider.

**Core resolution (`AuthenticationService`)**
- Defaults come from `defaultChatAgent.providerScopes[0]`.
- Only `defaultChatAgent.provider.default.id` (`github`) and `.enterprise.id` (`github-enterprise`) accept the request. Any other provider, or a missing/empty scope list, throws `Authentication provider '<id>' does not define default scopes.`
- `getSessions` and `createSession` resolve the request to that list and pass it to the provider, so a default request matches exactly, like an explicit scope list.
- The pending "Sign in to use X" menu entries, account picker, session-access requests and ext host request de-duplication handle the new request kind. Client-ID telemetry uses the resolved scopes.

**Migrated callers**
- `extensions/github`: uses `{ defaultScopes: true }`.
- Copilot: `getAlignedSession` and the aligned branch of `getAnyAuthSession`. **Minimal mode and the `user:email` / `read:user` fallbacks are unchanged** (still an open decision).
- `DefaultAccountService.signIn` uses `{ defaultScopes: true }`, or an explicit list of the defaults plus extras when chat setup passes extra scopes. It still accepts the legacy `user:email` / `read:user` sessions when matching.
- Cloud sandbox: gets the default list from the shared helper instead of `FALLBACK_SCOPES`, and keeps its own fallback to the narrowest session with extra scopes.
- Mission Control sharing: drops its hardcoded list.

## Reviewer notes
- Builds without `providerScopes` (e.g. the dev fallback product) now get a clear error from these callers instead of a silent hardcoded list.
- Because the proposed overload is declared last, `sinon.stub(authentication, 'getSession')` infers the default-scopes signature; Copilot's `session.test.ts` needed a cast. A single overload taking the union would avoid this.
- Not included: external extensions (Pull Requests, GitHub Repositories, Live Share) and the distro `product.json` allowlist.

## How to test

Automated (all passed locally):
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run vscode-dts-compile-check`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` on `authenticationService.test.ts`, `extHostAuthentication.integrationTest.ts`, `defaultAccount.test.ts`, `cloudSandboxApiService.test.ts`, `missionControlContribution.test.ts`: 715 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadAuthentication.integrationTest.ts`: 6 passing
- `npm run eslint` on changed files: clean
- Earlier commits on this branch (unchanged by the latest one): `extensions/copilot` `npm run typecheck` and `npx vitest run src/platform/authentication/test/node/session.spec.ts` (33 passing); `tsc -p extensions/github/tsconfig.json --noEmit`

Manual:
1. Sign out of GitHub, then use a Git/GitHub feature (e.g. Publish to GitHub). The consent prompt should request `read:user`, `user:email`, `repo`, `workflow`.
2. Sign in to Copilot. No second GitHub prompt should appear, and Accounts should show a single GitHub session.
3. With only a GitHub token that has extra scopes (e.g. `gist`), Git and Copilot ask to sign in for the default scopes, as they do today with explicit lists.

title: update: remind users to update once their build is two months old
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

People can stay on a very old build without noticing, for example when background update checks fail silently behind a proxy, or when updates are turned off. They then run into problems that newer builds have already fixed. This adds a gentle reminder once a build gets old.

### What changed

- **New `OutdatedBuildReminderContribution`** (desktop only). Once the build is **60 days old** (based on `product.date`), it shows a banner: _"This version of Visual Studio Code is 3 months old. Update to get the latest features and fixes."_
- **At most once every 30 days.** Windows claim each interval atomically in shared application storage (`compareAndSwapApplicationSharedValue()`), so only one window shows it. It checks at startup in the last-focused window and again whenever a window gains focus, so windows left open for weeks are covered too.
- **Shown to everyone on desktop:** Stable and Insiders, every `update.mode`, and policy-managed installs. Web is excluded because a browser client can't update itself.
- **The actions follow the update state** and change live:
  - Idle: **Check for Updates** and **Open Download Page**
  - Available, downloaded, or ready: **Download Update**, **Install Update**, or **Restart to Update**
  - Updates disabled (by setting, policy, or running as admin): **Open Download Page**
  - Checking or downloading: keeps the current actions
- **Agents window:** it never creates the banner part, so it shows a sticky notification with the same message and actions instead. That notification uses a new `NotificationTelemetryId.UpdateOutdatedBuildReminder`.
- **Kill switch:** the new setting `update.showOutdatedBuildReminder` (default on) is experiment-controlled (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`). To turn the reminder off for everyone, set the ExP treatment `config.update.showOutdatedBuildReminder` to `false`; open windows hide a visible reminder right away. Users can also turn it off in Settings, and a value they set wins over the experiment. To try it locally, set `"experiments.override.config.update.showOutdatedBuildReminder": false`.
- **Experiment trigger:** `experimentTrigger` is logged when a build is old enough for the reminder, before the setting is read and only when the user has not set it, so a triggered scorecard can be limited to users who are actually on old builds.
- The banner uses the neutral style and the lowest banner priority, so Restricted Mode and the managed-settings update banner take precedence. It is announced to screen readers with `status()`.

### Worth discussing

- "Everyone" includes people who can't update, such as installs pinned by policy or on OS versions we no longer support. They will see the reminder monthly, with only the download-page link.
- The banner itself has no telemetry (banners have none built in). The Agents-window notification gets the standard notification telemetry.

### Demo


<url>


### How to test

1. In the repo root, create `product.overrides.json` (gitignored, and only read when running from sources) with a `date` at least 60 days in the past:
  ```json
  { "date": "2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z", "downloadUrl": "<url>" }
  ```
2. Launch Code OSS with a fresh `--user-data-dir`. A few seconds after startup, the banner shows the build's age. Dev builds have updates disabled, so only **Open Download Page** is offered.
3. Close the banner and run **Developer: Reload Window**. The banner stays hidden; it would return after 30 days.
4. Delete `product.overrides.json` afterwards.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/test/common/notificationTelemetry.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: 26 passing
- `npm run eslint -- <blob>.ts <blob>.test.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/update/browser/update.contribution.ts src/vs/platform/notification/common/notificationTelemetry.ts src/vs/platform/update/common/update.config.contribution.ts`: passed
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- Hygiene pre-commit hook: passed
- Manual check in Code OSS using the steps above, recorded in the demo video.

title: Recognize userPromptTransformed plugin hooks in Copilot sessions
body:
## Why

An Agent Plugin whose only contribution is a `userPromptTransformed` hook appears enabled in VS Code, but never reaches Copilot. Adding an unrelated `sessionStart` hook makes the same prompt-transform hook run.

The platform parser drops the event, and the workbench also filters it out of the recognized hook types. With no recognized contributions left, VS Code skips forwarding the plugin to the agent host.

This recognizes `userPromptTransformed` through both layers and adds its SDK adapter. Successive commands receive the previous command's transformed prompt and return `modifiedTransformedPrompt` to Copilot. The original submitted prompt stays unchanged. Hook availability remains specific to Copilot.

## Testing

Regression tests cover discovery and forwarding of a plugin containing only this hook, prompt replacement, sequential transformations, empty replacements, failed commands, and isolation between messages. The affected Node and workbench suites pass (491 tests), along with client typechecking and targeted lint.

The original failure and the `sessionStart` workaround were reproduced in installed VS Code 1.144.0. The patched source has been validated through the build and tests above; it has not yet been exercised in an interactive Copilot session.

To check in Copilot, install an Agent Plugin with only `com.github.copilot/hooks/hooks.json` contributing `userPromptTransformed`. Have its command append a recognizable marker to `transformedPrompt` and return it as `modifiedTransformedPrompt`. Start a fresh Copilot session and verify the command runs and the model receives the marker without adding a `sessionStart` hook or a skill.

- `test/e2e/cli.stest.ts` has been marked `ssuite.skip` since it was added in November 2025, so CI never runs it. Running it locally needs a personal GitHub token and live model calls.
- It has had no commits in the last two months, and no PR or doc mentions running it. Since April 30, its only edits have been 1–3 line compile fixes by people changing Copilot CLI code (7 edits by 3 people): upkeep with nothing in return.

### 2. Remove dead simulation helpers and a stale baseline copy
- **Helpers that lost their last caller when #344484 retired the legacy panel and inline simulations:**
  - the inline chat strategy helpers (`simulateInlineChatWithStrategy`, `simulateInlineChatIntent`, `forInline`, `forInlineChatIntent`) and the two `EditTestStrategy` members only they used
  - 16 assertion helpers in `stestUtil.ts` and `outcomeValidators.ts`
  - `compileTSWorkspace` and its private helpers in `tsc.ts`

- **`AIEvaluationService`** (`src/extension/testing/node/aiEvaluationService.tsx`). Its only consumer was the deleted `assertCriteriaMetAsync`, so the simulator registered it for nothing.
- **`test/simulation/baseline.old.json`**, a scratch file committed with the June 2025 import. 1,539 of its 1,667 entries are scenarios that no longer exist. `script/compareStestAlternativeRuns.ts` rewrites it from `HEAD`'s `baseline.json` on every run, so it's now in `.gitignore`. The simulation workbench reads the per-run `baseline.old.json.txt` in the output folder, not this file.

## How dead code was identified
Each removed export has no reference anywhere in `extensions/copilot` (sources, tests, scripts, `.vscode`, `package.json`) other than its declaration or other removed code. I re-ran the check until it found nothing new. Kept on purpose:
- `toFile`, `assertInlineEdit` and `assertNoDiagnosticsAsync`: `feedbackReporter.ts` generates stest code that calls them.
- `logComments` in `review.stest.ts`: a debugging aid.
- Next-edit-owned code (`test/simulation/inlineEdit`, `test/pipeline`).

## Not in this PR
No remaining in-repo suite uses these, but they may have users outside this repo, so their owners should decide:
- The `--sidebar` and `--inline` external-scenario modes, and the panel code mapper simulator.
- The simulation workbench's AML results mode.

title: Agents: keep the grid answerable while the panel alignment moves its views
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Switching the panel alignment of the Agents window (center ↔ justify) moves the editor and the panel in the workbench grid. The grid lays out its views partway through a move, and the Sessions Part then asked it whether the side pane shows (`DesktopWorkbench.isEditorPaneVisible` → `Grid.isViewVisible(editorPartView)`) while the editor was taken out. This logged `Splitview: Failed to layout view` with `Invalid grid element`.

While `setPanelAlignment` moves the grid's views, whether the side pane shows is now answered from before the move (`_editorPaneVisibleWhileGridMoves`), the same way the alignment already pins the editor's maximum dimensions.

No issue: found while splitting the Agents window layout work into independent blocks.

**How to test**
1. Agents window, desktop layout, with the editor and the panel showing.
2. Switch the panel alignment between center and justify several times.

title: chat: reduce full scans on sandbox feed renewal
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Routine renewal of the cloud session-update connection currently requests a full task inventory scan even when the old connection remains available until its replacement is ready. This can repeatedly trigger expensive paginated reads.

- Distinguish seamless renewal, reconnect after a connection gap, and individual task-change hints.
- Use incremental inventory catch-up after seamless renewal, while retaining full recovery after connection gaps and the existing periodic full-scan requirement.
- Preserve task-change hints coalesced with renewal, including targeted checks for removed or inaccessible tasks.
- Preserve incremental intent when renewals queue behind an in-flight scan; an explicitly queued full refresh still takes precedence.
- Add per-attempt `cloudSandboxDiscovery` telemetry and focused regression coverage across the shared feed, API, and Agents Window provider.

Polling intervals, initial/manual full scans, uncapped pagination, and sandbox-identification rules remain unchanged. This does not revert the completeness fixes in #341823. Entries unavailable through incremental discovery still rely on a subsequent periodic/manual full scan.

## Telemetry

`cloudSandboxDiscovery` reports the trigger, requested/actual mode, outcome, elapsed time, parsed page count, list HTTP attempts, unique returned tasks, returned sandbox tasks, sandbox summaries absent from or different from the starting cache, and checkpoint advancement.

The event emits once per API discovery attempt, including partial, failed, and cancelled attempts. It uses existing telemetry consent controls and adds no task IDs, task content, repository names, URLs, or cursors. Every number and boolean is classified as a measurement. Page counts are not unique backend pages; changed summaries are a local-cache comparison, not an authoritative server change count. List-attempt counts include issued requests subsequently cancelled, unlike the existing aggregated outcome counter.

## Related changes

- Complements #344841, which fixes following task pagination links.
- Complements #345060, which fixes renewal timing when client clocks differ from the server. This PR does not include that timing change; preserve both behaviors when integrating the overlapping feed code.

## Validation

Successful validation from this implementation was reused for PR creation:

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed, including the final incremental output refresh.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACM -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --` — passed for all 11 changed files before committing; the final comment-only changes also passed targeted lint.

## How to test

2. Interrupt the old connection before its replacement is ready. Verify full recovery still occurs.
3. Check that task hints during renewal still refresh the named tasks, and that an overlapping manual full refresh is not downgraded.
4. Inspect `cloudSandboxDiscovery` events to compare renewal-triggered scan modes, page/attempt counts, and outcomes after rollout.

title: chat: give the narrow image batch fixture its own images (fixes flake)
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes the intermittent `<blob>` screenshot change, most recently reported on an unrelated PR in [#344959 (comment)](<url>). This follows #343082, which fixed a different flake in the same fixtures.

## Cause

- The Screenshots job renders fixtures with 8 workers. Each worker renders its contiguous slice of fixtures in a single page, without reloading. `BatchGridNarrow` renders right after `BatchGrid`.
- All batch fixtures draw their images with the same `createImage(width, height, index)` calls, so they produce byte-identical `data:` URLs. `BatchGrid` is 760 px wide, so it draws them larger.
- Chromium appears to draw the narrow grid's thumbnails from those larger decodes when they are still around. Only portrait thumbnails are affected. They are drawn at the smallest scale: 68 px tall from 1356 px, about 1/20, versus about 1/15 for squares and landscapes. Whether the decodes are reused varies from run to run, so the antialiased edges of the sun and mountain move by a few levels.

## Evidence

**CI history.** I fetched the screenshot service manifests for about 700 `main` commits. Since its last intentional change (#343609), `BatchGridNarrow/Light` has had two hashes:

- `12dec515`, 145 times.
- `35f07299`, 3 times today (0f33e8274d, fc8954c90f, d41a36a4d8). Each time the next commit went back to `12dec515`.

The other `BatchGrid*` fixtures kept a single hash. I checked two flipped and two normal runs: they used the same runner image, Chromium 149.0.7827.55, `node_modules` cache, and 1949 fixtures. The difference is 772 px with a max channel delta of 12/255, all in portrait thumbnails #3, #5 and #8. The layout is identical.

**Local repro.** I used a small Playwright script on macOS that renders fixtures in one page like the CLI does, with the same `--disable-partial-raster` launch flag. Before this PR, the narrow grid's output depends on what rendered earlier in the page:

| Rendered before `BatchGridNarrow` | Before this PR | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `BatchGridLoading` (no images) | `1fe68475` | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGridLoading`, `BatchGrid` | `df6ef8b8`: portraits #3, #5, #8, #10 differ | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGridLoading`, `BatchGridInProgress` | `472139da`: portraits #3, #5 differ | `77715b40` |
| `BatchGrid`, `BatchGridInProgress`, `BatchGridLoading` | `472139da` | `77715b40` |

The tiles that change are the portraits that the preceding fixture rendered. `BatchGridInProgress` leaves #8 generating and has no #10. Each sequence gave the same hash on repeated runs.

**Same mechanism as CI.** I compared CI's flake (`35f07299` − `12dec515`) with the local leak after `BatchGrid` (`df6ef8b8` − `1fe68475`) pixel by pixel. The leak covers 99% of CI's changed pixels, and the deltas correlate with Pearson r = −0.99. So on `main` the usual render (145 of 148) is the one drawn from `BatchGrid`'s decodes, and the rare one is the clean render.

## Fix

`renderBatchGrid` takes a `firstVariant` offset, and `BatchGridNarrow` passes 10. Its images keep the same palettes and dimensions but are labelled `11 / …` to `20 / …`, so no other fixture renders the same bytes. Other fixtures are unchanged.

## Expected screenshot changes

The screenshot report on this PR should list only `BatchGridNarrow/Light` as changed, because of the new labels and portrait edges no longer drawn from `BatchGrid`'s decodes. It is not in `blocks-ci-screenshots.md`, so no baseline update is needed.

## How to test

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed, on the branch rebased onto current `main`.
- `npm run eslint -- <blob>.fixture.ts`: passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer render --project ./test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --workers 1 --fixture-id-regex '(chatAutoModeResolutionContentPart/Routing|chatGeneratedImages/BatchGrid(Narrow)?)/Light$'`, 3 times: passed. With this PR, `BatchGridNarrow/Light` was `77715b40` every time, and `BatchGrid/Light` was unchanged at `a3344193`. With the old code, this exact order gave a stable, non-leaking `1fe68475` on my machine, so this command confirms the fix is stable but does not reproduce the flake. The table above varied the preceding fixtures to show the leak.
- The real confirmation is the hash history on `main`: after merge, `BatchGridNarrow/Light` should keep a single hash.

title: chat: back off short-lived session feed connections
body:
Back off session-feed reconnects when sockets repeatedly complete their handshake but close shortly afterward.

- Reuse `computeReconnectDelay` for exponential delays with a one-second base, a 60-second cap, and upper-half jitter.
- Reset the attempt counter only after 60 seconds continuously connected, not immediately after a successful handshake.
- Own the healthy-connection timer in the socket's disposable store.
- Preserve scheduled credential renewal, authoritative refresh after reconnect, and the existing behavior that failed HTTP negotiation or malformed messages stop feed retries for the current lifetime.

The shared delay helper now accepts only the policy fields it actually reads; existing remote-agent-host callers and delay calculations are unchanged.

title: chat: use server-relative session feed renewal
body:
Use the session-feed service's `expires_in` and `reconnect_in` millisecond durations instead of comparing its renewal timestamp to the client's wall clock.

- Preserve the optional relative fields through the typed task client and serialized IPC.
- Validate the relative fields as a pair, require renewal before expiry, and reject delays that would overflow a native timer.
- Subtract monotonic WebSocket-setup elapsed time before scheduling renewal.
- Preserve the existing absolute-timestamp behavior when an older server omits both relative fields.

## Problem

In the Agents window, **Merge Changes** on a worktree session silently does nothing when the parent repository has uncommitted changes. title: Agent Host: let the Copilot sandbox read files and folders the user attaches
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Problem

With terminal sandboxing on, the agent can't read a file the user attaches from outside the workspace. Its Read fails with "Outside the sandbox's readable paths", and it asks the user to change the sandbox policy. That breaks the main scenario of the new **+ > Files…** entry (#344792): attaching a file from `~/Desktop`. Attached paths were never added to the sandbox's readable paths.

## Repro

1. Turn on terminal sandboxing and create `~/Desktop/mockup.txt`.
2. In the Agents window, start a session in any folder. Click **+**, then **Files…**, and attach `mockup.txt`.
3. Send `Summarize the attached file.`

## What changes

- Files and folders attached to a message become **read-only** in that session's sandbox before the turn runs. The grant covers only the exact attached path, lasts for the session, and is never saved to settings. Denied paths still win.
- An attached folder that contains the workspace or another writable folder isn't granted, so it can't make that folder read-only. The agent asks for specific files instead.
- In Manual permissions, reading an attached file or folder no longer asks "Allow reading file outside of workspace?". Writes still ask, and so does a symlink that escapes an attached folder.
- If an organization's managed policy sets its own read-only list, attachments aren't added. The agent then says the file is blocked by policy and asks the user to paste its content, instead of asking them to change the policy.

**Open question:** should an explicit attachment be allowed to widen a managed read-only list, for example behind a runtime-owned managed setting? This PR keeps the conservative default.

title: test: stop the last 8 unit test suites from leaking registrations
body:
Follow-up to #344872. It fixes the 8 unit test suites that its registry leak check allowlisted, and removes the allowlist, so every suite now has to dispose what it registers.

## What each suite leaked, and the fix

| Suite | Leak | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `RetryChatAction` | `registerChatTitleActions()` in `setup`, never disposed | The helper returns a `DisposableStore`. The suite registers in `suiteSetup` and disposes in `suiteTeardown` |
| `Chat code-block action telemetry` | `registerChatCodeBlockActions()`, never disposed | Same |
| `ChatMcpAuthenticationContentPart` | `registerChatAccessibilityActions()`, never disposed | Same |
| `Inline chat zone widget — menu contributions` | `registerChatContextActions()` disposed its own actions but not the prompt file actions (`registerPromptActions()`, the existing `TODO@jrieken`) | `registerPromptActions()` and the 6 helpers it calls return a `DisposableStore`, and `registerChatContextActions()` adds it to its store |
| `AgentSessionsActions` | `registerAction2` ran when the file loaded and was disposed in `suiteTeardown`, so the suite *unregistered* something it didn't register | Register in `suiteSetup` |
| `ExtHostLanguageFeatureCommands` | `MainThreadCommands` (`_generateCommandsDocumentation` and the extension host's commands) was never disposed | Dispose it in `suiteTeardown` |
| `Edit session sync` | `EditSessionsContribution`, which `_register`s its actions, was never disposed | Dispose it in `suiteTeardown` |
| `Sessions - Layout Actions` | Dynamic imports of contributions in `suiteSetup` add permanent module-level registrations | Await the same dynamic imports at the top level of the file, so they load with the file and are part of every suite's baseline |

Product behavior is unchanged. The product callers of these helpers run them once at module load and ignore the returned store, the same way they already use `registerChatExecuteActions()` and `registerChatToolActions()`.

## Validation

- **The 8 suites, without the allowlist:**
  - All 8 files together: 129 passing in Chromium and 130 in Electron, with no leak-check failures.
  - Each file alone in Chromium: 14, 51, 22, 2, 9, 17, 5 and 9 passing.
- **Full Chromium browser suite:** 49,917 passing with no leak-check failures. The only failure is the unrelated local `Extensions viewlet notification layout` network-error test.

- eslint is clean on all changed files, and tsc reports no errors in the touched areas.

title: agentHost: map completed edit parts and review diffs through resourceUris
body:
Fixes #344969

### Problem

In remote editor windows (such as WSL, SSH, or Dev Containers), clicking an edited file pill or review entry in the chat window causes the editor to report that the file does not exist and prompts to create it (`FILE_NOT_FOUND`). Concurrently, Allow and Discard/Accept operations fail or behave unexpectedly.

While PR #342158 (#342112) updated pending tool confirmations to map edit resources through `resourceUris.fromAgentHost(edit.resource)`, the same mapping was missing in several other areas:
1. Completed tool call edit pills (`completedToolCallToEditParts` and `fileEditToExternalEdit`) wrapped file URIs into `toAgentHostUri(normalized.resource, connectionAuthority)` instead of using the connection's `resourceUris.fromAgentHost(...)`.
2. Response file changes in `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider` and `changesetEditToEntryDiff` formatted `modifiedURI` with `toAgentHostUri(...)` rather than `this._connection.resourceUris.fromAgentHost(...)`.
3. Working set review changes in `toWorkingSetFileChanges` and `agentHostSessionInputPills` created diffs without passing `resourceUris`. Because `file.diff.modifiedURI` was wrapped in `vscode-agent-host://` instead of the workspace URI, editor review model reference creation (`createModelReference`), dirty state checking (`textFileService.isDirty`), document saving, and change tracking failed to target the client's workspace document.

### Fix

- Updated `completedToolCallToEditParts` and `fileEditToExternalEdit` in `stateToProgressAdapter.ts` to accept `resourceUris: IAgentHostResourceUriMapper` (defaulting to `createAgentHostResourceUriMapper(connectionAuthority)`) and map `uri` and `originalUri` via `resourceUris.fromAgentHost(...)`.
- Updated callers in `agentHostSessionHandler.ts` and `stateToProgressAdapter.ts:turnsToHistory` to pass the connection's `resourceUris`.
- Updated `agentHostChangesetFileToEntryDiff` and `changesetEditToEntryDiff` in `agentHostResponseFileChanges.ts` to accept `resourceUris` and map `modifiedURI` through `resourceUris.fromAgentHost(...)`.
- Updated `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider._convertFileEdit` and `_changesetEditToEntryDiff` to map through `this._connection.resourceUris`.
- Updated `toWorkingSetFileChanges` in `agentHostEditReview.ts` and callers in `agentHostSessionInputPills.ts` to pass `connection.resourceUris`.
- Added unit tests in `stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts` and `agentHostResponseFileChanges.test.ts` verifying that completed file edits and changeset diffs map through the connection's resource URI mapper across both local and remote authorities while preserving content snapshots.

### Tests

- Added regression tests in `stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts` verifying that `completedToolCallToEditParts` maps completed file edits through `resourceUris` for both local and remote authorities.
- Added regression tests in `agentHostResponseFileChanges.test.ts` verifying that `agentHostChangesetFileToEntryDiff` maps changeset diffs through `resourceUris` across local and remote authorities.

title: eslint: prefer events and observables over callback dependencies
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Add `local/code-prefer-event-or-observable`, an opt-in suggestion rule for callback dependencies in constructors and public APIs. The diagnostic recommends events for notifications, observables for changing values, and an injected service or return value for request/response behavior. There is deliberately no automatic fix because these changes affect API design and ownership.

This PR includes two bounded migrations and enables the rule only for those cleaned-up modules:

- MCP main-thread transport: replace the stop/send constructor closures with the existing typed extension-host RPC proxy and server ID.
- Extension-host quick input: replace disposal constructor callbacks with a one-shot disposal event. The subscriber owns and evicts its registrations; standard disposable bases and a disposable sessions map manage cleanup. Preserve the existing cleanup-before-notification order.

The rule/MCP change, quick-input migration, and disposal review fixes are kept in separate commits. Other areas are left for follow-up PRs. No linked issue.

## Rollout and limitations

- Enabling the rule checks constructors and public methods by default. `checkPublicMethods: false` limits it to constructors.
- Detection is syntax-only, including same-file callback aliases and callable interfaces. Imported callback aliases, inferred callback types, and callback properties nested in options objects are not resolved.
- Ordinary callback call sites, including collection operators, Promise executors, and event/observable subscriptions, are not inspected.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto current `origin/main`:

- `npm run compile-client` — passed; compilation and type checks completed with zero errors.
- `node --test --test-reporter=spec .eslint-plugin-local/tests/code-prefer-event-or-observable.test.ts` — passed, 69 tests.

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

The lifecycle tests cover message routing, disposal idempotency, hidden and live quick-input sessions, stale RPC events, reentrancy, owner teardown, and eviction of 40 completed subscriptions. The disposal-order regression tests failed before the ordering fix and pass afterward.

title: agentHost: restore configured URL approval parity with Local
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #344205.

## What changes

Users who already configured URL approvals in Local should not have to approve the same fetches again when a new chat uses the Copilot Agent Host harness.

Local's fetch tool consults `chat.tools.urls.autoApprove`, but the runtime's `web_fetch` requests were going through a host permission path with no URL-pattern check. Switching harnesses therefore exposed a feature-parity gap: the existing preference stopped taking effect.

For example:

```json
"chat.tools.urls.autoApprove": {
  "<url>": true
}
```

Before this change, Agent Host still displayed "Fetch URL?" for this approved host. After this change, matching fetches proceed using the user's existing approval, including in a new session. This restores the configured URL-approval behavior of Local; it does not introduce a new approval setting or require Allow All.

## Implementation and scope

- Forward the existing global URL approval preference through the configuration-sync path and reuse Local's URL matcher from the platform layer, including its domain/path pattern semantics.
- Require approval for **both requests and responses** before auto-approving a runtime fetch. Local can confirm these separately; the runtime has one permission callback, so request-only or response-only consent conservatively still prompts.
- Treat forwarded approvals as client-owned configuration, so the host cannot revive revoked grants from a persisted snapshot after restart.

This is deliberately scoped parity, not a claim that the two fetch tools are identical. Workspace/folder approvals are not forwarded into host-global configuration shared across windows. The change does not add an "Always Allow This Host" action to the runtime confirmation card or address the separate enterprise network-filter work in #337539. Managed asks and sandbox-bypass requests must still prompt.

## Real Code OSS verification

Tested on Windows in a built-from-source Code OSS window with the real Copilot harness, GPT-5.6 Luna, **Manual permissions**, and isolated user-data, extensions, and shared-data directories. No mocked provider was used.

To reproduce the baseline in the same product build, the compiled permission manager was temporarily replaced with its unmodified version from base `69e9e92f233`; the fixed output was restored before the after-tests. The initial setting approved `<url> and `<url>

The parity column below describes the existing configured-approval contract; the result column records the actual Agent Host OSS runs, not a separate live Local-harness comparison.

| Scenario | Existing URL-approval behavior being matched | Real OSS result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Approved `<url> original host permission manager | The configured approval should suppress confirmation | **Reproduced the gap:** "Fetch URL?" appeared |
| Same approved URL, fixed host permission manager | Reuse the configured approval | Fetched **Example Domain** without a prompt |
| Subsequent fetch to `<url> | A host approval applies to subsequent matching URLs | Completed without a prompt |
| Matching URL in a fresh session | User configuration is not a session-only grant | Completed without a prompt |
| Direct fetch to unapproved `<url> | Approval of one host does not authorize another | Confirmation appeared |
| Remove the `example.com` approval while OSS is running, then fetch it again | Removing an approval restores confirmation | Confirmation returned |
| Approved `httpbin.org` returns HTTP 302 to unapproved `<url> | Approval of the initial host must not silently authorize an unapproved redirect destination | Runtime prompted for **`example.org`**; selecting Skip denied the fetch |

An additional different-path fetch to `<url> proceeded without confirmation but returned HTTP 404 from the server; successful content checks used the root/query URLs above. The redirect test covers the observed single cross-host 302, not every redirect topology. Managed-policy behavior is covered by the permission-flow tests, not by a live enterprise-policy scenario.

### Reproduce manually

1. Set the object-shaped `chat.tools.urls.autoApprove` preference shown above in user settings.
2. Start a new **Copilot** harness chat with **Manual permissions**.
3. Ask it to use built-in `web_fetch` to fetch `<url> then another matching URL. Both should proceed without confirmation.
4. Fetch `<url> confirmation should appear.
5. Add `"<url>": true` to the same setting and fetch `<url> Confirmation should identify `<url> not silently approve the destination.
6. Remove the `example.com` approval and fetch it again; confirmation should return.

<details>
<summary>Executed regression commands and results</summary>

The targeted tests were run before and after the implementation. The initial regression failed because both approved-host requests returned no auto-approval; the fixed runs below passed.

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\sessionPermissions.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentConfigurationService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\common\agentHostSchema.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\common\tools\builtinTools\chatUrlFetchingPatterns.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\common\tools\builtinTools\chatUrlFetchingPaths.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatConfiguration.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\electron-browser\tools\builtinTools\fetchPageTool.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\electron-browser\tools\builtinTools\fetchPageToolPaths.test.ts --reporter dot
```

**Passed: 355 tests; one existing Windows-specific shell-redirect test skipped.**

```powershell
.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentSideEffects.test.ts --reporter dot
```

**Passed: 291 tests**, including URL auto-approval and managed-ask precedence.

The product used for the real OSS verification was built with `node build\next\build-fast.ts` — **passed**.

</details>

title: sanity: require webview assets for artifact validation
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes <url>

## What changes

Artifact sanity tests should not spend a minute waiting for a Markdown preview whose webview bootstrap assets were never uploaded. Server-web validation now requires explicit preparation of the tested commit's Web assets and waits for that stage before starting.

- Reject server-web artifact-sanity configurations without a Product build and `VSCODE_BUILD_WEB=true` during template expansion, before allocating agents.
- Make the macOS, Windows, Alpine and Linux artifact-sanity stages depend on Web. ARM32-only runs, which do not exercise server-web, keep their no-Web path.
- Interrupt preview render/load waits when bootstrap or resource requests fail. Report HTTP status, URLs without credentials/query/fragment, frame URLs, console errors and page errors instead of only a heading timeout.

## Observed failure

[Build 490268: baseline main artifact sanity (no publish)](<url>) tested revision `98da3bad3433b6aa1abf5638cddc014d70739838` with artifact sanity enabled, `VSCODE_PUBLISH=false`, and **`VSCODE_BUILD_WEB=false`**. Its timeline contains no Web stage or CDN upload.

The workbench loaded, but the Markdown preview screenshot displayed **HTTP 404 / `WebContentNotFound` / "The requested content does not exist."** [The failing Run Sanity Tests task](<url>) instead reported a 60-second heading timeout and "Failed webview resources: none observed," because its HTTP error filter did not include the CDN bootstrap URL.

This was a real missing prerequisite in the validation environment, not evidence that the Markdown renderer needed a longer timeout. Nothing in that run was going to upload the files; waiting for its platform archive would not resolve it. The corrective action is a Product validation run with Web explicitly enabled, followed by sanity after the matching assets are uploaded. A successful matching rerun of that exact revision has not been independently verified here; this does not establish shipped-user impact.

## Scenarios and recovery guidance

| Scenario | Before | With this change | Action for the person investigating |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Server-web artifact sanity enabled, Web disabled, as in [490268](<url>) | Platform build proceeds; the preview later times out on missing assets. | Template expansion rejects the incompatible configuration before allocating agents. | Queue a **Product** build with **`VSCODE_BUILD_WEB=true`**. |
| Artifact sanity and Web both enabled, but the upload has not finished | Artifact sanity has no dependency on Web and can race the upload. | Artifact-sanity stages wait for Web to complete successfully. | No manual waiting or retry is needed for ordering. If Web fails, fix that producing stage first. This is a prevented race, not a claim that it caused 490268. |
| Prerequisites are satisfied but a webview asset request still fails | A timeout can obscure the failed request. | The test fails promptly with the status/URL, frames and diagnostic context. | For a 404, verify the same commit/quality's Web upload and asset path; if those are correct, investigate CDN delivery. A 401 or connection failure needs its own authorization/network diagnosis, not a longer timeout or blind retry. |

The configuration error reads:

> Server-web artifact sanity requires a Product build with VSCODE_BUILD_WEB=true (uploads webview assets to the CDN even with VSCODE_PUBLISH=false)

The runtime failure includes the failed request, such as `HTTP 404 <url> and:

> For server-web artifact sanity, verify that the same commit's Web stage uploaded its webview assets before this test.

**Operational consideration:** Web already uploads assets to the shared CDN even with `VSCODE_PUBLISH=false`. This change requires explicit opt-in rather than silently enabling that upload. The Markdown assertion remains enabled; the runtime hint supplies a next investigation step, not an automatic diagnosis of every HTTP/network failure.

## How to test

Validated locally on Windows after removing the standalone diagnostic browser-test suite:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run compile --prefix test/sanity` | Passed |
| `npm run eslint -- test/sanity/src/uiTest.ts test/sanity/src/webviewDiagnostics.ts` | Passed |

One-off local browser fault injection during development exercised bootstrap 404s, resource 401s, connection failures and real service-worker registration against a loopback HTTP 503 server, as well as successful rendering and diagnostic edge cases. The diagnostic implementation is unchanged since that validation. The standalone browser-test suite and its npm command were subsequently removed; no additional browser suite or CI job is included in this PR.

Azure Pipelines preview-only requests (`POST .../_apis/pipelines/111/runs?api-version=7.1`, with `previewRun: true` and the modified YAML supplied as `yamlOverride`) verified five configurations:

- Product + artifact sanity + Web enabled: expands successfully; all four artifact-sanity stages depend on Web.
- Product + server-web artifact sanity + Web disabled: rejected with the prerequisite message.
- CI + server-web artifact sanity + Web enabled: rejected because CI does not produce the Web stage.
- ARM32-only artifact sanity + Web disabled: expands successfully without a Web dependency.
- Artifact sanity disabled + Web disabled: expands successfully.

No product build, actual CDN upload, or end-to-end packaged server-web run was performed for this change.

title: agentHost: record the head when repairing from an older checkpoint
body:
Follow-up to #344992. Addresses its review comment: <url>

### Problem
#344992 added `headSha` to the repair checkpoint that "When No Changes Were Made" merging (`ifUnchanged`) uses as its baseline. A checkpoint saved by an older build has no `headSha`. When a new repair started, it reused that checkpoint unchanged. Repairs can now push from any checkout. If the repair pushed from another worktree while the recorded checkout stayed clean at its old commit, `unchangedForMerge()` still passed, and the repaired head could be merged.

### Fix
When a repair reuses a checkpoint for the current merge generation that has no `headSha`, it now records the head this repair starts from. The checkpoint keeps its recorded chat, directory, and commit, so both the local baseline and the head must stay unchanged. Checkpoints that already have a `headSha` are not changed.

### Validation
- Added a regression test: restore an old-format checkpoint, repair from a chat without a checkout, then move the head while the recorded checkout stays clean. Without the fix the test fails and the repaired head is merged (`mutations: ['merge']`). With the fix, unchanged-only merging turns itself off and nothing is merged.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run` with `githubPullRequestArtifactIntegration`, `artifactIntegrationServerTools`, `artifactServerTools`, `clientArtifactIntegrationEndpoint`, `sessionArtifactRemoval`, and `artifactIntegrations`: passed (232 tests).
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.

title: agentHost: resolve remote Working Set files and track parallel edits
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

This fixes two problems with the session Working Set ("N files changed" above the chat input) in Copilot harness (Agent Host) sessions.

There is no issue for these reports. #308847 shows a similar symptom for file links in chat responses when connected to a Linux server; this PR does not change that code path.

### Remote windows: clicking a changed file opens a path on the client

In a window attached to a remote (WSL, dev container, SSH), the window's own agent host runs on the remote, but its sessions resolve with the reserved `local` authority. The Working Set, the editor review (`AgentHostEditReview`) and the Keep/Undo matching converted the host's changeset files with that authority. `toAgentHostUri` leaves `file:` URIs unwrapped for `local`, so a container file such as `file:///workspaces/app/src/a.ts` was treated as a file on the client: on a Windows client it showed as `\workspaces\app\src\a.ts` and failed to open. The old diff view worked because it only read snapshot content through the agent host; since #344477, Working Set rows open the file itself.

The Working Set diffs, the Keep/Undo matching and the editor review now use the authority of the connection's resource URIs, as artifact pills already did since #343483. That helper moved from `agentHostSessionInputPills.ts` to `agentHostResponseFileChanges.ts` as `getAgentHostResourceAuthority`. Local windows and separately connected remote agent hosts are unchanged.

### Parallel edits of one file: the Working Set under-counts and Keep/Undo disappears

`FileEditTracker` kept one pending and one completed edit per file path. A batch of tool calls runs all of its `preToolUse` hooks before any of its tools, so when several calls edited the same file, each `trackEditStart` replaced the previous call's entry:

- Only the first call to finish recorded an edit, from the original file to its own change. The other calls recorded nothing, so the Working Set showed, for example, +1 −1 for seven edits.
- The other calls' coordinator leases leaked, so `isEditing` stayed true until the session ended. The editor review skips a file that is being edited, so it showed no inline diff or Keep/Undo, and the host's discard (Undo) waited 30s and failed with "The agent is still editing".

`FileEditTracker` now keeps per-file queues of pending and completed edits:

- `trackEditStart` and `completeEdit` take the tool input, as `takeCompletedEdit` already did, so each call finds its own entry; calls without input are paired in order. In the reporting session's logs, the hook arguments and the `tool.execution_start` arguments were structurally equal for all 22 edit calls.
- An edit that started before other edits of the file completed begins from what the last of them wrote.
- Every lease is released when its edit is taken or dropped. Entries skipped by a later matched call, whose completion was never delivered, are dropped too.
- A file's state is forgotten once it has no edits, so no content is retained.

The Copilot hooks and the Claude file-edit observer now pass their tool input; both providers share the tracker. Pairing relies on the edits of one file completing in the order they started, which held for every batch in the logs. Two agents editing the same file at the same moment could still be attributed to the wrong call.

### How to test

Remote window (Windows client with WSL or a dev container):

1. Set `chat.editor.workingSet.enabled` to `true` and start a Copilot harness chat.
2. Ask the agent to edit a file, then click the file in the Working Set. It opens through the agent host instead of failing on a `\`-separated path on the client.

Parallel edits (any window):

1. Set `chat.editor.workingSet.enabled` to `true` and use the Copilot harness with a model that batches tool calls, such as Claude Sonnet 5.5.
2. Ask it to edit three non-adjacent lines of a file "with exactly three parallel edit tool calls in a single response".
3. The Working Set shows +3 −3, the editor shows "Keep / Undo / 3 of 3", and keeping or undoing a single change works.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: passed, 290 passing.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/*.test.js"`: passed, 12,367 passing and 74 pending.
- The new tests fail without the source changes: the remote Working Set resolves `file:///repo/file.ts` on the client, the editor review never loads the file, and the tracker reports `editing: true` with later calls not recorded.
- `npm run eslint -- <the 9 changed files>`: passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run build-fast` (client, built-in extensions and Copilot): passed.
- Manual, parallel edits: a Code OSS build of this branch with the Copilot harness and Claude Sonnet 5.5. The SDK ran one response with three `edit` calls (one `preToolUse` batch of 3). The Working Set showed +3 −3 and the review "3 of 3"; Keep gave "2 of 2", Undo gave "1 of 1" with the file restored, and Keep cleared the rest.
- Not run: a real Windows window attached to WSL or a dev container. Unit tests cover the remote case by modeling the remote window's ambient connection (the `local` authority with a remote resource URI mapper).

title: Fix: Add/Move selection to next/previous find match ignores regex find mode
body:
## Summary
Fixes #107090.

`Add Selection To Next Find Match` (and the previous-match / move variants) always searched with `isRegex: false`, even when the Find widget had regex mode enabled and owned the search string. This meant pressing Ctrl+D while regex search was active would search for the regex pattern literally instead of as a regex, so it silently failed to find matches (or found the wrong ones) whenever the pattern wasn't also valid as a literal string.

## Root cause
`MultiCursorSession` never tracked whether its `searchText` should be interpreted as a regex. `_getNextMatch`, `_getPreviousMatch`, and `selectAll` all hardcoded `isRegex: false` when calling into `ITextModel.findNextMatch` / `findPreviousMatch` / `findMatches`.

## Fix
- `MultiCursorSession` now carries an `isRegex` flag.
  - When the session is driven by the Find widget (`isFindWidgetSearch`), it uses `findState.isRegex`.
  - When the session is derived from the current selection/word (selection literally owns what is searched for), it is always `false`, since that search text is never a regex.
- `_getNextMatch`, `_getPreviousMatch`, and `selectAll` now pass `this.isRegex` instead of a hardcoded `false`.

This mirrors the existing, already-correct handling for `Select All Occurrences of Find Match` in `MultiCursorSelectionController.selectAll`, which reads `findState.isRegex` directly for the find-widget-driven path.

## Testing
Added a regression test `issue #107090: Add selection to next find match does not work with regex find mode`, modeled on the existing `issue #5400` test for `selectAll`, verifying that repeated `Ctrl+D` with a regex search string (`some+thing`) now selects all three regex matches (`something`, `someething`, `someeething`).

Note: I verified the fix by careful manual review against the `ITextModel.findNextMatch` / `findPreviousMatch` / `findMatches` signatures in `model.ts` and the `FindReplaceState.isRegex` getter in `findState.ts`, and by checking all call sites of the `MultiCursorSession` constructor. I was not able to run the full build/test suite in my environment (requires Node 24 per `.nvmrc`), so please have CI confirm.

## Test plan
- [ ] CI unit tests pass, including the new regression test in `multicursor.test.ts`
- [ ] Manually verify: enable regex search in the Find widget, place cursor in matching text, press Ctrl+D repeatedly — selections should expand to each regex match

title: terminal-suggest: scan each PATH folder once per lookup
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What

`PathExecutableCache.getExecutablesInPath` now scans each uncached `PATH` folder at most once per lookup, even when `PATH` lists the folder more than once. The PR also adds a regression test for a `PATH` that lists a folder twice.

## Why

The first lookup scans all uncached `PATH` folders concurrently, and the scans share the set of labels found so far, so each executable is added by only one scan. A folder that `PATH` listed twice was scanned twice: its executables were split between the two scans, but only the first occurrence's result was cached. Later lookups read from the cache and missed whatever the other scan had found. As a result, "results are the same on successive calls" failed whenever the first occurrence's scan lost the race.

This surfaced during the pnpm migration. `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` put the repository's root `node_modules/.bin` on `PATH` twice (once as the package's bin folder and once as the workspace root's), where `npm run` put it once. On macOS CI, the second lookup missed all of `node_modules/.bin`. Users whose `PATH` lists a folder twice could lose that folder's executables from terminal completions in the same way.

This is cherry-picked from the pnpm migration branch (`b765aa87fff`) so the fix can land independently of that migration.

## How to test

- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite terminal-suggest --grep PathExecutableCache`: **passed**. All 5 tests pass on `main`, including the new "results are the same on successive calls when PATH lists a folder twice". I ran it with a short `--user-data-dir` (through `API_TESTS_EXTRA_ARGS`) because the local worktree path is longer than the macOS IPC socket path limit.
- `node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/terminal-suggest/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: **passed**
- `npm run eslint -- extensions/terminal-suggest/src/env/pathExecutableCache.ts extensions/terminal-suggest/src/test/env/pathExecutableCache.test.ts`: **passed**

title: MCP: route server cancelled notification to incoming requests
body:
Fixes #344911

### Cause
Per the Model Context Protocol specification, `notifications/cancelled` parameter `requestId` *"MUST correspond to the ID of a request previously issued in the same direction"*. A cancellation notification arriving from the MCP server can therefore only refer to an incoming, server-to-client request (e.g. `elicitation/create` or `sampling/createMessage`).

Previously:
1. `McpServerRequestHandler.handleCancelledNotification` invoked `this._rpc.cancelPendingRequest(requestId)`, which looked up the editor's *outgoing* requests (`_pendingRequests`). If an incoming request and an editor outgoing request (such as `tools/call`) shared an ID, the unrelated outgoing request was erroneously rejected as cancelled, while the server-initiated request remained open.
2. The truthy check `if (request.params.requestId)` skipped ID `0`, which is the first request ID used by the MCP TypeScript SDK.
3. `JsonRpcProtocol._handleRequest` did not track cancellation token sources for in-flight incoming requests, and late responses from abandoned handlers were still dispatched.

### Solution
1. Added `cancelIncomingRequest(id)` to `JsonRpcProtocol` to track in-flight incoming request `CancellationTokenSource`s and cancel them when requested.
2. Handled disposal and suppress sending late responses/errors from cancelled incoming request handlers in `JsonRpcProtocol._handleRequest`.
3. In `McpServerRequestHandler.handleCancelledNotification`, invoked `this._rpc.cancelIncomingRequest(request.params.requestId)` with `request.params.requestId !== undefined`.
4. Added unit tests in `jsonRpcProtocol.test.ts` and updated `mcpServerRequestHandler.test.ts` to verify that incoming cancellations cancel the server request's token and do not affect outgoing editor requests even when IDs collide.

title: agentHost: allow fallback models with omitted supported_endpoints (#344974)
body:
Fixes #344974

### Problem
In `requestRouter.ts`, `readFallbackModel` required `cloud_fallback_model` to explicitly declare an array of `supported_endpoints`:
```ts
if (!Array.isArray(value.supported_endpoints) || !value.supported_endpoints.includes('/chat/completions')) {
	return undefined;
}
```
When an on-device local model is selected in Auto mode and the routing payload provides a cloud fallback model that omits `supported_endpoints`, `readFallbackModel` rejects it as `undefined`. This triggers `fallbackNotChat`, silently discarding the valid local model selection and reissuing a cloud-only request.

### Fix
Allow fallback models when `supported_endpoints` is undefined/omitted, rejecting only when `supported_endpoints` is explicitly specified and does not include `/chat/completions`.

### Tests
Added regression test in `requestRouter.test.ts` verifying that a `cloud_fallback_model` with omitted `supported_endpoints` routes to `patch` instead of failing with `reissue:fallbackNotChat`.

title: agentHost: preserve static MCP OAuth client ID in projected HTTP configurations (fixes #344965)
body:
Fixes #344965

### Summary

For HTTP MCP servers configured with `oauth.clientId` in `mcp.json`, `projectMcpServerConfiguration` only projected `url`, `transport`, and `headers`, dropping `launch.oauth`. Consequently, the projected configuration forwarded to Agent Host sessions had `oauth: undefined`. When passed to the Copilot runtime via `toCopilotMcpServerConfiguration`, the static client ID was not forwarded as `oauthClientId`, causing the session to fall back to Dynamic Client Registration and prompt the user for registration details on authorization servers requiring pre-registered clients (such as Keycloak or Slack).

### Fix

- In `projectMcpServerConfiguration`, preserve `oauth: launch.oauth?.clientId ? { clientId: launch.oauth.clientId } : undefined` on projected HTTP server configurations so static OAuth client IDs are forwarded to the Copilot SDK.
- Add a unit test in `agentHostMcpServerSupport.test.ts` verifying that `oauth.clientId` is preserved in the projected configuration for HTTP MCP servers.

title: agentHost: allow fallback models with omitted supported_endpoints (#344974)
body:
### Summary
Fixes #344974

In `readFallbackModel` (`<blob>.ts`), cloud fallback models where `supported_endpoints` is omitted/undefined were unconditionally rejected by `!Array.isArray(value.supported_endpoints)`.

Across CAPI and the Copilot client (such as in `chatEndpoint.ts`), `supported_endpoints` is optional on model metadata and defaults to `/chat/completions`. When CAPI's `/auto` response returns `cloud_fallback_model` without an explicit `supported_endpoints` array, `readFallbackModel` failed and caused `evaluateAutoResponse` to return `{ kind: 'reissue', reason: 'fallbackNotChat' }`. This caused the on-device Auto selection to be rejected and re-routed cloud-only.

This PR relaxes the check in `readFallbackModel` so that when `supported_endpoints` is omitted (`undefined`), the fallback model is accepted and defaults to `/chat/completions`, while still rejecting models that explicitly declare non-chat endpoints (such as `['/responses']`).

### Changes
- Updated `readFallbackModel` to check `if (value.supported_endpoints !== undefined && (!Array.isArray(value.supported_endpoints) || !value.supported_endpoints.includes('/chat/completions')))`
- Added test case in `requestRouter.test.ts` verifying that `cloud_fallback_model` with omitted `supported_endpoints` evaluates to `patch`.

title: Agent host: spawn fewer git processes
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

**Draft.** Reduces how many git processes the agent host starts, and how much each start costs. This follows the Windows Agent Host E2E investigation in #344991; the SQLite part of that investigation is #345014.

### Why
- Starting git costs about 25 ms on Windows CI vs about 7 ms on Linux. Terminal and shell tests were 3.9× slower than on Linux, and git and worktree tests 1.9× slower.
- In the E2E agent host logs, every session ran `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` three times, always in a folder that isn't a repository. Those were the only git commands those sessions ran.
- Every git call launches bare `git`, so on Windows each call first searches the working directory and every PATH entry for `git.com` and `git.exe`.

### Changes
1. **Find git once per PATH** (new [gitProcess.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/gitProcess.ts), `GitExecutableResolver`).
  - The search mirrors Node's own lookup: on Windows it only tries `.com` and `.exe` and ignores PATHEXT, because `execFile` can't run `git.cmd` without a shell.
  - It falls back to bare `git` whenever the result could differ from Node's search, such as relative or empty PATH entries or no PATH at all.
  - If the git it found disappears (ENOENT when launching), it searches again on the next call.
  - Used by every git launch in `AgentHostGitService` and by the edit attribution service's `readGitState`, which runs every 30 s for each tracked repository.
2. **Skip `rev-parse --show-toplevel` outside repositories** (`mayBeInGitRepository`).
  - git is skipped when neither the folder, its real path nor any parent folder has a `.git` entry, and the environment doesn't set `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE`. In every other case, including any doubt, git runs as before.
  - The check runs on every lookup that would otherwise start git, including `refreshIfNone`, so a later `git init` or a new worktree is picked up immediately. A plain negative cache would go stale.
  - Lookup results and the existing "not a repository" cache entries are unchanged.
3. **Combine git calls.**
  - The session git state now reads the push remote, the base branch refs and whether the default remote branch exists with one `for-each-ref` instead of three commands. That's 2 git launches instead of 4 per refresh, with the same two sequential steps.
  - The branch diff safety check reads both `core.virtualfilesystem` and `core.sparsecheckout` with one `git config -z --get-regexp`.

**Saving:** 3 launches per session in a folder that isn't a repository, about 75 ms per session on Windows. Every other git launch also skips the PATH search.

### Behavior changes and risks
- On Windows, a `git.exe` in the working directory no longer takes priority over PATH. This is intentional and avoids running a planted binary.
- If git is moved while the agent host runs, one git call fails before git is found again.
- Launch error messages such as `spawn … ENOENT` now show git's full path.
- In a bare repository with no `.git` entry, "not a repository" is now cached even when `safe.bareRepository=explicit` would have logged a warning.

### Follow-ups (not in this PR)
- `getDefaultBranch`: two `show-ref` calls could be one `for-each-ref`.
- `getHEAD`, `getDefaultBranch2` and `_readGitInfo`: `symbolic-ref`, `for-each-ref`, `remote` and `remote -v` could share fewer calls.
- `captureWorkingTreeAsTree`: two `rev-parse` calls could be one, but an unborn HEAD complicates it.
- `getCurrentBranch`: `branch --show-current` plus a fallback `rev-parse`.

### Validation
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/gitProcess.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: 120 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh` with the `agentHostServices`, `missionControlProjects`, `agentEditAttributionService`, `agentHostReviewService`, `agentHostGitStateService` and `shared/worktreeIsolation` tests: 288 passed
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run …/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts`: 113 passed. Tests about caching or ordering for a folder that isn't a repository now create an empty `.git` folder so git still runs, and a new test covers the case where git is skipped.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run …/protocol/sessionDiffs.integrationTest.ts`: 4 passed
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run …/agentHostReviewService.integrationTest.ts`: 1 passed, 7 pending (that suite was already skipped on main)
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>` and `npm run typecheck-client`: passed

title: Sessions: ignore drag and drop onto workspaces outside top-level order
body:
Fixes #344908

### Cause
When extra workspaces overflow and are revealed via "+N more workspaces", they are appended to the rendered list items but are not part of `_topLevelOrder`. When a user dragged another workspace or session group onto one of these revealed workspaces:
1. `getHeaderDrop` returned `{ kind: 'topLevel', targetId: target.id, position }` because `parentId === undefined`. This drew a drop line indicator as if it were a valid reordering drop target.
2. In `applyHeaderDrop`, `_sessionGroupsService.moveGroup` or `moveSection` was invoked, but `reorder(this._topLevelOrder, ...)` had no effect because `drop.targetId` was not in `_topLevelOrder`. This led to either a no-op or detaching a group without reordering it.

### Solution
1. Ensure `getHeaderDrop` returns `undefined` if the target workspace/group section ID is not in `_topLevelOrder`, correctly preventing drop indicator rendering on overflow workspaces.
2. Guard `applyHeaderDrop` for `case 'topLevel'` by checking `topLevelOrder.includes(drop.targetId)` before calling `moveGroup` or `moveSection`.

title: agentHost: avoid `**` in the default watcher excludes
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Related to #334248

The agent host watches each session's repository root recursively with `DEFAULT_AGENT_HOST_WATCH_EXCLUDES`, and every one of them started with `**`. Parcel matches each exclude as a regular expression (`std::regex`) against every path it crawls when a watch starts on Linux and Windows, and against every event on all platforms. An exclude with `**` in front of a name is much more expensive: about 13 µs per path, against 0.35 µs for `*/name`. The defaults of `files.watcherExclude` avoid `**` for this reason (see the comment in `files.contribution.ts`).

This PR keeps the same excludes, but only for the watched folder and the folders directly inside it (for example `.git/objects/**` and `*/.git/objects/**`), like the defaults of `files.watcherExclude`.

## Impact

CPU time of one full crawl of this repository (282k entries) with Parcel's brute-force backend, the code path of the Linux and Windows startup crawl, measured in one batch on macOS:

| Excludes | Globs | CPU time |
|---|---|---|
| Agent host defaults before this PR | 9 | 36.1 s |
| Agent host defaults with this PR | 18 | 5.1 s |
| For comparison: `files.watcherExclude` defaults | 6 | 3.4 s |

Together with #343807, which also excludes the paths of the root `.gitignore`, the crawl takes 3.5 s and visits 26k entries.

## Trade-off

Repository metadata and watchman cookies two or more folders below the watched root are no longer excluded. That is also the case for `files.watcherExclude`.

## How to test

In a session on a large repository on Linux, the agent host's file watcher process should use much less CPU when the session starts. Changes in `.git/objects` and `.git/index.lock` should still not be reported.

## Validation

- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: passed (84 passing). The existing test for repository metadata now also covers a nested repository one folder down.
- Mutation check: without the `*/` prefix, `filters known repository metadata noise before debouncing` fails.

- Pre-commit hygiene: passed

Not run: smoke tests.
