title: Agent host: use SQLite's write-ahead log for local databases
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

The agent host databases (`agent-host.db` and each session's `session.db`) used SQLite's defaults. Every commit created a rollback journal, flushed the disk at least twice and deleted the journal. Reads also wait behind every queued write. Where disk flushes are slow, as on Windows, every session pays for this.

On Windows CI, compared with Linux:
- Catalog writes took 142 ms vs 35 ms.
- `disposeSession` took 473 ms vs 33 ms; 436 ms of that was a step that only reads from the database.
- Agent Host E2E took about 2.2× as long overall.

### Change
- `AgentHostDatabase` and `SessionDatabase` now switch a database file on a local file system to the write-ahead log (WAL) with `synchronous = NORMAL` ([agentHostSqliteJournal.ts](src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostSqliteJournal.ts)).
- A commit now appends to the log, and the disk is flushed only when SQLite checkpoints the log into the database file.
- **Durability:** after a power loss or OS crash, the last commits can roll back, but the database stays consistent. A crash of the process loses nothing.
- **Network paths keep the rollback journal**, because WAL needs shared memory. That covers Windows UNC paths (for example a redirected AppData folder), drives that resolve to one (such as mapped network drives), and Linux network or FUSE file systems: NFS, SMB/CIFS, 9P (WSL's `/mnt/c`), Ceph, AFS and sshfs. A path whose locality can't be determined also keeps the rollback journal. macOS paths count as local, because macOS has no stable file-system type numbers.
- **Databases that moved:** WAL is stored in the database file, so a database that moved from a local disk to a network share is switched back to the rollback journal when it's opened.
- **Concurrent connections:** if another connection's open transaction prevents a switch either way, the database keeps its current mode until a later open retries.
- Copies of session databases already go through `VACUUM INTO`, which is safe in WAL mode. Nothing else copies or reads these database files directly.

### Measured impact
Measured in experiment #344991: same machine, same shard, compared with the average of a baseline run before and after.

| Windows CI suite | Before | WAL |
|---|---|---|
| Conformance (slowest in shard 1) | 612 s | 440 s (−28%) |
| Copilot (slowest in shard 2) | 554 s | 381 s (−31%) |
| Claude, Codex, Copilot OTel, Copilot managed settings | | −28% to −49% |

That brings both Windows Agent Host E2E shards to about 10 minutes, from 13.2 minutes p50, without adding a shard. It also saves about 6 runner-minutes per run. Moving the temp directory to a Dev Drive made no difference (±2%), so disk flushes, not the file system, were the cost.

### Tests
- New `agentHostSqliteJournal.test.ts` covers which paths use WAL on each platform, using a fake host, including mapped, substituted and unresolvable Windows drives. It also checks the journal of a local database, a network database, a database moved from local to network storage, and one whose switch is blocked by another connection's transaction.
- `agentHostDatabase.test.ts` "migrates a fresh database in a single write transaction" now counts commit frames in the WAL instead of SQLite's file change counter, which WAL commits don't increment. It also checks the database's file format.
- `sessionDatabase.test.ts` checks that a session database file is stored in WAL mode.

### Validation
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/platform/agentHost/test/node/**/*.test.js"`: 13,993 passed, 75 pending
- `./scripts/test-agent-host-e2e.sh --runList <Conformance and Copilot managed settings>` on macOS: both suites passed (376 and 15 tests)
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: passed
- `npx tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed

title: Markdown: harden copy destination checks in Restricted Mode
body:
Follow-up to #344989, addressing its review comments and a Windows bug found while verifying it in Code OSS.

In Restricted Mode, the Markdown extension only copies pasted or dropped files to destinations inside the workspace. The check from #344989 had three problems:

- **Path casing:** it compared paths case-sensitively. On Windows, the workspace folder URI and the document URI can differ in drive letter case (`/C:/...` vs `/c:/...`), so every destination looked outside the workspace and no media file was copied at all. Containment now uses `vscode.workspace.getWorkspaceFolder`, which follows the case sensitivity of the workspace folder's file system.
- **Backslashes:** it treated `\` as a separator everywhere. On POSIX, `\` is a regular file name character, so `../../project\other/img.png` could pass the check while resolving outside the workspace. Destinations whose path below the workspace root contains `\` are now rejected on every platform.
- **Symbolic links and junctions:** the check was purely lexical. A folder inside the workspace that links to a folder outside it let a paste write outside. Each existing path segment below the root, including an existing target file, is now checked with `vscode.workspace.fs.stat`, and destinations that pass through a link are rejected.

When a configured destination is rejected, the file is copied next to the document instead; if that is rejected too, the file is not copied and the link points to the original file. Trusted workspaces are unchanged.

Tests: unit tests cover each case, and all `markdown-language-features` tests pass. Verified in Code OSS on Windows in a Restricted Mode workspace that sets `markdown.copyFiles.destination` to a path outside the workspace and contains a junction to an outside folder:

| Build | Paste into `README.md` | Paste into `docs/README.md` (junction) |
|---|---|---|
| #344989 + casing fix, without link check | – | ❌ file written outside the workspace |
| This PR | ✅ copied into the workspace, nothing written outside | ✅ not copied, nothing written outside |

title: Spare custom editor cursor lines on auto save in side-by-side diffs and with different path casing
body:
Fixes <url>

<url> made auto save leave the cursor line alone when trimming trailing whitespace and final newlines in custom text editors such as the Markdown editor. It looks for visible editors that show the saved file and uses the selection they report through the proposed `customTextEditorNavigation` API. Two cases were missed and still trimmed the line being typed on:

- **Side-by-side custom diff:** a custom editor shown as one side of a side-by-side diff sits inside a `DiffEditorInput`, whose resource is undefined when the two sides differ. The lookup now also checks the primary and secondary panes of a `SideBySideEditor`, as `EditorService` does for visible text editor controls.
- **Path casing:** resources are now compared with `IUriIdentityService`, so a custom editor input with different path casing still matches the text model on case-insensitive file systems.

Both changes apply to the cursor lookup and to the fallback that skips trimming when a non-code editor reports no cursor.

## Validation

- New save participant tests cover a custom editor inside a side-by-side diff, with and without a reported cursor.
- All save participant tests, the `src` typecheck, and ESLint pass.

Found in the Copilot review of <url> Its third comment, about the selection arriving after the edit with a very short auto save delay, is not addressed here: a proper fix needs the API to report the document version along with the selection.

title: chat: clear the source draft after forking with /fork prompt
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What

In an agent-host chat, `/fork prompt <prompt>` creates a peer chat, sends the prompt to it, and opens it. When you returned to the source chat, its input still showed `/fork prompt <prompt>`. With this change it is cleared once the fork succeeds.

## Why

The fork opens before the `/fork` slash command settles. Opening it released the source chat's model, which tore down its agent-host draft sync. That teardown flushed the submitted text to the source chat's draft on the agent host. The success callback then cleared the input of an already-disposed model, so the clear never reached the host. Reopening the source chat restored the host draft, which takes precedence over the local copy.

The agent host only persists what the client sends: `ChatDraftChanged` is client-dispatched, and the host cannot tell that a fork's `initialMessage` came from the source chat's composer. So the fix belongs in the client.

## How

- The captured source input (`captureForkPromptSourceInput`) now holds a reference to the source chat until the fork's outcome is known.
  - On success, it clears the draft if it is unchanged since submission, then releases the chat. The cleared draft is what syncs to the host.
  - If the fork is not dispatched or fails, it releases the chat with the draft intact, so the prompt can still be retried as before.
- The `/fork` `prompt` argument parsing (`parseForkPromptArgument`) and the source-draft ownership now live together in `chatForkActions.ts`. The `/fork` slash command and the chat widget share them instead of each keeping its own copy of the parsing. The widget keeps only its submission gating and plumbing.

## How to test

1. In the Agents window, open an agent-host chat with at least one completed turn.
2. Type `/fork prompt Do XYZ` and press Enter. The fork opens and receives `Do XYZ`.
3. Go back to the source chat. Its input is empty, and it stays empty after reloading the window.

Validation:

- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: passed (461 passing, 4 pending)

title: agentHost: allow pull request repairs from chats without a checkout
body:
Address Comments, Fix Checks, and Resolve Conflicts / Update Branch on a recorded pull request artifact were disabled in every chat whose own folders did not have the PR's head branch checked out. That happens whenever the agent creates the worktree with a shell command (for example `git worktree add`) instead of the chat's workspace, and the reason only appeared in the disabled button's hover.

### Changes
- The three repair actions are available from any chat of the artifact's session, and automatic repairs no longer wait for the recording chat to have a checkout. The repair chat must still belong to the session.
- When the chat has a checkout of the PR's repository on its head branch, the prompt names it and keeps the existing "verify, never switch" instruction. Otherwise, the prompt gives the repository and branch and asks the agent to work in an existing checkout of that branch, such as a Git worktree, or to create a new worktree or clone, never switching an existing checkout's branch.
- Merging only unchanged PRs ("When No Changes Were Made") could previously detect repair changes only through the repair's local checkout. Because a repair can now push from any checkout, the repair checkpoint also records the head the first repair started from. Unchanged-only merging turns itself off when the head moves. It still requires a clean checkout in the recording chat. Checkpoints from older builds, which have no `headSha`, are still accepted.
- Background checkout verification now covers only the recording chat instead of every chat in the session.
- `ARTIFACT_INTEGRATIONS_PROPOSAL.md` describes the new behavior.

### How to test
1. In an Agents window session, record a PR from a chat whose folders do not have the PR branch checked out.
2. Open the PR's artifact details. Address Comments (or Fix Checks / Resolve Conflicts) is enabled.
3. Run it. The prompt names the repository and branch and asks the agent to use or create a checkout of that branch.

title: Experiment: measure Windows Agent Host E2E storage costs (do not merge)
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

**Experiment, do not merge.** It measures why the Agent Host E2E suites take about 2.2× as long on Windows as on Linux.

### Background
- Linux runs all six suites on one 8-core runner, with temporary storage in RAM (`tmpfs`). The Copilot suite takes about 282 s there.
- Windows splits them across two 8-core runners, with temporary storage on the OS disk. The same suite takes about 623 s.
- Across 793 tests that ran on both platforms, Windows time ≈ 0.89 s + 1.5 × Linux time. Most of the gap is a fixed cost paid by every test, not a few slow tests.
- The agent host uses SQLite's default settings: a rollback journal plus a full disk flush on every commit. Database reads also wait behind every queued write.
- Catalog writes take 142 ms median on Windows vs 35 ms on Linux. `disposeSession` takes 473 ms vs 33 ms; 436 ms of that is a step that only reads from the database.
- Defender real-time scanning is off on GitHub-hosted runners, so it isn't a factor.

### What this changes
- `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_SQLITE_WAL=1` opens the agent host databases (`AgentHostDatabase` and `SessionDatabase`) with `journal_mode = WAL` and `synchronous = NORMAL`. It is off by default, so default behavior is unchanged.
- After the normal run, each Windows Agent Host E2E shard reruns its suites on the same machine in four passes:
  1. TEMP on the Dev Drive
  2. SQLite WAL
  3. Both
  4. Neither (control)

  The step never fails the job and prints a table of results at the end.

### Validation
- `cd build && node --test lib/test/detectChanges.test.ts lib/test/agentHostTestSelection.test.ts lib/test/detectMissingCaches.test.ts`: 33 passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/sessionDatabase.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostDatabase.test.ts`: 280 passed
- The same two test files with `VSCODE_AGENT_HOST_SQLITE_WAL=1`: 279 passed, 1 failed, as expected. The failing test, "migrates a fresh database in a single write transaction", counts commits through SQLite's file change counter, and switching to WAL adds one.
- Opening both databases with the variable set produced WAL headers (version 2); without it they stayed on the rollback journal (version 1).
- `npm run eslint` on the changed TypeScript files: passed
- `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed

title: Markdown: keep copied files inside the workspace in Restricted Mode
body:
When a file is pasted or dropped into a Markdown document, the Markdown extension can copy it into the workspace. The destination comes from `markdown.copyFiles.destination` and is resolved relative to the document, so it can also point outside the workspace.

This change tightens that behavior in Restricted Mode:

- `markdown.copyFiles.destination` and `markdown.copyFiles.overwriteBehavior` are now restricted configurations, so workspace values are ignored while the workspace is untrusted.
- While the workspace is untrusted, a copied file is only written inside the document's workspace folder (or inside the document's folder if it is not part of a workspace). If the configured destination is outside, the file goes next to the document. If that is also outside, the file is not copied.

Trusted workspaces are unchanged.

Tests: added unit tests for the new destination check; all `markdown-language-features` extension tests pass.

title: Spare the Markdown editor's cursor line when trimming whitespace on auto save
body:
Fixes <url>

With `files.autoSave` and `files.trimTrailingWhitespace` enabled, typing a word followed by a space in the Markdown editor and pausing lost the space: auto save trimmed it, and the editor received the trimmed document. Typing `Hello `, pausing, and typing `world` produced `Helloworld`.

In the text editor this does not happen: on auto save, the trim save participants (`files.trimTrailingWhitespace`, `files.trimFinalNewlines`) leave the lines with a cursor alone. They only knew about code editor cursors, though. A custom text editor such as the Markdown editor is not a code editor, so every line was trimmed.

Custom text editors that implement the proposed `customTextEditorNavigation` API (used for Outline and breadcrumbs) already report their selection in document positions, and the Markdown editor does. The trim participants now treat that selection like a code editor cursor on auto save:

- Trailing whitespace: the cursor line keeps its whitespace up to the cursor; all other lines are still trimmed.
- Final newlines: nothing at or above the cursor line is removed.
- If a visible editor that is neither a code nor a diff editor shows the file but does not report a cursor (no navigation API, or no text selection), auto save skips both trims instead of trimming the line being typed on.

Explicit saves trim as before.

## Validation

- New save participant tests cover a custom editor that reports its cursor and one that does not.
- Reproduced in Code OSS with `files.autoSave: afterDelay` (1000 ms), `files.trimTrailingWhitespace: true`, and the Markdown editor, by typing ` Hello `, waiting for auto save, then typing `world`:
  - Before: the file contained `First paragraph. Helloworld`.
  - After: `First paragraph. Hello world`, while another line `Other line  ` in the same file was trimmed to `Other line` by the same auto save.

## Limitations

`customTextEditorNavigation` reports one selection per panel, so only one cursor per custom editor is spared.

## What changed

Linux PR checks now use the ripple test plan, as macOS and Windows already do (#342907). Today, Linux runs every unit and integration test on every push.

**`pr-linux-test.yml`**
- `Electron-Unit (electron)`, `Electron-Unit (node)`, `Browser-Unit`, `Electron (node.js)` and `Agent-Host-E2E` set `TEST_SELECTION`. They download the `test-plan` artifact and pass `unit.txt` / `integration.txt` to the runners with `--runList`. This uses the same steps as `pr-darwin-test.yml`, and every test runs when there is no plan.
- New `electron_node_affected` input, so the separate `Electron (node.js)` job is skipped when the plan selects no node.js integration test. `electron_affected` now gates only `Electron (extension host)`.

**`pr.yml`**
- The Linux caller uses the `selected-unit-tests`, `selected-browser-unit-tests`, `selected-node-integration-tests` and `selected-agent-host-e2e` outputs, like macOS and Windows.
- Comments, the step summary and the ripple warnings no longer say that Linux runs everything.

**`build/ripple/vscode.jsonc`**
- Under `runEverything`, the `test job definition` group adds `pr-linux-test.yml` and the Linux machine setup scripts (`apt-retry.sh`, `xvfb.init`). The `dependency installation` group adds `setup-env.sh`. A change to any of these runs every test, as `exec.ps1` already does for Windows.

**Tests and docs**

Unchanged: ripple does not plan the extension host, smoke, Browser or Remote jobs. They still run whenever `Detect Changes` says the change can affect them.

## Why

To see how long Compile & Hygiene and the Linux jobs take when Linux runs only the tests a change can affect.

## Measuring (temporary commit)

This PR edits `pr.yml`, `pr-linux-test.yml` and `vscode.jsonc`, which are all in ripple's `runEverything` list. On its own, the first commit would plan "run everything", and the Linux timings would match today's. The temporary commit:

- refactors `Marker.toString` in `markersModel.ts` without changing behavior, so the plan selects a typical, small set of tests.

The local plan for this branch (`ripple plan --base HEAD~2 --head HEAD`) selects 2 unit test files (`markersModel.test.ts`, `markersView.test.ts`) and 0 integration test files. That is close to the median pull request in ripple's replay (about 2% of unit test work). Expected Linux behavior:

title: agentHost: use the OAuth client configured in VS Code for MCP authentication
body:
Fixes #344965

## Summary

An MCP server with `oauth.clientId` in `mcp.json` still triggers Dynamic Client Registration when it is used through the Copilot harness. If the authorization server refuses anonymous registration, VS Code shows "Dynamic Client Registration not supported" and asks for a client ID that is already configured.

The cause is that the agent host copy of an HTTP server is built from `url`, `transport` and `headers` only (`projectMcpServerConfiguration` in `agentHostMcpServerSupport.ts`, and `getPartialSupportReasons` reports `OAuthClientConfigurationIgnored`). The challenge the agent host reports therefore has no `oauthClient`.

- `resolveMcpServerAuthentication` now uses the OAuth client configured in VS Code when the challenge carries none. It finds the HTTP server at the same URL in the MCP registry and uses its `oauth.clientId`, plus the client secret from secret storage if one is stored (same key as `mainThreadMcp.ts`: `mcpOAuthClientSecretStorageKey` with `launch.uri.toString(true)`).
- The client is used only when the match is unambiguous and safe, and otherwise authentication falls back to Dynamic Client Registration as before:
  - exactly one enabled HTTP server is served at the challenged endpoint (or below it, when the endpoint is the origin advertised by root metadata), whether or not it has a client configured;
  - the server is not `oauth.enterpriseManaged`;
  - `${...}` variables in the client ID resolve without prompting (`${input:...}` and `${command:...}` do not);
  - every authorization server is advertised by the configured endpoint's own resource metadata, so a remote agent host cannot send a stored client secret to an issuer it chose.
- The lookup lives in the one function every authentication path calls, so no signature changes. A client in the challenge still takes precedence.

The `OAuthClientConfigurationIgnored` reason text ("Migrate this server to keep its OAuth client ID") is unchanged. If dropping the client was intentional, this PR can be closed.

## Validation

- `agentHostAuth.test.ts` — 127 passing, including eleven new cases (public client, stored secret, client ID with a variable, origin-level challenge, and no client for another URL, enterprise-managed, no client ID, disabled server, `${input:}` client ID, two servers at one endpoint, unadvertised issuer).
- Browser unit tests for `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions` and `remoteAgentHost` — 4642 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run eslint` and `npm run typecheck-client` on the changed files — no errors.
- Three existing test files needed `IMcpService` and `ISecretStorageService` stubs.

Reproduced with `--disable-extensions` and a clean profile on stable 1.143.1.

title: sessions: improve worktree cleanup selection and management
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

- Select eligible worktrees with no matching session by default, including unknown-size worktrees. Under a nonzero age filter, unknown-age worktrees remain unchecked unless explicitly selected. Preserve individual and Select All choices across scan updates, cleanup refreshes, and age-filter changes.
- Separate the editor into three virtualized tables: **Available for cleanup**, **Progress and results** (measuring storage, queued/running cleanup, and retained completed results), and **Needs attention** (failed/deferred cleanup and protected worktrees). Keep non-destructive retries for failed requests in the current cleanup batch.
- Add **Sort by** for size (largest first) or session recency (newest first). Unknown values sort last. Sorting preserves checkbox choices without rescanning.
- In **Needs attention**, offer initially unchecked row checkboxes and a separate **Select All** for verified failed/deferred or in-use worktrees on hosts that explicitly support forced cleanup. A single **Force Remove Worktrees** action confirms the whole selected batch, warning that uncommitted changes and ignored/untracked files are permanently discarded, usage by other sessions/chats is overridden, and those sessions/chats may stop working. Committed changes, branches, and session history remain. Normal cleanup never includes this separate selection.
- Negotiate destructive cleanup through an optional host capability. Older hosts retain ordinary cleanup behavior. Explicit force overrides other session/chat usage references and stale branch metadata, using the current registered branch, but keeps host ownership, managed-path/current-branch validation, locking, and restored-owning-session protection. Failures remain durable; automatic retries never inherit destructive intent or these overrides.
- Scheduling failures also offer unchecked forced-removal checkboxes even if the host's status remains unknown. On supported hosts, the failed-batch retry action becomes **Force Remove Failed Worktrees** and requires the same destructive confirmation rather than repeating ordinary cleanup and hitting the same usage or stale-branch guard.
- Restrict managed worktree inventory and explicit managed/forced cleanup to current registered branches starting with `agents/`. Validate the current branch on the host, including before missing-directory handling and immediately before removal. Primary, external, symlinked, and nested worktrees remain protected. Ordinary cleanup still rejects changed branch metadata; confirmed force can remove the managed worktree on its current `agents/` branch.
- Apply the same branch-prefix filter to client inventory, linked sessions with known branch metadata, cached rows, and retained failed-batch rows, so unsupported worktrees never appear in any cleanup table or selection.
- Drop stale discovered worktrees no longer listed by the host rather than showing unselectable Needs attention rows. Track verification only for submitted cleanup requests, including scheduling failures, hide unlisted candidates even across later empty snapshots, and retain confirmed removal results without treating inventory absence as proof of deletion. Still-listed failures remain selectable for confirmed forced removal.
- Update accessibility help and eligibility guidance, retain the existing Select All action, and fix progress notification capitalization.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client` - passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/common/worktreePaths.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 322 tests. Includes filtering foreign branches across all tables and cached batch results, dropping stale inventory, hiding unlisted failed-batch rows across empty snapshots, recording availability after failed submissions, retaining verified removal results, unknown-existence verification and cancellation, listed-failure force selection, confirmed retries, stale branch metadata with simultaneous usage references, final-guard branch changes, and automatic retry safety.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 145 tests after the bulk-selection update, including independent category selection, filtered/off-screen Select All, confirmation cancellation and one confirmation for multiple forced removals.
- `./scripts/test.sh --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/electron-browser/agentHostProtocolClient.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/protocolServerHandler.test.ts --reporter dot` - passed, 1,071 tests; 1 existing pending test.
- `./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentHostGitService.integrationTest.ts --grep 'removeWorktree|forced removal|explicit discard' --reporter dot` - passed, 9 real-Git tests, including explicit discard versus normal recovery-ref preservation.
- `git diff --name-only -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 npm run eslint --` - passed for all changed TypeScript.
- `git diff --name-only -z -- '*.ts' | xargs -0 node build/hygiene.ts` - passed for all nine TypeScript files in the latest follow-up.
- `npm run stylelint -- <blob>.css` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `npm run typecheck-client` - blocked only by the existing unrelated `src/vs/platform/terminal/node/terminalProcess.ts:603` error: `IPty` lacks `setParentWindow`. No diagnostics in changed files.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - blocked by the same existing terminal type error.
- The fast-build entry point was previously blocked by an installed Copilot SDK/runtime version mismatch; client transpilation succeeds. No dependencies or registry settings were changed.

Keyboard navigation, row migration/focus, virtualization, selection persistence, confirmation cancellation, force failures, restored-owning-session protection, explicit-force usage and stale-branch overrides, branch-prefix validation, protocol negotiation, and automatic retry safety are covered by the focused tests. An isolated Agents window with eight synthetic entries was visually inspected earlier: three tables, independent Needs attention selection, one confirmation for two selected worktrees, cancellation preserving selection and data, and recency sorting all verified with synthetic-only cleanup backends. After the latest follow-up, the isolated window was reloaded and its live inventory-backed cleanup editor was visually inspected: stale unlisted rows were absent and eligible checkboxes remained available. No cleanup or force-removal action was invoked on real worktrees. A live provider-backed removal and full integration/smoke suites were not run.

## Manual Test

1. Open Worktree Cleanup with linked and unlinked worktrees. Verify managed discovery and all three tables exclude known branches not starting with `agents/`, including cached failed-batch entries. Eligible unlinked worktrees are selected by default, including unknown-size rows. A nonzero Untouched For filter should leave unknown-age rows unchecked but manually selectable.
2. Verify measuring and queued/running worktrees appear in Progress and results, eligible worktrees appear in Available for cleanup, and failures/protected worktrees appear in Needs attention. Measurement completion and cleanup outcomes should move rows to the appropriate table. Completed batch rows remain visible until reopening.
3. Use Select All and individual checkboxes, change age/workspace filters, and let scans complete. Explicit choices should persist; selection and cleanup should respect the current filter.
4. Change Sort by between Size and Session Recency. Verify ordering within each table, unknown values last, and unchanged checkbox choices.
5. In a disposable test repository, reproduce multiple cleanup failures on a supported host. In Needs attention, verify rows start unchecked, row checkboxes and the category's Select All select only eligible worktrees in the current filter, and normal cleanup selection remains separate. Activate Force Remove Worktrees using the keyboard. Cancel first and verify nothing was removed and selection is preserved; then confirm once for the whole batch and verify the worktrees are removed while their branches and committed history remain. Uncommitted/ignored/untracked files are intentionally lost only after confirmation.
6. In a disposable `agents/` test worktree referenced by another session/chat, verify normal cleanup remains blocked, but Needs attention offers a checkbox and Select All includes it. Verify the bulk confirmation warns about overriding usage and breaking affected sessions/chats. Cancel without removing anything; only confirm for disposable test data. Restoring the owning session must still stop removal. Older hosts must not show Force Remove. Normal and automatic retries must continue preserving changes and respecting usage references.
7. Reproduce an ordinary scheduling failure caused by usage or stale displayed branch metadata. Verify the failed row gains an initially unchecked force checkbox and the batch action reads Force Remove Failed Worktrees on supported hosts. Cancel first and verify nothing changes. With disposable data only, change to another `agents/` branch and confirm forced retry: it should remove the worktree on its current branch rather than repeating the ordinary scheduling error. A current branch outside `agents/`, a foreign path, or a restored owning session must still block removal.
8. Refresh after a worktree disappears from its host's managed inventory. It must not remain as an unselectable Needs attention row or reappear from a failed batch after another refresh. Still-listed failures must keep their force-removal checkboxes. Submitted cleanup requests must retain confirmed removal results, but missing inventory or an unknown existence check must never be reported as successful removal.

No linked issue; reported directly in the session.

title: sessions: Run Dev Container startup commands in one container shell
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

<url>

## Summary

Each `devcontainer exec` launch costs about 5s, because the CLI re-runs its Docker checks, container lookup, and user environment probe every time. In a recorded startup, 17 CLI launches took about 79s before the relay started, while `up` itself took about 7s. After `up`, startup still made around ten sequential execs.

This PR runs the startup commands through **one long-lived container shell**, similar to the Dev Container CLI's `ShellServer`:

- A single `devcontainer exec ... /bin/sh` is started after `up`. Commands are written to its stdin one at a time, and per-command markers separate each command's stdout, stderr, and exit code.
- Each command still runs in its own `/bin/sh -c` without stdin, as it did in a separate exec. Exits, `set -e`, and syntax errors therefore stay isolated, and no command can consume the protocol stream.
- A handshake keeps the CLI's own startup log out of the first command's stderr. If the shell exits unexpectedly, running and later commands are rejected with the CLI's exit code and stderr.
- The `ISshExec` interface is unchanged, so the Git setup, platform detection, cache, CLI install, and endpoint lookup and polling code all use the shell without changes. Registration polls now take milliseconds instead of seconds each.
- The **Agent Host start command keeps its own exec**, because it runs for the host's lifetime. The **relay** also keeps its own exec, because it carries a byte stream.
- The shell, the start command, and the relay pass **`--container-id`**, so the CLI inspects the started container directly instead of looking it up by label.
- The shell closes before the relay starts, and on failure or cancellation through the connection's disposable store.

The pre-`up` `read-configuration` is unchanged. Its result decides `up`'s own arguments (the cache `--mount` and the sandbox override), so `up --include-merged-configuration` cannot replace it.

Expected savings: startup goes from about ten sequential CLI launches after `up` to three (shell, Agent Host start when needed, relay). With Docker Desktop warm, a separate exec measured 1.8–2.8s and a command through the shell 7–63ms, so that is roughly 20–25s; the earlier recording measured about 5s per launch, which would make it 35–45s. I did not measure a full session startup.

## Validation

- Windows: `scripts\test.bat --run vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\devContainerAgentHostService.test.js --run ...devContainerShell.test.js --run ...devContainerServerCache.test.js --run ...devContainerSandbox.test.js --run ...devContainerSamples.test.js`: passed (120 passing, 11 pending; the pending tests include the 4 new real-shell tests, which skip on Windows).
- Linux (WSL Ubuntu 24.04, `/bin/sh` is dash): `node node_modules/mocha/bin/mocha.js test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/devContainerShell.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts`: passed (80 passing, 1 existing pending), including the new real-shell tests.
- New tests cover:
  - routing: startup commands go through one shell, the Agent Host start command through a separate exec, and the shell, exec, and relay all use `--container-id`, with and without sandboxing
  - the shell closing before the relay starts, and when startup fails
  - the production shell's CLI arguments, a shared shell process, exit codes, stderr, failure errors, stdin isolation, and exclusion of the CLI's startup log
  - shell robustness: syntax errors, `exit`, `set -e`, 200 KB of output, multi-byte UTF-8, an unexpected shell exit carrying the CLI's error, and cancellation of a running command
- Live check against real `devcontainer exec` (CLI 0.88.0, Docker Desktop on Windows) in `mcr.microsoft.com/devcontainers/base:1-bookworm` (dash) and `base:alpine` (BusyBox `ash`), using the transpiled `DevContainerShell`:
  - Separate exec: 2.1–2.8s by label lookup, 1.8–2.2s with `--container-id`. Shell start plus the first command: 1.8–2.6s.
  - The original startup commands through the shell (Git root, `uname`, musl detection, `id`, `safe.directory`, identity) took 116–170ms in total. Git's dubious-ownership message came through on stderr, and Alpine reported `musl`.
  - Syntax errors, `exit`, `set -e`, 200 KB of output, UTF-8, and `cat` behaved as in the unit tests. Two commands reported the same parent shell. Disposing closed the shell with exit code 0. The CLI's startup log stayed out of the first command's stderr.
  - A missing container ID rejects with the CLI's stderr. The CLI itself exits 1 without an error message in this case, as it does for a separate exec.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `node build/hygiene.ts <changed files>`: passed.

title: files: support `!` exclude exceptions in files.exclude and search.exclude
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #869. Implements the approach discussed in #134415.

## What changed

A `!`-prefixed key in `files.exclude` or `search.exclude` is now an **exclude exception**:

```jsonc
"files.exclude": {
  "node_modules": true,
  "!node_modules/@types": true // shown, including everything inside it
}
```

**Rule:** a path is excluded if it, or one of its parent folders, matches an exclude pattern, and neither the path nor any parent folder matches an exception.

- **Order doesn't matter.** Settings scopes merge as before, and an exception key can be set to `false` in another scope to disable it.
- **Exceptions only show things.** They never add exclusions, so `{"!*.js": true}` alone has no effect. This avoids the "negations match everything" problem raised in #134415.
- **`false` is unchanged.** It still disables a key.
- **No exceptions, no change.** `parseExcludeExpression` returns exactly what `glob.parse` returns.
- **Exceptions override `.gitignore`**, both for `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` and for search ignore files.
- **Exceptions are relative to the folder.** Absolute `!` keys are ignored. They still apply when an absolute exclude pattern matches.
- **Version control folders stay excluded.** `.git`, `.svn`, `.hg` and `.jj` are not re-included or walked under an exception unless an exception names them, for example `!.git/hooks`.
- **Only these two settings are affected.** `files.watcherExclude`, `files.readonly*`, `explorer.autoRevealExclude`, `workbench.localHistory.exclude` and the extension API keep treating `!` literally. Exclude patterns from the search view input and from the API are escaped to `{!}`.

### Where it applies
- **`glob.ts`:** new `parseExcludeExpression`, which exposes `matches`, `matchesExclude`, `isExcepted` and `couldExceptionMatchBeneath`.
- **Explorer:** shows excepted items and the folders that lead to them. Those folders are not dimmed. An exception that starts with `**` shows every folder that could contain a match.
- **Search, Node (ripgrep):** ripgrep cannot express exceptions and does not descend into excluded folders. After the normal run, the file and text engines run ripgrep once more per folder, with `--no-ignore` and these `-g` globs:
  - `!*`, then folder-only globs for the folders that lead to each exception (for example `/node_modules/`), then the exceptions themselves. Only those folders are walked.
  - If an exception starts with `**`, only the exceptions are whitelisted, because the whole folder has to be walked anyway.
  - The results are checked against the exceptions with VS Code's glob matcher, because ripgrep globs can match more (ripgrep matches `**.js` at any depth). Results already reported by the normal run are skipped, the query's includes are applied, and folders of the query that are inside the searched folder are skipped.
- **Tree walks, everywhere else:** the explorer, breadcrumbs, the web-worker search, the file-system provider search, the file walkers and the Agents window file search all share `glob.evaluateExcludeTreeEntry`, which decides whether an entry is excluded and whether to walk into it. This also fixes `QueryGlobTester.includedInQuery` ignoring synchronous exclude matches when it evaluates sibling clauses asynchronously.
- **Extension search providers** receive the same excludes as today, without exceptions, so exceptions aren't honored there yet.
- **Other readers of these settings:** the Problems view and quick open history.
- **Settings:** the schemas for both settings accept `!` keys with their own description. The Settings editor and `settings.json` diagnostics are in the follow-up #345013.
- **Telemetry:** `searchComplete` and `textSearchComplete` now report exception counts, and `searchComplete` also reports exception run count and time. All new fields are measurements.

### Known limits
- **No re-excluding inside an exception.** That needs ordered rules, which settings objects can't express.
- **Exceptions starting with `**`** make the explorer show every folder in excluded regions, and make search walk the whole folder without ignore files.

## How to test
1. Add `"files.exclude": { "node_modules": true, "!node_modules/@types": true }` to workspace settings. In the explorer, only `node_modules/@types` should be visible under `node_modules`, and `node_modules` should not be dimmed.
2. Quick open and text search should find files under `node_modules/@types` only. This should also work when `node_modules` is gitignored.
3. Replace the exception with `!**/node_modules/@types` and check that nested `node_modules/@types` folders are found too.

## Performance
Measured on this repo (about 21k files, gitignored `node_modules`), median of 7 warm runs with the built-in ripgrep engines. The extra runs were measured again for the single run per folder: 8 ms for `!node_modules/@types` and 1190 ms for `!**/node_modules/@types`.

| Configuration | File search | Text search |
|---|---|---|
| Default excludes, no exceptions | 164 ms | 944 ms |
| `!node_modules/@types` | 170 ms (extra run: 8 ms) | 931 ms |
| `!**/node_modules/@types` | 1210 ms (extra run: 1035 ms) | 1208 ms |

- **No exceptions:** no change. `parseExcludeExpression(...).matches` is the plain `glob.parse` result, ripgrep runs once with the same arguments, and no deduplication set is created. Micro-benchmark: 25.1 vs 25.7 ms per 10k parses of the default excludes; identical matching speed over 200k paths.
- **Exceptions with a folder path:** one extra ripgrep run that only walks the folders leading to the exceptions.
- **Exceptions starting with `**`:** one extra run over the whole folder, including gitignored folders. This is the cost of making `!**/node_modules/@types` work when `node_modules` is gitignored. To limit the cost:
  - Exceptions don't look into `.git`, `.svn`, `.hg` or `.jj` unless an exception names them. This applies to search and the explorer, and saved about 110 ms with a 2 GB `.git`.
  - `settings.json` shows an info hint on these exceptions (#345013).
  - The `unanchoredExcludeExceptionCount` and `excludeExceptionTime` telemetry fields track how often this happens and what it costs.
- **Memory:** only paths that match an exception are kept for deduplication.

## Validation
Run on the branch merged with current `main`:
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed

title: Hide watermark Open Chat when chat is disabled after first render
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #340454

## Problem

The empty-editor watermark kept offering **Open Chat** (with its keybinding) after `chat.disableAIFeatures` was set, for the rest of the session. The issue reporter correctly identified both causes in `editorGroupWatermark.ts`:

1. Entry `when` clauses were evaluated only during render. The watermark listened for its own setting and workbench-state changes, but not for context-key changes. So when `chatSetupHidden` flipped, nothing triggered an update.
2. `cachedWhen` (the previous session's result, used to avoid entries popping in while keys settle at startup) was consulted *before* the live evaluation and only refreshed at shutdown. So even a re-render would have kept the entry.

This also covered the case where the setting arrives after the first render, e.g. via an extension's `configurationDefaults`.

## Fix

In `EditorGroupWatermark`:

- Listen to `IContextKeyService.onDidChangeContext`, filtered to the keys that watermark entry `when` clauses reference.
- For each affected entry, replace the cached result with the live evaluation. Once a condition has actually changed, the live value is authoritative.
- Re-render only when the visibility of an entry evaluated in the current render actually flips. This keeps the startup no-flicker behavior and avoids reshuffling the filler entries on unrelated or no-op key changes.

The chat gating stays as it was (`chatSetupHidden == false && chatSetupDisabledInWorkspace == false`). `chatSetupHidden` already follows `chat.disableAIFeatures`. No imports from `vs/workbench/contrib`, so layering is unchanged.

## How to test

1. Open a window with no editors (close Welcome, or set `"workbench.startupEditor": "none"`). The watermark shows **Open Chat**.
2. Set `"chat.disableAIFeatures": true`. **Open Chat** disappears immediately.
3. Set it back to `false`. **Open Chat** reappears.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep EditorGroupWatermark`: **passed** (23 passing, including 3 new tests: hide/restore on context change, dropping a stale cached entry, and no re-render when visibility doesn't change). Without the source change, the 2 behavioral tests **fail** (21 passing, 2 failing), confirming they cover the bug.
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/parts/editor/editorGroupWatermark.ts <blob>.test.ts`: **passed**.

  - disabled: `["Show All Commands","Start Debugging","Go to File"]`
  - re-enabled: `["Open Chat","Show All Commands","Start Debugging"]`

title: artifacts: let extension integrations add actions to list items
body:
Lets extension artifact integrations put actions on individual details list items, like the built-in GitHub pull request integration already does (Rerun Check, Resolve Comment). Core already supports item actions; the `chatArtifactIntegrations` proposal didn't expose them yet.

Motivating case: a test plan item (TPI) integration in VS Code Team Tools lists the issues reported against a TPI and needs **Fix Issue** (send a prompt to the artifact's chat) and **Copy Link** on each issue row.

## API (`vscode.proposed.chatArtifactIntegrations.d.ts`)

- `ChatArtifactDetails.itemActions?: ChatArtifactItemAction[]` and `items[].actions?: string[]`, the same shape as the core `ArtifactDetails`.
- An item action has one of two forms:
  - **Direct** (no `actionId`): runs `ChatArtifactDetailsModel.runItemAction(itemId, actionId, token)` in the extension, without run tracking. This is the existing core contract, for effects that are safe to repeat, such as copying a link.
  - **Registered** (`actionId`): runs the integration's registered `ChatArtifactAction` for the item, with `{ detailsId, itemId }` as `ChatArtifactActionContext.input`. The item then gets the action's confirmation, run tracking and, for a prompt action, the artifact's chat. The registered action must be offered and enabled in the state's actions, as for any manual run.

## Implementation

- **Extension host:** `convertDetails` forwards `itemActions` and per-item `actions`. It rejects an item action whose `actionId` isn't a registered action, and direct item actions on a model without `runItemAction`. The new `$runItemAction` revalidates against the current details before calling the extension.
- **Main thread:** `ExtensionArtifactDetails.runItemAction` forwards to the extension host.
- **Manual invocation input:** `IArtifactModel.invoke` and the executor take an optional `input`. It is threaded through the service, composite model, agent host transport (validated as JSON) and the agent host bridge, and stored on the run. `ArtifactRun.input` already existed for automation runs, so it reaches `prepare`/`providePrompt` unchanged. Reusing a request ID with different input is rejected.
- **Agents window:** a registered item action's row button follows the registered action's availability. It shows as running until that item's own run settles, so the same item can't request it twice, while other items stay available. Code actions close the panel, as top-level code actions do.

## Notes for reviewers

- A registered action used by item actions must also be offered among the state or general actions, so it also gets its own button and can run without `input`. The d.ts says this explicitly. For the TPI case that is intended: the top-level Fix Issue lets you pick several issues. If we want item-only actions, I'd add an availability flag in a follow-up.
- Agent tools (`get_artifact_status` / `run_artifact_action`) don't expose item actions yet.

## Validation

- New tests:
  - extension bridge (direct and registered item actions, validation, input reuse);
  - transport (input crosses the agent host protocol and is validated);
  - Agents window (row runs the registered action with the item input, follows availability, stays busy until its run settles).
- `npm run typecheck-client`, eslint on changed files, and all artifact unit tests (709 passing).

body:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.

* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.

Fixes #344950

After a window reload, chat editor tabs for non-local sessions (agent host, Copilot CLI, and other contributed session types) showed the generic title "Chat" until they were revealed. Their title is only known once the session is loaded, and `IChatService.getSessionTitle` only knows local sessions.

This change caches each tab's last known title in its serialized editor state. A restored tab shows that title right away. Once the session loads, the live title takes over as before.

- `ChatEditorInput.getKnownTitle()` returns the title `getName()` would show, or `undefined` when only the generic fallback is known.
- `ChatEditorInputSerializer` stores it as the new `IChatEditorOptions.restoredTitle`.
- `getName()` prefers `restoredTitle` over `title.preferred`, because the title the editor was opened with can be stale after a rename.
- `restoredTitle` is a separate option rather than `title.preferred`, because `ChatEditor.setInput` pushes `title.preferred` into the session title of contributed sessions.
- `copy()` (split/duplicate) still opens a new chat without a title.

title: Agent Host: propagate BYOK request cancellation through the renderer bridge
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses the BYOK provider cancellation issue reported in #340983 for local Agent Host sessions.

When an Agent Host request is stopped, the underlying renderer language model request can continue running after the HTTP client disconnects, leaving provider inference active unnecessarily.

This change propagates cancellation from the HTTP proxy through the BYOK IPC bridge to the renderer language model handler. It also allows pending proxy and IPC operations to settle on cancellation without waiting for late responses.

**Scope:** This PR focuses on cancellation propagation only. It does not implement incremental response streaming or change the existing buffered response architecture.

## Changes

- Add an optional `CancellationToken` parameter to `IByokLmBridgeConnection.chat()`.
- Forward cancellation across the Agent Host BYOK IPC channel to the renderer handler.
- Use `raceCancellationError` to release cancelled bridge operations without waiting for an outstanding renderer response.
- Connect HTTP request aborts to a request-scoped `CancellationTokenSource`.
- Handle already-destroyed HTTP responses and clean up cancellation listeners and resources.
- Extend regression coverage using real IPC serialization and cancellation protocols, including:
  - Cancellation forwarding and isolation between concurrent requests.
  - Cancellation during initialization and connection disposal.
  - Already-cancelled requests and late responses.
  - HTTP client disconnects, shutdown, and upstream aborts.
  - Bundled SDK abort propagation and renderer-side cancellation handling.

## Validation

Tested against VS Code 1.145.0 development (base commit `0f33e8274d74`).

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run compile` | Passed, 0 errors |
| Agent Host BYOK IPC channel tests | 15 passing |
| BYOK HTTP proxy tests | 36 passing |
| Copilot BYOK provider integration tests | 5 passing |
| Chromium renderer BYOK handler tests | 15 passing |
| ESLint on all changed TypeScript files | Passed |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

**Total: 71 passing tests, 0 failures.**

Cancellation behavior was also tested previously with a local BYOK provider setup using an earlier VS Code build. A separate end-to-end Stop-button UI test has not been performed on this development checkout.

## Notes

This PR addresses the cancellation aspect of #340983. Streaming improvements are intentionally outside its scope.

I am happy to coordinate with existing work and adjust the implementation based on maintainer feedback.

This contribution was developed with AI coding assistance. The changes were validated through compilation, linting, and the targeted regression tests listed above.

title: workbench: avoid doubled compact sidebar dividers
body: Fixes #337503. ## Summary - Keep the first connected tab's square, borderless leading edge when horizontal scrolling reconstructs its clipped cap. This avoids adding a second stroke beside the sidebar/editor divider. - Snap Compact layout's painted card separators to native border thickness using the effective device-pixel ratio, including display scaling and window zoom. - Keep that ratio local to each workbench window and update it through the existing pixel-ratio monitor when the window's display scale changes. ## Issues addressed | Severity | Issue | Resolution | |---|---|---| | Low | #337503: an extra leading border appears when the first connected tab is scrolled | Preserve the source cap's square leading-edge state in the overflow cap, and clear the state when clipping is reset. | | Low | The divider below the tab strip looks heavier at fractional zoom | Use the same snapped stroke width for all four painted card edges. | | Medium | Review finding: window zoom alone omits monitor DPI | Use each window's effective pixel-ratio monitor and compare the result against native borders, including fractional display scales. | ## Validation Validation ran with Node 24.22.1 in a clean detached worktree containing only these eight intended changes. Unrelated local edits were excluded from the validation and PR. | Command | Result | |---|---| | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run build-fast -- --client-only` | Passed. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run typecheck-client` | Passed. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 bash scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --run .test.ts --reporter dot` | Passed: 186 tests. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --browser webkit --run src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts --run .test.ts --grep 'window zoom factors\|device pixel ratios\|compact painted dividers\|preserves the first Connected tab edge\|keeps the connected outline inside the visible scroll area' --reporter dot` | Passed: 5 tests in Chromium and 5 in WebKit. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run eslint -- .ts src/vs/workbench/browser/window.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/modernUI/test/browser/modernUI.contribution.test.ts .test.ts src/vs/workbench/test/browser/window.test.ts` | Passed. | | `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/browser/media/floatingPanels.css .css` | Passed. | | `npm run -s precommit` (Git hook) | Passed. | | `git diff --check` | Passed. | The new regressions were confirmed to fail before the corresponding fixes. Coverage includes first/non-first tab transitions, theme and density changes, fractional zoom, clipping-state cleanup, per-window pixel-ratio isolation, display-change notifications, and listener disposal. An additional Chromium renderer probe loaded the candidate's actual stylesheet and compared painted strokes with a real CSS border across 36 combinations of display scales (1×, 1.25×, 1.5×, 2×) and zoom factors. All comparisons matched. In particular: - 125% display scaling at default zoom: painted and native borders both resolve to `0.8px`. - 2× display scaling at 150% zoom: painted and native borders both resolve to `1px`. ### How to test 1. Enable Modern UI, select Compact density, and open enough files for horizontal tab overflow. 2. Select the first tab and scroll it partly out of view. The sidebar/editor seam should not gain a rounded second border. 3. Check that the divider remains the same thickness through the tab strip, breadcrumbs, and editor body. 4. Repeat with fractional window zoom and display scaling. Switching between first and later tabs should retain the later tabs' normal outlines. ## Visual evidence The before image was captured from an unmodified detached worktree at the current-main base `6aeca3c02f4cc1f2315efa2644bd2a972ea030c9`. The same worktree was then given only the curated eight-file patch to capture the after image. Both use identical sample files, Dark 2026, Compact density, 172.8% window zoom, a 2× display (effective pixel ratio 3.456), and a 40px tab scroll offset. The baseline's overflow cap adds a `0.868056px` leading stroke and a `7px` radius; the candidate keeps both at `0px`. The baseline's painted separator remains `1px`, while the candidate matches the native `0.868056px` border. The comparison is cropped to the same sidebar/editor boundary in both captures. The temporary worktree and capture processes were removed after validation. ## Review status - Unresolved actionable findings: None. - Residual risks: A physical Windows desktop and live multi-monitor moves were not exercised; native display-scale rendering and per-window change propagation are covered by the checks above. Screenshot upload and remote CI verification remain outstanding.

Follow-up to #344484 and #344610, which retired the legacy panel and inline chat simulations but left their fixtures, scenarios and helpers behind.

This removes Copilot simulation test (stest) code that can never run, plus test data and helpers that nothing references anymore. Every remaining suite still covers shipping code, and all 130 remaining scenarios replay from the cache with unchanged scores. No product code, cache recordings or CI gates change.

**506 files deleted, 15 edited (4 insertions, 49,103 deletions).** Almost all of it is test data, so reviewing commit by commit is easiest:

### 1. Remove simulation tests that never run
- The `notebook (mbpp)` suite (61 scenarios). `const shouldEvaluate = 1 >> 1` is always 0, so the suite was permanently optional: CI never ran it, and its code-execution check was unreachable. It had no cache recordings, and 43 of its 61 baseline scores were 0. Its two fixtures, its 61 baseline entries and the Python execution check that only it used go with it.
- `slashDoc.py.stest.ts`. It defined no tests and wasn't registered in `simulationTests.ts`; its helper was only exercised by its own unit test.
- The `stest.skip` "command center" case in `settingsEditorSearchResultsSelector.stest.ts`, skipped since at least the June 2025 open-source import.

### 2. Remove simulation fixtures and helpers left orphaned
- 298 unreferenced files under `test/simulation/fixtures/`, and the 199 files in 17 of the 18 folders under `test/scenarios/` (only `test-cli` is still used). Most were left behind by #344484; a few were unreferenced even before it.
- Modules nothing imports (`toolSimTest.ts`, `validate.ts`, `evaluators/pythonFix.ts`, `fileUtils.ts`), `NoopTestToolsService`, the unused tool-call scenario loaders, and the `setupCase`/`json` scenario fields that only `toolSimTest.ts` used.
- Matching `.eslint-allowed-javascript-files` entries, and a stale `.github/CODENOTIFY` entry for the already deleted `inlineEditCode.stest.ts`.

### 3. Tidy dead code in remaining simulation tests
- Commented-out tests in `notebooks.stest.ts` and `devContainerConfigGenerator.stest.ts`.
- The unreachable `server` provider branch in `inlineEdit.stest.ts`, and the `--runServerPoweredNesProvider` simulator flag that only fed it (no server-powered NES provider exists anymore).
- The `typescript` case in `debugTools.stest.ts`. It passed `['javascript']`, so it sent the same request as the `javascript` case and replayed the same cached response. Its baseline and outcome entries go with it.

## How orphans were identified
- **Fixtures:** a fixture counts as used if a non-fixture source file names its path, or names one of its multi-segment parent folders as a string literal. An independent review arrived at the same set. Kept on purpose: the NES recordings under `fixtures/inlineEdits/` (their loader picks up companion files by convention), the two files `summarizedDocumentRendering.spec.tsx` reads, and `notebook/LICENSE`. The cache-only simulation run is the runtime check: a remaining test that loaded a deleted fixture would fail it.
- **Modules:** import reachability from the real entry points (simulator, simulation workbench and extension, vitest/mocha specs, scripts), plus a search for path-based loads.
- **Authorship:** almost all removed lines date from the June 2025 open-source import. Later edits to them were mechanical, such as the `no-unexternalized-strings` rollout and the `@workspace` removal.

## Deliberately kept
- `test/e2e/cli.stest.ts`: skipped in CI, but its author has kept it up to date for manual runs.
- The switched-off printout in `debugTools.stest.ts`: it generates `KNOWN_DEBUGGABLE_*` in `debuggableCommandIdentifier.ts`.
- Test-framework APIs that now have few or no callers (`ssuite.optional`, `stest.skip`, `fromFixtureDir`).

## Validation
Run on top of `0f33e8274d7` (`main` at the time of writing):
- `npm run typecheck` in `extensions/copilot` (all four projects): passed.
- `npm run eslint -- <the 11 modified .ts files>`: passed. `git diff --check`: clean.
- `node dist/simulationMain.js --ci --require-cache` (what `npm run simulate-ci` runs): passed, "Score unchanged in 130 scenarios". The baseline goes from 192 to 130 entries: the 61 mbpp scenarios and the duplicate `typescript` case, nothing else.

title: sessions: link uncommitted files in worktree hint, simplify files picker
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Follow-up to #344870, which added the experiment-controlled `sessions.chat.worktreeSuggestion` setting. The setting stays **off by default**; this changes two of its presentations.

- **Inline Hint** (`inlineHint`): the number of uncommitted files in "main has 6 uncommitted files. Worktrees allow agents to run on a separate copy of the files." is now a link.
  - Clicking it, or pressing Enter or Space on it, opens the uncommitted changes in the Changes editor and the Changes view, like the file rows of the isolation picker, and logs `reviewed`. The hint stays open.
  - The link has a "Show Changes" hover, and is underlined in high contrast themes and with `accessibility.underlineLinks`.
  - Translators get the whole sentence, which is split around the link afterwards.
- **Uncommitted Files Count** (`uncommittedFilesCount`): the isolation picker is more compact.
  - It no longer shows the explanation banner ("main has 6 uncommitted files. On Branch, the agent works alongside them, so its changes can mix with yours.") above its options. The banner's dismiss state and the `explanationClosed` telemetry action are removed with it.
  - The listed files no longer show their folder, which took too much space. The lines added and removed stay. Each row shows the file's path as its tooltip, so same-named files can be told apart, and screen readers still hear the folder.

## How to test

1. Open a Git repository with a few uncommitted files in the Agents window and select Branch isolation for a new session.
2. Run **Developer: Preview Worktree Suggestion...**, pick **Inline Hint**, and start typing. Click the number of uncommitted files: the Changes editor and view open with the uncommitted changes, and the hint stays.
3. Run the command again and pick **Uncommitted Files Count**, then open the isolation picker: it lists the files with their lines added and removed, without a banner or folders.

## Validation

Run using Node.js 24.22.1, after rebasing onto `main` and including the review fix:

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"` — 9042 passed, 25 pending.
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run <blob>.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/newChatWidget.test.ts` — 240 passed.
- `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.ts' | xargs ./node_modules/.bin/eslint --no-cache` — passed.
- `npm run stylelint -- <blob>.css` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `npm run check-cyclic-dependencies` — passed.
- `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer render -p test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex "sessions/chat/(newWidget|isolationPicker)/" --target /tmp/wt-fixtures` — 144 fixtures rendered without errors.

The hint and the isolation picker were also rendered with the real controller, service and picker in temporary component fixtures (not committed), in the dark, light and high contrast themes, with keyboard focus on the link, and with a long file name. They were not exercised in Code OSS for this change.

title: Fix custom agent name collisions in the Copilot agent host
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  <url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Addresses #318422 for the Copilot agent-host harness, building on merged #344780.

- In Copilot bundles only, preserve colliding agent filenames in URI-derived directories and list their paths explicitly in the manifest. Uniquely named files keep their legacy flat paths. When collisions elsewhere change a mixed bundle's nonce, restoration translates unambiguous old flat selections within the same host-owned cache namespace and persists the current URI. Claude and Codex retain the previous layout. Original filenames, authored names, and file contents remain unchanged.
- Preserve same-named definitions when Copilot parses client-supplied plugins, and assign every forwarded definition a stable `vscode-agent-<sha1>` SDK name derived from its logical source URI. Keep friendly `displayName` values and SDK-native agent identities unchanged. Registration, selection, switching, resume, and recovery use the same mapping. SDK descriptions also expose the authored name on one line, including a name-only fallback when no description is authored, so the model can discover agents without relying on displayName.
- Distinguish duplicate picker labels with their extension display name or plugin source in both the editor and Agents Window. Unique names remain plain. Preserve source labels through the client cache and include them in accessible labels/help.

## Provenance and compatibility

The host publishes optional, validated `vscode.sourceUri` metadata identifying the client-supplied file before materialization. The client resolves that URI through its existing origin records and extension discovery; extension display names are not sent to the host or SDK. Missing, malformed, or unavailable provenance retains generic source/file-location fallbacks. Selection remains URI-based; restore-only translation canonicalizes unambiguous legacy flat cache URIs. The optional provenance metadata is not used for SDK identity or execution.

Native plugin parsing keeps its existing name-deduplication behavior unless the Copilot client-supplied-definition path explicitly opts out. No protocol schema or configuration changes are required.

## Validation

Initial implementation validation on rebased commit `5789102975a` (based on main `6c21985de64`); final follow-up validation is listed separately below.

- `npm run install-fast` — passed after closing the demo instance that held native-module file locks.
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- Changed unit suites — **1,586 passed**, using the following PowerShell commands:

```powershell
Remove-Item Env:COPILOT_PROXY_KERBEROS_SPN -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
$testArgs = @('--reporter', 'dot')
foreach ($file in (git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD -- '*.test.ts')) {
  $testArgs += @('--run', ($file -replace '/', '\\'))
}
& .\scripts\test.bat @testArgs
```

- `.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSdkNativeAgents.integrationTest.ts --reporter dot` — **19 passed**, against the bundled real SDK without model requests, covering both SDK modes and create/resume/recovery/live switching.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Changed-file ESLint — **30 files passed**, using:

```powershell

npm run eslint -- @changedFiles
```

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.

### Review follow-up (`5b07b396177`)

- Fixed logical-source identity comparison without rewriting it as a materialized path. Agent-free MCP relocation stays a no-op; the previously failing MCP restart replay passes.
- Case-distinct opaque host URIs retain distinct attribution. Optional extension-caption discovery failures are logged and do not remove agents; cancellation still propagates.
- The synthetic plugin-delegation test resolves SDK IDs from the actual model-facing task catalog. Its negative case reuses an ID advertised before model invocation was disabled, rather than passing an already-invalid authored name. Workspace-native subagent tests intentionally retain their SDK-native names and replay unchanged; no recording edits are needed for those cases.
- Added real-SDK legacy flat-selection resume coverage in both modes. Unique filenames retain flat paths; the follow-up below also handles nonce changes in mixed bundles without guessing ambiguous collision slots.
- Unit selection: **1,777 passed** (`.\scripts\test.bat`, with `--run` for the unit files returned by `git diff --name-only origin/main -- '*.test.ts'`, `--reporter dot`).
- `.\scripts\test-integration.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSdkNativeAgents.integrationTest.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\providerIntegration\copilotMockLlm.integrationTest.ts --reporter dot` — **27 passed**.

### Final restoration follow-up (`62a089c7759`, `f0516f27cf9`)

- Restore only unambiguous legacy flat selections inside the same known host-materialized cache namespace, including mixed bundles whose overall nonce changed. Preserve strict live selection, reject foreign/direct-host/ambiguous aliases, and persist the canonical resource without overwriting newer user choices.
- Canonicalize serialized Windows drive letters without folding case-distinct resource paths. Regression coverage exercises first materialization, cold resume, worktrees, previous cache revisions in both SDK modes, and case-distinct flat files.
- Final PR-only unit selection: **1,597 passed**:

No additional tools, eager-tool slots, reminders, or system-prompt lines were added; the name is configuration-constant agent-description metadata.

### Merge with origin/main (`4a52a40b253`)

title: Leave hidden UI and stylesheets out of copied chat responses
body:
Fixes <url>

Copying a selection from a chat response and pasting it into a Markdown-aware input (such as the chat input) could insert content the reader never saw. This included the hidden file changes summary (`0 files changed+0-0`), its file list, and thousands of characters of Monaco list CSS from the list's embedded `<style>` element. The plain-text clipboard flavor was clean. Only the HTML flavor, which chat writes itself when a selection touches a link, carried the leak.

## Cause

When a selection contains links, `ChatListWidget` writes its own `text/html` flavor so links that only resolve inside VS Code are not shared. It built that HTML by cloning the selected DOM, which also cloned elements that are not rendered. Examples are a summary hidden with `display: none`, the body of a collapsed `<details>`, and the `<style>` element that Monaco lists embed. The HTML-to-Markdown converter then printed the stylesheet as text. The response footer's toolbar, an empty `<ul role="toolbar">`, also became a stray `-` list item.

## Changes

- `chatClipboard.ts`: new `cloneVisibleSelection`, moved here from `ChatListWidget.cloneSelectedContents`. It clones the selection together with its ancestors as before. It then leaves out toolbars and elements the reader cannot see. These are elements that are not rendered, and bodies that collapsed sections hide with `visibility: hidden` or `opacity: 0`. `display: contents` wrappers are kept, because their children render. Hidden elements are marked only for the duration of the clone, and the marks are removed in a `finally` block.
- `htmlToMarkdown.ts`: `style`, `script`, `template` and `noscript` elements produce no text. This also covers HTML pasted from other sources.
- Tests: a regression test in `chatClipboard.test.ts` uses a link, a hidden file changes summary with an embedded list stylesheet, and a footer toolbar. It asserts that formatting survives and none of that UI does. A converter test in `htmlToMarkdown.test.ts` covers the dropped element types.

## Validation

- `chatClipboard.test.ts` and `htmlToMarkdown.test.ts` pass, along with eslint on the changed files and `typecheck-client`.
- Manually tested in Code OSS (Agents window). An agent turn edited a file, and I expanded and collapsed its file changes summary. I then selected from that response into the next turn, copied, and pasted into the chat input.

Before (`main`): the paste contains the hidden file list and its stylesheet.

![before-unfixed-paste](<url>)

After (this PR): only content that is visible in the selection.

![after-fixed-paste](<url>)

Visible chat UI inside the selection, such as the summary header or the response timestamp and model, is still copied, because it is also part of the selected text.

Before, the exemption stayed active while the replaced draft was being deleted, so returning to the replacement chat after visiting another unsent chat kept that chat's input instead of restoring the replacement's own draft. This is the open review thread on #344945.
- Three source comments added by that PR are removed.

## Why

The exemption from the first PR applied to every chat set during a switch, which let another chat's text overwrite a stored draft in a narrow window.

## Things to know

- A pending switch that lands on another unsent chat of the target harness would still carry the typed text, and drafts of chats deleted by a switch stay in the in-memory LRU until evicted. Both are minor and left alone.
- Inline `#file` references and surviving a window reload are still out of scope, as in #344945.

## How to test

The new unit test visits another unsent chat and returns to the replacement while `deleteChat` is pending. In the Agents window, the original flow from #344945 still passes: new chat (Cmd+T), type without sending, switch to the original chat and back, and the prompt is still there.

## Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run <every *.test.ts in src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser, src/vs/sessions/browser/parts/test/browser and src/vs/sessions/test/browser>` on current main plus this branch: 2303 passing, 2 pending.

- Live in Code OSS with `--agents` on a build with the same code: the original repro, the cleared-input case and the sent-prompt case pass. Not run live: the harness switch (needs a session with more than one chat harness) and two simultaneous unsent chats (Cmd+T reuses the single unsent peer chat). Both are covered by unit tests only.
