message:
Engineering - generate the CG NOTICE before compiling in the Quality job (#345073)

* Engineering - generate the CG NOTICE before compiling in the Quality job

Every platform compile job blocks on the Quality job's notice_output artifact
before packaging ("Apply CG NOTICE"). notice@0 often times out against the
NOTICE API after ~4 min and is retried, so in about a third of scheduled
insiders every compile job waited for it, up to 11.7 min on macOS where it
directly delays signing and publishing.

Run the NOTICE steps (built-in extension CG details, Component Detection,
notice@0, cache fallback, merged NOTICE upload) right after dependencies are
installed, before the 3.3 min compile and hygiene step, so the artifact is
ready ~3.3 min earlier. Component Detection reads manifests and lockfiles,
compile only adds copies of src cgmanifest.json files under out-build, so the
detected components are unchanged.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

* Engineering - remove the NOTICE intermediates before the Quality job's lint checks

ESLint rejects the compiled .oss-build-out scripts and hygiene rejects the indentation of ThirdPartyNotices.generated.txt, now that both exist when the compile and hygiene checks run. The NOTICE outputs are already in the artifact staging directory.

agentHost: add scoped permission rules and smart approvals (#345113)

* agentHost: add scoped permission rules and smart approvals

Replaces the tool-wide "Allow in this Session" approval for shell, URL, and file
tools in the agent host. The old approval allowed every later call of the tool. Now
the host offers scoped grants. The grants use permission rules in the format of
Claude Code. The local VS Code client keeps these rules in sync with its settings.

- Adds a permission rule parser and matcher for `Shell(...)`, `WebFetch(...)`,
  `Read(...)`, `Edit(...)`, and bare tool names. Shell rules support wildcard,
  `/regex/`, and `commandLine:` forms. WebFetch rules use VS Code URL patterns with
  https as the default scheme.
- Adds `permissions.ask` next to `allow` and `deny`. A deny rule rejects the call,
  also when Allow All is set. An ask rule always prompts. Rules from the chat, the
  session, and the host are combined.
- Changes the shell and URL confirmations. "Allow Once" is the default. The options
  are "Allow `cmd …` in this Session", "Allow Exact Command in this Session", "Always
  Allow …", "Allow Fetching <host> in this Session", and "Always Allow Fetching
  <host>". Read and write confirmations offer grants for the file and for the
  nearest git root folder. The option ID contains the grant rules, so a client
  cannot forge a grant.
- Moves the default terminal auto-approve rules to a shared platform module. VS Code
  and the agent host use the same rules. The host applies them only where no
  explicit rule matches.
- Syncs `chat.tools.urls.autoApprove`, `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove`, and
  `chat.tools.terminal.ignoreDefaultAutoApproveRules` from user settings to the
  local agent host at start and when they change. "Always Allow" grants on the local
  host are written back to user settings. Remote agent hosts do not sync.

scroll event and the rows container stayed at the estimated offset, showing the
wrong part of the rows.

* Support `!` exclude exceptions in files.exclude and search.exclude

A `!`-prefixed key in files.exclude or search.exclude now marks an exception: matching paths and everything inside them are not excluded, even when another pattern or .gitignore excludes them. Exceptions never add exclusions and do not depend on key order, so settings scopes still merge as before, and `false` keeps disabling a key. Expressions without exceptions parse exactly as before.

The explorer shows the folders that lead to an exception, search re-includes excepted paths with an extra ripgrep run per exception root, and the Settings editor gains an Add Exception action plus a quick fix for `"pattern": false` entries that disable nothing. Other glob settings and the extension API keep treating `!` literally.

message:
Batch stored shell output lookups when restoring Agent Host chats (#341926)

* Batch stored shell output lookups when restoring Copilot sessions

Restoring a Copilot session awaited one SQLite query per completed non-PTY
shell call to find stored full output, so a 2000-turn session with 8000 shell
calls issued 8000 sequential queries. Collect the candidates across the parent
and subagent chats and look them up with a single getTerminalOutputSizes query
that binds the ids as one JSON array, which keeps large sessions within
SQLite's bound-parameter limit.

up all of a chat's restored shell calls with one getTerminalOutputSizes query
instead. Claude still attaches output only where a row exists, and Codex still
reads stored content only for present rows whose replayed output was not
retained.

message:
sessions: Run Dev Container startup commands in one container shell (#344981)

* sessions: Batch Dev Container startup probes and target exec by container ID

Each Dev Container CLI exec takes about five seconds to start. Startup ran the platform, user and Git root probes as five separate execs, and the safe.directory and Git identity setup as up to six more. Probe everything in one exec, and apply safe.directory and identity in one script each, keeping identity after safe.directory and preserving the existing skip and failure behavior.

Pass the started container's ID to every exec and the relay, so the CLI inspects it directly instead of looking it up by label each time.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

* sessions: Run Dev Container startup commands in one container shell

Replace the batched startup scripts with one long-lived /bin/sh, started by a single Dev Container CLI exec, that runs the startup commands one at a time. Each separate exec took about five seconds to start, and startup still made around ten of them.

Each command still runs in its own /bin/sh -c without stdin, so exits, failures and syntax errors stay isolated. The Agent Host start command keeps its own exec because it runs for the host's lifetime, and the relay keeps its own because it carries a byte stream. The shell, both execs and the relay target the started container by ID. The shell closes before the relay starts, and when startup fails or is cancelled.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

message:
cli: decode large msgpack messages in linear time, retry initial resolve (#345146)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

<url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Refs #337090

Two independent fixes found while investigating why **Open in VS Code**
for a Dev Container session on a tunnel host hangs at "Installing
server".

### cli: decode large msgpack messages in linear time

Dev Containers installs the VS Code server (currently ~220 MB) by piping
the downloaded tarball through the Remote - Tunnels exec server as a
single `stream_data` message on the control connection. `MsgPackCodec`
re-ran `rmp_serde::from_read` from the start of the buffer on every
socket read; `from_read` copies the partial binary payload before
hitting EOF, so decoding one large message is O(n²). Reads from a
forwarded port are at most one SSH packet (~32 KB), and no other RPC on
the connection (e.g. `ping`, `spawn`) is processed until the message
completes.

The codec now finds the end of each message with a resumable scanner
over msgpack headers, skipping string/binary/ext payloads by their
declared lengths, and deserializes only complete messages with
`rmp_serde::from_slice`. Nesting deeper than 1024 and the reserved
`0xc1` marker are rejected as invalid data.

Measured with a ~218 MiB `stream_data` message decoded as
`PartialIncoming`, fed in 32 KB chunks:

| Decoder | Time |
|---|---|
| Before (release build) | 384 s |
| After (debug build) | 0.14 s |

### extensions: retry initial remote authority resolution

`_resolveAuthorityInitial` did `return
this._resolveAuthorityWithLogging(...)` inside `try` without `await`, so
rejections escaped the `catch` and the retry loop added in #156444 has
not retried anything since 06b97f6be73 (January 2023). It now awaits,
restoring up to 5 attempts for error ...

Each window caches application storage and syncs it with a delay, so two windows checking within that gap could both show the reminder. A window read the clock before its shared read, so a claim another window made while that read was pending looked like a future timestamp. Add update.showOutdatedBuildReminder (default on) with experiment: { mode: 'auto' }, so ExP can turn the reminder off through the config.update.showOutdatedBuildReminder treatment if it backfires. <!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

## Prerequisite


[microsoft/vscode#345149](<url>)
merged into `main` and provides the generic WebSocket/WebRTC/popup
hardening used here. This branch is rebased directly onto the merged
commits.

## Summary

This enables desktop canvases published by a remote Agent Host to render
in the existing native BrowserView canvas editor.

Remote canvas URLs retain their original URL, including `127.0.0.1`,
while the BrowserView resolves the network from the exact owning
session/chat. The canvas requires that network, preventing a
disconnected, unsupported, or disabled remote from falling back to the
client or an unrelated workspace remote.

## Architecture

```text
Remote Agent Host publishes CanvasState.url
  │
  ▼
AgentHostCanvasCollection projects the exact chat-owned canvas
  │
  ▼
CanvasService creates an unlisted BrowserView for the owning chat
  │
  ▼
SessionBrowserNetworkContribution resolves chat → session → host authority
  │
  ▼
BrowserViewWorkbenchService requires that resolved network
  │
  ▼
Existing authenticated Agent Host BrowserView proxy
  │
  ▼
Remote Agent Host network, including its loopback canvas server
```

### Fail-closed behavior

- `CanvasService` supplies the exact chat owner and requests strict
network resolution.
- `BrowserViewWorkbenchService` resolves the owner even when remote
proxying is disabled, then rejects if that network cannot be used.
- Ambient remote Editor windows delegate TCP to their Agent Host
connection.
- Non-ambient remote hosts present canvases only in the Agents window,
where owning-session resolution exists.
- Local canvases retain their current behavior.

message:
cli: decode large msgpack messages in linear time

The control server re-deserialized the buffered message from its start on every read, copying the partial binary payload each time. A single large stream_data message, such as the ~220 MB VS Code server that Dev Containers pipes through a tunnel exec server, took minutes of CPU and blocked all other RPCs on the connection.

Find message boundaries by incrementally scanning msgpack headers, skipping string and binary payloads by their declared lengths, and deserialize only complete messages.

Refs #337090

message:
Agent Host: let the Copilot sandbox read files and folders the user attaches (#345057)

## Problem

With terminal sandboxing on, the agent can't read a file the user attaches from outside the workspace. Its Read fails with "Outside the sandbox's readable paths", and it asks the user to change the sandbox policy. That breaks the main scenario of the new **+ > Files…** entry (#344792): attaching a file from `~/Desktop`. Attached paths were never added to the sandbox's readable paths.

## Repro

1. Turn on terminal sandboxing and create `~/Desktop/mockup.txt`.
2. In the Agents window, start a session in any folder. Click **+**, then **Files…**, and attach `mockup.txt`.
3. Send `Summarize the attached file.`

## What changes

- Files and folders attached to a message become **read-only** in that session's sandbox before the turn runs. The grant covers only the exact attached path, lasts for the session, and is never saved to settings. Denied paths still win.
- An attached folder that contains the workspace or another writable folder isn't granted, so it can't make that folder read-only. The agent asks for specific files instead.
- In Manual permissions, reading an attached file or folder no longer asks "Allow reading file outside of workspace?". Writes still ask, and so does a symlink that escapes an attached folder.
- If an organization's managed policy sets its own read-only list, attachments aren't added. The agent then says the file is blocked by policy and asks the user to paste its content, instead of asking them to change the policy.

**Open question:** should an explicit attachment be allowed to widen a managed read-only list, for example behind a runtime-owned managed setting? This PR keeps the conservative default.

The inline title-rename input in the session header stopped propagation of
every keydown, so the window-level keybinding dispatcher never saw Cmd/Ctrl+V,
C, X, A or Z. On desktop these are workbench keybindings for plain inputs, so
paste, copy, cut, select all and undo did nothing while renaming.

Only intercept Enter and Escape, matching the sessions list rename inputs.
Plain-key shortcuts such as Space are focus-scoped or guarded by !inputFocus,
so typing still cannot trigger them.

* sessions: let paste and editing shortcuts work in the chat tab rename

The chat tab inline rename input had the same catch-all stopPropagation as
the session header rename, so Cmd/Ctrl+V, C, X, A and Z never reached the
workbench keybinding dispatcher. Only intercept Enter and Escape. The tab's
own Space/arrow/Home/End handlers only react when the tab itself is the
event target, so typing in the input does not switch chats.

chat: give the narrow image batch fixture its own images (fixes flake) (#345062)

The BatchGridNarrow/Light screenshot intermittently differs in the
antialiased edges of its portrait thumbnails. The screenshot runner
renders a contiguous slice of fixtures per worker in one page without
reloading, and BatchGridNarrow follows BatchGrid and BatchGridInProgress,
which render byte-identical data: URL images at larger sizes. Chromium
can then draw the narrow grid's ~1/20-scale portrait thumbnails from
those larger decodes, so the pixels depend on which fixtures rendered
earlier in the page and on what is still cached.

Offset BatchGridNarrow's image variants so that its images (same
palettes and dimensions, different labels) are never shared with the
wider batch fixtures.

message:
agentHost: resolve remote Working Set files and track parallel edits (#345031)

In a window attached to a remote (WSL, dev container, SSH), the ambient agent host runs on the remote but its sessions resolve with the reserved `local` authority. The session Working Set, the editor review and Keep/Undo matching converted the host's changeset files with that authority, which leaves `file:` URIs unwrapped, so clicking a changed file opened a path on the client's disk (shown with Windows separators on a Windows client) and failed. They now use the authority of the connection's resource URIs, as artifact pills already did.

FileEditTracker kept one pending and one completed edit per file path. When a batch of tool calls edited one file in parallel, each start replaced the previous one: only one call's edit was recorded and the other calls' edit leases leaked, so the file stayed marked as being edited for the rest of the session. The Working Set then under-counted the agent's changes, the editor review skipped the file and Undo timed out. Edits are now tracked per tool call, matched by tool input or else in order; an edit that starts while others of the file are pending begins from what the last of them wrote; and every lease is released when its edit is taken or dropped.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

message:
chat: clear the source draft after forking with /fork prompt (#344995)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

<url>
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## What

In an agent-host chat, `/fork prompt <prompt>` creates a peer chat,
sends the prompt to it, and opens it. When you returned to the source
chat, its input still showed `/fork prompt <prompt>`. With this change
it is cleared once the fork succeeds.

## Why

The fork opens before the `/fork` slash command settles. Opening it
released the source chat's model, which tore down its agent-host draft
sync. That teardown flushed the submitted text to the source chat's
draft on the agent host. The success callback then cleared the input of
an already-disposed model, so the clear never reached the host.
Reopening the source chat restored the host draft, which takes
precedence over the local copy.

The agent host only persists what the client sends: `ChatDraftChanged`
is client-dispatched, and the host cannot tell that a fork's
`initialMessage` came from the source chat's composer. So the fix
belongs in the client.

## How

- The captured source input (`captureForkPromptSourceInput`) now holds a
reference to the source chat until the fork's outcome is known.
- On success, it clears the draft if it is unchanged since submission,
then releases the chat. The cleared draft is what syncs to the host.
- If the fork is not dispatched or fails, it releases the chat with the
draft intact, so the prompt can still be retried as before.
- The `/fork` `prompt` argument parsing (`parseForkPromptArgument`) and
the source-draft ownership now live together in `chatForkActions.ts`.
The `/fork` slash command and the chat widget share them instead of each
keeping its own copy of the parsing. The widget keeps only its
submission gating and plumbing ...

message:
Agent host: use SQLite's write-ahead log for local databases (#345014)

* Agent host: use SQLite's write-ahead log for local databases

The agent host databases used SQLite's defaults: every commit creates a
rollback journal, flushes the disk at least twice and deletes the
journal, and reads queue behind writes. Where flushes are slow, such as
on Windows, this cost every session: on Windows CI, catalog writes took
142 ms against 35 ms on Linux, and disposing a session 473 ms against
33 ms.

AgentHostDatabase and SessionDatabase now switch a database file on a
local file system to the write-ahead log with synchronous = NORMAL. A
commit then appends to the log, and the disk is only flushed when the
log is checkpointed. After a power loss or an OS crash the last commits
can roll back, but the database stays consistent, and a crash of the
process loses nothing.

Databases on Windows UNC paths and on Linux network or FUSE file
systems keep the rollback journal, as the write-ahead log needs shared
memory. When another connection's lock prevents the switch, the
database keeps its journal until a later open.

On Windows CI, the Agent Host E2E suites take 28% to 49% less time,
which brings both Windows shards to about 10 minutes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

* Agent host: keep the rollback journal on mapped network drives and moved databases

A drive letter on Windows can be a mapped network drive, so the journal
check now also resolves the database's directory to its real path and
keeps the rollback journal when that is a UNC path, or when it cannot be
resolved.

The write-ahead log persists in the database file, so a database that
moved from a local disk to a network share stayed in it. Opening a
database file that cannot use the write-ahead log now returns it to the
rollback journal, unless another connection's transaction prevents
that, in which case a later open retries.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

The first lookup scans all PATH folders concurrently, and the scans share the
set of labels found so far, so each executable is added by only one scan. A
folder that PATH lists twice was scanned twice: its executables were split
between the two scans, but only the first occurrence's result was cached.
Lookups that read the cache then missed the executables that the other scan
had found, so "results are the same on successive calls" failed whenever the
first occurrence's scan lost the race.

pnpm run (and pnpm exec) put the repository's root node_modules/.bin on PATH
twice, as the package's and as the workspace root's bin folder, where npm run
put it once. The extension host tests run through pnpm run test-extension, and
on macOS CI the second lookup missed all of node_modules/.bin. Users whose PATH
lists a folder twice could lose its executables from completions in the same
way.

Scan each folder once per lookup, and test a PATH that lists a folder twice.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

message:
Batch chat table scrollbar measurements to avoid a layout per table (#342234)

* Batch chat table scrollbar measurements to avoid a layout per table

Each markdown table in a chat response re-measured its horizontal
scrollbar with scanDomNode(), which reads the table's layout and then
updates the scrollbar DOM. Running these back to back forced one
synchronous layout of the transcript per table (44 forced layouts,
~280 ms, when switching to a session with 44 tables).

Schedule the tables instead: all pending tables in a window are read in
one dom.measure callback and their scrollbars are updated in a later
dom.modify callback in the same animation frame.

Refs #341282

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

* Measure a chat table in the window it moved to

A table is wrapped before its markdown is mounted, so its first scrollbar measurement is queued on the main window. When the chat is shown in an auxiliary window, later layout requests were ignored because the table was already queued, so its scrollbar stayed unmeasured until the main window drew another frame, which never happens while that window is minimized.

A table that is already queued for another window now leaves that queue and is measured with the window that currently shows it.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

* Test that resizing a markdown part re-measures its tables in one frame

The markdown part's resize observer runs the same table layout callbacks that
now only queue their table, so a resize already measures every table together
at the next animation frame. Let tests pass a fake resize observer to the part
and add a test that drives that observer with four tables. On the previous
table code, the same test sees 24 layout reads inside the resize callback,
20 of them after a scrollbar update.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <<email>>

message:
Markdown: harden copy destination checks in Restricted Mode (#345008)

Follow-up to #344989, addressing its review comments and a Windows bug
found while verifying it in Code OSS.

In Restricted Mode, the Markdown extension only copies pasted or dropped
files to destinations inside the workspace. The check from #344989 had
three problems:

- **Path casing:** it compared paths case-sensitively. On Windows, the
workspace folder URI and the document URI can differ in drive letter
case (`/C:/...` vs `/c:/...`), so every destination looked outside the
workspace and no media file was copied at all. Containment now uses
`vscode.workspace.getWorkspaceFolder`, which follows the case
sensitivity of the workspace folder's file system.
- **Backslashes:** it treated `\` as a separator everywhere. On POSIX,
`\` is a regular file name character, so `../../project\other/img.png`
could pass the check while resolving outside the workspace. Destinations
whose path below the workspace root contains `\` are now rejected on
every platform.
- **Symbolic links and junctions:** the check was purely lexical. A
folder inside the workspace that links to a folder outside it let a
paste write outside. Each existing path segment below the root,
including an existing target file, is now checked with
`vscode.workspace.fs.stat`, and destinations that pass through a link
are rejected.

When a configured destination is rejected, the file is copied next to
the document instead; if that is rejected too, the file is not copied
and the link points to the original file. Trusted workspaces are
unchanged.

Tests: unit tests cover each case, and all `markdown-language-features`
tests pass. Verified in Code OSS on Windows in a Restricted Mode
workspace that sets `markdown.copyFiles.destination` to a path outside
the workspace and contains a junction to an outside folder:

| Build | Paste into `README.md` | Paste into `docs/README.md`
(junction) |
|---|---|---|
| #344989 + casing fix, without link check | – | ❌ ...

message:
Spare custom editor cursor lines on auto save in side-by-side diffs and with different path casing (#345004)

Fixes <url>

<url> made auto save leave the
cursor line alone when trimming trailing whitespace and final newlines
in custom text editors such as the Markdown editor. It looks for visible
editors that show the saved file and uses the selection they report
through the proposed `customTextEditorNavigation` API. Two cases were
missed and still trimmed the line being typed on:

- **Side-by-side custom diff:** a custom editor shown as one side of a
side-by-side diff sits inside a `DiffEditorInput`, whose resource is
undefined when the two sides differ. The lookup now also checks the
primary and secondary panes of a `SideBySideEditor`, as `EditorService`
does for visible text editor controls.
- **Path casing:** resources are now compared with
`IUriIdentityService`, so a custom editor input with different path
casing still matches the text model on case-insensitive file systems.

Both changes apply to the cursor lookup and to the fallback that skips
trimming when a non-code editor reports no cursor.

## Validation

- New save participant tests cover a custom editor inside a side-by-side
diff, with and without a reported cursor.
- All save participant tests, the `src` typecheck, and ESLint pass.

Found in the Copilot review of
<url> Its third comment,
about the selection arriving after the edit with a very short auto save
delay, is not addressed here: a proper fix needs the API to report the
document version along with the selection.

title: [eslint-plugin-react-hooks] 7.1.1 still accepts zod-validation-error 3.5.4, which has no ./v4 export (ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED)
body:
### Summary

`<email>` (the current `latest`) still declares `"zod-validation-error": "^3.5.0 || ^4.0.0"`, but its CJS build does `require('zod-validation-error/v4')`. `<email>` satisfies that range and does not export `./v4`, so when a package manager picks 3.5.4 the plugin fails to load:

```
Error [ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED]: Package subpath './v4' is not defined by "exports" in
…/node_modules/zod-validation-error/package.json
```

This is the same bug as #35045, which was auto-closed as stale ("please create a new issue if it is still present in the latest release"). It is still present in 7.1.1. The fix PR, #36486 ("Fix zod-validation-error dependency range"), was closed without being merged.

### How we hit it

- pnpm 10.33, `nodeLinker: hoisted`
- `<email>` → `<email>`
- Another dev dependency in the same project (`@figma/<email>`) depends on `zod-validation-error@^3`. pnpm dedupes both onto **3.5.4**, which satisfies both ranges, and `eslint` / `expo lint` crash while loading the config.

### Expected

The declared range should exclude versions without the `./v4` export. #36486's `>=3.5.0 <3.5.4 || ^4.0.0` does that, and so would plain `^4.0.0`.

### Workaround

A scoped pnpm override:

```yaml
overrides:
  'eslint-plugin-react-hooks>zod-validation-error': ^4.0.2
```

title: act warns for an awaited call when Zone.js patches queueMicrotask
body:
## Environment

- React: 19.3.1
- Zone.js: 0.16.3
- Runtime: Bun 1.4.4

## Reproduction

```js
import "zone.js";
import { act } from "react";

globalThis.IS_REACT_ACT_ENVIRONMENT = true;
await act(async () => {});
```

Running this prints:

```text
You called act(async () => ...) without await. This could lead to unexpected testing behaviour, interleaving multiple act calls and mixing their scopes. You should - await act(async () => ...);
```

The `act` result is awaited, and the callback is empty. The warning also reproduces with React Testing Library's `await act(async () => cleanup())` teardown. It does not reproduce when the same thenable is adopted by calling its `then` method directly:

```js
await new Promise((resolve, reject) => act(async () => {}).then(resolve, reject));
```

## Expected behavior

An awaited `act` call should not emit the unawaited-call warning when Zone.js is present.

## Impact

Tests that use Zone.js for asynchronous context propagation receive a false positive from React's `act` warning, making genuine unawaited `act` calls harder to identify.

Bug: Submitting or resetting forms crashes when form fields are named "reset" or "method"
body:
### React version:
19.x / main branch

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Include an `<input name="reset" />` inside a form using React 19 form actions:
```jsx
<form action={myAction}>
  <input name="username" defaultValue="test" />
  <input type="reset" name="reset" value="Reset" />
</form>
```
2. Include an `<input type="hidden" name="method" value="DELETE" />` inside a form using `useFormStatus()`.

### Current Behavior
In HTML DOM, named form controls shadow properties on `HTMLFormElement`:
1. In `resetFormInstance`, calling `form.reset()` throws `TypeError: form.reset is not a function` because `form.reset` is the input element.
2. In `FormActionEventPlugin`, reading `form.method` returns the `HTMLInputElement` instead of `'get'` or `'post'`, which corrupts `useFormStatus().method` and crashes if rendered into JSX (`Objects are not valid as a React child`).

### Expected Behavior
1. React should invoke `HTMLFormElement.prototype.reset.call(form)` to ensure the form is safely reset.
2. React should read `form.getAttribute('method')` to normalize `useFormStatus().method` to a valid string (`'get'`, `'post'`, `'dialog'`).

```

### Current Behavior
React checks `isUnitlessNumber(name)`. Because `shapeImageThreshold` and `mathDepth` are not in `unitlessNumbers`, React automatically appends `'px'`, generating:
`shape-image-threshold: 0.5px; math-depth: 1px;`
Per the CSS Shapes Level 1 and MathML specs, these properties only accept unitless numbers. Browsers reject values with `px` units as invalid CSS and silently discard them.

### Expected Behavior
React should recognize `shapeImageThreshold`, `mathDepth`, and `maskBorder*` properties as unitless numbers and output them without `'px'`.

title: Bug: onResize does not use SyntheticUIEvent (event.view and event.detail are undefined)
body:
### React version:
19.x / main branch

### Steps To Reproduce
1. Render an element with an `onResize` listener (e.g. `<video onResize={e => console.log(e.view, e.detail)} />`).
2. Dispatch or trigger a native `resize` event (`new UIEvent('resize', { view: window, detail: 0 })`).

### Current Behavior
In `packages/react-dom-bindings/src/events/plugins/SimpleEventPlugin.js`, `SyntheticUIEvent` is used for `scroll` and `scrollend`:
```javascript
case 'scroll':
case 'scrollend':
  SyntheticEventCtor = SyntheticUIEvent;
  break;
```
However, `case 'resize':` is missing from the switch statement. As a result, `onResize` falls back to base `SyntheticEvent`. Because `SyntheticEvent` does not implement `UIEventInterface`, properties like `event.view` (the Window) and `event.detail` evaluate to `undefined`.

### Expected Behavior
Per the W3C UI Events specification, `resize` is an instance of `UIEvent`. `onResize` should instantiate `SyntheticUIEvent` alongside `scroll` and `scrollend` so that `event.view` and `event.detail` are properly normalized.

The transition mounts no new Suspense boundary, so React waits for X instead of showing a fallback. - The 100 ``s make a full render of `` take about 300 ms, time-sliced. They are only there so that X resolves while React is rendering the deferred lane (see "Timing" below). ## The current behavior The page shows "before" until `value` resolves, and then shows "value". `'initialValue'` is never committed, although X resolved about 3 seconds earlier: ```text [157ms] X (lazy component) resolved [3304ms] committed: value ``` With `?value=never`, the transition never commits, and the page stays on "before". ## The expected behavior The transition commits `'initialValue'` once X has resolved, and switches to `value` when it resolves. 19.2.9 and 19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731 do this with the same code: ```text [157ms] X (lazy component) resolved [759ms] committed: initialValue [3004ms] committed: value ``` ## Results I ran the code above in headless Chromium (Playwright 1.62) with the default timings: X at 150 ms, `value` at 3000 ms. Each run loads the page, clicks the button, and records when `#content` changes, in ms after the click. In all runs below, X resolved 157–164 ms after the click. Production builds, 30 runs each: | React | committed `initialValue` first | skipped `initialValue` (first commit was `value`) | first commit (ms after click) | |---|---|---|---| | 19.3.0-canary-278794d7-20261002 | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 3303–3306 | | 19.3.0-canary-dc9aed36-20261027 | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 3302–3306 | | 19.3.0 | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 3303–3311 | | 19.3.1 | 0 / 30 | 30 / 30 | 3303–3310 | | 19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731 | 30 / 30 | 0 / 30 | 759–769 | | 19.2.9 | 30 / 30 | 0 / 30 | 759–776 | | 19.3.0-canary-278794d7-20261002 with the `getEntangledLanes` line removed from `markRootSuspended` | 30 / 30 | 0 / 30 | 759–769 | A bundle built with the exact commands from "Steps To Reproduce" (278794d7) also skipped `initialValue` in 10 / 10 runs (first commit at 3303–3306 ms). With `?value=never` (production, 10 runs each, 3 s timeout), 278794d7 and dc9aed36 never committed (10 / 10 each). cbb046ab and 278794d7 without the line committed `initialValue` at 759–763 ms (10 / 10 each). Development builds behave the same (10 runs each). 278794d7 and dc9aed36 skipped `initialValue` in 10 / 10 (first commit at 3304–3309 ms). cbb046ab, 19.2.9 and 278794d7 without the line committed `initialValue` first in 10 / 10 (763–768 ms). ### Timing The bug needs X to resolve after the transition render has suspended on it and before the deferred render finishes. In this repro the deferred render starts about 9 ms after the click and, if nothing restarts it, takes about 300 ms, so X at 150 ms is in the middle of that window. Sweeping X's delay with `?lazy=` (production, 4 runs per point): | X resolved (ms after click) | 278794d7: `initialValue` skipped | 278794d7 without the line: `initialValue` skipped | |---|---|---| | 1 | 0 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 7 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 31 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 61 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 109 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 211 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 259 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 289 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 307 | 4 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 322–324 | 0 / 4 | 0 / 4 | | 402–403 | 0 / 4 | 0 / 4 | At 1 ms, X resolves before the transition render has finished, and that render commits `initialValue` (at 303 ms). From about 320 ms on, X resolves after the deferred render has finished. T is pinged while nothing is rendering, so React renders T next and commits `initialValue` (at 625–706 ms). ## Lane trace This is from the same repro on a production build of 278794d7 with logging added to `prepareFreshStack` ("render start"), `pingSuspendedRoot`, `markRootSuspended` (state after it ran) and `commitRoot`. The indented lines are my notes. - `T = 0x100` is the transition lane. - `D = 0x40000` is the deferred lane spawned by `useDeferredValue`. - `0x40000000` is `DeferredLane`. ```text [1ms] render start lanes=0x100 (T) Content: useDeferredValue -> 'initialValue' (spawns D) LazyWidget suspends on X; no new boundary to show a fallback [2ms] markRootSuspended in=0x100 spawned=0x40000 root.suspended -> 0x100 [9ms] render start lanes=0x40000 (D) entangled=0x40040100 (DeferredLane | D | T) Content: useDeferredValue -> value (pending) -> suspends [158ms] X resolved [159ms] ping lanes=0x100 (T) wipRenderLanes=0x40000 root.pinged -> 0x100 not recorded in workInProgressRootPingedLanes (T is not a subset of the render lanes) [159ms] ping lanes=0x40000 (D) wipRenderLanes=0x40000 recorded; the D render restarts [159ms] render start lanes=0x40000 entangled=0x40040100 root.suspended=0x100 root.pinged=0x100 Content suspends on value again [460ms] markRootSuspended in=0x40000 root.pinged 0x100 -> 0x0 root.suspended -> 0x40040100 (nothing is scheduled; T is never rendered again) [3002ms] ping lanes=0x40000 (value resolved) [3003ms] render start lanes=0x40000 entangled=0x40040100 [3303ms] commit lanes=0x40000 -> committed: value ``` On 19.3.0-canary-cbb046ab-20260731 the same run looks the same up to the second `markRootSuspended`. There, `markRootSuspended` leaves T pinged, and React renders T next: ```text [459ms] markRootSuspended in=0x40000 root.pinged 0x100 -> 0x100 root.suspended -> 0x40100 [459ms] render start lanes=0x100 [759ms] commit lanes=0x100 spawned=0x80000 -> committed: initialValue ``` In the Next.js app where I first saw this, the lanes were `T = 0x200` and `D = 0x80000`. There was no ping for D, so the D render was not restarted. The end is the same: `markRootSuspended(D)` clears T's ping. ## Where it happens `markRootSuspended` in `ReactFiberWorkLoop.js`: ```js // When suspending, we should always mark the entangled lanes as suspended. suspendedLanes = getEntangledLanes(root, suspendedLanes); suspendedLanes = removeLanes(suspendedLanes, workInProgressRootPingedLanes); ... _markRootSuspended(root, suspendedLanes, spawnedLane, didAttemptEntireTree); // root.pingedLanes &= ~suspendedLanes ``` The `getEntangledLanes` line was added by #37290 ("[flags] Enable enableParallelTransitions"). The code path is unchanged on `main` after #37771 ("[flags] clean up enableParallelTransitions"). The sequence: 1. The transition render (T) suspends on X. `markRootSuspended(T, spawnedLane = D)` calls `markSpawnedDeferredLane`, so `entanglements[D] |= DeferredLane | T`. 2. `getNextLanes` prefers the non-suspended D over the suspended T. Rendering D pulls in T and `DeferredLane` through `getEntangledLanes`, so `mountDeferredValueImpl` returns `value`, and the render suspends on it. 3. X resolves during that render. `pingSuspendedRoot` sets `root.pingedLanes |= T`, but records into `workInProgressRootPingedLanes` only when `isSubsetOfLanes(workInProgressRootRenderLanes, pingedLanes)`. T is only entangled into the current render, so the ping is not recorded. 4. D suspends. `markRootSuspended(D)` expands to the entangled lanes, which include T, and clears T's ping. With `didAttemptEntireTree`, it also adds T to `warmLanes`, so T is not prerendered either. 5. Nothing will ping T again. The root wakes only when `value` resolves and pings D. ## Verified changes The first column is this repro (production build of 278794d7 with the change applied, default timings). The second column is from the Next.js app E2E reproduction described under "Impact in Next.js" (the "never commits" variant). | Change | This repro: `initialValue` skipped / runs | App E2E: stalled / runs | |---|---|---| | none (baseline) | 30 / 30 | 6 / 30 | | remove the `getEntangledLanes` expansion in `markRootSuspended` (pre-#37290 behavior) | 0 / 30 | 0 / 40 | | keep the expansion, but do not re-suspend entangled lanes that are already pinged: `suspendedLanes = getEntangledLanes(root, suspendedLanes) & ~(root.pingedLanes & ~renderedLanes)`, where `renderedLanes` is the `suspendedLanes` argument before the expansion | 0 / 20 | 0 / 30 | | in `pingSuspendedRoot`, check `getEntangledLanes(root, workInProgressRootRenderLanes)` instead of `workInProgressRootRenderLanes` | 20 / 20 | 8 / 30 | The last change is not sufficient. The ping on T restarts the D render, and the next `markRootSuspended(D)` clears the ping again. In this repro the D render is already restarted by D's own ping, so the change makes no difference here. I'm not suggesting the second change is the right fix for every parallel-transition case. It only shows that the lost ping is the cause. ## Impact in Next.js (Cache Components / partial prefetching) The App Router's layout router renders every segment through `useDeferredValue(rsc, prefetchRsc)`. On a navigation into a prefetched shell: - `prefetchRsc` is the shell. - `rsc` is the dynamic data that is still streaming. - X is a client component chunk referenced by the shell. The RSC client starts loading it when the prefetch response is decoded. **Without any test tooling,** the navigation sometimes skips the shell and waits for the dynamic data instead. I measured this by delaying the dynamic response by 3000 ms and the destination's JS chunk by 0–116 ms (30 runs): - Baseline: when the chunk was delayed 28–52 ms, 7/30 navigations committed at 3055–3072 ms. Every other run committed at 43–174 ms. - With the expansion removed: all 30 committed at 41–124 ms and showed the shell. **Under Next's Instant Navigation testing lock,** the dynamic data is withheld until the lock is released, so the same sequence never commits. The test times out. ## Related - #37805 and #37830 (fixed by #36134; backport #38013): also a dropped ping followed by `markRootSuspended` clearing it. That case is a synchronous ping during the render of the same lane. Here the ping arrives asynchronously for a lane that is only entangled into the render (the deferred lane D), and the entangled expansion clears it. #36134 is already included in `278794d7` and does not cover this case. --- _This report was prepared with the help of an AI coding agent. The repro, measurements and traces above come from actual runs._

[Compiler Bug]: Rust port panics on non-ASCII identifiers ending with `Ref` (`is_ref_like_name`)
body:
The Rust port panics in `is_ref_like_name` when a `*Ref` identifier starts with a multi-byte character.

### Repro

```tsx
import { useRef } from 'react';

export function Component() {
  const 한글Ref = useRef(0);
  return <div onClick={() => { 한글Ref.current += 1; }} />;
}
```

```
panicked at .../react_compiler_typeinference/src/infer_types.rs:
end byte index 1 is not a char boundary; it is inside '한' (bytes 0..3 of string)
```

Observed through oxlint 1.89.0, which vendors these crates. The line is unchanged on `main` (`compiler/crates/react_compiler_typeinference/src/infer_types.rs:249`). Any `*Ref` identifier whose first character is multi-byte (Korean, Japanese, emoji, ...) triggers it on `.current` access. The TS compiler is unaffected.

### Cause

```rust
&& object_name[..1]
  .chars()
  .next()
  .is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '$' || c == '_')
```

`[..1]` slices a byte, not a character. The TS original (`/^(?:[a-zA-Z$_][a-zA-Z$_0-9]*)Ref$|^ref$/`) returns `false` for these names.

### Suggested fix

```rust
&& object_name
  .chars()
  .next()
  .is_some_and(|c| c.is_ascii_alphabetic() || c == '$' || c == '_')
```

Same class of bug as #37539.

title: Bug: [Flight] A Node.js Buffer is sent as binary at the root but through toJSON when nested
body:
<!--
  Please provide a clear and concise description of what the bug is. Include
  screenshots if needed. Please test using the latest version of the relevant
  React packages to make sure your issue has not already been fixed.
-->

React version: 19.3.1

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Pass a Node.js `Buffer` to the client, once as the root and once inside an object.
2. Look at the different outcomes of `createFromNodeStream`.


server.mjs (`node --conditions react-server server.mjs`):

```js
import { renderToPipeableStream } from "react-server-dom-webpack/server.node";

const buffer = Buffer.from([1, 2, 3, 4]);
const model =
  process.argv[2] === "root"
  ? buffer
  : { nested: buffer, viaPromise: Promise.resolve(buffer) };
renderToPipeableStream(model, {}).pipe(process.stdout);
```

client.mjs (`node client.mjs`):

```js
import { createFromNodeStream } from "react-server-dom-webpack/client.node";

const result = await createFromNodeStream(process.stdin, {
  moduleMap: {},
  serverModuleMap: null,
  moduleLoading: null,
});
if (ArrayBuffer.isView(result)) {
  console.log("root:", result);
} else {
  console.log("nested:", result.nested);
  console.log("viaPromise:", await result.viaPromise);
}
```

```sh
node --conditions react-server server.mjs | node client.mjs
node --conditions react-server server.mjs root | node client.mjs
```

Link to code example: <url>

## The current behavior

```text
nested: { type: 'Buffer', data: [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ] }
viaPromise: Uint8Array(4) [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]
root: Uint8Array(4) [ 1, 2, 3, 4 ]
```

As the root, or as the value of a Promise, the Buffer arrives as a Uint8Array. Inside an object or array it goes through `Buffer.prototype.toJSON` first and arrives as `{type: 'Buffer', data: [...]}`.


## The expected behavior

I'd expect a Buffer to be sent as binary everywhere, the same way it already is at the root. It is a Uint8Array, and structuredClone treats it as one too (`structuredClone(Buffer.from([1]))` is a Uint8Array).

`fs.readFile`, zlib, crypto, and libraries that decode data from Node streams all hand out Buffer, and it's difficult for users to convert every instance.

It came up for us through a bug report against a protobuf library: on Node.js, decoded bytes fields can be Buffers, and passed to a Client Component they don't arrive as bytes.

title: Bug: Fabric renderer should call dispatchNativeEvent when the event target is null
body:
React Native PR <url> (for <url>) lets `dispatchNativeEvent` accept a null target and still release the JS responder. This issue tracks the matching change in React.

React version: main (react-native-renderer, `ReactFabricEventEmitter.js`)

## Steps To Reproduce

1. In React Native, turn on `enableNativeEventTargetEventDispatching` and start a touch on a view.
2. Unmount that view before the touch ends, then tap any Pressable.

Link to code example: the React Native issue above has the details.

## The current behavior

The `eventTarget != null` guard in `ReactFabricEventEmitter.js` makes the renderer skip `dispatchNativeEvent` when the target is null. The touch end never reaches the JS responder. The old responder stays set, the touch count stays one too high, and the next tap is lost.

## The expected behavior

Remove the guard and let the Flow type for the target allow null. Then `dispatchNativeEvent` runs with a null target and releases the responder. React Native syncs this code from this repo, so the change must be made here. It must land after the React Native PR merges, because the current `dispatchNativeEvent` crashes on a null target.

title: [Compiler Bug]: React Compiler loses the sign of negative zero
body:
### What kind of issue is this?

- [x] React Compiler core (the JS output is incorrect, or your app works incorrectly after optimization)
- [ ] babel-plugin-react-compiler (build issue installing or using the Babel plugin)
- [ ] eslint-plugin-react-hooks (build issue installing or using the eslint plugin)
- [ ] react-compiler-healthcheck (build issue installing or using the healthcheck script)

### Link to repro

<url>

### Repro steps

When a prop selects between `0` and `-0`, the compiled component returns `Infinity` for `1 / value` in both branches. The negative-zero branch should return `-Infinity`.

#### Steps To Reproduce

##### Playground

1. Open the [React Compiler Playground reproduction - playground.react.dev](<url>).
2. Inspect the compiled output for this component:

```jsx
export function SignedZero({ condition }) {
  let value;
  if (condition) {
  value = 0;
  } else {
  value = -0;
  }
  return <output>{1 / value}</output>;
}
```

##### Reproduction repository

The [repository reproduction](<url>) includes setup instructions and a runtime comparison using React **19.3.1** and the TypeScript compiler built from commit [`9ffcb463b`](<url>). It was tested on macOS arm64 with Node.js 22.22.2 and Yarn Classic 1.22.22.

#### The current behavior

##### Playground

The compiler folds `1 / value` to `Infinity`, regardless of `condition`:

```jsx
t1 = <output>{Infinity}</output>;
```

##### Reproduction repository

The runtime comparison reports:

```text
condition=true expected=Infinity actual=Infinity
condition=false expected=-Infinity actual=Infinity
condition=true expected=Infinity actual=Infinity
Bug reproduced: the compiled result loses the branch-dependent sign.
```

#### The expected behavior

The compiled component should distinguish `0` from `-0`. For `true → false → true`, it should return `Infinity → -Infinity → Infinity`, matching the original component.

### How often does this bug happen?

Every time

### What version of React are you using?

19.3.1

### What version of React Compiler are you using?

React Compiler, built from react/react commit 9ffcb463b0ab01a42e781d4dc2e00f3a1b97a188

body:

title: [Compiler Bug]: Local copy of a module-level variable is replaced by the variable itself inside closures
body:
### What kind of issue is this?

- [x] React Compiler core (the JS output is incorrect, or your app works incorrectly after optimization)
- [ ] babel-plugin-react-compiler (build issue installing or using the Babel plugin)
- [ ] eslint-plugin-react-hooks (build issue installing or using the eslint plugin)
- [ ] react-compiler-healthcheck (build issue installing or using the healthcheck script)

### Link to repro

<url>

### Repro steps

Inside a function nested in a component (an event handler, for example), a local copy of a module-level `let` is replaced by the module variable itself. When the handler then reassigns the variable, every later use of the "copy" sees the new value.

Input:

```js
let pending = 'value';

export function Component() {
  const handleClick = () => {
  const copy = pending;
  pending = null;
  console.log(copy); // expected: 'value'
  };
  return <button onClick={handleClick}>Click</button>;
}
```

Output (the handler is outlined to `_temp`):

```js
function _temp() {
  pending = null;
  console.log(pending); // logs null
}
```

`const copy = pending` is dropped and `copy` is rewritten to `pending`, which is read after the assignment. The copy has to survive because the variable is reassigned before it is read.

What I checked with babel-plugin-react-compiler directly (the same output in `1.0.0` and `0.0.0-experimental-a1856f3-20260507`):

- **Outlining is not required.** When the handler captures a prop and stays inline, the copy is still dropped (`value = null; console.log(label, value);`).
- **Sync or async makes no difference.**
- **Only functions inside components are affected.** The same function outside a component compiles unchanged. In the render body itself, the compiler bails out of the component, as expected.

How we hit it in production: a PWA install button kept Chrome's `beforeinstallprompt` event in a module-level variable (it fires before the component mounts). The click handler did `const event = deferred; deferred = null; await event.prompt();`, which compiled to `deferred = null; await deferred.prompt();`, so every press threw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'prompt')`. Workaround: move that logic into a plain function outside the component (or use `'use no memo'`).

Possibly related to other bugs in how the compiler handles closures and `_temp` outlining (#34901, #35342, #35386), though those are about locally scoped variables lost when a function is moved out to module scope. Here the variable already is module-scoped.

### How often does this bug happen?

Every time

### What version of React are you using?

19.3.0 (Next.js 16.3.8, `reactCompiler: true`)

### What version of React Compiler are you using?

babel-plugin-react-compiler 1.0.0 (also reproduced on 0.0.0-experimental-a1856f3-20260507 and the current Playground)

title: Bug: TypeError in ReactDOM.prefetchDNS() when called with null or prototype-less options in DEV
body:
React version: 19.1.0-canary (main branch)

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Call `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('<url>', null);` or `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('<url>', Object.create(null));`.
2. Run in development mode (`__DEV__`).

## Link to code example:

```javascript
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom';

// Passing null or Object.create(null) as the second argument:
ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('<url>', null);
```

## The current behavior

In development mode, `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS` checks if extra arguments are provided to warn callers:

```javascript
// packages/react-dom/src/shared/ReactDOMFloat.js
const options = arguments[1];
if (
  typeof options === 'object' &&
  options.hasOwnProperty('crossOrigin')
) {
```

Because `typeof null === 'object'`, passing `null` as the second argument attempts to call `null.hasOwnProperty(...)`, throwing an unhandled exception:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'hasOwnProperty')
  at prefetchDNS (packages/react-dom/src/shared/ReactDOMFloat.js)
```

Similarly, passing `Object.create(null)` throws:
```
TypeError: options.hasOwnProperty is not a function
```

This prevents React from reaching its intended diagnostic warning and crashes the render.

## The expected behavior

`ReactDOM.prefetchDNS` should verify `options != null` and use safe `hasOwnProperty` lookup:

```javascript
if (
  options != null &&
  typeof options === 'object' &&
  hasOwnProperty.call(options, 'crossOrigin')
) {
```

When called with `null`, it should gracefully log:
> ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(): Expected only one argument, `href`, but encountered `null` as a second argument instead. This argument is reserved for future options and is currently disallowed. Try calling ReactDOM.prefetchDNS() with just a single string argument, `href`.

title: Bug: dev-only "two <ViewTransition name> mounted at the same time" warning is a false positive after `name` changes to undefined/another name
[DevTools] Keep unmatched console specifiers literal in single-string formatter
body:
formatConsoleArgumentsToSingleString builds the message key for errors and warnings logged during render, commit and passive effects. Its replace callback always shifted an argument, even when none were left or when the specifier was escaped (%%s). With no argument left, a specifier became 'undefined' or 'NaN', so '%s %s' with one argument gave 'value undefined' and '%d %d' with one argument gave '1 NaN'. An escaped specifier also shifted an argument, coerced it and put it back, so '%%d %s' with 'abc' gave '%d NaN', and '%s %%s' with one argument appended ' undefined'.

Leave a specifier as is when it is escaped or when no argument is left, like the browser console, Node's util.format and the sibling formatConsoleArguments helper (fixed in #36930) already do.

Fixes #37126

title: [DevTools] Normalize BigInt values in facade inspection results
body:
The facade's normalizeValue() is documented to turn props and hook values into a serialization-safe shape, and it does so for undefined, functions, symbols, React elements and objects. BigInt fell through to the final `return val`, so getComponentByUid() returned raw BigInts in props and hook values. JSON.stringify() throws on BigInt, so consumers that serialize the result (such as the CDT MCP integration) failed to inspect any component holding one.

Convert BigInt to its decimal string with an "n" suffix, the same format DevTools uses for BigInt previews elsewhere. A string keeps the full precision (converting to Number would not) and the suffix keeps it distinguishable from a plain number or string. Only the normalized output changes; the application's values are not touched.

Fixes #37602

title: [DevTools] Find non-resource hoistable instances in the facade
body:
getComponentByHostInstance reported React-managed <title>, <meta> and non-resource <link> elements as "not managed by React", even though the same fibers show up in getComponentTree and resolve by uid.

The facade's getHostInstanceForFiber only read a HostHoistable's DOM node from memoizedState.instance, which is where Resources (e.g. <style precedence>, <link rel="stylesheet" precedence>) keep it. Hoistables that aren't Resources have a null memoizedState and keep their instance on stateNode, the same as a HostComponent (see updateHostHoistable and the HostHoistable mutation path in the reconciler), so findByHostInstance could never match them.

Return stateNode when the hoistable has no Resource, and keep reading the Resource's instance otherwise. Add tests for both kinds.

Fixes #37604

title: [DevTools] Keep special characters in Open in Editor paths
body:
## Summary

"Open in editor" inserts a file system path into the editor URL as is, which breaks two kinds of path:

- `#` or `?` ends the URL's path, so the rest of the path and the line number move into the fragment or query.
- `$$` and `$&` are treated as `String.replace` patterns, so `/app/routes/$$.tsx` becomes `/app/routes/$.tsx`.

This encodes `#` and `?` in file system paths and inserts the path with a replacer function. Paths from `file:///` URLs are already encoded and stay unchanged.

## How did you test this change?

title: [Flight] Let Fizz retry lazy chunks that hit a stack overflow while decoding
body:
## Summary

Fizz already recovers from stack overflows in very deep trees: it catches `Maximum call stack size exceeded` and retries the work in a new task with a fresh stack (#30419, #36977). Flight defeated that. When decoding a lazy model (or requiring a lazy module) overflowed during an SSR render, `initializeModelChunk` / `initializeModuleChunk` permanently marked the chunk `ERRORED`, so Fizz's retry just read back the cached error and the render failed.

This change lets those transient overflows be retried:

- `readChunk` (the synchronous lazy read during rendering) initializes with `canRetry = true`. Outlined models initialized inside that read inherit it via a module-level `initializingWithRetry` flag.
- On a stack overflow `RangeError`, a model chunk is reset to `RESOLVED_MODEL` (keeping its serialized model and original `reason`) and the error is rethrown so Fizz can trampoline. This only happens when the overflow came from the parse itself (`!parsed`), the chunk is still `BLOCKED`, and nothing subscribed to it during the parse. Otherwise resetting could drop listeners in cyclic cases, so we fall back to `ERRORED`.
- A module chunk rethrows without changing state, since nothing has changed before `requireModule` throws.
- Eager initialization from stream callbacks still rejects the chunk, since there's no render task to retry it.

If the retry overflows again, Fizz sees no progress and terminates with the error instead of looping.

### Things to watch out for

1. **Debug chunks (DEV only).** `initializeDebugChunk` runs before the `try` in `initializeModelChunk`. It calls `initializeModelChunk(debugChunk)` without an explicit `canRetry`, so it inherits `initializingWithRetry = true`. If a debug chunk overflows, it now resets itself and rethrows past the parent's `try`, leaving the parent `BLOCKED`. Main already has this "throws outside the try" problem when a debug chunk errors (see the existing TODO there), but this adds a new way to reach it. Passing `false` there is likely the right fix.
2. **Engine-specific detection.** The check matches the V8/JSC message `Maximum call stack size exceeded`. Firefox's `InternalError: too much recursion` falls back to the old behavior. This matches how Fizz detects overflows.
3. **Client renders.** `readChunk` also backs lazy initialization on the client (Fiber). There, an overflow now leaves the chunk re-parseable instead of caching the error. Fiber has no trampoline, so a later render just tries again. That should be harmless, but it's a behavior change beyond SSR.
4. **A broad flag.** `initializingWithRetry` is module-level state, so synchronous callbacks that run during a parse could in theory see `true`. I haven't found a concrete way for that to break, but it's broader than strictly needed.

## How did you test this change?

Added tests to `ReactFlightDOMNode-test.js`. They simulate overflows at the `JSON.parse` / `__webpack_require__` boundary so they don't depend on the engine's stack size:

- Lazy model overflow, inline and outlined, with 1 and unlimited overflows. A single overflow renders correctly. Unlimited overflows terminate after one retry. A `SyntaxError` is not retried.
- Lazy client module overflow, with 1 and unlimited overflows.
- Eager decoding errors reject the chunk without throwing from the stream callback.
- Retrying after a partial parse that already registered a listener on a pending reference.
- No retry when a partial parse leaves cyclic listeners on the chunk.

Against main's `ReactFlightClient.js`, 7 of the new tests fail. With this change:

```
yarn test packages/react-server-dom-webpack/src/__tests__/ReactFlightDOMNode-test.js  # 49 passed
yarn test --prod packages/react-server-dom-webpack/src/__tests__/ReactFlightDOMNode-test.js  # 49 passed
yarn flow dom-node  # No errors
yarn linc  # passed
```

title: [compiler] Bail out on calls in switch case tests
[Fiber] Ping a throttled retry when a new render cancels its timeout
body:
When a retry finishes rendering and its commit is throttled, its lanes are marked suspended and the finished work is held behind a timeout. If another render starts before the timeout fires, prepareFreshStack cancels the timeout and throws that work away. The retry's data has already resolved, so nothing pings it again. Its lanes stay suspended until some other work commits. If the render that interrupted it keeps suspending, the retry never runs again.

This is how a transition gets stuck after giving up hydrating a dehydrated boundary (#38029). The same thing happens on the client when an unrelated transition interrupts a throttled retry and then suspends again: the boundary stays on its fallback until that transition's data arrives, or forever if it never does.

Fix this by pinging the throttled lanes when prepareFreshStack cancels the timeout, so the retry renders again once the interrupting render finishes or suspends. This also covers the hydration case, so the earlier fix in #38030 (pingSuspendedRetryLanes in updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent and updateDehydratedActivityComponent) is not needed.

Adds ReactSuspenseThrottledRetry-test.js with two cases: the interrupting transition commits, and it suspends again. The second fails without this change. The two hydration tests from #38030 are kept.

Fixes <url>
Closes <url>

title: Untrack previous ViewTransition name when it changes
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37866.

In DEV, `ReactFiberDuplicateViewTransitions` keeps a module-level `name -> fiber` map. Names are added during the layout commit, but they are only removed on deletion or when an Offscreen tree is hidden. When a mounted `<ViewTransition>` changes `name` from `"a"` to `undefined` or `"b"`, the `"a"` entry is never removed. A later, different `<ViewTransition name="a">` then logs:

> There are two <ViewTransition name="a"> components with the same name mounted at the same time…

This happens even though only one boundary is named `"a"`.

Fix: in `commitLayoutEffectOnFiber` (`case ViewTransitionComponent`), if `current.memoizedProps.name !== finishedWork.memoizedProps.name`, call `untrackNamedViewTransition(current)` before the existing `trackNamedViewTransition(finishedWork)`.

- The fiber is always visited on a name change. `updateViewTransition` sets `Ref` whenever `name` changes, and `Ref` is part of `LayoutMask`.
- `untrackNamedViewTransition(current)` reads the old name. It does nothing for `null`/`undefined`/`"auto"`, and it only deletes the entry if it belongs to `current` or its alternate, so it never clears another boundary's entry.
- Untracking runs before tracking, so a rename `"a" -> "b"` still registers `"b"`, and a real duplicate of the new name still warns.
- Hidden subtrees are unaffected: hide already untracks and reappear re-tracks the current name.

Known limitation (unchanged by this PR): if, in the same commit, one boundary renames away from `"a"` and a boundary *earlier in tree order* mounts with `"a"`, the earlier one is checked first and still warns. Fixing that would need an extra pass before layout.

## How did you test this change?

I added two tests to `ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js`:
- `does not warn about duplicate names after a ViewTransition drops its name`
- `tracks the new name when a ViewTransition is renamed`. The old name is free again, and a real duplicate of the new name still logs the expected warning.

Both tests failed before the fix with an unexpected `There are two <ViewTransition name="shared">` console error, and pass after it.

```

yarn test -r=stable packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js  # 31 passed
yarn test --prod packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js  # 31 passed
yarn test ViewTransition  # 3 suites, 43 passed

prettier --check / eslint on changed files  # clean
```

title: [Fizz] Preserve the external runtime configuration when resuming
body:
## Summary

Resuming a prerender with an empty HTML shell can emit external-runtime instructions without loading the runtime that processes them. The postponed state preserves the data streaming format, but the runtime URL and integrity metadata were only kept in the original render state. This leaves completed Suspense content hidden when no shell was flushed before postponing.

Preserve the external runtime configuration in resumable state and restore it when creating the resumed render state. Existing resource deduplication prevents emitting the runtime again when it was already included in the shell.

title: Bump undici from 5.28.4 to 6.29.1
body:
Bumps [undici]() from 5.28.4 to 6.29.1.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

title: Safely access form reset and method when shadowed by named inputs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #38043

In the HTML DOM, form controls with `name` attributes shadow built-in properties on `HTMLFormElement`. When a form contains elements named `reset` or `method`:
1. Calling `form.reset()` in `resetFormInstance` invokes the `HTMLInputElement` instead of the native method, throwing `TypeError: form.reset is not a function`.
2. Accessing `form.method` in `FormActionEventPlugin` returns the `HTMLInputElement` instead of a string, corrupting `useFormStatus().method` and causing a crash when rendered into JSX (`Objects are not valid as a React child`).

This change:
- Uses `HTMLFormElement.prototype.reset.call(form)` in `resetFormInstance` to guarantee safe reset invocation.
- Adds `getFormMethod(form)` in `FormActionEventPlugin` that safely reads `form.method` when it's a string, or falls back to `form.getAttribute('method') || 'get'`.

## How did you test this change?

Added a unit test in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMForm-test.js` asserting that forms with input elements named `reset` and `method` submit, reset, and update `useFormStatus()` without throwing.

title: Add mathDepth and shapeImageThreshold to unitlessNumbers
body:
## Summary

Fixes #38042

Per CSS Shapes Module Level 1 and MathML Core specifications, `shapeImageThreshold` and `mathDepth` only accept unitless numbers.

Previously, because they were not included in `unitlessNumbers`, React erroneously appended `'px'` to numeric values (e.g. `shape-image-threshold: 0.5px; math-depth: 1px;`), causing browsers to reject them as invalid CSS.

This change adds both `mathDepth` and `shapeImageThreshold` to the `unitlessNumbers` set in `packages/react-dom-bindings/src/shared/isUnitlessNumber.js`.

## How did you test this change?

Updated `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/CSSPropertyOperations-test.js` to verify that `mathDepth: 1` and `shapeImageThreshold: 0.5` render without `px` suffix:
`expect(html).toContain('"flex:0;opacity:0.5;math-depth:1;shape-image-threshold:0.5"')`

title: [Flight] Convert Windows file paths to file:// URLs in fake stack frames
body:
## Summary

The Flight client only turns server filenames that start with `/` into `file://` URLs when it builds fake stack frames. On a Windows server, V8 reports paths like `C:\code\App.js`, so they skipped that branch and showed up as `C:%5Ccode%5CApp.js` instead of a file URL. This adds a drive-letter check that produces `file:///C:/code/App.js`, in both `ReactFlightClient` and `ReactFlightReplyClient`.

Fixes #38039

## How did you test this change?

Added a Windows frame to the "should handle exotic stack frames" test in `ReactFlight-test.js`. It fails on main with `C:%5Ccode%5CApp.js` and passes with the fix. Also ran `yarn test packages/react-client`, `yarn test --prod packages/react-client`, `yarn linc` and `yarn flow dom-node`.

title: [Fiber] Don't reset work stack when updating a different root with a pending commit
body:
## Summary

`scheduleUpdateOnFiber` called `prepareFreshStack(root)` whenever `root.cancelPendingCommit !== null`, without checking that `root` is the root currently rendering. If the update is scheduled during a *different* root's render (e.g. a synchronous `useSyncExternalStore` notification), `resetWorkInProgressStack()` unwinds the rendering root's work stack. That pops its context providers and host context, producing `Unexpected pop` / `Expected host context to exist`, a recoverable error (#520 in prod), and corrupted context defaults (`null` instead of the default) in later, unrelated roots.

## Fix

When the update targets a root other than the one currently rendering (during render phase), only cancel that root's pending commit and let the update schedule normally, leaving the active work stack untouched. Other cases are unchanged.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test in `ReactSuspenseyCommitPhase-test.js`: root A has a suspended commit, root B synchronously notifies A's store during render, root C reads a context default. Fails before the fix (`Expected host context to exist`, `Unexpected pop`), passes after.
- The test is gated on `enableSuspenseyImages`; run with `yarn test -r=www-modern --variant=true packages/react-reconciler/src/__tests__/ReactSuspenseyCommitPhase-test.js`.
- `packages/react-reconciler` and `ReactDOMFloat-test.js` pass in default, `www-modern --variant=true`, and stable. Flow, lint and prettier pass.

Fixes #38040

title: [React] Restore actQueue when act callback throws or rejects
body:
## Summary

When the callback passed to `act` throws synchronously or by promise rejection, `popActScope` only unwinds `actScopeDepth` and does not restore `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue = prevActQueue`. As a result, `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue` continues pointing to the abandoned queue, causing subsequent state updates outside `act` to be pushed to the orphaned queue without flushing or rendering.

This change:
1. Restores `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue = prevActQueue` inside `popActScope` so both synchronous throws and asynchronous rejections unwind the active act queue.
2. In the synchronous return path, calls `popActScope` after `flushActQueue` so the queue remains active while flushing synchronous work before unwinding the scope.
3. In the asynchronous resolution path, maintains `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue = queue` while flushing work before clearing `actQueue` when the queue drains.
4. Resets `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue = null` if async flush or recursive work encounters errors before rejection.

Fixes #38031

[DOM] Guard against form control name-clobbering in resetFormInstance and useFormStatus
body:
## Summary
In HTML DOM forms, form controls named `"reset"` or `"method"` shadow properties on the `HTMLFormElement` instance:

1. In `resetFormInstance`, calling `form.reset()` throws `TypeError: form.reset is not a function` if `<input name="reset" />` exists. Calling `HTMLFormElement.prototype.reset.call(form)` ensures the form can always be reset safely.
2. In `FormActionEventPlugin`, reading `form.method` directly returns the `HTMLInputElement` if a field is named `"method"` (e.g. `<input type="hidden" name="method" value="DELETE" />`). This breaks `useFormStatus().method` and throws when rendered into JSX. Safely reading `form.getAttribute('method')` ensures `method` is normalized to `'get'`, `'post'`, or `'dialog'`.

## How did you test this change?
- Ran `yarn test ReactDOMForm` (all 47 passed)
- Ran `yarn prettier`

title: [DOM] Add shapeImageThreshold and missing CSS properties to isUnitlessNumber
body:
## Summary
Several CSS specifications define properties that accept unitless numbers:
- `shapeImageThreshold` (CSS Shapes Module Level 1) only accepts a `<number>` between 0.0 and 1.0. Appending `px` generates invalid CSS syntax (`0.5px`) that browsers reject and discard.
- `mathDepth` (MathML Core / CSS Math) accepts unitless integers.
- `maskBorderOutset`, `maskBorderSlice`, and `maskBorderWidth` (CSS Masking Module Level 1) accept unitless numbers, mirroring the existing `borderImage*` properties.

This PR adds these properties (and WebKit aliases) to `isUnitlessNumber.js` and adds assertions in `CSSPropertyOperations-test.js`.

## How did you test this change?
- Ran `yarn test CSSPropertyOperations`
- Ran `yarn prettier`

title: [DOM] Use SyntheticUIEvent for onResize
body:
## Summary
Per the W3C UI Events specification, `resize` is an instance of `UIEvent` (implementing `UIEventInterface` with `view` and `detail`).

While `onResize` is registered as a simple event in `DOMEventProperties.js`, it was omitted from the switch statement in `SimpleEventPlugin.js`. As a result, it fell back to base `SyntheticEvent`, leaving `event.view` and `event.detail` un-normalized (`undefined`).

This PR:
1. Adds `case 'resize':` in `SimpleEventPlugin.js` so it instantiates `SyntheticUIEvent`.
2. Adds a test suite `SyntheticUIEvent-test.js` covering `onResize`, `onScroll`, and `onScrollEnd`.

- Ran `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier`
