[Fiber] Restore the previous act queue when an act scope throws
body:
[Fiber] Restore the previous act queue when an act scope throws

## Summary

`act` installs `ReactSharedInternals.actQueue` when it enters a scope and
only clears it on the success paths, after flushing. Both error paths call
`popActScope`, which restores `actScopeDepth` but not the queue, so a scope
whose callback throws or rejects leaves its queue installed.

From then on every update scheduled outside of `act` is pushed onto that
abandoned queue: `scheduleCallback` takes the `actQueue` branch and never
notifies Scheduler, so the work is queued but never flushed, and the update
never renders. The next successful `act` call is what eventually drains it.

This is reachable in tests that assert on an expected error and then wait
for an update outside of `act` — for example Testing Library's `waitFor`,
which leaves the act environment while it polls. Those tests time out.

The fix restores the queue the scope found, on both error paths.
`prevActQueue` is the enclosing scope's queue for a nested `act`, so nesting
keeps working; it is `null` for the outermost scope, which is the case that
leaks today. The success paths are deliberately untouched: they keep the
queue installed until they have flushed it, because
`recursivelyFlushAsyncActWork` reads it to keep draining work that was
scheduled in a microtask.

Fixes #38031

## How did you test this change?

Added three cases to `ReactIsomorphicAct-test`: a throwing sync callback, a
rejecting async callback, and a nested `act` that throws inside an outer
one. The first two fail without the fix — the update scheduled after the
throwing scope never reaches Scheduler, so the log is empty — and pass with
it. The nested case covers the scope the fix must not tear down.

ReactIsomorphicAct, ReactTestRendererAct, ReactTestUtilsAct and
ReactNoopRendererAct also pass in experimental dev, plus ReactIsomorphicAct
in prod and in the stable channel, together with ReactTestUtils,
ReactErrorBoundaries, ReactDOMFiber, ReactCompositeComponent, ReactHooks,
ReactTransition, ReactStrictMode and ReactSuspenseWithNoopRenderer. flow,
linc and prettier are clean.

title: [Fiber] Ping throttled hydration retries when a transition gives up hydrating
body:
Fixes #38029

## Summary

A transition can get stuck forever when it updates a server-rendered Suspense or Activity boundary that hasn't hydrated yet.

The transition can't finish until that boundary hydrates, so it waits. When the boundary's data arrives, React hydrates it in a retry, but holds the retry's commit back for a moment (the normal retry throttle). If the transition wakes up during that moment, React drops the held-back retry and renders the transition instead. The transition still can't finish, so it waits again. Nothing ever schedules the retry again, so neither one commits.

With this change, when a render gives up on hydrating a boundary, it wakes up any of that boundary's retries that are stuck waiting. The retry runs again and commits, and then the transition can finish. If there's no stuck retry, nothing changes.

Another option is to change `resolveRetryWakeable` so the retry never gets throttled in the first place. That also fixes the test, but it only closes one of the ways to get into this state.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a test for Suspense and one for Activity. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. They don't use `act`, because `act` turns off the retry throttle.
- Ran the new tests in stable, experimental, and www-modern.
- The hydration, Suspense, and Activity test suites pass.
- `yarn linc` and `yarn flow dom-node` pass.

title: [compiler] Evaluate the target of compound assignments and updates once
body:
## Summary

React Compiler evaluates the target of a compound assignment or update twice when it has side effects:

```js
getObj()[getKey()] += 1;
// compiles to
getObj()[getKey()] = getObj()[getKey()] + 1;
```

BuildHIR uses the object and computed property temporaries for both the load and the store, and codegen emits the expression of an unnamed temporary at each use, so calls in the object or key position run twice and the store can hit a different key than the load. `++`/`--` on members have the same problem.

This stores those operands in promoted temporaries first (`const t0 = getObj(); const t1 = getKey(); t0[t1] = t0[t1] + 1;`). Identifiers, literals and property loads of those are left as before, so no existing fixture output changes. The Rust port gets the same change so both compilers keep producing the same HIR. This is separate from #35205 (postfix member updates), which is unchanged.

## How did you test this change?

Added `compound-assignment-member-side-effects.js`. Without the change, sprout reports:

```
Found differences in evaluator results
Non-forget (expected):
(kind: ok) [{"a":8,"b":10,"nested":{"a":1,"b":0}},10,["getObj","getKey","getObj","getKey","getObj","getKey","getObj","getKey"]]
Forget:
(kind: ok) [{"a":9,"b":10,"nested":{"a":0,"b":0,"undefined":null},"undefined":null},null,["getObj","getObj","getKey","getKey", ...]]
```

With the change:
- `yarn snap -p compound-assignment-member-side-effects.js` and `yarn snap --rust -p ...` pass (the Rust run fails the same way without the Rust change)
- full `yarn snap` and `yarn snap --rust`: same results as main apart from the new fixture (run on Windows, where some unrelated fixtures also fail on main)
- `scripts/test-rust-port.ts PruneHoistedContexts` on the 110 fixtures with compound assignments or update expressions: 110/110 match
- `cargo check --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`, eslint and `tsc --noEmit` for the compiler package

I used Claude Code to write this change.

title: [rust-compiler] Expose typed ErrorCategory and ErrorSeverity on CompilerErrorDetailInfo
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #36173. In that PR's discussion, Biome's maintainer ([comment](<url>)) pointed out that the Rust compiler emits errors as strings, so integrations have to classify diagnostics by string comparison, and asked that `CompilerErrorDetailInfo`'s `category` expose `ErrorCategory` instead of rendering a string first (and that the enum get docstrings). This PR does that first step.

**Before:** `CompilerErrorDetailInfo.category` and `.severity` were `String`s, built with `format!("{:?}", d.category)` / `format!("{:?}", d.severity())` at five construction sites in `program.rs` and `pipeline.rs`. In-process consumers of `CompileResult` (the oxc and swc frontends, Biome, oxlint) only ever saw `"Hooks"`, `"EffectDependencies"`, `"Warning"`, etc.

**After:** the two fields are `ErrorCategory` and `ErrorSeverity` from `react_compiler_diagnostics`, and the `format!` calls are gone. Consumers can `match` on the enums, and `ErrorCategory::severity()` / `logged_severity()` are available on the value they already hold.

**Wire format is unchanged.** Both enums already derive `serde::Serialize` with no `rename` attributes, so a unit variant serializes to its name, which is exactly what `format!("{:?}", ..)` produced and exactly the string value the TS `ErrorCategory` / `ErrorSeverity` enums carry (`Hooks = 'Hooks'`). The napi bridge, the JS shim, and logger events see identical JSON. A new unit test iterates all 26 categories and asserts the serialized `category` and `severity` equal their `Debug` names, so a future `#[serde(rename_all)]` can't silently change the logger contract.

Also ported the TS doc comments from `CompilerError.ts` onto the Rust `ErrorCategory` and `ErrorSeverity` variants.

**Compatibility:** no change for Babel/napi users. For Rust crate consumers this is a type change on two public fields of a `0.0.1` pre-release struct; code that compared `detail.category == "Hooks"` becomes `detail.category == ErrorCategory::Hooks` (or `format!("{:?}", detail.category)` to keep the string).

**Not in this PR:** typing `reason` (free-form text in the TS compiler as well) and `CompilerErrorItemInfo.kind` (`"error"` / `"hint"`). Both would be natural follow-ups if this direction is welcome.

## How did you test this change?

Everything `compiler_rust.yml` runs, locally on macOS arm64 (rustc 1.99.1, Node 22.22.0, yarn 1.22.22):

```
cd compiler
cargo fmt --all -- --check  # clean
cargo check && cargo build  # ok
cargo test --workspace  # all green, includes the 2 new tests in compile_result.rs
bash scripts/test-babel-ast.sh  # 1822/1822 round-trip, 1823/1823 scope info, 1808/1808 scope rename
bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh  # 1842 passed, 0 failed (events + code), all 22 per-pass comparisons clean
yarn workspace snap run build && yarn snap --rust  # 1843 Tests, 1843 Passed, 0 Failed
```

`scripts/test-rust-port.sh` runs every fixture through both the TS and the Rust Babel plugins and diffs the logger events (including each `CompileError` detail's `category` and `severity`) and the generated code, so it directly checks that the serialized shape did not move.

No `.expect.md` fixtures changed.

title: Preserve painted SSR fallback DOM when hydration re-suspends on recoverable boundary
body:
## Preserve painted SSR fallback DOM when hydration re-suspends on recoverable boundary

Fixes #37620

### Root Cause

When a Suspense boundary outputs a recoverable fallback on the server (e.g. when a component requests browser-only rendering via `ReactDOM.browser()` and Fizz bails out on that boundary with `REACT_RECOVERABLE_DIGEST`), the server fallback DOM is painted and visible to the user.

If the component then suspends **again** on the client (e.g. on a client-only promise such as a `setTimeout` promise, `localStorage`, or IndexedDB query):
1. In the first pass of hydration retry (`retrySuspenseComponentWithoutHydrating`), React queues the server-painted `DehydratedFragment` fallback fiber for deletion, clears `memoizedState`, and begins rendering primary children.
2. When the primary children suspend on the client promise, React re-enters the boundary in the second pass (`updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent` with `didSuspend = true`).
3. Previously, React fell through to `mountSuspenseFallbackAfterRetryWithoutHydrating`, which deleted the already-painted server fallback and mounted a fresh client-rendered fallback.

Deleting and remounting an identical fallback resets DOM state and restarts CSS-driven spinner/progress animations (the reported issue in #37620). Furthermore, in some update orderings, returning from `bailoutOffscreenComponent` can hand the raw `DehydratedFragment` (unit of work tag 18) directly back to the work loop, crashing with `Unknown unit of work tag (18)`.

### Fix

When restarting on a recoverable fallback (`isSuspenseInstanceFallback(suspenseInstance) && getSuspenseInstanceFallbackErrorDetails(suspenseInstance).digest === REACT_RECOVERABLE_DIGEST`):
1. **`updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent` (restart path):** Un-queue the deletion of `DehydratedFragment`, mount the primary children into a hidden Offscreen fiber (`mode: 'hidden'`), re-attach the preserved dehydrated fragment as the boundary's fallback sibling, set `SUSPENDED_MARKER`, initialize the `OffscreenInstance`, and return `null` so the raw fragment is never begun by the work loop.
2. **`updateSuspenseFallbackChildren`:** When current fallback child is the preserved `DehydratedFragment`, reattach it as-is without cloning, and undo the primary pass's queued deletion (clearing `ChildDeletion` if empty).
3. **`updateSuspenseComponent` (showFallback tail):** If `primaryChildFragment.sibling` is the preserved `DehydratedFragment`, return `null` instead of calling `bailoutOffscreenComponent`, preventing tag 18 from being surfaced as a unit of work.

When the client promise resolves, standard Suspense retry scheduling swaps the primary content in and tears down the preserved fallback DOM normally.

### Test Plan

- `ReactDOMFizzServer-test`: regression tests pass
  - `keeps the fallback DOM when hydration suspends again on a client promise` (asserts fallback DOM identity and state retention)
  - `keeps the fallback DOM across sequential client suspensions`
  - `can opt a component into browser-only rendering after streaming the fallback`
- Suspense reconciler suites all pass (100%):
  - `ReactSuspenseFallback-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactSuspense-test.internal.js`: PASS
  - `ReactSuspenseList-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactSuspenseCallback-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactCPUSuspense-test.js`: PASS
  - `ActivityLegacySuspense-test.js`: PASS
  - `ActivitySuspense-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactSuspenseEffectsSemantics-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactSuspenseWithNoopRenderer-test.js`: PASS
  - `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration-test.internal.js`: PASS (67/67)

title: [rust-compiler] Fix non-ASCII panic in is_ref_like_name
body:
## Summary

`is_ref_like_name` checked the first character with `object_name[..1]`, which slices one byte. When a `*Ref` name starts with a multi-byte character like `한글Ref`, that byte cuts into the character and the compiler panics on `.current` access. Reading the first char with `.chars().next()` fixes it, and those names now return `false` like the TS regex does.

Fixes #38023

## How did you test this change?

Added `repro-ref-like-name-non-ascii.js`. It panicked before this change and compiles cleanly after:

```
bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh InferTypes packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/repro-ref-like-name-non-ascii.js
```

`yarn snap` (1844 passed), `yarn snap --rust` (1844 passed), `scripts/test-rust-port.sh` (1843 passed) and `cargo fmt --check` are all green locally.

title: [compiler] Skip memoization passes in lint mode for functions without manual memoization
body:
## Summary

Addresses part of #35395 (`eslint-plugin-react-hooks` rules dominating lint time).

When `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` runs the compiler, it uses `outputMode: 'lint'`, and lint mode never uses the compiled output: `processFn` in `Program.ts` returns `null` for lint mode right after compiling. Even so, `runWithEnvironment` runs every function through the whole pipeline. That includes reactive scope inference, about 15 `prune*`/`align*`/`merge*` passes, `renameVariables` and `codegenFunction`.

This PR adds an `enableLintFastPath` environment option. It is off by default and the ESLint plugin turns it on. With it enabled in lint mode, a function **without manual memoization** returns right after the last HIR validation (`ValidateStaticComponents`). Functions that use `useMemo`/`useCallback` still run the full pipeline.

On the DevTools and compiler playground sources, **total ESLint time goes down by 11–31%**, and **the time spent in the compiler-based rules goes down by 14–40%**. The reported lint messages are identical. Benchmarks are below.

### How I found where the time goes

1. **Reproduced what the plugin does.** I wrote a harness that does exactly what `RunReactCompiler.ts` does per file: parse with Hermes or Babel, then call `transformFromAstSync` with the compiler in lint mode and the plugin's environment config. I ran it on `packages/react-devtools-shared/src` (243 files, 52k lines).
2. **Ruled out the obvious Babel overhead.** I tried `code: false` (skip Babel's generator) and `cloneInputAst: false`. Neither gave a measurable win.
3. **Timed each pass.** I timed passes through `logger.debugLogIRs`, which fires after every pass. The passes after the last validation added up to about 30% of the compiler's pass time: `PropagateScopeDependenciesHIR`, `BuildReactiveScopeTerminalsHIR`, `PromoteUsedTemporaries`, `RenameVariables`, `Codegen`, etc.
4. **Checked which of those passes can report anything lint shows.** Codegen and the reactive-scope passes only record `Todo` or `Invariant` errors. The rules for those categories are `LintRulePreset.Off`. The single exception is `ValidatePreservedManualMemoization` (`PreserveManualMemo`, which is in the recommended preset). Every error it records requires a manual memo block: they are all under `state.manualMemoState != null`, which is only set by `StartMemoize`/`FinishMemoize` instructions. `DropManualMemoization` inserts those instructions only for `useMemo`/`useCallback` calls in the function's own body.

So for a function with no `StartMemoize` instruction, everything after `ValidateStaticComponents` is work whose result lint mode throws away.

### The change

- **`Environment.ts`:** new `enableLintFastPath` config. It defaults to `false`, so tools that run in lint mode and rely on `CompileSuccess` or late-pass errors keep their current behavior. `react-compiler-healthcheck` (`noEmit`) is one such tool.
- **`Pipeline.ts`:** after `ValidateStaticComponents`, if the mode is lint, the option is on and there are no manual memo markers, return the recorded errors or `Ok(null)`. `runWithEnvironment`/`compileFn` now return `CodegenFunction | null`, and `null` is only possible with the option on.
- **`Program.ts`:** `processFn` treats `null` as "validated, nothing to emit". It does not log `CompileSuccess`, because memo stats aren't computed. The `'use no memo'` `CompileSkip` event is still logged.
- **`eslint-plugin-react-hooks`:** enables `enableLintFastPath`. A user can still pass `environment: {enableLintFastPath: false}` through the rule options.
- **Rust port:** the same change is mirrored in `pipeline.rs`, `program.rs` and `environment_config.rs`, so `yarn snap --rust` and `test-rust-port` stay in sync.

### Behavior differences (with the option on)

- **Recommended rules:** no lint message changes in any of the corpora below or in the compiler fixtures.
- **`Todo`/`Invariant` errors (off by default):** errors that only the skipped passes would raise are no longer reported for functions without manual memoization. In the 1842 compiler fixtures run in lint mode this affected 6 errors, all `Todo`/`Invariant`.
- **Bug fix as a side effect:** for `rules-of-hooks/error.invalid-hook-for.js`, an `Invariant` thrown later in the pipeline (`Unexpected empty block with goto terminal`) currently replaces the two Rules of Hooks errors already recorded for the function, so lint reports nothing useful. With the fast path, those two `Hooks` errors are reported. This is covered by a new fixture.

## How did you test this change?

**New fixtures** (all `@outputMode:"lint" @enableLintFastPath`):
- `lint-fast-path-without-manual-memo`: no `CompileSuccess` is logged (`@expectNothingCompiled`).
- `error.lint-fast-path-without-manual-memo`: validation errors (refs) are still reported.
- `error.lint-fast-path-with-manual-memo`: `PreserveManualMemo` is still reported when `useMemo` is present.
- `error.lint-fast-path-hooks-in-for-loop`: the Hooks errors that are currently hidden behind an invariant.

**Suites:**
- `yarn snap`: 1847/1847 passed.
- `yarn snap --rust`: 1847/1847 passed.
- `compiler/scripts/test-rust-port.sh`: 1846/1846, both log and code parity.
- `cargo check`, `cargo build` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
- `yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-hooks test`: 5088/5088 passed. Typecheck is clean.
- `yarn prettier`, `yarn linc` and `yarn flow dom-node` pass.

**Lint-output equivalence:** I compiled all compiler fixtures and the DevTools sources in lint mode, with the option off and on, and diffed every `CompileError` event (file, category, reason, location). The differences are only the `Todo`/`Invariant` and Hooks cases described above.

**End-to-end ESLint benchmark.** ESLint 7.32 runs `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` bundled from this branch with the `recommended` config. Three configurations are interleaved in one process:
- **before:** `enableLintFastPath: false` on every compiler rule.
- **after:** the default.
- **no compiler rules:** only `rules-of-hooks` and `exhaustive-deps`. It is used to isolate the compiler's share.

The numbers are process CPU time, median over 8–20 rounds, on an Apple Silicon Mac with Node 24. "Manual memo" is how many files call `useMemo`/`useCallback`.

| Corpus | Files | Manual memo | Total ESLint before → after | Compiler rules only | Lint messages |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `react-devtools-shared/src` (Flow) | 243 | 48 files (235 calls) | 1989 → 1739 ms (**−12.6%**) | **−15.4%** | 89 = 89 |
| `react-devtools-shell/src` (Flow) | 49 | 4 files | 344 → 253 ms (**−26.4%**) | **−29.3%** | 12 = 12 |
| playground + flight-parcel (TSX) | 23 | 1 file | 130 → 89 ms (**−31.1%**) | **−40.1%** | 1 = 1 |

As expected, the speedup is larger when fewer components use manual memoization. That matters more as code moves to the compiler and drops `useMemo`/`useCallback`.

This is independent of and complementary to #37976, #37977 and #37980, which speed up the passes themselves. This PR avoids running the passes lint doesn't need. All of them touch `Pipeline.ts`, so whichever lands second may need a small rebase.

title: [compiler] Fix refs false positive on sibling reads after passing obj.prop to a JSX ref
body:
## Summary

Addresses the main case of #34775 and the first repro in #37507.

This is the same fix as #37518 (@rh0kzy) and #37523 (@itamark), both opened on Sep 4 and not yet reviewed. This PR adds three things on top of that fix:

- the same change in the Rust port. Without it, the new fixtures fail under `yarn snap --rust`.
- coverage in eslint-plugin-react-hooks
- two `error.*` fixtures checking that real `.current` reads are still reported

If either of those PRs picks up the Rust side, I'm happy to close this one in their favor.

### Problem

When any property of an object is passed to a JSX `ref` attribute, `react-hooks/refs` (`validateNoRefAccessInRender`) reports every *other* property read on that object as a ref access during render:

```js
function Child(props) {
  return <div ref={props.myRef} className={props.className} />;
  //  ^^^^^^^^^^^  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ both reported
}
```

The same happens with `ref={props.ref}` forwarding and with floating-ui's `ref={refs.setFloating}`. Because of this, components that use these patterns are not compiled.

### Root cause

1. `InferTypes` (with `enableTreatRefLikeIdentifiersAsRefs`) unifies the value passed to a JSX `ref` attribute with `BuiltInUseRefId`. Here that value is the temporary for `props.myRef`.
2. `collectTemporariesSidemap` aliases the lvalue of every non-`.current` `PropertyLoad` to its base object, so the temporary for `props.myRef` gets aliased to `props`.
3. `Env.set` resolves writes through that alias. When the main pass records the temporary as `Ref`, the value lands in `props`'s slot. `props.className` then loads from a `Ref` object, which makes it a `RefValue`, and it is reported when passed to JSX.

### Fix

In `collectTemporariesSidemap`, don't alias a `PropertyLoad` whose lvalue is itself a ref (`isUseRefType`). That temporary already carries its own ref type, so it doesn't need the alias, and dropping the alias stops the write-back onto the object. Non-ref property loads keep the existing aliasing.

The same one-line guard is added to `collect_temporaries_sidemap` in `validate_no_ref_access_in_render.rs`.

### Not fixed by this PR

These cases go through a different path: `Structure` values don't track individual fields. They are left for a follow-up:

- A real ref stored in an object literal, then a sibling read: `const ctx = {inputRef, files}; <input ref={ctx.inputRef} />; ctx.files` (second repro in #37507). #37566 takes a broader approach that scopes the taint to the exact property path and covers this case.
- The `useMemo` object containing a ref from the #34775 thread.

Other reports in the #34775 thread (`cloneElement`, callbacks passed to unknown hooks) are unrelated to this change.

## How did you test this change?

New compiler fixtures:

- `allow-ref-prop-does-not-taint-sibling-props`: `ref={props.myRef}` + `props.className`
- `allow-ref-from-hook-object-does-not-taint-sibling-props`: floating-ui `refs.setReference` / `refs.setFloating`
- `error.invalid-read-props-ref-current`: `{props.ref.current}` must still be reported
- `error.invalid-read-ref-current-via-object-property`: `const obj = {ref}; obj.ref.current` must still be reported

New cases in the `refs` suite of eslint-plugin-react-hooks `ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts`: 2 valid (props sibling, floating-ui) and 1 invalid (`props.ref.current`).

With this change:

- `yarn snap` (compiler/): 1847 tests, 1847 passed. No existing fixture output changed.
- `yarn snap --rust`: 1847 tests, 1847 passed
- `cargo check` and `cargo build`: pass
- `bash scripts/test-babel-ast.sh`: round-trip 1826/1826, scope info 1827/1827, scope resolution 1812/1812
- `bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh`: 1846/1846
- `yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-hooks test`: 4 suites, 5091 tests passed
- prettier on the changed TS/JS files and rustfmt on the changed Rust file: clean

Without this change (sanity check):

- TS and Rust: both `allow-*` fixtures above fail with "Cannot access refs during render". Both `error.*` fixtures produce the same error as with the patch.
- eslint: the 2 new valid cases fail.

I also checked the variants listed in #37507:

- `ref={ctx.a.inputRef}` (nested chain): compiles without errors with this change
- `const r = ctx.inputRef; ref={r}` (via a local): compiles without errors with this change
- object-literal variant: still errors, as noted above

title: Preserve painted SSR Suspense fallback DOM during client re-suspend
body:
## Summary

When a component calls `use(ReactDOM.browser())` and then suspends on a client-created promise during hydration, React can replace the Suspense fallback that was already rendered by the server with a new fallback. This causes CSS animations, such as progress bars, to restart unexpectedly.

This pull request fixes that by hydrating the existing server-rendered fallback while the client-side content is still loading. The fallback keeps its DOM identity and continues to work as a normal React component, including its event handlers, refs, effects, and state updates.

Once the pending promise resolves, React replaces the fallback with the actual content as expected. The change is restricted to the recoverable browser-bailout scenario so ordinary server-error fallback recovery retains its existing behavior.

## What changed?

- Updated Suspense hydration to hydrate the existing server-rendered fallback instead of unnecessarily remounting it.
- Added handling for Fizz fallback metadata during hydration.
- Updated Suspense hydration state and event handling so the fallback remains interactive while the primary content is pending.
- Added regression tests covering DOM identity, interactivity, refs and effects, props and context updates, sibling updates, unmounting, and recovery from mismatching fallback markup.

## Testing

- `ReactDOMFizzServer-test.js`: 186 tests passed; 3 failures were reported in tests marked `GATED, SHOULD FAIL` and identified in the local test report as pre-existing.
- Hydration and server-rendering tests: 54 passed.
- Reconciler Suspense tests: 84 passed.
- Server integration tests: 75 passed.
- ESLint passed for `ReactFiberBeginWork.js` and `ReactDOMFizzServer-test.js`.
- `git diff --check` passed.

Flow validation and a full production build have not been run.

Fixes #37620

title: [build] Use transform plugins instead of deprecated Babel proposal plugins
body:
## Summary

`@babel/plugin-proposal-class-properties` and `@babel/plugin-proposal-object-rest-spread` are deprecated on npm: "This proposal has been merged to the ECMAScript standard and thus this plugin is no longer maintained. Please use @babel/plugin-transform-class-properties instead." ([class-properties](<url>), [object-rest-spread](<url>)). The transform plugins are their maintained successors and accept the same `loose` / `useBuiltIns` options ([docs](<url>), [docs](<url>)).

This switches the root Babel config (used by the Jest preprocessor) and the Rollup build's `babelPlugins` to the transform plugins:

- `babel.config.js`, `scripts/rollup/build.js`: plugin names only, options unchanged.
- `package.json`: drop the two proposal plugins and declare `@babel/plugin-transform-object-rest-spread@^7.25.9`. `@babel/plugin-transform-class-properties` was already a root devDependency (used by `babel.config-ts.js`).

`yarn.lock` does not change: both transform plugins already resolve to 7.25.9 from the existing entries, and the proposal entries remain for other dependents (`@babel/preset-env`, the DevTools packages). The DevTools packages' own Babel config is left as is.

Similar to #34715 for the compiler.

## How did you test this change?

In a `node:20-bookworm` container (yarn 1.22.22), on `main` first and then with this change:

- `yarn install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts`. With the change it reports `success Already up-to-date.`
- `RELEASE_CHANNEL=experimental node ./scripts/rollup/build.js --type=NODE_DEV,NODE_PROD,FB_WWW_DEV,FB_WWW_PROD,RN_OSS_DEV,RN_OSS_PROD,ESM_DEV,ESM_PROD,BUN_DEV,BUN_PROD`, plus `node ./scripts/rollup/build.js react-refresh --type=NODE_DEV,NODE_PROD`. `diff -rq` of the two `build/` outputs, 197 files, reports no differences. (`eslint-plugin-react-hooks` fails to build in this environment with `TS2307: Cannot find module 'babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/Entrypoint'` on `main` as well, so it is not covered.)
- `yarn test --ci packages/react/src/__tests__ packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMComponent-test.js packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactCompositeComponent-test.js packages/react-reconciler/src/__tests__/ReactHooks-test.internal.js`: 674 passed, 1 skipped, the same before and after.
- `yarn test --ci --prod packages/react/src/__tests__`: 392 passed, 1 skipped, the same before and after.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the changed JS files pass.

Found with unstale, a tool I'm building so nobody has to read every changelog to catch changes like this one. Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code) and verified as described above.

title: [DOM] Dedupe modulepreload links that omit the default `as` type
body:
## Summary

`ReactDOM.preloadModule` dedupes against links that are already in the Document by querying for a matching `<link>`. The selector it built always required an `as` attribute:

```js
const preloadSelector = `link[rel="modulepreload"][as="${as}"][href="${href}"]`;
```

But for the default module type we deliberately don't write `as` — `rel="modulepreload"` already implies `script`, so `ReactDOM.preloadModule(href)` emits `<link rel="modulepreload" href="...">` with no `as` attribute (see the existing `preloads scripts as modules` test, where both the server and browser output for `ssr default` / `browser default` omit it).

So the query could never match a link that React itself inserted, nor one the server emitted for the same module. `preloadPropsMap` hides this for repeated calls within the same render, but as soon as the hint already exists in the Document — the server preloaded the module and a client component asks for the same one during hydration, or the bundler put the modulepreload link in the HTML shell — a second, identical `<link rel="modulepreload">` is appended to `<head>`.

The mismatch is also visible in the identity check: an existing link with `as="worker"` *is* found (the selector has an attribute to match), while the same link without `as` is not.

## Fix

For the default type we now accept both spellings of the same preload: a link without `as` (what we and the server emit) and a link that spells out `as="script"` (possible when authored by hand). Explicit `as` types are unchanged, so e.g. an existing `as="worker"` link does not suppress the script preload for the same href.

I kept this as two plain selectors rather than `:is(...)` because jsdom's selector engine (used by many test setups, including this repo's) doesn't handle `:is()` here.

## How did you test this change?

Two tests in `ReactDOMFloat-test.js` (both fail on `main`, pass with the fix):

- `does not add a duplicate link when the module is already preloaded in the Document` — pre-inserts `href="plain"` (no `as`), `href="explicit"` (`as="script"`) and `href="worker"` (`as="worker"`), then calls `preloadModule` for each. Before: a second `plain` link is appended. After: the link list is unchanged, and the `as="worker"` case keeps its own identity.
- `does not add a duplicate link for a module preloaded by the server` — renders `preloadModule('server')` through `renderToPipeableStream`, then hydrates a client component that calls `preloadModule('server')` again. Before: 2 links. After: 1.

Ran:

- `yarn test ReactDOMFloat` (experimental, dev and prod) — pass
- `yarn test -r=stable ReactDOMFloat` — pass
- `yarn test -r=www-modern ReactDOMFloat` — pass
- `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier` — clean

## Notes

- #38009 touches the neighbouring `preload()` function (stylesheet preload vs. inlined `<style>`); the hunks don't overlap, but whoever lands second will need a trivial rebase.
- The scope is client-side dedupe only. The Fizz server keeps its own `moduleScriptResources` bookkeeping, which is keyed by href and unaffected.

title: [Flight] Serialize nested Node.js Buffers as binary
body:
## Summary

A Node.js `Buffer` passed at the root or through a Promise already arrives on the client as a `Uint8Array`, but inside an object or array `resolveModel` called its `toJSON` first, so it arrived as `{type: 'Buffer', data: [...]}` and logged a warning. Now `resolveModel` skips `toJSON` for `ArrayBuffer` views, so a nested `Buffer` reaches the existing `Uint8Array` branch and is sent as binary like everywhere else. The warning added in #36873 can no longer fire, so I removed it.

Fixes #38014

## How did you test this change?

Changed the Buffer test in `ReactFlightDOMNode-test.js` to expect a `Uint8Array` with the same bytes. It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.

- `yarn test packages/react-server packages/react-client packages/react-server-dom-webpack` (only `ReactFlightDOMEdge` "should break up large sync components" fails, and it fails on `main` too)
- `yarn test --prod` and `-r=www-modern` on `ReactFlightDOMNode-test.js`

title: [19.2.x] Record synchronous render-phase pings while suspended with delay
body:
This PR resolves #37830 #37805

## Summary

This is a backport of #36134 to 19.2.x.

When a thenable pings synchronously during the render and the root is already suspended with delay, React drops the ping. After that, `markRootSuspended` marks those lanes as suspended and nothing schedules the root again, so the transition never commits until another update comes. Next.js apps on 19.2 face it on navigations, both issues above have the details.

It's already fixed on main and 19.3.x, so this is just a clean cherry-pick of that commit. dan is still the author and there is no extra change.

## How did you test this change?

First I reverted the work loop change and the two tests failed. Then with the fix:

```

Tests: 88 passed, 88 total
```

title: [compiler] Allow ref access in FinalizationRegistry cleanup callbacks
body:
## Summary

`new FinalizationRegistry(callback)` was not modeled in `HIR/Globals.ts`, so the compiler treated the constructor as an unknown function that may invoke its arguments during render. The cleanup callback only runs after a registered target is collected (GC), so a ref read/write inside it was incorrectly reported:

```js
function useCleanupLogger() {
  const ref = useRef(null);
  return new FinalizationRegistry(() => {
  ref.current = performance.now(); // error: Cannot access refs during render
  });
}
```

`react-hooks/refs` reports *Cannot access refs during render* / *Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render* for this component. Verified against the compiler `dist` built from `main` (`e9df86c`): the positive fixture added here fails with exactly that error before the change and compiles after it.

## Fix

Add `FinalizationRegistry` to `TYPED_GLOBALS` with the same shape as the other retained-callback constructors (`IntersectionObserver` #37764, `ResizeObserver`/`MutationObserver` #37895, `PerformanceObserver`/`ReportingObserver` #37996): the callback is retained rather than invoked by construction, so its positional parameter is `Effect.Freeze` and the instance stays opaque (`Type::Poly`). The Rust port (`crates/react_compiler_hir/src/globals.rs`) is updated in lockstep.

`registry.register(target, heldValue)` is intentionally left as an opaque method call on an opaque value, matching how `observe()` is handled for the observers above.

## Tests

Two new fixtures:

- `allow-ref-access-in-finalization-registry.ts` — a ref write inside the cleanup callback compiles.
- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-finalization-registry.js` — negative case: mutating a `useMemo` value inside the same callback still errors, i.e. freezing the callback does not weaken the frozen-value validation.

Verification:

- Full fixture sweep with the compiler built from this branch: **1845 fixtures, `25 changed / 3 failed`** — identical to the pre-change baseline, so there is no snapshot churn beyond the two new fixtures.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `babel-plugin-react-compiler` passes; prettier passes on the changed files.
- Rust: this environment has no Rust toolchain, so `cargo test -p react_compiler_hir` was **not** run locally. The Rust change is a mechanical port of the TS entry; the `Test babel-plugin-react-compiler-rust` and `Test snap` jobs compare both backends byte-for-byte.

title: [DOM] Treat font-size-adjust, shape-image-threshold, and math-depth as unitless
body:
`font-size-adjust` takes a `` and `shape-image-threshold` takes an `` (` | `). Neither accepts a length, but both are missing from the `isUnitlessNumber` table, so React appends `px` to numeric values: ```jsx
``` is serialized as `font-size-adjust:0.5px` by the server, and the same string is assigned to `element.style` on the client. Browsers treat a length as invalid for these properties and drop the whole declaration, so the style silently never applies. ```jsx // before renderToString(
) // '
' // after // '
' ``` The same applies to `math-depth`, whose grammar is `normal | | auto-add | add()`: ```jsx // before renderToString(
) // '
' ``` Both the client (`CSSPropertyOperations`) and the server (`ReactFizzConfigDOM`) read the same table, so one change fixes both paths and keeps SSR output consistent with what the client would apply. ### Scope Every property currently in the table was checked against its grammar, and the full set of CSS properties whose value is a bare ``/`` was compared against it. These three are the ones that were missing. ### How did you test this change? Added a case to `CSSPropertyOperations-test` that renders `{fontSizeAdjust: 0.5, shapeImageThreshold: 0.5}` and asserts both the SSR string and the client `element.style` values. It fails before the change with `font-size-adjust:0.5px;shape-image-threshold:0.5px` and passes after. Because JSDOM's `CSSStyleDeclaration` does not know `math-depth` and drops it silently, the client half cannot be asserted for that property; a second case asserts the SSR string (`math-depth:2`, previously `math-depth:2px`), and the shared table is what both renderers read. `CSSPropertyOperations`, `ReactDOMServerIntegration`, `ReactServerRendering` and `ReactDOMFizzServer` pass in development and production. `flow check`, eslint and prettier are clean.

title: [compiler] Fix purity false positives for closures not called during render
body:
## Summary

`react-hooks/purity` reports impure calls such as `Date.now()` as "called during render" inside functions that only run from event handlers or timers. It happens in three cases:

1. A handler closure is created inside a `.map()` callback and calls a function that holds the impure call.
2. A closure references a `const` declared after it.
3. A function references itself, for example a `setTimeout(tick, …)` polling loop.

None of these functions runs during render, so there should be no diagnostic.

**Cause:** `AliasingState.mutate()` in `InferMutationAliasingRanges.ts` reported a function's effects whenever the function's node was reached by a mutation, even when the function was never mutated or called:

- Forward edges: a hoisted context variable is mutated at its declaration. The mutation propagated into every closure that captured it, and those closures were treated as called.
- Capture edges: `items.map(cb)` conditionally mutates `cb`. That mutation reached `open`, which `cb` only closes over and never calls.

**Fix:** only report a function's effects when the function itself is the mutation target. Functions reached through a forward edge are skipped. Functions reached through a capture edge are skipped unless the capturing function's own body mutates or calls the captured variable (`functionMayMutate`). That check keeps existing detection working for real indirect calls, such as `indirectSetGlobal` calling `setGlobal()`.

`functionMayMutate` is a heuristic. It looks for a mutate effect on the captured variable in the capturing function's aliasing effects.

Fixes #37761

## How did you test this change?

Added regression tests:

- Compiler fixtures `impure-call-in-unrendered-fn-{map,forward-ref,forward-ref-timer,self-ref}`. They use `@validateNoImpureFunctionsInRender`, because the snapshot runner doesn't enable the rule by default.
- Purity cases in `ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts`: four valid cases for the repros from the issue, and three controls that must still report real render-time `Date.now()` calls (direct, via a helper, and inside `.map()`).

Without the fix, the four valid cases fail (`4 failed, 20 passed`). With the fix they pass.

Commands run and results:

```
cd compiler
yarn snap
# 1847 Tests, 1847 Passed, 0 Failed

yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler run jest
# Tests: 44 passed, 44 total

yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler run tsc --noEmit
# no errors

yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler build
cd ../packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks
yarn jest
# Tests: 5095 passed, 5095 total
```

Prettier and ESLint are clean on the changed compiler source file. Existing error fixtures still pass, including `error.invalid-global-reassignment-indirect` and `error.invalid-impure-functions-in-render`.

title: [DOM] Don't insert a stylesheet preload when the style is already inlined as a hoistable <style>
body:
## Summary

`ReactDOM.preload(href, {as: 'style'})` on the client skips inserting a `<link rel="preload" as="style">` when the document already contains `link[rel="stylesheet"][href="…"]`, but not when the href is already represented by a hoistable `<style precedence href>` resource. This checks the root's `hoistableStyles` map (the same lookup `preinitStyle` does first) and returns early when a `style` resource is registered for that key.

Where it shows up: Next.js `experimental.inlineCss` inlines the stylesheet into the document as `<style data-precedence="next" data-href="…css">`, which hydrates into a `style` resource. A later RSC response (e.g. after a Server Action `redirect()`) serializes the same CSS as `<link rel="stylesheet" href precedence="next">`; Flight auto-emits an `HL` preload hint for it and the client runs `preload(href, 'style')`. The `<link rel="stylesheet">` element dedupes against the `<style>` resource (same `href` key), so the preload is appended and never used; Chrome logs "The resource … was preloaded using link preload but not used within a few seconds". Reported in vercel/next.js#100734; analysis in <url>

## How did you test this change?

- New test in `ReactFlightDOM-test.js` for the Flight scenario: Fizz renders a document with `<style precedence="default" href="foo">`, the client calls `hydrateRoot(document, …)`, then renders a Flight response containing `<link rel="stylesheet" href="foo" precedence="default" />`. Expects the head to still contain only the `<style>`, with no `<link rel="preload">` inserted. Fails on `main` (the preload is inserted), passes with this change.
- `yarn test` and `yarn test --prod` on `ReactFlightDOM-test.js` + `ReactDOMFloat-test.js`: 192 passed, 1 skipped (both).
- `yarn flow dom-node`, `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier` clean.
- End-to-end on the Next.js repro (16.5.0-canary.27, inlineCss + Server Action redirect, headless Chromium): before, 1 `link[rel=preload][as=style]` after the redirect plus the console warning; after, 0 preloads, 0 `link[rel=stylesheet]` (the inlined `<style>` stays the only copy) and no warning. First load and reload unchanged.

The change was written with AI assistance (Claude Code); I did the investigation, repro and verification above.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](<url>)

title: Hydrate browser-only Suspense fallbacks after client suspension
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37620.

When a component calls `use(browser())` and then suspends on client data, hydration currently replaces the server-rendered fallback with an identical client fallback. This restarts animations and loses DOM continuity.

Hydrate the existing fallback after the primary client attempt suspends, provided the boundary's props and context have not changed. This preserves its DOM while attaching refs, effects, and event handlers. Once hydrated, it behaves like an ordinary mounted Suspense fallback and can receive updates while primary content remains pending.

The existing dehydrated state remains in place during fallback hydration, allowing suspension and mismatch recovery to stay within the boundary. Successful completion converts it to the ordinary suspended state, schedules retries, retires Fizz's bailout metadata, and unblocks event replay. This includes stylesheets that suspend rendering or delay commit. No persistent state fields or flags are added, and the fix does not delay the entire root's commit.

This path is restricted to the intentional recoverable digest used by `browser()`. Ordinary server errors retain their existing recovery behavior. Changed props/context and fallback hydration mismatches use a local client fallback instead of retaining stale server attributes.

Related work: #37641 also explores hydrating fallbacks. This implementation detects fallback hydration through the existing dehydrated state and branch layout, without adding a persistent Suspense state field or per-attempt failed-boundary bookkeeping. The historical root-commit delay approach in #24236, reverted by #24434, is not restored.

## How did you test this change?

- Reproduced the issue on `main` (`a6b912fbe77f698ad43c922f206db0d4f4ad7485`): the existing browser-only test fails when strengthened to assert DOM identity.
- Full `ReactDOMFizzServer-test` development coverage: **195/195 tests and 2/2 snapshots passed** in seven fresh name-filtered processes. The batches were audited for missing/duplicate tests and unchanged source hashes. A single process exceeded the local machine's memory budget; batches used Node 20.19.0, a 768 MB heap cap, `--runInBand`, and `--testTimeout 30000`.
- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzServer-test --runInBand --prod --testNamePattern browser-only --testTimeout 30000`: **15 passed**.
- The same 15 tests passed with `--releaseChannel www-modern` and `--releaseChannel www-classic`.
- Regression coverage includes DOM identity and removal mutations, interactive fallback hydration, refs and effect cleanup, props/context updates before and after hydration, unrelated sibling updates, unmount before promise resolution, local mismatch recovery, fallback suspension, nested Suspense with actual client `useId` values, immediate primary completion, and event replay during stylesheet-delayed commit.
- Negative control: reverting only the tree-reflection change causes the delayed-commit event test to fail with zero handler calls instead of one.
- ESLint, Prettier, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Focused Flow validation for the test renderer, including the no-hydration path: **0 errors**. The focused dom-node check is **not clean**: it reports 567 errors, with the first 50 displayed in installed `react-native-web` dependencies. The rest were truncated, so this does not establish that the changed DOM code is type-clean.

No full-repository build/test run or standalone Next.js/browser end-to-end run was performed.

title: [RN] Call dispatchNativeEvent when the event target is null
body:
## Summary

With `enableNativeEventTargetEventDispatching` on, the Fabric renderer skipped `dispatchNativeEvent` when the touched view had already unmounted, so the touch end never reached the JS responder and the next tap got lost. This passes the null target through instead, so React Native can still release the responder. It needs react/react-native#59522 to land first, since `dispatchNativeEvent` there throws on a null target today.

Fixes #38006

## How did you test this change?

Added a test in `ReactFabric-test.internal.js` that unmounts a view, dispatches a touch end to its old instance handle, and expects `dispatchNativeEvent` to get a null target. It fails on main and passes with this change. Also ran `yarn test packages/react-native-renderer` (default, `--prod`, www-modern), `yarn flow fabric`, `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier-check`.

title: Preserve painted SSR Suspense fallback DOM on client re-suspend (Fixes #37620)
body:
Fixes #37620

## Summary
Preserves the painted SSR Suspense fallback DOM nodes when client hydration suspends again on a client-created promise (e.g. `use(browser())` followed by Web APIs like `localStorage`, `IndexedDB`, or client timers).

## Background
On full page load with React 19 / Fizz, when a component triggers a recoverable browser bailout, Fizz flushes the painted `<Suspense>` fallback into HTML.
During client hydration, when the component re-suspends on a client-only promise, React previously entered `mountSuspenseFallbackAfterRetryWithoutHydrating`, deleting the server-rendered fallback and mounting an identical client fallback. This drops existing DOM state and abruptly restarts CSS animations (such as progress bars and skeleton loaders).

## Solution
1. **Preserve `DehydratedFragment`**:
  - In `updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent`, when a boundary has a recoverable digest (`REACT_RECOVERABLE_DIGEST`) and a valid `DehydratedFragment`, remove the fragment from `workInProgress.deletions` instead of queuing it for deletion.
  - Wire the preserved `DehydratedFragment` as the sibling of the hidden offscreen primary child.
2. **Prevent Redundant Re-render**:
  - In `updateSuspenseFallbackChildren` and `updateSuspenseComponent`, handle `fallbackChildFragment.tag === DehydratedFragment` so the live DOM is left intact without re-invoking or cloning fallback children.
3. **Offscreen State**:
  - Maintain the primary children inside a hidden offscreen fiber until client promises resolve.

## Testing
- Added regression tests to `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzServer-test.js` validating:
  * Fallback DOM nodes (`span`) stay strictly identical across client hydration.
  * Multi-step client promise chains remain on the same painted fallback without remounting.
  * Standard error boundary fallback paths remain unaffected.

title: [Flight] Allow dev tooling to provide a scoped evaluator for debug-only eval
body:
## Summary

In dev, the Flight client uses `eval` to rebuild server stack frames. Runtimes that block `eval`, like workerd, fall back to frames that lose the server file, line and column. Some of these runtimes still offer a dev-only scoped evaluator. For example, the Cloudflare Vite plugin gives each runner worker workerd's `UnsafeEval` binding.

This PR lets tooling install one at `globalThis[Symbol.for('react.debug_eval')]`:

```js
globalThis[Symbol.for('react.debug_eval')] = (code) => env.__VITE_UNSAFE_EVAL__.eval(code);
```

If the hook is set, React's dev-only eval sites and `checkEvalAvailabilityOnceDev` use it instead of global `eval`. There's no change in production or when the hook isn't set.

## How did you test this change?

- New test in `ReactFlight-test.js`: with `eval` disabled and the hook set, error stack frames point to the server source. It fails if the hook is ignored.
- New test in `ReactFlightDOMReplyEdge-test.js`: with the hook set, there's no eval warning.
- `yarn test` and `yarn test --prod` pass on the affected Flight suites. `yarn flow` (dom-node, dom-browser, dom-edge-webpack, custom, noop), `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier` are clean.

title: [compiler] Don't treat use-named constants and properties as hooks
body:
Fixes #29900.

Related: #30493 (same validator, reported through eslint-plugin-react-compiler). I did not reproduce #30493 separately, and this PR does not claim to close it.

## Summary

The compiler decided whether a value is a hook from its name alone in three places, so valid code that maps over a `use*`-named constant or property failed to compile:

- A module-level constant (`const useCases = [...]`) got a hook type from its name, so using it as a method receiver or as a value reported "Hooks may not be referenced as normal values".
- A hook-named property of a module-level object (`thisIsSafeBut.useCases.map(...)`) was treated as a known hook, producing the same error.
- A `PotentialHook` value (for example `props.useItems`, or a local named `useItems`) passed the hook kind to every property, so `props.useItems.map(...)` was reported as a dynamic or conditional hook call.

Changes in `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler`:

- `HIRBuilder.ts` / `HIR.ts`: a module-level binding that is never reassigned and is initialized to a literal, array, or object is marked `isNonHookConstant` (a new optional field on the `ModuleLocal` binding).
- `Environment.ts`: `getGlobalDeclaration` gives such bindings no name-based hook type.
- `ValidateHooksUsage.ts`: such bindings are `Local` rather than `Global`. Property and destructure reads from a `PotentialHook` keep the hook kind only when the property name is hook-like, matching the existing `Local` branch.

The Rust port mirrors the same rules in a second commit (`[rust-compiler]`): `compiler/crates/*` and `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler-rust/src/scope.ts`. The scope info carries `isNonHookConstant`, and the Rust hooks validator applies the same logic, so the `React Compiler (Rust)` job passes. The new fixture's expected input is refreshed to the formatted source that the snapshot runners compare.

What stays the same:

- Real hook calls and module-level hook functions and arrow functions are still validated (conditional and dynamic calls, and hooks passed as values).
- A hook used as a method receiver, such as `useFoo.call(null)` inside a condition, still errors.
- No existing `.expect.md` output changed.

Known gap, unchanged and pinned by existing fixtures: a hook-named property of an undeclared global or unknown import used as a value (`Foo.useCases` where `Foo` is not declared) still reports the error, the same as `Foo.useFoo` in `error.propertyload-hook`.

## How did you test this change?

I reproduced the bug first with fixtures that fail before the fix. The issue's playground code produces the two "referenced as normal values" errors. The new fixtures also fail on valid code before the fix: `props.useItems.map` reports "Hooks must be the same function on every render", and a ternary around it reports "Hooks must always be called in a consistent order". Those same fixtures pass after the fix.

New fixtures (under `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/`): `use-named-module-constant-not-hook`, `use-named-property-not-hook`, `use-named-constant-as-prop-not-hook`, and the guards `error.module-local-hook-as-prop` and `error.module-local-arrow-hook-conditional`.

Commands, all on Linux (Node 20.19.2, yarn 1.22.22):

```
cd compiler && yarn snap  # 1841 tests, 1841 passed, 0 failed
yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler lint  # pass
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler  # pass
yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler jest  # 16 suites, 44 tests passed
./scripts/react-compiler/build-compiler.sh && ./scripts/react-compiler/link-compiler.sh \
  && yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-hooks test  # 4 suites, 5086 tests passed
cd .. && yarn prettier && yarn linc  # pass
yarn flow dom-node  # pass
yarn test ReactHooks  /  yarn test-www ReactHooks  # pass (source and www)

# Rust port (the "React Compiler (Rust)" job, run in CI order)
cargo check && cargo build && cargo fmt --check  # pass
bash compiler/scripts/test-babel-ast.sh  # pass
bash compiler/scripts/test-rust-port.sh  # 1840 passed, 0 failed
yarn workspace snap run build && yarn snap --rust  # 1841 passed, 0 failed
```

Not run: the devtools `compiler-integration` test, which needs a full `yarn test --build`. Its inputs use only `React.useState`, so this change does not reach it.

## Unapplied review findings

- [ ] needs-human: `error.propertyload-hook.js` and `error.hook-property-load-local-hook.js` pin that a hook-named property of an undeclared global or unknown import used as a value is an error. Changing that reverses a deliberate behavior, so it needs a decision. Options: keep the current behavior, or relax value references for such properties and update `error.propertyload-hook`.

title: [DOM] Re-enable events while a View Transition is waiting to start
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37997

When a commit starts a View Transition, the mutation phase is deferred until the browser calls the `startViewTransition` update callback, which can be several frames later. The before-mutation phase has already called `prepareForCommit` by then, which disables the event system. `resetAfterCommit` doesn't run until the mutation phase, so events stay disabled for the whole wait.

Keystrokes in a controlled input during that window never reach `onChange`, so the input loses characters. This happens in the issue's repro, where a `useDeferredValue` list wrapped in `<ViewTransition>` refreshes while someone types.

This PR:

- Calls `resetAfterCommit` after before-mutation when a View Transition is starting. That re-enables events and restores the selection.
- Calls `prepareForCommit` again right before the mutation phase runs.

If an event fires during the wait, `finishEventHandler` calls `flushSyncWork`. That cancels the pending transition and commits the held work, so the keystroke interrupts the animation instead of being dropped. This matches how typing behaves without `<ViewTransition>`.

### Notes for reviewers

- Typing during the start window now cancels the View Transition, so that animation is skipped.
- The existing DEV warning ("A flushSync update cancelled a View Transition…") will also fire in this case. Its wording mentions `flushSync`, which may be misleading when a keystroke triggers it.
- The return value of the second `prepareForCommit` call (`activeInstance`, used with `enableCreateEventHandleAPI`) is ignored. It is only used for before-blur handling, which already ran in the first phase.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test in `ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js`, using a mocked `startViewTransition` that holds `update()`. It fails without the change (`onChange` called 0 times) and passes with it.
- Ran the `react-dom` and `react-reconciler` suites, plus `yarn test --prod` (covering only `react-dom` and `react-reconciler`, not the whole repo), `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier` and `yarn flow dom-node`. `ReactDOMFizzShellHydration` ("recovers from a large component stack during SSR") fails with and without this change.
- Ran the issue's repro in Chrome with Playwright against a production build, with delays of 0–60 ms. Input was lost in 5 of 21 trials without the change and 0 of 21 with it.

title: [compiler] Allow ref access in PerformanceObserver / ReportingObserver callbacks
body:
## Summary

`new PerformanceObserver(cb)` and `new ReportingObserver(cb)` are compiled with a false positive when the callback touches a ref:

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  4 |  return new PerformanceObserver(() => {
  |  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render
```

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it asynchronously once the observation fires — never during render — so reading (or writing) a ref from the callback is safe. `IntersectionObserver` (#37764) and `ResizeObserver` / `MutationObserver` (#37895) are already modelled exactly this way; these two were just missed and fall back to the unknown-constructor default, whose `Freeze` on the callback trips `ValidateNoRefAccessInRender`.

This is the same class of fix as #37895, which is now on `main`.

## Fix

Add both to `TYPED_GLOBALS` (TypeScript) and `build_typed_globals` (Rust) using the same signature shape as the existing observers:

| Global | Constructor signature |
| --- | --- |
| `PerformanceObserver` | `(callback)` → `[Freeze]` |
| `ReportingObserver` | `(callback, options)` → `[Freeze, Read]` |

`ReportingObserver`'s second argument is a genuine constructor argument (unlike the observers whose options belong to `observe()`), so it is read rather than retained.

Both backends are updated so TS and Rust stay in parity.

## Tests

Four new fixtures:

- `allow-ref-access-in-performance-observer.ts`
- `allow-ref-access-in-reporting-observer.ts`

  Both fail before the change with `Cannot access refs during render` and compile to memoized constructors after it.

- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-performance-observer.js`
- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-reporting-observer.js`

  Negative controls proving `Freeze` is not weakened: mutating a `useMemo` value inside the callback still reports `` `entries` cannot be modified ``.

Validation run locally:

- Full fixture suite (1840 fixtures): `25 changed / 3 failed` — identical to the pre-existing baseline (`fbt/*`, `debugger*`), no new diffs.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint src`, `prettier check-changed` all clean.
- Rust side mirrors the TS change 1:1 but was not compiled locally (no toolchain in this environment); relying on the `babel-plugin-react-compiler-rust` CI job.

title: [compiler] Preserve signed zero in constant propagation and code generation
body:
## Summary Fixes #37994 The TypeScript and Rust compilers lose the distinction between `0` and `-0` when merging branch constants and generating code. This can make `1 / value` return the wrong infinity. To reproduce, compile this component and toggle `condition`: ```jsx function Component({condition}) { let value; if (condition) { value = 0; } else { value = -0; } return
{1 / value}
; } ``` The result should alternate between `Infinity` and `-Infinity`, but the compiled component keeps returning `Infinity`. Both backends now preserve signed zero when merging constants and emit negative zero explicitly. NaN merging behavior and JavaScript equality semantics remain unchanged. ## How did you test this change? On macOS arm64 with Rust installed through Homebrew, I first created a Cargo symlink for the path used by `test-babel-ast.sh`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.cargo/bin ln -s /opt/homebrew/opt/rustup/bin/cargo ~/.cargo/bin/cargo ``` I then manually ran these commands from the repository root: ```bash cd compiler yarn install --frozen-lockfile cargo test --workspace --locked yarn snap:build yarn snap yarn snap --rust cd .. bash compiler/scripts/test-babel-ast.sh ``` Rust workspace tests and Babel AST/scope checks passed. All tests in the full compiler snapshot suite passed on both TypeScript and Rust backends. The selected fixtures also passed runtime evaluation on each backend.

title: Fix render-phase state update lost after same-value eager bailout
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37967.

When a state update is eagerly bailed out in `dispatchSetStateInternal` (because the new state matches the currently rendered state), React calls `enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout(fiber, queue, update)`. Previously, that helper passed `lane = NoLane` to `enqueueUpdate`, but left `update.lane` set to its dispatch priority (for example, `SyncLane`).

When a subsequent render pass occurred at a lower priority (such as `DefaultLane` from a parent re-render):
1. `updateReducerImpl` checked `isSubsetOfLanes(renderLanes, update.lane)`. Because `isSubsetOfLanes(DefaultLane, SyncLane)` evaluates to false, React treated the eagerly bailed-out update as a skipped higher-priority update, called `markSkippedUpdateLanes(SyncLane)`, and retained `hook.baseQueue`.
2. If a render-phase update occurred during that lower-priority render pass, `rerenderReducer` skipped updating `hook.baseState` because `hook.baseQueue !== null`.
3. Because `SyncLane` was marked as skipped on the fiber root, React scheduled an immediate follow-up render at `SyncLane`. In that pass, `updateReducerImpl` restarted evaluation from `baseState`, replayed the eager update, and discarded the render-phase update.

This change sets `update.lane = NoLane` inside `enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout`. Bailed-out updates carry no pending render work, so clearing their lane prevents them from bubbling as unrendered work or blocking subsequent render-phase state transitions.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test in `packages/react-reconciler/src/__tests__/ReactHooks-test.internal.js` covering the exact sequence from #37967:
  1. Mount component with `useState(true)`.
  2. Dispatch same-value update `setValue(true)` at sync priority via `root.unstable_flushSync`.
  3. Dispatch lower-priority update via `act` that invokes a render-phase update `setValue(false)`.
  4. Verified that the component renders `'false'` and does not revert to `'true'`.
- Ran the full `ReactHooks-test.internal.js` test suite (73 passing tests).
- Verified code formatting with `yarn prettier`.
- Verified linting on changed files with `yarn linc`.

title: [DOM] Reset forms whose reset method is shadowed by a named control
body:
## Summary

`resetFormInstance` calls `form.reset()` on the form instance. In browsers, a form's controls are exposed as named properties on the form element itself, and `HTMLFormElement` is annotated with `[LegacyOverrideBuiltIns]` ([spec](<url>)), so a control named `reset` shadows the form's own method: `form.reset` is an `Element`, and calling it throws `TypeError: form.reset is not a function`.

React calls this during the commit phase whenever it automatically resets an uncontrolled form after a form action completes (`commitMutationEffects` → `resetFormOnFiber` → `resetFormInstance`), so the throw aborts the rest of the commit rather than just skipping the reset.

```jsx
<form action={action}>
  <input name="reset" defaultValue="Initial" />
</form>
```

This is the same root cause as #37837, but a different call site: the four open PRs there (#37838, #37858, #37877, #37880) only change the Fizz pre-hydration submit listener. A sweep of the renderer for other reads of shadowable `HTMLFormElement` members found no other affected call site (`form.action` is only read by that Fizz listener, and every other form/action read goes through fiber props).

## Fix

Read the method from the prototype instead of the instance. While here, restore the event system in a `finally` block — the event system is deliberately enabled for the duration of `form.reset()` so that `onReset` fires, and a throwing `reset()` previously left it enabled for the rest of the commit.

## Verification

- New test in `ReactDOMForm-test` fails on `main` with `TypeError: form.reset is not a function` at `ReactFiberConfigDOM.js:7000`, passes with the fix. JSDOM does not implement the form named getter, so the test emulates it with `Object.defineProperty` (the same technique used in #37838) and asserts the shadowing is active before resetting.
- `ReactDOMForm-test`, `ReactDOMFizzForm-test`, `ReactDOMInput-test`, `ReactDOMSelect-test`, `ReactDOMTextarea-test`, `ReactDOMServerIntegrationUserInteraction-test` all pass.
- `flow check .`, `linc` and `prettier --check` pass.

title: [Fizz] Preserve postponed state when aborting a stalled replay walk
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37907.

When a prerender aborts while a resumed boundary is stalled above a resumable slot (for example, inside a component performing a replay walk), React previously treated the incomplete replay walk as a tree mismatch or errored the replay task.

Because replay tasks have `task.blockedSegment === null`, `finishAbortedTask` did not track the postponement, causing the boundary to be marked as `CLIENT_RENDERED`, untracked from postpones, and emitted as an error with a null postponed state (`$RX(...)`).

This change:
1. Updates `finishAbortedTask` in `packages/react-server/src/ReactFizzServer.js` to handle replay tasks (`task.replay !== null`) under an aborted prerender by calling `trackPostponeReplay`, aborting pending fallbacks, decrementing pending replay tasks, and finishing the task cleanly.
2. Introduces `postponeNewSuspendedReplayTask` and calls it in `renderNode` when a suspended replay task aborts under a tracked prerender.
3. Guards the tree mismatch assertions ("Couldn't find all resumable slots by key/index during replaying") in `replaySuspenseBoundary`, `replayElement`, `replayFragment`, and `retryReplayTask` when the boundary is postponed or the request has aborted.
4. Adds automated regression tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js` covering both asynchronous and synchronous aborts during stalled replay walks.

## How did you test this change?

Executed Jest in container sandbox matching the regression tests:
```bash
node ./scripts/jest/jest.js --config ./scripts/jest/config.source.js packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js -t "preserves postponed state" --runInBand --watchman=false
```

Output:
```
PASS packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js (44.458 s)
  ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser
  ✓ preserves postponed state when a resumed boundary aborts asynchronously while replay walk is stalled above the resumable slot (30060 ms)
  ✓ preserves postponed state when a resumed boundary aborts synchronously while replay walk is above the resumable slot (5810 ms)
```

Verified ESLint and Prettier pass cleanly:
```bash
./node_modules/.bin/eslint packages/react-server/src/ReactFizzServer.js packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js
./node_modules/.bin/prettier --check packages/react-server/src/ReactFizzServer.js packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js
```

title: [Fiber] Preserve forwardRef props identity during state updates
body:
## Summary

Fixes #35028.

A `forwardRef` component receiving a `ref` currently gets a new ref-free props object on every internal state update. This needlessly invalidates `useMemo([props])` and memoized children receiving the whole props object.

Keep the ref-free copy in a reusable private cache box on each ForwardRef Fiber. Unchanged original input reuses the copy; new parent input gets a new copy. Current and alternate Fibers have separate boxes, preserving committed props during interrupted work. Carry the cache through bailouts and suspended replay, and restore it with hook state during legacy Suspense recovery. Original Fiber props, refs and memo-comparator inputs stay unchanged.

Public instance APIs continue returning null for ForwardRef. The private box also prevents pre-change DevTools backends from interpreting ordinary props such as `context`, `measure` or `setNativeProps` as instance APIs. Cache lifetime follows the component rather than a global WeakMap.

## How did you test this change?

Validated source: `fd4fbaa7ff4e63439bfa11ff54c421478d191787`.

- Nine related source suites: **411 development / 410 production tests passed**, including **79 focused ForwardRef/test-renderer tests**.
- ForwardRef suites: **41 passed** on each of stable and www-modern.
- DevTools inspection: **49 passed**, six skipped, 64 passing snapshots. The compatibility case also passes against the pre-change backend from `38a968f9`; it fails against the earlier unboxed cache.
- Regression coverage includes ref presence/changes, state-only memoization, new parent inputs, Strict Mode, render-phase updates, suspended replay, interrupted transitions, early bailouts, legacy Suspense rollback and instance-field compatibility.
- Flow dom-node, scoped ESLint, Prettier and diff checks passed. Full repository suites were not run.

**Production benchmarks against main** (`c5ec5c6d180ad951048668ed113c443211bc2623`): Apple M1 Pro, 16 GiB RAM, Node v22.16.0, experimental NODE_PROD reconciler with the noop host. Only the reconciler bundle differs between compared runtimes. Completed render counts and output are asserted.

There are 220 timing-process samples and 50 retained-heap samples. Timing uses ten alternating paired fresh-process samples per workload, 128 components per operation. Parent/mount confirmations use 1,600 warmup operations and approximately one-second measured batches; state cases use 800 warmup operations. Values are median paired elapsed-time changes with bootstrap 95% intervals; negative means faster.

| Workload | Time change | 95% interval |
|---|---:|---:|
| State updates, 8 payload fields | -28.4% | -33.2% to -25.0% |
| Fresh parent props, 8 payload fields | +0.7% | -7.7% to +2.0% |
| Fresh parent props, 64 payload fields | -0.6% | -2.8% to +1.6% |
| Mount/unmount churn | -2.2% | -11.5% to +0.2% |
| State updates, omitted ref | +2.7% | -2.0% to +4.6% |
| Fresh parent props, omitted ref | -0.3% | -1.4% to +3.4% |
| State updates with expensive useMemo([props]) | -94.1% | -94.2% to -93.6% |

The confirmed parent/mount intervals span no change. The expensive memo case performs 5,000 integer-arithmetic iterations per calculation; its saving is specific to that synthetic workload.

Mounted cache memory remains a tradeoff: **+1.74 MiB** for 12,000 components with eight payload fields, and **+2.32 MiB** for 4,000 with 64 fields. With the root facade and original elements retained, unmounting the 12,000-component case leaves 8,360 extra bytes (paired range -5,536 to 13,360). Separate root-disposal runs confirm sampled original props are collectable. Heap measurements use five pairs per configuration and forced GC; boxes are reused across ordinary updates.

These are warmed renderer measurements on one host, covering managed retained heap. Browser/layout, cold-start performance, peak RSS and application FPS were not measured.

title: [DevTools] Avoid retaining tree operations before frontend connection
body:
Fixes #37874

## Summary

Before a frontend connects, the Fiber backend currently traverses each commit and retains its serialized operations. A tree that stays the same size can therefore accumulate an unbounded history of operation packets while DevTools is closed.

Keep the renderer attached for console diagnostics, but defer tree tracking until a frontend connects or profiling starts. A normal late connection uses the existing initial-root traversal to send the current tree. Starting profiling before connection first queues a baseline and then preserves the profiling operations, including updates after recording stops that are needed to reach the current tree. Saved filters can be applied before tracking begins.

## Validation

- Added 12 regression cases for late connection, subsequent updates, removed and multiple roots, empty roots, render/passive diagnostics, saved filters, Suspense reveal, and profiling started before connection. The same tests report 8 failures on the base and all 12 passing with this change.
- `yarn test --build --project=devtools --runInBand`: 43 suites pass, 608 tests pass, 25 skipped, 607 snapshots pass, against local experimental React builds.
- `yarn flow dom-browser`, scoped ESLint, and Prettier pass.
- Built the production core backend and compared it with the base in Chrome through `connectWithCustomMessagingProtocol`. After 1,000 keyed React DOM commits, the base sends 1,001 packets, while this change sends one current-tree packet. Render/passive warnings and post-connection updates are preserved. Startup profiling keeps its history. Production React also sends one initial packet after 1,000 commits. Browser runs had no page errors.

Browser validation used the core backend's public messaging API in Chrome; an installed extension and React Native were not exercised.

title: [DOM] Use SyntheticTransitionEvent for onTransitionRun, onTransitionStart, and onTransitionCancel
body:
Fixes #37984

## Summary

When support for CSS transition events (`onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, `onTransitionCancel`) was added in #27345 alongside `onTransitionEnd`, the events were registered as simple events in `DOMEventProperties.js` and defined in `DOMEventNames.js`, but they were not added to the switch statement in `SimpleEventPlugin.js`.

As a result, while `onTransitionEnd` uses `SyntheticTransitionEvent`, `onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, and `onTransitionCancel` were defaulting to base `SyntheticEvent`. Because `SyntheticEvent` does not implement `TransitionEventInterface`, properties such as `propertyName`, `elapsedTime`, and `pseudoElement` were not normalized onto the synthetic event object, evaluating to `undefined`.

This PR:
1. Imports `TRANSITION_CANCEL`, `TRANSITION_RUN`, and `TRANSITION_START` into `SimpleEventPlugin.js`.
2. Adds cases for them in `extractEvents` so they instantiate `SyntheticTransitionEvent`.
3. Adds a regression test suite `SyntheticTransitionEvent-test.js` validating property normalization across all four transition events.

## How did you test this change?

- Added `packages/react-dom/src/events/__tests__/SyntheticTransitionEvent-test.js` covering `onTransitionEnd`, `onTransitionRun`, `onTransitionStart`, and `onTransitionCancel` (fails on `main` with `propertyName: undefined` and passes with this fix).
- Ran `yarn test SyntheticTransitionEvent-test` (passed).
- Ran `yarn test SyntheticAnimationEvent-test ReactDOMEventPropagation-test` (passed).
- Ran `yarn prettier` and `yarn linc` (clean).

title: [Hooks] Preserve render-phase state after eager bailouts
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37967.

An eagerly bailed-out update can remain queued at a priority excluded from a later render. Retaining that unchanged update in the base queue prevents a subsequent render-phase update from becoming the base state, so a follow-up render restores the old value.

When processing a skipped update, omit it from the remaining base queue only if its cached eager result equals the accumulated state, there are no preceding retained updates, and it is not marked as originating in a hidden tree. Preserve the skipped lane on the fiber and root before that check: the pending lane must still block later dispatches from eagerly computing against an unfinished render's `lastRenderedState`.

This leaves the stored update lane unchanged and retains the existing render-phase persistence rules. It can retain the existing extra render pass; it fixes the state loss rather than trying to eliminate that work.

Related: #37971 and the interrupted-render counterexample in <url> This uses queue processing rather than clearing the update's lane.

## How did you test this change?

Added nine cases covering direct/functional/repeated/transition bailouts, deferred update visibility, ordering behind an earlier skipped update, urgent functional updates after interruption, noncommutative update replay, and actual Suspense suspension. The original four loss cases fail without the fix; the safety cases protect the existing ordering and eager-computation behavior.

### Current HEAD verification — 27 October 2026

Freshly tested commit `c416bee81a59bd1d622cc1bae9bcffddb0561ff9` after the upstream merge. All nine added regression cases pass in each configuration:

| Configuration | Passed | Failed |
