| Experimental development | 9 | 0 |
| Experimental production (`--prod`) | 9 | 0 |
| Stable development (`--release-channel=stable`) | 9 | 0 |
| www-modern development (`--release-channel=www-modern`) | 9 | 0 |

These focused runs selected the nine added cases; the other 97 tests in the file were not run. This includes the exact interrupted-render regression reproduced on #37992: urgent output remains `false`, and the deferred update subsequently commits `true`. It also covers the four original loss variants, a later eager update behind an earlier skipped update, urgent functional updates after interruption, noncommutative replay ordering, and Suspense suspension.

<details>


title: [compiler] Recognize oxlint-disable suppressions
body:
## Summary

The compiler skips a component or hook when a React lint rule is suppressed inside it (`eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps`, `/* eslint-disable react-hooks/rules-of-hooks */`, ...), because that code may break the Rules of React. It only recognizes the `eslint-` prefix.

[oxlint](<url>) supports the same directives under an `oxlint-` prefix, with the same `react-hooks/*` rule names. Projects that move from ESLint to oxlint often rewrite their `eslint-disable` comments to `oxlint-disable`. That's oxlint's own form, and it's required when `respectEslintDisableDirectives` is off. After that rewrite, the compiler no longer sees the suppressions and compiles code it used to skip, with no warning.

This change makes the compiler treat `oxlint-disable-next-line`, `oxlint-disable`, and `oxlint-enable` the same way as their `eslint-` counterparts, in both the Babel plugin (`Suppression.ts`) and the Rust port (`suppression.rs`). oxc's port of the compiler already recognizes both prefixes.

## How did you test this change?

- Added two fixtures, both mirroring existing ESLint fixtures:
  - `error.invalid-oxlint-suppression`: a next-line suppression reports the suppression error.
  - `unclosed-oxlint-suppression-skips-all-components`: a block suppression skips every component.
- `yarn snap`: 1838 passed, 0 failed.
- `compiler/scripts/test-rust-port.ts`: 1837 passed, 0 failed. With the Rust change reverted, `unclosed-oxlint-suppression-skips-all-components` fails, so the fixtures cover the Rust port too.
- `cargo test -p react_compiler`, `cargo fmt --check`, `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler lint`, and Prettier pass.

title: fix(react-dom): guard null and prototype-less options in prefetchDNS DEV check
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37885.

In `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href, ...)` under `__DEV__`, verifying extra arguments previously checked `typeof options === 'object' && options.hasOwnProperty('crossOrigin')`. Because `typeof null === 'object'`, passing `null` as the second argument threw:
`TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'hasOwnProperty')`
Passing prototype-less objects created via `Object.create(null)` threw:
`TypeError: options.hasOwnProperty is not a function`

This change imports `hasOwnProperty` from `shared/hasOwnProperty` and guards against `null` (`options != null && typeof options === 'object' && hasOwnProperty.call(options, 'crossOrigin')`). Calling `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS` with `null` or prototype-less options now logs the diagnostic warning instead of throwing an unhandled exception.

## How did you test this change?

- Added unit tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFloat-test.js` verifying `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(url, null)`, `ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(url, Object.create(null))`, and prototype-less options containing `crossOrigin` log their respective warnings without throwing errors.
- Ran tests via Jest:
  `yarn test packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFloat-test.js -t "prefetchDNS"`
- Verified code changes pass linter:
  `yarn linc`

title: [compiler] Stop compiling a function after its first error when errors are not observed
body:
## Summary

Since the fault-tolerance work (#35873 through #35884), `runWithEnvironment` keeps running every pass after an error is recorded, so that all errors can be reported, and only returns `Err` after codegen. A function with any recorded error is skipped either way.

When nothing can observe those errors, the extra passes are wasted work. That's the case when:

- `outputMode` is not `'lint'`,
- no `logger` is configured,
- and `panicThreshold` is `'none'` (the default).

That's the default setup when the plugin runs in a regular Babel build.

This adds `Environment.collectsAllErrors`, which is true in lint mode, when a logger is set, or when `panicThreshold` can turn errors into exceptions. When it's false, `runWithEnvironment` returns the recorded errors at the next checkpoint instead of continuing. The checkpoints come right after `lower`, after `dropManualMemoization`, after the early hooks and capitalized-call validations, before `inferReactivePlaces`, after `validateExhaustiveDependencies`, and right before codegen. The final `hasErrors()` check is unchanged, so whether a function compiles or bails out doesn't change.

Behavior in the observed modes:

- **Lint mode:** unchanged. Every error is still collected.
- **With a logger:** unchanged. The logger gets the same `CompileError` events (one per error) as before.
- **With `panicThreshold: 'critical_errors'` or `'all_errors'`:** unchanged. The thrown error still lists every detail.

Without a logger in client/SSR mode, a failing function stops at its first checkpoint, and its error object can hold fewer details. Nothing reads that object in this configuration.

Two things worth knowing:

- **Outlined function names can be numbered differently.** `outlineFunctions` reserves names like `_temp`, `_temp2` file-wide (through `generateUidIdentifier`), including for functions that later bail out. Those functions now stop before outlining, so outlined functions later in the same file can get lower `_tempN` suffixes. The code is otherwise identical. Only reserving names for functions that end up compiled would avoid this, but that would also renumber current output in the observed modes, so I left it alone.
- **An invalid `moduleTypeProvider` config error can be skipped.** That error is thrown during type inference, so for a function that already failed while lowering, it's no longer raised (in the unobserved configuration only). That matches behavior before the fault-tolerance change. Valid configurations aren't affected.

While testing I also noticed that compiling past an inline `class` declaration currently ends in an invariant in `InferMutationAliasingEffects` ("Expected value kind to be initialized") instead of reporting the unsupported syntax. This PR doesn't change that in the observed modes.

## How did you test this change?

- New `src/__tests__/StopAfterFirstError-test.ts`. It uses `moduleTypeProvider` calls to detect whether compilation continued past an error recorded while lowering. Without a logger, compilation stops; with a logger, in lint mode, or with `panicThreshold: 'all_errors'`, it continues. On main, the first test fails and the other three pass.
- `yarn snap`: 1836 passed. Note that snap always attaches a logger, so it runs the unchanged path.
- `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler jest`: 48 passed. `lint` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean. `yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-compiler test`: 33 passed, 27 skipped (same as main).
- Output: I compiled the 149 non-test files under `packages/react-devtools-shared/src/devtools/views` and the 1835 compiler fixtures, without a logger, using the built `dist/index.js` from main and from this branch. The transformed code (or error) is byte-identical for every file. Neither corpus hits the `_tempN` renumbering described above. With a logger attached, the `CompileError`, `CompileSuccess`, `CompileSkip` and `CompileUnexpectedThrow` counts are identical too.
- Timing, with no logger, using the same script and method as #37976: Node 22, a fresh process per run, interleaved, median of per-round ratios.

title: [compiler] Detect frozen known-mutable functions stored in object literals
[DevTools] Ignore stale standalone socket disconnections
body:
## Summary
When a new client replaces the standalone server's current connection, the previous socket can emit close after the new connection has initialized. Its handler then clears the current connection and resets DevTools even though the replacement client is still connected. A delayed error from the previous socket has the same problem.

Only handle close/error for the socket that is still active. This also preserves the active reference so a later connection can close the right previous client.

## How did you test this change?
- Added regression coverage for a replaced socket closing or erroring, and for an active socket still disconnecting normally. The stale-socket cases fail before the fix.
- yarn test-build-devtools standalone backend-test bridge-test --runInBand: 3 suites, 8 tests passed.
- Built standalone DevTools and connected two real WebSocket clients: the old socket's delayed close no longer fires the disconnect callback for the replacement client.
- ESLint and Prettier on the changed files; git diff --check.

title: [compiler] Build babel-plugin-react-compiler with target es2022
body:
## Summary

`babel-plugin-react-compiler` is bundled by tsup with `target: 'es2015'`, so esbuild lowers syntax that every Node version able to run the plugin already supports. In `dist/index.js` on main:

- every `yield*` in the HIR visitor generators (`eachInstructionLValue`, `eachInstructionOperand`, `eachInstructionValueOperand`, ...) goes through esbuild's `__yieldStar` helper (24 sites);
- every `#private` field access goes through the WeakMap-based `__privateGet` / `__privateAdd` / `__privateSet` helpers (358 references), including the hot `InferenceState` methods;
- object spread goes through `__spreadValues` / `__spreadProps` (283 references).

With `target: 'es2022'` the bundle contains none of these helpers. In a CPU profile of compiling the DevTools views on main, `__yieldStar` alone was 5.7% of samples (inclusive).

This only changes the syntax of the plugin's own bundle, which runs inside Babel on Node. The code the compiler emits is unchanged. `react-compiler-runtime`, which ships in app bundles, keeps its es2015 target. eslint-plugin-react-hooks bundles the compiler from source with its own build, so it isn't affected either.

Node support doesn't change in practice. The source already calls `Array.prototype.at`, which needs Node 16.6+, and the es2022 bundle needs Node 16.11+ (class static blocks). As a check, I ran the es2022 bundle on Node 16.20.2. `es2018` would be enough to drop `__yieldStar` and the spread helpers, but it keeps the private-field helpers.

This is independent of #37976 (lazy invariant messages), and the two gains add up.

## How did you test this change?

- `yarn snap` (it builds the plugin with this tsup config; the built bundle has no `__yieldStar`): 1836 tests, 1836 passed.
- `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler jest`: 44 passed. `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler lint` is clean.
- `yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-compiler test`: 33 passed, 27 skipped (same as main).
- Output is unchanged. With the same two corpora and script as #37976 (the 149 non-test files under `packages/react-devtools-shared/src/devtools/views`, and the 1835 compiler fixtures), the transformed code (or error) is byte-identical to main for every file.
- Timing, same method as #37976: a fresh Node 22.14 process per run doing 3 passes with `@babel/core` `transformSync` (times include parsing and codegen), arms interleaved over 8 rounds (5 for the fixtures), median of per-round ratios against main.

title: [compiler] Only build invariant messages when the invariant fails
[compiler] Retain declared Freeze effects on already-frozen values for ref validation
body:
## Summary

When an operand is already frozen (e.g. a memoized value), `applyEffect` drops a declared `Freeze` effect because nothing new gets frozen. Ref validation reads the declared `Freeze` effects of known signatures, so it misses them in this case. For example, with `PanResponder.create`'s signature:

```js
const ref = useRef(0);
const config = useMemo(() => ({onPanResponderRelease: () => { ref.current = 0; }}), []);
const responder = PanResponder.create(config); // false positive: ref access reported
```

This keeps the declared effect on the instruction when the value is already frozen, as suggested by @javache in #37970. This is metadata only: nothing extra is frozen.

**Note:** the literal diff from review (always `effects.push(effect)`) regressed 11 snapshot fixtures. A retained `Freeze` sets `operand.effect === Effect.Freeze` in `InferMutationAliasingRanges`, which `ValidateNoFreezingKnownMutableFunctions` reads, so it started reporting an extra "Cannot modify local variables after render completes" error on already-frozen operands. It also made the valid `allow-mutate-global-in-effect-fixpoint` fixture fail, and added a duplicate error to e.g. `error.assign-ref-in-effect-hint`, `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-intersection-observer` and `error.todo-reassign-const`.

So this PR keeps the effect for ref validation only: the retained effect is marked `alreadyFrozen`, and `InferMutationAliasingRanges` skips it when computing operand effects. All other passes see what they saw before. The same change is made in the Rust port (`already_frozen`).

## How did you test this change?

- Added `panresponder-ref-in-memoized-config.js` (the `useMemo` example above, using the `shared-runtime` `PanResponder.create` signature). It fails with "Cannot access refs during render" without this change and passes with it.
- `yarn snap` in `compiler/`: the failure list is identical to `main` (the same 20 pre-existing failures, mostly fbt fixtures in my local setup); no snapshots changed other than the new fixture.
- `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler tsc --noEmit` and `lint`, prettier: pass.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo check --workspace`, and `cargo test` for `react_compiler_hir`, `react_compiler_inference` and `react_compiler_validation`: pass. I did not run the Rust fixture comparison against snap.

title: [Fizz] Preserve postponed holes when replay aborts
body:
Fixes #37907

## Summary

When calling `resumeAndPrerender` on a previously postponed prerender, aborting the replay above a pending resumable slot (before reaching the inner postponed content) previously caused the `SuspenseBoundary` to transition to `CLIENT_RENDERED` (`$RX`). Because the boundary was already emitted in the initial prelude, marking it as client-rendered discards the remaining postponed paths/slots and forces the client to render the boundary from scratch instead of allowing a subsequent `resume` to complete it on the server.

This change preserves the remaining replay work when a resumed replay aborts:
* Tracks `contentNodes` and `contentSlots` on `resumedBoundary.tracked` during `replaySuspenseBoundary` so mutated replay state remains accessible if interrupted.
* Updates the synchronous catch block in `replaySuspenseBoundary` to check if the request aborted while `trackedPostpones` is active and remaining child nodes/slots exist, recording the boundary via `trackPostponedBoundary` instead of marking it `CLIENT_RENDERED`.
* Updates `finishAbortedTask` for asynchronous aborts where `segment === null` (replay tasks without a new segment) to preserve `boundary.tracked.contentNodes` and `contentSlots` on the postponed boundary node and flush pending fallback tasks cleanly.

## How did you test this change?

* Added unit tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js` (`preserves postponed holes when aborting a resumed replay above a slot (synchronously / asynchronously)`) verifying a 3-stage flow:
  1. Initial `prerender` aborts and produces a postponed state.
  2. `resumeAndPrerender` suspends and aborts (both synchronously and asynchronously) in a wrapper component above the inner slot, asserting that `second.postponed` remains non-null and does not emit `$RX`.
  3. Final `resume` resolves the inner component and streams the completed `<section>Hello</section>` content into the existing boundary.
* Ran tests in development and production modes:
  * `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js`
  * `yarn test --prod ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser-test.js`
* Verified formatting, linting, and Flow types:
  * `yarn prettier`
  * `yarn linc`
  * `yarn flow`

title: [DOM] Copy `altitudeAngle` and `azimuthAngle` onto synthetic pointer events
body:
## Summary

`PointerEvent` has `altitudeAngle` and `azimuthAngle` (Pointer Events Level 3, Baseline 2024), which describe the pen orientation as angles. `PointerEventInterface` copies `tiltX`, `tiltY` and `twist` but not these two, so a pointer event handler reads `event.altitudeAngle` and `event.azimuthAngle` as `undefined` even when the native event has them.

Adding both to the interface copies them off the native event the same way `tiltX` and `tiltY` are copied.

## How did you test this change?

Added a test to the SimpleEventPlugin suite that dispatches a `pointerdown` event with both angles and asserts the synthetic event exposes them. It fails on main and passes with the fix. Also ran `yarn test packages/react-dom/src/events`, `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier`, and `yarn flow dom-node`.

title: Clear the lane on an update that bailed out eagerly
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37967.

When `setState` is called with a value equal to the current one and the queue
is empty, `dispatchSetStateInternal` computes the next state eagerly, sees it
is unchanged, and bails out without scheduling a render. It still queues the
update, via `enqueueConcurrentHookUpdateAndEagerlyBailout`, so that it can be
rebased later. That function deliberately enqueues at `NoLane` — nothing is
scheduled, so there is no work to mark — but the update object keeps the lane
it was dispatched at.

Nothing will ever render that lane, and leaving it on the update is what breaks
the issue's case:

1. The next render happens at some other lane, so `updateReducerImpl` finds the
  update's lane is not a subset of `renderLanes` and skips it. Skipping sets
  `hook.baseQueue` to the skipped update and re-schedules its lane on the
  fiber.
2. The component then updates state during that render — the "storing
  information from previous renders" pattern. `rerenderReducer` applies it to
  `memoizedState`, but because `hook.baseQueue` is no longer `null` it does
  not persist it to `hook.baseState`.
3. The lane that step 1 re-scheduled renders, replays the base queue from that
  `baseState`, and the update made during render is gone.

So clear the lane on the update as well as on the enqueue. The update is then
never skipped, its lane is never re-scheduled, and the base queue stays empty
so the render-phase update reaches `baseState`.

This cannot change the state the update produces. The eager path only runs when
the fiber has no pending lanes, which means the hook's queue is empty and its
`baseState` equals the `lastRenderedState` the eager state was computed from, so
applying the update in a later render at any lane yields the same value it
yielded eagerly. What it does remove is the extra render pass that the
re-scheduled lane used to cause for a bailed-out update.

## How did you test this change?

Added a regression test next to the existing render-phase-update regression
tests in `ReactHooksWithNoopRenderer-test.js`, following the repro in the issue:
mount, `setValue(true)` at discrete priority while `value` is already `true`,
then `setFlag(false)` at default priority so the child updates `value` during
render.

Before the change it fails with the extra render from the issue's console log:

```
  - Expected
  + Received

  Array [
  "value: false",
  +  "value: true",
  ]
```

After it passes.

- `yarn test packages/react-reconciler` — same result as on `main` apart from
  the new test passing (1144 vs 1143 passing; the same 4 failures in
  `ReactMemo-test` and `ReactUse-test` are there with and without this patch).
- `yarn test --prod ReactHooks` — 206 passing.
- `yarn test --release-channel=stable ReactHooks` — 207 passing.
- `yarn test --release-channel=www-modern ReactHooks` — 207 passing.
- `yarn lint` on both changed files — clean.

I paid particular attention to the two existing eager-bailout tests in
`ReactHooks-test.internal.js`. "bails out multiple times in a row without
entering render phase" still sees three eager `Compute state (0 -> 0)` calls
and still reuses all four eager states in the render phase, since the enqueue
lane was already `NoLane` and is what that test turns on. "can rebase on top of
a previously skipped update" never reaches this path at all, because its eager
state differs from the current state.

title: [compiler] Type react-native PanResponder.create to fix react-hooks/refs false positive
body:
Fixes #37955

**Depends on #37975** (retains declared `Freeze` effects for already-frozen values, as suggested by @javache). Until that merges this PR's diff also shows its commit.

## Summary

`react-hooks/refs` reports "Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render" for callbacks passed to React Native's `PanResponder.create({...})`, because the compiler treats `PanResponder` imported from `react-native` as an unknown function that may call its arguments during render. `PanResponder.create()` only stores the handlers and invokes them later from gesture events.

The compiler already has a signature for exactly this (`PanResponder.create` freezes its config and doesn't call it during render), but it only exists in the test-only `shared-runtime` type provider in `snap`, so real code never gets it. This adds the same signature for `react-native` to `defaultModuleTypeProvider` (TypeScript, and the Rust port in `default_module_type_provider.rs`), so the callbacks are treated as deferred, like the `IntersectionObserver` fix in #37764.

Other unknown functions still report errors when given ref-accessing callbacks.

## How did you test this change?

Added a valid case to `packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/__tests__/ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts` (the repro shape from the issue). Snap fixtures can't cover this because `snap` replaces the module type provider with its own.

- Without the fix: `cd packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks && npx jest ReactCompilerRuleTypescript` → `1 failed, 15 passed` (the new case).
- With the fix: `yarn build:compiler && npx jest` in `packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks` → `4 suites passed, 5087 tests passed`.
- `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler tsc --noEmit` and `lint` (in `compiler/`) pass; `yarn lint` at the root passes; prettier check passes on the changed TS files.
- `cargo check -p react_compiler_hir` and `cargo fmt --check` pass for the Rust change (I did not run the Rust test suite).
- `yarn snap` in `compiler/`: identical results with and without this change (1812 passed, 20 failed; the failures are pre-existing, mostly fbt fixtures in my local setup).
- Also added a memoized-config case (`useMemo` config passed to `PanResponder.create`); with #37975 the eslint-plugin suite passes (5088 tests).
- `yarn flow` not run: the change touches no Flow-typed code.

title: [Flight] Record the parent of a written object instead of its path
body:
## Problem

Flight dedupes objects. `writtenObjects` maps each object it has written to a reference, and if the same object shows up again it writes `$1:posts:3:content` instead of a copy. The reference is a path string, built for every nested object when it is written:

```js
writtenObjects.set(value, writtenObjects.get(parent) + ':' + propertyName);
```

Each object costs a WeakMap lookup, a string concat, and a string that lives until the request ends. Almost none of the strings are used. A blog page with 22.7k plain objects has three shared ones. Building 22.6k strings to emit 70 references is 35% of the serializer's main-thread time and most of the GC work.

## Fix

Store the parent instead of the path:

```js
writtenObjects.set(value, parent);
```

If the object shows up again, build the path then: resolve the parent's reference the same way, find the object in the parent by identity, cache the result.

The output of a Server Component is recorded as the element, which has the same reference. A lazy's resolved model or a `toJSON` result can't be found in the parent by identity, so it still gets a path string.

## Parent must already be recorded

A child is recorded only if its parent is. Otherwise, if the parent is recorded later at a different place, the child's path would point there instead of where the child was written.

The first commit keeps the `writtenObjects.has(parent)` check. The second removes it: `renderModelDestructive` sets a flag for the container it returns, like it sets `task.model` on the way in, and `resolveModel` passes it to the children. The flag is reset on entry, so a path that doesn't set it means no dedupe for those children, not a wrong reference.

## Tests

Output is byte-identical to `main` on the Flight suites and on a differential fuzz of 6,000 random models. New tests: an element that suspends behind a lazy, and an object first rendered inside a keyed Server Component, each shared again later.

## Numbers

Serializer microbench, NODE_PROD `react-server-dom-webpack` server bundle, 5 interleaved rounds vs `main`. Process CPU includes GC threads.

| model | wall | process CPU |
|---|---|---|
| blog-like data, 697KB, 22.7k objects | −9.5% | −64% |
| element-dominated page, 278KB | ±0 | −39% |
| dashboard-like page, 182KB, client references | ±0 | −38% |

Next.js e2e, 16 VM boots, both arms per VM, 2 runs, 8 clients under load. n.s. = 95% interval includes zero. Bytes identical on every route.

| | /blog 1 | /blog 8 | /dashboard 1 | /dashboard 8 | /docs 1 | /docs 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| rps | n.s. | +8.2% ±7.0 | +4.4% ±3.4 | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. |
| p95 | −7.1% ±5.1 | n.s. | −8.4% ±5.6 | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. |
| TTFB | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. | n.s. |

The remaining dedupe cost is the WeakMap get and set per object.

title: Preserve painted SSR fallback DOM when hydration suspends again on a recoverable boundary
body: ## Preserve painted SSR fallback DOM when hydration suspends again on a recoverable boundary Fixes #37620 ### Root cause When hydration begins on a Suspense boundary whose server-rendered output was a **recoverable fallback** (e.g. the component requested a browser-only dependency via `ReactDOM.browser()` and Fizz bailed out on that boundary), and the primary children suspend **again** on the client (a client-only `use(promise)` that is still pending at hydration time), React can re-enter the boundary while its client data is unresolved. The flow is: 1. Pass 1 begins the dehydrated boundary and attempts the primary children. Because they suspend, `retrySuspenseComponentWithoutHydrating` runs on the restart: it **queues the server-painted `DehydratedFragment` fallback fiber for deletion**, sets `memoizedState = null`, and begins rendering fresh fallback DOM via `mountSuspenseFallbackAfterRetryWithoutHydrating`. 2. Pass 2 lands in `updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent` with `didSuspend = true` and enters `mountSuspenseFallbackAfterRetryWithoutHydrating`, which deletes the already-painted (SSR) fallback DOM and mounts an **identical client-rendered fallback in its place**, and makes the *new* fallback the tracked fallback. Deleting and remounting an identical fallback restarts CSS-driven spinner/progress animations (the reported bug). Worse, depending on ordering, the raw `DehydratedFragment` (unit-of-work tag 18) can be handed back to the work loop — e.g. returned from `updateSuspenseFallbackChildren`'s tail `bailoutOffscreenComponent(null, primaryChildFragment)`, whose `return` chain ends on `primaryChildFragment.sibling`, i.e. the tag-18 fragment — crashing beginWork with `Unknown unit of work tag (18)`. The existing behavior has no way to preserve the fallback fiber because the retry path unconditionally recreates fallback DOM from props. ### Fix (3 small hunks, all in `ReactFiberBeginWork.js`) When the boundary is being restarted on a *recoverable* fallback (`isSuspenseInstanceFallback(suspenseInstance) && getSuspenseInstanceFallbackErrorDetails(suspenseInstance).digest === REACT_RECOVERABLE_DIGEST`), keep the server-painted fallback mounted instead of deleting it: 1. **`updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent` (restart path):** un-queue the deletion of the `DehydratedFragment`, mount the primary children into a **hidden** offscreen fragment (`mountWorkInProgressOffscreenFiber` with `mode: 'hidden'`) so they can still complete when the pending client data resolves, re-attach the preserved fragment as the boundary's live fallback child, set the standard `SUSPENDED_MARKER`, and create the `OffscreenInstance` (the normal path would do this in `bailoutOffscreenComponent`; here we return `null` so the raw fragment is never begun). 2. **`updateSuspenseFallbackChildren`:** when the current fallback child is the preserved `DehydratedFragment` (tag 18), reattach it as-is instead of `createWorkInProgress`-cloning it into a position React would try to begin (which crashes on tag 18), and undo the primary pass's queued deletion, clearing the leftover `ChildDeletion` flag when the deletion list becomes empty. 3. **`updateSuspenseComponent` (showFallback tail):** if the fallback sibling on the freshly derived primary child is the preserved `DehydratedFragment`, return `null` instead of `bailoutOffscreenComponent(current.child, primaryChildFragment)`, which would otherwise surface that same tag-18 fragment as the next unit of work. Everything else behaves normally: the retry scheduling that flips a suspended boundary back to content is untouched, so once the client promise resolves the boundary renders its primary content and the preserved fallback DOM is removed in the ordinary way. ### Evidence Base (unpatched) behavior for the new test: the DOM-identity assertion fails with the classic *"serializes to the same string"* result — the fallback DOM is torn down and an identical node is mounted (and the subsequent resolve flow cannot complete: the first retry render's act Times out) — i.e. the remount bug directly. After this change, the new test `keeps the fallback DOM when hydration suspends again on a client promise` covers the complete flow: - SSR paints `Loading`; the boundary bails out on the server (`onBrowserBailout`). - Hydration passes the `browser()` check on the client, then suspends again on a pending client promise; the fallback DOM node **keeps its identity** (`container.querySelector('span')` is the *same node* it was before hydration) and no recoverable errors are dispatched. - Resolving the client promise swaps in the content (`Content`), which is additionally verified after the standard fallback-commit throttle (`jest.advanceTimersByTime(FALLBACK_THROTTLE_MS)`), matching how other suites in this repo handle throttled retry commits. Also worth noting: the sibling test `can opt a component into browser-only rendering`, which was crashing in competing implementations of this issue, passes along with the rest. ### Tests - `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzServer-test.js`: **185/185 passed** (including the new test). - `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration-test.internal.js`: 66/67 — the single failure is the pre-existing `[GATED, SHOULD FAIL]` case (identical on unpatched `main`). - Reconciler suites (`ReactSuspense-test.internal`, `ReactSuspenseFallback-test`, `ReactSuspenseList-test`, `ReactSuspenseWithNoopRenderer-test`, `ReactSuspenseEffectsSemantics-test`, `ReactSuspenseCallback-test`, `ReactCPUSuspense-test`, `ActivitySuspense-test`, `ActivityLegacySuspense-test`): **all pass**. - `yarn flow dom-node`: no errors.

title: Fix crash when a deleted hidden Activity's suspended data resolves
body:
When a component inside a hidden Activity suspends and there's no Suspense boundary in between, the Activity's Offscreen fiber acts as the suspense handler. At commit, `attachSuspenseRetryListeners` binds `resolveRetryWakeable` to that Offscreen fiber and attaches it to the thenable.

If the Activity is deleted before the thenable settles, it nulls out the Offscreen fiber's `stateNode`. There's no way to remove a listener from a promise, so when the thenable later resolves or rejects, the retry still runs against the detached fiber.

  TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading '_retryCache')

Because this runs inside a promise callback, it surfaces as an unhandled error rather than something an error boundary can catch.

The Suspense and SuspenseList branches of `resolveRetryWakeable` already treat a null `stateNode` as "no retry cache", and `markUpdateLaneFromFiberToRoot` already null-checks a deleted Offscreen instance (#24734).

Several apps have hit this in production and worked around it in userland: cevi/conveniat-webpage#1471, ACM-VIT/ExamCooker#460, remotion-dev/remotion#12303.

Added a regression test to `ActivitySuspense-test.js` that renders a hidden Activity around a suspending child, deletes it, then resolves the data. It throws without the fix.

title: [DevTools] Fix the "parse hook names" icon
body:
Stacked on #37962.

## Summary

#36944 started rendering every button icon as `<path d={icon}>`. The "parse hook names" icon is an SVG group, not a path string, so it rendered `d="[object Object]"`: the button lost its icon, and the browser logged an error on every render. These are the `<path> attribute d` errors reported in #37649.

Icons that aren't path data now render as-is again, as before #36944.

## How did you test this change?

- New `ButtonIcon-test.js`. Fails without this change.

title: [DevTools] Symbolicate all frames of a stack at the same time
body:
Stacked on #37961.

## Summary

Fixes #37649.

Stack views resolve their frames with `use()` in a loop, and each `use()` waits for its frame before the next one even starts. So 35 frames meant 35 lookups, one after another.

We now start all frames up front. Together with the previous PR, one click makes at most one resource-list request and one Network-log request.

## How did you test this change?

- `symbolicateSource-test.js`: every file of a stack starts loading right away.
- Headless Chrome with the 8.0.0 extension and this stack applied; app with 3,150 modules and ~18k network requests; one click (35 frames):

| | time to show "rendered by" | line numbers |
|---|---|---|
| 8.0.0 | 19.5–20.8 s | compiled |
| this stack | 1.0–1.25 s | original |
| this stack, after a page reload | 0.53 s (15.8 s without this PR) | original |

title: [DevTools] Share pending resource and HAR lookups between file fetches
body:
Stacked on #37960.

## Summary

Part of #37649.

Every file lookup asks the browser for the page's full resource list or Network log, and the browser serializes the whole thing each time. Lookups that run at the same time now share one pending request, so nothing goes stale: later lookups still make a fresh request.

This has no effect alone. The next PR makes the lookups run at the same time.

## How did you test this change?

- `fetchFileWithCaching-test.js`: 3 concurrent lookups make 1 request. Fails without this change.

title: [DevTools] Don't read source-mapped originals as scripts in Chrome
body:
Stacked on #37959.

## Summary

Part of #37649.

Vite serves the compiled `App.tsx` at `/src/App.tsx`, and its source map points back to the same URL. After a page reload, Chrome lists the original source under that URL instead of the compiled script. DevTools then found no source map in it and showed compiled line numbers.

We now skip those source-mapped entries (`sm-script`) and get the compiled script elsewhere.

On its own this costs one Network-log read per file (slow with a big log). The next two PRs reduce it to one read per click.

## How did you test this change?

- `fetchFileWithCaching-test.js`: a source-mapped original is skipped. Fails without this change.
- After a reload, "rendered by" shows `LegendItem.jsx:9` instead of `:12`.

title: [DevTools] Don't also fetch from the page when the file is in the HAR
body:
Stacked on #37958.

## Summary

Part of #37649.

When the extension found a file in the browser's Network log, it returned the file but then downloaded it again from the page anyway, because of a missing `return` (present since #22285). We now stop after the match.

## How did you test this change?

- New `fetchFileWithCaching-test.js` with a mocked `chrome` API. Fails without this change.

title: [DevTools] Reuse a file's source map for all of its stack frames
body:
Stacked on #37957.

## Summary

Part of #37649.

Results were cached per stack frame. Several frames in the same file re-downloaded the script and re-parsed its source map each time, and for a bundled library that map can be several MB.

We now cache the parsed source map per file (the last 50 files).

## How did you test this change?

- `symbolicateSource-test.js`: two frames in one file fetch it once.
- Same scenario as the PR below: 3.3 s → 2.9 s.

title: [DevTools] Decode inline source maps instead of fetching them
body:
Stacked on #37956.

## Summary

Part of #37649: in Vite apps, selecting a component freezes DevTools for tens of seconds.

For every stack frame, the extension "fetched" the source map. An inline `data:` map is never one of the page's resources, so each frame fell back to reading the browser's entire Network log. After a while of developing, that log has thousands of requests, so one click took ~20 s and stalled DevTools.

The map is already in the URL, so we now decode it directly.

## How did you test this change?

- `symbolicateSource-test.js`: inline maps are decoded without a fetch, and UTF-8 survives.
- App with 3,150 modules and ~18k network requests, one click (35 frames): 19.5 s → 3.3 s, and no Network log reads.

title: [DevTools] Resolve sources of inline source maps against the script URL
body:
## Summary

Part of #37649.

To show where a component was rendered, DevTools maps compiled stack locations back to the original files using source maps. In development, Vite embeds each module's source map inline as a `data:` URL and lists the original file relative to the module (e.g. `"App.tsx"`). We resolved that relative path against the `data:` URL, which can't work. Mapping failed silently, and every app frame showed compiled line numbers.

Browsers resolve these paths against the script's own URL. Now we do too.

## How did you test this change?

- New `symbolicateSource-test.js`. The inline case fails without this change.
- In a Vite-style app, "rendered by" shows `LegendItem.jsx:9` (the real line) instead of `:12`.

title: [DevTools] Fix string value reset in native style editor
body: ## Summary Fix a parsing error when canceling a string edit in the native style editor. Previously, pressing Escape restored `"left"` without its quotes, causing `JSON.parse` to throw when the field lost focus. The field initializes its local state as JSON text: ```js const [localValue, setLocalValue] = useState(JSON.stringify(value)); ``` Reset the value as JSON text too, so it can be parsed when the field loses focus: ```diff -setLocalValue(value); +setLocalValue(JSON.stringify(value)); ``` ## How did you test this change? Start the DevTools shell with [a temporary adjustment to the backend activation order]() to enable the native style panel: ```bash yarn install cd packages/react-devtools-inline ../../node_modules/.bin/cross-env NODE_ENV=development ../../node_modules/.bin/webpack --config webpack.config.js cd ../react-devtools-shell yarn start ``` Manually verified that changing `textAlign` from `"left"` to `"right"`, pressing Escape, and then pressing Tab restores `"left"` with its quotes and leaves the editor usable.

title: [Flight] Escape colons in reference paths and keep undefined object keys
body:
Two gaps the fuzz found once it had leaves for them: an object with a colon in a key, and a key whose value is `undefined`. Both change what arrives on the other side.

## Property names with a colon (<url>)

A reference to a value inside another model is the model's id and the property names on the way to the value, joined with colons, like `$2:props:items:0`. A property name that contains a colon couldn't be part of one, so the writer skipped dedupe for values under such names. URL keys are the common case: `{[url]: data, other: data}` sent `data` twice, and an object that reaches itself through a URL key has no reference to break the cycle with, so the writer recursed until the stack overflowed. The reply encoder threw on the circular structure instead.

Colons and percent signs in a name are now percent-escaped on the way into a path and unescaped where the path is split. Names without either character pass through unchanged. Writer, client, reply encoder and reply decoder all change, since each one builds or splits paths. Tests: `can pass a cyclic object under a property name with a colon` in both Edge suites.

## Object keys whose value is undefined (<url>)

`{prop: undefined}` arrived as `{}`. Both readers revive a parsed model by walking it and deleting a key when the walk produces `undefined`, which is what a `JSON.parse` reviver would do, but the writer sends `undefined` as `"$undefined"`, so the key was lost while an array kept its slot. The key now stays when the raw value was `"$undefined"`. `should transport undefined object values` has asserted this since #26478 under `@gate FIXME`; the gate comes off. `can pass undefined as a reply` asserted the old behavior, with a comment saying it should be the other way, and now asserts that.

With these the fuzz's exclusion list is empty: every leaf and move is in the random graphs. A 64-seed sweep passes on all three hosts in DEV and production.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](<url>)

title: [compiler] Keep SSR event handlers that run during render
[Flight] Let stream items and shared streams take part in cycles
body:
The fuzz still had to avoid two shapes: a stream item that is part of a cycle, and a stream that is held in more than one place. Both are writer bugs. This PR fixes them and removes the restrictions from the generator. After it, the fuzz skips no known case; two leaves stay out of the random graphs until #37952.

## A stream item that refers to itself (<url> <url>)

A stream item is written straight into its stream's row, so it has no id. Cycles are broken by writing a reference to an id, so an item that reaches itself has nothing to refer back to and the writer recurses until the stack overflows. The reply encoder throws instead, because `JSON.stringify` sees the circular structure.

The item now gets an id before it is written. If anything refers to that id while the item is written, the item goes out as a row of its own and the stream row points at it:

```
3:["first","$3"]
1:"$3"
```

If nothing refers to it, the item is written inline as before and the id is dropped. A later reference to an item that got a row arrives as the same object; it used to arrive as a copy. The reply encoder does the same with a part, and keeps the part when a stream was written inside the item, since the stream can only be read once and a later holder has to refer to it through the part.

## A stream held in more than one place (<url>)

A stream can only be read once. The writer did not record where it wrote a stream, so a second holder read it again and got "ReadableStream is locked". The stream is now registered under its row when it is first written, like a Promise, so a second holder gets a reference.

This only works server to client. The reply decoder rejects a second reference to a stream it already started, so on the reply host the generator keeps streams in one place. Sync iterators stay in one place everywhere: they are drained into an array where they are first met.

## An Error whose cause is itself (<url>)

In DEV an Error's cause is outlined into a row every time the Error is written. An Error that is its own cause outlines itself from inside its own cause until the stack overflows. A cause that was already written is now referred to by its existing reference, and a cause that is a server component that suspended is referred to lazily, as the first occurrence of the element was.

The default fuzz seeds pass on all three hosts in DEV and production.

title: [Flight] Check for a plain object before the built-ins
body:
In `renderModelDestructive`, an object that isn't an element, a promise or a reference is checked against Map, Set, FormData, Error, every typed array, DataView, Blob, ReadableStream and Date before the code concludes it is a plain object. On a data-heavy payload nearly every object is a plain object, so that is twenty failed `instanceof` checks per object. All of those built-ins have a prototype other than `Object.prototype`, so this checks the prototype once, right after `isArray`, and only runs the chain for objects that aren't plain. The iterator and async iterator probes still run for plain objects, since a plain object can carry those symbols. Nothing about the output changes.

Serializer only (Flight stream into a sink, no SSR), a model of 200 posts of rich text (~10k plain objects), 400 iterations, three alternating rounds on one machine:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| median | 1.74 / 1.75 ms | 1.62 / 1.65 / 1.67 ms |
| cpu | 1105–1153 ms | 1033–1125 ms |
| bytes | 854,814 | 854,814 |

About 6% of serializer time on this shape, 2–3% of a full serialize + parse + SSR pipeline. Element-heavy payloads should see less.

Through Next.js (sandbox bench, 16 boots, this PR against its merge base on canary): `/blog`, which passes ~35k small objects to one Client Component, is **+3.9%** rps single-client (median **−3.6%**, TTFB **−4.2%**, boot-level p < 0.01); `/blog` under load and the element-heavy `/dashboard` and `/docs` are not significantly different. HTML and Flight bytes are identical.

title: Preserve SSR Suspense fallback when a browser-only boundary re-suspends on the client
body:
Fixes #37620. (BountyHub $100 bounty on this issue.)

## Summary

When a Suspense boundary is left in a permanent fallback state by the server — the shape `use(browser())` produces — and the first client render suspends again on a client-created promise (`setTimeout`, `localStorage`, IndexedDB, …), React deleted the server-rendered fallback DOM and mounted an identical new fallback in its place. The markup looks the same, so nothing appears wrong, but the DOM nodes are new: CSS animations (e.g. a Progress bar) restart and any DOM state the fallback picked up is lost.

This change keeps the server's fallback mounted while the boundary is in that state, instead of remounting it.

## What changed

`packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberBeginWork.js`

- In `updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent`, when the retried client render suspends and the boundary's suspense instance is a permanent fallback with the recoverable digest (the intentional client-render case, e.g. `browser()`), the new `mountSuspenseFallbackPreservingDehydratedFragment` is used instead of `mountSuspenseFallbackAfterRetryWithoutHydrating`. It reuses the dehydrated fragment fiber as the boundary's fallback branch (cancelling the deletion the first pass queued for it) and parks the primary tree in an Offscreen fiber beside it for the retry, mirroring the shape of a normal suspended boundary. The fragment is deleted later through the normal path when the primary content commits and replaces it.
- `updateSuspenseFallbackChildren` now recognizes a preserved dehydrated fragment as the current fallback and keeps it mounted as-is across subsequent suspensions, instead of cloning it into a regular fallback fragment.
- `beginWork` gained a `DehydratedFragment` case that bails out: a preserved fragment has no children to render and its DOM is already in place. (Normally a dehydrated fragment is never begun, because its parent boundary bails out first.)

`packages/react-reconciler/src/ReactFiberCompleteWork.js`

- `DehydratedFragment` joins the bubble-properties group in `completeWork`, for the same reason.

The gate is intentionally tight — permanent fallback + recoverable digest only — so ordinary error fallbacks and abandoned hydration of real content keep the existing client-render path, including the existing "extra node inside Suspense fallback" hydration warnings.

This pursues the same goal as #24236 (reverted in #24434) but does not discard any commit: it rewires the boundary's children during the render phase, so the existing fallback nodes stay mounted throughout.

## Test plan

New tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzServer-test.js`, next to the existing `browser()` tests:

- `preserves the SSR fallback node when a browser-only boundary suspends again on the client` — regression test: tags the server fallback node, hydrates into a client suspension, and asserts the fallback in the DOM is the *same node* (attribute intact). Fails on main, passes with this change.
- `preserves the SSR fallback node across sequential client suspensions` — two chained client promises; the fallback node identity survives both suspensions before the content commits. Fails on main, passes with this change.
- `replaces the SSR fallback when a browser-only boundary does not suspend on the client` — control: with no re-suspension, the content commits and the server fallback is removed as before. Passes before and after.

Suites run (all passing, except one pre-existing failure noted below):

- `ReactDOMFizzServer-test` — full file passes.
- `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration-test`, `ReactDOMHydrationDiff-test` — pass. (One `[GATED, SHOULD FAIL]` LegacyHidden test in PartialHydration errors inside the test harness; it fails identically on unmodified main.)
- `ReactDOMFizzShellHydration-test`, `ReactDOMServerPartialHydrationActivity-test`, `ReactDOMServerSelectiveHydration-test` (+ its Activity variant), `ReactDOMServerSuspense-test`, `ReactDOMSuspensePlaceholder-test`, `ReactDOMFizzSuspenseList-test` — all pass.
- Full `ReactDOM` run: 86 suites, 3,371 tests — 3,368 passed, 2 skipped, 1 failed. The one failure is the gated LegacyHidden test above, in `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration-test.internal.js`; it is the same failure seen in the targeted runs and on unmodified main.
- `yarn flow dom-node` — no errors. Prettier — clean.

---

Submitted by Travis Briggs. This fix was developed with AI assistance (Muse); Travis is the human of record accountable for this PR.
