title: [compiler] Allow ref access in ResizeObserver / MutationObserver callbacks
body:
## Summary

`new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current)` and `new MutationObserver(() => ref.current)` currently report a false positive:

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  > 6 |  return new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current);
  |  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render
```

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it asynchronously after the observation fires — never during render — so reading a ref inside the callback is safe. The same reasoning was applied to `IntersectionObserver` in #37764; the remaining two DOM observer constructors were still unmodeled and fell back to the default effects for unknown constructors.

This PR models both the same way in the TypeScript and Rust compilers:

- `ResizeObserver(callback)`: single `Freeze`d callback. (Unlike `IntersectionObserver`, whose options object is a second constructor argument, the `{box}` option of `ResizeObserver` belongs to `observe(target, options)`.)
- `MutationObserver(callback)`: single `Freeze`d callback.

## Validation

- `allow-ref-access-in-resize-observer.ts`: plain callback compiles, and `observe(target, {box})` options do not trip the validation.
- `allow-ref-access-in-mutation-observer.ts`: callback compiles.
- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-resize-observer.js`: mutating a `useMemo` value inside the callback is **still** rejected (`This value cannot be modified`), i.e. the `Freeze` effect is preserved and only the ref false positive is removed.
- Unknown constructors are unaffected: `new Observer(() => ref.current)` still errors.
- Full fixture suite: 1835 fixtures, 25 changed / 3 failed — identical to the pre-existing baseline in this environment (`fbt/*`, `debugger*`, `conflict-codegen-instrument-forget`), so no new snapshot deltas.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `prettier check-changed` pass.

## Notes

The observers' instance methods (`observe`/`unobserve`/`disconnect`) are intentionally left unmodeled, matching `IntersectionObserver`.

title: [compiler] Infer function names from assignments, object properties, and patterns in Rust port
body:
## Summary

In the TypeScript reference implementation (`getFunctionName` in `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/Entrypoint/Program.ts`), names for anonymous `FunctionExpression` and `ArrowFunctionExpression` nodes are inferred from four parent AST contexts (including when wrapped in `React.forwardRef(...)` or `React.memo(...)`):
1. `VariableDeclarator` (`const Foo = () => {}`, `const useHook = () => {}`)
2. `AssignmentExpression` with `=` operator (`useHook = () => {}`, `Foo = () => {}`, `Namespace.useHook = () => {}`)
3. Non-computed `ObjectProperty` (`{ useHook: () => {} }`, `{ Foo: () => {} }`)
4. `AssignmentPattern` (`const { useHook = () => {} } = {}`, `({ useHook = () => {} } = {})`)

Previously, `FunctionDiscoveryVisitor` in the Rust port (`compiler/crates/react_compiler/src/entrypoint/program.rs`) only tracked a single `current_declarator_name: Option<String>` from `VariableDeclarator` nodes, missing `AssignmentExpression`, `ObjectProperty`, `AssignmentPattern`, and `PascalCase.useHook` `MemberExpression` hook targets.

This PR closes that gap in the Rust compiler crates:
1. Extends `Visitor<'ast>` and `AstWalker` in `compiler/crates/react_compiler_ast/src/visitor.rs` with paired enter/leave hooks for `AssignmentExpression`, `ObjectProperty`, and `AssignmentPattern`.
2. Replaces `current_declarator_name` in `FunctionDiscoveryVisitor` (`compiler/crates/react_compiler/src/entrypoint/program.rs`) with a scoped `inferred_name_stack` of `InferredNameEntry` items that match the target function expression (unwrapping transparent TS/Flow type expressions and up to one level of `React.forwardRef` / `React.memo` call wrapper).
3. Supports both `Identifier` names (for component/hook heuristic classification and `CompileSource.fn_name`) and `PascalCase.useHook` `MemberExpression` targets (`InferredFunctionName::HookMemberExpression`, classifying the function as `ReactFunctionType::Hook` with `fn_name: None` to match `Program.ts`).
4. Adds unit tests in `compiler/crates/react_compiler/src/entrypoint/program.rs` covering all four parent contexts, named `FunctionExpression` precedence, `memo`/`forwardRef` wrappers, and negative edge cases (compound assignments, computed keys, non-React call wrappers, and LHS expressions).

## How did you test this change?

- `cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml -p react_compiler_ast`
- `cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml -p react_compiler`
- `cargo test --manifest-path compiler/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets`

title: Keep the server fallback mounted when hydration re-suspends
body:
Fixes #37620.

When `use(browser())` makes the server bail out, it leaves the fallback it already sent as a dehydrated fragment. If hydration then suspends again on a client-created promise (`setTimeout`, `localStorage`, IndexedDB - the shape in the repro), we were deleting that fragment and mounting an identical fallback in its place. The markup is the same, so nothing looks wrong, but the nodes are new: a CSS animation restarts and any DOM state the fallback picked up is gone.

Since the fallback we're about to render already exists in the DOM, the fix is to keep the server's fragment and park a hidden primary tree beside it for the retry to carry on in.

This is the same goal as #24236, which got reverted in #24434 because it threw the commit away and that broke late mutations on WWW. This version rewires the fiber tree instead of discarding the commit, so the existing nodes stay mounted.

The new branch is gated on the recoverable digest, so an ordinary error fallback still client-renders through the previous path. I checked that this gate matters: loosening it makes the existing "extra node inside Suspense fallback" hydration warning tests fail.

### Test plan

- Added a regression test that calls `use(browser())`, suspends on a client promise, and asserts the fallback keeps node identity (plus an attribute set on it before hydration). It fails on main and passes with the fix.
- Ran `ReactDOMFizzServer-test`, `ReactDOMServerPartialHydration-test` (including the Activity variant), `ReactDOMHydrationDiff-test`, `ReactDOMServerSuspense-test`, `ReactDOMFizzShellHydration-test`, the SuspenseList/SuspensePlaceholder/Activity/Offscreen suites, and the full `ReactDOM` suite - 3335+ passing. The three `__DEV__ is not defined` stack-depth failures fail the same way on unmodified main, so they aren't from this change.
- `yarn flow dom-node`: no errors. Prettier: clean.

title: [Fizz] Resume stack overflow recovery from the frame that reset the output
body:
## Summary

`renderNode` recovers from `Maximum call stack size exceeded` by resetting the segment's write pointers to the checkpoint it took on entry and spawning a continuation task. The continuation starts from `task.node`, the deepest node `renderNodeDestructive` stashed. That matches the checkpoint only when the innermost `renderNode` frame is the one that catches.

Close to the stack limit, the catch block itself can overflow while it spawns the continuation. The error then escapes to the next `renderNode` frame up, which resets the output to its own, shallower checkpoint but still spawns the continuation from the deepest `task.node`. Everything written between the two frames is dropped: host open and close tags, and the `useId` tree positions with them. Nothing errors and the HTML stays well-formed, it is just missing elements, and hydration mismatches.

In optimized code this happens in runs, because several adjacent frames fail their catch before one succeeds. A 200-level chain of `Context.Provider` → `<section id={useId()}>` renders 196 of 200 sections with the development build on Node 22 and 195 on Node 26. The production build has smaller frames and does not overflow at that depth, but it loses nodes the same way once it does: 188 of 200 with `--stack-size=256`, 1188 of 1200 for a 1200-level chain with the default stack. 19.3.1 and `main` behave the same.

The render path of `renderNode` now resumes from its own `node` and `childIndex` with the context it snapshotted on entry, and pushes the component stack frame for that node the way `renderNodeDestructive` would have, since `retryNode` does not. `task.row` joins that snapshot because `renderSuspenseListRows` does not restore it on the throw path. The replay path keeps resuming from `task.node`: nothing is written during replay, and `replayElement` splices consumed replay nodes while the error unwinds, so re-walking from the outer frame's node would not find them again.

`createRenderTask` and `createReplayTask` now bump the pending counters after the task exists and is in the abort set. They run inside that catch block, and when constructing the task overflowed after the counters were incremented, the request waited forever for a task that was never scheduled. The new test hit this as a hang when it ran after the other deep tree tests in the file.

This is separate from #36977, which retries a task in `retryRenderTask` once `task.node` advanced. That path still applies when an overflow escapes every `renderNode` frame, and `task.node` then points at the outermost frame that reset the output.

The existing deep tree test nests 1200 function components with no host elements between frames, so there was nothing to lose between a checkpoint and the resume node, and it only asserts on the leaf.

## How did you test this change?

Added `preserves host elements and ids when recovering from stack overflow in very deep trees` to `ReactDOMFizzServer-test`: 1200 levels of `<section id={useId()}>`, asserting the element count, their order and that every id is unique. On `main` it fails with 1187 of 1200 sections in DEV and 1185 with `--prod` (Node 20.19.0). Run after the other stack overflow tests in the same file, `main` hangs instead and writes nothing, which is the counter leak above; with only the counter reorder applied it fails with 1187 again.

With the fix, on Node 20.19.0 and 22.23.3:

title: [compiler] Fix catch clause bindings captured in nested lambdas
body:
## Summary

When a `catch (e)` clause parameter is captured inside a nested function/lambda (e.g. `try { ... } catch (e) { foo(() => e); }`), `BuildHIR`'s `BlockStatement` lowering previously included the `CatchClause` binding in `hoistableIdentifiers` / `hoistable` (since in Babel the `CatchClause` body block shares the `CatchClause` scope where `e` has `binding.kind === 'let'`). Because the `catch` binding is declared in the `CatchClause` header rather than inside the block's statement list, visiting the nested function before seeing a declaration inside the block caused `BuildHIR` to emit a spurious `DeclareContext` (`HoistedLet`) for `e` even when `e` was not a context variable (`StoreLocal` + `LoadLocal`), triggering an invariant failure in `ValidateContextVariableLValues`:

`Invariant: Expected all references to a variable to be consistently local or context references`

This PR fixes the issue in both the TypeScript compiler (`BuildHIR.ts`) and the Rust port (`build_hir.rs`):
1. Excludes `CatchClause` bindings (`!binding.path.isCatchClause()` in TS and `b.declaration_type != "CatchClause"` in Rust) from `hoistableIdentifiers` / `hoistable` during `BlockStatement` lowering, as catch parameters are always initialized at the start of the catch handler before its body executes.
2. Normalizes `InstructionKind.Catch` to `InstructionKind.Let` when emitting `StoreContext` in `lowerAssignment` / `lower_assignment` so that catch parameters that are both reassigned and captured by inner closures are properly lowered as context variables without triggering `Unexpected context variable kind`.
3. Renames `error.bug-context-variable-catch-in-lambda` and `error.bug-invariant-local-or-context-references` (removing the `error.bug-` prefix), updates their snapshots, and adds `context-variable-catch-reassigned-in-lambda`.

## How did you test this change?

- `cd compiler && yarn snap` (1833/1833 passed)
- `cd compiler && yarn snap --rust` (1833/1833 passed)
- `cd compiler && bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh HIR` (1832/1832 passed, 1738/1738 per-pass HIR parity)
- `cd compiler && bash scripts/test-e2e.sh packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/context-variable-catch-in-lambda.js`
- `cd compiler && bash scripts/test-e2e.sh packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/context-variable-catch-reassigned-in-lambda.js`
- `cd compiler && bash scripts/test-e2e.sh packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/bug-invariant-local-or-context-references.js`

title: [ReactDOM] Fix TypeError in prefetchDNS when called with null or prototype-less options
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37885

In `packages/react-dom/src/shared/ReactDOMFloat.js`, `prefetchDNS` checks whether the second argument (`options`) is an object with a `crossOrigin` property using `typeof options === 'object' && options.hasOwnProperty('crossOrigin')`.

Because `typeof null === 'object'`, passing `null` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'hasOwnProperty')`. Passing `Object.create(null)` throws `TypeError: options.hasOwnProperty is not a function`.

This PR:
1. Guards against `null` with `options != null`.
2. Uses `shared/hasOwnProperty` to safely check for property existence on objects without prototype chains.

title: Fix ViewTransition crash in ShadowRoot container
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37765

When a root is mounted on a `ShadowRoot`, `containerInstance` in `restoreRootViewTransitionName` is a `DocumentFragment` rather than an `Element`. Because `ShadowRoot` does not implement `ElementCSSInlineStyle`, reading `containerInstance.style.viewTransitionName` throws a `TypeError`. This crashes passive effect cleanup and prevents `documentElement.style.viewTransitionName` from being reset back to `''`.

This guards `containerInstance.style != null` before reading `viewTransitionName`, allowing `ShadowRoot` roots to restore the document's transition name cleanly.

## How did you test this change?

Added a regression test in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js` verifying that rendering and toggling a `ViewTransition` inside a `ShadowRoot` container mounts, commits updates, and resets `document.documentElement.style.viewTransitionName` without throwing. Verified with `yarn test ReactDOMViewTransition` and `yarn linc`.

title: Fix form action replay when a field is named "action"
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37837

In HTML forms, form controls with `name="action"` (such as `<button name="action">` or `<input name="action">`) shadow the `form.action` DOM property via named element getters on `HTMLFormElement`.

In `listenToFormSubmissionsForReplaying` (`ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetShared.js`), `let action = form.action` caused `action` to evaluate to the shadowing element instead of the form's action URL string. As a result:
- The check `action !== EXPECTED_FORM_ACTION_URL` evaluated to `true`.
- `event.preventDefault()` was never called.
- The submit event was not queued into `root['$$reactFormReplay']`.
- In browsers, the form navigated to the `javascript:` placeholder URL, throwing `Uncaught Error: React form unexpectedly submitted.`

This PR updates `listenToFormSubmissionsForReplaying` to read `form.getAttribute('action')` instead of `form.action`. This matches how `submitter.getAttribute('formAction')` is already handled and avoids named property shadowing.

The compiled instruction string in `ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetInlineCodeStrings.js` was updated via `yarn generate-inline-fizz-runtime`.

## How did you test this change?

1. Added two regression tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js`:
  - `should replay a form action after hydration when a field is named "action"`
  - `should replay a form action after hydration when a button is named "action"`
2. Verified that without the fix, both tests fail with `Navigate to: [object HTMLButtonElement]` / `[object HTMLInputElement]`, and with the fix, all 17 tests in `ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js` pass in both development and production (`yarn test --prod ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js`).
3. Ran `yarn test packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMForm-test.js` (45 passed).
4. Ran `yarn linc` (0 errors).

title: [Flight Reply] Decode FormData part ids as hex
body:
## Summary

A `FormData` passed to a Server Action is deserialized as an **empty** `FormData` whenever its part id is 10 or higher, silently dropping every field.

The wire format is `$K<id>` with `id` in hex, like every other reference in the protocol. But the backing entries are written by the client under `<formFieldPrefix>_<refId>_<key>`, where `refId` is interpolated as a **decimal** number:

```js
// react-client/src/ReactFlightReplyClient.js
const refId = nextPartId++;
const prefix = formFieldPrefix + '_' + refId + '_';
value.forEach((originalValue, originalKey) => {
  data.append(prefix + originalKey, originalValue);
});
return serializeFormDataReference(refId); // '$K' + refId.toString(16)
```

`parseModelString` then used the raw hex substring as the key prefix instead of converting it back:

```js
const stringId = value.slice(2);
const formPrefix = response._prefix + '_' + stringId + '_';
```

The two representations only agree below 10, so for any id >= 10 the lookup matches nothing. `consumeBackingEntries` returns an empty `FormData` and, because it doesn't advance the cursor, the entries are left behind for the rest of the reply.

Every other id-carrying branch in the same function already decodes hex before building a backing key — `parseTypedArray` (`parseInt(reference.slice(2), 16)`), `'B'` (`parseInt(value.slice(2), 16)`), `getOutlinedModel` (`parseInt(path[0], 16)`) and `getChunk` (takes a `number`). `'K'` was the only exception.

This is reachable from `encodeReply` whenever ten or more parts are outlined before the `FormData` (promises, `Blob`s, typed arrays, iterators, other `FormData`s...), and from bound Server Actions whose bound arguments include one.

## Test

Added a case to `ReactFlightDOMReply-test.js` that outlines nine promises first, so the `FormData` becomes part 10 — the first id whose hex form differs from its decimal form. Failing output before the fix:

```
● ReactFlightDOMReply › can pass FormData after at least ten outlined parts

  expect(received).toEqual(expected) // deep equality

  - Expected  - 6
  + Received  + 1

  - Array [
  -  Array [
  -  "hello",
  -  "world",
  -  ],
  - ]
  + Array []
```

## Verification

- `ReactFlightDOMReply` (webpack / Node / Edge), `ReactFlightDOMForm`, `ReactFlightTurbopackDOMReply`, `ReactFlightDOMNode` — all pass on `experimental`, plus `-r=stable` and `--prod` for the reply suites.
- `yarn linc` and `prettier check-changed` clean.
- No overlap with #37822, which touches `parseTypedArray` further down the same file and adds its tests earlier in the same `describe` block.

title: Fix false positive duplicate name warning when ViewTransition name changes
body:
Fixes #37866

### Problem

When a mounted `<ViewTransition>` updates its `name` prop to another string or to `undefined`, `mountedNamedViewTransitions` does not remove the previous name. If another `<ViewTransition>` later mounts with that earlier name while the first component remains in the DOM, `trackNamedViewTransition` reports a false-positive duplicate name warning (`"There are two <ViewTransition name=...> components with the same name mounted at the same time."`).

### Solution

1. In `updateViewTransition` (`ReactFiberBeginWork.js`), keep `ViewTransitionNamedStatic` in DEV when transitioning from a named component so `commitLayoutEffects` still runs `trackNamedViewTransition`, and clear the static flag once `memoizedProps` has dropped the name.
2. In `trackNamedViewTransition` and `untrackNamedViewTransition` (`ReactFiberDuplicateViewTransitions.js`), check `fiber.alternate` to remove the previous name from `mountedNamedViewTransitions` when `name` changes.

### Testing

Added tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js`:
- Verified that switching `name` from `"cover-1"` to `"cover-2"` or `undefined` allows subsequent mounts with `"cover-1"` or `"cover-2"` without warnings.
- Verified that simultaneously mounting two `<ViewTransition name="duplicate">` components continues to trigger the expected duplicate warning.

title: Fix pre-hydration form replay when a field is named "action"
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37837.

When a form contains a control (such as `<button name="action">` or `<input name="action">`), HTMLFormElement exposes that control on `form.action`, shadowing the standard action property.

During server rendering with a function action, React renders a placeholder `javascript:throw new Error('React form unexpectedly submitted.')` URL on the form's `action` attribute. When the form was submitted prior to hydration, `listenToFormSubmissionsForReplaying` checked:

```js
let action = form.action;
...
if (action !== EXPECTED_FORM_ACTION_URL) {
  return;
}
```

Because `form.action` returned the shadowed DOM element rather than the action URL string, the equality check failed. Consequently:
1. `event.preventDefault()` was never called.
2. The submission was never queued into `$$reactFormReplay`.
3. The browser attempted native navigation to the placeholder `javascript:` URL, throwing `Uncaught Error: React form unexpectedly submitted.` and dropping the submission.

This change reads `form.getAttribute('action')` instead of `form.action`, matching how `submitter.getAttribute('formAction')` is handled.

## How did you test this change?

- Added regression tests in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js` for `<button name="action">` and `<input name="action">` before hydration.
- Verified that both tests fail without the fix (`Navigate to: [object HTMLButtonElement]` and `[object HTMLInputElement]`) and pass with the fix.
- Ran tests in development and production modes:
  - `yarn test packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js` (17 passed)
  - `yarn test --prod packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizzForm-test.js` (17 passed)

title: Allow resumeAndPrerender to postpone an existing boundary again
body:
`resumeAndPrerender` fails when the same already emitted Suspense boundary needs to postpone again. This predates #37853: prerendering a suspended boundary, aborting, resuming it while it still suspends, and aborting again hits the missing postponement metadata even when both aborts happen outside rendering.

Initialize tracking for resumed boundaries and preserve the boundary ID already referenced by the emitted HTML. When a pass finishes with postponed holes, flush completed segments as partial output and retain the fallback until a later resume completes the boundary.

Switch the full-flow regression from #37853 from `it.failing` to `it`, asserting prerender → resumeAndPrerender → final resume, intermediate HTML, JSON round trips, and removal of placeholders. Add a regression using external aborts to directly cover the existing API bug. Also verify that one resumed boundary can complete while a sibling aborts and postpones again, both at the root and through an already completed Suspense ancestor.

Follow-up to the merged #37853. This PR contains only the resumeAndPrerender fix and its regression tests.

The browser prerender suite passes in development and production on stable and experimental channels. ESLint and Prettier pass.

title: [DOM] Fix crash when a form control or id is named `nodeName`
body:
## Summary

A `<form>` exposes its named controls as properties that override its built-in ones ([spec](<url>)), and `window` exposes elements by `id` ([spec](<url>)). So `<input name="nodeName">` makes `form.nodeName` that input, and `<div id="nodeName">` makes `window.nodeName` that div. React calls `nodeName.toLowerCase()` on the event target (or `window` when there's no target instance), which throws:

```
TypeError: elem.nodeName.toLowerCase is not a function
```

- Events targeting such a form aren't dispatched, so `onSubmit` doesn't run and the browser submits natively. If any element on the page has `id="nodeName"`, the same happens to events targeting the root container, e.g. `onMouseEnter` when the pointer moves from the container onto a child.
- Every commit throws while such a form has focus (`hasSelectionCapabilities`).
- Hydrating such a form fails and React client renders instead (`canHydrateInstance`).

A non-string `nodeName` only occurs on a form, `window` or `document`, none of which is a form control, so `ChangeEventPlugin`, `isTextInputElement` and `hasSelectionCapabilities` now treat it as not matching. During hydration it can only be a `<form>`. This keeps the existing checks rather than `instanceof`, which fails for nodes from other frames (#6311, #10076).

Fixes #6284
Fixes #23324

## How did you test this change?

Added tests for each case, all failing on `main`: `ChangeEventPlugin-test.js` (form `onSubmit`, `onMouseEnter` from the root container), `ReactDOM-test.js` (update while the form is focused) and `ReactServerRenderingHydration-test.js` (hydration, and the DEV mismatch diff). jsdom implements named properties on `window` but not on forms, so the form tests define `nodeName` on the form the way browsers expose it.

In Chromium 149 and Firefox 155, all four cases fail with react-dom 19.3.0-canary and pass with these changes applied to it.

- `yarn test`, plus `yarn test --prod`, `yarn test-stable`, `yarn test-www` and `yarn test-classic` (both variants) on `packages/react-dom`
- `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier-check`, `yarn flow-ci` for every renderer

title: Fix ViewTransition crash when root container is a ShadowRoot
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37765.

When React mounts inside a `ShadowRoot`, `restoreRootViewTransitionName` treats `rootContainer` as `containerInstance`. Unlike standard DOM elements, a `ShadowRoot` does not have a `style` property (`containerInstance.style` is `undefined`).

Evaluating `containerInstance.style.viewTransitionName === 'root'` threw an unhandled `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'viewTransitionName')`. This interrupted passive effect execution and prevented subsequent cleanup from running (`documentElement.style.viewTransitionName = ''`), leaving `viewTransitionName: none` stuck on `<html>` and breaking future root transitions.

This change checks `containerInstance.style != null` before reading `viewTransitionName`, allowing cleanup to complete cleanly when the root is hosted inside a `ShadowRoot`.

## How did you test this change?

- Added unit test in `packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js` (`does not throw when container is a ShadowRoot`) reproducing the unhandled error.
- Verified test failure before fix and success after fix:
  - `yarn test ReactDOMViewTransition --watchman=false` (27/27 passed)
  - `yarn test ReactDOMViewTransition --prod --watchman=false` (27/27 passed)
  - `yarn linc` passed with 0 errors.

title: Fix false positive duplicate ViewTransition warning on name change
body:
## Summary

fix(react): close children iterators when mapping throws (#37427)
body:
## Summary

`React.Children.map` (and the other `React.Children` helpers that share the same traversal) iterates over non-array, non-element children using the iterator protocol. If the mapping callback throws, the error escaped the `while` loop in `mapIntoArray` without ever calling `iterator.return()`, so generators with cleanup in `finally` blocks (and other iterables with resource-release logic) were never closed.

This fixes #37427 by wrapping the iteration loop in a try/catch: when an error is thrown while processing a yielded child, the iterator is closed once (defensively, in case `return()` itself throws) and the original error is re-thrown.

## How did you test this change?

Added two regression tests to `packages/react/src/__tests__/ReactChildren-test.js`:

1. A generator function with a `finally` block that sets a flag; `React.Children.map` with a callback that throws. The test asserts the original error is thrown **and** that the generator's cleanup ran.
2. A custom iterable object with a `return()` method on its iterator; same assertions.

Both tests fail on `main` (cleanup flag stays `false`) and pass with this change.

```

Tests:  44 passed, 44 total

title: [Fizz] Restore view-transition-class after a Suspense reveal
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37652.

When a streamed Suspense boundary is revealed with a view transition, `$RV` temporarily overrides `view-transition-name` and `view-transition-class` on the affected elements, and pushes `[element, previousName, previousClass]` onto `restoreQueue`. The restore loop in `transition.ready.finally` read the previous class from `restoreQueue[i + 1]` (the name slot) instead of `restoreQueue[i + 2]`, so after the reveal an element's `view-transition-class` ended up holding its `view-transition-name` value.

This changes the index to `i + 2` and regenerates `ReactDOMFizzInstructionSetInlineCodeStrings.js` with `yarn generate-inline-fizz-runtime`. The generated diff is the same one-character change.

## How did you test this change?

Added a regression test to `ReactDOMFizzViewTransition-test.js`. It gives the fallback an authored name and class, reveals the boundary, and then checks that both values are restored.

- Without the fix, the new test fails with the exact symptom from the issue:
  ```
  Expected: "authored-class"
  Received: "authored-name"
  ```
- With the fix:
  - `yarn test ReactDOMFizz`: 13 suites, 347 tests passed
  - `yarn test -r=www-modern --variant=true ReactDOMFizzViewTransition`: passed
  - `yarn test --prod ReactDOMFizzViewTransition`: passed

title: [react-refresh] Clean up helpersByRoot when a root unmounts before its first render commits (#37804)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37804.

When a root is unmounted before its initial render commits (for example during StrictMode effect double-invocation in development), `onCommitFiberRoot` enters the `!wasMounted && !isMounted` branch.

Previously, `helpersByRoot.set(root, helpers)` was called unconditionally at the beginning of `onCommitFiberRoot`, but was only deleted in the `wasMounted && !isMounted` branch. In the `!wasMounted && !isMounted` branch without errors, the entry was retained indefinitely in `helpersByRoot`, preventing garbage collection of the root and its container DOM nodes.

This change deletes the root from `helpersByRoot` when `!wasMounted && !isMounted` and `!didError`.

## How did you test this code?

Ran `yarn test ReactFreshIntegration` (86 tests passed, including the new regression test verifying that an early-unmounted root is cleaned up from tracked root entries).

title: [Flight] Mark anonymous async frames as async in parsed stack traces
body:
## Summary

`parseStackTrace`'s string fallback decides whether a frame is an async resume with

```js
let isAsync = parsed[8] === 'async ';
```

but `frameRegExp` has no eighth capture group:

```js
/^ {3} at (?:(.+) \((?:(.+):(\d+):(\d+)|\<anonymous\>)\)|(?:async )?(.+):(\d+):(\d+)|\<anonymous\>)$/
```

Groups 1–4 belong to `at name (file:line:column)` and groups 5–7 to the nameless `at file:line:column`, so `parsed[8]` is always `undefined` and that branch is dead. It came in with #33739, and the regexp has had seven groups since it was written.

That leaves the second V8 async format undetected. V8 has two:

```
  at async outerName (/tmp/app.js:2:29)  // named: the name group carries `async `
  at async /tmp/app.js:2:16  // nameless: no name to hang it off of
```

The nameless form is what an async function without a name of its own prints, e.g. an anonymous async arrow that awaits a rejecting call:

```
$ node -e 'async function inner(){await null;throw new Error("boom")}
(async () => { await inner(); })().catch(e=>console.log(e.stack))'
Error: boom
  at inner (/private/tmp/asy6.js:1:43)
  at async /private/tmp/asy6.js:2:16
```

The regexp already consumes the `async ` prefix of that form, but it is written as a non-capturing group, and capturing it there would shift groups 5–7 (which are used for the filename, line and column of the same alternative), so the prefix is read off the frame instead. The `name.startsWith('async ')` branch no longer needs to set the flag by hand, since it covers the same frames.

This is not purely cosmetic: `ReactFlightServer.hasUnfilteredFrame` deliberately skips async frames ("they're not 'real'") when deciding whether an I/O entry's Promise was created in first party code, which is the whole point of #33739, and the flag is also part of the frames sent to the client.

`packages/react-devtools-shared/src/backend/utils/parseStackTrace.js` is a copy of this parser and has the same dead check, so it gets the same fix.

## How did you test this change?

I added a case to `ReactFlightStackConfigV8-test` that pins the nameless form. Against `main` it fails with the flag reporting `false`:

```
  ● ReactFlightStackConfigV8 › marks an anonymous async frame as async in an already formatted stack

  -  true,
  +  false,
```

With the fix it passes, next to the existing named-form case.

- `ReactFlightStackConfigV8`, `ReactFlightServer` and `ReactFlightAsyncDebugInfo` pass. The single failing snapshot in `ReactFlightAsyncDebugInfo` (a `enableComponentPerformanceTrack` timing) fails on `main` in this environment too, verified by re-running the suite with the production change stashed.
- `linc` and `prettier` are clean on all four changed files.
- I could not run the DevTools project tests locally because they require `--build`; the change there is the same parser, and its new case asserts the same input shape as the server one.

title: ci: add npmscan dependency security check
body:
### What does this PR do?
Integrates `npmscan-action` as a non-blocking supply-chain security check on Pull Requests.

`npmscan` checks incoming PRs for:
- Lockfile overrides that could pull in malicious transitive dependencies
- Unexpected new `postinstall` scripts
- Tarball swaps and checksum mismatches

### Why?
Supply-chain attacks (like the recent ChainDrop and malicious axios typosquats) often sneak in via lockfile updates in otherwise benign PRs. This check helps reviewers spot those anomalies automatically.

### Configuration Notes
- **Non-blocking**: Configured with `mode: warn` and `fail-on-error: false`. It will only post a warning annotation if an issue is found and will **never fail the CI build**, ensuring it doesn't disrupt your workflow.
- **Immutable Action**: The action is pinned to a specific commit SHA (`de14168f65640a4ed1f0e82ad3ad8c80483d360d`) rather than a floating tag, following security best practices.

title: Preserve the rendered shell on synchronous prerender abort
body:
#37709 showed that a synchronous prerender abort can discard a retried task's rendered shell, then resume only an inner slot. #37710 addressed the missing markup by postponing the whole task, but that could overlap replay paths from child tasks; #37852 reverted that approach.

Preserve the parent segment and continue rendering its text and host elements after abort. When a component or other render callback returns after abort, discard its children and track a postponed hole at that node. This includes function and class components, lazy and forward-ref components, Context.Consumer render props, iterables, and thenables. Already-created arrays are read normally; getters and host prop serialization follow React's render-purity rules. SuspenseList rows use the same postponement path and existing row task bookkeeping.

Preserve individual holes only while rendering an unfinished Suspense boundary. Tasks without a blocked boundary unwind through the existing root abort path: a postponed root cannot flush any shell and must render again in full. Tests cover root aborts during the initial render, in a retried child, and during a subsequent resumeAndPrerender, followed by a complete final resume.

This restores the tests from #37710, #37850, and #37851 and adds coverage for indexed retries, static host children after abort, iterators and thenables, forward refs, render-phase updates, nested fallbacks, and SuspenseList rows. A full-flow regression for repeated aborts during resumeAndPrerender is marked `it.failing`: it exposes an existing bug in postponing an already emitted boundary, fixed separately in #37876.

The browser prerender suite passes in development and production on stable and experimental channels, including the expected failure. ESLint and Prettier pass.

title: Revert sync abort replay restoration pending a complete fix
body:
Revert #37710 and #37850 while we revisit how synchronous prerender aborts preserve replay state.

Restoring the aborted task root as a replay point can overlap postpones from child tasks. #37850 suppresses one form of the overlap, but an indexed parent slot can still coexist with a descendant replay node and fail during resumption. This removes the incomplete change so we can address the replay invariants together.

This deliberately restores the behavior reported in #37709: if a prerender abort interrupts a task after it has rendered part of its shell, the later resume can omit that markup. That regression needs a follow-up fix.

This supersedes #37851.

Tests: `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --runInBand` and `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStaticBrowser --prod --runInBand` (34 passed in each mode).

title: Prune descendant replay paths after a parent postpone
body:
Follow-up to #37850. Extracting the suspended and aborting children into a component still leaves a nested child replay path beneath a Suspense boundary whose whole content was postponed. Resume rerenders that content but then finds the stale child path, reports a replay mismatch, and leaves the fallback visible.

When recording a whole-content replay slot, clear descendant replay paths already tracked and avoid attaching later paths beneath it. The new regression test wraps the children in a component and verifies that both render after resume.

Tests:
- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStatic --runInBand` (60 passed)
- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzStatic --prod --runInBand` (60 passed)
- `yarn test ReactDOMFizzSuspenseList --runInBand` (13 passed)
- `yarn linc`

title: Fix overlapping replay slots after a prerender abort
body:
## Summary

A prerender can abort during a retry after the retried task has spawned a suspended child. Abort cleanup records a replay slot for the whole task, then tries to record a child slot at the same key path. Resuming the parent already renders that child, so the existing assertion turns a resumable abort into a prerender error. This surfaced after the abort unwind change in #37710.

Keep the parent slot and ignore the redundant child slot. The regression test verifies that both children render after resuming.

title: Do not select the first option in list box <select> with unmatched value
body:
## Summary

When a controlled `<select>` renders as a list box (`size > 1`) and the `value` does not match any `<option>`, `updateOptions` fell back to selecting the first non-disabled option on every render. List boxes are allowed to have no selection (the browser leaves nothing highlighted in that case), so the fallback should only apply to dropdowns.

This fixes `<select size="2" value="not-an-option">` incorrectly selecting the first option (and re-selecting it on every re-render).

## Details

`ReactDOMSelect.updateOptions` collects the first non-disabled option as a fallback target when no option matches the controlled value. This behavior is correct for dropdowns (the browser itself auto-selects the first option there), but wrong for list boxes, where an empty selection is a valid state.

The fix gates the fallback on `node.size <= 1`, so dropdowns keep the existing behavior and list boxes honor the unmatched value by leaving nothing selected.

## Test plan

- Added two regression tests in `ReactDOMSelect-test.js`:
  - `size > 1` with an unmatched `value`: no option is selected (mount and re-render), `selectedIndex === -1`
  - `size > 1` with a matching `value`: the matching option is selected
- `yarn test ReactDOMSelect-test` — 63 passed
- `yarn test ReactDOMOption-test ReactDOMSelect` — 77 passed (3 suites)
- ESLint on changed files — passed

Fixes #24469

title: [DevTools] Stop polling the backend manager from the content script
body:
## Summary

Fixes #27992.

The proxy content script runs on every page and posted `{source: 'react-devtools-content-script', hello: true}` to the page every 500ms until a backend initialized. The backend manager is only injected once DevTools is opened on a page with React, so on every other page the extension kept posting messages, and any page listening to `message` events received them for as long as it stayed open.

The polling was there for the case where the content script is injected before the backend manager. That case is now covered by the `backend-manager-injected` message: the backend manager announces itself when it's injected, and the content script answers with a hello. So a single hello when the content script is injected is enough in either order:

- Content script first: its hello finds no listener, then the backend manager announces itself and gets a hello back.
- Backend manager first: its announcement finds no listener, then the content script's hello reaches it.

This removes the interval and the `backendInitialized` bookkeeping that only existed to stop it, and updates the comment in `backendManager.js` to match.

## How did you test this change?

- I ran a temporary Jest test (not included in this PR) that loads `proxy.js` and `backendManager.js` in jsdom with a mocked `chrome` API. With this change, the backend manager is welcomed in both injection orders, and the content script posts one hello in 10 seconds when there is no backend manager. The same test on `main` posts 21 hellos in that time, and both injection orders also work there.
- `yarn test --build --project devtools --release-channel=experimental packages/react-devtools-extensions`: 2/2 pass. `ignoreList-test.js` builds the extension in development and production modes.
- `yarn flow dom-browser` passes, and ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.

I didn't test it in a real browser.

title: [DevTools] Release host instances deleted from a still-mounted component
body:
## Summary Fixes #37802. With the React DevTools extension installed, DOM nodes that React removes from a component that stays mounted are kept alive by DevTools until the page reloads, even when DevTools is never opened. Examples are a component that swaps a keyed ``, or one that conditionally shows one. `publicInstanceToDevToolsInstanceMap` gets an entry for every host fiber on mount. Host fibers are filtered by default, so they have no DevTools instance of their own and are never in `remainingReconcilingChildren`. Their entries are only released from `untrackFiber`, which runs when the nearest tracked instance unmounts and only walks that fiber's current children. A host fiber deleted while its owner stays mounted is never visited, so its entry keeps the detached node and its subtree. This change releases the filtered fibers in `nextFiber.deletions` while reconciling the parent, using the existing `untrackFiber`, which also covers filtered descendants of the deleted subtree. Tracked instances in a deleted subtree are still unmounted through the remaining set as before. The release is skipped when `prevFiber === nextFiber`, so a stale `deletions` array from an earlier commit is never read. ## How did you test this change? I added a test to `store-test.js`. It replaces a keyed `
` in a mounted component, then removes it, and checks that `agent.getIDForHostInstance` no longer resolves the removed nodes. Without the fix it fails: the removed `
` still resolves to the mounted component. - `yarn build-for-devtools && yarn test --build --project devtools --release-channel=experimental`: everything passes except the two `ignoreList-test.js` cases, which shell out to `yarn build:chrome` and fail in my local setup for unrelated reasons. - `yarn flow dom-node` passes, and ESLint and Prettier pass on the changed files.

title: [Fizz] Read the action attribute when replaying form submissions
body:
Fixes #37837

## Summary

Before hydration, the inline Fizz runtime catches submits of forms with a function action and queues them for replay. It recognizes those forms by comparing `form.action` to the `javascript:` placeholder. A field named `action` shadows `form.action`, so the check fails, the browser runs the placeholder URL and the submit is lost.

The listener now reads the attribute with `Element.prototype.getAttribute.call(form, 'action')`. Calling `form.getAttribute` directly breaks the same way with a field named `getAttribute`.

## How did you test this change?

The first commit adds a test that covers the current behavior and passes on `main`. JSDOM doesn't implement named properties on forms, so the test defines `action` and `getAttribute` on the form. It removes the `getAttribute` one before hydrating, since hydration diffing in DEV calls `form.getAttribute` too. The second commit is the fix and flips the assertion.

The test fails with the runtime on `main` (`undefined`) and with a version that calls `form.getAttribute` directly (`TypeError`).

- `yarn test` and `yarn test --prod` for `ReactDOMFizzForm`, at both commits
- `-r=stable`, `-r=www-modern` and `-r=www-classic` for `ReactDOMFizzForm`
- `yarn test packages/react-dom/src/__tests__/ReactDOMFizz`: 348 passed
- `yarn generate-inline-fizz-runtime`: no diff
- `yarn flow dom-node`, `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier`: clean

I also ran the inline runtime in Chrome 152 with a field named `title`, `action` or `getAttribute`. On `main` the `action` case throws and nothing is queued. With this change all three are queued.

title: [compiler] Assign hoisted function declarations that escape their scope
body:
## Summary Fixes #37833. When a nested function declaration gets the hoisted flag but no real reference to it survives (a `typeof fn` type annotation, or a closure that is never called), the compiler doesn't bail out. It still declares `let fn;` outside the memo block, but `PruneHoistedContexts` left the `StoreContext` as a `Function` kind, so codegen emitted a block-scoped `function fn() {}` inside the `if`. That inner declaration shadows the outer `let`, so `fn` is `undefined` on every cache miss. `PruneHoistedContexts` already rewrites `let`/`const` stores declared by a scope into reassignments. This does the same for the hoisted function once its definition is reached, so the output becomes `fn = function fn() {}`, which matches the non-hoisted case. The Rust port gets the same one-line change. ## How did you test this change? Added `hoisted-function-declaration-escapes-scope.js`. Without the fix its eval output is `
{}
` (the prop is `undefined`). With the fix it is `
{"onClick":"[[ function params=0 ]]"}
`. I also checked both repros from the issue with `yarn snap compile`. - `yarn snap`: 1829 passed - `yarn snap --rust`: 1829 passed - `bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh`: 1828 passed, 0 failed - `yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler jest` and `lint`, `cargo fmt --check`

title: [DevTools] Keep x_react_sources metadata aligned with sources
body:
## Summary

Named hooks reads React metadata out of the extended source map fields. For `x_react_sources` it skipped the nulls before walking the array:

```js
const reactMetadataArray = sourcemap[REACT_SOURCES_EXTENSION_KEY];
reactMetadataArray.filter(Boolean).forEach(updateMap);
```

`updateMap(metadata, sourceIndex)` uses that index to look up `basicMap.sources[sourceIndex]`. Filtering compacts the array, so the index it receives no longer points at the source the entry describes — every entry after the first null is attributed to the source that many positions earlier.

The field is defined as an array that lines up with `sources` (`ReactSourcesArray` = `$ReadOnlyArray<?ReactSourceMetadata>` in `SourceMapTypes.js`), so a null entry simply means "this source has no React metadata". The `x_facebook_sources` branch a few lines below carries the same information in a different shape and keeps the index while skipping nulls:

```js
fbMetadataArray.forEach((fbMetadata, sourceIndex) => {
  const reactMetadata = fbMetadata != null ? fbMetadata[REACT_METADATA_INDEX_IN_FB_METADATA] : null;
  if (reactMetadata != null) {
  updateMap(reactMetadata, sourceIndex);
  }
});
```

So the two fields currently disagree about which source a metadata entry belongs to. This change walks `x_react_sources` with `forEach` and keeps the index, matching the sibling branch. When the array has no nulls the two implementations pass identical arguments, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

## How did you test this change?

I added `SourceMapMetadataConsumer-test.js`, which is the first unit test for this class. It builds a two-source map where only the second source has metadata:

```js
x_react_sources: [null, [{names: ['useState'], mappings: ''}]],
```

Before the change the metadata is attributed to `src/a.ts`:

```
● SourceMapMetadataConsumer › assigns metadata to the source at the same index when an entry is null
  expect(received).toBe(expected) // Object.is equality
  Expected: false
  Received: true
  27 |  expect(consumer.hasHookMap('src/a.ts')).toBe(false);
```

After the change both assertions hold. The suite also asserts the same scenario through `x_facebook_sources`, so the two fields are pinned to the same behaviour.

- New suite: `node ./scripts/jest/jest.js --config ./scripts/jest/config.source.js SourceMapMetadataConsumer --runInBand` → 2 passed. (I ran this through the OSS source config because the `devtools` jest project needs `yarn build-for-devtools`; the test itself is picked up by that project's `testRegex`.)
- The existing `x_react_sources` fixtures in `updateMockSourceMaps.js` are single-element arrays with no nulls, so their compiled maps are unaffected.
- `yarn prettier-check`, `yarn linc`: clean.

title: [compiler] Compile tagged templates with interpolations
body:
Fixes #35029.

## What was going wrong

A tagged template with an interpolation, such as `` css`color: ${color}` ``, stopped HIR lowering with `Handle tagged template with interpolations`. That `UnsupportedNode` skips the rest of the component. A `setState` call inside an effect in the same function was then not reported, so `set-state-in-effect` went silent whenever any interpolated tag was present. Tags with no interpolation, such as `graphql\`...\``, already compiled.

## Why this shape

`TemplateLiteral` already lowers each interpolation to a temporary and keeps the quasis as raw/cooked pairs. A tagged template is that same literal plus a callee. Extending `TaggedTemplateExpression` to `{tag, subexprs, quasis}` lets the existing operand visitors treat the interpolations as inputs, so `` tag`hello ${name}` `` is memoized on `name` and still calls `tag`.

The other bailout in the same function stays: a quasi whose cooked value differs from its raw value is still unsupported. That is a separate TODO, and this change does not take it.

## How it works

`BuildHIR` lowers the tag first, then each interpolation, and stores every quasi. Visitors yield and rename `subexprs` next to the tag. Codegen emits `templateElement`s and the interpolation expressions, the same way it already emits a template literal. `PruneNonEscapingScopes` already reads operands from those visitors, so the interpolated values become reactive-scope inputs without a separate change there.

Before, the component bailed out and the effect rule did not run. After, the same component compiles and logs `EffectSetState`. A component that returns `` tag`hello ${name}` `` caches that call on `name`:

```js
if ($[0] !== name) {
  t1 = tag`hello ${name}`;
  $[0] = name;
  $[1] = t1;
}
```

Eval of that fixture returns `"hello Ada"`.

## Left unchanged

- Quasis whose cooked value differs from raw.
- Interpolation-free tags (`tagged-template-literal`, `tagged-template-in-hook`). Those fixtures still pass.
- Babel 8 destructured parameter defaults.
- `useSyncExternalStore` snapshot caching.

## How it was checked

From `compiler/`, with `NO_COLOR` and `FORCE_COLOR` unset:

- `yarn tsc --noEmit --pretty false -p packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/tsconfig.json` (exit 0)
- `yarn eslint` on the six changed compiler sources (exit 0)
- `yarn snap` — 1830 tests, 1830 passed, 0 failed

title: [DevTools] Stop filtering by an Activity slice once its Activity unmounts
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #37826.

When an Activity slice filter is applied (#34908), everything outside of the focused Activity is filtered. If that Activity unmounted, the backend kept filtering by it. The Components tree stayed empty. A new Activity rendered in its place wasn't shown either, because filtering only ends at the Fibers of the focused Activity.

Applying the same filters again showed the whole tree: `updateComponentFilters()` doesn't focus an Activity that no longer exists, and tells the frontend that the slice was unfocused (`TREE_OPERATION_APPLIED_ACTIVITY_SLICE_CHANGE` with `0`). The Store then marks the Activity slice filter as invalid.

Now the backend does the same after a commit that unmounted the focused Activity: it stops filtering by the slice, mounts all roots again, and tells the frontend. The re-mount part of `updateComponentFilters()` moved into `remountAllRoots()` so both paths share it.

Re-mounting while profiling would break the commit data, so in that case this happens after the first commit once profiling stops.

Not covered here: the slice can also stop matching anything when the focused Activity is hidden by another filter, e.g. the Activity element type filter. That's a separate issue.

## How did you test this change?

- New tests in `storeComponentFilters-test.js`: one where the focused Activity unmounts and then mounts again, and one where it unmounts while profiling. Both fail without the change.
- `yarn test --build --project=devtools`: 42/42 suites pass. The five related suites gave identical results across three runs.
- `yarn flow dom-browser` and `yarn linc` pass.
- In a randomized test that compares the Store after incremental updates with a remount, slice-filter mismatches dropped from 15 to 4 of 400 seeds. The remaining 4 also fail without this change and come from the case above. That test isn't part of this PR.

title: [DevTools] Handle roots without children consistently
body:
## Summary

React reports a root that renders `false`, an empty array, or an empty Fragment as mounted in `hook.getFiberRoots()`. DevTools doesn't mount roots without children (#34467), so such a root has no instance in `rootToFiberInstanceMap`. Every code path that goes over all roots of the hook assumed that each one has an instance:

| Path | What happened |
|---|---|
| `flushInitialOperations()` (a new frontend connects, e.g. after reopening the browser DevTools) | The root was mounted for the new Store. Once it rendered children, `handleCommitFiberRoot()` mounted it again with the same root instance: "Cannot add node … because a node with that id is already in the Store." |
| `updateComponentFilters()` | "Expected the root instance to already exist when applying filters" |
| `startProfiling()` | "Expected the root instance to already exist when starting profiling" |
| `inspectRootsRaw()` (inspecting another root) | "Expected a root instance to exist for this Fiber root" |
| `handlePostCommitFiberRoot()`, when a passive effect cleanup logs an error while its root unmounts or loses all of its children | "Should have a root instance for a committed root. This is a bug in React DevTools." |

Like `handleCommitFiberRoot()`, these paths now skip roots without children.

The first case is one way to get the "already in the Store" error that is reported in #26340, #27185, #27728 and #32852, although those reports don't have enough detail to tell which cause they hit.

## How did you test this change?

- New tests in `store-test.js` (`roots without children`), one per path above. All 6 fail without the change, each with the error from the table.
- `yarn test --build --project=devtools`: 42/42 suites pass.
- `yarn flow dom-browser` and `yarn linc` pass.
- These cases also came up in a randomized test that compares the Store after incremental updates with a Store built from a remount. That test isn't part of this PR.

title: [compiler] Memoize past a literal destructuring default
body:
Fixes #37735.

A destructuring default such as `{items = []}` or `const {data: {user} = {}} = useQuery()` lowers to `value === undefined ? [] : value`. The fresh literal was inferred as mutable. A later call that might store into that binding extended the literal's mutable range across the hook in between, so the reactive scope was dropped and `formatter(items)` ran on every render. The same component memoizes when the default is a module-level constant.

The other branch is already frozen (props, or a hook return). A write to the binding might be a write to that frozen value, so the fallback literal is now treated as frozen too. The join stays frozen, and the call after the hook can be memoized.

`items.push(...)` is unchanged: it still runs unconditionally, same as pushing onto a prop.

## Test plan
- [x] `yarn snap -p destructure-default-literal-memoized-after-hook` in `compiler/`
- [x] `yarn snap` (1829 passed)
- [x] `yarn tsc --noEmit -p packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler` in `compiler/`

title: [DevTools] Render the highlight overlay in the top layer
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37534.

The element highlight overlay (used by the Inspect button and when hovering the Components tree) sits above the page with `z-index: 10000000`. A z-index can't stack anything above top layer elements, so when a modal `<dialog>` (opened with `showModal()`) is on screen, the overlay draws underneath it. When you inspect something inside the dialog, you get no highlight.

This makes the overlay container a `popover="manual"` element and calls `showPopover()` after mounting it, so the overlay also renders in the top layer. The TraceUpdates canvas already does the same thing (#32614). The default popover UA styles (border, padding, background, margin, overflow) are reset so the container itself stays an invisible 0×0 box. `pointer-events: none` keeps it from intercepting clicks. Environments without the Popover API keep the existing z-index behavior.

## How did you test this change?

I bundled the real `Overlay.js` (flow types stripped) into a page that opens a modal `<dialog>`, then used Playwright with Edge to compare screenshots of the dialog area before and after calling `overlay.inspect()` on an element inside the dialog:

| | overlay visible over the dialog | container in top layer (`:popover-open`) | container size |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` | no | no | 1280px wide (block div) |
| this PR | yes | yes | 0×0 |

- `yarn prettier`, `yarn linc`
- `flow check` for `dom-node`: no errors

title: [Flight Reply] Check that a typed array's backing entry is a Blob
body:
## Summary

Refs #37560.

`parseTypedArray` in `ReactFlightReplyServer` looks up the backing entry for a typed array or `ArrayBuffer` reference (`$A`, `$O`, `$o`, `$U`, `$S`, …) and calls `.arrayBuffer()` on it without checking its type. If a reply body points that reference at a plain string field, or at an entry that doesn't exist, decoding fails with an opaque `TypeError`:

- string entry: `backingEntry.arrayBuffer is not a function`
- missing entry: `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'arrayBuffer')`

The `$B` (Blob) case already guards this with `instanceof Blob` (#36055). This PR adds the same guard to `parseTypedArray`, so both paths reject with `Referenced Blob is not a Blob.` The message reuses the existing error code, so no new code is needed.

The issue's open question (whether a reference may come before its values) is left alone. A typed array reference always needs its bytes, so a missing or non-Blob entry is invalid either way.

## How did you test this change?

I added two tests to `ReactFlightDOMReply-test.js`, mirroring the existing `$B` test: one where a `$U` reference points at a string field and one where its entry is missing. Both fail on `main` with the TypeErrors above and pass with this change.

- `yarn test ReactFlightDOMReply`: 45 passed
- `yarn test -r=www-modern ReactFlightDOMReply`: 45 passed
- `yarn test -r=stable ReactFlightDOMReply`: 45 passed
- `yarn test --prod ReactFlightDOMReply`: 45 passed
- `flow check` (dom-node): no errors
- `yarn prettier`, `yarn linc`: clean

title: [DOM] Report an empty Fragment as preceded by its host parent
body:
## Summary

`FragmentInstance.compareDocumentPosition()` positions an empty Fragment against its host parent (`compareDocumentPositionForEmptyFragment`). When `otherNode` **is** that parent, it returned only `DOCUMENT_POSITION_CONTAINS`:

```js
if (parentHostInstance === otherNode) {
  result = Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_CONTAINS;
}
```

An ancestor both contains **and precedes** its descendant, so `DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING` was being dropped. Per the DOM spec, when `other` is an ancestor the result is `DOCUMENT_POSITION_CONTAINS | DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING`.

This makes the empty path disagree with two things it should match:

1. **The non-empty path, for the same node.** In `ReactFiberConfigDOM.js`, a non-empty Fragment reports `CONTAINS | PRECEDING` for its host parent. The existing test documents this ("containerRef precedes and contains the fragment").
2. **The empty path itself, for higher ancestors.** Comparing the *same* empty Fragment against `document.body` already returns `CONTAINS | PRECEDING`, because that goes through `parentResult` rather than the `=== otherNode` branch. So an ancestor one level up behaved differently from an ancestor two levels up.

Verified against jsdom (the DOM implementation used by these tests):

```
child.compareDocumentPosition(parent) = 10 -> PRECEDING(2) | CONTAINS(8)
```

The empty path returned `8`.

The fix restores the missing bit. It also applies to Fabric, which shares `ReactDOMFragmentRefShared.js`, and to the portaled empty-Fragment path, where the comparison is made against the portal container.

## How did you test this change?

Added the assertion to the existing `handles empty fragment instances` test, and confirmed it fails before the fix:

```
● FragmentRefs › compareDocumentPosition › handles empty fragment instances
  - Expected  - 1
  + Received  + 1
  -  "preceding": true,
  +  "preceding": false,
```

Two further existing assertions in `handles empty fragments` and `positions empty portaled fragments against the portal container` encoded the same `preceding: false` for the portal container and are updated to `true`, with comments.

```
yarn test --silent --no-watchman ReactDOMFragmentRefs-test --runInBand
# Tests: 89 passed, 89 total

yarn test --silent --no-watchman ReactDOMFragmentRefs --runInBand
# Tests: 99 passed, 99 total

yarn test --prod --silent --no-watchman ReactDOMFragmentRefs --runInBand  # passes
yarn test --silent --no-watchman --release-channel=www-modern ReactDOMFragmentRefs --runInBand  # passes
yarn test --silent --no-watchman --release-channel=stable ReactDOMFragmentRefs --runInBand  # passes
yarn linc  # Lint passed for changed files
yarn prettier-check
```

I searched the tree for other instances of this pattern: the only other `DOCUMENT_POSITION_CONTAINS` reference is a read (`documentPosition & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_CONTAINS`) in `validateDocumentPositionWithFiberTree`, which is not affected.

Adjacent to the recent Fragment document-position fixes (#37162, #37163, #37579, #37613); this is a distinct remaining case in the same function.

title: [DevTools] Bind standalone server to the configured host
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37624. `startServer(port, host)` never passed `host` to `httpServer.listen()`, so the standalone server always listened on all interfaces, even with `HOST=127.0.0.1`.

- `host` is now passed to `listen()`. Without a host, the server still listens on all interfaces and clients are told to connect to `localhost`, as before. React Native on physical devices and the app's LAN-IP snippet rely on this.
- The Electron app passes `HOST` only when it's set. Defaulting it to `localhost` would bind `::1` only on Node 17+, breaking IPv4 clients such as the Android emulator (`10.0.2.2`).

**Behavior change:** an explicit `HOST`/`host` now restricts where the server listens. To only change the host clients connect to, use `REACT_DEVTOOLS_CLIENT_HOST`/`clientOptions.host`. The READMEs are updated.

**Known issue, to be fixed separately:** if binding fails (for example, a `HOST` that doesn't resolve), the existing retry-on-error path schedules two retries per failure, so retries double every second.

## How did you test this change?

- New `standalone-test.js` checks the address the server listens on. Before this change it gets `::` instead of `127.0.0.1`.
- Built the Electron app from this branch and ran it with `HOST` unset. It connected to `fixtures/devtools/standalone` via both `localhost` and the LAN-IP snippet. It also connected to a React Native app on the iOS Simulator via both `localhost` and the LAN IP.
- With `127.0.0.1`, connecting through the LAN IP is now refused; before this change it succeeded.

message:
[Fiber] Ping a throttled retry when a new render cancels its timeout (#38061)

When a retry finishes rendering and its commit is throttled, its lanes
are marked suspended and the finished work is held behind a timeout. If
another render starts before the timeout fires, prepareFreshStack
cancels the timeout and throws that work away. The retry's data has
already resolved, so nothing pings it again. Its lanes stay suspended
until some other work commits. If the render that interrupted it keeps
suspending, the retry never runs again.

This is how a transition gets stuck after giving up hydrating a
dehydrated boundary (#38029). The same thing happens on the client when
an unrelated transition interrupts a throttled retry and then suspends
again: the boundary stays on its fallback until that transition's data
arrives, or forever if it never does.

Fix this by pinging the throttled lanes when prepareFreshStack cancels
the timeout, so the retry renders again once the interrupting render
finishes or suspends. This also covers the hydration case, so the
earlier fix in #38030 (pingSuspendedRetryLanes in
updateDehydratedSuspenseComponent and updateDehydratedActivityComponent)
is not needed.

Adds ReactSuspenseThrottledRetry-test.js with two cases: the
interrupting transition commits, and it suspends again. The second fails
without this change. The two hydration tests from #38030 are kept.

Fixes <url>
Closes <url>

[Fizz] Preserve the external runtime configuration when resuming (#38059)

## Summary

Resuming a prerender with an empty HTML shell can emit external-runtime
instructions without loading the runtime that processes them. The
postponed state preserves the data streaming format, but the runtime URL
and integrity metadata were only kept in the original render state. This
leaves completed Suspense content hidden when no shell was flushed
before postponing.

Preserve the external runtime configuration in resumable state and
restore it when creating the resumed render state. Existing resource
deduplication prevents emitting the runtime again when it was already
included in the shell.

message:
[compiler] Preserve AST source offsets and declarator ranges (#36921)

## Summary

Preserve original source offsets and declarator ranges when React
Compiler rebuilds AST nodes in both Rust and TypeScript, so downstream
AST consumers can identify the correct source ranges.

Generated nodes can retain `loc` while losing node-level `start` / `end`
offsets. Declarator ranges derived from transformed children can become
reversed after constant propagation or exclude the closing parenthesis
of a cast initializer.

This change:

- Carries raw AST offsets through Rust lowering and codegen
independently of `loc.start.index` / `loc.end.index`, storing them as
internal, non-serialized HIR metadata.
- Restores TypeScript node offsets from the original AST during codegen.
- Carries statement and declarator locations separately in the existing
instruction and instruction-value fields, then emits the original
declarator range. Absent source metadata stays absent.
- Adds shared declaration-range assertions to snap, unit coverage for
missing and shifted metadata, and `cargo test --workspace` to the Rust
compiler CI workflow.

### Related
- vercel/next.js#97392
- web-infra-dev/rspack#15350

## How did you test this change?

- `cargo test --offline --locked --workspace`: 59 tests passed.
- Targeted Jest run for `CodegenReactiveFunction-test.ts`: 3 tests
passed, including shifted and absent raw offsets.
- `yarn snap` and `yarn snap --rust`: 1,832 fixtures passed in each
backend. The five `source-locations/` fixtures automatically assert
original declaration ranges after constant propagation, for grouped
declarations, loop initializers, and parenthesized casts.
- `bash scripts/test-babel-ast.sh`: 1,811 AST round-trip, 1,812
scope-info round-trip, and 1,797 scope-resolution rename fixtures
passed.
- TS/Rust comparison for the five `source-locations/` fixtures: HIR and
generated code matched in all five cases.
- TypeScript type checking, Rust formatting, Prettier, and scoped ESLint

View Transitions: update error message classification for Chrome 153 (#38034)

Chrome 153 updated the `InvalidStateError` error messages for view
transitions
([chromium@bed98a9](<url>)),
e.g. `Transition was aborted because of invalid state. Document hidden`.
These now bubble up through `onRecoverableError` whereas previously we
suppressed them by exact message.

Don't switch to .startsWith() which would hide every reason; instead
just match the unactionable ones (`Document hidden`, `Viewport size
changed`, and the reason-less message). Also add the analogous Firefox
messages.

`Duplicate view-transition-name` is defined in the Blink enum but
doesn't actually ever surface; instead these show up as `Snapshot
capture failed` or `Animation start failed`, so add a helpful more
helpful message in \_\_DEV\_\_ for those.

message:
[rust-compiler] Fix non-ASCII panic in is_ref_like_name (#38025)

## Summary

`is_ref_like_name` checked the first character with `object_name[..1]`,
which slices one byte. When a `*Ref` name starts with a multi-byte
character like `한글Ref`, that byte cuts into the character and the
compiler panics on `.current` access. Reading the first char with
`.chars().next()` fixes it, and those names now return `false` like the
TS regex does.

Fixes #38023

## How did you test this change?

Added `repro-ref-like-name-non-ascii.js`. It panicked before this change
and compiles cleanly after:

```
bash scripts/test-rust-port.sh InferTypes packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/repro-ref-like-name-non-ascii.js
```

`yarn snap` (1844 passed), `yarn snap --rust` (1844 passed),
`scripts/test-rust-port.sh` (1843 passed) and `cargo fmt --check` are
all green locally.

message:
[RN] Call dispatchNativeEvent when the event target is null (#38007)

## Summary

With `enableNativeEventTargetEventDispatching` on, the Fabric renderer
skipped `dispatchNativeEvent` when the touched view had already
unmounted, so the touch end never reached the JS responder and the next
tap got lost. This passes the null target through instead, so React
Native can still release the responder. It needs
react/react-native#59522 to land first, since `dispatchNativeEvent`
there throws on a null target today.

Fixes #38006

## How did you test this change?

Added a test in `ReactFabric-test.internal.js` that unmounts a view,
dispatches a touch end to its old instance handle, and expects
`dispatchNativeEvent` to get a null target. It fails on main and passes
with this change. Also ran `yarn test packages/react-native-renderer`
(default, `--prod`, www-modern), `yarn flow fabric`, `yarn linc` and
`yarn prettier-check`.

[compiler] Preserve signed zero in constant propagation and code generation (#37995) ## Summary Fixes #37994 The TypeScript and Rust compilers lose the distinction between `0` and `-0` when merging branch constants and generating code. This can make `1 / value` return the wrong infinity. To reproduce, compile this component and toggle `condition`: ```jsx function Component({condition}) { let value; if (condition) { value = 0; } else { value = -0; } return
{1 / value}
; } ``` The result should alternate between `Infinity` and `-Infinity`, but the compiled component keeps returning `Infinity`. Both backends now preserve signed zero when merging constants and emit negative zero explicitly. NaN merging behavior and JavaScript equality semantics remain unchanged. ## How did you test this change? On macOS arm64 with Rust installed through Homebrew, I first created a Cargo symlink for the path used by `test-babel-ast.sh`: ```bash mkdir -p ~/.cargo/bin ln -s /opt/homebrew/opt/rustup/bin/cargo ~/.cargo/bin/cargo ``` I then manually ran these commands from the repository root: ```bash cd compiler yarn install --frozen-lockfile cargo test --workspace --locked yarn snap:build yarn snap yarn snap --rust cd .. bash compiler/scripts/test-babel-ast.sh ``` Rust workspace tests and Babel AST/scope checks passed. All tests in the full compiler snapshot suite passed on both TypeScript and Rust backends. The selected fixtures also passed runtime evaluation on each backend.

message:
[compiler] Allow ref access in PerformanceObserver / ReportingObserver callbacks (#37996)

## Summary

`new PerformanceObserver(cb)` and `new ReportingObserver(cb)` are
compiled with a false positive when the callback touches a ref:

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  4 |  return new PerformanceObserver(() => {
  |  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render
```

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it
asynchronously once the observation fires — never during render — so
reading (or writing) a ref from the callback is safe.
`IntersectionObserver` (#37764) and `ResizeObserver` /
`MutationObserver` (#37895) are already modelled exactly this way; these
two were just missed and fall back to the unknown-constructor default,
whose `Freeze` on the callback trips `ValidateNoRefAccessInRender`.

This is the same class of fix as #37895, which is now on `main`.

## Fix

Add both to `TYPED_GLOBALS` (TypeScript) and `build_typed_globals`
(Rust) using the same signature shape as the existing observers:

| Global | Constructor signature |
| --- | --- |
| `PerformanceObserver` | `(callback)` → `[Freeze]` |
| `ReportingObserver` | `(callback, options)` → `[Freeze, Read]` |

`ReportingObserver`'s second argument is a genuine constructor argument
(unlike the observers whose options belong to `observe()`), so it is
read rather than retained.

Both backends are updated so TS and Rust stay in parity.

## Tests

Four new fixtures:

- `allow-ref-access-in-performance-observer.ts`
- `allow-ref-access-in-reporting-observer.ts`

Both fail before the change with `Cannot access refs during render` and
compile to memoized constructors after it.

- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-performance-observer.js`
- `error.invalid-mutate-hook-value-in-reporting-observer.js`

Negative controls proving `Freeze` is not weakened: mutating a `useMemo`
value inside the callback still reports `` `entries` cannot be modified
``.

[compiler] Type react-native PanResponder.create to fix react-hooks/refs false positive (#37970)

Fixes #37955

**Depends on #37975** (retains declared `Freeze` effects for
already-frozen values, as suggested by @javache). Until that merges this
PR's diff also shows its commit.

## Summary

`react-hooks/refs` reports "Passing a ref to a function may read its
value during render" for callbacks passed to React Native's
`PanResponder.create({...})`, because the compiler treats `PanResponder`
imported from `react-native` as an unknown function that may call its
arguments during render. `PanResponder.create()` only stores the
handlers and invokes them later from gesture events.

The compiler already has a signature for exactly this
(`PanResponder.create` freezes its config and doesn't call it during
render), but it only exists in the test-only `shared-runtime` type
provider in `snap`, so real code never gets it. This adds the same
signature for `react-native` to `defaultModuleTypeProvider` (TypeScript,
and the Rust port in `default_module_type_provider.rs`), so the
callbacks are treated as deferred, like the `IntersectionObserver` fix
in #37764.

Other unknown functions still report errors when given ref-accessing
callbacks.

Added a valid case to
`packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks/__tests__/ReactCompilerRuleTypescript-test.ts`
(the repro shape from the issue). Snap fixtures can't cover this because
`snap` replaces the module type provider with its own.

message:
[compiler] Retain declared Freeze effects on already-frozen values for ref validation (#37975)

## Summary

When an operand is already frozen (e.g. a memoized value), `applyEffect`
drops a declared `Freeze` effect because nothing new gets frozen. Ref
validation reads the declared `Freeze` effects of known signatures, so
it misses them in this case. For example, with `PanResponder.create`'s
signature:

```js
const ref = useRef(0);
const config = useMemo(() => ({onPanResponderRelease: () => { ref.current = 0; }}), []);
const responder = PanResponder.create(config); // false positive: ref access reported
```

This keeps the declared effect on the instruction when the value is
already frozen, as suggested by @javache in #37970. This is metadata
only: nothing extra is frozen.

**Note:** the literal diff from review (always `effects.push(effect)`)
regressed 11 snapshot fixtures. A retained `Freeze` sets `operand.effect
=== Effect.Freeze` in `InferMutationAliasingRanges`, which

`new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current)` and `new MutationObserver(() =>

```
Error: Cannot access refs during render
  > 6 |  return new ResizeObserver(() => ref.current);
  |  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Passing a ref to a function may read its value during render

Both constructors only *retain* the callback and invoke it

message:
Ensure unique `useId` values in large trees (#37916)

## Summary

Fixes #37911
Closes <url> (uses `slice()` which
always allocates a new string)

When the tree position id exceeds 30 bits, `pushTreeContext` splits the
low bits into a base 32 overflow string. The chunk is always a whole
number of 5 bit groups, but `toString(32)` drops leading zero
characters, erasing the boundary between the overflow digits and the
remaining digits. Two structurally different tree positions could then
serialize to the same id.

We now pad the overflow chunk with `padStart(numberOfOverflowBits / 5,
'0')`. `padStart` short-circuits when the chunk is already full width,
so the common case allocates nothing extra (it also beats a sentinel-bit
plus `slice(1)` approach, which always allocates for these short
strings).
