### Additional information

- Versions: habluetooth 7.1.2, bluetooth-auto-recovery 1.6.4, bluetooth-adapters 2.4.0, bleak 3.0.2, BlueZ 5.86, kernel 6.12 (openSUSE Leap 16.0). The container has host networking, NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW, and D-Bus.
- Caveat on the first log block: during 17:20–17:24 the adapter's firmware was also hung (`Opcode 0x0c03 failed: -110` in the kernel log), so a start on hci0 would have failed as well. It still shows that the scanner never tries the new name. In the second block the adapter was healthy on hci1 (kernel firmware load OK at 17:26:50); I reloaded the entry by hand after 23 s.
- Same pattern seen before with a second adapter on this host: a Realtek RTL8821CU combo dongle whose BT firmware hung (`command 0xfcf0 tx timeout`) flipped hci0 ↔ hci2 on each kernel reset, and its entry stayed in `setup_in_progress` until Home Assistant was restarted.
- Integrations that create their own scanner on a specific adapter have the same problem. I submitted a fix for one of them (ronnnnnnnnnnnnn/renpho_fitness_scale_ble#24); it works around it by checking the address → name mapping every 60 s.
- Side note, possibly unrelated: once during the hang, `habluetooth.manager` logged `Missing required permissions for Bluetooth management. Automatic adapter recovery is unavailable. Add NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW capabilities to the container`, although the container has both. It looks like a mgmt-socket failure being reported as missing permissions.

title: 2026.11.0b0  - requirement for venv/container is an undocumented breaking change that breaks legitimate manual installs
body:
### The problem

### The problem

In 2026.11 (introduced via #168155), Home Assistant now calls `validate_environment()` **before** argument parsing and immediately exits with:

`Home Assistant must be run in a Python virtual environment or a container.`

unless `is_virtual_env()` or `is_docker_env()` returns true.

This is **not** a soft warning and there is **no** CLI override (unlike `--ignore-os-check` for the OS check). The call site is hard-coded in `homeassistant/__main__.py` and cannot be skipped without patching the source.

### Why this is a problem

The PR description and changelog only talk about removing the old `<config>/deps` installation path:

> “Remove support for installing Python dependencies in the config dir”  
> “There’s no supported installation method where this is needed”

That part is fine. Completely removing the ancient deps-in-config-dir behaviour is reasonable.

However, the code does something much broader: it turns a cleanup of an obsolete feature into a hard runtime gate that forbids **any** non-venv / non-container install. This includes perfectly valid system-package installations that never used the deps mechanism.

I maintain a Gentoo overlay that packages Home Assistant Core through the normal distro packaging path (python-exec + system site-packages). This is a clean, intentional install method that does **not** rely on the old deps directory. After the 2026.11 beta I now have to sed-patch `__main__.py` on every release just to make the process start. That is neither elegant nor sustainable, and it is completely unnecessary for the stated goal of the PR.

### Expected vs actual

**Expected** (based on the PR title and description):  
- Stop supporting installation of Python packages into `<config>/deps`.  
- Continue allowing the process to start on any otherwise valid Python environment.

**Actual**:  
- Process is forcibly killed unless it detects a virtualenv or a container.  
- No documented announcement that system-package / bare-metal-style installs were being banned.  
- No escape hatch.

### Request

1. Either remove the hard `sys.exit(1)` (or turn it into a warning), **or**
2. Explicitly document this as a breaking change with clear rationale, and provide a supported way for packaging systems (or advanced users) to opt out.

Gatekeeping the runtime environment this aggressively, without prior announcement and under a PR that claimed only to remove an obsolete feature, is a poor fit for an open-source project that has historically allowed multiple installation methods.

Please reconsider the hard requirement. Patching core on every release is not a reasonable expectation for downstream packagers.

title: Matter Wi-Fi dimmers fail to turn on via scenes after repeated activation, while sequential light.turn_on actions work
body:
### The problem

Matter Wi-Fi dimmers fail to turn on via scenes after repeated activation, while sequential light.turn_on actions work

Description

I am experiencing an issue with two KlikAanKlikUit MAWD-250 Matter-over-Wi-Fi dimmers when controlling them through Home Assistant scenes.

Both dimmers work reliably when controlled individually through the Home Assistant interface, including switching them on and off and adjusting their brightness.

However, Home Assistant scenes that switch these dimmers on at a specified brightness stop working after repeated scene activations.

Steps to reproduce

  1. Add two KlikAanKlikUit MAWD-250 Matter-over-Wi-Fi dimmers to Home Assistant.
  2. Create a scene that switches both dimmers on at specified brightness levels.
  3. Create another scene that switches both dimmers off.
  4. Manually switch both lights on.
  5. Activate the off scene. Both lights switch off correctly.
  6. Activate the on scene. Initially, both lights may switch on correctly (though not always or only one of two)
  7. Activate the off scene again.
  8. Try activating the on scene again.

Actual behavior

After the initial successful activation, the on scene no longer switches the lights on. In this fault state, the individual lights appear to be visually presented as "on" with sliders to their specific brightness in their dashboard tiles, while being physically off. Basically, the fault is making the scenes feature not work at all in this particular case.

The off scene continues to work correctly.

The problem also occurs when using an on scene containing only one dimmer.

Individual control of both dimmers through the Home Assistant interface continues to work reliably.

Expected behavior

Home Assistant scenes should reliably switch on Matter dimmers and restore their configured brightness levels, regardless of previous scene activations.

Confirmed workaround

I created a Home Assistant script that separates switching the lights on from setting their brightness.

The script performs these actions:

  1. Turn on the kitchen dimmer without specifying brightness.
  2. Turn on the dining table dimmer without specifying brightness.
  3. Wait 500 milliseconds.
  4. Set the kitchen dimmer brightness to 68%.
  5. Set the dining table dimmer to its configured brightness.

Result: This script works reliably, including after repeated executions and switching the lights off between executions.

This suggests that the problem may be related to how Home Assistant scenes handle power-state and brightness commands for these Matter devices.

The underlying cause has not yet been confirmed.

Device information

Property | Kitchen dimmer | Dining table dimmer -- | -- | -- Manufacturer | KlikAanKlikUit | KlikAanKlikUit Model | MAWD-250 | MAWD-250 Firmware version | 1.0 | 1.0 Hardware version | 1.0 | 1.0 Connection | Matter over Wi-Fi | Matter over Wi-Fi

Additional observations

  • Both Matter dimmers respond reliably to individual commands.
  • The issue appears related to scene activation rather than general connectivity.
  • Scenes that switch the lights off continue to work.
  • Scenes that switch the lights on can fail after previously (partly) working.
  • A scene containing only one dimmer can exhibit the same issue.
  • Sequential light.turn_on commands, followed by brightness adjustments after a 500 ms delay, consistently work.

Possible investigation area

Interaction between Home Assistant scene activation and the Matter OnOff and LevelControl clusters.

This is a hypothesis based on the observed behavior, not a confirmed root cause.

title: Shelly Pro 3EM firmware 2.1.x - Authentication fails with HTTP 401 and 429
body:
### The problem

I am experiencing an authentication issue with Shelly Pro 3EM running firmware 2.1.1.

When password authentication is disabled on the Shelly device, the Home Assistant Shelly integration works correctly.

When password authentication is enabled, Home Assistant discovers the device and asks for the password. However, entering the correct password results in an "Invalid authentication" error.

The same password works correctly when accessing the Shelly web interface.

**Environment:**
- Home Assistant Core: 2026.10.4
- Home Assistant OS: 18.4
- Integration: Shelly (official)
- Device: Shelly Pro 3EM
- Model: SPEM-003CEBEU
- Firmware: 2.1.1
- Enhanced Security: Disabled

**Steps to reproduce:**

1. Enable password authentication in the Shelly Pro 3EM web interface.
2. Open Home Assistant → Settings → Devices & Services.
3. Add the Shelly integration and enter the device IP address.
4. Home Assistant successfully connects to the device and requests the password.
5. Enter the correct password.
6. Home Assistant displays "Invalid authentication".

Disabling password authentication immediately resolves the problem.

Another Shelly Pro 3EM device without password authentication works correctly on the same Home Assistant installation.

**Debug log findings:**

The WebSocket connection is established successfully.

Home Assistant retrieves the device information and detects that authentication is enabled.

It then sends authenticated RPC requests using SHA-256.

The device responds with:

- HTTP/RPC error 401 with a digest authentication challenge.
- HTTP/RPC error 429: Too many requests.
- DeviceConnectionError(RpcCallError(429, 'Too many requests'))

The authentication challenge contains a nonce in a different format from the one sent by Home Assistant.

**Expected behavior:**

Home Assistant should successfully authenticate using the configured Shelly password and establish a working connection.

**Actual behavior:**

Authentication fails, preventing the device from being added.

Could you please investigate whether this is a compatibility issue between the Shelly firmware 2.1.1 authentication mechanism and the aioshelly library?

title: Update pnpm to 12.15.0
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](<url>) | [Confidence](<url>) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [pnpm](<url>) ([source](<url>)) | [`12.14.0` → `12.15.0`](<url>) | ![age](<url>) | ![confidence](<url>) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>pnpm/pnpm (pnpm)</summary>

### [`v12.15.0`](<url>): pnpm 12.15

[Compare Source](<url>)

This release lets `pnpm-workspace.yaml` delegate settings to other files and config dependencies with `include`, adds `lockfile.integrityTarget: tar` and tar-registry support, accepts zstd-compressed registry responses, and honors `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` in `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install`. It also rejects registry metadata that names a different package than the one requested and speeds up workspace installs and macOS file linking.

##### Minor Changes

- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` can now delegate settings to other YAML files and to config dependencies through a new `include` field. Each source may define only the settings the root manifest delegates to it. Every setting has one owner. Commands that change settings write each one to the file that owns it. A relative path in an included file is relative to that file. See [Splitting Settings Across Files](<url>).

  A config dependency supplies its settings through the YAML file named in the `pnpm.config` field of its `package.json`. The new `bootConfig` setting sets the release-age and trust policy pnpm uses to install config dependencies and the pnpm version from `packageManager`.

- Added the `lockfile.integrityTarget` setting. With `integrityTarget: tar`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` pins the hash of every package's uncompressed tar, so the lockfile no longer changes when a registry recompresses its tarballs or serves them as tars. pnpm learns a version's tar hash from the store or by downloading it once. `pnpm audit signatures` ties the tar hash to the signed `.tgz` integrity.

  ```yaml title="pnpm-workspace.yaml"
  lockfile:
  integrityTarget: tar
  ```

- pnpm can now install from a registry that serves uncompressed tars with zstd or gzip content coding. `pnpm-lock.yaml` records the hash of each tar. Declare such a registry with `serverType: pnpr` in `registries` to keep tarball URLs out of the lockfile. See [Tar registries](<url>).

  pnpm now decodes the content coding of tarball downloads itself. It rejects a zstd response whose window is larger than 8 MiB.

  Added the `maxTarballUnpackedSize` setting. It caps the bytes the files of one package may unpack to, 4 GiB by default.

- Registry revisions now always pin the hash of the uncompressed tar, the original included. pnpm records an original selected through the revision protocol, for example with a `+r0` specifier, as `revision: 0` in the lockfile and fetches it from the registry's digest route. pnpm checks a revision's tar whether the registry sends it as a tar, gzip, or zstd. Revision metadata must list revision 0 and mark the selected revision. pnpm rejects incomplete revision metadata with `ERR_PNPM_MALFORMED_METADATA`.

- pnpm now accepts zstd-compressed responses. Registries that serve zstd send package metadata in fewer bytes than with gzip, most of all the full metadata that settings such as `minimumReleaseAge` and `trustPolicy` read.

- `pnpm deploy` and `pnpm install` now use the `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` environment variable as an upper bound for timestamps in `node_modules/.modules.yaml` and `node_modules/.pnpm-workspace-state-v1.json`. With an equivalently prepared deploy target and an epoch no later than the timestamps that would otherwise be recorded, deploying the same project twice produces identical files [#​17171](<url>).

- `pnpm update --interactive` now highlights the row under the cursor in cyan while keeping the colors of its version changes.

##### Patch Changes

##### Security

- pnpm now fails with `ERR_PNPM_REGISTRY_NAME_MISMATCH` if a registry returns metadata for a package other than the one requested. Before, pnpm installed the package under the name in the metadata, so `allowBuilds` rules for the requested package did not apply to it.

- `minimumReleaseAgeExcludePrune` and `trustPolicyExcludePrune` now keep exclusions for resolved configuration dependencies and their transitive dependencies [#​17142](<url>).

##### Resolving dependencies

- When `pnpm install` resolves a dependency again, it now reuses a version that the install already resolved for the same package, as a fresh install does. Before, it kept the version the lockfile pinned and added a second copy of the package. A locked version still stays when nothing else in the install prefers another version. To pin a transitive dependency on purpose, use `overrides` [#​17084](<url>).

- When another workspace project adds a different version of a package, a project's auto-installed peer on that package now moves to the version a fresh install picks. It used to stay on its locked version while any other project still accepted that version [#​17058](<url>).

- A package that lists the same dependency in `dependencies` and as an optional peer now gets the peer bound when a project adds a provider for it later. The lockfile now records every peer a package declares, including one its own dependency supplies [#​17056](<url>).

- `pnpm install --prod` and `pnpm deploy --prod` no longer drop a dependency that a package declares both as an optional peer and as its own dependency, when the package resolved it as its own dependency and a dev dependency provides the same package under another alias.

- `pnpm install` with an existing lockfile and a second `pnpm dedupe` now keep optional peer bindings that point into a dependency cycle or back into the dependent package. Before, the second run dropped the optional peer binding from the lockfile snapshot key.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm dedupe` now preserve own-dependency and peer-dependency bindings when reusing a lockfile whose peer suffixes were hashed by `peersSuffixMaxLength`.

  Upgrading a direct dependency in one workspace project now refreshes matching transitive pins in sibling projects during the same `pnpm install` pass.

- With `resolvePeersFromWorkspaceRoot: false`, a workspace project no longer binds a peer to a version that only another project's dependencies provide. pnpm now auto-installs a version that satisfies the peer range for that project. Before, the project got a version outside the range, with no peer warning.

- `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and `pnpm update` now reuse the lockfile's resolution for dependencies that take part in a dependency cycle, such as `mlly` and `pkg-types`. They re-resolved those packages and everything that depends on them from the registry before [pnpm/tasks#130](<url>).

- pnpm now measures a `pnpm.overrides` entry written as a `workspace:` path, such as `workspace:./packages/foo`, from the directory holding `pnpm-workspace.yaml`. It used to be measured from each package the override rewrote. The install then linked a directory that does not exist, or failed if workspace packages were injected [#​17010](<url>).

- `pnpm install` now removes config dependencies that are no longer declared, including when the entire `configDependencies` setting is removed. Frozen installs reject a lockfile that still records removed config dependencies.

- `pnpm install --update-checksums` now re-resolves every locked package and records the integrity the registry reports now.

- `pnpm add` and `pnpm install` now accept `gist:<id>` dependencies and GitHub Gist URLs, and install them from the gist's archive. `pnpm pkg fix` normalizes a `gist:` repository the way `npm pkg fix` does, `pnpm licenses` links a gist package to its gist page, and `pnpm sbom` reports the repository of a package whose `repository` field is a `gist:` shorthand.

- `pnpm add` now reads the package name correctly from a tarball URL under a registry URL that has a path, such as `<url> and installs a registry tarball URL with a malformed percent escape as a plain tarball URL. Before, the registry path became part of the name, so a scoped package failed with `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`.

- With `minimumReleaseAge` set, pnpm now revalidates a package's cached full metadata with a single ETag request so an unchanged registry answers with `304`, even when the registry does not list a publish time for every version. Previously, pnpm downloaded that metadata again whenever the cached copy was older than `minimumReleaseAge`. With `resolutionMode` set to `lowest-direct` or `time-based`, pnpm also reuses that metadata across every workspace project that depends on the package.

- When pnpm revalidates cached registry metadata, it now sends `If-Modified-Since` when the registry's modification time is a date without a time, and no longer crashes when the modification time is before 1970.

- Added protocol versioning between the pnpm client and pnpr server, verified applied resolution policies in resolution responses, and preserved structured error codes across the wire.

##### Performance

- Sped up `pnpm install` on macOS. On a 12-core Mac, installing 1352 packages from a warm store took 1.3 seconds, down from 2.2. pnpm now writes package files into `node_modules` with 4 threads on macOS, whatever the number of CPU cores. Set the `PNPM_MACOS_LINK_THREADS` environment variable to use a different number of threads, or to `0` to write files with the threads pnpm uses for the rest of the install.

- `pnpm install` is faster and uses less memory in large workspaces with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`. Each project's install no longer reads the manifests of every other workspace project again. Installs that wait for their workspace dependencies now count toward `workspaceConcurrency` [#​16966](<url>).

- Sped up workspace project discovery, dependency resolution, lockfile up-to-date checks, and peer dependency checks in large workspaces [#​16839](<url>) [pnpm/tasks#9](<url>). On a workspace with 6,833 projects, the lockfile up-to-date check uses about 1 second less CPU time. The peer dependency check at the end of an install now checks linked workspace projects against the manifests already in memory, without reading each `package.json` again.

- Sped up bin linking and build planning during `pnpm install`. Package binary targets and shebang runtimes are now precalculated during tarball extraction and served in `pnpr` registry metadata alongside verified `requiresBuild`, tarball size, and file-count metadata.

- Lowered peak memory when pnpm downloads many packuments, such as during lockfile verification with `trustPolicy` on Linux. In one 1,800-entry workspace, a lockfile update now peaks at 1.8 to 2.0 GB. It peaked at 2.6 to 3.7 GB before [#​17020](<url>).

- `pnpm install` in a Cargo workspace skips crates that an earlier install already unpacked into the store. Before, a repeat install processed every crate in `Cargo.lock` again. `pnpm install --force` unpacks every crate again [pnpm/tasks#69](<url>).

##### Linking node_modules and workspaces

- Concurrent installs that import the same package into one project now all complete. One of them used to fail with `ENOTEMPTY` when its copy of the package collided with the copy another install had already placed [pnpm/tasks#48](<url>).

- `pnpm install` now succeeds when `node_modules` is a symlink to an existing directory. Dependency hoisting previously rejected a symlinked `node_modules` as an invalid destination [#​17157](<url>).

- A filtered first install under the isolated linker now links every workspace project by name into `node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules`, not only the selected ones [pnpm/tasks#155](<url>).

- With `nodeLinker: hoisted`, a filtered install such as `pnpm --filter app add <pkg>` keeps the root `node_modules` links and bins of the workspace projects it did not select. A project with no dependencies of its own lost them until the next full install.

- `pnpm install --filter` with `nodeLinker: hoisted` and `--prod` or `--dev` now preserves previously installed dependency groups for unselected workspace projects [pnpm/tasks#164](<url>). Repeat filtered installs also re-resolve when a transitive injected workspace dependency or a linked dependency's version changes.

- With `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, `pnpm install` now runs the workspace root's pnpmfile for every project, after the project's own pnpmfile. Before, it ran only the pnpmfile in the project's directory.

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` now detect peer dependency issues and report linked package versions in linked projects that use `package.json5` or `package.yaml` [pnpm/tasks#172](<url>).

- `pnpm install` and `pnpm peers check` no longer report an unmet peer when a workspace package's peer is provided by a remote tarball URL. pnpm now compares the peer range with the version in the tarball's manifest [#​17037](<url>).

- `pnpm prune` now removes extraneous direct packages from `node_modules` when `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` are already in sync. `pnpm prune` also honors `--filter`, `--recursive`, `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false`, and the `trustLockfile` setting and `--trust-lockfile` flag. With the lockfile trusted, `pnpm prune --prod` works offline when every package is in the store [#​16999](<url>).

##### Injected workspace packages

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now fails with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE` when a local directory dependency or injected workspace package changes a dependency to a different tarball URL or git commit [#​17129](<url>). It also fails when an injected workspace package changes a dependency's named-registry range, such as `work:^2.0.0`, to one the locked version no longer satisfies.

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` now accepts the lockfile it wrote for a `file:` dependency on a directory without a `package.json`. It also accepts the lockfile for an injected workspace package that bundles a dependency in `bundledDependencies`, lists a dependency in both `dependencies` and `optionalDependencies`, or publishes from a `publishConfig.directory` whose `package.json` lists other dependencies than the project's own. Before, these failed with `ERR_PNPM_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE`.

- The lockfile now records a `catalog:` peer dependency of an injected workspace package as written in its `package.json`. It recorded the catalog's range before, so editing the catalog changed the consumer's lockfile entry [pnpm/tasks#153](<url>).

- `pnpm install` now resolves a git, tarball, or tag dependency of an injected workspace package again when its spec changes. Before, it kept the old version.

- Repeat installs and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now re-check projects that inject a modified workspace package, including when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false` [#​17007](<url>), and accept aliased `workspace:` ranges on linked dependencies.

- An injected workspace package that was linked now becomes a copy when the project that depends on it starts providing one of its peers at a version the package's own workspace context lacks. The link used to stay until that dependency was updated, so the package could not find the peer the project provides [#​17057](<url>).

- An injected workspace package now keeps only the files its manifest lists after a lifecycle script or a script named in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` rebuilds it. Before, these refreshes copied every file of the package directory into the injected copy, including files that `files` or `.npmignore` leave out. With `deployAllFiles: true` the copy still gets every file.

- A script listed in `syncInjectedDepsAfterScripts` now keeps a package's links to its own files as links in the injected copies, the way `pnpm install` writes them, and updates those copies when `sharedWorkspaceLockfile` is `false`. Before, a directory link the script added became a real directory or went missing with `deployAllFiles`, and with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` the copies kept the files from the last install.

##### Running scripts and checking dependencies

- Pressing Ctrl+C during `pnpm -r run` or `pnpm --filter <pkg> run` no longer reports `ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_RUN_FIRST_FAIL`. pnpm now ends with the interrupted script's status, such as 130 for a script that SIGINT ended on Linux or macOS [#​16964](<url>).

- With `enableGlobalVirtualStore`, a Node.js resolve hook that a script registers now sees the importer as `context.parentURL` after pnpm's `NODE_PATH` fallback fails to find a bare specifier. Hooks that resolve tsconfig `paths` aliases from the importer failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` [#​16979](<url>).

- `pnpm run`, `pnpm exec`, and `pnpm restart` now pass the install flags they were given, such as `--lockfile-dir`, `--modules-dir`, `--store-dir`, `--offline`, and `--ignore-scripts`, to the `pnpm install` that `verifyDepsBeforeRun: install` starts. When that install leaves the dependencies out of date, pnpm now prints a warning.

- A repeated `pnpm install --filter` now finishes without reinstalling when the selected projects are up to date, and so does `pnpm install` once filtered commands have installed every project. After a filtered install, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now install a selected project whose dependencies changed in between [#​17011](<url>), require the workspace root when a filtered install with `pruneDirectDependencies: true` skipped it [pnpm/tasks#181](<url>), and preserve the recorded ignored build scripts of unselected projects.

- The check that runs before a script now holds the workspace projects that the selected project depends on, including with `sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false` and for workspace dependencies declared with `link:`. `--filter=<project>...` now selects `link:` dependencies as well. In a workspace that has no `package.json` at its root, `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` no longer reinstall before every command when the dependencies are up to date.

- `verifyDepsBeforeRun` and repeat `pnpm install` runs now apply `overrides` before comparing a modified `package.json` with `pnpm-lock.yaml` [#​17127](<url>). `pnpm install` with `optimisticRepeatInstall` now re-runs when `configDependencies` changed, `verifyDepsBeforeRun` reports `node_modules` out of date when `useGitBranchLockfile` is enabled and the branch lockfile is missing, and in a single-project repository both checks record a successful lockfile check so later runs skip it until the lockfile changes [#​16993](<url>).

- `pnpm install` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now compare manifests, lockfiles, and patch files by content hash. They notice an edit that kept the file's modification time, as `cp -p`, `rsync -a`, or an archive extraction leave it, and a patch file that was copied or touched without changing its content no longer marks dependencies as outdated [#​16988](<url>).

##### Deploying, packing, and other commands

- `pnpm deploy` now deploys `file:` dependencies that live outside the workspace directory. It failed with "Refusing to deploy unsafe lockfile path" [#​16983](<url>).

- `pnpm deploy` now records the peer dependencies of the workspace packages it copies into the deployed lockfile. Before, pnpm rejected that lockfile with `--frozen-lockfile` when a deployed workspace package declared a peer and `injectWorkspacePackages` was off [#​17093](<url>).

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `verifyDepsBeforeRun` now succeed inside a directory created by `pnpm deploy`. `pnpm deploy` writes self-contained workspace and lockfile settings, prunes unused `patchedDependencies`, and preserves workspace-level dependency resolutions on deployed directory dependencies.

- On macOS, `pnpm deploy` no longer writes a second, unused copy of every package to `node_modules/.pnpm/@` in the deploy directory [#​17116](<url>).

In `switchbot_cloud`, `SwitchBotCloudSmartRadiatorThermostat._set_attributes` was overwriting `_attr_native_target_temperature` with `_attr_native_current_temperature` in `PRESET_HOME` mode, ignoring the `targetTemperature` field returned by the SwitchBot Cloud API (`/v1.1/devices/{id}/status`).

This causes the entity target temperature to always match the ambient room temperature, preventing automations from detecting heating demand when a user sets a target temperature on a physical SwitchBot climate panel, TRV dial, or the SwitchBot app.

This change checks if `targetTemperature` is present in coordinator data and uses it as `_attr_native_target_temperature`, falling back to `_attr_native_current_temperature` only if `targetTemperature` is not provided. A unit test has been added to verify this behavior.

title: Reconnect Yeelight bulbs when they announce themselves
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

After a power cut (for example a wall switch), a Yeelight bulb takes a long time to come back in Home Assistant, or does not come back at all for minutes:

- The old TCP connection is dead, but nothing tells HA. Without music mode, the library notices after 2 × 75 s without data. With music mode, it never notices on its own: its keep-alive only writes and does not wait for an answer.
- Once HA knows the connection is lost, the library retries only every 15 to 30 s.

Bulbs multicast an `ssdp:alive` (`NOTIFY * HTTP/1.1` to 239.255.255.250:1982) when they join the network. I measured 3 of them, 6 s apart, about 2 s after the bulb accepts TCP again. In my logs (HA's 60 s searches do not trigger them), they only came after a power-up.

This PR listens for these announcements and reconnects the bulb right away:

- `scanner.py`: an `SsdpAdvertisementListener` per source IP, next to the existing search listeners. An alive advertisement is processed like a search response (so IP changes and capabilities are handled the same way), and sends a dispatcher signal for the bulb's id.
- `device.py`: `async_reconnect()` drops the connection and connects again with `AsyncBulb.async_stop_music(force=True)`, which is what the library itself uses to drop a music mode connection, then turns music mode back on if it was on (and the light did not already do that), and reads the bulb's state again, since a power cut may have changed it. It skips the reconnect if the connection is less than 15 s old, because a boot sends 3 announcements within 12 s.
- `__init__.py`: connects the entry to that signal, by its unique id, and runs the reconnect as a background task of the entry (not while Home Assistant is stopping). It only reconnects if the announced address is the entry's address; an address change is left to the existing discovery flow, so HA never reconnects to an old address that may now belong to another bulb. If the reconnect fails, the entry is reloaded, because the library's own retry loop was stopped with the old connection.

The reconnect does not check whether the old connection still works. In music mode there is no way to check (the bulb sends no answers), and a write to a stale connection only gets the bulb's reset at TCP's next retransmission when older data is still unacknowledged, which can take minutes.

Tested on my YLDP02YL bulbs (fw 65) with HA 2026.10.4, in normal and in music mode: after an announcement, the bulb is connected again 0.12 s later (normal mode) and 0.19 s later (music mode, music mode on again).

body:

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Improve typing of template `forgiving_int` and `forgiving_float`.

Both functions took and returned `Any`, so the default value's type was lost entirely. They now use a generic `_T` for the default, mirroring `forgiving_boolean`, so the return type is `int | _T` and `float | _T` respectively. Jinja's `do_int` annotates its `default` parameter as `int` even though it returns the given value unchanged, so passing the generic default through needs a targeted `type: ignore`.

title: Log each distinct report_usage issue for the same integration line
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Log every distinct issue `report_usage` finds for the same line in an integration, instead of only the first one.

`report_usage` deduplicates reports it identifies via the integration's stack frame on the integration's file and line. So when one call in an integration triggers several reports, only the first is logged and the rest are dropped. For example, `device_registry.async_get_or_create(..., default_manufacturer=123)` from a custom integration only logs "passes a non-string value"; the warning that `default_manufacturer` is deprecated never shows.

The deduplication key now also includes where in core `report_usage` was called from:
- **Different issues** have their own `report_usage` call in core, so each is logged once for the same integration line.
- **The same issue with different details** in the message (entity ids, device ids, config entry ids) comes from the same call in core, so it is still only logged once. Callers don't need to change their messages.

Reports identified by `integration_domain` (keyed on the domain and the message) and reports without an integration (not deduplicated) are unchanged. Generic wrappers that report many different issues from one place, such as the deprecated constant helper in `deprecation.py`, still share one key per integration line, as before.

`test_prevent_flooding` now reports through a single helper like core code does, and also checks that the same report with different details isn't logged again while a report from another place in core is. `test_get_or_create_reports_each_deprecation_once` covers the device registry case above.

title: Update HomeKit security system valid values in place
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Follow-up to #172752: when an alarm control panel's `supported_features` change, the HomeKit security system now updates its valid values in place instead of being reloaded.

Today, HomeKit only notices a features change while the entity stays available. If the integration reloads to apply the change, the new arm modes don't reach HomeKit until a restart or HomeKit reload. For example:

- Editing a template alarm panel in the UI: its options flow reloads the entry, so the entity is briefly `unavailable`.
- `template.reload` for a YAML panel without a `unique_id`: its state is removed and added back.

Now the accessory compares the arm modes HomeKit can show (stay, away, night) on every update:

- Unchanged: nothing happens.
- Changed: both characteristics get the new valid values via `override_properties`, and the accessories hash is updated, bumping the config number (`c#`) so controllers fetch the new modes. A current value that's no longer valid falls back to disarmed first, as in a rebuilt accessory, without pyhap logging it as invalid (ikalchev/HAP-python#491).

`supported_features` no longer reloads this accessory; other accessory types are unchanged. The hash update moves from `HomeKit` to `HomeDriver` so the accessory can call it.

title: Remove the duplicate constant pylint checker
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

-->
## Breaking change
<!--

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.

-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove the `home-assistant-duplicate-const` pylint checker (C7413), added in #170848.

It flags an integration constant that has the same name and value as one in `homeassistant.const`, and asks for the generic constant to be imported instead. That works against the move to give constants context, where integrations define their own enums (`<X>ServiceArgument`, `<X>EntityStateAttribute`, …) rather than reusing generic `ATTR_*`/`CONF_*` names. Context matters more than de-duplication here.

Reusing a `homeassistant.const` name only because the string matches is also misleading when the key belongs to something outside Home Assistant, for example:
- keys of data returned by a library or a device API (`data["temperature"]` is the library's field, not `ATTR_TEMPERATURE`);
- fields of a protocol payload, such as an MQTT or webhook message sent by a device;
- discovery properties (zeroconf, SSDP, DHCP, Bluetooth);
- query parameters, headers or body fields of an HTTP request to a third-party service.

In these cases the value is defined by the external party and can change independently of Home Assistant, so the integration should own the name.

The checker, its tests and its README entries are removed. No code disables the message.

When Supervisor can't be reached, the hassio system health section links to the observer so the user can check what is wrong. Since it was added in #43074, that link has pointed at `<url>>:4357`. ## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove the two extra warnings `async_get_or_create` has for a deprecated `via_device`: one when it doesn't match a registered device, and one when it points to the device itself. The behavior doesn't change: such a `via_device` is still ignored, so no via device is linked.

These warnings can be removed because the `via_device` parameter itself is already deprecated. Every call that passes `via_device` reports "calls `device_registry.async_get_or_create` with a deprecated `via_device` parameter; use `via_device_id` instead", with `breaks_in_ha_version="2027.8.0"` (see `_DEPRECATED_DEVICE_INFO_PARAMETERS`). That report runs first, before the two removed ones, so for integrations they are never shown:
- **Custom integrations:** `report_usage` deduplicates on the integration's file and line, so a second report from the same `async_get_or_create` call is dropped.
- **Core integrations:** the `via_device` deprecation is an error, so the call raises before the later reports are reached.

The removed reports were also out of date:
- **Unknown `via_device`:** its `breaks_in_ha_version` of 2025.12.0 passed without any plan to raise.
- **Self-referencing `via_device`:** it said it would raise in 2027.8, when `via_device` is removed anyway.

Integrations moving to `via_device_id` already get an error for an unknown or self-referencing id, so nothing is lost once `via_device` is removed.

The tests now check the `via_device` deprecation count per call instead of the removed messages. This also replaces two assertions in `test_specifying_via_device_create` and `test_specifying_via_device_update` that were wrapped in a set literal, so they always passed.

title: Fix Hanna dosing volume sensors state class
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The Hanna pH acid/base and chlorine dosing sensors used `state_class: measurement` with `device_class: volume`. Home Assistant does not allow that combination, so it logged a warning for each sensor at startup.

The device reports these values as a dosing counter: during a dosing cycle the volume goes up from 0 (for example 0 → 19 mL), and it goes back to 0 when the cycle ends. The sensors now use `SensorStateClass.TOTAL_INCREASING`, which removes the warning, and the long-term statistics now sum the dosed volume.

The sensors were also named "flow rate", which is not correct for a volume in mL. They are renamed to "pH acid/base injection" and "Chlorine injection" (translation keys `ph_acid_base_injection` and `chlorine_injection`). This only changes the default names; entity IDs of existing entities do not change.

Existing installations will see a repair to fix the statistics of these 2 sensors, because their state class changes.

A test checks that both sensors report `total_increasing`.

title: Remove deprecated string flow result types from data entry flow
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
Custom integrations whose config, options or other data entry flows return a step result with a plain string `type` (such as `"form"` or `"abort"`) instead of the `FlowResultType` enum are no longer supported. This has logged a deprecation warning since Home Assistant 2022.7 and was scheduled to stop working in 2025.1. Use the flow helpers, such as `async_show_form`, `async_create_entry` and `async_abort`, or `FlowResultType`, to build step results.


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Remove the deprecated conversion of plain string flow result types to `FlowResultType` in the data entry flow manager.

#72955 added the `FlowResultType` enum and a fallback that converted plain string types and logged a warning, with `breaks_in_ha_version="2025.1"`. This removes the fallback and the warning. The check for a flow removed during its step now compares with `is not FlowResultType.ABORT`, since string types no longer need handling there.

**Custom integration impact:** We scanned all 4,290 repositories in the HACS default integration list (snapshot from 2026-10-30) and found no custom integration that returns a flow step result with a plain string `type`.
- An AST scan of every flow file looked for result dicts with `"type"` set to a result type string, `*FlowResult(type=...)` calls and `result["type"] = ...` assignments. It found a single match, which turned out to be config entry data rather than a step result.
- A manual review also looked for indirect cases, such as types set from string constants, hand-built result dicts and the old `RESULT_TYPE_*` constants. It found no real uses. The only hand-built result with a string type is in a helper that is never called.

title: Propagate errors from sum statistics adjustment so jobs retry
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
`_adjust_sum_statistics` catches `SQLAlchemyError`, logs it and carries on. `adjust_statistics` calls it twice in one `session_scope` — once for `StatisticsShortTerm`, once for `Statistics` — so a swallowed failure has three bad effects:

- **No retry.** `@retryable_database_job("adjust_statistics")` never sees the `OperationalError` (e.g. MySQL/MariaDB lock wait timeout 1205 / deadlock 1213), so a retryable error is never retried.
- **Half-applied adjustment is committed.** If the second update fails, `session_scope` still commits the first: the 5-minute sums are shifted and the hourly sums are not, and the two tables disagree from that point on.
- **The log line is broken.** It formats the builtin `id`, producing `Unexpected exception when updating statistics <built-in function id>` instead of the metadata id.

This PR re-raises the `SQLAlchemyError` after logging, so `session_scope` rolls back the whole adjustment and the job retries on retryable errors. The log message is corrected to use `metadata_id`. A test asserts the error propagates and the log names the statistic.

title: Keep other Portainer containers available when one disappears
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

When a container is removed after the coordinator lists the containers but before it fetches their stats, Portainer answers the stats request with a 404 and pyportainer raises `PortainerNotFoundError`. Nothing catches that, so the whole update fails and every Portainer entity goes unavailable until the next successful poll. The reporter sees this once or twice a day with short-lived containers.

With this change the stats are fetched before the containers are mapped. A container whose stats request returns 404 is left out of that poll, so only its own entities go unavailable and the others keep updating. If the container still exists at the next poll it comes back. Any other error is handled as before.

The new test `test_container_removed_during_poll` makes the first container's stats call raise `PortainerNotFoundError` and checks that only that container's sensor goes unavailable. It fails on `dev` and passes with this change.

I haven't tried @leomoty's case from the issue (a running container whose image tag was replaced), so this may not cover it. A traceback from that case would show which call fails.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Only provide the Flic Twist number entities that the configured push-twist mode supports.

**This needs to be added to the 2026.11 beta.** `flic_button` is new in 2026.11, and this fixes two review points from #182198 that affect the integration as it ships.

**Numbers left behind after a mode change** ([Markus98](<url>))
- Changing the push-twist mode in the options reloads the entry, but the numbers of the previous mode stayed in the entity registry. After selector → default, the user was left with 12 slot entities that the integration no longer provides, and had to delete them by hand.
- Setup now removes the registry entries of the numbers the current mode doesn't provide. They are looked up by their exact unique IDs, so nothing else is touched.
- Switching back brings them back with the same entity IDs, names and areas, because the registry keeps the settings of removed entities. The last position is restored too.

**No numbers in continuous mode** ([Copilot](<url>), [frenck](<url>))
- The review asked for a library fix so that a written position holds in continuous mode. That can't work on the device:
  - In continuous mode, the Twist's LED ring shows the raw rotation of the dial ([pyflic-ble sets the continuous LED mode for all modes](<url>)).
  - In the Twist firmware, a position write only moves the lower limit of the mode, which that LED mode doesn't use.
  - So the device never shows a written position, while the number in Home Assistant changes: the two drift apart.
- Continuous mode now provides no numbers. Its rotation still comes through the event entity as twist and push-twist increment and decrement events, as before.
- The other library bugs in that part of frenck's review are fixed in pyflic-ble 0.2.6 (#189543).

Tests:
- A new parametrized test covers selector → default, default → selector, default → continuous and continuous → default. It fails on the old code.
- The continuous-mode snapshots are removed, since that mode has no number entities now.

Tested on a Flic Twist in a dev instance: default → selector → continuous → default, and selector → default directly. Each time only the numbers of the current mode were registered. A position set before a default → selector → default round trip was written back to the Twist when the position number came back.

## Breaking change
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Let the UniFi update listener schedule the reload when the entry data changes, instead of `async_update_reload_and_abort` in the reauth and reconfigure steps.

The hub's update listener applies option changes live, while reauth and reconfigure reloaded the entry with `async_update_reload_and_abort`. Combining an update listener with that helper logs "has an update listener and should use it for scheduling a reload", and #189565 turns it into an error for core integrations.

**Behavior**
- The listener compares the entry data with the data the hub was set up with. If it changed, it schedules a reload. Otherwise it applies the options as before.
- Reauth and reconfigure on a loaded entry use `async_update_and_abort`, so the listener does the single reload.
- Reauth on an entry that is not loaded (for example after setup failed with an auth error) has no listener, so it still uses `async_update_reload_and_abort`.

The reauth and reconfigure tests now check that the entry is reloaded exactly once, and `test_reauth_flow_reloads_not_loaded_entry` covers reauth on an entry that is not loaded.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

-->
Let the Awair update listener schedule the reload when zeroconf discovery changes the host of a local entry, instead of `_abort_if_unique_id_configured`.

Local entries register an update listener that reloads the entry when its title changes. Zeroconf discovery also updated the host with `_abort_if_unique_id_configured(updates=...)`, which schedules its own reload, so a loaded entry got the warning "has an update listener and should use it for scheduling a reload" (#181297). #189565 turns that warning into an error for core integrations.

Zeroconf now passes `reload_on_update=False`, and the listener reloads when the title or the host differs from what the coordinator was set up with. An entry in setup retry has no listener and is still reloaded by the discovery branch of `_abort_if_unique_id_configured`.

`test_zeroconf_host_change_reloads_local_entry` sets up a loaded local entry, discovers it on a new host and checks that it reloads once without the warning.

-->

SmartThings only refreshes its OAuth token in `async_setup_entry`. After that, the only caller of `async_ensure_token_valid()` is `refresh_token_function`, and pysmartthings only calls it for REST requests and when it opens the event stream. A healthy event stream makes no requests. So the 24 hour token expires in place, and some time later SmartThings stops delivering device events on the open stream. The `welcome` keepalives keep arriving, so pysmartthings never times out or reconnects. Entities freeze on their last state. A device that went offline before the stall never gets its `ONLINE` health event, so it stays `unavailable`. Only a reload brings it back, because the reload refreshes the expired token.

This PR checks the token every minute with `async_ensure_token_valid()` while the entry is loaded. The token is now refreshed within about 40 seconds of its expiry, using the existing lock, validation and reauth handling of `OAuth2Session`. A failed refresh is logged at debug level and retried on the next tick. If the refresh token is rejected, `async_ensure_token_valid()` starts reauth as it already does.

Evidence from my instance (2026.10.4, pysmartthings 4.0.3, three Samsung ACs and a fridge):

- The HA backup taken at 03:00 UTC on 30 Oct stored `expires_at` = 29 Oct 17:20:12 UTC. The token had been expired for almost 10 hours and nothing had refreshed it.
- The fridge reports `powerConsumptionReport` every ~13 minutes. Its last delivered event was at 18:04:44 UTC on 29 Oct. Nothing from any device arrived until a manual reload at 07:34:56 UTC on 30 Oct. That reload stored a new token with `expires_at` 31 Oct 07:34:55 UTC.
- One AC went `OFFLINE` at 17:15 UTC and stayed `unavailable` for 14 hours. At the reload it was heating.
- The log has no SmartThings lines for the whole window.

Others in #176244 measured the same mechanism. Delivery resumes when the stored token is refreshed, and the subscription does not need to be re-created ([comment](<url>)).

The hourly reconciliation in #182687 is still a useful safety net for events lost for other reasons. This PR addresses the token expiry, which in the data from #176244 and from my instance is what causes the daily stalls.

Add a `TargetIdKey` enum to `homeassistant.const` for the five ID keys of a target: `entity_id`, `device_id`, `area_id`, `floor_id` and `label_id`. A target selects what an action, trigger or condition applies to.

New-style triggers and conditions validate their `target:` block with `cv.TARGET_FIELDS` and resolve it with `TargetSelection`, so they pick up the enum through these helpers.

Keys of trigger, condition and device automation configs keep their `CONF_*` constants.

The `ATTR_*` constants stay as they are. The helpers no longer import them, and the dropped imports are not used through these helper modules elsewhere in core, nor by any custom integration in the HACS default list.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Raise an error for core integrations when `_abort_if_unique_id_configured` (with `updates`) or `async_update_reload_and_abort` would schedule a reload of a config entry that has an update listener. Custom integrations keep the current behavior: a warning is logged and the entry is reloaded.

Combining both can reload the integration twice, or race between the two reloads. #169198 deprecated this with a log message and announced that it would raise in 2026.12. A check of the HACS default custom integrations found about 550 that would break on reconfigure or reauth if this raised for everyone, so custom integrations only get the warning. The `breaks_in_ha_version` is removed, since there is no date planned for custom integrations.

The error only triggers when the entry has an update listener at the time the helper runs. Listeners are removed when setup fails and on unload, so a reauth flow started because setup failed is not affected. It triggers for reconfigure or runtime reauth on a loaded entry, and for `_abort_if_unique_id_configured(updates=...)` when discovery changes the data of a loaded entry.

In core, only `unifi` fails in CI. `awair` (#181297) hits the warning at runtime when zeroconf updates the host of a loaded local entry, but its tests don't cover that path. Both are migrated first, so this PR stays a draft until they're merged:
- #189570 (awair)
- #189571 (unifi)

The tests cover both cases, for reauth and reconfigure: core integrations raise, and custom integrations log the warning and still reload the entry.

title: Bump caldav to 3.7.0a0
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Bump caldav from 3.5.0a0 to 3.7.0a0. Like 3.5.0a0, this is the companion release of 3.7.0 without the hard `niquests` dependency, so the integration keeps using `requests`.

The main reason is python-caldav/caldav#832, which fixes python-caldav/caldav#831: `vcal.fix()` now drops a `VTIMEZONE` that has no `STANDARD` or `DAYLIGHT` observance, as the OneCalendar app writes it. vobject cannot parse such an object, so reading `vobject_instance` raised `ParseError`, and one such event made the whole CalDAV calendar fail to load, both the calendar view and the entity state:

```
vobject.base.ParseError: "In transformToNative, unhandled exception on line None: <class 'ValueError'>: at least one component is needed (<VTIMEZONE| [<TZID{}Europe/Amsterdam>]>)"
```

With 3.7.0a0, the `TZID` of such an event is resolved by name and the event shows up at the right time.

Other upstream changes worth knowing about:
- caldav now depends on `calendaring-config` (same maintainer, `GPL-3.0-or-later OR Apache-2.0`, only depends on PyYAML). caldav uses it only to read its own config file through `get_davclient()`, which the integration does not use.
- 3.6.0: `save(no_create=True)`, which the to-do platform uses when updating an item, now leaves the existence check to the server with `If-Match: *`.
- 3.7.0: a request other than GET or HEAD that is redirected to another host or port is no longer followed; same-host redirects are now repeated with their method and body.

The parts of the caldav API the integration uses are unchanged between 3.5.0a0 and 3.7.0a0, so no integration code changes are needed.

title: Add event loop timing to the profiler
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Adds `profiler.start_loop_timing`, `dump_loop_timing` and `stop_loop_timing`.

While on, every callback of the event loop is timed and counted per function, class and config entry. Callbacks over `threshold` (default 100 ms) are listed one by one, numbered so a reader can tell new ones from those it has seen. `dump` logs or returns the result, `stop` does the same and ends the timing.

```
custom_components.foo.coordinator.FooCoordinator._handle_refresh_interval [foo: Living room]: 120 calls, 3410.5 ms total, longest 1205.3 ms at 2026-10-30T14:32:07+00:00
```

Until now the only way to find a callback that holds the loop was `set_asyncio_debug`, which is too expensive to leave on. This can run for hours.

It replaces `asyncio.events.Handle._run` while on and restores it when off, so it costs nothing while off. Per callback, i5-8400T:

| | off | on | asyncio debug |
|---|---|---|---|
| task step | 3.1 µs | 5.5 µs | 41 µs |
| `call_soon` callback | 2.6 µs | 4.2 µs | 38 µs |

Callbacks of `async_track_time_interval` and `async_track_point_in_time` show as the helper class with the entry. Work without a config entry context has no entry.

title: Bump pyElectra to 1.2.14
body:
## Proposed change

Bump pyElectra to 1.2.14. The integration itself is unchanged; this moves the
pinned dependency to the current release.

Everything since 1.2.10 is additive: no symbol the integration uses was renamed
or removed, and the two getters that widened from `bool` to `bool | None`
(`get_turbo_mode`, `get_shabat_mode`) only differ on a unit that omits the
field, which now reads `None` instead of raising `KeyError`.

- 1.2.11 adds a getter and setter for the `IFEEL`, `SLEEP` and `TIMER` `OPER`
  flags, following the tri-state rule `get_filter_clean_required()` already
  used, and replays a request once with a renewed session id when the cloud
  reports the session as refused.
- 1.2.12 exposes the server-side timers as events (`get_events`,
  `create_event`, `update_event`, `delete_event`, `ElectraEvent`) plus the
  per-device events flag.
- 1.2.13 carries the corrected `OPER.TIMER` docstrings.
- 1.2.14 moves the decoding of the `DIAG_L2` sensor health flags into the library
  (`get_indoor_coil_sensor_fault()`, `get_return_air_sensor_fault()`), where the
  knowledge that the healthy value differs between models belongs.

body:

  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

-->

Adds a Power profile select and a Keep awake switch, using the system controls System Bridge 5.20.0 already supports.

The select lists the profiles the device reports, such as balanced, performance and power-saver (Linux with power-profiles-daemon). The switch keeps the device from idling until it's turned off (Linux). Each entity is only added once the device first reports it, so devices without support don't get them, and it goes unavailable if the device stops reporting it.

An error response from System Bridge, or a closed connection, raises an error when the option is picked or the switch is toggled.

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

  write it towards our users, not us.

-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Bump pyflic-ble from 0.2.5 to 0.2.6.

**This needs to be added to the 2026.11 beta.** `flic_button` is new in 2026.11, and this release fixes library issues raised in the review of #182198 that affect the integration as it ships.

Fixes in 0.2.6 that matter for `flic_button`:
- **Twist position numbers:**
  - Position writes after a reconnect now land where the dial is. Before, they could be computed in the wrong frame.
  - A small twist after setting a position no longer fires dozens of `twist_increment` events.
  - A restored position is no longer lost when the connection drops just before it is written.
  - An update the Twist dropped is sent again.
- **Pairing errors:** these now raise the matching exceptions, so the config flow shows `pairing_failed` or `invalid_signature` instead of `unknown`.
- **Out of range:** failed reconnect attempts while a button is out of range are logged at debug. Before, each attempt logged two errors.
- **Failed start:** a start that fails after connecting no longer leaves a half-open link that stops the reconnect loop.
- **Replayed presses:**
  - After a reconnect, buttons no longer replay button events that were already handled.
  - After a restart, old queued presses are dropped, so automations don't fire again.
- **Flic 2 and Duo:** handled button events are now acknowledged and pings are answered, as the protocol specifications require.

No code changes are needed in Home Assistant. The config flow already maps `FlicPairingError` and `FlicAuthenticationError`. There are no new dependencies.

title: Tolerate missed LIFX polls before marking a light unavailable
body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Since the move to `lifx-async`, a light becomes unavailable the first time one poll times out, and is back on the next one. The `aiolifx`-based integration gave each poll up to 90 seconds. Now a light keeps its last state until it misses three polls in a row.

Two reads stay strict:
- The first read at setup has no last state to keep, so setup still retries.
- The read before a partial write now checks `last_read_succeeded` instead of `last_update_success`. A write is never merged over a state the light did not just return.

title: Reconcile the LIFX test doubles with real products
body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The LIFX test doubles had drifted from real hardware:
- an impossible Ceiling: 64 downlight zones, product 55, and a chain
- tile orientations the library never reports ("Right Side Up" instead of "Upright")
- a default model name missing from the product registry

Tests passed against devices that cannot exist. This PR rebuilds the doubles from real products. It changes tests only.

### Summary

```diff
 tests/components/lifx/
 ├── helpers.py
-│  create_mock_* (MagicMock(spec=...) with hand-set state)
-│  _create_reference_* (overrides on top of the basic doubles)
+│  one factory per capability, built from a real product id
+│  real lifx-async device instances, state from the library's from_* classmethods
+│  only network methods are AsyncMock
 ├── snapshots/test_diagnostics.ambr  # colour and Thread devices only
 └── test_*.py  # repeated code paths trimmed
```

Per-product values come from lifx-emulator's product specs, with a one-line pointer in `helpers.py`:
- zones, tile size, firmware and uplight
- model names and capability flags from lifx-async's registry
- the Ceiling's uplight zone from the product's published `uplight_coords`, the same way lifx-async derives it

Tests that only repeated a code path another test already covers were removed.

### Evidence

- **Before:** 343 tests on `dev`, against doubles such as the 64-zone, product 55 Ceiling.

title: Fix Gree availability when devices stop responding
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Sorry, my previous description wasn't clear.

I use this integration with four Gree air conditioners at home, bridged to HomeKit. Everything worked initially, but the units sometimes stopped responding in Home Assistant. Recovery could take a long time, especially after restarting HA.

I used Claude and GPT to help investigate. In tests from HA, broadcast discovery found none of the four units, while unicast discovery found all four.

During that investigation, we also found the bug this PR fixes: each successful UDP send updated the "last response" time, even when the device never replied. With requests sent every 60 seconds, the normal 120-second response check could not detect a device that had stopped replying.

This change updates that timestamp when DATA or RESULT replies arrive, rather than when a request is sent. It also keeps failed polls from making an unavailable device appear available again.

I kept discovery and reconnection changes out of this PR to avoid overlapping with the ongoing work in [#187623](<url>) and the related manual-IP support in [#186046](<url>). This PR only fixes availability reporting; it does not fix the broadcast discovery or reconnection problem.

<details>
<summary>Validation details and limits</summary>

Validation on macOS arm64, CPython 3.14.10, greeclimate 3.5.2, based on dev 57ed3662b030e9bc057a11a13616085f19e2771c:

- `uv run --no-sync --offline pytest tests/components/gree -q --timeout=60`: 147 passed, including 10 new cases; all 5 existing snapshots passed.
- The same new test module against the unmodified dev coordinator: 8 failed, 2 passed. Cases cover sends without replies, continued unavailability, DATA/RESULT freshness and recovery, one lost reply, repeated send timeouts, publication timing, and independent devices.

title: Teach bots where integration constants belong
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Adds a line to `AGENTS.md` about where constants go: `const.py` only for constants more than one module uses, otherwise keep the constant in the module that uses it.

Background: in #188992 I moved the Control4 polling into a coordinator module and `SCAN_INTERVAL` ended up in `const.py`, even though only `coordinator.py` reads it. Claude wrote the refactor, Copilot reviewed it, I reviewed it, and @MartinHjelmare was the one who caught it. If I'd been writing that code from scratch I don't think I'd have put it there, but in a refactor `const.py` looks like the obvious place to park things, and nothing the bots read says otherwise. It's not in `AGENTS.md`, not in the `ha-integration-knowledge` skill, and the contributors docs just say `const.py` holds "Constants, like `DOMAIN`".

Before writing this down I wanted to check it's actually a shared convention and not one reviewer's preference, so I had Claude pull the inline review comments on this repo from the last six months (~80k, April to October) and pick out the ones about constant placement. Reviewers ask for this in #182074, #182079, #174142, #172593, #166868, #178733, #177247, #175804, #169782, #169700 and #165602, and nobody asked for the opposite. It's also not applied consistently: PRs that moved single-module constants into `const.py` got merged without comment, Copilot has itself suggested moving a constant into `const.py` (#179346), and one reviewer in #165602 says outright "It seems to be a 50/50 of whether we put these in the `const.py` or the `coordinator.py`."

The details in the wording all come from those threads: tests don't count as a user (#166868), entity descriptions and service schemas follow the same rule (#177247, #178733), shared constants go in `const.py` rather than being imported from a platform module (#175484), and constants a PR doesn't touch are left alone (#182074 left an existing single-module `SCAN_INTERVAL` in `const.py` and Martin merged it).

`.github/copilot-instructions.md` regenerated with `script/gen_copilot_instructions.py`.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

This PR addresses the two follow-up suggestions from the [review of #158505](<url>), which added the Powersensor integration, and fixes a bug that was reported on Discord after it was merged. Each change is a separate commit, and only the bug fix is user visible.

- **Follow-up 1: Remove a redundant reset in `async_added_to_hass`** (`entity.py`). Core integrations now [change an entity ID in place](<url>), so `async_added_to_hass` runs once per entity, and `__init__` already sets `_has_recently_received_update_message` to `False`.
- **Follow-up 2: Use joules as the native unit of the energy entities** (`sensor.py`). The devices report energy in joules. The energy totals of sensors and plugs, and the household view's four energy totals, now have `UnitOfEnergy.JOULE` as their native unit and kWh as their suggested unit, so core does the conversion and `_joules_to_kwh` is removed. The household view's `formatter` is now optional: the power entities keep `formatter=int`, and the energy totals store `VirtualHousehold`'s joules unchanged.

  The states are unchanged. Core's J→kWh conversion is the same division the integration did, and `suggested_display_precision` applies to the suggested unit, so there is no visible change to the user (the entities show the same values with the same precision as before).

  On the unit test change, `test_energy_converted_from_joules` used to check only that the state was approximately 1 (`pytest.approx(1.0, rel=1e-4)`). It now asserts the exact state, `"1.0"`, and that the unit is kWh, which shows that core converts the joules to the suggested unit. The snapshots only gain the `sensor.private` suggested unit on the seven energy entities.
- **Bug fix: Allow deleting a device while the integration isn't loaded** (`__init__.py`). Problem: Unloading an entry deletes its `runtime_data`, but the device page still offers **Delete** while the integration is disabled or unloaded, and core calls `async_remove_config_entry_device` regardless of the entry's state. The integration reads `config_entry.runtime_data.dispatcher`, causing the deletion to fail with an `AttributeError` ("Unknown error" in the UI) and the device staying on the UI. Fix: While the entry isn't loaded, nothing tracks which devices are on the network, so a plug or sensor can now be deleted. Plugs and sensors that are still on the network are set up again when the integration loads. Deleting the household view is still refused regardless of the entry's state.

  For unit tests, `test_device_can_be_deleted_while_unloaded_and_returns_on_load` discovers a plug or a sensor, unloads the entry and deletes the device, then loads the entry again and checks that the device comes back when it is discovered. `test_household_view_cannot_be_deleted` used to run only with the entry loaded. It now also runs with the entry unloaded, and checks that the household view is still refused.

title: Filter SolarEdge battery -FLT_MAX sentinel to unknown
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
