-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
SolarEdge inverters mark "not implemented" battery float32 registers with a `+/-FLT_MAX` sentinel (word-swapped `0xFF7FFFFF`, decoding to `-3.4028234663852886e+38`) rather than the IEEE NaN sentinel the decoder filters. The `solaredged` library already normalises the same `+/-FLT_MAX` pattern for `site_limit`, but the battery block fields (`dc_current`, `dc_voltage`, `temperature_average`, `energy_available`, `max_charge_peak_power`, `max_discharge_peak_power`) have no equivalent handling, so the sentinel is published as a real measurement. It lands in the recorder and wrecks battery sensor history charts.

This PR filters the sentinel in `SolarEdgeModbusBatterySensorEntity.native_value`: a float value whose magnitude reaches `_BATTERY_FLOAT_SENTINEL` (1e37, the same bound the library uses for `site_limit`) is reported as `None`/`unknown` instead. The check sits on the entity layer so it applies to every current and future battery float sensor; physically impossible magnitudes are the only values dropped.

The included test seeds the six affected register pairs with the actual sentinel bytes on the mock Modbus unit and asserts all six entities read `unknown`.

title: Update coverage to 7.17.0
body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Change | [Age](<url>) | [Confidence](<url>) |
|---|---|---|---|
| [coverage](<url>) | `==7.16.2` → `==7.17.0` | ![age](<url>) | ![confidence](<url>) |

---

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>coveragepy/coveragepy (coverage)</summary>

### [`v7.17.0`](<url>)

[Compare Source](<url>)

- Dropped support for Python 3.10.

- Binary wheels are now provided for iOS and Android. This allows the use of
  the optimized C tracer on mobile platforms.

- Fix: three or more levels of nested `with` statements could make a `with`
  line look like a branch with an exit that can never happen. Using the
  sys.monitoring core, these phantom branches were reported as partial. Other
  cores hid the problem but still counted the phantom branches in the total.
  Closes `issue 1987`\_.

- Fix: a comment or string that merely mentioned `if True:` or
  `while True:` could mark its line as a branch that is known to be partial,
  so a branch that never ran was reported as taken.  These built-in patterns
  now only match at the start of the statement. Closes `issue 2314`\_.

- Fix: region detection missed functions defined in unusual places, such as
  `else` and `except` clauses. This is now fixed.

- Fix: recent versions of the lcov tool complain if the same function name
  appears more than once in a report. Python can have multiple same-named
  functions in a few ways, for example, getters/setters or conditionally
  defined functions. These are now disambiguated by adding a `@<line number>`
  suffix to the function name. Fixes `issue 2335`.

- Fix: The "Can't combine statement coverage data with branch data" error now
  names the two data files it couldn't combine. The :ref:`error description <error_cant_combine>` in the docs now lists common causes and how to find the
  process that wrote the file.

- Fix: at coverage totals close to 0 or 100, the XML report could get incorrect
  `line-rate` values like `8.333e-05` or `1`. This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2293`\_ and `issue 2294`\_.

- Fix: a parallel data file saved more than once kept the hash of its first
  save in its file name. Combining could then skip it as a duplicate of another
  file that had the same data at that point, and delete it, losing the data
  recorded after the first save. Each save now updates the hash. This had been
  a problem since 7.13.1. Fixes `issue 2338`\_.

- Fixes for obscure but legal file names:

  - File names (and plugin names) can contain control characters, which are
  legal in POSIX paths but unsafe in reports: in XML 1.0 they make the
  document non-well-formed, and in a terminal they act as escape sequences
  (colors, title/clipboard sequences, cursor moves that forge output). Now
  the XML report, the text and Markdown summary reports, and `coverage debug
  data` replace non-printable characters in names. Printable names are
  unchanged.

  - A file pattern (from `include`, `omit`, or a `[paths]` alias)
  containing a newline sent the glob-to-regex translation into an infinite
  loop, hanging the process. Newlines in patterns are now handled like any
  other character.

- Fixes in the implementation of the C tracer:

  - If a plugin's `dynamic_source_filename` method raised an exception, lines
  in that function could be recorded as belonging to a different file. Also
  fixed some minor memory leaks in the C tracer.

  - The refcount of `None` was mismanaged during function calls, including
  comprehensions. This was unlikely to cause an actual problem, but is now
  fixed. Thanks, Andrew Dalke.

  - The C tracer held borrowed references to dictionary values, which was
  unsafe on free-threaded Python.  Now it takes its own references.

  - An internal error while recording a new file could be reported as a
  confusing `SystemError` instead of the actual exception.

- Performance: the text summary report (`coverage report`) held on to every
  file's parsed source until it finished, so its memory use grew with the size
  of the project: ten times or more what 7.14 used on large projects.  Now it
  keeps only what it needs to print. Fixes `issue 2277`\_.

- Performance: HTML reports should be about 5% faster to produce.

- Kept the political banner in the README. Closes `issue 2344`\_.

title: Fix LG soundbar power updates after manual power changes
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->


Manually turning an LG soundbar on or off can leave Home Assistant showing its previous power state. The soundbar can stop sending updates without closing the TCP connection, while commands still work. I know there was a recent similar fix but i've still had issues on my soundbar, this fix had bin stable for me for a week now :)

Replace archived Temescal with [BarTalk 0.1.1](<url>), our Apache-2.0 Python library with compatible commands. It reconnects and requests state after 30 idle seconds while on or power is unknown, then rebinds once five seconds after shutdown. Confirmed standby has no recurring state queries. Connection checks and unloaded entities close their clients.

BarTalk also:

- Reads split TCP packets completely and recovers from malformed replies.
- Retries failed commands once and reports persistent failures instead of silently losing them.
- Backs off unusable sessions up to 30 seconds and avoids five-second reconnect loops on models without power status.
- Keeps receiving updates after a callback raises an exception.

The client has been used in a custom integration on an LG S95Q. All 25 current-Core LG tests and 31 library tests pass.

title: Fix blocking jsonschema load in MCP tool calls
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
**Cause:** The first session.call_tool() makes the MCP client validate the tool's output schema. It imports jsonschema lazily at that point, and jsonschema_specifications reads its bundled metaschema files from disk (scandir, open, read_text). All of that happened inside the event loop, which is what produced the three warnings.

**Fix:** `homeassistant/components/mcp/__init__.py` now runs a small `_load_jsonschema()` helper in the executor before the coordinator's first refresh. It imports jsonschema and runs check_schema({}), which loads the metaschemas once, off the loop.

title: Put the BLUETTI Modbus built-in battery on a child device
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Puts the built-in battery's readings on a child device of the power station, named "Built-in battery", using the child devices introduced in <url>

The Balco 260's battery is part of the power station, not a product of its own: it reports the power station's serial number as its pack serial number (`b_serial` at unit ID 1 equals `d_serial` on my unit), and BLUETTI's app shows it as pack 1 with that same serial number. That is what a child device is for. The BC260 expansion packs in #188253 are separate products, with their own serial number, model and firmware, so they will stay devices of their own linked through `via_device`.

- The power station's device is registered before the platforms are set up, as before, and its registry ID is kept in the runtime data as the child's parent.
- The battery voltage, current, SoC, SoH, cycle count, cell count, temperature sensor count, and total charged and discharged energy move to the child device.
- Unique IDs are unchanged, so existing entities keep their entity IDs and history. Device-targeted automations keep working, since targeting the power station includes its children.
- These readings are the built-in battery's own, read at the power station's unit ID; BLUETTI confirmed that this block holds per-pack values. The state of charge of all packs together (`b_soc_total`, read at unit ID 250 in #188251) belongs on the power station, not here.
- A child device has no firmware of its own, so the battery's BMS firmware (`b_ver_1`, 50008.01.10 on the three Balco 260s I have diagnostics from) is added to the power station's software version, after ARM, DSP and IoT. `b_ver_count` and `b_ver_1` are read once at setup for this, with the library's retry; the other version slots stay out of the read plan. A read that still fails raises `ConfigEntryNotReady`, like a failed first refresh.
- Their names drop the "Battery" prefix, as the device name carries it: "Battery voltage" becomes "Built-in battery Voltage" in the frontend. Voltage and current take their device class's name. A new install gets `sensor.balco_260_built_in_battery_voltage`.

Verified on hardware (Balco 260, ARM 50011.01.13, DSP 50014.01.11, IoT 50012.01.21) with a configuration that already had the nine battery entities on the power station: the child device "Built-in battery" was created under it, the nine entities moved to it with their entity IDs unchanged (`sensor.balco260_battery_voltage` and so on), and they showed the battery's readings as "Built-in battery Voltage", "Built-in battery SoC", etc.

Tests cover the child device and its parent, the software version with and without a BMS version, setup retry when the BMS version can't be read, and an entity registered on the power station before this change keeping its entity ID once it moves to the child device. The sensor snapshot is updated for the new names.

title: Report the Bitcoin sensor values as numbers
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

-->

The Bitcoin sensors now report numbers instead of rounded text. Templates and automations get the full value, for example `6448.36` instead of `6448.4`; the dashboard still rounds it for display. The statistics timestamp is now a date and time instead of a number of milliseconds.

The blocks size now has a unit. Setups that already existed keep showing bytes, new setups show megabytes. You can change the unit in the entity settings.

Most sensors now keep long-term statistics. The exchange rate does not, because its unit is the currency you selected; the market price in USD does.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Next step after #188579, still one thing per pull request: the sensors report numbers instead of preformatted strings.

- Each value is the real number, with the same conversion as before (satoshi to BTC, H/s to PH/s). The rounding moves from the integration into `suggested_display_precision`.
- State classes, so long-term statistics are kept: measurement for most sensors, total increasing for the total supply and the total blocks.
- Device classes where one fits: duration for the time between blocks, data size for the blocks size, timestamp for the statistics time.
- The blocks size is in bytes with megabytes as the suggested unit. Home Assistant stores a suggested unit only the first time a sensor is registered, so existing setups keep bytes, which is what they show today. A test covers that.
- The exchange rate gets no state class on purpose: its unit is the chosen currency, and long-term statistics cannot convert between currencies. The market price in USD keeps them.

Entity IDs and names do not change. In the snapshot every new value, rounded the way the old string was, matches the old string.

body:

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Brings the System Bridge media player up to what the backend supports, and adds the audio devices.

Needs connector 5.23.0, from #189513.

**Media player**
- Seek when the backend reports `is_seek_enabled`.
- Set the volume when the backend reports one.
- Set shuffle and repeat, only when the backend reports the player. That's Linux only: Windows reports shuffle and repeat but can't set them.
- A failed control or a closed connection now raises an error, rather than being ignored.
- Pick which player it follows with the source list: `Automatic` (the backend's pick) or any player the backend reports. Controls go to the picked player. The pick isn't kept across restarts.

**Audio devices**
- An `Audio` media player for the system default output, with volume and mute. It follows the default when it changes, and its source list picks which output is the default.
- A media player for each output, with volume and mute.
- For each input, a volume number and a mute switch. An `Audio input` select picks the default input.
- Devices connected later get their entities when they first show up, and go unavailable while disconnected.

The audio module isn't in `MODULES`. Backends before 5.16.0 never answer a request for it, so setup only asks for it when the backend reports 5.16.0 or later (`AUDIO_MIN_VERSION`). The data listener registers for it either way, so older backends just never send it.

Per-app volume is left out, as apps come and go too often to be entities.

title: Set PARALLEL_UPDATES for Bluesound platforms
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Set `PARALLEL_UPDATES = 1` on the Bluesound media player and button platforms to complete the `parallel-updates` quality scale rule.

Each config entry has a single player, so this only serializes commands sent to the same speaker. State comes from the coordinator's long-poll loops and the entities don't poll themselves, so in practice this only limits concurrent actions. For the buttons it keeps a set and a clear of the sleep timer from racing, since `clear_sleep_timer` keeps calling `sleep_timer()` until it reads 0.

body:

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.

-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Once Core calls Supervisor over its Unix socket (#189360), any request to the Supervisor API over TCP that uses Core's `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN` comes from user configuration (usually `command_line` or `shell_command`) or a custom integration. home-assistant/supervisor#7447 raises a `deprecated_tcp_api_request` issue with context `core` for these requests. This PR turns that issue into a repair.

- New non-fixable repair `issue_core_deprecated_tcp_api_request`. It shows the path of the first request that triggered it and points users to `command_line`, `shell_command` and custom integrations as the likely sources.
- Supervisor repairs can now set a `learn_more_url` and a `breaks_in_ha_version`, through two new dicts in `const.py` keyed by issue key (`ISSUE_LEARN_MORE_URLS`, `ISSUE_BREAKS_IN_HA_VERSION`). The version is also passed to the repair text as the `breaks_in_ha_version` placeholder. Other Supervisor issues will be moved to the learn more URL in a follow-up PR.
- This repair links to a new more info page (see the docs PR) and breaks in 2027.6.0, six months after it first ships in 2026.12.0.

Draft until home-assistant/supervisor#7447 is merged.


## Type of change
<!--

title: Add a notify entity to Kodi and deprecate the YAML notify platform
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Adds a notify entity to every Kodi config entry with a `kodi.send_message` entity action, and deprecates the legacy Kodi notify platform that is set up in YAML (`notify` with `platform: kodi`).

- Every Kodi config entry gets a notify entity on the device of its media player, with `NotifyEntityFeature.TITLE`. It sends notifications through the existing Kodi connection (`pykodi` `send_notification`), so it can be used with `notify.send_message`.
- New `kodi.send_message` entity action for the options the legacy action took via `data`: `message`, `title`, `icon` (`info`, `warning`, `error`, or an image that the Kodi device can open, as a URL or as a path on the Kodi device; defaults to `info`), and `displaytime` (milliseconds, at least 1500; defaults to 10000).
- The legacy `notify.<name>` actions from YAML keep working unchanged while the YAML is present. Each YAML `platform: kodi` block gets a deprecation repair issue (`breaks_in_ha_version="2027.6.0"`):
  - If a Kodi config entry matches the host (without `<url> or `<url>), port and credentials of the block, the issue names the replacement notify entity of that entry and asks to remove the YAML once the new notify entity and actions are in use. The first matching YAML `name` becomes the entity ID of the notify entity when it is created (through the entity registry). Once created, the entity keeps its ID through the entity registry. The name itself is not stored in the entry.
  - If only a disabled Kodi config entry matches, the issue asks to enable that Kodi device. Once it is enabled, its notify entity is set up and the issue is replaced by the one above.
  - If no Kodi config entry matches, the issue says so and points to the Kodi documentation to add the Kodi device. Ignored discovery entries never match.
- The YAML blocks are read in `async_setup` and validated with the same platform schema the notify integration uses (`YAML_NOTIFY_SCHEMA` in `issue.py`, which `notify.py` uses as `PLATFORM_SCHEMA`). Invalid blocks are skipped and left for the notify integration to report, so they can't name an entity or link an entry.
- The media player snapshot test is limited to the media player platform; the notify entity has its own snapshot and tests.

This is part of the effort to migrate integrations from the legacy notify service to notify entities. Unlike prowl, Kodi config entries are full media player entries, so the YAML is not imported into a new config entry: users without a matching entry add their Kodi device first.

title: Bump bluetti-modbus to 0.57.0
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Bump `bluetti-modbus` from 0.52.0 to 0.57.0.

BLUETTI Modbus is new in 2026.11, so please consider this for the 2026.11 beta.

The release that matters for this integration is 0.56.0: the battery current (`b_c`, register 51220) decodes a raw value of 0 as unknown instead of 3000 A. The register stores the current as an offset from 30000, so a 0 means "no reading", and the Battery current sensor would record 3000 A in its long-term statistics. A Balco 260 expansion pack was seen sending it while reporting its type, voltage and SOC (bluetti-community/bluetti-modbus#138). This integration reads the same field at the power station's own unit, where it has not been seen yet: reads of my unit gave 29939 (6.1 A) and 4.6 A there.

The rest of the range does not change what this integration reads:

- 0.55.0 decodes the inverter fault and warning registers as flags. This integration leaves both registers out of its read plan, so nothing changes until a follow-up uses them.
- 0.53.0, 0.54.0, 0.55.0 and 0.57.0 otherwise only change other models (Apex 300, AC500, FridgePower), which this integration does not support. The Balco 260 profile itself is unchanged.

title: Suggest device area from Matter Actions cluster room groups
body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
When a Matter bridge (e.g. a Hue Bridge) exposes its rooms through the `Actions`
cluster (0x0025), newly created bridged devices now get their area suggested
from the `Room`-type `EndpointListStruct` entries in `EndpointLists`, instead
of landing with no area and requiring the user to assign one manually.

Implementation (`get_suggested_area()` in `matter/adapter.py`):
- Scans every endpoint of the node for an `Actions` cluster (a bridge may put
  it on any endpoint, not just the Aggregator).
- Only considers `EndpointListStruct` entries of type `Room` (`Zone` and
  `Other` are ignored).
- Resolves composed devices by also matching their part endpoint IDs, not
  just the compose parent's.
- Returns `None` (no suggestion, no guessing) when a device is in no room, or
  in more than one room with conflicting names.

The suggestion is passed as `suggested_area` to
`device_registry.async_get_or_create()`, which only applies it when the
device is created for the first time, so an area the user already assigned
is never overridden.

Tested against a real Hue Bridge: bridged lights/plugs were correctly created
in their Hue app room ("Salon") without manual area assignment.

title: Report storage write failures to the caller of an awaited save
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
A storage-mode Lovelace dashboard save could return normally and emit `lovelace_updated` even when the backing storage write failed. `Store._async_handle_write_data` catches `WriteError`/`SerializationError` and only logs them, so `Store.async_save` always resolved successfully, and `LovelaceStorage.async_save` had already committed the new config to memory and fired the event before awaiting the write. The result: the frontend is told the save succeeded, the live dashboard instance serves the new config, but the file on disk still holds the old one.

Two changes:

- `Store.async_save` (the awaited save path) now propagates `WriteError`/`SerializationError` to its caller after logging, via a `raise_errors` flag on `_async_handle_write_data`. Delayed saves and final writes keep the existing log-only behavior, since no caller is awaiting those writes. This means every awaited `store.async_save` across core now correctly reports a failed write instead of silently losing data.
- `LovelaceStorage.async_save` now awaits the store write *before* updating `self._data`, invalidating the cached JSON and firing `lovelace_updated`, so a failed save leaves the in-memory dashboard consistent with what is actually on disk and emits no update event.

The websocket save handler (`lovelace/config/save`) propagates the raised error through `_handle_errors`, so the frontend receives an actual failure response.

body:

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.

-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

ESPHome satellites can now stream the audio from before a microWakeWord detection (esphome/esphome#21885, esphome/aioesphomeapi#1980). That lets Home Assistant verify the wake word, so devices can detect at a lower cutoff.

This PR adds the plumbing. It doesn't verify anything yet: the default is to accept the wake word unless it is a duplicate wake-up.

- **`assist_pipeline`:** `async_pipeline_from_audio_stream` takes an optional `wake_word_detection: wake_word.DetectionResult`. Its `timestamp` is the length in ms of the wake word audio at the start of the stream.
  - The pipeline accepts the detection with `WAKE_WORD_END`, or rejects a duplicate wake-up with the new `WAKE_WORD_REJECTED` event.
  - On acceptance, it removes the wake word audio before speech-to-text.
- **`assist_satellite`:** `async_accept_pipeline_from_satellite` passes `wake_word_detection` through.
- **ESPHome satellite:**
  - Maps the start request's wake word audio to a `DetectionResult`, using the buffered byte count of the channel being streamed. The channels are offset independently.
  - Picks the audio channel at the start of the run, from the STT engine's `audio_processing`, because the wake word audio arrives before `STT_START`.
  - Maps `WAKE_WORD_REJECTED` to the device. On rejection it ends the audio stream, since the device stops streaming without sending end-of-audio.
  - Requesting wake word audio from devices is behind `_request_wake_word_audio`, which is `False` for now. When to request it is decided in a follow-up: when the pipeline's STT (partial transcripts) or an audio-input conversation agent can verify the wake word.

Tested end to end on a Voice PE with `_request_wake_word_audio` temporarily set to `True`: the wake word audio was skipped before speech-to-text.

This is a draft until aioesphomeapi with esphome/aioesphomeapi#1980 is released and bumped here. Firmware: esphome/home-assistant-voice-pe#653.

body:
<!--

## Proposed change
<!--

-->
Add media artwork / cover art support to the System Bridge media player.

System Bridge sends media artwork in `media.thumbnail` (such as base64-encoded `data:`
URLs read from `mpris:artUrl` on Linux, or standard HTTP/HTTPS URLs). This PR adds
support for displaying this artwork in Home Assistant:
- Decodes base64 `data:` URLs via `async_get_media_image` so Home Assistant can proxy
and serve them locally (`/api/media_player_proxy/...`) without bloating the state
machine or recorder.
- Safely validates against allowed image MIME types (`image/gif`, `image/jpeg`,
`image/png`, `image/webp`).
- Caches decoded thumbnails on the entity instance to avoid re-decoding base64 data
during frequent state updates.
- Computes SHA-256 cache hashes for `data:` URLs to handle image cache busting
properly.
- Passes through remote HTTP/HTTPS URLs directly as remote images.

-->

Adds a `binary_sensor` platform to the Škoda integration, using the vehicle status (`status.overall` and `status.detail`) that the integration already fetches on every update:

- Lock (device class `lock`), based on `reliableLockStatus`, falling back to `locked` when the vehicle doesn't report it
- Doors, windows (device classes `door`, `window`)
- Sunroof (device class `window`), only created when the vehicle has one (`UNSUPPORTED` is skipped)
- Trunk, hood (device class `opening`)
- Lights (device class `light`)

A read-only lock entity is not used, as the integration cannot lock or unlock the vehicle. `UNKNOWN` values are reported as `unknown`.

A binary sensor for the charging plug is not included, since `skoda-public-api` 1.3.0 doesn't parse `plugConnectionState`/`plugLockState` yet. That can follow after a library update.

body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change

Part of the series splitting #189108 into one entity platform per PR. This adds the cooking mode of Overkiz ovens (`ogp:Oven`, widget `DynamicOven`, for example Sauter / Brandt / De Dietrich models such as the SOP6615LB) as a select.

- The options are read live from `core:AvailableModesState`, so only the modes the appliance advertises are offered (14 on the SOP6615LB). Selecting a mode sends `setMode`.
- `core:ModeState` and `core:AvailableModesState` are also exposed by other devices that support `setMode` (alarms, heaters, HVAC zones and air vents, 12 device types in the pyoverkiz setup data), so the description is scoped to ovens with a `device_types` filter, like binary_sensor already has.
- The select is unavailable while the oven blocks remote control (`localControl` in `ogp:UnavailableFeaturesState`), through the `OverkizExecutableEntity` base class also introduced in #189467.
- The options are the raw tokens `setMode` expects (`conventionalFan`, `keepingWarm`, ...). They are not translated here: hassfest rejects camelCase translation keys, so translating them needs a mapping layer, better kept for a follow-up.

### How this was tested

On a Sauter SOP6615LB through the Sauter Smart Control server:

- Selecting `keepingWarm`, `bottomFan` and `defrost` from Home Assistant changed the mode on the appliance, and the select followed within a few seconds.
- When a cycle ended or was stopped, the oven went back to its default mode, and the select followed without any command.
- With the oven taken out of its Wi-Fi mode, the select became unavailable, and it came back once the Wi-Fi mode was enabled again.

New tests cover the options read from the device, their update on events, the command and the `localControl` availability.

The oven fixture is the same as in #189241, and `OverkizExecutableEntity` and its test helpers are the same as in #189467, so they will drop out of this diff once those are merged. No new dependency is required.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the

-->

The NX584 client was created without a request timeout, so a call to an unresponsive NX584 server could block forever. This affects config entry setup, the config flow connection check and the zone event watcher.

`pynx584` 0.9.0 (bumped in #189304) added a `timeout` argument to `Client`. This passes a 10 second timeout. For the event long-poll the library adds it on top of the 60 second poll window, so the watcher keeps working as before.

A timeout raises `requests.exceptions.Timeout`, which is already handled: setup raises `ConfigEntryNotReady`, the config flow shows "cannot connect" and the watcher logs the error and retries.

title: Poll Overkiz events every 25 seconds on Sauter Smart Control
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change

While adding support for Sauter ovens to this integration (#189108, split into #189241 and follow-ups), I noticed that the oven state in Home Assistant regularly stopped following the appliance.

On Sauter Smart Control, device state changes that are not triggered by a Home Assistant command can be lost: the end of a cooking cycle, the door being opened or closed, or anything done on the appliance itself. The state then stays wrong until the next command sent from Home Assistant.

The cause is the listening session lifetime. On this server, a session with a registered event listener expires after 25 to 30 seconds without a fetch. With the default 30 second update interval, the next poll regularly hits an expired session, so pyoverkiz logs in again and registers a new, empty listener, and every event received in between is lost. Polling only speeds up after a command, which is why changes made from Home Assistant still show up.

This PR reduces the update interval to 25 seconds for Sauter Smart Control, in the same way the local API and assumed state setups already get their own interval.

This also lowers the load on the server: at 30 seconds the integration logs in again roughly every third poll (each relogin means a middleware JWT request, a login and a new listener), while at 25 seconds it keeps a single session.

### How this was tested

All tests were done on a Sauter oven (SOP6615LB) through the Sauter Smart Control server.

1. **Session lifetime.** A standalone pyoverkiz client registered a listener and fetched events with growing gaps, recording whether the listener had to be registered again. 10, 20 and 25 seconds kept the listener; 30, 35 and 45 seconds ended in `NotAuthenticatedError` followed by a new listener.
2. **Events lost by the integration.** With the current 30 second interval, the oven state stopped updating in Home Assistant while the cloud kept the right value: a door closed on the appliance never showed up, while `/setup/devices` returned the correct state at the same time. Reloading or re-adding the integration did not help.
3. **Before and after, with the integration.** 2 minute timed cycles were started from Home Assistant, and I waited for each cycle to end on its own, with debug logging enabled to count relogins:

| Update interval | End of cycle seen by Home Assistant | Relogins during the run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 30 s (current), run 1 | 7 s after the end (no relogin right after the end) | 3 |
| 30 s (current), run 2 | never, stuck on "cooking" (relogin right after the end) | 2 |
| 25 s (this PR) | 7 s after the end | 0 |

At 30 seconds, an event is lost whenever the next poll hits an expired session, so whether a given change shows up depends on timing.

4. **Stability at 25 seconds.** Over 10 minutes without any command, all 24 polls were 25 seconds apart and kept the same session (no relogin). During that window, the door was opened and closed three times on the appliance, and all six events were received.
5. **Unit test.** A new test checks that a Sauter Smart Control entry polls after 25 seconds. It fails without this change.

This is different from the limitation documented in home-assistant/home-assistant.io#36791: here the device does broadcast its state changes, and they are lost by the integration.

Brandt uses the same Overkiz cluster (`ha3-1.overkiz.com`) and the same middleware as Sauter Smart Control, so it is likely affected as well. I could not verify it without a Brandt account, so it is left out of this change.

body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The `get_prices_for_date` action now returns the prices the coordinator already has stored, instead of calling the Nord Pool API every time.

As raised in #188796, templates that call the action whenever the price sensor updates make a new API request every 15 minutes, even though the coordinator already holds yesterday's, today's and (when published) tomorrow's prices.

The action now uses the stored `DeliveryPeriodData` when the requested date is stored, the currency matches the config entry and all requested areas are part of the config entry. title: Update Marketplace update entities when a repository is refreshed from its page
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Opening a repository page in the Marketplace panel refreshes the repository from GitHub (`marketplace/repository/info`), but only the panel is told about the result. The update entity is not, so its state keeps the versions from the last catalog refresh (up to 6 hours old). When a new release was just published, the page says "Update available" while the Update button opens the more-info dialog of the update entity, which still says "Up-to-date" with the install button disabled.

The repository now notifies the entity coordinator of its category in `async_dispatch_changed`, next to the signal that tells the panel. Every path that refreshes a repository goes through it (the repository page, setting a version, installs, the background refresh), so the entity and the panel see the same versions at the same time. The entity only writes state when `last_fetched` moved, as before. The explicit coordinator call in the refresh command is removed since it is now redundant.

title: Bump lifx-async to 7.13.2
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Bump `lifx-async` from 7.13.1 to 7.13.2.

7.13.2 fixes request timeouts on Linux. `UdpTransport` set `SO_REUSEPORT` on every bind, and every connection binds port 0, so the kernel could give a new socket a port another connection already held. Replies for both connections then went to only one of them, and the other connection's request timed out even though the bulb answered every retry. lifx-async now sets `SO_REUSEPORT` only when the caller asks for a fixed port.

`LifxTimeoutError` messages also now name the request that went unanswered, for example `No response to GetVersion from 192.0.2.1 after 11 attempts`, so a bulb that ignores one query can be told apart from one that is offline.

title: Deprecate silent and default speeds in Velux covers
body:
<!--

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR adds the standard `slow` cover speed to Velux covers and deprecates the Velux specific `silent` and `default` speeds.

The cover entity component defines `fast`, `medium` and `slow` as standard speeds, and moving without a speed uses the device's default speed. Velux exposed the pyvlx velocity names `silent`, `fast` and `default` instead.

**Behavior**
- `slow` moves the cover with `Velocity.SILENT` and `fast` with `Velocity.FAST`. Velux has no medium speed.
- `silent` still moves the cover with `Velocity.SILENT`, and creates the `deprecated_speed_silent` repair issue asking to use `speed: slow` instead.
- `default` still moves the cover at its default speed (pyvlx handles `velocity=None` the same as `Velocity.DEFAULT`), and creates the `deprecated_speed_default` repair issue asking to remove the `speed` option.
- The repair issues are created when a deprecated speed is used, have a stable issue ID per speed, mention the entity it was last used with, and break in 2027.6.0.

The deprecated speeds `silent` and `default` stay in `supported_speeds` until they are removed, because the cover entity drops any speed that is not in `supported_speeds` before it reaches the integration. `capability_attributes` is overridden to only advertise `slow` and `fast`, so the deprecated speeds can't be selected anymore while existing automations and scripts keep working until they are updated.

Related to: #189429

Imou cloud live URLs are short-lived. Home Assistant caches the `Stream` created from the first `stream_source()` call, so reopening later can reuse an expired URL.

title: Add water heater platform to Modbus
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Add a `water_heater` platform to the Modbus integration.

Heat pump water heaters and boilers with a Modbus interface could so far only be added as a `climate` entity, which does not fit them: HVAC modes don't map to water heater operation modes like eco, heat pump or electric, and the device does not show up as a water heater in the UI.

The new platform is configured in YAML under `water_heaters:` and supports:

- current and target temperature, with the same data type, scale and offset options as climate (`current_temp_scale`, `target_temp_scale`, …)
- operation mode via `operation_mode_register`, mapping register values to `state_off`, `state_eco`, `state_electric`, `state_performance`, `state_high_demand`, `state_heat_pump` and `state_gas`. A mode can have a list of values; the first one is written.
- on/off via `onoff_coil` or `onoff_register` (with `on_value` / `off_value`), which enables `WaterHeaterEntityFeature.ON_OFF` and adds `off` to the operation list

The configuration keys follow the existing climate keys where they mean the same thing. The schema is also added to `PLATFORM_SCHEMAS`.

```yaml
modbus:
  - name: hub1
  type: serial
  port: /dev/ttyUSB0
  baudrate: 9600
  bytesize: 8
  method: rtu
  parity: N
  stopbits: 1
  water_heaters:
  - name: "Heat pump water heater"
  slave: 1
  address: 0x0049
  target_temp_register: 0x0302
  min_temp: 15
  max_temp: 75
  temp_step: 1
  onoff_register: 0x0305
  operation_mode_register:
  address: 0x0304
  values:
  state_heat_pump: 2
  state_eco: 9
  state_high_demand: [10, 11]
  state_electric: 12
```

Tested on a Foshan Aircarrier YT-300TK2 heat pump water heater over RS-485 (Modbus RTU).

title: Add reboot button to Watergate
body:
Add a button platform with a single Reboot entity that calls the client's async_reboot. A lost response is expected while the device restarts, so WatergateIndeterminateError is treated as success; any other WatergateApiException raises HomeAssistantError.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->


Add a `button` platform to Watergate with one entity, **Reboot** (`ButtonDeviceClass.RESTART`, `EntityCategory.CONFIG`), which calls the client's `async_reboot()`.
The client marks the reboot command as non-idempotent, so it is never retried after an ambiguous timeout, and the integration does not retry either. A lost response is normal while the device restarts, so a `WatergateIndeterminateError` ("sent, outcome unknown") is logged at debug level and **not** reported as a failure. Any other `WatergateApiException` raises `HomeAssistantError` (`reboot_failed`), the same pattern as the valve/switch/number actions.
Pressing the button adds no sleeps or forced refreshes: state is refreshed by the next poll or the device's `online` webhook.

title: Add standard navigation actions to media player and remote entities
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Add a standard way to send navigation (d-pad) actions to media players and remotes, so automations, blueprints and the frontend do not need each integration's raw key codes.

Architecture discussion: <url> This PR is a prototype for that discussion and stays a draft until it is settled.

- New `MediaPlayerEntityFeature.NAVIGATE` and `media_player.navigate` entity service with a required `direction` field: `up`, `down`, `left`, `right`, `select`, `back`, `home`, `menu` (`MediaPlayerNavigation`).
- The same on `remote` (`RemoteEntityFeature.NAVIGATE`, `remote.navigate`, `RemoteNavigation`), so both options in the discussion can be compared.
- A `supported_navigation` capability attribute on both platforms, listing the directions a device supports. It defaults to all directions. A direction outside the list is rejected with a service validation error.
- `navigate` / `async_navigate` on `MediaPlayerEntity` and `RemoteEntity` for integrations to implement.
- Android TV Remote implements both of its entities by mapping each direction to its Android key code (`DPAD_UP`, `DPAD_CENTER`, `BACK`, `HOME`, `MENU`, ...), sharing the mapping between them.

Other integrations are not changed here.

title: Fix Reolink two way audio on the second lens of dual lens cameras
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

On dual lens cameras such as the Reolink Duo, two way audio is only offered on the lens 0 camera entity. The lens 1 entity never gets the mic button.

`reolink_aio` detects the `two_way_audio` capability in the channel capabilities loop of `get_channel_data`, which iterates `_channels` (`[0]` on a dual lens camera) rather than `_stream_channels` (`[0, 1]`). The capability therefore only ends up on channel 0, while the camera entity checks it on its own lens channel.

Two way audio is a property of the camera as a whole, not of a single lens, so the camera entity now looks up the capability on channel 0 when the camera is a dual lens camera. This mirrors how `reolink_aio` itself falls back to channel 0 for dual lens cameras in `api_version`.

The existing two way audio test is extended with a dual lens case where the mock reports the capability only for channel 0 and the lens 1 entity is checked. The host mock is set to a standalone camera for all cases, since the conftest default is an NVR that returns the same camera UID for every channel, which makes the lens 1 entities collide on unique ID and get dropped.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Adds a reauthentication flow to A Better Routeplanner, which brings the integration to the **silver** quality scale. It is the flow that was split off from the initial PR (#174058) to keep that one small.

- `reauth` / `reauth_confirm` steps, following Withings. Confirming runs the normal account-linking flow again.
- The new token must belong to the same ABRP account as the entry, checked against the id_token subject (the config entry's unique ID). A different account aborts with `wrong_account`; a token without a refresh token aborts with `oauth_error`. On success the token is updated and the entry reloads. Reauth does not re-read the garage; setup does that on reload.
- Reauth starts from the OAuth2 session when a token refresh is rejected, and from the coordinator when the telemetry stream reports `AUTH_FAILED`, so a revoked session no longer leaves the entry unavailable until it is removed and re-added.
- `reauthentication-flow: done` in `quality_scale.yaml` and `"quality_scale": "silver"` in the manifest. Every other silver rule was already done or exempt.

title: Fix Sofar reload loop and phantom sensors after a night setup
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Fix the asleep setup from <url> new in 2026.11: a night setup now builds its entities from the components the last answered setup stored, so a PV-only inverter no longer gets six phantom meter sensors, and the first answer reloads only when the inverter turns out to serve something else, which stops the repeated reloads at dawn (six in seven minutes on a KTLX-G3).
Without that reload, the firmware versions are read in the background. The listener removes itself on the first answer and needs no unload hook, since the coordinator shuts down on unload. The stored set also covers the fault log, replacing `has_fault_log`, which only 2026.11.0b0 ever wrote.
A night setup can store readings the type does not predict, such as on a serial only the masks identify, so entities now pick their coordinator from sofar-modbus’s READING_COMPONENTS instead of the type’s guess.

Beta fix for 2026.11, live-tested on a KTLX-G3 through a proxy that makes the inverter sleep and wake.

title: Improve two entity names of NRGkick integration
body:
Re-generate snapshot for sensors.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Two NRGkick sensors had misleading names:

- **Charging current**: the device documents this value as the "max current signaled to EV", the current the car is allowed to draw. It's not the measured current. In a live test with charging paused, it showed 14 A while 0.02 A was flowing. It also had the same name as the "Charging current" number entity that sets the current. Renamed to **Offered charging current**.
- **Charging voltage**: this is the average voltage of all phases, and it is reported also while not charging. Renamed to **Average voltage**.

Only the names change. Translation keys and unique IDs stay the same, so existing entity IDs and history are kept.
The original names were corresponding to the API names, but the new names consider the description of the entities.

title: Ask to accept the La Marzocco privacy policy in config and reauth flows
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

La Marzocco now rejects cloud requests with a 403 (`USER_MUST_ACCEPT_POLICY`) until the user has accepted the latest privacy policy. pylamarzocco 2.5.3 (#189408) raises `PolicyAcceptanceRequired` for this and adds `accept_privacy_policy()`.

- Config flow: when listing the machines requires policy acceptance, a new `accept_policy` step is shown. Submitting it accepts the privacy policy, with optional profiling and commercial consents, after which the flow continues as before (machine selection, discovery or reauth).
- Setup and coordinator updates raise `ConfigEntryAuthFailed` on `PolicyAcceptanceRequired`, so a reauth flow is started that leads the user to the same step.

title: Send VAD end for provider endpointing and use it for Cloud STT v2
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->


## Proposed change

STT v2 detects the end of speech itself, so it no longer requires external VAD. When the provider ends the voice command, the pipeline now sends STT_VAD_END with the timestamp of the last audio chunk. This allows satellites to stop their microphone early and report the status more accurately.

Since STT v2 falls back to STT v1 for some languages, added async_get_audio_processing(metadata) to STT entities and legacy providers so audio processing can depend on the request.

body:

`async_get_available_entity_id` cuts the generated entity ID at 255 characters. When the cut lands right after an underscore, the entity ID ends with `_`, which is not a valid entity ID, and adding the entity fails with `InvalidEntityFormatError`. Seen with MQTT discovery from teddyCloud, where an entity name containing a long description produced `number.teddycloud_encode_stream_max_size_..._you_ll_need_`. As suggested by @jbouwh in #189192, this fixes it in core instead of in MQTT.

title: Use the discovery subtype for the Midea token check
body:
## Proposed change

Keep the subtype that LAN discovery reports instead of overwriting it with the cloud model number.

`async_step_auto()` unconditionally did:

```python
self.found_device[CONF_SUBTYPE] = device_info.get("model_number")
```

Since midea-local 15.0.0 `discover()` returns a typed `subtype` (`_extract_subtype()`), this line replaced the correct integer with the cloud string (`"5"`). The entry then stored `"5"`, and `MideaDevice._subtype` is compared against integer constants (`X31_SUBTYPE = 5`), so the string never matched and a B1 oven fell back to the X00/X01 query set, which that model ignores — setup ended with `No supported query protocol` at the token-check connection.

The cloud value is now only used when discovery does not know the subtype, and it is coerced to `int`; the config entry conversion is coerced as well so entries written by older flows (which stored the cloud string verbatim) keep working.

Verified against midea-local 15.0.0 on three devices on the same network, `_extract_subtype()` returns the expected value (oven `0BS5051W` → 5, AC `22013005` → 0, dishwasher `7600645N` → 3), and the cloud `modelNumber` agrees.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The v1 → v2.1 config entry migration added in #184863 resolves the deprecated `curtain`, `ceiling_light`, `hygrometer` and `plug` sensor types by parsing the model from the device's last advertisement. SwitchBot devices only send the model (service data) in the scan response, which a passively scanning adapter or proxy never receives. When a passive proxy held the best advertisement, `parse_advertisement_data()` returned no model and the migration raised `ConfigEntryNotReady` forever, even though the entry worked on the legacy type in 2026.10.x. The error also said the device could not be found, while it was in range and advertising.

This PR changes the migration to:

- Check the advertisement of every scanner that hears the device (`bluetooth.async_scanner_devices_by_address`), not only the best one. An actively scanning proxy in range now resolves the exact model, for example `curtain_3`.
- Keep the legacy type when a scanner currently hears the device but no advertisement carries the model, if that type is still supported (`curtain`, `ceiling_light`). This is the type these entries ran on before the upgrade, and the coordinator parses their passive advertisements with the model hint. Devices no scanner hears still retry, as before.
- Raise a dedicated `model_not_determined_error` with `ACTIVE_ADVERTISEMENT` reachability diagnostics for the types that must still wait (`hygrometer`, `plug`), instead of reusing `device_not_found_error` with connection diagnostics.

Known trade-off: if only passive scanners have reported a Curtain 3 or Ceiling Light Pro when the migration runs, it keeps the legacy type for good. It works as before, but the Curtain 3 speed settings are not offered. Resolving the exact model again on a later setup could be a follow-up.

`async_setup` starts the discovery as a background task, which `async_block_till_done()` doesn't wait for. title: Add local RGM and conductor power sensors to Teslemetry
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

For Teslemetry energy sites paired with their Powerwall for local control, this adds two power sensors read from the Powerwall gateway's local status, which the Tesla cloud does not provide: `solar_rgm_power` and `conductor_power`, the real power the gateway reports for its `SOLAR_RGM` and `CONDUCTOR` meter locations, parsed by aiopowerwall's `current_power()`. Both are disabled by default, like the existing `generator_power`, and go on the existing energy site device from the local status coordinator. Each one is only created when the gateway reports its meter in the first refresh; if that first refresh fails, both are created and stay unavailable until the gateway answers, matching the local binary sensors. A failed poll makes them unavailable until the gateway answers again.

This builds on core <url> (local grid and site binary sensors and `TeslemetryLocalStatusCoordinator`), which has merged and is on fork dev, so this PR's diff is only its own change. It runs next to dev's `enable_local_polling` cloud/local merge on the live and info coordinators, which it does not change. Beyond reuse, it changes no 186730 code except moving its paired-site test helper into `tests/components/teslemetry/__init__.py` as `setup_paired_platform` so the sensor tests share it, and adding the `SOLAR_RGM` and `CONDUCTOR` meters to its `powerwall_status.json` test fixture.

title: Add option to pregenerate TTS so that media players don't time out on long messages
body:
## Proposed change

Various media players have timeouts that trigger when they are waiting for a long TTS message to be synthesized and played. This PR adds an optional pregenerate option to the TTS service which waits with calling the media player till the TTS message has been synthesized. title: Fix Axis Companion camera streams
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
AXIS Companion cameras (e.g. AXIS Companion Cube L) reject media and event requests unless the `Axis-Orig-Sw=true` query parameter is present. Without it the RTSP stream and the still image return 403 Forbidden, and the RTSP event stream never starts, so the camera shows as unavailable/idle and no binary sensors or lights are created.

The `axis` library already supports this through `Configuration.is_companion` (added in Kane610/axis#527, released in v65), but the integration never enabled it, and `camera.py` builds its own URLs without the parameter.

This PR:
- Detects Companion devices in the config flow from the product full name (basic device info, falling back to the `root.Brand` parameters) and stores the result in the config entry. Existing entries are detected once on their next setup.
- Enables the library's companion mode after VAPIX initialisation, which also fixes the event stream. It can't be enabled before, as Companion devices reject the initialisation requests (e.g. `apidiscovery.cgi`) when `Axis-Orig-Sw` is present.
- Adds `Axis-Orig-Sw=true` to the still image, MJPEG and RTSP URLs for Companion devices.

Non-Companion devices are unaffected.

Tested on an AXIS Companion Cube L and an AXIS Companion Cube LW (both firmware 9.80.132) on Home Assistant 2026.10.4: live video now plays, and the IR light, PIR, sound, day/night and motion entities are created. An AXIS P3265-LV (AXIS OS 10.12) continues to work unchanged.

title: Abort the WattWächter config flow for devices set up through MQTT
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The WattWächter can also publish MQTT discovery for Home Assistant. Users who first connected the device through MQTT and then add this integration (for example from the zeroconf discovery) end up with every sensor twice, which also double counts consumption if both are added to the Energy dashboard.

The config flow now aborts with `already_configured_mqtt` when the MQTT integration already has a device for it. The device's MQTT discovery uses its MQTT client ID as the device identifier, so the flow reads the client ID from the device settings it already fetches for the device name, and looks for a device with the identifier `("mqtt", <client ID>)` that belongs to an enabled MQTT config entry. The check runs in the zeroconf step (so the discovery isn't offered) and again when the discovery is confirmed, in the user step and in the auth step. If the settings can't be read, the flow continues as before. Existing config entries, reauthentication and reconfiguration are not affected; the check only runs when adding the device.

The abort message explains how to switch: turn off MQTT on the device and delete its MQTT device in Home Assistant.

body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Add a reconfigure flow so users can change the IP address of an already configured Sonic device without deleting and re-adding the integration (Gold rule `reconfiguration-flow`).
- `async_step_reconfigure` pre-fills the current IP and validates it by connecting to the device with the same code the user step uses (extracted into `_async_get_serial_number`, no duplication; same `cannot_connect` error key).

- `strings.json`: `reconfigure` step and `wrong_device` abort (`reconfigure_successful` comes from the shared strings). `quality_scale.yaml`: `reconfiguration-flow: done`.

title: Treat missing iCloud Reminders zone as an acceptable state
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->

No. Accounts that already have Reminders data behave exactly as before.

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Since the to-do platform was added (#181058), the reminders coordinator
polls the CloudKit Reminders zone for every iCloud account. An account
that has never used Reminders has no such zone, so every poll failed and
logged:

`Error fetching icloud data: Error fetching reminders: Zone changes
failed: ZONE_NOT_FOUND (Zone does not exist)`

A missing zone is a permanent account state, not a failure: the user
simply does not use Reminders, so there is nothing to fetch and nothing
to repair. This PR treats it as an acceptable state:

- The `ZONE_NOT_FOUND` payload pyicloud attaches to `RemindersApiError`
  is detected; every other failure keeps the existing `UpdateFailed`
  behaviour.
- The state is logged once at info level, and polling backs off to an
  hour instead of failing every 5 minutes.
- The last known snapshot is returned (not an empty dict), so existing
  to-do entities are never removed from the registry by
  `_sync_lists()`.
- Normal polling resumes, and lists appear by themselves, once the
  account has Reminders data.

title: Share cached English translation strings across languages
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
This PR makes the English translation cache the single source for the English fallback strings of all other languages.

Currently, every load of a non-English language reads the English translation files again and builds the English fallback strings twice: once into the requested language's cache, and once into the English cache if it isn't there yet. Each copy is flattened and validated separately, so the same fallback strings exist in several places and are loaded once per additional language.

With this change:

- English is loaded once into the English cache. Other languages are seeded from it, and only the requested language's own file is read and overlaid on top.
- All languages share the same English key and value strings, instead of each holding its own copy.
- `_async_get_component_strings` loads a single language, which removes the multi-language bookkeeping from it and from `_async_load`.
- The translation invalidation behaviour is kept: all file I/O happens first, and components invalidated during it are discarded before anything is cached. The existing invalidation test was adapted to the per-language loads.

The resulting cache contents are unchanged (verified by comparing a digest of the full cache before and after this change).

### Impact

Measured on the translation cache for all 1112 built-in integrations with translations. Non-English files were synthesised from `en.json` with about 70% of strings translated, since a source checkout only has `en.json`. Memory is what's retained after `gc.collect()`, measured with `tracemalloc`. Time is the median of 3 runs and includes the synthetic translation step, so it is indicative only.

| Scenario | Retained memory (dev → PR) | `en.json` reads (dev → PR) | Time (dev → PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Load `de` | 41.6 MiB → 26.1 MiB (−37%) | 1098 → 1098 | 1.71 s → 1.46 s |
| Load `en`, then `de` | 45.5 MiB → 26.1 MiB (−43%) | 2196 → 1098 | 1.88 s → 1.79 s |
| Load `de`, then `fr` | 56.1 MiB → 30.9 MiB (−45%) | 2196 → 1098 | 4.49 s → 2.71 s |

Real installations only load set-up integrations, so absolute numbers are smaller, but the saving scales with the number of loaded integrations. English-only installations are unaffected.

title: Don't fail Tibber setup on consumption backend errors
body:
A Tibber backend error (e.g. GraphQL INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR on the consumption endpoint) raised UpdateFailed in the data coordinator, which made the first refresh fail and put the whole config entry into setup_retry. The price sensors and Data API entities, which use separate endpoints, never loaded.

Fetching consumption data, production data and inserting statistics are now independent optional steps. A retryable error in one of them logs a warning once (debug afterwards), logs an info message on recovery, and is retried on the next 20 minute update. Fatal errors keep reloading the entry.

<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
`TibberDataCoordinator` fetches consumption and production data and inserts long-term statistics. A Tibber backend error in any of those steps was turned into `UpdateFailed`. This happens, for example, when Tibber answers a GraphQL `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` for `viewer.homes[].consumption`, which pyTibber raises as `RetryableHttpExceptionError`.

`async_setup_entry` awaits `async_config_entry_first_refresh()` for this coordinator, so the whole config entry ended up in `setup_retry`. The price sensors and Data API entities use separate endpoints that still work, but they never loaded.

This PR makes consumption fetch, production fetch and statistics insertion independent optional steps:
- A `RetryableHttpExceptionError` in one step logs a warning once (debug on repeats) and an info message on recovery. The step is retried on the next 20 minute update.
- The other steps and all other entities are unaffected.
- `FatalHttpExceptionError` still reloads the entry, so auth problems behave as before.

title: Fail fast when the Ollama server cannot be reached
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important

  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.

-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

When the Ollama host is up but drops connections, Assist waits about two minutes and then fails with a generic error. Two things cause it.

The client created in `__init__.py` had no timeout, so a dropped connection waited for the OS TCP timeout. It now has a connect timeout of `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` (5 s). The read stays unbounded, so slow models can still take their time to answer.

With `stream=True`, `client.chat()` only returns a generator. The HTTP request runs while the stream is read, outside the `try`, so connection errors and `ResponseError` from the server escaped as unexpected errors. In `entity.py`, reading the stream is now inside the `try`, which also catches `httpx2.HTTPError`. In the stream path, ollama-python raises `httpx.ConnectError`, not the builtin `ConnectionError` the issue mentions.

New tests raise a connection error and a `ResponseError` from the stream, and check the client timeout. Without the change, all three fail. Two config flow tests now accept the extra `timeout` argument.
