title: Connect to Supervisor over its Unix socket
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Supervisor now offers Core a Unix socket and passes its path in `SUPERVISOR_SOCKET` (home-assistant/supervisor#7420). Supervisor identifies the caller by the socket, so no token is needed. When that variable is set, every Core -> Supervisor request goes over the socket:

- the aiohasupervisor client (`unix_socket` support added in aiohasupervisor 0.9.0)
- the legacy `HassIO.send_command` passthrough
- the frontend passthrough view (`HassIOView`)
- the Core -> Supervisor hop of ingress
- the system health ping

Without `SUPERVISOR_SOCKET`, Core keeps using TCP with `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`, so older Supervisors keep working.

Changes:

- New `SupervisorConnection` in `handler.py` holds the session, base URL, socket path and auth headers, from the `get_supervisor_connection(hass)` singleton. The aiohasupervisor client, `HassIOView`, ingress and system health all use it. `HassIO` keeps only `send_command` and is reached through `get_legacy_supervisor_client(hass)`, so a search for that function shows exactly what still uses the legacy passthrough (`websocket_api`, `llm`).
- `system_health.async_check_can_reach_url` takes an optional `session`, so the ping can go over the socket.
- The socket session is a plain `aiohttp.ClientSession` with a `UnixConnector`, because HA's client session helpers always use a TCP connector. It uses `DummyCookieJar`: every response over the socket comes from host `localhost`, so a real jar would store cookies an app sets through ingress and replay them to every app, user and Supervisor. Over TCP, aiohttp's jar already ignores cookies for IP hosts. It also uses HA's larger header limits and is closed on `EVENT_HOMEASSISTANT_CLOSE`.
- `async_setup` now requires `SUPERVISOR`, plus either `SUPERVISOR_SOCKET` or `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN`, and logs which one is missing. The environment variable names are now constants.

**Why `SUPERVISOR` stays required.** `SUPERVISOR_TOKEN` is only needed for TCP and will go away once TCP from Core is removed. `SUPERVISOR` (Supervisor's IP) is needed permanently, even after Core and Supervisor talk to each other over Unix sockets in both directions:

1. Supervisor still checks that the frontend works over TCP, because clients reach Core over TCP and a socket check would not prove that. Core therefore still excludes Supervisor's IP from the IP ban list (`http/ban.py` via `get_supervisor_ip()`).
2. System health links to the observer at `<url>>:4357` for more information when Supervisor can't be reached. The socket can't provide that.

This is WP1.3 of home-assistant/supervisor#7389 (epic home-assistant/epics#146). Earlier packages: home-assistant/supervisor#7408, home-assistant/supervisor#7420 and home-assistant-libs/python-supervisor-client#449.

title: Limit how often UniFi device CPU, memory and temperature sensors update
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
UniFi OS consoles push a full record for every device about every 2 seconds. On my Cloud Gateway Fiber the CPU, memory and temperature values change on most of those pushes, so each push becomes a new state. Over 24 hours the gateway memory sensor wrote 53,957 states and the CPU sensor 41,214: about 22 % of everything my HA instance recorded. #184334 shows the same on another UCG-Fiber, where these sensors were 98 % of all states. Rounding doesn't help, because the CPU reading moves by several points between pushes.

This adds an optional `min_update_interval` to `UnifiSensorEntityDescription`, next to the existing `value_changed_fn`, and sets it to 15 s (the default scan interval, the same rate System Monitor uses) for device CPU, memory and temperature sensors. A changed value is accepted only when 15 s have passed since the last accepted one. Otherwise it is skipped, and the next push after that writes the current value. No timers are added.

The limit is skipped when the entity is added, after a websocket reconnect, when the entity comes back from unavailable, and for changes to or from unknown, so those still show immediately. Availability is still written straight away by the base entity.

I replayed 6 hours of my recorder history through this logic:
- Gateway CPU: 1,650 → 217 states per hour. Gateway memory: 2,146 → 216.
- 5-minute means stay within about 2 points for CPU and 0.2 for memory.
- The cost: CPU peaks shorter than 15 s no longer show up, so the 5-minute max in long-term statistics is on average about 9 points lower for gateway CPU.
- APs and switches are practically unchanged, because their values rarely change between pushes.

`test_device_system_stats` and `test_device_temperatures` now move the clock 15 s before sending the second update, since that update would otherwise be held back. Two new tests cover the limit and the cases where it is skipped.

<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the

Replace the `pico2wave` binary with the [py-nanotts](<url>) library. Pico TTS no longer needs an external binary in the `PATH`, so it now works on any installation type, not just the container image where `pico2wave` is built in.

title: Fix System Monitor IP sensor setup with missing addresses
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Fix a System Monitor sensor platform setup failure when IP address data is temporarily unavailable from the coordinator.

Currently, `get_ip_address()` assumes that `entity.coordinator.data.addresses` is always a mapping. However, this value can be `None` during sensor initialization, resulting in:

```text
TypeError: argument of type 'NoneType' is not a container or iterable
```

This exception can interrupt the entire System Monitor sensor platform setup, leaving unrelated CPU, memory, and disk sensors unavailable.

The proposed change adds a defensive check that returns `None` when address data has not yet been collected, allowing sensor initialization to proceed normally.

A regression test has been added to verify this behavior.

**Validation performed:**

- Reproduced the original exception using Home Assistant Core 2026.10.4 in an isolated Docker environment.
- Verified that the patched implementation handles `addresses=None` without raising an exception.
- Confirmed that valid IPv4 address resolution remains unchanged.
- Successfully initialized the System Monitor integration and verified operational CPU, memory, disk, and IPv4 sensors in the patched QA environment.
- Executed the official System Monitor test suite against the `dev` branch using Python 3.14.10: **39 tests passed, 90 snapshots passed**.
- Ruff lint and formatting checks passed.

The integration requires these to be enabled for setup to complete but current behaviour means that it will just raise a "UnknownEndpointError".

The PR adds the required exception handling in the coordinator to accommodate this changed exception path.

title: Fix literal translations in Midea washer, dryer and fridge strings
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
Several English state names of the `midea` washer, dryer and fridge sensors are literal translations from Chinese and don't make sense in English (and are hard to translate). See #189329.

The HACS `midea_ac_lan` integration (where `midea-local` comes from) has both the Chinese originals (`zh-Hans.json`) and corrected English for these values. This PR uses those names, so every change here is backed by the Chinese original:

| Key | Before | After | Chinese |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dry_program.four_piece_suit` | Four piece suit | Bedding set | 床品四件套 |
| `dry_program.sun_quilt` | Sun quilt | Quilt airing | 晒被子 |
| `dry_program.western_trouser` | Western trouser | Dress trousers | 西裤 |
| `dry_program/wash_program.bucket_self_clean` | Bucket self clean | Drum clean | 筒自洁 |
| `dry_program/wash_program.big` | Big | Bulky items | 大件 |
| `dry_program.big_60` | Big 60 | Bulky items 60 | 大件60 |
| `dry_program.big_dry` | Big dry | Bulky items drying | 大件烘 |
| `dry_program.bracket_dry` | Bracket dry | Rack drying | 支架烘 |
| `dry_program.little_fast_dry` | Little fast dry | Quick dry small load | 少量快烘 |
| `dry_program.small_piece_dry` | Small piece dry | Small items | 小件烘 |
| `dry_program.fresh_remove_smell` | Fresh remove smell | Deodorizing refresh | 清新除味 |
| `dry_program.cold_air_fresh_air` | Cold air fresh air | Cool-air refresh | 冷风清新 |
| `dry_program.wool_nurse` | Wool nurse | Wool care | 羊毛护理 |
| `dry_program/wash_program.fiber` | Fiber | Synthetics | 化纤 |
| `dry_program/wash_program.cotton` | Cotton | Cotton and linen | 棉麻 |
| `wash_program.single_dehytration` | Single dehydration | Spin only | 单脱水 |
| `wash_program.jacket` | Jacket | Outdoor jackets | 冲锋衣 |
| `variable_mode.freeze_warm` | Freeze warm | Freeze / warm | 冷冻 / 保温 |
| `variable_mode.fresh_product` | Fresh product | Fresh produce | 鲜品 |
| `wash_program.water_cold_wash` | Water cold wash | Cold wash | 冷水洗 |
| `wash_program.water_eco` | Water eco | Energy saving | 节能 |
| `wash_program.water_fiber` | Water fiber | Synthetics | 化纤 |
| `wash_program.water_intelligent` | Water intelligent | Smart wash | 智能洗 |
| `wash_program.water_mixed_wash` | Water mixed wash | Mixed wash | 混合洗 |
| `wash_program.water_remove_mite_wash` | Water remove mite wash | Mite removal | 除螨洗 |
| `wash_program.water_steep` | Water steep | Soak wash | 浸泡洗 |
| `wash_program.water_underwear` | Water underwear | Underwear | 内衣 |
| `wash_program.new_water_cotton` | New water cotton | Cotton and linen | 棉麻 |

**Spin (washing machines, `da`/`db`).** 脱水 means spin here; `midea_ac_lan` already uses "Spin" for it (脱水时间 = "Spin time", 单脱水 = "Spin only"):

| Key | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `sensor.dehydration_level` (entity name) | Dehydration level | Spin level |
| `sensor.dehydration_speed` (entity name) | Dehydration speed | Spin speed |
| `sensor.dehydration_time` (entity name) | Dehydration time | Spin time |
| `wash_program.dehydration_min` | Dehydration min | Spin min |
| `wash_program.rinsing_dehydration` | Rinsing dehydration | Rinse and spin |

**Timed programs** (after review, see the discussion with @NoRi2909). Midea writes minutes as 60′ and drops the ′ in code names, e.g. `wash_drying_60` = "洗烘60′" in the user manuals:

| Key | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `wash_program.fast_wash_30` | Fast wash 30 | Quick wash 30 min |
| `wash_program.fast_wash_60` | Fast wash 60 | Quick wash 60 min |
| `wash_program.wash_drying_60` | Wash and dry 60 | Wash and dry 60 min |
| `dry_program.quick_dry_20` | Quick dry 20 | Quick dry 20 min |
| `dry_program.quick_dry_30` | Quick dry 30 | Quick dry 30 min |
| `dry_program.big_60` | Bulky items 60 | Bulky items 60 min |

The `water_` prefix on wash programs carries no meaning in the Chinese originals, so those are plain program names. A few of the new names coincide with existing ones (e.g. `water_fiber` and `fiber` are both "Synthetics"), the same as in `midea_ac_lan`; they come from different device variants.

Only `strings.json` values change; keys are untouched.

**Why the test snapshot changed:** the program names above are sensor *state* translations, and the snapshot stores states by their keys (e.g. `'cotton'`), so those need no test change. The three spin sensors are different: there the *entity name* changes, and the snapshot stores the name (`original_name`, `friendly_name`) and the entity ID generated from it (`sensor.front_load_washer_dehydration_time` → `sensor.front_load_washer_spin_time`). So `tests/components/midea/snapshots/test_sensor.ambr` is updated for those three entities only; the diff looks large because snapshot entries are sorted by name and the renamed entries moved from "d" to "s". Existing installations keep their entity IDs (same `translation_key` and `unique_id`); only newly added devices get `…_spin_…` IDs. The rice cooker modes and a few wash programs (`heart_wash`, `embathe`, `green_wool`, `love`, `ssp`) are left as they are, because no Chinese source was found for them. Those are still open in #189329.

I found these while translating Home Assistant into Hungarian.

title: Recommend Intermediate v6 and clarify the http SSL profile repair
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

-->
## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Follow-up to #183916. It changes the recommended (and default) SSL profile to Intermediate v6, and rewrites the repair text. The `ssl_profile_outdated` repair was hard to understand for users, and it read as if the SSL certificate was outdated and needed to be regenerated. The text changes:

- The title is now "Update the HTTPS encryption settings" instead of naming the SSL profile.
- The dialog opens by saying that the HTTPS encryption settings are outdated, which profile is in use, and that the SSL certificate is not affected.
- It explains the v4/v6 naming (Mozilla recommendation versions) and replaces the cipher suite jargon (CBC, RSA key exchange, DHE) with "older encryption methods".
- It states which clients are affected: only those connecting to Home Assistant over HTTPS (browsers, the apps, wall tablets, webhook callers, speakers fetching TTS or media from HA). Outgoing connections still use the v4 client cipher lists and are not affected.
- The Windows 7/8.1 note is only shown in the Intermediate v6 confirm step, and now says it applies to RSA certificates. Windows 7/8.1 SChannel lacks ECDHE-RSA with AES-GCM (added in Windows 10), so with an ECDSA certificate these clients keep working.
- The confirm steps describe what will happen ("will restart") and who restores the old profile.

### Recommend Intermediate v6 instead of Modern v6

Mozilla describes Intermediate as the "recommended configuration for a general-purpose server", and Modern as being for "modern clients that support TLS 1.3, with no need for backwards compatibility". Home Assistant is a general-purpose server for many kinds of clients, and smart home devices in particular are not known for updating their TLS stacks quickly. Some examples of clients that connect to Home Assistant and only support TLS 1.2:

- **Home Assistant Voice Preview Edition** (firmware 26.9.0, ESPHome 2026.6.0): downloads TTS responses and other media from Home Assistant's URL. It only offers TLS 1.2 for that, so it stops speaking with Modern v6 (esphome/esphome#21780). A fix is proposed in esphome/esphome#21786, but the current firmware does not include it yet.
- **Home Assistant Android app on Android 6 to 9**, which the app still supports: connects to Home Assistant for the frontend, the API and its webhook (location and sensor updates). Android only gained TLS 1.3 with Android 10 (home-assistant/android#1477).
- **Other Android apps on older phones and tablets**: for example GPSLogger sending location updates to a Home Assistant webhook (mendhak/gpslogger#971), or old tablets showing dashboards as wall panels.
- **Sonos**: when Home Assistant plays TTS or media on a Sonos speaker, the speaker downloads it from Home Assistant's URL. Sonos' documented HTTPS requirements for media streams only cover TLS 1.2 (<url>).
- **Self-built ESP8266 firmware** using the Arduino BearSSL client, for example to call a Home Assistant webhook or the REST API: BearSSL implements TLS 1.2 only.

Intermediate v6 still removes every CBC cipher (and, for `intermediate_v4` users, SHA-1, RSA key exchange and DHE). I found no report of a client that works with the previous default but would fail with Intermediate v6.

Since the default profile is the recommended one, this also changes the default for new installations to Intermediate v6. Modern v6 stays available for setups where every client supports TLS 1.3.

The trial with automatic rollback only protects against losing access from the browser, and the confirm dialog has to be answered within 5 minutes. So the confirm steps now tell users to confirm once the browser connects, then check their devices and apps, and where to switch back if something no longer connects.

title: Add NeoPool virtual integrations
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!
  Please, DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! (unless instructed).
-->

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

The NeoPool control system (originally made by Sugar Valley, acquired by Hayward in 2016) is sold under many brand names. An owner whose unit is badged "AquaRite", "Bayrol" or "Brilix" has no way to guess that the matching integration is called "NeoPool", so they cannot find it during onboarding.

This adds virtual integration rebrand pointers (`supported_by: "neopool"`) for the brands under which NeoPool hardware is sold, so each brand name surfaces in the integration search and routes the user to the existing NeoPool config flow:

- AquaRite (`aquarite_neopool`)
- Hayward (`hayward_neopool`)
- Bayrol (`bayrol_neopool`)
- Certikin (`certikin_neopool`)
- Brilix (`brilix_neopool`)
- Sugar Valley (`sugar_valley`)

Vendor brands that also sell non-NeoPool products use a `neopool`-suffixed domain so the pointer does not claim the bare brand name (and, for Bayrol, so it does not collide with the existing unrelated Bayrol cloud integration). Sugar Valley, the original platform maker, keeps a plain domain.

Each pointer is a single manifest; the generated `integrations.json` is updated by hassfest. No logos are included in this PR; a home-assistant/brands entry can follow separately and is not required for these pointers to work.

title: Keep Withings device polling active with webhooks
body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

When Withings webhooks connect, the shared subscription listener disables device polling even though the subscribed notifications do not refresh device inventory or battery data. Keep the device coordinator's existing hourly polling, following the goals coordinator's existing approach.

The regression checks repeated battery updates while connected, cloud disconnect/reconnect and cancellation on unload. All 70 Withings tests and 159 snapshots pass, along with changed-file hooks and the full CI-style MyPy check. content: # Deno [![]()]() [![Twitter badge][]][Twitter link] [![Bluesky badge][]][Bluesky link] [![Discord badge][]][Discord link] [![YouTube badge][]][YouTube link] [Deno]() ([/ˈdiːnoʊ/](), pronounced `dee-no`) is a JavaScript, TypeScript, and WebAssembly runtime with secure defaults and a great developer experience. It's built on [V8](), [Rust](), and [Tokio](). Learn more about the Deno runtime [in the documentation](). ## Installation Install the Deno runtime on your system using one of the commands below. Note that there are a number of ways to install Deno - a comprehensive list of installation options can be found [here](). Shell (Mac, Linux): ```sh curl -fsSL | sh ``` PowerShell (Windows): ```powershell irm | iex ``` [Homebrew]() (Mac): ```sh brew install deno ``` [Chocolatey]() (Windows): ```powershell choco install deno ``` [WinGet]() (Windows): ```powershell winget install --id=DenoLand.Deno ``` [Scoop]() (Windows): ```powershell scoop install main/deno ``` ### Build and install from source Complete instructions for building Deno from source can be found [here](). ## Your first Deno program Deno can be used for many different applications, but is most commonly used to build web servers. Create a file called `server.ts` and include the following TypeScript code: ```ts Deno.serve((_req: Request) => { return new Response("Hello, world!"); }); ``` Run your server with the following command: ```sh deno run --allow-net server.ts ``` This should start a local web server on [](). Learn more about writing and running Deno programs [in the docs](). ## Additional resources - **[Deno Docs]()**: official guides and reference docs for the Deno runtime, [Deno Deploy](), and beyond. - **[Deno Standard Library]()**: officially supported common utilities for Deno programs. - **[JSR]()**: The open-source package registry for modern JavaScript and TypeScript - **[Developer Blog]()**: Product updates, tutorials, and more from the Deno team. ## Contributing We appreciate your help! body:
### OS Version

Debian Trixie

## Issue

I originally isntalled `deno` with `apt` using `apt install deno`, then recently I was shown via `apt list --upgradable` there was a update available. So I upgraded deno from deno, using `deno upgrade`. Upgrade was successful, but now `apt` complains that there is an *upgrade* with the completely backward versions.

# deno --version

deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
v8 15.0.245.2-rusty
typescript 6.0.3

# sudo apt update
# apt list --upgradable

deno/trixie 2.9.8-1~griffo amd64 [upgradable from: 2.9.7-1~trixie]

# sudo deno upgrade

Current Deno version: v2.9.7
Looking up stable version
Found latest stable version v2.9.8
Attempting delta upgrade (1 step)
Downloading delta patch <url>
Delta upgrade checksum verified
Delta upgrade applied successfully (96.1 MB binary)
Deno is upgrading to version 2.9.8

# deno --version

deno 2.9.8 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
v8 15.0.245.2-rusty

title: deno_core: cached dynamic import can resolve before static top-level await completes
TextDecoder in streaming mode drops a U+FEFF that starts a later decode() call
`deno install --prod` installs devDependencies when deno.lock already lists them
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.8 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

`deno install --prod` (added in #33248) skips `devDependencies` only when there is no `deno.lock`. If the lockfile already contains the dev dependencies, which is the normal state of a CI checkout, they get installed anyway. The same happens with `--frozen` and with `deno ci --prod`.

### Repro

```sh
echo '{ "dependencies": { "ms": "^2.1.3" }, "devDependencies": { "is-number": "^7.0.0" } }' > package.json

# 1. no lockfile: works
deno install --prod > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "no lockfile:  $(ls node_modules | xargs)"

# 2. deno.lock already lists the devDependency (e.g. a CI checkout)
rm -rf node_modules deno.lock
deno install > /dev/null 2>&1
rm -rf node_modules
deno install --prod > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "with lockfile:  $(ls node_modules | xargs)"

rm -rf node_modules
deno install --prod --frozen > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "with lockfile, frozen: $(ls node_modules | xargs)"

deno ci --prod > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "deno ci --prod:  $(ls node_modules | xargs)"
```

Output:

```
no lockfile:  ms
with lockfile:  is-number ms
with lockfile, frozen: is-number ms
deno ci --prod:  is-number ms
```

### Expected

`ms` only in all four cases. `is-number` is a devDependency, and `--prod` should exclude it whether or not `deno.lock` lists it. The lockfile should pin versions, not decide which dependency groups get installed.

### Notes

- The `install_production` spec tests (`tests/specs/install/install_production`) don't include a `deno.lock`, so this path isn't covered.
- Context: we hit this while compiling a CLI in BYONM mode (`deno compile --node-modules-dir=manual`). That mode embeds the whole `node_modules`, so we need a production-only install. The workaround is to install from a copy of `package.json` with `devDependencies` removed.

title: Bundle '--external' option now requires '=' character
body:
Hi,

I have been using the following bundle command for quite some time now without any issue until recently:

```sh
deno bundle --minify --platform browser --external elasticlunr src/main.ts -o static/bundle.js
```

But with Deno versions 2.9.7 and 2.9.8, it stopped working properly. It returned `Bundled 0 modules in 12ms` instead of `Bundled 6 modules in 54ms`. The last known working version is 2.9.4.

After some testing, I made it work as expected by using an equal character between the option name and its value:

```sh
deno bundle --minify --platform browser --external=elasticlunr src/main.ts -o static/bundle.js
```

`node:fs.existsSync` throws `NotCapable` for special paths instead of returning `false` (breaks Vite 8 under scoped permissions)
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.8

After updating vite to 8.3.5 I've noticed the following error:

```
$ deno run --allow-env --allow-read --allow-write --allow-sys --allow-ffi vite build

error: Uncaught (in promise) NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", run again with the --allow-all flag
  if (fs.existsSync("/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop") || fs.existsSync("/run/WSL")) return !isInsideContainer();
  ^
  at Object.existsSync (ext:deno_node/_fs/_fs_exists.ts:1:1053)
  at isWsl (file:///workspace/node_modules/.deno/<email>/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:14848:9)
  at file:///workspace/node_modules/.deno/<email>/node_modules/vite/dist/node/chunks/node.js:14851:62
```

#### Reproduction

`repro.mjs`:

```js
import fs from "node:fs";
for (const p of ["/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", "/run/WSL", "/proc/self/cgroup", "/does/not/exist"]) {
  try { console.log(p, "->", fs.existsSync(p)); }
  catch (e) { console.log(p, "-> THREW", e.name + ":", e.message); }
}
```

```sh
deno run --allow-read repro.mjs
```

**Actual (Deno 2.9.8, `--allow-read`):**

```
/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop -> THREW NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop", run again with the --allow-all flag
/run/WSL -> false
/proc/self/cgroup -> THREW NotCapable: Requires all access to "/proc/self/cgroup", run again with the --allow-all flag
/does/not/exist -> false
```

**Expected (matches `node repro.mjs`, and `deno run -A repro.mjs`):**

```
/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc/WSLInterop -> false
/run/WSL -> false
/proc/self/cgroup -> true
/does/not/exist -> false
```

Returning `false` for a special path the program isn't allowed to touch would be enough. It matches Node's contract and leaks nothing, since the program can't access the path either way.

title: v2.9.8 is tagged but has no release; v2.9.7 still trusts the distrusted eMudhra root
body:
The 2026-10-17 eMudhra incident left eight Global TLS intermediate CA keys recoverable (they were integers 4, 56, 115, ...). Browsers blocked them via OneCRL/CRLSet and are distrusting `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`; `webpki-roots` 1.0.10 (2026-10-19) and Go 1.26.10/1.27.3 carry the removal.

**What we see in this repo:**
- Tag `v2.9.8` exists (`fe7ed012`), but there is **no GitHub release and no binaries** — the latest published release is still **v2.9.7 (2026-09-17)**, which predates the removal.
- The root store compiled into v2.9.7 still contains the eMudhra root, and Deno does not consult the OS store by default.

So anyone installing today gets a build that trusts the distrusted hierarchy, even though the fix is already on a tag.

**Ask:** publish v2.9.8 (or a 2.9.7 patch) with the updated root set, or say whether you are waiting on something upstream. If the root comes from `webpki-roots`, the bump is `1.0.10`.

No code issue claimed here — this is a release/remediation gap during a live incident. Happy to re-test and close if you consider it out of scope.

Disclosure: found with AI-assisted code review; the version facts above were checked against the GitHub releases API on 2026-10-21.

title: node:module does not expose documented enableCompileCache API
body:
### Description

The Deno Node.js API reference documents `Module.enableCompileCache`, but the API is `undefined` at runtime.

This also prevents Changesets CLI 3.0.3 from starting under Deno. Its CLI checks whether `process.getBuiltinModule` exists, then calls `enableCompileCache()` from the returned `node:module` object. ### Reproduction

Run:

```sh
deno eval 'import { Module } from "node:module"; console.log(typeof Module.enableCompileCache); console.log(typeof process.getBuiltinModule("node:module").enableCompileCache);'
```

### Expected behavior

Both values should be `"function"`, consistent with the documented `Module.enableCompileCache` API:

<url>

### Actual behavior

Both values are `"undefined"`.

Changesets 3.0.3 consequently fails at startup with:

```text
TypeError: enableCompileCache is not a function
```

Changesets CLI entry point:

<url>

### Environment

- Deno 2.9.0 (stable, aarch64-apple-darwin)
- Deno 2.9.7 (stable, aarch64-apple-darwin)

Intermittent SIGSEGV at startup on macOS arm64: sqlite3_initialize race between parallel CacheDB eager init threads
body:
Version: Deno 2.7.14 (aarch64-apple-darwin)

We bundle Deno in Quarto, and our nightly CI on GitHub `macos-latest` (Apple Silicon) sees a `Segmentation fault: 11` about 20ms after the deno process starts. It is rare: 3 crashes in about 40 nightly runs, each run launching deno ~2000 times, each time during a different render, and never on our x86_64 Linux runners. Users reported the same random crash on Apple Silicon since 2024 (quarto-dev/quarto-cli#10426), so it is not only a CI thing.

We collected the macOS crash reports for two of them. Both have the same faulting stack at the same image offsets: `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (SIGSEGV)`, `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000`, pc at 0, on a `tokio-runtime-worker` thread. Symbolicated with panic.deno.com:

- Crashing thread: <url>
- Another worker thread at the same moment: <url>

From what I can tell, two `CacheDB::spawn_eager_init_thread` tasks open their connections in parallel:

<url>

The crashing thread goes `ensure_safe_sqlite_threading_mode` -> `sqlite3_mutex_alloc` -> `sqlite3_initialize` -> `sqlite3MutexInit` and calls `sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit`, which is NULL. The other thread is already in `openDatabase`, so it went through `sqlite3_initialize` just before.

This is `sqlite3MutexInit` ([source](<url>), same code in the SQLite 3.50.2 bundled by libsqlite3-sys 0.35.0):

```c
int sqlite3MutexInit(void){
  int rc = SQLITE_OK;
  if( !sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexAlloc ){
  /* ... */
  pTo->xMutexInit = pFrom->xMutexInit;
  /* ... other methods ... */
  sqlite3MemoryBarrier();
  pTo->xMutexAlloc = pFrom->xMutexAlloc;
  }
  assert( sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit );
  rc = sqlite3GlobalConfig.mutex.xMutexInit();
  /* ... */
}
```

The thread that does the copy writes `xMutexInit`, then a barrier, then `xMutexAlloc`. The thread that finds `xMutexAlloc` already set skips the block and loads `xMutexInit` with no barrier in between. On arm64 these two loads can be reordered, so it can see `xMutexAlloc` set and still read the old NULL `xMutexInit`. On x86_64 loads are not reordered this way, which would explain why we only see it on Apple Silicon.

The disassembly of the 2.7.14 release binary (`deno-aarch64-apple-darwin.zip`, Mach-O UUID `4c4c4435-5555-3144-a10b-c1c14dc2d9bc`, same as in the crash reports) matches this:

```
0x1c80ef0: stp  x29, x30, [sp, #-0x10]!
0x1c80ef4: mov  x29, sp
0x1c80ef8: adrp  x8, #0x5df5000
0x1c80efc: ldr  x8, [x8, #0x608]  ; xMutexAlloc
0x1c80f00: cbnz  x8, #0x1c80fc8  ; already set: skip the copy
  ...  ; copy block: stores, dmb ish, store xMutexAlloc
0x1c80fc8: adrp  x8, #0x5df5000
0x1c80fcc: ldr  x8, [x8, #0x5f8]  ; xMutexInit, no barrier since the load above
0x1c80fd0: blr  x8  ; x8 == 0 -> pc 0
0x1c80fd4: dmb  ish  ; return address in the crash report (imageOffset 29888468)
```

<details>
<summary>Crash report excerpt (deno-2026-10-12-053833.ips)</summary>

```
"os_version":"macOS 26.6.2 (25G83)", "cpuType":"ARM-64"
procLaunch: 2026-10-12 05:38:23.8794  captureTime: 2026-10-12 05:38:23.9047
exception: EXC_BAD_ACCESS SIGSEGV KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS at 0x0000000000000000
faultingThread: 6 (tokio-runtime-worker)
  ?  +0
  deno +29888468
  deno +29886848
  deno +29888192
  deno +23717972
  deno +2798292
  deno +2796796
  deno +22493920
  deno +2794828
  deno +2880900
  deno +25617872
  deno +25634576
  deno +24463852
  libsystem_pthread.dylib _pthread_start
thread 5 (tokio-runtime-worker): lstat <- deno +29983132 <- +29901544 <- +30068504 <- +29949032 <- +23718032 <- (same frames as above)
```

The second report (2026-10-13) has the exact same faulting frames.

</details>

I could not reproduce it on demand: it needs arm64 and it is about one crash per tens of thousands of launches, so this is based on the crash reports and reading the code. The eager init threads are still there in v2.9.7 and SQLite master has the same `sqlite3MutexInit`, so I think current versions are affected too, but I have not tested.

If this is right, one way to avoid it on the Deno side (entirely your call) could be to call `sqlite3_initialize()` once on the main thread before the eager init threads are spawned. `sqlite3_initialize()` is [documented as threadsafe](<url>), so the missing barrier on the reader path is maybe also worth reporting to SQLite.

Does that match your understanding ?

title: deno_core: integer overflow in apply_source_map when the looked-up token's source line is u32::MAX
body:
Version: deno_core 0.411.0 (and `main`), sourcemap 9.2.0 (this repo's lockfile; >= 9.3.0 adds a second trigger, see comments)

### What happened

When a JS error is thrown, source-mapping its stack trace (in `format_stack_trace`) aborts the process with an overflow panic:

```
thread '...' panicked at deno_core-0.411.0/source_map.rs:143:27:
attempt to add with overflow
  2: core::panicking::panic_const::panic_const_add_overflow
  3: <deno_core::source_map::SourceMapper>::apply_source_map
  4: deno_core::error::apply_source_map
  5: <deno_core::error::JsStackFrame>::from_callsite_object
  6: deno_core::error::format_stack_trace
  7: deno_core::error::prepare_stack_trace_callback
  ... (V8 PrepareStackTrace callback)
  21: <deno_core::error::JsError>::inner_from_v8_exception
  22: <deno_core::error::JsError>::from_v8_exception
  23: deno_core::error::exception_to_err
  24: deno_core::error::exception_to_err_result
  25: <deno_core::runtime::jsruntime::JsRuntime>::resolve_promise_inner
  26: deno_core::runtime::bindings::watch_promise
  ... (V8 function callback)
```

(Published `deno_core 0.411.0`; the panicking line is `source_map.rs:143`, which is `libs/core/source_map.rs:233` on `main`.)

This aborts only on an overflow-checks build; a release build wraps to a wrong line number instead.

### Likely cause

The token's `get_src_line()` is `u32::MAX`, so `apply_source_map`'s `token.get_src_line() + 1` overflows. The `sourcemap` decoder computes `src_line = (i64::from(src_line) + delta) as u32` (`decoder.rs:201`), so a cumulative source line of `-1` wraps to `u32::MAX`.

A negative source line is out of spec, so the source map is malformed. It came from a bundler I was using, not from deno, so producing the bad map is not a deno bug. I am only flagging the deno_core side in case it is worth guarding: it aborts on such input rather than tolerating it. deno hardened a different source-map panic before (#21989), so this seemed worth raising in the same spirit.

### Reproduction

Minimal unit test for `libs/core/source_map.rs`. The mapping `"AADA"` is `[genCol 0, srcIdx 0, srcLine delta -1, srcCol 0]`, so the decoded token `src_line` is `u32::MAX`:

```rust
#[test]
fn test_apply_source_map_out_of_range_src_line_does_not_overflow() {
  let mut loader = SourceMapLoader::default();
  loader.map.insert(
  Url::parse("file:///a.js").unwrap(),
  SourceMapLoaderContent {
  source_map: Some(
  ascii_str!(
  r#"{"version":3,"sources":["file:///a.ts"],"names":[],"mappings":"AADA"}"#
  )
  .into(),
  ),
  },
  );
  let mut source_mapper = SourceMapper::new(Rc::new(loader));
  let _ = source_mapper.apply_source_map("file:///a.js", 1, 1);
}
```

Result:

```
thread '...' panicked at libs/core/source_map.rs:233:27:
attempt to add with overflow
```

### Expected

`apply_source_map` should tolerate a malformed source map (out-of-range source line) without aborting.

node:child_process: forked child's IPC socket (NODE_CHANNEL_FD) is not close-on-exec, grandchildren inherit the parent's IPC channel
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.7 and 2.8.3 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, official release binaries). Node 26 does not have this behavior.

In a child started with `child_process.fork()` (or `stdio: [..., "ipc"]`), the IPC socket the child receives as `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` (fd 3) is not close-on-exec. Every process the child spawns therefore inherits the parent's IPC channel.

### Reproduction

```js
// ipc_fd_leak.mjs
import { fork, spawnSync } from "node:child_process";

if (process.env.IPC_FD_CHILD) {
  const fds = spawnSync("ls", ["-l", "/proc/self/fd"], { stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "ignore"] });
  process.send(fds.stdout.toString());
  setTimeout(() => process.exit(0), 50);
} else {
  const child = fork(new URL(import.meta.url).pathname, [], {
  env: { ...process.env, IPC_FD_CHILD: "1" },
  });
  child.on("message", (fds) => console.log("grandchild's open fds:\n" + fds));
}
```

Deno 2.9.7 (identical on 2.8.3):

```
$ deno run -A ipc_fd_leak.mjs
grandchild's open fds:
total 0
lr-x------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 0 -> /dev/null
l-wx------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 1 -> pipe:[12941267]
l-wx------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 2 -> /dev/null
lrwx------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 3 -> socket:[12943831]
lr-x------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 4 -> /proc/3719219/fd
```

Node 26.8.2:

```
$ node ipc_fd_leak.mjs
grandchild's open fds:
total 0
lr-x------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 0 -> /dev/null
lrwx------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 1 -> socket:[12945297]
lrwx------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 2 -> /dev/null
lr-x------ 1 tim users 64 Oct 19 00:10 3 -> /proc/3719289/fd
```

fd 3 (`socket:[...]`) is the parent's IPC channel, visible from inside `ls`, which the child spawned with only stdout piped.

### Consequences

- The parent's IPC channel does not reach EOF when the child exits; it stays open until the last grandchild exits. For a child that leaves a daemon behind (esbuild's service process is the common case, started with `stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "inherit"]` and never stopped), the parent's read loop never sees `CLOSE` until that daemon dies.
- On 2.9.7 this late EOF is what makes the `readLoop` / exit-path double `disconnect()` crash reachable in practice (#37040). Fixing the inheritance would make that race practically unreachable, though the race itself still needs its own guard.
- Any grandchild can read and write the parent's IPC channel.

### Expected

Match Node, where libuv opens the channel fd with `O_CLOEXEC`: the child's `NODE_CHANNEL_FD` should be marked close-on-exec once the runtime has adopted it (the Rust side opens it in `op_node_child_ipc_pipe`, `ext/node/ops/ipc.rs`), so that `spawn()` from the child does not pass it on.

WebCrypto: importKey accepts EC public keys that are not on the curve
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.4

`crypto.subtle.importKey` accepts P-256, P-384, and P-521 public keys whose point is not on the curve, for the `jwk`, `raw`, and `spki` formats. The Web Crypto spec says import must throw a `DataError` in that case ("If the key value is not a valid point on the Elliptic Curve identified by the namedCurve member of normalizedAlgorithm throw a DataError"). Node.js, Bun, Chromium, and Firefox all reject these keys at import.

```js
const b64 = (bytes) => btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes)).replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
const jwk = { kty: "EC", crv: "P-256", x: b64(new Uint8Array(32).fill(1)), y: b64(new Uint8Array(32).fill(1)) };

const key = await crypto.subtle.importKey("jwk", jwk, { name: "ECDH", namedCurve: "P-256" }, true, []);
// Expected: DataError. Actual: resolves.
```

The key then fails later, with a different error for each operation:

- `exportKey("jwk" | "spki")`: `OperationError: expected valid public EC key`
- ECDSA `verify`: `TypeError: Invalid key format`
- ECDH `deriveBits`: `TypeError: Unexpected error decoding private key` (the private key is fine; it is the public key that is invalid)

`deriveBits` does reject the point, so ECDH never computes a shared secret from it. This is a conformance problem, not an invalid-curve attack.

The import code only builds or parses the SEC1 encoding and checks for the identity point. `EncodedPoint::from_affine_coordinates` (JWK) and `EncodedPoint::from_bytes` (raw, spki) in `ext/crypto/[import_key.rs](<url>)` don't check that the point is on the curve. The check happens later, when `PublicKey::from_encoded_point` is called in `deriveBits`, and that failure is mapped to `CryptoError::DecodePrivateKey`. Validating with `PublicKey::from_encoded_point` (or `from_sec1_bytes`) at import time and returning a `DataError` would fix the import and make the later errors unreachable.

Investigated with help from Claude, the reproduction and results were verified by hand.

title: The state of Deno after the Cloudflare announcement
body:
## The state of Deno after the Cloudflare announcement

Last week we announced that the Deno company is joining Cloudflare ([Deno blog post](<url>), [Cloudflare blog post](<url>)).


This issue explains where the Deno runtime stands right now, and we'll keep it pinned and updated as things change.


## What's happening

The Deno Company (now Cloudflare) will continue maintain Deno until October 2027:

- **Monthly releases.** We'll publish a 2.9.x LTS release every month with bug  fixes and security updates.
- **Security reports.** Report vulnerabilities the same way as before (see [SECURITY.md](<url>)). We'll triage reports as they come in.
- **Canary builds.** Canary builds will keep being published automatically from `main`, so new fixes show up there first.

## What's changing

- **Well written fix PRs will be merged.** Bug fix PRs are welcome, we'll review and merge them.
- **No new feature work.** We don't plan to develop any new features. Feature PRs will be closed without merging them.
- **Feature requests stay open.** Existing and new feature request issues will be labeled, not closed.
- **Canary-only features will be reverted.** Features that landed on `main`  after the 2.9 branch was cut (for example `deno sync-types` and the removal of the internal TypeScript fork) will be reverted so that `main` matches 2.9. If you use any of these in canary, expect them to go away. We'll post the full list here once we've put it together.

## Forks and further development

Deno is MIT-licensed open source, and anyone is free to fork it.

We are considering ways to organize development beyond October 2027 - please get in touch with @bartlomieju if you're interested.

title: node:assert deepEqual is not symmetric for array holes vs undefined
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.7 (also on main a18ce33)

In loose mode, `assert.deepEqual` treats an array hole and an own `undefined` element as equal in one argument order but not the other:

```js
import assert from "node:assert";
assert.deepEqual([1, , 3], [1, undefined, 3]); // passes in Deno, throws in Node
assert.deepEqual([1, undefined, 3], [1, , 3]); // throws in both
```

Node 22 and Node 26 throw in both orders (a hole never equals an own `undefined`, even loosely). `assert.notDeepEqual([1, , 3], [1, undefined, 3])` throws in Deno for the same reason.

Cause: `objEquiv` in `ext/node/polyfills/internal/util/comparisons.ts:1286-1292` (introduced by #32763) only applies the own-property check in strict mode; in loose mode it falls through to `innerDeepEqual(undefined, undefined)`. The reverse order goes through `sparseArrayEquiv`, which does check.

I have a small patch that ports Node's condition (a hole never matches, while loose mode still lets `null` match `undefined`), plus a unit test in `tests/unit_node/assert_test.ts` that fails on 2.9.7. Happy to open a PR if that's welcome.

Disclosure: this was found, reproduced and patched by an AI agent (Claude Code), which ran the reproduction and tests quoted above. It has not been separately reviewed by a human.

title: deno_core: use-after-free of fast-call CFunction overloads during isolate teardown (deno lint with a plugin intermittently segfaults)
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.6, 2.9.7 and `main` (a18ce3371), Linux x86_64 `deno lint` with a lint plugin occasionally segfaults on exit, roughly 1–2% of runs when several run in parallel. The crash is a use-after-free in deno_core's isolate teardown: the op contexts that hold each op's fast-call `CFunction` overload are freed before the isolate is disposed, while a concurrent TurboFan job may still read them. ### Mechanism - With V8 150.x, `FunctionTemplateInfo` stores raw pointers to the `CFunction` overloads passed to `FunctionTemplate::build_fast`. deno_core passes a slice that lives inside each `OpCtx` (`OpCtx::fast_fn_overloads`, `libs/core/ops.rs`). The comment there assumes that "`OpCtx` lives until isolate disposal". - It doesn't. `::drop` calls `cleanup()`, which calls `JsRealmInner::destroy()`. That drops the realm's `ContextState`, and with it `op_ctxs`, before `ManuallyDrop::drop(&mut self.v8_isolate)`. V8 only cancels and joins its concurrent optimization jobs inside `Isolate::Dispose`. - A TurboFan job still running at that point that inlines a fast API call reads the freed slice: ``` OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::CompileTask::Run PipelineCompilationJob::ExecuteJobImpl InliningPhase JSCallReducer::ReduceCallApiFunction fast_api_call::GetFastApiCallTarget FunctionTemplateInfoRef::c_functions_with_signatures v8/src/compiler/heap-refs.cc:2071 <-- SIGSEGV ``` When it crashes, the lint `PluginHost` thread is in `::drop`, and the main thread is dropping the `CliFactory` at the end of `lint()` (`cli/tools/lint/mod.rs`). - There is also a secondary cause: `PluginHost::create` (`cli/tools/lint/plugins.rs`) detaches the plugin host thread (`let _join_handle = std::thread::spawn(...)`), so the process can reach `exit()` while that thread is still tearing down its isolate. This probably dates from the V8 150 upgrade (#36098), which made the overload slice need to outlive the templates. `OpCtx` was later reshaped in #36693 / #36696. ### Reproduction You need a lint plugin, a few medium-sized files, and parallel runs (so TurboFan is still busy when a run finishes). The scripts below need nothing besides `deno`.
setup.sh: creates the project ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash # Creates a lint project: a small plugin and a few generated ~500-line files. set -euo pipefail dir=${1:-lint-repro} mkdir -p "$dir/src" cd "$dir" cat > deno.json <<'JSON' { "lint": { "plugins": ["./plugin.ts"] } } JSON cat > plugin.ts <<'TS' export default { name: "repro", rules: { "visit-all": { create(ctx) { let n = 0; return { Identifier(node) { n += node.name.length; }, CallExpression(node) { n += node.arguments.length; }, MemberExpression(node) { if (node.computed) n++; }, "FunctionDeclaration > Identifier"(node) { n += node.range[0]; }, StringLiteral(node) { n += node.value.length; }, "Program:exit"() { if (n < 0) ctx.report({ node: ctx.sourceCode.ast, message: String(n) }); }, }; }, }, }, } satisfies Deno.lint.Plugin; TS for f in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do { echo "// generated file $f" for i in $(seq 1 60); do cat < s.length > ${i}).map((s) => s.trim()); } TS done } > "src/file$f.ts" done wc -l src/*.ts | tail -1 ```
run.sh: runs deno lint N times, P in parallel, and counts exit codes ```sh #!/usr/bin/env bash # Usage: run.sh [parallelism] # Runs `deno lint` times, at a time, and counts crashes. deno=$1; dir=$2; runs=$3; par=${4:-4} cd "$dir" seq 1 "$runs" | xargs -P "$par" -I{} sh -c '"$0" lint -q >/dev/null 2>&1; echo $?' "$deno" \ | sort | uniq -c ```
```sh bash setup.sh proj bash run.sh "$(which deno)" proj 1000 4 # 981 0 # 19 139 <- SIGSEGV ``` ### Measurements (Linux x86_64, 8 cores, 4 parallel runs) | Binary / setup | SIGSEGV (exit 139) | |---|---| | 2.9.7 release | 19 / 1000 | | 2.9.7 release, `DENO_V8_FLAGS=--no-concurrent-recompilation` | 0 / 1000 | | `main` (a18ce3371, `--profile release-lite`) | 13 / 1000, 28 / 2000 | On a larger real-world project I saw the same pattern: 2.9.6 crashed 16/1000, 2.9.7 crashed 9/1000, 17/1000 and 23/1500, there were no crashes without the lint plugin (0/1000), and none when running sequentially (0/400). Backtrace of the faulting thread from the `main` build under gdb: ``` Thread 2 "V8 DefaultWorke" received signal SIGSEGV, Segmentation fault. #0 c_functions_with_signatures () at v8/src/compiler/heap-refs.cc:2071 #1 v8::internal::compiler::fast_api_call::GetFastApiCallTarget(JSHeapBroker*, FunctionTemplateInfoRef, unsigned long) at v8/src/compiler/fast-api-calls.cc:387 #2 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceCallApiFunction(Node*, SharedFunctionInfoRef) at v8/src/compiler/js-call-reducer.cc:4597 #3 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceJSCall(Node*, SharedFunctionInfoRef) #4 v8::internal::compiler::JSCallReducer::ReduceJSCall(Node*) at v8/src/compiler/js-call-reducer.cc:5177 #5 v8::internal::compiler::GraphReducer::Reduce(Node*) ... #8 v8::internal::compiler::InliningPhase::Run(TFPipelineData*, Zone*) at v8/src/compiler/pipeline.cc:952 #10 v8::internal::compiler::PipelineImpl::CreateGraph(Linkage*) #11 v8::internal::compiler::PipelineCompilationJob::ExecuteJobImpl(RuntimeCallStats*, LocalIsolate*) #12 v8::internal::OptimizedCompilationJob::ExecuteJob(RuntimeCallStats*, LocalIsolate*) #13 v8::internal::OptimizingCompileTaskExecutor::CompileTask::Run(JobDelegate*) at v8/src/compiler-dispatcher/optimizing-compile-dispatcher.cc:60 #14 v8::platform::DefaultJobWorker::Run() ``` At the same moment, the plugin host thread is inside `InnerIsolateState::drop`, past `cleanup()` (in this sample it is dropping `JsRuntimeState`, before the isolate): ``` #21 core::ptr::drop_in_place #22 alloc::rc::Rc::drop_slow #23 ::drop #24 core::ptr::drop_in_place ``` The crash needs concurrent recompilation (it never happens with `--no-concurrent-recompilation`), a lint plugin (which gives the plugin host its own isolate that is torn down at exit), and other load on the machine (sequential runs don't crash). ### Suggested fix Keep the op contexts alive until the isolate has been disposed: `JsRealmInner::destroy()` hands them back, and `InnerIsolateState` drops them only after `v8_isolate`. Separately, keep the lint `PluginHost` thread's `JoinHandle` and wait for it on drop, with a bound. I'll open a PR. _The investigation and this write-up were done with AI assistance (Claude Code)._

desktop: page-triggered downloads should ask where to save
body:
### What

In `deno desktop` apps, a page that saves a file (`<a download>`, a blob
export, a `Content-Disposition: attachment` response) has no consistent save
flow:

- Linux (webview/WebKitGTK): the file is written silently into the XDG
  downloads directory, with no UI.
- Windows (webview/WebView2): WebView2's own in-app download UI.
- macOS (webview/WKWebView): the download can't proceed (no destination
  without host support).
- CEF backend: page downloads are cancelled.

### Request

Ask where to save using the OS save dialog, consistently on every backend:
`NSSavePanel` on macOS, `IFileSaveDialog` on Windows, `GtkFileChooserDialog`
on Linux, CEF's Save As on the CEF backend. The engine already streams the
bytes; the destination decision is the only missing piece.

### Proposal

The laufey side is implemented in littledivy/laufey#126. Once that PR is
merged and a laufey release is cut, the Deno-side change is a pin bump:

- `cli/rt_desktop/Cargo.toml` (`laufey = "0.7.0"` -> new release)
- regenerate `cli/laufey_sums.lock`
- update the `runtime/desktop/dialogs` docs (its "native file-picker API is
  on the roadmap" note covers pickers, not downloads)

### Design note

The dialog is shown for every page-triggered download; on Linux this replaces

title: Cached 404 from an unauthenticated request ignores `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` for 15 minutes
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

## Background

#35138 caches 404 responses for 15 minutes and deliberately skips authenticated requests, since private hosts respond with 404 to unauthorized requests. However, the [cache read path](<url>) serves a cached 404 without checking whether the current request carries credentials. A single run without `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` therefore blocks a private module (e.g. on `raw.githubusercontent.com`) for 15 minutes, even after the token is set.

## Steps to reproduce

```ts
// server.ts
Deno.serve({ port: 4545 }, (req) =>
  req.headers.get("authorization") === "Bearer secret"
  ? new Response("export default 1;", { headers: { "content-type": "application/javascript" } })
  : new Response("not found", { status: 404 }));
```

```sh
deno run --allow-net server.ts &
export DENO_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
deno cache <url>
DENO_AUTH_TOKENS=secret@localhost:4545 deno cache <url>
```

## Expected behavior

The second `deno cache` sends the token and succeeds, as it does with `--reload`.

## Actual behavior

The second `deno cache` fails with `error: Module not found "<url>".` without sending a request, until the entry expires or `--reload` is used.

title: deno desktop 2.9.7 regression: node:net from an npm package fails to resolve ext:core/mod.js at runtime
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.7

### What happened

A desktop app packaged with `deno desktop --engine=quickjs` works on Deno
2.9.6 and fails on 2.9.7. The server starts and binds its port, but the first
request crashes module resolution, so the window stays blank.

The app is open source (GPL-3.0): <url>
— the failing build is release 0.2.3. No LDAP server is needed to reproduce:
the crash happens at startup, before any connection.

### Error

Runtime loaded successfully from: .../libruntime.dylib
Runtime started
Listening on <url>
TypeError: Cannot resolve module "ext:core/mod.js" from "node:net"
  at async file:///.../_fresh/server/server-entry.mjs:6034:32
  ...
  code: "ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND"

### Repro

1. Fresh 2 app using an npm package that imports `node:net`
  (reproduced with `npm:<email>`, which opens the LDAP socket
  through `net`).
2. `deno desktop --engine=quickjs --allow-net --allow-read --allow-write
  --allow-env --target aarch64-apple-darwin --output app.dmg .`
3. Install and launch the app: the window opens but never renders.

### Environment

- Deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, aarch64-apple-darwin) — broken
- Deno 2.9.6 (same machine, same build) — works

### Notes

- The built bundle carries `node:net` as a bare specifier (it comes from
  `npm:ldapts`; the app does not import `node:net` directly).
- Under the desktop runtime, Deno's `node:net` shim resolves to
  `ext:core/mod.js`, which is not mapped in the QuickJS desktop runtime —
  the CLI runtime resolves it fine.
- No app code changed between the two builds; only the Deno version differs.

title: Windows: utimeSync / fs.utimesSync fail with "Access is denied" on read-only files
node:child_process spawnSync/execFileSync still pass the parent environment to the child (#27343 fixed only spawn)
body:
## Problem

`child_process.spawnSync`, `execFileSync` and `execSync` give the child the parent's whole environment plus the `env` they are passed. Node gives the child only the `env` it is passed. So a variable that the caller removed from `env` still reaches the child.

Async `spawn` was fixed for this in #27343 (PR #27340), and it now clears the environment. The sync path was not fixed. On `main` (a18ce33715e30cd2b0d99c7e322ef11a65490e4d), `ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts` has two call sites:

- `ChildProcess` constructor (async `spawn`): `nodeSpawnChild(cmd, { args: cmdArgs, clearEnv: true, cwd, env, ... })`
- `spawnSync`: `nodeSpawnSyncChild({ args: [...], cwd, env: mapValues(env, ...), ..., clearEnv: false, ... })`

`normalizeSpawnArguments` already sets `env` to `options.env || Deno.env.toObject()`. So `clearEnv: true` would not change the default case, where no `env` is passed.

This hit us on GitHub Actions. A test removed `CI` from a copy of `process.env` and ran a script with `execFileSync`. The script still saw `CI=true` on every Deno runner, and it took its CI branch: [disk-space-saviour#31](<url>), run [38003106785](<url>).

## Reproduce

```js
// probe.mjs
import { spawn, spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

const env = { ...process.env };
delete env.PROBE;
const script = 'echo "${PROBE-<unset>}"';

console.log('spawnSync:', spawnSync('sh', ['-c', script], { env, encoding: 'utf8' }).stdout.trim());
spawn('sh', ['-c', script], { env, stdio: 'inherit' }).on('close', () => {});
```

```sh
PROBE=leaked node probe.mjs  # spawnSync: <unset>  then  <unset>
PROBE=leaked deno run -A probe.mjs  # spawnSync: leaked  then  <unset>
```

(Deno 2.9.6.) The exact repro from #27343 shows the same thing with the sync API: `spawnSync('env', { env: { test: 'test' } })` prints the parent's variables as well as `test=test`.

## Workaround

Pass a blank value instead of deleting the key, as in `{ ...process.env, CI: '' }`. A blank value overrides the parent's value on every runtime. This only helps when the child treats an empty variable as unset.

## Suggested fix

In `spawnSync` in `ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts`, pass `clearEnv: true` as the async path does:

```diff
  uid,
  gid,
-  clearEnv: false,
+  clearEnv: true,
  extraStdio: extraStdioNormalized,
```

Port Node's `test-child-process-spawnsync-env.js` and an `execFileSync` variant of the #27343 test, to keep the sync path from drifting again.

title: npm peer resolution during deno run --no-config installs a version outside the declared peer range for a remote module's graph
body:
### Summary

When a program running with `--no-config` imports a module from an `https:` URL whose own imports pull in an npm graph, peer dependencies in that graph are resolved to the **newest published version even when it is outside the declared peer range**. The same graph resolved statically (`deno info`) — or resolved by a run that has a config file present — picks the highest version that satisfies the range instead. Programs then crash at `require()` time because the out-of-range peer is not API-compatible.

### Versions

* `deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)`
* `deno 2.9.7+a18ce33 (canary, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)` (commit `a18ce33`, 2026-10-06)
* Windows 11; both binaries reproduce the same behaviour.

### Minimal repro

`repro.mjs` (no config file next to it):

```js
await import('<url>')
```

That remote module imports `npm:eslint-plugin-jsdoc`, which depends on `@typescript-eslint/<email>` → `@typescript-eslint/<email>`, whose peer is `typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`. `<email>` is `latest` and does **not** satisfy that range; `<email>` does.

1. Static resolution — correct (highest satisfying version):

```
$ deno info --no-config <url>
...
npm:/@typescript-eslint/<email>@6.0.3 (382.58KB)
npm:/<email> (23.22MB)
```

2. Runtime with `--no-config` — wrong (newest, out of range):

```
$ deno run --allow-all --no-config repro.mjs
Warning The following peer dependency issues were found:
└─┬ <email> (imported by <url>)
  └─┬ @typescript-eslint/<email>
  ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/<email>
  │ ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/<email>
  │ │ ├─┬ @typescript-eslint/<email>
  │ │ │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
  │ │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
  │ └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
  └── peer typescript@>=4.8.4 <6.1.0: resolved to 7.0.2
```

3. Same run with a `deno.json` present (e.g. `{ "nodeModulesDir": "none" }`) — no peer warning, resolves `<email>`.

Also reproduced with the jsDelivr copy of the same module (`<url>), so it is not host-specific.

### Real-world impact

`fount` documents linting through a `deno install`-generated shim (`~/.deno/bin/eslint`), whose command is:

```
deno run --allow-all --minimum-dependency-age 0 --no-config npm:eslint
```

and whose flat config (`eslint.config.mjs`) imports the remote config above. eslint loads that config at runtime, the peer resolves to `<email>`, and `@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree` crashes while being required, because TypeScript 7's package root no longer exposes the compiler API (`"exports"."."` is `./lib/version.cjs`; the API moved to `typescript/unstable/*`), so `ts.Extension` is `undefined`:

```
ESLint: 10.12.0

TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'Cjs')
  at Object.<anonymous> (.../npm/registry.npmjs.org/@typescript-eslint/typescript-estree/8.71.1/dist/create-program/shared.js:64:18)
  at Object.<anonymous> (.../typescript-estree/8.71.1/dist/create-program/getWatchProgramsForProjects.js:45:18)
```

Exit code 2, no file is ever linted — even though `<email>`, which satisfies the peer range, is available and is what the static resolver selects.

### Expected

`deno run` (runtime) and `deno info` (static) should agree on peer resolution, and a peer dependency should not be auto-installed at a version outside its declared range. Failing that, resolution should fail loudly rather than warn and install an incompatible version.

### Workarounds

* Adding `import 'npm:<email>';` to the program (or to the config that is imported at runtime) makes the peer resolve to 6.0.3 and the crash disappears. This is what I use locally for now.
* Running without `--no-config` avoids it, but the shim that `deno install` generates passes `--no-config`, so that is not something a user of that shim can change.

### Possibly related

* #36607 ("match peer fallbacks when checking peer resolution cache") — this graph resolves `typescript` through the auto-installed peer fallbacks in both cases, so the fallback/cache keying may be where the two paths diverge.

title: `npm:` subpath specifiers resolve no type declarations when the package ships sibling `.d.ts` files or uses a `"./*"` export pattern
body:
### Summary

For `npm:` specifiers, `deno check` fails to find type declarations for **subpath** exports in two cases that TypeScript (`moduleResolution: nodenext`) and Node resolve correctly, while `deno run` executes all of them fine:

- the export entry has no `types` condition and the declaration lives next to the **resolved** file (e.g. `dist/foo.d.ts` for `"./foo": "./dist/foo.js"`)
- the export key is a **pattern** (`"./*"`), even when that entry *does* have a `types` condition

Resolving types next to the resolved target is what TypeScript does, so packages that ship `dist/*.js` with sibling `dist/*.d.ts` end up untyped on Deno.

Version: `deno 2.9.7+a18ce33` (canary, release, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc), Windows.

### Real-world reproduction (no setup needed)

```sh
echo 'import { Effect } from "npm:effect/Effect"; console.log(typeof Effect);' > main.ts
deno check main.ts
```

```
TS2307 [ERROR]: Cannot find module 'npm:effect/Effect' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

`<email>` has `"./*": "./dist/*.js"` and ships `dist/Effect.d.ts` right next to `dist/Effect.js`. The package root works, so this is specific to subpaths:

| specifier | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm:effect` (`".": "./dist/index.js"`) | resolves types |
| `npm:effect/Effect` (`"./*": "./dist/*.js"`, `dist/Effect.d.ts` present) | `TS2307` |
| `npm:effect/unstable/http` (`"./unstable/http": "./dist/unstable/http/index.js"`, `dist/unstable/http/index.d.ts` present) | `TS2307` |
| `npm:zod/v4` (entry has a `types` condition) | resolves types |

`deno run` on all of these prints the expected value, so only type resolution is affected.

### Minimal repro

Each package below is packed with `bun pm pack` (or `npm pack`) and served from a local registry (`NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`), then checked with a one-line `main.ts` that imports `npm:<pkg>/foo`:

| package `exports` | declaration location | `deno check` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"./foo": { "types": "./dist/foo.d.ts", "default": "./dist/foo.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | ok |
| `"./foo": { "default": "./dist/foo.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `"./foo": { "default": "./foo.js" }` | `foo.d.ts` (package root) | ok |
| `"./*": { "types": "./dist/*.d.ts", "default": "./dist/*.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `"./*": { "default": "./dist/*.js" }` | `dist/foo.d.ts` | `TS2307` |
| `".": { "default": "./dist/index.js" }` | `dist/index.d.ts` | ok |
| `"main": "./dist/index.js"` | `dist/index.d.ts` | ok |

The last two rows show the package root behaving differently from subpaths: for the root entry Deno does look next to the resolved target.

The `"./*"` package above resolves fine when it is loaded from `node_modules` (`"nodeModulesDir": "manual"`, bare specifier instead of `npm:`), so this is specific to the `npm:` resolver.

`tsc --noEmit` with `"module": "nodenext"` / `"moduleResolution": "nodenext"` resolves every row above (including the `"./*"` ones) to the right declaration file.

### Expected

`deno check` should resolve declarations the same way TypeScript does: apply the `types` condition for pattern keys too, and when an entry has no `types` condition, fall back to the declaration file next to the resolved target rather than `<package root>/<subpath>.d.ts`.

WebGPU: A manual blit may be required on devices without `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`
body:
The Vulkan extension `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format` allows configuring a view of a swapchain surface in a different format. This is useful to translate between sRGB and linear RGB. The extension is widely supported on desktop but support is [spottier on Android](<url>).

The WebGPU API offers configuration of `viewFormats` in `GPUCanvasConfiguration`, and `wgpu` has a corresponding field in `SurfaceConfiguration`. However, on devices that lack `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`, attempts to configure a non-identity view format mapping will fail due to lacking the `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` downlevel flag.

Firefox and Servo do not use a swapchain to present WebGPU canvases, so are willing to treat adapters as WebGPU compliant even if they lack `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` (<url>). I am not sure the current compliant-adapter filtering behavior in Deno, but if Deno wants to support surface view formats on devices that do not have `VK_KHR_swapchain_mutable_format`, a manual blit will be needed (see closed PR <url> for an example). Alternatively, Deno could leave the gap in place (in which case a validation error not described by the WebGPU spec would be raised on these devices), or could decline to expose a GPU through WebGPU if it lacks `SURFACE_VIEW_FORMATS` (which would require a special case on top of `wgpu`'s compliant adapter determination).

Related:
- #23563 <!-- Tracking issue for using WebGPU to render on the window of the desktop environment -->
- <url>
- <url>
- <url> (issue claims a polyfill is needed, but that is incorrect because Firefox doesn't present with a Vulkan swapchain).

title: node:fs: utimesSync / statSync drop sub-millisecond file times (mtimeNs is always a whole millisecond
body:
**Version:** deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
 
In Deno's `node:fs`, file times only keep milliseconds, in both directions:
 
- **writing:** `fs.utimesSync(f, 1700000000.123456789, ...)` sets the file's mtime to
  `.123000000` (Node sets `.123456000`);
- **reading:** `fs.statSync(f).mtimeMs` is a whole number of milliseconds, and even
  `fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs` is a whole number of milliseconds times
  10^6, also for a file whose times have nanoseconds on disk (set by `touch`).
Repro:
 
```js
import fs from "node:fs";
import os from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
 
const f = path.join(fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), "subms-")), "f");
fs.writeFileSync(f, "x");
fs.utimesSync(f, 1700000000.123456789, 1700000000.123456789);
console.log(fs.statSync(f).mtimeMs);
console.log(fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs);
```
 
| | Deno 2.9.7 | Node 22.22.0 |
|---|---|---|
| `mtimeMs` | `1700000000123` | `1700000000123.456` |
| `mtimeNs` (bigint) | `1700000000123000000n` | `1700000000123456000n` |
| on disk after `utimesSync` (`stat -c %y`) | `...20.123000000` | `...20.123456000` |
 
Reading a file set with `touch -d @1700000000.123456789 f` (on disk
`...20.123456789`): Deno's `fs.statSync(f, { bigint: true }).mtimeNs` is
`1700000000123000000n`, Node's is `1700000000123456789n`. `Deno.statSync` /
`Deno.utimeSync` behave the same way (milliseconds).
 
**Expected:** the same precision as Node: `utimes` passes the fractional seconds on
(Node: microseconds), and `stat` reports what the file system has (`mtimeMs` with a
fraction, `mtimeNs` / `atimeNs` / `ctimeNs` / `birthtimeNs` with the nanoseconds).
 
**Why it matters:** Emscripten's test `test_fs_subms_times` (sub-millisecond file
times through NODEFS / NODERAWFS, i.e. host files through `node:fs`) cannot pass
under Deno, so it was disabled there: emscripten-core/emscripten#27898.

title: deno desktop: preventDefault() on BrowserWindow "close" event does not keep the window open
body:
## Version ``` deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu) v8 15.0.245.2-rusty typescript 6.0.3 ``` OS: Ubuntu 26.04.1 LTS (Linux 7.0.0-34-generic x86_64), Wayland session ## Description The [Closing the app]() docs say that calling `event.preventDefault()` in a `BrowserWindow` `close` listener stops the window from closing, for example to show a "Save?" dialog: ```ts win.addEventListener("close", async (e) => { if (hasUnsavedChanges) { e.preventDefault(); const ok = await win.executeJs("confirm('Discard changes?')"); if (ok) win.close(); } }); ``` That doesn't work. The listener runs, but the event isn't cancelable, `preventDefault()` does nothing, and the window closes anyway. A desktop app has no way to confirm or block a user-initiated close (the native close button or Alt+F4). From reading the source: - `cli/rt/desktop.rs`, in the `closeRequested` case: the event is dispatched as `new Event("close")`. That event isn't cancelable, and the result of `dispatchEvent` is ignored. - `cli/rt_desktop/lib.rs`, in `on_close_requested`: since #36718, after forwarding `CloseRequested` to JS the runtime calls `laufey::Window::from_id(ev.window_id).close()` straight away. The comment there says the JS "close" event "is a plain notification (not cancelable)". As far as I can tell from the source, the event has never been cancelable in any 2.9.x release. On 2.9.4/2.9.5 (laufey 0.5.0) the window closes natively without waiting for JS. On 2.9.6 (laufey 0.7.0) it never closes at all (#36715). So the docs example has never worked. ## Reproduction `main.ts`: ```ts Deno.serve(() => new Response( "

Click the window's close button (X)

" + "

Expected: the window stays open.

", { headers: { "content-type": "text/html" } }, ) ); // The first construction adopts the startup window. const win = new Deno.BrowserWindow({ title: "close preventDefault repro" }); win.addEventListener("close", (e) => { e.preventDefault(); console.log( `close event: cancelable=${e.cancelable} defaultPrevented=${e.defaultPrevented}`, ); }); ``` Run, then click the window's close button (X) or press Alt+F4: ```sh deno desktop --hmr main.ts ``` ## Actual output The window closes, and the terminal shows: ``` close event: cancelable=false defaultPrevented=false ``` ## Expected vs actual - expected: `cancelable=true defaultPrevented=true`, and the window stays open until `win.close()` is called - actual: `cancelable=false defaultPrevented=false`, and the window closes ## Possible fix laufey 0.7.0 already defers the close until `Window::close()` is called, so the runtime could let JS decide: - `cli/rt_desktop/lib.rs`: don't call `Window::close()` in `on_close_requested`, and leave `closed_windows`/`open_windows` alone until the close actually goes ahead. - `cli/rt/desktop.rs`: dispatch `new Event("close", { cancelable: true })`, and call `target.close()` if `dispatchEvent` returns `true` (not prevented). If cancelling isn't meant to be supported, the docs example should be removed instead. ## Impact Desktop apps can't ask "Do you want to close?" or "Save changes?" before quitting, even though the docs show exactly that pattern. Apps that follow the docs lose unsaved state when the user closes the window, and nothing logs an error, so it's easy to assume the listener isn't attached rather than that the event can't be cancelled.

title: OTel log export replaces Latin-1 characters with U+FFFD when the console line has no character above U+00FF
body:
## Version

```
deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
v8 15.0.245.2-rusty
typescript 6.0.3
```

OS: Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS on WSL2 (Linux 6.6.87.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 x86_64)

## Description

With `OTEL_DENO=true`, a `console.log` line whose characters all fit in Latin-1 (U+0000–U+00FF) is exported
with every non-ASCII character replaced by U+FFFD (`ef bf bd`). The same text is exported correctly as soon
as the line also contains one character above U+00FF.

Stdout is correct in both cases; only the OTLP log record body is wrong.

My guess is that V8 stores such a string as a one-byte (Latin-1) string, and the telemetry path reads those
bytes as UTF-8 instead of converting them. I have not checked this in the source.

## Reproduction

`receiver.ts`, a minimal OTLP/HTTP receiver that prints the raw bytes after each marker it finds in a
`/v1/logs` request body:

```ts
const markers = ['latin1-only', 'with-euro'];
Deno.serve({ port: 4318, onListen: () => console.log('receiver listening on :4318') }, async (request) => {
  const body = new Uint8Array(await request.arrayBuffer());
  if (new URL(request.url).pathname === '/v1/logs') {
  const latin1 = new TextDecoder('latin1').decode(body);
  for (const marker of markers) {
  const at = latin1.indexOf(marker);
  if (at < 0) continue;
  const bytes = body.subarray(at, at + marker.length + 20);
  console.log(marker.padEnd(12), [...bytes].map((b) => b.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')).join(' '));
  }
  }
  return new Response(null, { status: 200 });
});
```

`log.ts`:

```ts
console.log('latin1-only: Médicale');
console.log('with-euro: Médicale €');
```

Run:

```sh
# terminal 1
deno run --allow-net receiver.ts

# terminal 2
OTEL_DENO=true \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=<url> \
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/protobuf \
deno run log.ts
```

## Actual output

Terminal 2 (stdout is correct):

```
latin1-only: Médicale
with-euro: Médicale €
```

Terminal 1 (the exported log bodies):

```
receiver listening on :4318
latin1-only  6c 61 74 69 6e 31 2d 6f 6e 6c 79 3a 20 4d ef bf bd 64 69 63 61 6c 65 0a 32 18 0a 0c 6c 6f 67
with-euro  77 69 74 68 2d 65 75 72 6f 3a 20 4d c3 a9 64 69 63 61 6c 65 20 e2 82 ac 0a 32 18 0a 0c
```

## Expected vs actual

`é` (U+00E9) after `M` in the first line:

- expected: `4d c3 a9 64` (`M`, `é` in UTF-8, `d`)
- actual: `4d ef bf bd 64` (`M` + U+FFFD + `d`)

The second line contains `€` (U+20AC), which is outside Latin-1, and the same `é` in it is exported
correctly as `4d c3 a9 64`.

## Impact

Deno Deploy collects console output through this export, so a hosted app's logs show `Imagerie M�dicale`
where the code printed `Imagerie Médicale`. The text in the program is intact, and stdout and local runs
show it correctly, so this is easy to misread as an encoding bug in the app. The affected lines are common:
any French, German or Spanish text (é, à, ü, ñ, Î…) printed without a character above U+00FF in the
same line.

title: `--watch` restart doesn't kill child processes that were `unref()`'d (leaks one per restart)
body:
Version: Deno 2.9.7 (also 2.9.5), aarch64-apple-darwin

When `deno run --watch` restarts the program after a file change, child processes spawned by the previous run are killed, **unless they were `unref()`'d**. Unref'd children survive every restart, so a long-lived child leaks once per restart. They stay children of the same `deno` process and are only reaped when the watcher exits.

This happens with both `Deno.Command` + `ChildProcess.unref()` and `node:child_process` + `child.unref()`.

## Repro

`dep.ts`:
```ts
export const v = 0;
```

`main.ts`:
```ts
import { v } from "./dep.ts";
const child = new Deno.Command("sleep", { args: ["1000"] }).spawn();
child.unref(); // remove this line and the leak goes away
console.log("ready", v);
setInterval(() => {}, 1000);
```

```sh
deno run -A --watch main.ts &
# edit dep.ts 3 times (e.g. bump v), waiting for each "ready" line
ps -eo ppid=,command= | grep "sleep 1000"  # 4 children of the deno pid; expected 1
```

Results after 3 restarts (count of `sleep 1000` children of the watcher process):

| spawn | children |
|---|---|
| `node:child_process` `spawn()` | 1 ✅ |
| `node:child_process` `spawn()` + `child.unref()` | 4 ❌ |
| `node:child_process` `spawn()` + `child.unref()` + `stdin/stdout.unref()` | 4 ❌ |
| `Deno.Command().spawn()` | 1 ✅ |
| `Deno.Command().spawn()` + `child.unref()` | 4 ❌ |

## Expected

The restart should tear down the previous run's children whether or not they were unref'd. `unref()` only means "don't keep the event loop alive", but the restart ends that runtime regardless. This is the same cleanup that #21759 verified for ref'd children; that issue was closed after testing a plain, ref'd `sleep` child.

## Real-world impact

esbuild's npm package spawns its long-lived `esbuild --service` child and immediately calls `child.unref()`. So any tool that uses esbuild under `deno run --watch` gains one `esbuild --service` process per restart. We hit this with a Fresh 2 dev server (whose bundler uses esbuild) under `--watch`: a long-running session accumulated 13 workers. Workaround on our side: an `unload` listener that terminates the process's own `esbuild --service` children.
