title: Deno.serve: request body read alongside a streamed response stops and never resumes (HTTP/1.1)
node:https: after piping a ranged `fs.createReadStream()` that is read in one chunk, the next request on the same keep-alive connection is never answered
body:
**Title:** node:https: after piping a ranged `fs.createReadStream()` that is read in one chunk, the next request on the same keep-alive connection is never answered

**Version:** deno 2.9.7 (stable) and the current canary, 2.9.7+7a96f1b; Linux x86_64 (Debian 13)

### Description

A `node:https` server pipes `fs.createReadStream(file, { start, end })` into the response. When that range is read in a single chunk, the client gets the full response. The connection then stays open, but the next request sent on it is never answered.

These variants all work:

- `node:http` with the same handler;
- the same stream without `start`/`end`;
- a range large enough to need several reads;
- Node 24.21 with the same script.

The pattern is common in practice. Express's `express.static` uses `send`, which always passes `start` and `end` to `createReadStream`. Any Express app that serves HTTPS directly from Deno therefore leaves a connection stuck after every small static file, such as the favicon or a small JS chunk. A browser reusing its six connections to the host stalls within seconds: requests sit in "waiting", and Chrome reports `net::ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES`.

### Reproduction

```js
// repro.mjs — needs cert.pem / key.pem, e.g.:
// openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout key.pem -out cert.pem -days 1 -subj /CN=localhost
import { createReadStream, readFileSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"
import { createServer as https } from "node:https"
import { createServer as http } from "node:http"

writeFileSync("one-byte.txt", "x")
const handler = (req, res) => {
  if (req.url === "/") return res.end("ok")
  res.setHeader("Content-Length", "1")
  createReadStream("one-byte.txt", { start: 0, end: 0 }).pipe(res)
}
const [proto, port] = process.argv.slice(2)
const server = proto === "https" ? https({ cert: readFileSync("cert.pem"), key: readFileSync("key.pem") }, handler) : http(handler)
server.listen(Number(port), "127.0.0.1")
```

```sh
deno run -A repro.mjs https 8443 &
# two requests on one keep-alive connection: the file, then a plain response
curl -sk -m 4 -w "%{http_code} " -o /dev/null <url> -o /dev/null <url>
```

| runtime | protocol | output |
|---|---|---|
| deno 2.9.7 | https | `200 000` — the second request times out |
| deno 2.9.7+7a96f1b (canary) | https | `200 000` |
| deno 2.9.7 | http | `200 200` |
| node 24.21.0 | https | `200 200` |

On the same `node:https` server, under deno 2.9.7, these handlers all return `200 200`:

- `createReadStream("one-byte.txt")` without `start`/`end`;
- `res.end(readFileSync(...))`;
- a 200 KB file with a range.

Destroying the read stream when the response finishes, as `send` does through `on-finished`, makes no difference either way.

### Expected

The second request on the connection is answered, as it is under `node:http` and under Node.

### Notes

- Possibly related, already fixed: #36496 (truncate streaming responses to content length), #36690 (preserve keep-alive after reading request body), #27223 (a stream chunk that hangs the connection). This case still reproduces on 2.9.7, which includes all three.
- Workaround: send `Connection: close` on every response, so each request gets a new connection.

title: deno lint --fix resets file permissions

Deno Desktop: upstreaming a series of fixes and features (stable app origin, deep links, window API, …)
body:
Hi @crowlKats @littledivy (cc @bartlomieju),

We've been shipping real apps on Deno Desktop (2.9.7) and ran into enough gaps that we built a
patched runtime: [Brainwires/deno](<url>) (branch `denext/v2.9.7`, every change listed in
[DENEXT.md](<url>)) and
[Brainwires/laufey](<url>). We'd like it all to land upstream so we can
drop the fork. We'd rather ask how you want it before opening a pile of PRs.

Everything is tested on macOS (arm64 and x64), Linux (x64 and arm64) and Windows x64 with both the
webview and CEF backends, on Deno's own CI bar (lint, fmt, `cargo test --lib`, unit and spec) and
an end-to-end suite that packages and launches an app per area.

**1. Small fixes against current main (laufey 0.7.0, no new API).** Each would be one PR with a test that fails on main:
- `Dock.setBadge(null)` shows the text "null" instead of clearing the badge
- `op_desktop_alert_async` is deleted at bootstrap, so the uncaught-error dialog never shows
- `Notification.close()` can deadlock (the map lock is held while the backend fires `close`)
- the window `close` event can't be cancelled (#36913)
- Node-API addons crash on Windows (#36596, the Windows half; #36718 fixed Linux)
- a full event channel drops discrete events (a lost `contextmenuclose` wedges `showContextMenu`)
- `BrowserWindow`/`Tray`/`Dock`/`Notification` panic in workers
- the HTTPS error report can hang exit; a hidden bootstrap window gets revealed anyway in tray-only apps; a few `desktop.*` keys missing from the config schema

**2. Foundations**
- the in-process memory transport (#35675) plus two follow-ups (an absolute-form `http+memory:`
  target over TCP is refused; `node:http` serves on it)
- a stable custom-scheme app origin (`desktop.app.origin`, e.g. `myapp://app`): a scheme handler
  bridging into `Deno.serve` over the memory transport, plus a loopback relay for WebSockets that only
  accepts the app's exact `Origin`. This fixes #35444 and #35576. Storage persists across launches, and
  OAuth providers that check `Origin` accept it.
- handing the app identifier to every backend (per-app storage; #36768), building on #35662
- letting the runtime provide its own environment variables without `setenv` once the UI thread runs

**3. Features** (each needs its laufey half released first; we have PRs open there, littledivy/laufey#84, littledivy/laufey#85, littledivy/laufey#86, littledivy/laufey#87, littledivy/laufey#88, littledivy/laufey#89, littledivy/laufey#90, littledivy/laufey#91, littledivy/laufey#92 and littledivy/laufey#93):
deep links, opened files and single instance (completing #35465); OS scheme registration and the
`.msi` keys; maximize/minimize/fullscreen, size limits, bounds and screens, title-bar styles and
backdrops, `quit()` (on top of #36761 and #36789); menu accelerators on every backend; notification
actions and scheduling; native file dialogs; drag and drop with paths; HTML and image formats on

title: desktop: staged update is swapped in by the already-loaded old dylib, so it runs one launch late and rollback never covers it
body:
## Summary

The [auto-update docs](<url>) say:

> When the app restarts, the launcher swaps the staged update into place before anything else runs.

On Linux this isn't what happens. `apply_pending_update` runs inside the app dylib, not in the launcher: the launcher `dlopen`s the **old** dylib, then that code moves `<dylib>.update` into place. The process doing the swap keeps running the old code it has already mapped. The new version only runs on the launch **after** that.

That has two consequences:

1. **The update appears to need two restarts.** The launch that does the swap still reports the old Deno.desktopVersion`, so `Deno.autoUpdate()` finds the same patch in `latest.json`, downloads it again, and fires `onUpdateReady` a second time for a version that is already on disk.
2. **Rollback never protects the new version.** `op_desktop_confirm_update` writes `<dylib>.update-ok` whenever `<dylib>.backup` exists (per #36574). The first boot where that's true is the swapping launch, which is still the old code, so it confirms the update before the new dylib has ever run. On the next launch the runtime sees `.backup` + `.update-ok`, cleans up the backup, and only then runs the new code. If the new version crashes on startup, there is no backup left to roll back to, and `onRollback` can never fire.

## Environment

- Deno 2.9.7, laufey 0.7.0 (`.downloaded` = `v0.7.0`), CEF backend
- Linux x86_64 (CachyOS); reproduced with a plain-directory build and with a `--compress=xz` AppImage (which unpacks to `~/.local/share/...`, so the dylib is writable)

## Evidence that the swap lives in the dylib

In a built app directory, the launcher contains none of the update strings; the dylib does:

```
$ grep -c -a 'update-ok' MyApp MyApp.so
MyApp:0
MyApp.so:1
$ grep -c -a 'Failed to write update' MyApp MyApp.so
MyApp:0
MyApp.so:1
```

## Reproduction

Staging an update manually without an update server.

`main.ts`:

```ts
// v1 and v2 differ only in this marker
Deno.writeTextFileSync(Deno.env.get("OUT")!, JSON.stringify({ marker: "v1" }));
Deno.exit(0);
```

```sh
# v1 and v2, same app name, both self-extracting so the dylib is writable
deno desktop -A --compress=xz --output ./v1/App.AppImage main.ts
sed -i 's/"v1"/"v2"/' main.ts
deno desktop -A --compress=xz --output ./v2/App.AppImage main.ts

# run each once so they unpack, then find their unpacked dirs
OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v1/App.AppImage; OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v2/App.AppImage
D1=~/.local/share/com.deno.desktop.app/<v1 hash>/App
D2=~/.local/share/com.deno.desktop.app/<v2 hash>/App

# stage v2's dylib as an update for v1
cp "$D2/App.so" "$D1/App.so.update"

for i in 1 2 3; do
  OUT=/tmp/o.json ./v1/App.AppImage; cat /tmp/o.json
  ls "$D1" | grep -E '\.so\.(update|backup|update-ok)$'
done
```

Observed:

| Launch | Code that ran | Files beside the dylib afterwards |
| ------ | ------------- | --------------------------------- |
| 1  | **v1**  | `App.so.backup`, `App.so.update-ok` |
| 2  | v2  | (none)  |

Expected (per the docs): launch 1 runs v2, and `.update-ok` is only written once v2 has booted.

In an actual `Deno.autoUpdate` flow, using a toast suggesting a restart means that the user sees two toasts saying the same update is available and doesn't receive the update until the second restart.

## Suggested fix

Do the `.update` > dylib swap (and the rollback check) in the launcher, before it loads the dylib, as the docs describe. That fixes both the late apply and the rollback window, since the first code to write `.update-ok` would then be the new version.

## Workaround we're shipping

At startup, if `<dylib>.backup` exists, the app knows it is the stale process that just swapped. It spawns itself again (through `$APPIMAGE` when set) and exits, guarded by an env var so it relaunches at most once. That fixes the double "update ready". It can't restore rollback: deleting `.update-ok` from the stale process would make the next launch roll back before the new code ever ran, so the app has no way to get a real boot check.

title: Cross-process locking for DENO_DIR and build outputs (Cargo-style cache locks)
body:
It is common to have several `deno` processes running against the same `DENO_DIR` and the same project at once: the language server, a dev server, a test run, CI fanning out `deno test` / `deno compile` in parallel. Today the only cross-process coordination is the `node_modules` lock (`LaxSingleProcessFsFlag`). Some of the problems this leads to:

- #35804 and #36423: concurrent `run` / `test` corrupting `node_modules`, and os error 32 rewriting `.bin` shims on Windows.
- Two `deno test --coverage=cov` runs: the second clears `cov/` while the first is still writing, and the first then reports from a half-deleted directory.
- Two `deno compile --output out`: each deletes `out.tmp-*` files "left over from interrupted compilations" at startup, which includes the other run's in-progress temp file. Similar for `deno bundle --outdir` and `deno doc --html --output` (which removes the output directory first).
- `deno.lock`: each writer writes what it read at startup plus its own additions, so with two concurrent writers the last one silently drops the other's entries.
- `deno clean` can delete cache entries another process is reading, and a safe automatic cache GC (#36396, #32932) needs a mode that excludes readers before it can delete anything.

## Proposal

Adopt Cargo's model ([`cargo::util::cache_lock`](<url>)):

- **Package cache locks with three modes** over two lock files in `DENO_DIR/locks/`:
  - `Shared`: held by commands that finish on their own (check, test, compile, cache, install, ...) for their run. Long-running commands (run, serve, LSP, `--watch`) hold no command-wide lock, so `deno clean` doesn't wait for an editor to close.
  - `DownloadExclusive`: held around each HTTP fetch into the cache, in every command. It doesn't block `Shared`, since cache writes are already temp-file-and-rename.
  - `MutateExclusive`: excludes everything; used by `deno clean` and would be what a cache GC takes.
  - Fixed lock order (mutate before download), recursive within a process, out-of-order or upgrade requests refused rather than risking deadlock.
- **Exclusive locks on build outputs** for the whole command: the `--coverage` directory, `compile --output`, `bundle --outdir/--output`, `doc --html --output`. Lock files live under `DENO_DIR/locks/artifacts/` keyed by the normalized path, so nothing is left in published or read-back directories.
- **`deno.lock` writes** become read-merge-write under a lock on the lockfile, reusing `deno_lockfile`'s existing merge-conflict logic, so concurrent writers don't drop each other's entries.
- **Real OS locks** (`flock` / `LockFileEx` via `sys_traits::FsFileLock`): try without blocking, and if contended print Cargo's `Blocking waiting for file lock on <what>` and block. The OS releases them on any exit, so no staleness heuristics are needed. Best effort when the file system doesn't support locking or `DENO_DIR` is read-only.

The existing `node_modules` lock would be left as is; #36423's agreed fix (skip unchanged shim writes) is orthogonal.

## Implementation

I have a working implementation on a fork branch, based on current `main`: <url> It has unit tests for the lock modes and the lockfile merge, plus spec tests that drive real concurrent `deno` processes (clean waits for readers, readers wait for a mutation, downloads exclude downloads, two coverage runs, compile output, lockfile merge). They pass on Linux, macOS and Windows in the fork's CI.

Open questions I'd welcome input on: whether long-running commands should hold `Shared` during startup (graph build / type check) and release it before running user code, and whether lock files under `DENO_DIR` (rather than next to outputs) is the right trade-off.

If this direction is acceptable, I'm happy to open a PR.

Disclosure: the implementation and this write-up were prepared with the help of an AI coding assistant (Claude) and reviewed by me.

title: Deno desktop: options to turn off CEF background networking and to answer permission requests
body:
**Environment:** Deno 2.9.7 (aarch64-apple-darwin), `deno desktop` with the CEF backend (laufey
0.7.0), macOS 26.

### CEF connects to Google on its own

With no request from the page, the packaged app's network service opens HTTPS connections to
Google addresses (2001:4860::/32), which looks like Chromium's background services (component
updates, safe browsing and the like). Apps that promise users a short list of connections can't
keep that promise.

**Ask:** pass `--disable-background-networking` and turn off component updates by default in
`deno desktop`, or give apps a documented switch for both.

### No API to answer permission requests

The window API has no hook for CEF's permission requests (camera, microphone, location,
notifications and so on), so an app can't deny them itself. We work around it with a
`Permissions-Policy` header on every response, which stops the page from asking.

**Ask:** a permission-request callback on the window, or a build-time allow-list, with deny as
the default.

---

Thanks for `deno desktop`. Everything else we checked was what we hoped for: one listener on
127.0.0.1, no debug port by default, and the page's CSP and Permissions-Policy honoured.

`deno run` coverage reports untaken top-level branches as covered when the V8 code cache is warm
body:
> This issue was written by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5).

Version: Deno 2.9.6 (also seen with 2.9.4), macOS arm64

When `deno run` collects coverage, it still loads modules from V8's code cache in `DENO_DIR` (`v8_code_cache_v2`). V8 compiles a module loaded from the code cache without block coverage counters. The coverage profile then describes the module's top-level function as one range with `isBlockCoverage: false`, and `deno coverage` reports every top-level line as covered, including branches that never ran.

The first run in a fresh `DENO_DIR` gives correct coverage, because nothing is cached yet. Every later run gives inflated coverage. This happens with `deno run --coverage=DIR` and with `deno run` when `DENO_COVERAGE_DIR` is set. `deno test --coverage` does not seem to be affected, because `deno test` does not use the code cache. However, `deno run` processes started by a test inherit `DENO_COVERAGE_DIR`, and those processes are affected. In CI, the result also depends on whether a cached `DENO_DIR` restored from an earlier job contains the code cache.

### Steps to reproduce

`main.ts`:

```ts
if (Deno.args.length > 0) {
  console.log("has args");
}
console.log("done");
```

```sh
export DENO_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
DENO_COVERAGE_DIR=cov1 deno run main.ts
DENO_COVERAGE_DIR=cov2 deno run main.ts
deno run --coverage=cov3 main.ts
deno run --no-code-cache --coverage=cov4 main.ts
deno coverage --detailed cov1
deno coverage --detailed cov2
deno coverage --detailed cov3
deno coverage --detailed cov4
```

### Expected

All four reports are the same, with lines 2 and 3 uncovered:

```
cover file:///.../main.ts ... 50.000% (2/4)
  2 |  console.log("has args");
  3 | }
```

### Actual

Only `cov1` (the first run, with an empty code cache) and `cov4` (run with `--no-code-cache`) look like that. `cov2` and `cov3` both report:

```
cover file:///.../main.ts ... 100.000% (4/4)
```

The raw profiles show the difference. This is the top-level function of `main.ts` in each:

```
cov1: isBlockCoverage: true,  ranges: [0-78 count 1], [26-56 count 0]
cov2: isBlockCoverage: false, ranges: [0-78 count 2]
```

### Workaround

Pass `--no-code-cache` to every `deno run` that collects coverage, or delete `v8_code_cache_v2` from `DENO_DIR` before each such run. Neither is practical for processes that a test starts, since they share the same `DENO_DIR` and each one reads the cache that the previous one wrote.

### Possible fix

`CliOptions::code_cache_enabled()` in `cli/args/mod.rs` could return false whenever `coverage_dir()` returns a directory. `coverage_dir()` already covers both `--coverage` and `DENO_COVERAGE_DIR`. Every user of the code cache (the module loader, the worker factory, and the cache warm-up in `cli/factory.rs`) checks `code_cache_enabled()`, so this one change would stop coverage runs from reading or writing the cache. In local testing this makes all four reports above match.

title: fix(ext/process): clear error for non-string env values in Deno.Command
body:
Fixes #18556

(The issue was assigned in 2023 but has had no linked branch or PR since. Happy to step back if someone is still working on it.)

Passing a non-string value in the `env` option of `Deno.Command` (for example
`env: { HELLO: undefined }`) fails with an opaque deserialization error that
doesn't mention `env` or which variable is wrong:

```
error: Uncaught (in promise) TypeError: serde_v8 error: invalid type; expected: string, got: undefined
  at spawnChildInner (ext:deno_process/40_process.js:206:17)
  at spawnChild (ext:deno_process/40_process.js:232:10)
  at Command.spawn (ext:deno_process/40_process.js:828:12)

into the op, and throws a `TypeError` that names the variable and the received
type:

```

values (skipping `undefined`) before spawning.

### Tests

Added `commandEnvValueNotString` to `tests/unit/command_test.ts`. It checks
`undefined`, `null` and a number against `spawn()`, `output()` and
`outputSync()`. It fails on `main` with the `serde_v8` message and passes with

title: fix(core): await cached async modules before resolving dynamic imports
body:
Fixes #37097.

A cached module can have V8 status `Evaluated` while its async evaluation promise is still pending. The shortcut only checks dynamic-evaluation records, so a statically evaluated root or an async descendant can expose its namespace too early (including uninitialized exports).

Skip this shortcut for async graphs and let the existing evaluation-promise path settle them. Synchronous graphs retain the fast path. No new API, dependency, module graph, or wrapper is introduced.

The regression starts a static graph with host-resolved TLA, imports either its root or its async dependency, checks that the import stays pending, then resolves it and checks the value and cached namespace identity/single evaluation.

Validation performed:
- The regression body was executed as a standalone public-API embedding test against the patched published deno_core0.413.0 package.
- An independent embedding matrix covers root/descendant fulfillment and rejection, error identity, cached namespace identity and single fetch/evaluation; full embedding suites passed117 normal/116 JITless (existing2/3 ignored).
- The same matrix fails on the unmodified crate because settlement occurs before the resolver.
- New Rust test formatted with the repository's max_width80/tab_spaces2/edition2024 settings.

Full monorepo `./x fmt`, `./x lint`, and core tests have not been run locally; keeping this draft pending upstream CI/review. No performance benchmark is claimed: already-settled async graphs also take the general path with this conservative fix.

AI assistance: prepared with OpenAI Codex. The checks listed above were actually executed; unrun monorepo checks are explicitly distinguished.

title: feat(publish): run the jsr CLI for `deno publish` and `deno pack`
body:
`deno publish` and `deno pack` now run the [jsr CLI](<url>), which does the publishing and packing. Deno keeps the flags and the type check. This lets JSR change how packages are published without a Deno release.

Target `main`, backport to `v2.9`.

## How it works

1. Deno type checks the package as before: the package source, then (without `--allow-slow-types`) the public API output. Slow types and other publish problems are left to the jsr CLI, which reports them.
2. It resolves the newest jsr CLI version in `>=0.15.0 <1.0.0` from the `jsr` package on the npm registry (respecting `.npmrc`).
3. It downloads `jsr-<target>.zip` from that jsr-io/cli GitHub release, checks it against the release's `.sha256sum`, and caches it in `DENO_DIR/dl/jsr-cli/<version>`. When the version can't be resolved (for example offline), it uses the newest cached version in the range.
4. It runs `jsr publish` / `jsr pack` with the same flags and exits with its exit code. `JSR_BIN_PATH` overrides the binary.

## Removed

- `cli/tools/publish`, `cli/tools/pack`, `cli/registry.rs` and `cli/tools/unfurl_utils.rs`, plus code only they used.
- The `p256`, `spki` and `wasmparser` dependencies of `cli`.
- `tests/specs/publish`, `tests/specs/pack`, `tests/integration/publish_tests.rs` and `tests/specs/jsr/excluded_export_module`. These tests run in jsr-io/cli now.

## Tests

`tests/specs/jsr_cli` replaces the jsr binary with a script that prints its arguments. It covers flag forwarding, `--no-check`, exit codes, a type error, and the `pack` arguments. `jsr/no_unused_params` checks that unused parameters in the public API output still aren't type errors.

## Open

- jsr-io/cli 0.15.0, the lower bound of the version range, isn't released yet.

title: fix(cli): serialize SQLite first-time init across cache eager-init threads
body:
Started digging after seeing the crash dumps in #37045 — two parallel `CacheDB` eager-init threads both end up inside `sqlite3_initialize()`, and the bundled SQLite's `sqlite3MutexInit()` has a store/load ordering hole on arm64: the thread that loses the race observes `xMutexAlloc` already set, skips the vtable copy, then reads a stale NULL `xMutexInit` and calls through it. pc=0 SIGSEGV, exactly what the crash reports show.

Rather than patching around it per cache, this serializes the process-wide first init through a `std::sync::Once`:

- `ensure_sqlite_initialized()` opens a throwaway in-memory connection under the Once, which drives `sqlite3_initialize()` to completion exactly once.
- `CacheDB::from_path()` calls it before spawning the eager-init thread, so in practice the init finishes on the thread constructing the cache (usually the main thread at startup) and every eager thread then takes the already-initialized fast path.
- `actually_open_connection()` calls it too, since `in_memory()` caches skip `from_path()`.

After the Once fires, later `sqlite3_initialize()` calls hit the `isInit` early-return, so the racy first-enter window is gone entirely. Cost is one in-memory open once per process, a few microseconds.

Other rusqlite consumers (webstorage, node:sqlite) open lazily on their own thread and don't spawn parallel first-opens at startup, so I left them alone — happy to extend the guard if you'd rather have it shared.

Added a regression test that constructs 16 on-disk caches from 16 threads at once. Fair warning: the crash itself is an arm64 memory-ordering thing, so the test can't deterministically reproduce the segfault on CI hardware — it exercises the parallel-open path under contention and would catch the serialization being dropped.

Tests: `cargo test -p deno --lib cache::cache_db` — 11 passed, including the new one. `rustfmt --check` clean.

title: fix(ext/web): avoid retaining oversized resource stream buffers
body:
Fixes #37063.

Resource-backed streams allocate a 64 KiB buffer for each read. When a read produces only a small chunk, the default reader receives a view that keeps the entire backing buffer alive. Retaining many chunks from a chunked HTTP response can therefore retain substantially more memory than the response body.

Enqueue an exact-sized copy for short reads consumed by default readers in both resource-backed stream implementations. Full-buffer reads keep their existing path, and BYOB readers retain the supplied buffer, offset and transfer behavior.

Validation:
- All eight new regression tests pass against a normal Linux source build. Five compact-buffer cases fail on the original implementation; the full-chunk boundary and two BYOB cases already pass.
- The existing `streams_test`, `fetch_test`, `file_test`, `stdio_test` and `net_test` suites pass through the official Rust unit-test harness with the fixed executable.
- A local benchmark retains a 4 MiB response using 1,000-byte, 16 KiB and 64 KiB server chunks, with and without Content-Length, three runs per case. The 1,000-byte chunked case retains 263 MiB of backing buffers before the fix and 4 MiB after it. All six fixed cases retain exactly 4 MiB. This is retained ArrayBuffer capacity, not process RSS; timings from this shared development machine are not a controlled throughput benchmark.
- Formatting, JavaScript lint and `git diff --check` pass. The full repository test suite was not run.

The built executable was copied to the Linux filesystem for the tests; its SHA256 matches the build output.

title: fix(ext/web): preserve BOMs after streamed ASCII chunks
body:
Fixes #37090.

After decoding an ASCII chunk with `stream: true`, `TextDecoder` currently treats a BOM at the start of the next chunk as the beginning of the stream and removes it. For example, decoding `a` followed by `\uFEFFb` produces `ab` instead of `a\uFEFFb`. This also affects `TextDecoderStream` when the bytes arrive in separate chunks.

Track whether the ASCII streaming fast path has already consumed the initial BOM position. Carry that state into subsequent decoding and clear it when the stream ends, while retaining the ASCII fast path. Leading BOM handling and the public `ignoreBOM` setting remain unchanged.

Regression coverage exercises every byte split in two inputs with both `fatal` and `ignoreBOM` settings, final and streaming chunks, empty chunks, decoder reuse, and the `TextDecoderStream` pipeline.

Validation: all 30 encoding unit tests pass through the official Rust unit-test harness against a normal source build. All three new regressions fail on unchanged source (27 existing tests pass). Full formatting and JavaScript lint checks pass. The Windows-mounted build executable was slow to load under WSL, so the passing harness run used its supported executable override with a SHA256-identical copy on the Linux filesystem. The full repository test suite was not run.

title: fix(ext/websocket): time out the closing handshake
body:
Fixes #27924.

`WebSocket.close()` sends a close frame and moves the socket to CLOSING, then waits for the peer's close frame with no bound. A peer that never answers, because it is wedged, behind a broken proxy, or simply does not implement the handshake, leaves the socket in CLOSING forever: `close` never fires, and anything waiting on it (reconnect logic, cleanup, memory) hangs with it.

RFC 6455 §7.1.1 lets an endpoint drop the connection when the closing handshake does not complete, and browsers bound the wait (Firefox's `network.websocket.timeout.close` defaults to 20 s). This PR does the same: `close()` arms a timer, and if the socket is still CLOSING when it fires, the socket becomes CLOSED, a `close` event with `wasClean: false` and code 1006 is dispatched, and the resource is closed. A close frame that arrives in time cancels the timer, as it already cancels the idle-timeout timer. The event loop ignores whatever the dropped resource yields afterwards, so `close` fires once.

It applies to both roles: #27924 is the server calling `close()`, and the same hang hits a client whose server goes silent. We hit the client side in production: `@nktkas/rews`, the reconnecting socket under the Hyperliquid SDK, closes a socket whose keep-alive ping went unanswered and waits for `close` before reconnecting, so a network blip left it "connecting" for 11 hours.

The timeout is 5 s here. I'm happy to change it, or to make it configurable, if you prefer a different value.

The new unit test runs a TCP server that completes the upgrade and then never sends another frame, and checks that the client's `close()` ends with a 1006 close.

**AI disclosure:** this PR was written with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5): it diagnosed the production hang, wrote the fix and the test, and drafted this description. A human reviewed it, and the fix was verified by building Deno and running `tests/unit/websocket_test.ts` (all 49 tests pass; the new one hangs on an unpatched build).

title: fix(ext/node): stream file-backed blobs and positional slices
body:
Fixes #32316.

`fs.openAsBlob()` currently reads the entire file and copies it into a memory blob before returning. This adds a file-backed BlobPart with reader-scoped descriptors and positional reads, so opening a blob reads metadata and a sliced blob reads only its selected range. Streams yield at most 64 KiB per chunk, support cancellation/BYOB, and release their descriptors on completion, cancellation, or collection. Unread blobs retain no open descriptor.

File identity/metadata are checked before and after reads, changes produce `NotReadableError`, and reopening uses the filesystem abstraction and current read permissions. File parts remain integrated with Blob/File composition, FormData and object URLs. Embedded VFS files without native handles retain the memory-backed fallback.

The Rust BlobPart API now exposes fallible ranged reads and optional reader creation; Blob::read_all returns a Result, with its callers updated. Memory parts still lend their bytes.

Validation on Linux:
- Built deno and denort; full CLI cargo check passed.
- 128 JS tests passed (14 new regressions and existing node:fs/Blob/File tests), 20 existing tests ignored.
- 3 Rust blob tests passed, including positional sparse-file reads and borrowed memory ranges.
- New compile/open_as_blob spec passed using an embedded VFS asset.
- Repository formatter, JS lint and Clippy with repository deny flags passed.
- A local debug-build 256 MiB sparse-file probe reduced open-time RSS growth from about 513 MiB to 1.4 MiB (517 ms to 0.82 ms); its final 100-byte slice read correctly. These are single-run observations, not a benchmark suite.

Includes Windows directory behavior coverage, but Windows execution was not available locally.

title: fix(ext/node): throw on invalid brotli input in brotliDecompressSync
body:
zlib.brotliDecompressSync accepted malformed Brotli streams and returned
the partially decoded output instead of throwing the way Node.js does.
The underlying sync decode op ran the decoder but ignored its result
code, so a stream that errors mid-decode (for example one that declares
a single block type and then issues a block switch) produced whatever
bytes had been written so far rather than an error. Besides diverging
from Node, this let a tiny input expand into megabytes of output before
quietly returning.

This detects BROTLI_DECODER_RESULT_ERROR in the sync path and surfaces
it through the same onerror mechanism the async write path already uses,
so both paths now report the decoder error consistently. It also updates
the Brotli crates (brotli 9.1.0 / brotli-decompressor 6.2.0) to pick up
the upstream fix for CVE-2026-111497; Deno was never affected by the
related RCE since it uses the memory-safe Rust decoder rather than the C
one, but the newer decoder reports the invalid stream with the correct
block-switch error code.

title: fix(install): respect --prod with an existing lockfile
body:
## Summary

An existing full `deno.lock` causes `deno install --prod` to materialize development-only npm packages from the complete resolution snapshot, even though their root requirements have been filtered out. The same issue affects frozen production installs and `deno ci --prod`.

Track production manifest roots and successfully resolved explicit module-graph requirements separately from the complete lockfile resolution. At file materialization, use the existing resolution subset and its dependency closure. This preserves the full resolution and lockfile, dependencies shared by production and development paths, and explicitly imported runtime packages.

Add isolated and hoisted regression coverage for full lockfiles, frozen installs, `deno ci`, and entrypoint installs.

Fixes #37082

## Validation

- **Patched installer library:** all 90 scenarios met their expected package selection. The matrix covers isolated/hoisted linkers, workspace dependencies, shared production/dev dependencies, peer/optional dependencies, dev-only projects, explicit entrypoint roots, frozen installs, and in-place transitions. Resolution root sets and lockfile bytes were unchanged across all 90 baseline/patched pairs.
- Final installer-library unit tests: **46 passed**.
- Existing snapshot subset test: **passed**.
- Targeted installer-library Clippy using the upstream deny options: **passed**.
- Formatting check for all eight changed files: **passed**.
- Production spec suite against official Deno 2.9.7: **five existing cases passed; all eight new regression variants detected development packages on disk**.

title: fix(tsc): make raw import stubs ambient
body:
## Summary

- emit ambient declarations for synthetic bytes, text, and CSS raw-import modules
- add coverage for `deno check --unstable-raw-imports --all` with a CSS import

## Rationale

Raw-import sources are type-only synthetic modules. Declaring their bindings as ordinary uninitialized `const` variables works while the shim remains an implementation detail, but `--all` type-checks the synthetic module itself and reports TS1155/TS2454.

Using `declare const` expresses the intended ambient/type-only semantics and keeps the generated module valid when checked directly.

Fixes #36534

title: fix(ext/node): ignore late IPC CLOSE after child exit
body:
Fixes #37040.

## Problem
The child-exit path may disconnect an IPC channel while readLoop is waiting for a read. A subsequent internal CLOSE message then triggers a second disconnect(), raising ERR_IPC_DISCONNECTED even though shutdown was already handled.

## Change
Only disconnect in the CLOSE handler if the channel is still connected. Leave explicit user-initiated repeated disconnect calls unchanged.

## Regression coverage
Add a Unix-only regression test covering late channel closure after a child exits, repeated 25 times.

## Validation
Not executed locally; CI and race reproduction are required before moving this draft PR to ready for review.

title: fix(node): prevent child IPC socket inheritance by grandchildren
body:
Fixes #37041.

## Problem
The IPC socket a forked child receives via NODE_CHANNEL_FD remains open across exec on Unix. Grandchildren can inherit the socket, delaying EOF in the parent and unintentionally retaining IPC access.

## Change
Set FD_CLOEXEC on the adopted child IPC descriptor with fcntl(F_GETFD/F_SETFD), preserving existing descriptor flags.

## Regression coverage
Add a Linux-only fork/spawn test verifying that an exec'd grandchild does not inherit the parent's IPC socket.

## Validation
Not executed locally. Please validate on Linux CI (and other Unix platforms as appropriate) before marking this draft PR ready.

title: fix(fs): allow updating timestamps on read-only files on Windows
body:
Fixes #36997.

## Problem
On Windows, path-based utime/utimes fails for files with FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY, including Git object files. `filetime::set_file_times` requests GENERIC_WRITE although updating timestamps only requires FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES.

## Change
Open the file with FILE_WRITE_ATTRIBUTES and FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS on Windows, then call `filetime::set_file_handle_times`. Keep the non-Windows path unchanged. This covers sync and async Deno APIs and the node:fs wrappers.

## Regression coverage
Add Windows-only tests for Deno.utimeSync, Deno.utime, fs.utimesSync, and fs.utimes on a read-only temporary file.

## Validation
Not executed locally. Please run Windows CI and review before marking ready; this is a draft patch.

title: fix(cli): require = for deno upgrade --unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors
body:
Since flag parsing moved from clap to `deno_cli_parser` (#35982),
`deno upgrade --unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors 1.46.0` parses `1.46.0` as
a host to ignore certificate errors for instead of as the version to upgrade
to. The version is dropped, so the command behaves like a plain
`deno upgrade`, and certificate errors are ignored only for a host named
`1.46.0`.

clap defined this flag once, in `unsafely_ignore_certificate_errors_arg()`,
with `num_args(0..)` and `require_equals(true)`. In
`libs/cli_parser/src/defs.rs` the shared definition in `COMPILE_ARGS` kept
`.require_equals()`, but the separate copy in `UPGRADE_SUBCOMMAND` did not.
Without it the parser takes every following non-flag argument as a value.
This adds `.require_equals()` to the upgrade copy. A bare flag again means
all hosts, and `--unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors=host,...` works as
before.

This is the same kind of port regression as #37075 (`deno bundle
--external`). It came up while comparing the other ported flags against their
clap definitions for that fix, and it was the only other mismatch.

Tests: a parser test in `libs/cli_parser/src/tests_full.rs` checks that
`deno upgrade --unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors 1.46.0` gives version
`1.46.0` and an empty ignore list, and that
`--unsafely-ignore-certificate-errors=deno.land,localhost 1.46.0` still
parses both. It fails without the fix and passes with it. The full
`deno_cli_parser` test suite, `cargo clippy -p deno_cli_parser --all-targets
-- -D warnings` and rustfmt pass.

It generated the fix and the test.

title: fix(bundle): make --external take exactly one value per flag
body:
Fixes #37074

Since flag parsing moved from clap to `deno_cli_parser` (#35982),
`deno bundle --external elasticlunr src/main.ts` treats `src/main.ts` as a
second external instead of the entrypoint, so the command reports "Bundled 0
modules". clap defined `--external` with `ArgAction::Append` and
`num_args(1)`; the port used `NumArgs::ZeroOrMore`, and without
`require_equals` the parser then consumes every following non-flag argument
as a value. `--external=elasticlunr` was unaffected.

This changes `--external` to `NumArgs::Exact(1)` and keeps `Append`, so each
occurrence takes one value and the flag can still be repeated
(`--external=a --external b`).

Tests: two parser tests in `libs/cli_parser/src/tests_full.rs`, next to the
`--sourcemap` ones from #36723, cover `--external elasticlunr main.ts` and
`--external=a --external b main.ts`. Both fail without the fix (the
entrypoint ends up in `external`) and pass with it. The full
`deno_cli_parser` test suite, `cargo clippy -p deno_cli_parser --all-targets
-- -D warnings` and rustfmt pass.

title: fix(core): don't overflow on an out-of-range source map line

title: fix(ext/http): honor Connection: close in HTTP/1 responses
body:
Fixes #37050.

The raw HTTP/1 server does not check application response headers when deciding whether to reuse a connection. An application response containing `Connection: close` can therefore leave the connection reusable. When the server already intends to close it, the response serializer also adds another close header.

This change honors a case-insensitive `close` token in application response headers across the direct and asynchronous response paths. Both response-head writers retain the application's header without appending a duplicate close header.

Regression coverage includes pipelined requests with empty, small, and larger request bodies and synchronous, asynchronous, and streaming responses. A serializer test checks fixed-length and chunked response heads through both output APIs, including mixed-case comma-separated tokens.

- Built the modified Deno runtime and test server.

title: fix(ext/node): return false from exists permission errors
body:
Fixes #37062.

`node:fs.exists()` and `node:fs.existsSync()` report filesystem and permission failures as `false`; they do not surface those failures through an error channel. Deno's permission check propagated `NotCapable`, which made the sync API throw and left the callback-based API with a rejected internal promise whose callback was never invoked.

This change makes both ops return `false` when permission resolution rejects the path. The regression coverage exercises both the sync return value and the asynchronous callback under a no-read-permission test.

Validation:

- `rustfmt --edition 2024 --check ext/node/ops/fs.rs`

title: fix: upgrade quinn-proto to 0.11.19
body:
We were pinned to `quinn-proto` 0.11.16, which is behind on five RUSTSEC advisories. This is a semver-compatible lockfile bump — `quinn` 0.11.8 requires `quinn-proto ^0.11.12`, so there are no code changes.

All five are remotely reachable by an unauthenticated peer: both through `Deno.QuicEndpoint` / `Deno.connectQuic` (`--unstable-net`) and through `WebTransport`, which is exposed on the global scope unconditionally along with `Deno.upgradeWebTransport`.

| Advisory | Issue | Patched in |
|---|---|---|
| [RUSTSEC-2026-0341](<url>) (High, 7.5) | The stream reassembly memory-exhaustion guard added in 0.11.15 can be bypassed via the unordered-read deduplication path. Small gapped STREAM frames keep memory pressure below the defragmentation threshold so the check never fires — ~3 GB of receiver memory from 125 MB of accounted stream data under default config. | 0.11.17 |
| [RUSTSEC-2026-0342](<url>) | Zero-length DATAGRAM frames bypass the receive buffer limit. | 0.11.17 |
| [RUSTSEC-2026-0339](<url>) | Unbounded growth of pending connection ID retirements. | 0.11.17 |
| [RUSTSEC-2026-0338](<url>) | Remote peer can panic the connection with zero-length STREAM frames during unordered reads. | 0.11.18 |
| [RUSTSEC-2026-0340](<url>) (High) | Peer minimum ACK delay can panic when ACK_FREQUENCY transmission is enabled. Not reachable today — `ack_frequency_config` defaults to `None` and we never set it in `ext/net/quic.rs` — but fixed here regardless. | 0.11.18 |

[RUSTSEC-2026-0343](<url>) does not apply to us (`unaffected < 0.11.17`), and 0.11.19 carries its fix too.

### Not related to the QPACK "Header Accordions" attack

For anyone who finds this while looking into [that disclosure](<url>) and [hyperium/h3#378](<url>): we aren't affected by it. We have no `h3` dependency, `Deno.serve` is HTTP/1.1 + HTTP/2 only, and `reqwest` is built without the `http3` feature. The one QPACK decoder we do have is the minimal one in `web-transport-proto`, used for the WebTransport extended CONNECT handshake, and it has none of the attack preconditions: it rejects dynamic-table references outright (killing reference amplification), decodes into a `HashMap` rather than a panicking `http::HeaderMap`, and its input is already capped at 64 KiB by `MAX_HANDSHAKE_FRAME_SIZE` (#36068), enforced incrementally on both the SETTINGS and CONNECT read loops.

### Verification

`cargo check --locked --bin deno` passes, and the relevant suites are green locally:

- `cargo test --locked unit::quic_test` — 1 passed
- `cargo test --locked --test specs webtransport` — 3 passed (`run::webtransport`, `run::webtransport_datagram_overflow`, `run::webtransport_failed_datagrams`)

title: fix(cli): list the lts channel in the deno upgrade usage
body:
## Summary

`deno upgrade` accepts `lts` as a release channel, but the usage block that `deno
upgrade` prints when it rejects a version or hash does not list it, so the only
user-facing enumeration of channels is incomplete.

- `cli/lib/shared.rs:75` — `ReleaseChannel::deserialize` maps `"lts" => Self::Lts`
  (and `:58` serializes `Self::Lts => "lts"`).
- `cli/tools/upgrade.rs:1236` — `RequestedVersion::from_upgrade_flags` tries
  `ReleaseChannel::deserialize(&val.to_lowercase())` on the positional
  `version_or_hash_or_channel`, so `deno upgrade lts` resolves to
  `Latest(ReleaseChannel::Lts)`.
- `cli/tools/upgrade.rs:391-397` — the update notification for an LTS release tells the
  user "Run `deno upgrade lts` to install it", and `:455-459` handles
  `ReleaseChannel::Lts` when comparing versions, so the channel is not just parseable, it
  is what deno itself recommends typing.
- `cli/args/flags.rs:47-53` — the `Channel` block of `UPGRADE_USAGE` listed only
  `stable`, `alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, `canary`. That string is printed by the two
  `bail!` sites at `cli/tools/upgrade.rs:1263` and `:1273`.

The fix adds `lts` after `stable`, in the existing most-stable-to-most-unstable order,
and updates the three spec snapshots that embed the printed block
(`tests/specs/upgrade/invalid_version/{shorthand,canary,version}.out`).

Users already reach for it: #28194 and #29443 are both about `deno upgrade lts`.

title: fix(ext/webgpu): don't sleep 10ms after device_poll in mapAsync and onSubmittedWorkDone
body:
Fixes #37042

`GPUBuffer.mapAsync()` and `GPUQueue.onSubmittedWorkDone()` poll the device with `PollType::wait_indefinitely()` and then `tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(10))` before re-checking whether the callback has fired. The blocking poll already waits for the GPU and runs the callback, so the sleep only adds a fixed delay: every call takes at least ~10 ms (about 11-15 ms on Windows), even with an idle GPU.

This replaces the sleep with `tokio::task::yield_now()`, so the receiver future gets polled, sets `done`, and the loop exits. If the callback has not fired yet, the next iteration blocks in `device_poll(wait_indefinitely())` again, as before; there is no busy loop.

Measured with the standalone repro in #37042 (200 calls each, p50, Deno 2.9.0 vs this change built locally, Windows 11, RTX 4090):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `mapAsync`, nothing queued | 11.4 ms | 0.01 ms |
| tiny copy + submit + `mapAsync` | 15.5 ms | 0.06 ms |
| empty submit + `onSubmittedWorkDone` | 15.4 ms | 0.04 ms |

In a real workload (a small conv net, one batch-64 forward + readback per step) a forward went from 16.9 ms to 5.2 ms, with byte-identical results.

Testing:
- `cargo fmt -p deno_webgpu -- --check` and `cargo check --bin deno` pass on `main` (toolchain 1.95.0); the change was also built as a release binary on v2.9.0 and exercised by the repro above and a full application workload.
- I did not add a unit test: the change is a latency one, and a timing assertion would be flaky in CI. Existing webgpu tests should cover the behaviour (the promise still resolves after the callback). I have not run `./x lint` or the webgpu unit tests locally; happy to fix anything CI reports.

title: fix(npm): repair dedup-removed edges in retained peer-only subtrees
body:
Fixes #37022.

### Summary

During incremental npm resolution, the version dedup pass (`run_dedup_pass`
in `libs/npm/resolution/graph.rs`) removes child edges pointing at
consolidated-away versions from every graph node, but only root packages were
queued for the post-dedup Phase 1 repair BFS. Phase 1 never descends into peer
dependency edges, so a retained package reachable only through peer edges (a
"peer-only" subtree, e.g. the old `@tiptap/<email>` kept alive by the retained
extension's peer context) never got its removed ordinary edge repaired. The
generated lockfile/snapshot then silently dropped a required dependency
(`prosemirror-view`).

### Fix

`run_dedup_pass` now tracks nodes that lose an ordinary (`Dep`-kind) child edge
during consolidation and queues those non-root nodes for the post-dedup Phase 1
BFS (in addition to the roots), so their edges are re-resolved to the
consolidated versions. The queue is sorted by node id for determinism; nodes
that are already roots are skipped since they are queued already.

### Evidence

- New regression test
  `dedup_repairs_removed_edges_in_retained_peer_only_subtree` in
  `libs/npm/resolution/graph.rs` mirrors the reported scenario (an
  override-pinned transitive dep consolidated away while a peer-only package is
  retained): fails before the fix (`<email>` loses its `leaf` dependency),
  passes after.
- `cargo test -p deno_npm --lib`: 249 passed, 0 failed (includes the new test).
- `cargo clippy -p deno_npm --lib --tests`: no new warnings (one pre-existing
  clippy.toml config warning). `cargo fmt --check`: clean.

### Honest limits

- The full `deno` binary build and CLI integration/spec tests were not run
  (very heavy; only the `deno_npm` crate's unit tests ran locally). CI must
  cover the rest.
- The repair re-processes the affected node's subtree from a root-scoped path,
  so ancestor-scoped npm overrides would not apply during that repair
  traversal; unconditional overrides (the reported case) are unaffected.

title: fix(ext/node): make deepEqual symmetric for array holes vs undefined
body:
Fixes #37029.

## Problem

In loose mode, `assert.deepEqual` treated an array hole and an own `undefined` element as equal in one argument order but not the other:

```js
import assert from "node:assert";
assert.deepEqual([1, , 3], [1, undefined, 3]); // passed, should throw
assert.deepEqual([1, undefined, 3], [1, , 3]); // threw (correct)
```

Node (22, 24, 26) throws in both orders: a hole never equals an own `undefined`, even loosely.

## Root cause

`objEquiv`'s array fast path in `ext/node/polyfills/internal/util/comparisons.ts` (relaxed for loose mode by #32763) skipped the own-property check in loose mode and fell through to `innerDeepEqual(undefined, undefined)`. The reverse argument order goes through `sparseArrayEquiv`, which does check own-property-ness, hence the asymmetry.

## Fix

Port the upstream Node condition (nodejs/node#61587, fixing nodejs/node#61583): the own-property check now applies in all modes, with a carve-out so loose mode still lets `null` equal `undefined`:

```ts
if (
  (a[i] !== undefined || !hasOwn(a, i)) &&
  (mode !== kLoose || a[i] !== null)
) {
  return false;
}
```

This also removes the now-dead loose-mode `innerDeepEqual` fallthrough that #32763 added (with the new first branch it can no longer return false).

One deliberate non-port: upstream #61587 also restructured the `else if` branch with a `(mode !== kLoose || b[i] !== null)` guard, which as a side effect makes `assert.deepEqual([5], [null])` pass in loose mode on current Node (verified empirically on v24.20.0 and v26.12.0) — contradicting `==` semantics. Deno's existing `else if` already handles `null` correctly via `innerDeepEqual`, so I left it untouched.

## Tests

- Added regression test in `tests/unit_node/assert_test.ts` ("[node/assert] deepEqual is symmetric for array holes vs undefined"): both orders throw, `notDeepEqual` passes both orders, holes still equal holes, loose `null`/`undefined` still equal, strict `null`/`undefined` still throws.
- Verified the exact old/new branch logic against Node v24.20.0 and v26.12.0 on a 14-case matrix (holes, undefined, null, values; loose and strict): the new logic matches Node on every case except the deliberate `[5]`-vs-`[null]` divergence noted above. The old logic reproduced the reported asymmetry.
- `tsc --noEmit` on the modified file: no new errors vs pristine (89 → 88; remaining errors are pre-existing artifacts of type-checking this primordials-based file outside Deno's build).

## Honest limits

- I could not execute Deno's own test suites here: building the `deno` binary was infeasible in this environment (2 vCPU / 7 GB RAM; a full build takes many hours and risks OOM at link time), and the node polyfill is baked into the binary at build time, so the new unit test could not be run locally. CI (`./x test` / node unit tests) must cover it.
- `./x verify` (fmt + lint-js) could not be run without a built binary; the change follows the file's existing formatting conventions (the touched file also carries `// deno-lint-ignore-file`).

## AI disclosure

Per the contributing guidelines: this PR was prepared with AI assistance (agentic coding helper, no human review of the patch yet). The fix is a direct port of the reviewed upstream Node change nodejs/node#61587, and the behavior matrix was verified empirically against Node v24.20.0 and v26.12.0 as described above. This work was claimed through the open Claim Protocol (claim comment 6238743908 on #37029).

title: fix(ext/web): ignore inherited signal in addEventListener options
body:
Fixes #37023.

If `Object.prototype.signal` is set to an `AbortSignal`, `addEventListener` recurses until it throws `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. For example:

```js
Object.prototype.signal = AbortSignal.timeout(5000);
new EventTarget().addEventListener("foo", () => {});
```

Node runs this without an error.

`addEventListenerOptionsConverter` returns an object literal, and that object only gets its own `signal` property when the caller passed one. `addEventListener` then reads `options?.signal`, which falls back to the polluted `Object.prototype.signal`. To attach its abort steps, it calls `signal.addEventListener("abort", abortListener)` with no options. That inner call builds another options object without its own `signal`, so it picks up the same inherited signal, and so on forever.

The fix always sets `signal: undefined` as an own property on the converted options, so the inherited value is never read. A `signal` given in the caller's options dictionary is still read the same way as before.

Test: `eventTargetIgnoresSignalOnPollutedObjectPrototype` in `tests/unit/event_target_test.ts`. It fails on `main` with the `RangeError` and passes with the fix. `cargo test unit::event_target_test`, `unit::abort_controller_test` and `unit::event_test` pass. `tools/format.js` (dprint) and `tools/lint.js --js` are clean for the changed files.

title: fix(ext/node): apply zlib dictionary option when deflating and raw inflating
body:
Fixes #37035.

The `dictionary` option of `node:zlib` was stored by the native binding but only ever used when `inflate()` returned `Z_NEED_DICT`. Deflate, DeflateRaw and InflateRaw never ask for a dictionary, so it was silently ignored there: compressed output was identical to compressing without a dictionary, and raw streams compressed with a preset dictionary by Node (or any zlib) failed to inflate with `invalid distance too far back`.

This mirrors Node's `ZlibContext::SetDictionary()`:

- After `deflateInit2`/`inflateInit2`, set the dictionary with `deflateSetDictionary` for Deflate/DeflateRaw and `inflateSetDictionary` for InflateRaw. Other inflate modes keep setting it on `Z_NEED_DICT`.
- Apply it again after `reset()`, since `deflateReset`/`inflateReset` discard it.
- Skip empty dictionaries, as Node does.

The existing `test-zlib-dictionary.js` compat test passes with and without this change, because it round-trips data within Deno, where ignoring the dictionary on both sides is self-consistent. The new unit test pins the bytes Node produces for raw and zlib-wrapped deflate, inflates Node's output, and covers deflating after `reset()`. It fails on Deno 2.9.4 and passes with this change.

Testing:
- `./x test-node zlib_test` passes
- `./x test-compat test-zlib`: `test-zlib-dictionary.js` and `test-zlib-dictionary-fail.js` pass. The 3 failures (`test-zlib-brotli-flush-invalid-kind`, `test-zlib-reset-during-write`, `test-zlib-brotli-dictionary`) also fail on 2.9.4 and aren't enabled in `config.jsonc`.
- `./x fmt` leaves no changes; `./x lint` passes

title: fix(ext/crypto): reject EC public keys not on the curve at import
body:
Fixes #37031

`crypto.subtle.importKey` accepted P-256, P-384, and P-521 public keys whose point is not on the curve, for the `raw`, `spki`, and `jwk` formats. The Web Crypto spec requires a `DataError` in that case, and Node.js, Bun, Chromium, and Firefox all reject these keys at import.

The import code only parsed the SEC1 encoding and checked for the identity point. The invalid key was then rejected later with an unrelated error that depended on the operation (`exportKey`, ECDSA `verify`, or ECDH `deriveBits`, where it was reported as a private key decoding error).

This validates the point with `PublicKey::from_sec1_bytes` at import time for all three formats and throws a `DataError` (`invalid P-<n> elliptic curve point`). For `spki`, the check runs after the curve mismatch check, so a key for the wrong curve still reports `curve mismatch`.

### Tests

Added `testImportEcPublicKeyNotOnCurve` to `tests/unit/webcrypto_test.ts`. For each curve and for both ECDH and ECDSA, it generates a key, exports it as `raw`, `spki`, and `jwk`, flips the last byte of `y` so the point is off the curve, and asserts that import rejects.

### AI disclosure

Developed with help from Claude. I reviewed the changes and ran the tests and the reproduction from the issue myself.

title: fix(lsp): respect minimumDependencyAge in completions and resolution
body:
## Summary

The CLI honors `minimumDependencyAge` (minutes, ISO 8601 duration, RFC3339 date, `false`/`0`, and the object form with `exclude`) when resolving npm and JSR versions. The language server did not: it built its npm/jsr search APIs and managed npm version resolver with empty newest-dependency-date options, so import-specifier completions and LSP-side matching of the newest version could offer versions newer than the configured cutoff.

This change shares the CLI helpers that turn a `MinimumDependencyAgeConfig` into npm and JSR newest-dependency-date options, including `exclude` exact names and wildcard prefixes and the `.npmrc` `min-release-age` / 24-hour fallbacks when no age is set. Those options are used for import completions, managed npm resolution, and JSR cache resolution. The process-global search APIs are rebuilt after the config tree refreshes, so editing `deno.json` updates completions.

Closes #31009

Versions newer than `2025-03-01` are omitted for `jsr:@denotest/add` and `npm:@denotest/min-release-age-latest`. `exclude` and `minimumDependencyAge: false` offer them again after a `deno.json` reload.

title: fix(core): keep op contexts alive until the isolate is disposed
body:
Fixes #37025

### The bug

With V8 150.x, `FunctionTemplateInfo` keeps raw pointers to the `CFunction` overloads passed to `FunctionTemplate::build_fast`. deno_core stores those overloads in each `OpCtx` (`OpCtx::fast_fn_overloads`), on the assumption that `OpCtx` lives until the isolate is disposed. It didn't: `InnerIsolateState::drop` → `cleanup()` → `JsRealmInner::destroy()` dropped the realm's `ContextState`, and with it `op_ctxs`, before `ManuallyDrop::drop(&mut self.v8_isolate)`. V8 only cancels and joins concurrent optimization jobs inside `Isolate::Dispose`. A TurboFan job that was inlining a fast API call at that moment read the freed slice and segfaulted in `c_functions_with_signatures` (`JSCallReducer::ReduceCallApiFunction` → `GetFastApiCallTarget`). The issue has the full backtrace and a standalone reproduction. In practice this showed up as `deno lint` with a lint plugin crashing in about 1–2% of parallel runs.

### The fix

- **`deno_core`:** `ContextState::op_ctxs` is now an `Rc<OpCtxs>`. `JsRealmInner::destroy()` returns it (`#[must_use]`), and `InnerIsolateState` stores it in a new `retired_op_ctxs` field. That field is dropped only after `v8_isolate` has been dropped, i.e. after `Isolate::Dispose` has joined every compile job. Everything that holds `v8::Global`s (the rest of `ContextState`, the module map, `JsRuntimeState`) is still dropped before the isolate, as before. The op contexts themselves hold no V8 handles: their `OpState` has already been cleared, and the op driver is already shut down. `prepare_for_snapshot` drops them right after `cleanup()`, because templates built for a snapshot have no fast-call overloads.
- **`deno lint`:** `PluginHost::create` used to detach the plugin host thread, so the process could reach `exit()` while that thread was still disposing of its isolate. `PluginHostProxy` now owns the thread. When the proxy is dropped, its sender is dropped first, which ends the host's run loop. The proxy then waits until the host's worker (and its isolate) has been dropped, and joins the thread if it has already finished. The wait is bounded (10s) and does not include the thread's tokio runtime shutdown, so a blocking task a plugin left running can't hang `deno lint`.

### Tests

- `runtime::tests::misc::op_ctxs_outlive_isolate` (deno_core) checks the ordering deterministically. It puts a probe in an isolate slot (slots are dropped by `OwnedIsolate::drop`, i.e. only once the runtime starts disposing the isolate) and asserts that the op contexts are still alive at that point and are released afterwards. It fails on `main` with "op contexts were freed before the isolate was disposed". A stress test that races TurboFan isn't practical here, because deno_core's own tests initialize V8 with `--predictable`, which disables concurrent recompilation.
- `tests/specs/lint/lint_plugin_shutdown` makes sure that work a plugin leaves pending (timers, an in-flight async read) doesn't keep `deno lint` from exiting now that it waits for the plugin host. All 18 `lint_plugin*` spec tests pass.

### Before/after

I used the standalone reproduction from #37025 (a tiny lint plugin and six generated ~480-line files) on Linux x86_64 with 8 cores. I built `--profile release-lite` from `a18ce3371` without and with this patch, then ran both binaries at the same time, 2000 runs each with 4 parallel per binary, so both saw the same load:

| Binary | SIGSEGV (exit 139) |
|---|---|
| `main` (a18ce3371) | 28 / 2000 |
| this PR | **0 / 2000** |

`cargo clippy -p deno_core -p deno --all-targets -- -D warnings`, rustfmt and dprint are clean.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed the change and ran the measurements above.

title: fix(check): resolve npm subpath declaration paths
body:
## Summary

`deno check` maps some `npm:` subpaths to JavaScript or a guessed path under the package root, losing sibling declarations and wildcard exports even when the package ships valid types.

Resolve concrete subpaths with the existing Node resolver in types mode before generating TypeScript paths.

## Changes

- Resolve exports conditions, wildcard substitutions and sibling `.d.ts`/`.d.mts`/`.d.cts` declarations through the existing resolver.
- Apply concrete source keys after root enumeration and compatibility fallbacks, preserving the package version selected for each specifier and import-map alias.
- Use exact ambient shims for exported untyped subpaths, without masking another version's declarations. Reject used blocked/private exports; unused invalid aliases do not fail discovery.
- Add registry-backed regressions for declaration formats, export precedence, aliases, two package versions, reversed import-map order and typed/untyped exports. Runtime and LSP resolver code is unchanged.

## Tests

Local verification on Windows x64:

- Core declaration matrix: 14/14 valid cases, with runtime, Node and TypeScript controls.
- Multi-version replay: 9/9 cases; all 28 typed wrong assignments rejected with TS2322, with runtime/info confirming the expected versions.
- Official `check_subpath_declarations` and `check_subpath_versions` specs: 12/12 pass.
- `cargo test --locked -p deno --lib tsc::tsconfig_gen`: 32/32 pass.
- Formatting and lint passed with documented process-local Windows adaptations: bounded argument batches preserve all JS lint inputs; a bindgen header restores the SDK C `wchar_t` typedef. Follow-up deno library clippy uses the upstream deny flags with `lsp-tracing` enabled.

Explicit missing `types` targets, root-package resolution in local mode, arbitrary CommonJS require conditions and version-qualified types conditions are outside this fix. The full cross-platform/symlink suite was not run.

Fixes #36988.

title: fix(ext/node): implement process.ref() and process.unref()
body:
Fixes #36993.

`process.ref()` and `process.unref()` are declared in the Node types (and shown on docs.deno.com) but were never implemented, so both were `undefined` at runtime.

This adds them to the `node:process` polyfill, matching Node's implementation: call the `Symbol.for("nodejs.ref")` / `Symbol.for("nodejs.unref")` method if present, otherwise fall back to the object's `ref()` / `unref()` method, and ignore anything else.

Also enables Node's `parallel/test-process-ref-unref.js` in the node_compat suite, which covers both the symbol protocol and the legacy `ref()`/`unref()` methods on timers.

I checked the new functions against the assertions from `test-process-ref-unref.js` under both Node and Deno, and ran `deno fmt` and the `prefer-primordials` lint config on the changed file. title: fix(cache): verify remote lock hashes after charset decode
body:
Fixes #37003

`deno cache` writes remote lockfile hashes from charset-decoded source text
(via `deno_graph`), but the HTTP cache verified the raw response bytes on a
later `--frozen` load. For a Latin-1 (or other non-UTF-8) `Content-Type`
charset the two hashes differ, so Deno rejects its own lockfile even though
the module is unchanged.

Add `Checksum::check_remote`, which applies the same charset decode that
`deno_graph` uses before hashing, and call it from the global HTTP cache and
file fetcher integrity paths.

### Validation

```
cargo test -p deno_cache_dir --lib cache::tests::remote_lock_checksum
# remote_lock_checksum_matches_decoded_latin1 ... ok
# remote_lock_checksum_utf8_unchanged ... ok

# Issue #37003 repro (Latin-1 remote + --frozen):
# stock deno 2.9.7: first cache exit 0, frozen exit 10 (Integrity check failed)
# this build:  first cache exit 0, frozen exit 0
```

Specs: `tests/specs/cache/latin1_lock_integrity` (iso-8859-1 fixture via the
test server `/encoding/` charset path).

I used AI tools to assist coding and testing. An AI coding agent (Grok Bot) on my account wrote this change and ran the tests above; I'm responsible for the PR.

title: fix(ext/node): keep onread user buffer backing store alive on detach
body:
Repro: register a socket read buffer with `net.connect({ onread: { buffer, callback } })`, then detach or transfer that buffer's ArrayBuffer (for example `buf.buffer.transfer()`). The next socket read lands in freed memory.
Cause: `UserBuffer` kept a raw `ptr`/`len` into the buffer but only retained the `Global<Uint8Array>`. Holding the view does not keep its backing store alive, so a detach frees it while `ptr`/`len` still point there, and `on_uv_alloc` (plus the TLS `useUserBuffer` path that copies decrypted plaintext in) then hands a dangling pointer to the read.
Fix: retain the `SharedRef<BackingStore>` in `UserBuffer` so the allocation outlives a detach or transfer, and skip resizable ArrayBuffers since they can shrink below `len`. This matches how deno_core's own `V8Slice` pins buffers.

Added a spec test under `tests/specs/node/net_onread_buffer_detach` that transfers the buffer right after connect and checks valid input is still delivered.

AI tooling was used to help prepare this change.

title: fix: strip leading UTF-8 BOM from .env and .npmrc files
body:
Fixes #36701

A `.env` or `.npmrc` file saved with a UTF-8 BOM (the default for PowerShell 5.1 `Set-Content -Encoding utf8` and several Windows editors) silently loses its first entry: the BOM becomes part of the first key, so `FOO=bar` is loaded as `"\u{feff}FOO"`.

This picks up #36702, which its author closed, and applies the review feedback from it. The BOM is stripped where *file content* enters the parsers, not in the shared dotenv parser. That keeps `node:util.parseEnv()`, a string API backed by the same parser, identical to Node, which keeps the BOM.

- `deno_dotenv::from_content_sanitized_iter_with_substitution`: covers `--env-file` (`cli/util/env.rs`) and the env embedded by `deno compile` (`cli/standalone/binary.rs`)
- `op_node_load_env_file`: `process.loadEnvFile()`
- `deno_npmrc::ini::parse_ini`: `.npmrc`

Each uses `strip_prefix('\u{feff}')`, so only one BOM, and only at the very start, is removed. A second BOM or one inside a value is kept as ordinary text.

Node itself keeps the BOM in `--env-file` and `process.loadEnvFile()` too (`Dotenv::ParsePath` doesn't strip it), so for those two this is a deliberate leniency, the same trade-off suggested in the #36702 review: be lenient with files, but stay byte-for-byte compatible for the `parseEnv()` string API.

AI disclosure: this change was written by an AI coding agent (Claude). The verification below comes from actually running the listed tests.

Tests:

- `libs/dotenv`: a leading BOM is stripped; a doubled BOM keeps one and a BOM inside a value is kept; `parse_env_content_hook` still keeps a leading BOM (Node parity for `parseEnv`). The first two fail on `main` with `left: [("\u{feff}FOO", "bar"), ("BAZ", "qux")]`.
- `libs/npmrc/ini.rs`: the same leading, doubled, and in-value cases at the `parse_ini` level.
- `tests/specs/run/env_file`: new `bom` case with a BOM'd copy of the existing `env` fixture.
- `tests/unit_node`: `process.loadEnvFile()` with a BOM'd file, and `util.parseEnv("\uFEFFFOO=bar")` keeps the BOM.

Ran locally on Linux x86_64 against a debug build: `cargo test -p deno_dotenv -p deno_npmrc`, `specs::run::env_file` (9/9), `unit_node::process_test`, `unit_node::util_test`, `tools/format.js --check`, `tools/lint.js --js`, and clippy on `deno_node`, `deno_dotenv` and `deno_npmrc`. The issue's repro was also checked by hand: with a BOM'd `.env`, `deno eval --env-file` and `process.loadEnvFile()` both see `FOO`, and a BOM'd `.npmrc` with a `registry=` line on its first line is now honored.

title: fix(npm): honor compatible automatic peer requirements
body:
## Problem

Automatic peer installation currently keeps only the first requirement for each package name. With two consumers requiring `peer@*` and `peer@1`, and registry versions 1.0.0 and 2.0.0, it can select 2.0.0 and report an avoidable mismatch. Renaming the consumers changes which requirement wins.

This standalone defect was found while investigating #36992. The minimal loopback-registry reproduction also fails with official Deno 2.9.7, for both static and dynamic imports. It does not establish the cause of the original static/dynamic discrepancy in that issue.

## Change

- Retain and deduplicate all required peer ranges before selecting an automatic fallback.
- Check candidates against each requirement directly, preserving union and prerelease semantics rather than constructing a synthetic intersection.
- Preserve linked-package precedence, dist-tags, the existing preference for `latest`, minimum dependency age, and trust-policy checks.
- Reconsider a fallback when newly reachable packages change its constraints, within the existing ten-round bound.
- Exclude abandoned fallback nodes from constraint collection and deduplication.

Explicit root and scoped dependency precedence is unchanged. Optional peers do not trigger automatic installation. For disjoint requirements with no common candidate, the existing first-requirement fallback and unmet-peer diagnostics remain. This is not a general SAT solver and does not rewrite snapshot provenance.

## Tests and local validation

The diff contains only the resolver change and eight repository regression tests: compatible ranges in both consumer orders and with dedup on/off; newly discovered constraints; stale constraints after fallback replacement; and version-selection coverage for intersections, tags/latest, linked packages, minimum dependency age, and trust policy.

Validated against base `a18ce33715e30cd2b0d99c7e322ef11a65490e4d`, using the pinned Rust 1.95.0:

- `cargo +1.95.0 test -p deno_npm --all-features --locked`: 256 passed.
- `cargo +1.95.0 test -p deno_npm --no-default-features --locked`: 256 passed.
- Scoped Clippy: `cargo +1.95.0 clippy -p deno_npm --all-targets --all-features --locked --no-deps -- -D warnings --deny clippy::unused_async --deny clippy::print_stderr --deny clippy::print_stdout --deny clippy::large_futures --deny clippy::allow_attributes_without_reason`: exit 0, with an unchanged Clippy configuration warning about unavailable `chrono::Utc::now`.
- `rustfmt +1.95.0 --check --config imports_granularity=item --config group_imports=StdExternalCrate libs/npm/resolution/common.rs libs/npm/resolution/graph.rs` and `git diff --check`: passed.
- A separate local finite-fixture harness passed 16 groups, including 48 compatible-range permutations, explicit/scoped versions, optional peers, incremental snapshots, replacement cascades, cycles, and bounded registry-cache queries. That harness and its logs are not part of this diff.
- The original minimal regression fails on the unpatched resolver.

## Draft / validation limits

A full patched Deno/V8 CLI build and runtime/spec integration suites have not been run. Full-workspace `./x lint` and full-repository `./x fmt` have not been run; the scoped checks above are not a full-repository pass. Clippy including dependencies is blocked by unchanged `libs/maybe_sync/lib.rs:87`, where `#[allow(clippy::len_without_is_empty)]` lacks a reason under the deny policy.

title: fix(ext/node): clear parent env in child_process sync APIs
body:

Root cause: the sync child_process path (spawnSync/execFileSync/execSync) calls the spawn op with `clearEnv: false` (ext/node/polyfills/internal/child_process.ts:2000), so the child inherits the full parent environment even when the caller passes an explicit `env` object. title: fix(ext/napi): check napi_create_typedarray length overflow
body:
napi_create_typedarray checks the view fits its ArrayBuffer with `length * soe + byte_offset > ab.byte_length()`, but the multiply and the add overflow usize for a large `length`, so the comparison wraps back under the bound (and panics under debug overflow checks) and the bogus length is handed to V8. This is the same overflow #36962 just fixed for napi_create_dataview, so I used the matching checked_mul/checked_add form here and added typedarray regression tests next to the dataview ones.

Reject self references with their source location and guidance to use a relative import. The check includes reachable internal modules and JavaScript type references; relative imports, sibling packages, and documentation examples remain valid.

title: fix(ext/web): abort still cancels a fetch body after the Response is collected
body:
Fixes #36982.

Aborting a fetch left `reader.read()` pending after the Response was garbage-collected. The body cancellation is registered through the internal abort-algorithm path, and that path did not keep the dependent signal reachable from its source. `addEventListener` already did. `[add]` now retains the dependent and does not ref the timer, so an internal cancellation does not pin the event loop.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p specs_tests --test specs -- fetch_abort_body_after_gc`
- `cargo test -p specs_tests --test specs -- abort_signal_any`

This pull request was written with assistance from Cursor.

title: fix(ext/node): finish empty TLS writes so HTTPS keep-alive continues
body:
Fixes #36965.

A one-byte ranged `fs.ReadStream` piped into an `https.Server` response is delivered, and the next request on that keep-alive connection is never answered. `node:http` with the same handler is fine, and so is a stream that ends on a later turn.

`res.end()` sends an empty chunk while the body write is still buffered. `TLSWrap::write_data` treats a zero-byte write as a no-op and returns without scheduling `oncomplete`, but it leaves `LastWriteWasAsync` set from the previous write. The JS side waits for a callback that never runs, so the response never emits `finish` and the socket stays assigned to the first response.

The zero-byte path now reports a synchronous completion. The new spec sends both requests on one TLS connection.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/specs/node/https_ranged_stream_keepalive` fails on Deno 2.9.7 (`file: HTTP/1.1 200 OK` then `timeout`)
- [ ] CI runs that spec against this branch

title: fix(bundle): show min-dep-age error instead of "Do not know how to load path"
body:
When `deno bundle` can't load an npm package because `--min-dep-age` excluded every matching version, it reported esbuild's "Do not know how to load path" (or panicked while resolving the package folder) instead of the existing min-dep-age message.

The bundler builds its graph with validation skipped, so that failure stays an error slot. `resolve_with_graph` treats the slot as missing and either looks up a package that was never snapshotted or hands esbuild an `npm:`/`jsr:` URL it can't load. This returns the graph's resolution error from the entrypoint, resolve and load paths, and appends the same `--min-dep-age=0` hint `exit_for_error` already uses.

Fixes #36899

Tested with `cargo test -p specs_tests --test specs -- bundle::min_dep_age`, covering an npm entrypoint and the same specifier imported from a local file. Also ran `./tools/format.js`, `./tools/lint.js --js` and clippy on the deno bin.

AI disclosure: I used an AI coding agent (Cursor) to help trace the bundle code path and write this change and test. I reviewed the diff and test results.

title: fix(run): kill unref'd children on watch restart
body:
Fixes #36970.

Unref'd child processes spawned by a `--watch` run should not survive when that run is replaced. Mark watcher-run process state so unref keeps its normal behavior outside watch mode, while children from a run are cleaned up when that run ends. Add an integration regression test covering both `Deno.Command().spawn().unref()` and `node:child_process` `spawn().unref()`.

Validation: `cargo test -p integration_tests --test integration -- run_watch_kills_unrefed_children_on_restart` passed locally (1 test).
