title: fix(completions): complete script paths for bare deno run in zsh
body:
The zsh completion script didn't account for the bare `deno [flags] <script>`
form, which runs the default `run` subcommand. The first positional only
offered subcommands, and the `case $line[1]` dispatch had no fallback, so
`deno -A ./<TAB>` and `deno ./<TAB>` produced nothing but a beep while
`deno run -A ./<TAB>` worked.

When the root command has a default subcommand, the first positional now
completes subcommands and files, any other leading word falls back to file
completion, and the default subcommand's visible flags are offered at the root.
Flag specs are rendered through one helper, so subcommand flags also get their
short forms.

Fixes #36959

title: fix(ext/http): keep request body readable alongside streamed response
body:
When a `Deno.serve` handler kept reading the request body in the background
while returning a streamed response over HTTP/1.1, the body read stopped at
whatever had arrived when the response was written and never resumed. The
response writer polls the shared socket for a client disconnect, and since
the socket keeps a single read waker, that poll replaced the parked body
reader's waker. Once the response finished, nothing woke the reader again.
#36629 only covered the case where the writer's poll actually read bytes.

The peer-close poll now leaves the socket alone while a body read is parked
on it (the reader observes EOF itself), and a body read dropped before
completing clears its waker so peer-close detection resumes.

Fixes #36966

title: fix(lint): preserve file permissions when using --fix
body:
# fix(cli): preserve file permissions when using deno lint --fix

Closes #36961 

Hey! This fixes the issue where running `deno lint --fix` wipes out file permissions (like resetting an executable `755` script to `644`).

While looking into this, I noticed the linter was using `atomic_write_file_with_retries` with a hardcoded `CACHE_PERM` (0o644) when applying fixes. Since atomic writes create a new temporary file and rename it over the original, the original inode and its permissions get completely replaced.

I swapped this out for a standard `std::fs::write`. This is what `deno fmt` already uses under the hood. `std::fs::write` opens the existing file with the `truncate` flag, which clears the contents but leaves the original inode and its permissions perfectly intact.

Verified manually locally with `stat` and the permissions are now correctly preserved!

- [x] Ensure `./x fmt` passes without changing files.
- [x] Ensure `./x lint` passes.
- [x] (Disclosing per the contributing guidelines: I used AI to help track down the atomic write behavior and draft the fix).

title: fix(runtime): release the file watch when a watcher is closed
body:
Fixes #36937

**AI disclosure:** this change, the test and this description were written with Claude Code (an AI assistant from Anthropic). A second AI agent reviewed the diff.

## The problem

`Deno.watchFs` and `node:fs.watch` keep a count of watchers per path in `WatcherInner::watched_paths`, and `op_fs_events_open` only calls `watcher.watch()` when that count is 0. The count was released in `Drop for FsEventsResource`, but `Resource::close` only cancelled the token. `op_fs_events_poll` holds an `Rc` to the resource while it waits, so a watcher closed during a poll isn't dropped until that poll returns.

So when a directory is deleted and recreated, and the old watcher is closed and a new one opened on the same path in the same tick, the new one sees a stale count, skips `watch()`, and is never registered on the new directory. On Linux the kernel drops the old inotify watch together with the deleted directory, so the new watcher gets no events. chokidar does exactly this, so Vite's dev server stops seeing changes in that directory.

## The change

- `watched` is now a `Mutex<Vec<..>>`, and a new `FsEventsResource::release_watches()` takes it and runs the existing decrement/unwatch loop. Taking the vec makes it safe to call more than once.
- `close()` calls it, and `Drop` still calls it too, so a resource that is never closed is handled as before.
- Removing the sender from the dispatch list stays in `Drop`, so how an in-flight poll ends is unchanged.
- The registration part of `op_fs_events_open` (everything after the permission checks) moved unchanged into `open_fs_events_resource`. The `op2` macro defines the underlying function inside a const fn, so a test can't call the op itself.

## Testing

New unit test `closing_a_resource_releases_its_watch_while_it_is_still_referenced`. It opens a watcher, holds the resource the way an in-flight poll does, closes it, and checks the count is released. It then reopens the same path, drops the old resource, and checks that the late drop doesn't release the new watch. It fails without the change (`left: Some(1), right: None`) and passes with it.

Run locally on macOS (arm64):

- `cargo test -p deno_runtime -p deno_v8 --lib`: 39 passed
- `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -p deno_runtime -p deno_v8 --lib --tests` with the repo's deny flags: clean

What I did not do:

- I did not run the JavaScript reproduction from the issue against a patched `deno` build on Linux. The bug only shows with inotify, and my machine is macOS, so the test checks the watch accounting that causes it.
- I did not run the existing `tests/unit/fs_events_test.ts` cases, which need a built `deno`. Relying on CI for those.

title: fix(ext/napi): check napi_create_dataview bounds for overflow
body:
`napi_create_dataview` checked `byte_length + byte_offset` against the buffer
size without guarding the addition. Addon-controlled values could overflow it:
debug builds panicked across the `extern "C"` boundary, and release builds
wrapped around, so the bounds check passed and V8 was handed an out-of-range
DataView. The sum is now computed with `checked_add`, and an overflow is
treated as out of range, throwing the same RangeError as any other bad offset.

Follow-up to #36942.

title: fix(compile): honor exclude-unused-npm for native addons
body:
Fixes #36931

Problem: `deno compile --bundle --minify --exclude-unused-npm` embeds every native-addon package from the managed npm snapshot, even when the entrypoint does not use it.

Root cause: `fill_bundle_native_addon_vfs` eagerly seeds every managed native-addon package without honoring `exclude_unused_npm`, so packages unreachable from the generated bundle are embedded.

Change: With `--exclude-unused-npm`, collect native-addon packages only from paths referenced by the generated bundle and their dependency closure. Preserve eager embedding when the flag is absent.

Validation: `./x fmt --check`, `./x lint`, and the `compile::bundle::exclude_unused_native_addon` and `compile::bundle::native_addon` specs passed. The baseline regression embeds 12.61 MB of node_modules and fails; the patched build embeds only the bundle and package metadata and passes. The native-addon spec also runs a referenced addon with and without the flag.

User-facing impact: Bundled executables using this flag no longer include unused managed native-addon packages.

Some coding work was AI-assisted; I reviewed the changes and verified the relevant tests.

body:
Fixes #35545.

When `deno run` executes a symlink to a file, the entrypoint URL currently keeps the symlink path. Relative imports then resolve beside the symlink instead of beside the target. Resolve file entrypoints through `canonicalize_path` when the real path differs.

Adds a Unix integration spec that runs a `.bin/cli` symlink with a sibling import and checks direct target execution as a control.

Validation: `./x lint`; `./x fmt`; `cargo test -p specs_tests --test specs -- run_bin_symlink -- --nocapture` (2 tests passed).

title: fix(runtime): interrupt spinning workers and add an awaitable Worker disposal barrier
body:
## Problem

`Worker.terminate()` only sets a flag and wakes the worker's event loop. A
worker that is spinning in JavaScript or WebAssembly never returns to that
loop, so it keeps running, and keeps writing to any `SharedArrayBuffer` it
shares, indefinitely. There is also no way to wait until a worker has actually
stopped executing, which an embedder needs before reusing memory the worker
could still write.

There is no existing issue for this. A minimal repro: start a worker that
increments a shared counter in a `while (true)` loop (or in a Wasm loop),
call `terminate()`, and observe that the counter keeps increasing.

## Changes

**Interrupting a worker**
- `terminate()` now also interrupts the worker's isolate (V8
  `TerminateExecution`), so spinning JS and Wasm stop.
- New `Worker[Symbol.asyncDispose]()`: requests termination and resolves only
  once the worker's JavaScript, and the native tasks in its runtime's blocking
  pool (nonblocking FFI calls, N-API async work, blocking reads), have stopped.
  While waiting it re-requests the stop every 10ms, because V8 can discard a
  termination (see below). Plain `terminate()` stays a single, non-blocking
  request.
- A host stop is recorded in a sticky isolate slot
  (`ExternalExecutionTermination`), so `node:vm` timeouts and other local
  cancellations cannot clear it.

**Keeping a stop from being lost or caught**
- V8 reports and clears any exception thrown by a promise hook that runs while
  C++ creates a promise (`NativeContext::RunPromiseHook`), termination
  included. Module evaluation checks the sticky slot afterwards and re-raises
  the stop.
- V8's `ThrowException` clears a pending termination, so an op that failed
  because its isolate was terminating turned the stop into a catchable error.
  The `#[op2]` error path (`throw_op_error`) and `throw_js_error_class` now
  leave a pending termination in place.
- Lazy and synthetic module loading, `require(esm)` (`mod_evaluate_sync`) and
  dynamic `import()` of lazily loaded modules propagate termination instead of
  panicking on `unwrap()`, reporting it as an ordinary JS error, or dropping it.

**Teardown with native code still running**
- A stopped worker is dropped as before, which releases its message port,
  locks, listeners and child workers promptly. Only FFI state that a running
  native call may still use (`UnsafeCallback` trampolines and libffi `Cif`s,
  and loaded libraries) is kept until the worker's blocking pool drains.
  Libraries are unloaded before callbacks are freed.
- Cross-thread callbacks are cancelled during shutdown, while the isolate is
  still alive. A callback invoked afterwards, including from a library's unload
  destructor, returns a zero value without entering V8.
- FFI callbacks no longer panic across the C boundary when they throw or are
  interrupted with an `isize`/`usize`/struct result, or when converting their
  return value fails. The libffi return slot is zeroed instead.
- N-API threadsafe-function queue slots are freed, and every blocked caller is
  woken, when shutdown discards queued calls. Previously a blocking call on a
  full queue could hang worker teardown.

## Tests

Each fix has a regression test that was committed failing before the fix.
Covered: core module-loading interruption cases, VM-timeout and host-stop
interaction, Worker disposal with spinning Wasm, a promise-hook-swallowed stop,
and native writes into shared memory. Also FFI callback lifetime during
disposal, prompt host-state release while a native call runs, library-unload
callbacks in both creation orders, wide and interrupted callback results, and
N-API full-queue disposal.

Local runs on macOS arm64: `deno_core` (494 passed), `deno_ops` (126), the
FFI and N-API integration suites, `unit::worker_test`, the Node `vm` unit
test, the worker startup spec, plus `./x fmt` and `./x lint`.

## Known limitations

- Plain `terminate()` sends one interrupt, so a stop that V8 discards in a
  promise hook can still leave a worker running. `Symbol.asyncDispose` is the
  reliable stop.
- Disposal does not cover descendant workers, detached OS threads or threads
  owned by native libraries, and it can wait indefinitely for a blocked native
  call. Every stopped worker's thread now stays alive until such calls return.
- Native code given a raw pointer into JS memory (N-API buffer info, FFI raw
  pointers) can still write after the isolate is dropped. This is unchanged
  from before.

## AI disclosure

This PR was written with AI assistance (Anthropic Claude via Claude Code, with
OpenAI Codex used as an independent reviewer). A human directed the work, and
every change was reviewed and tested as described above.

title: fix(lsp): alias node_modules files independent of the referrer
body:
Fixes #36664.

## Why

In a workspace member whose npm packages are installed in the root `node_modules`, `deno lsp` loads the same `.d.ts` under two names: `$node_modules/...` when the member imports a package directly, and `node_modules/...` when another package's types import it. TypeScript treats a file name as the module's identity, so classes with `private` or `#` fields from that package stop being assignable to themselves (TS2345/TS2322). `deno check` is unaffected.

The `$node_modules` alias came from `should_alias_node_modules_for_auto_import` in `cli/lsp/tsc.rs`. Since #34674 it asked whether the *referrer's* scope configures the file as a dependency. `pkg/main.ts` resolves to the `pkg` scope, which declares the package, so the file is aliased. `node_modules/b/index.d.ts` sits outside `pkg/`, falls back to the root scope, which declares nothing, so the same file is not aliased.

The fix keeps #34674's rule (only configured direct dependencies' entry and export files get the alias) but makes it a property of the file: a `node_modules` file is aliased when any scope configures it, whoever imports it.

## Scope

- `cli/lsp/resolver.rs`: new `LspResolver::is_configured_dep_resolution`, which checks every scope's configured dependency resolutions.
- `cli/lsp/tsc.rs`: `denormalize_with_auto_import_alias` uses it and loses its `scope` argument. `should_alias_node_modules_for_auto_import` is gone, and so is the now-unused `scope` argument of `insert_root_module_script_names`.
- Auto-import specifier naming in `cli/lsp/analysis.rs` still goes through `resource_url_to_configured_dep_key` with the real referrer and is unchanged.

## Verification

Built with `cargo build --bin deno` on macOS arm64.

- New test `lsp_node_modules_alias_independent_of_referrer` (workspace member, root `node_modules`, `b`'s types take `a`'s class with a private field) fails on main with `TS2345 ... '$node_modules/a/index").A' is not assignable to ... 'node_modules/a/index").A'. Types have separate declarations of a private property 'p'`, and passes with the fix.
- The issue's codemirror reproduction, driven through the issue's `lspprobe.mjs`: main reports 1 diagnostic (TS2345), the fix reports 0.
- `lsp_auto_import*` integration tests pass 9/9, including #34674's `lsp_auto_import_node_modules_alias_only_configured_deps`, so transitive packages are still not offered as auto-import sources. The `lsp::tsc` alias unit test passes.

title: fix(compile): skip non-script files during VFS CJS export analysis
body:
Closes #36746

### Overview

This PR fixes a critical regression introduced in Deno 2.9.0 where `deno compile` crashed with a `tokio-runtime-worker has overflowed its stack` fatal abort when compiling workspaces or modules with large `node_modules` trees containing non-script files (such as documentation `.mdx` files, licenses, and text files).

### Root Cause

In Deno 2.9.0, a loop over `vfs.iter_files()` was added in `cli/standalone/binary.rs` to precompute CommonJS export analysis for standalone binaries. The file matching logic included `MediaType::Unknown` under the assumption that it only applied to extensionless modules (like npm packages with `"main": "index"` without an extension). 

However:
1. `MediaType::from_specifier` also classifies **any unrecognized extension** (`.mdx`, `.txt`, `.yaml`, `.toml`, `.c`, `.h`, `.png`, etc.) as `MediaType::Unknown`.
2. In CommonJS packages (packages lacking `"type": "module"`), `cjs_tracker.is_maybe_cjs` returns `true` for all such files.
3. Every non-binary file with an unknown extension, plus declaration files (`.d.ts`) and extensionless non-code files (`LICENSE`, `README`), was consequently sent to SWC's ECMAScript parser for CJS analysis.
4. When SWC's recursive-descent parser parsed large Markdown or MDX files, markdown operators (such as lists `*`, `-`, and tables `|`) were interpreted as chained JavaScript expressions thousands of levels deep. This resulted in an immediate call stack overflow on the `tokio-runtime-worker` thread.
5. In `runtime/tokio_util.rs`, the Tokio runtime builder explicitly set a 2MB stack size, preventing the standard library from honoring the `RUST_MIN_STACK` environment variable when users attempted to increase stack depth.

### Changes

1. **`cli/standalone/binary.rs`**:
  - Differentiate unrecognized extensions from extensionless files: if `file_path.extension().is_some()` and `media_type == MediaType::Unknown`, skip it unconditionally.
  - Exclude declaration files (`MediaType::Dts`, `MediaType::Dmts`, `MediaType::Dcts`) since they contain no executable runtime code.
  - Filter known non-code extensionless files (case-insensitive check for `LICENSE`, `README`, `CHANGELOG`, `NOTICE`, `AUTHORS`, `Makefile`, dotfiles, etc.).
  - Check raw bytes for remaining extensionless files: skip files that do not contain `"exports"` or `"module"` and do not start with a shebang `#!`, as they cannot define CommonJS exports.
  - Cap serialized error strings in `CjsExportAnalysisEntry::Error` to 1,024 characters to prevent pathological error messages from inflating the VFS trailer.

2. **`libs/resolver/cjs/analyzer/mod.rs`**:
  - Update `should_skip_cjs_analysis` to check whether the specifier path has an extension, skipping unrecognized extensions and non-code extensionless text files.
  - Add the `should_skip_cjs_analysis` guard to `analyze_cjs_member_props`.

3. **`runtime/tokio_util.rs`**:
  - Update `create_basic_runtime` to inspect `DENO_TOKIO_THREAD_STACK_SIZE` and `RUST_MIN_STACK`, and increase the default release stack size from 2MB to 4MB.

4. **`libs/resolver/Cargo.toml`**:
  - Add the `"getrandom"` feature to `sys_traits` dev-dependencies so `cargo test -p deno_resolver` can be compiled and run in isolation.

5. **Tests**:
  - Added unit tests in `libs/resolver/cjs/analyzer/mod.rs` verifying that `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.yaml`, and `LICENSE` files are skipped, while legitimate extensionless CJS modules continue to be analyzed.
  - Added unit tests in `cli/standalone/binary.rs` for filename filtering and CJS keyword detection.
  - Added integration test `compile_skips_non_script_files_cjs_analysis` in `tests/integration/compile_tests.rs` embedding a 2,000-line `.mdx` file, `LICENSE`, `README.txt`, and `.d.ts` files, asserting successful compilation and standalone binary execution without stack overflows.

### Verification

- [x] `./x verify` passes without changing any files (formatting and linting clean).
- [x] `cargo test -p deno_resolver` passes (91 passed, 0 failed).
- [x] `cargo test -p deno --lib standalone::binary::tests` passes (4 passed, 0 failed).
- [x] `cargo test -p test_integration compile_skips_non_script` passes (1 passed, 0 failed).

title: fix(ext/napi): ignore the callback return value while an exception is pending
body:
Fixes #36941

Two places where Deno did not match Node when a Node-API call leaves an exception pending:

- `call_fn` rethrew the pending exception and then still set the callback's return value. Node ignores the return value in that case ([js_native_api_v8.cc](<url>), added in nodejs/node#39476), because addons can return an invalid `napi_value` after throwing. Deno dereferenced it and crashed.
- `napi_create_dataview` with `byte_offset + byte_length` past the end of the buffer threw the RangeError but returned `napi_ok`, leaving `*result` unset. It now returns `napi_pending_exception`, as Node does.

Both crash the Node-API conformance tests `js-native-api/test_function` and `js-native-api/test_dataview`.

Tests: `tests/napi` gets `test_throw_return_invalid` (throws, then returns `0xFFFFFFFFF`, the value Node's own `test_function.c` uses) and `test_dataview_out_of_range` (checks the status, that the exception is pending and that the result is unset).

Without the change in `ext/napi` and with the new tests, `exception_test.js` crashes on the new test (exit 139) and `dataview_test.js` fails with:

```
napi create_dataview out of range returns napi_pending_exception => ./dataview_test.js:17:6
error: AssertionError: Values are not equal.
  [
-  0,
+  10,
  true,
  false,
  ]
```

With it, `tests/napi` passes (`ok | 152 passed | 0 failed | 3 ignored`) and `cargo test -p integration_tests --test integration napi` passes all 6 tests, on Linux x86_64. The standalone addons from the issue now throw the same errors as Node instead of crashing.

This PR was written with help from Claude Opus 5.5. I reproduced both crashes with standalone addons on Linux and Windows, checked the behaviour against Node's source, and ran the napi tests with and without the change.

title: fix(lint): remove || from Deno.lint.BinaryExpression operator type
body:
Fixes #36934.

## Why

`Deno.lint.BinaryExpression["operator"]` listed `"||"`, but the lint AST never produces a `BinaryExpression` with that operator. `cli/tools/lint/ast_buffer/swc.rs` maps `BinaryOp::LogicalOr` to `LogicalExpression`, next to `&&` and `??`, and `LogicalExpression["operator"]` already declares `"||"`. A plugin that narrows on `node.operator === "||"` inside a `BinaryExpression` visitor type-checks but never matches.

The fix removes `"||"` from the `BinaryExpression` operator union. The other 21 operators match the `BinaryExpression` arms in `swc.rs` exactly.

## Scope

- `cli/tsc/dts/lib.deno.unstable.d.ts`: drop `"||"` from `BinaryExpression.operator`.
- `tests/unit/lint_plugin_test.ts`: new test `Plugin - BinaryExpression operator excludes ||`. It visits `a || b; a | b` and asserts the `BinaryExpression` visitor sees only `"|"`. It also assigns `"||"` to `Deno.lint.BinaryExpression["operator"]` under `@ts-expect-error`, so the type check fails if the union lists it again.

## Verification

- Before the fix, the new test fails type checking with `TS2578 Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive` at `tests/unit/lint_plugin_test.ts:715`. With `--no-check` its runtime half passes, which confirms the runtime already emits `LogicalExpression`.

title: fix(ext/node): keep embedded NUL in node:sqlite TEXT results
body:
Fixes #36923.

## Why

`node:sqlite` cut TEXT results off at the first NUL character. `StatementSync` read TEXT columns with `CStr::from_ptr`, which stops at the first zero byte, so `"a\0b"` came back as `"a"`. The stored bytes were correct (`hex(value)` returned `610062`). Node returns the whole string.

The fix reads the length from `sqlite3_column_bytes` and builds the string from that slice. The user-defined function argument path in `ext/node_sqlite/database.rs` already reads TEXT this way.

## Scope

- `tests/unit_node/sqlite_test.ts`: new test `[node/sqlite] StatementSync TEXT keeps embedded NUL`. It also covers an empty string, which takes the zero-length branch.

title: fix(ext/node): align X.509v1 certificate handling with OpenSSL
body:
`node:tls` accepts X.509v1 certificates under a caller-supplied `ca` for Node
parity, since webpki can't parse them. This validates those chains the way
OpenSSL's `X509_verify_cert` does with default flags (signatures, validity
window, `basicConstraints`, `keyUsage`, `extendedKeyUsage`), verifies

Rejections use Node's error codes.

title: fix(ext/web): mark special properties when inspecting buffers and DataView
body:
Node marks the `byteLength`, `byteOffset` and `buffer` entries of ArrayBuffers, SharedArrayBuffers and DataViews with brackets, since they are not own properties (nodejs/node#60131 and nodejs/node#60479). Deno still prints them like regular properties:

```js
import util from "node:util";

console.log(util.inspect(new DataView(new ArrayBuffer(4), 1, 2)));
```

Node:

```
DataView {
  [byteLength]: 2,
  [byteOffset]: 1,
  [buffer]: ArrayBuffer { [Uint8Contents]: <00 00 00 00>, [byteLength]: 4 }
}
```

Deno:

```
DataView {
  byteLength: 2,
  byteOffset: 1,
  buffer: ArrayBuffer { [Uint8Contents]: <00 00 00 00>, byteLength: 4 }
}
```

This ports that change to `ext/web/console/inspect.rs`. The keys are printed as extra entries after the formatter output instead of being added to the property list, and the typed array `showHidden` entries, which already had brackets, go through the same path now.

It also fixes inspecting a DataView whose buffer was detached. That currently prints `[Internal Formatting Error] TypeError: Cannot perform get DataView.prototype.byteLength on a detached or out-of-bounds ArrayBuffer` and a stack trace. Like Node, the key is now read from the buffer instead when the getter throws.

Since this is the shared formatter, `console.log` and `Deno.inspect` change too. I updated the three affected expectations in `tests/unit/console_test.ts` and added a test for DataViews, typed arrays with `showHidden` and the detached case.

One intentional difference: for a detached DataView, Node's `formatExtraProperties` raises `ctx.indentationLvl` before the getter throws and never lowers it, so that DataView and everything after it in the same `inspect` call ends up indented 4 spaces too far. Deno indents it normally. `test-util-inspect.js` asserts Node's output there (line 217), so if you would rather match it exactly, I can change that.

I compared Deno and Node 24.19 for 23 inputs (ArrayBuffers, SharedArrayBuffers, detached buffers, DataViews with and without own properties, typed arrays with `showHidden`, colors, `depth`, `maxArrayLength`, `breakLength` and `compact`). 21 differed before this change. Now only the detached DataView differs, as described above.

With this, #36927 and #36928 applied together, `test-util-format.js` passes (`cargo test --test node_compat -- test-util-format`), so it can go into `config.jsonc` once all three have landed. This PR and #36927 both change one line (the short `{ [byteLength]: n }` form); I will resolve that on whichever lands second.

title: fix(ext/node): respect Symbol.toPrimitive in util.format %s
body:
`util.format("%s", obj)` ignores a `Symbol.toPrimitive` method and inspects the object instead:

```js
import util from "node:util";

const obj = { [Symbol.toPrimitive]: () => "custom" };
console.log(util.format("%s", obj));
```

Node prints `custom`. Deno prints `{ Symbol(Symbol.toPrimitive): [Function: [Symbol.toPrimitive]] }`.

`hasBuiltInToString` in `ext/node/polyfills/internal/util/inspect.mjs` only looked for `toString`. This ports the current version from Node's `lib/internal/util/inspect.js`, which also checks `Symbol.toPrimitive` (nodejs/node#50992), both as an own property and along the prototype chain. It includes the follow-up fix (nodejs/node#57832), so objects whose `Symbol.toPrimitive` comes from a built-in such as `Date` are still inspected as before.

I compared `util.format("%s", x)` between Deno and Node 24.19 for 22 values: own, inherited and non-callable `Symbol.toPrimitive`, null-prototype objects, classes, `Date` and `Date` subclasses, plus plain objects, arrays, errors, boxed strings and maps as controls. 7 differed before this change and none differ now. Added a test to `tests/unit_node/util_test.ts`.

This is the second blocker in `test-util-format.js` after #36927. With both applied, the test gets past all the `Symbol.toPrimitive` cases and next fails at line 589, where a `SharedArrayBuffer` prints `byteLength` without brackets. That is a separate issue.

title: fix(ext/node): support numericSeparator in util.inspect and util.format
body:
Fixes #36926.

`numericSeparator` was dropped in three places:

- `ext/node/polyfills/internal/util/inspect.mjs`: `inspect()` only copies options that exist on `inspectDefaultOptions`, and `numericSeparator` was not one of them, so it went to `userOptions` and never reached the formatter. Node has `numericSeparator: false` in its defaults.
- `ext/web/console/inspect.rs`: numbers and bigints (plain, boxed and in typed arrays) were printed without looking at `ctx.numericSeparator`.
- `ext/web/01_console.js`: `formatNumber` and `formatBigInt`, which `util.format` uses for `%d`, `%i` and `%s`, ignored their third argument.

The separator logic is a port of `addNumericSeparator`, `addNumericSeparatorEnd` and `formatNumber` from Node's `lib/internal/util/inspect.js`, including its exceptions: exponent notation such as `1.5e-7` is left alone, and an ArrayBuffer's `byteLength` never gets separators.

I compared Deno's output with Node 24.19 for 37 cases (integers, fractions, negatives, `-0`, `NaN`, `Infinity`, `1e21`, bigints, boxed numbers, typed arrays, nested objects, `util.format`, `util.formatWithOptions` and `util.inspect.defaultOptions`). 23 of them differed before this change and none differ now. Added a case to `tests/unit_node/util_test.ts`. `test-util-format.js` still fails, but later, on a `%s` assertion about `Symbol.toPrimitive`, which is a separate issue.

title: fix(compile): check read permission for dynamically imported local files
body:
Compiled binaries didn't check read permission when `import()` or
`new Worker()` loaded a local file that isn't embedded in the binary. The
standalone module loader fell back to reading the file straight from disk,
so a binary compiled without `--allow-read` (or with it scoped to one
directory) could import any JSON file on disk and get its contents, or load
and run any `.ts`/`.js` file, while `deno run` rejects the same import with
"Requires read access". The fallback has been unchecked since #26494
(v2.0.3).

Non-embedded `file:` modules are now checked the same way `deno run` checks
them: `import()` subgraphs and worker main modules require read access,
while the embedded module graph is unaffected. The
`dynamic_import_typescript` test relied on the missing check, so it now
compiles with `--allow-read`.

title: fix(install): don't make transitive deps top-level when seeding from yarn.lock

title: fix(ext/web): use named groups for full-wildcard URLPattern components
body:
Fixes #28247

For context, I maintain [react-native-url-polyfill](<url>), a WHATWG URL implementation for React Native, and found this while comparing Deno's `URLPattern` with the spec and Node.js.

`URLPattern.prototype.exec()` has a fast path for components whose regular expression is exactly `^(.*)$`, and it always stored the match under the group name `"0"`. That is correct for an unnamed wildcard such as `*`, but not for a named group that spans the whole component:

```js
new URLPattern({ hostname: ":domain(.*)" }).exec({ hostname: "localhost" })
  .hostname.groups;
// before: { "0": "localhost" }
// after:  { domain: "localhost" }
```

The same happened for `protocol`, `username`, `search`, `hash`, and a `pathname` without a leading slash. The issue is labeled `upstream`, but the bug is in this fast path in `ext/web/01_urlpattern.js`; the parsed component already carries the right name in `groupNameList`.

This is the change @edgul [suggested in the issue](<url>), thanks! It uses `component.groupNameList[0]` in both places the fast path sets the group. Unnamed wildcards keep the `"0"` key because that is their group name.

Tests:

- Added unit tests for a named group spanning the whole hostname, including after a failed match (which reuses the result object), and for the reproduction from the issue. Both fail on Deno 2.9.7 and pass with this change (`cargo test -p unit_tests --test unit -- unit::urlpattern_test`).
- Removed `Pattern: [{"hostname":":domain(.*)"}]` from the four `urlpattern` WPT expectation blocks. It is the only WPT URLPattern case where a named group spans a whole component. With this change, `./tests/wpt/wpt.ts run -- urlpattern` passes; without the removal, the runner reports it under "expected failures that passed".
- dprint (same version and config as `./x fmt`) and `deno lint` with the repository rules, including the prefer-primordials plugin, pass on the changed files.

title: fix(ext/node_crypto): raw-private/raw-public KeyObject export format
body:
Fixes part of #35293 — support `raw-private` / `raw-public` asymmetric key formats.

This PR implements raw key import and export for EC, Ed25519, Ed448, X25519, and X448 keys, matching Node.js behavior.

### Changes

- Added `raw-private` and `raw-public` parsing and validation.
- Added native operations for importing and exporting raw asymmetric keys.
- Added compressed and uncompressed EC public-key support.
- Reused the existing OKP raw-key construction where possible.
- Aligned signature context and `ArrayBuffer` validation with Node.js.
- Enabled `test-crypto-sign-verify.js`.

### Notes

`test-crypto-key-objects.js` also covers raw key round trips, but remains ignored because an earlier RSA JWK modulus assertion depends on #36156, which is approved but not yet merged. Once #36156 lands, this test can be enabled to validate both changes together.

AI tools were used for code review, upstream behavior comparison, and debugging. The implementation and test results were manually reviewed and verified locally.

title: fix(core): keep inherited extension sources across chained snapshots
body:
Fixes #36910.

## Problem

Extension JavaScript is externalized when a snapshot is built: V8 stores the source strings by external-reference index and `JsRuntimeForSnapshot::snapshot()` writes their bytes into the sidecar. A runtime restored from that snapshot receives those strings (`snapshot_sources`) at the front of its external-reference table and registers no sources of its own, and the heap it inherited references them by index.

`snapshot()` only wrote the runtime's *own* sources (`original_sources`) into the new sidecar, so a second-generation snapshot had an empty source table while its heap still referenced every inherited string. Restoring it segfaults in V8's deserializer (`PostProcessExternalString`). Details and a standalone reproducer are in #36910.

## Commits

This PR has two commits.

1. **test(core)**: This commit adds the test `will_snapshot_chained_with_extension_sources`. The test does these steps:
  - Make a snapshot with an extension. The extension has one eager ES module and one lazy script.
  - Restore the snapshot into a `JsRuntimeForSnapshot`.
  - Make a second snapshot.
  - Make sure that the second sidecar starts with the strings of the first sidecar.
  - Restore the second snapshot.
  - Compile one function from each extension source for the first time.

  On `main`, the test fails at the sidecar check. The test binary does not crash.

2. **fix(core)**: This commit keeps the inherited strings in `IsolateAllocations`. `snapshot()` writes these strings first. Then it writes the sources of the runtime. `source_count` includes the two groups. The positions in the table do not change. Thus you can chain snapshots for any number of generations.

## Verification

- The test fails on the first commit and passes on the second.
- `./tools/format.js --check` passes; `cargo clippy -p deno_core` with the flags from `tools/lint.js` reports nothing.
- `cargo test -p deno_core --lib`: 479 passed, 1 failed (`tests::test_rebuild_async_stubs`, which fails identically on untouched `main` in this environment).

## Note on deno_core's own build

`create_snapshot`'s warm-up runtime is also a restored `JsRuntimeForSnapshot`, so with this change the warm snapshot's sidecar carries the inherited strings too (real bytes for consumed lazy sources, empty for the rest). That still loads, since the final consumer's own sources are appended after them, but it makes shipped snapshots larger by the consumed extension sources. If that is unwanted, the carry-over could be gated by a `RuntimeOptions` flag; happy to adjust.

## AI usage disclosure

This PR was written with the help of an AI assistant (Claude, via Claude Code): it helped with the root-cause analysis, the test, and the patch. I reviewed the changes, ran the reproducer, and ran the checks above myself.

title: perf(install): keep a copy of the lockfile in node_modules to avoid re-resolving
body:
Stacked on #36907 (the base branch is on my fork, so this is opened against `main` and includes that PR's commits until it merges).

## Summary

In the "node_modules" variation of the [vlt benchmarks](<url>) (node_modules kept, lockfile and caches deleted between runs) deno is at ~9 ms per package while pnpm is at 0.1 ms. pnpm keeps a copy of its lockfile at `node_modules/.pnpm/lock.yaml` and uses it when `pnpm-lock.yaml` is missing, so it never contacts the registry. Deno only kept the linking state in `node_modules/.deno/.setup-cache.bin`, so with the lockfile gone it re-resolved every package from the registry, which is the same cost as a clean install minus the tarballs.

This does the same thing as pnpm:

- After node_modules is set up, the workspace configuration and npm packages of the lockfile are written to `node_modules/.deno/deno.lock`.
- When the workspace has no lockfile but that copy exists, the lockfile is seeded from it. The seeded lockfile isn't marked as changed, so when the dependencies in the config files still match, the existing "everything is already resolvable" fast path applies and nothing is fetched. The workspace section of the copy lets the usual pruning handle dependencies that were removed from `package.json`/`deno.json`, and dependencies that were added are resolved like with any lockfile. `deno.lock` is then written back out, and `--frozen` still fails like it does for a missing lockfile.

Only the npm packages are kept in the copy, so deleting `deno.lock` still re-resolves jsr and remote dependencies.

## Benchmarks

Install with node_modules kept but the lockfile and caches deleted (the "node_modules" variation), vlt benchmark fixtures, all binaries built locally with the release profile on the same machine, best of 3 runs:

| fixture | packages | main | #36907 | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| svelte | 59 | 1.86 s | 0.84 s | 0.00 s |
| astro | 281 | 2.27 s | 1.18 s | 0.12 s |
| vue | 423 | 2.94 s | 2.61 s | 0.14 s |
| next | 331 | 2.19 s | 2.38 s | 1.09 s |
| large | 1278 | 1.87 s | 2.00 s | 0.15 s |

The remaining time for next is spent fetching the packuments of `next`, `eslint` and `rimraf`, which have `bin` entries or scripts and whose extra info is fetched from the registry when the cache is cold. That also happens with the lockfile present, so it's a separate follow-up.

title: fix: bump rand 0.9.x to patched version
body:
* `rand` 0.9.2 -> 0.9.3, fixes unsoundness where `ThreadRng` could
  hand out aliased mutable references when a custom logger accessing
  `rand::rng()` triggers a reseed during trace/warn-level logging
  (GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc, low). Reached through hickory-resolver and
  opentelemetry_sdk, both linked into the runtime binary.

Two other open advisories are not fixed here because the minimal,
lockfile-only update they need is blocked by version requirements in
Cargo.toml, and this change intentionally sticks to Cargo.lock:

* `rand` 0.8.5 is pinned exactly (`rand = "=0.8.5"`) in the
  workspace Cargo.toml and used directly by the `cli` crate, so
  `cargo update --precise 0.8.6` is rejected outright
  (GHSA-cq8v-f236-94qc, low).
* `hickory-proto`/`hickory-resolver` are pinned to `0.25.2`; the fix
  is `0.26.1`, which Cargo treats as a breaking bump for a 0.x crate
  and refuses under the current requirement
  (GHSA-q2qq-hmj6-3wpp, medium).

Both would require relaxing the version requirement in Cargo.toml,
which is out of scope here.

Given the size of this repo, this was validated with
`cargo metadata --locked` (succeeds) and `cargo fmt -- --check`
(clean) rather than a full build/clippy/test run; CI is relied on
for the rest.

title: perf(install): fetch abbreviated packuments under minimumDependencyAge when possible
body:
## Summary

Since #35458 `minimumDependencyAge` defaults to one day. Enforcing it needs each version's publish date (the `time` map), which only the full npm packument has, so `deno install` has been downloading the full packument for every package. Those are 2-10x larger than the abbreviated install manifest (vite: 4.6 MB vs 0.4 MB gzipped, 39 MB uncompressed) and they dominate cold-cache installs. This is why deno looks slow in the "clean" variation of the [vlt benchmarks](<url>).

This PR does what pnpm does for its `minimumReleaseAge`: request the abbreviated manifest first and only fetch the full packument for packages whose top-level `modified` date is at or after the newest allowed dependency date (or unknown). Publishing a version always bumps `modified`, so a package last modified before the cutoff can't have a version that's too new, and the resolver already treats a missing publish date as acceptable.

## Changes

- `NpmPackumentFormat` gains `AbbreviatedUnlessModifiedSince(date)`, a `new(npmrc, newest_dependency_date)` constructor shared by the call sites, and helpers for the request format and the full-packument decision.
- `RegistryInfoProvider` requests the abbreviated manifest, then refetches the full packument when required. Cached entries record `modified` so cache hits make the same decision. A cached full packument is refreshed as full so its etag still matches. If the full refetch 404s (registries that only serve metadata to requests with the npm `Accept` header), the abbreviated data is kept, like with `--cached-only`.
- The fast JSON indexer plucks the top-level `modified`, and the slimmed cache file keeps it. A response is recognized as a full packument when it has publish dates for versions, which covers registries that ignore the `Accept` header.
- `NpmCacheHttpClient::download_with_retries_on_any_tokio_runtime` takes the request format per call instead of the client holding a fixed one. Full packument downloads are marked in the progress output:
  ```
  Download <url> (full packument)
  ```
- The test registry now emits `modified` in abbreviated responses like the real registry.

## Benchmarks

Clean install (no cache, no lockfile, no node_modules) of the vlt benchmark fixtures. Both binaries built locally with the release profile on the same machine, best of 3 runs, home connection:

| fixture | packages | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| svelte | 59 | 1.96 s | 0.83 s |
| astro | 281 | 2.97 s | 2.01 s |
| vue | 423 | 3.70 s | 3.17 s |
| next | 331 | 4.15 s | 4.22 s |
| large | 1278 | 3.57 s | 3.54 s |

Packument traffic for the svelte fixture went from 122 full packuments (17.1 MB gzipped) to 109 abbreviated + 3 full (9.4 MB), and for the large fixture from 1154 full (39.9 MB) to 1154 abbreviated + 12 full (33.9 MB). The next fixture doesn't improve: `next` and the `@typescript-eslint/*` packages publish canaries daily so their full packuments are still needed, and the abbreviated manifests of packages with thousands of versions are large too. Over the last 90 days vite was modified within the previous 24 hours on 27% of days, rollup 20%, typescript 90%, next 96%.

## Notes

- Registries that support the abbreviated format but omit `modified` cost two requests per package when the age check is on.
- `deno_npm` and `deno_npm_cache` have breaking changes (new pub field on `NpmPackageInfoCacheMetadata` and `SerializedCachedPackageInfo`, new enum variant, trait signature).

title: feat(crypto): add opt-in FIPS 140 mode via aws-lc-rs
body:
## Description

Closes #36812.

Adds an opt-in `fips` Cargo feature. When built with `--features fips`,
`rustls/fips` swaps `aws-lc-sys` for `aws-lc-fips-sys` (NIST-validated)
across every TLS call site in the binary, with no per-site changes. Also
adds a fail-closed `DENO_REQUIRE_FIPS=1` startup check that refuses to start
on a binary not built with `--features fips`.

`ext/crypto/mldsa.rs`: AWS-LC-FIPS 3.x doesn't yet expose
`aws_lc_rs::unstable::signature`, which ML-DSA (WebCrypto PQC signatures)
depends on. Split into `mod real` (unchanged) and `mod fips_stub`
(`cfg(feature = "fips")`, same signatures, returns `NotSupportedInFipsBuild`).
No other call site changes. Everything else the issue asks for (TLS,
hashing, HMAC, ECDSA, RSA) works under FIPS; only this newer PQC algorithm is
unavailable until upstream exposes it.

`ext/node_crypto` (`node:crypto`) already depends on the workspace
`aws-lc-rs` directly (not `ring`), so it inherits the FIPS module for free --
no changes needed there.

## Testing

- `./x test-unit webcrypto` (full JS test harness, not just Rust unit
  tests) -- 129/129 pass non-FIPS, 129/129 pass FIPS (two previously-ML-DSA-
  unconditional tests plus the dedicated `webcrypto_mldsa_test.ts` suite now
  skip under FIPS via a `supports()` capability probe instead of failing).
- This run caught a real bug the narrow unit tests missed: `supports()`
  (`SubtleCrypto.supports()`) was reporting ML-DSA as available under FIPS
  from static-table membership alone, while `generateKey` actually threw.
  Fixed at the single chokepoint (`check_support_for_algorithm`) so the
  capability check is honest, then used that same fixed probe to gate the
  three affected test files.
- `cargo test -p deno_crypto --features deno_core/v8[,fips] --lib mldsa` --
  4/4 pass across both build modes (Rust-level stub/real behavior).
- `cargo clippy -p deno --no-deps` (with and without `--features fips`) --
  clean. `rustfmt --check` / `./x fmt` -- clean. `./x lint-js` -- no new
  violations on touched files.
- Manual smoke test on real built binaries: normal run, `fetch()` over TLS,
  and `DENO_REQUIRE_FIPS=1` all behave correctly on both non-FIPS and FIPS
  builds; ML-DSA works on non-FIPS and fails closed on FIPS.
- Full `cargo test`/spec/node-compat suite not run (needs the packaged V8
  snapshot, 1h+); the targeted `./x test-unit` run above exercises the
  actual code path this PR changes.

## Notes for reviewers

Requires `cmake`, Go, and Perl to build (`aws-lc-fips-sys` compiles the
validated module from C). On macOS the FIPS build produces a shared
`libcrypto.dylib` that needs `DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH`/rpath to be found by
build-script subprocesses at build time -- not fixed by this PR, flagging as
a possible follow-up for CI docs.

## AI disclosure

Drafted with AI assistance (Kiro). Reviewed by a human before submission.

title: fix(ext/node): add permission checks for op_inspector_port and op_inspector_enabled
body:
Add missing `--allow-sys=inspector` permission checks to both `op_inspector_port` (which backs Node.js' `process.debugPort`) and `op_inspector_enabled` to be consistent with `op_inspector_url`, `op_inspector_open`, and `op_inspector_connect`, all of which already require inspector sys permission.

title: fix(compile): honor `no-legacy-abort` unstable feature in standalone binaries
body:
Follow-up to #36307 / #36312, which made `"unstable": ["no-legacy-abort"]` in `deno.json` work for `deno run`. Binaries built with `deno compile` still ignore it.

`deno compile` already records the feature in the binary's `metadata.unstable_config.features`, and it gets enabled on the standalone `FeatureChecker`. But the standalone runtime hardcodes the worker option at <url>

```rust
no_legacy_abort: false,
```

As a result, in a compiled binary every `Deno.serve` `request.signal` aborts after a successful response, and the one-time "request.signal aborts on successful responses (legacy behavior)" warning is printed, even though the project opted out. This happens whether the feature comes from `deno.json` or from `--unstable-no-legacy-abort` at compile time.

Repro with Deno 2.9.7, using the `deno.json` and `main.ts` from the new spec test:

```console
$ deno run --allow-net main.ts
ok
aborted: false
$ deno compile --allow-net --output out main.ts && ./out
Deno.serve: request.signal aborts on successful responses (legacy behavior). [...]
ok
aborted: true
```

## Fix

Derive `no_legacy_abort` from the standalone `FeatureChecker`, which is populated from `metadata.unstable_config.features`:

```rust
no_legacy_abort: feature_checker.check("no-legacy-abort"),
```

#35733 would flip the default to `true`. Until that lands, this makes the opt-in work for compiled binaries.

## Test

`tests/specs/compile/no_legacy_abort` compiles a `Deno.serve` program with `"unstable": ["no-legacy-abort"]` in `deno.json`, runs the binary, and asserts that `request.signal` is not aborted once `info.completed` resolves after a successful response. The expected output is exact, so the legacy warning would also fail the test.

`./tools/format.js` leaves the tree unchanged. I have not yet run the spec test or `./tools/lint.js` against a local debug build.

title: fix(coverage): skip the V8 code cache while collecting coverage
body:
Fixes <url>

This commit message, and the change it describes, were written by an AI model (Claude Opus 5.5).

PROBLEM

Deno saves the bytecode V8 compiles for each module (the "code cache", stored in DENO_DIR) and reuses it on later runs. V8 compiles a module loaded from that cache without block coverage counters. Its coverage profile then reports the module's top-level function as one range with `isBlockCoverage: false`, so every top-level line reads as covered, even a branch that never ran. `deno run` used the code cache even when collecting coverage. For example, with this `main.ts`:

  if (Deno.args.length > 0) {
  console.log("has args");
  }
  console.log("done");

running `DENO_COVERAGE_DIR=cov deno run main.ts` with a fresh DENO_DIR reports lines 2 and 3 as uncovered (50%), but the same command run a second time reports 100%. `deno run --coverage=cov` behaves the same. Processes that `deno test --coverage` starts inherit DENO_COVERAGE_DIR, so they are affected too. `deno test` itself never uses the code cache.

SOLUTION

`CliOptions::code_cache_enabled()` now returns false whenever a coverage directory is in effect, from either the `--coverage` flag or the DENO_COVERAGE_DIR environment variable. Every consumer of the code cache (the module loader, the worker factory, the cache warm-up, and the compile path) goes through that method, so a coverage run neither reads nor writes the code cache.

The new spec test `coverage/code_cache` runs a script twice without coverage and checks that the second run hits the code cache. It then collects coverage of the script with DENO_COVERAGE_DIR, with `deno run --coverage`, and with `deno test --coverage`, and checks that all three reports show the untaken branch as uncovered. Before this change the test failed because the report for the DENO_COVERAGE_DIR run read 100% (4/4) instead of 50% (2/4); after it, the test passes, as do the other coverage spec tests and the code cache integration tests.

title: perf(ext/napi): track and deregister finalizers with BTreeMap instead of Vec
body:
`RefTracker::remove` locates entries with `rposition`, then calls `Vec::remove`, once per collected object via the GC callback (`Reference::reset` → `Env::remove_ref_finalizer`), so finalizing large numbers of objects can be extremely slow. 

Both `napi_wrap` and `napi_create_external` are affected, since they share
`add_ref_finalizer`.

This changes RefTracker::pending from Vec to BTreeMap. The IDs are monotonic, so the BTreeMap preserves insertion order and teardown order in `take_pending`. 

Minimum reproduction here: 
<url>

Results vs Node and after the change:

```sh
# node v24.21.0
node --expose-gc minimal.ts;
Average over 10 runs
n=10000 3.2 ms
n=20000 3.6 ms
n=40000 5.8 ms
n=80000 12.2 ms
Total time 247.2 ms

# deno 2.9.7 (stable, release, aarch64-apple-darwin)
deno run --allow-ffi --allow-read --v8-flags=--expose-gc minimal.ts;
Average over 10 runs
n=10000 60.8 ms
n=20000 239.9 ms
n=40000 923.1 ms
n=80000 3870.0 ms
Total time 50937.2 ms

# After change to BTreeMap
../deno/target/release/deno run --allow-ffi --allow-read --v8-flags=--expose-gc minimal.ts;
Average over 10 runs
n=10000 4.3 ms
n=20000 5.2 ms
n=40000 8.0 ms
n=80000 13.2 ms
Total time 307.8 ms
```

AI Disclosure:
While refactoring from Node to Deno I used claude to identify which function calls in a production system using @duckdb/node-api were taking the most time, which lead me to the napi_create_external() calls, which lead to this finalizer tracking and deregistering pattern.

Fixes #36894

title: fix(ext/node): honor ipv6Only when binding TCP servers to ::
body:
Fixes #36168

`uv_tcp_bind` in the libuv compat layer received the `UV_TCP_IPV6ONLY` flag but never applied it, so IPv6 sockets kept the operating system default for `IPV6_V6ONLY`. That default is 1 on Windows and 0 on Linux. As a result, a `node:net` server listening on `::` with `ipv6Only: false` (the default) refused IPv4 connections on Windows, and `ipv6Only: true` had no effect on Linux.

This change does what libuv does in `uv__tcp_bind` and `uv__tcp_try_bind`: for IPv6 addresses it always sets `IPV6_V6ONLY` from the flag before binding. As in libuv, a failure is returned on Unix and ignored on Windows. The JS constant `UV_TCP_IPV6ONLY` was 2 because of enum auto numbering. It is now 1, which matches libuv, Node and the Rust side. Only `node:net` TCP handles go through this code, so `Deno.listen` and UDP are unchanged.

Two tests are added to `tests/unit_node/net_test.ts`. The first listens on `::` with `ipv6Only: false` and connects over both `127.0.0.1` and `::1`. On Windows it fails before this change with `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1`. The second listens on `::` with `ipv6Only: true` and then listens on `0.0.0.0` with the same port, which only works when `IPV6_V6ONLY` is set. It targets Linux, where the dual stack socket used to hold the IPv4 port. The Unix code passes cargo check and clippy for Linux and macOS targets, but its runtime behavior on those platforms will first be exercised by CI.

Not changed here: on Windows, `listen()` without a host still binds `0.0.0.0`, because a comment in `_createServerHandle` says dual stack did not work there. That was most likely this bug, and switching it to `::` like Node could be a follow up. The round robin cluster ipv6Only test in `tests/node_compat/config.jsonc` is disabled on Linux and macOS with the `EADDRINUSE` error this fixes, so it may pass now. Open PR #35182 moves these constants to Rust with `UV_TCP_IPV6ONLY` set to 2, so it would need to use 1 after this lands.

AI disclosure: written with the help of Claude Code.

title: fix(ext/web): remove event handler listener when set to null
body:
Setting an event handler attribute such as `signal.onabort` to null did not remove its listener from the target. The handler stopped running, but the listener stayed registered. So a cleared `AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` still kept the process alive until the timer fired. The same applied to other targets that use `defineEventHandler`. For example, `port.onmessage = null` left a `MessagePort` refed.

The cause is in `defineEventHandler` in `ext/web/02_event.js`. On null it only cleared the wrapped handler and kept the wrapper as a listener.

This change follows the HTML spec for event handler attributes. Setting the attribute to null (or to any non-object) now removes the listener. Setting it again adds a new listener at the end of the list. Replacing one handler with another still keeps its original position.

Tests: `event_target_test.ts` checks listener order after null and re-set, ported from the WPT test `html/webappapis/scripting/events/event-handler-removal.window.js`. `timers_test.ts` checks that `AbortSignal.timeout()` with `onabort` set to null no longer keeps the process alive. Both fail without the fix and pass with it.

`FileReader` has its own handler setter with the same problem. I can send a separate fix for it.

fix(tests): make node_test_mock_timers Date assertion timezone-independent
body:
`Date is mocked and tracks tick` mocks the clock at 5000 ms past the epoch and asserted that `Date()` matches `/1970/`. `Date()` formats in local time, so west of UTC that instant is 31 December 1969:

```
AssertionError: The input did not match the regular expression /1970/. Input:
'Wed Dec 31 1969 16:00:05 GMT-0800 (Pacific Standard Time)'
```

That's what failed on a windows-aarch64 runner in Pacific time. The assertion threw before `mock.timers.reset()`, so the mock stayed enabled and the next seven tests failed with "MockTimers is already enabled".

This compares against `new Date(5000).toString()` instead, which is exact and holds in any timezone.

Reproduced with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles` (passes under `UTC`); with the change the file passes under `UTC`, `America/Los_Angeles`, `Etc/GMT+12` and `Pacific/Kiritimati`.

title: fix(check): pin @types/node and resolve it through the configured registry
body:
`deno check` installs `@types/node` for projects that don't bring their own (`ensure_types_node`). That download had two problems:

- it fetched the packument from a hardcoded `<url> ignoring the registry the project configured (`.npmrc`, `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`);
- with no version requirement it took whatever `dist-tags.latest` pointed at.

So type checking wasn't reproducible: the same code on the same commit can produce different diagnostics depending on when you run it, a private-registry or offline setup isn't honored, and our own spec tests reach live npm despite the test harness pointing them at the local registry. A DefinitelyTyped release then changes diagnostics for everyone — it has repeatedly broken `check_node_builtin_modules` (#36711, #36848, and again now, which blocks CI on every PR).

This resolves the package through the configured registry and pins the version to the one `cli/tsc/dts/node` is generated from, so the downloaded typings match the built-in ones. `tools/update_types_node.ts` reads the pin from the Rust constant, so bumping is one edit plus a regen.

One subtlety: a materialized copy was reused whenever it was complete, so a tree left by an older Deno (installed back when this followed `latest`) would be type-checked against forever. Reuse now requires the pinned version, and the extractor's "another process published this first" race check compares versions too, so a wrong-version tree is replaced rather than kept.

A project that wants different Node typings still wins by installing its own `@types/node` under `node_modules`; that branch is unchanged.

Verified locally: `check_node_builtin_modules` passes against the **unchanged** expectation files, resolving 24.2.0 from the vendored test registry rather than live npm. All 270 `check` specs, the `sync_types` spec and the `npm_compat` unit tests pass. Two new unit tests cover replacing a wrong-version tree and keeping a matching one.

Supersedes #36882, which just updated the expectation to today's `@types/node` output — a fix that would drift again on the next release.

### Also: timezone-dependent `node_test_mock_timers` (second commit)

Folded in from #36884 because the two unblock CI together: each needs the other for a reliably green run.

`Date is mocked and tracks tick` mocks the clock at 5000 ms past the epoch and asserted that `Date()` matches `/1970/`. `Date()` formats in local time, so west of UTC that instant is 31 December 1969. It failed on a windows-aarch64 runner in Pacific time, and because it threw before `mock.timers.reset()` the next seven tests failed too. It now compares against `new Date(5000).toString()`, which is exact in any timezone. Reproduced with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`; the fixed file passes under `UTC`, `America/Los_Angeles`, `Etc/GMT+12` and `Pacific/Kiritimati`.

title: fix(ext/node): support async describe body in node:test
body:
Closes #36876

### Cause
In standard runner mode (`ext/node/polyfills/testing.ts`), `wrapSuiteFn` ran the suite function synchronously. When `describe()` was passed an async callback, the function yielded on the first `await`, causing `currentSuite` to be restored to its previous value and `suite.execute()` to run prematurely before child tests or suites were registered. When the async callback resumed and called `it()`, the parent test step had already completed, throwing:
`error: Didn't complete before parent. Await step with await t.step(...).`

### Solution
- Track the active `TestSuite` on `NodeTestContext` using a private symbol (`kSuite`) so it remains accessible across `await` boundaries through `AsyncLocalStorage`.
- Await thenable return values in `wrapSuiteFn` before running hooks and executing the suite.
- Route suite-level registration (`test`, `suite`, `before`, `after`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`) through `getCurrentSuite()`.
- Add regression spec test under `tests/specs/node/node_test_async_describe/`.

title: fix(ext/http): apply backpressure while an HTTP/1.1 response is pending
body:
While a response is pending, the HTTP/1.1 serve path polls the socket to detect a client disconnect. Any bytes it reads are stashed in the connection buffer, where the body reader or the next request parse picks them up later. It kept reading for as long as data was available, so TCP flow control never applied during that window.

This limits that read-ahead to 64 KiB. Once the buffer is full, it stops reading until the buffer drains. Buffered bytes are consumed exactly as before.

One behavior change: if a client has 64 KiB of unconsumed data buffered and then disconnects, the server now notices only once that data has been consumed, not right away.

Tests:
- `deno_http_h1`: the read-ahead stops at the limit, the poll doesn't re-wake itself once the buffer is full, and a delayed body read still receives the whole body.
- `serve_test.ts`: client writes stall while a response is pending, for both a delayed handler and a streaming response.

title: fix(ext/node): don't lose http2 client 'end' on empty-body HEADERS
body:
<!--
IMPORTANT: If you used AI tools (e.g. Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, etc.)
to help write this PR, you MUST disclose it in the PR description. PRs will be
rejected if there is suspicion of undisclosed AI usage.

Before submitting a PR, please read <url>
-->

Fixes #36850

## Summary

A `node:http2` client stream that receives an empty-body response (204 / HEAD /
304 / 200 with no body) emits `'response'`, but `'end'` is lost if `data`/`end`
listeners attach *after* awaiting `'response'`. Node emits `'end'` in this
situation.

Cause: `on_frame_recv_callback` treated `END_STREAM` on HEADERS/PUSH_PROMISE as
a native read EOF and called `handle_data_end_stream()` after
`handle_headers_frame()`. That fires `onread(undefined, UV_EOF)` →
`stream.read(0)`, which emits `'end'` before the `await response` continuation
can attach listeners.

Fix: HEADERS / PUSH_PROMISE only call `handle_headers_frame`, matching Node's
`OnFrameReceive`. JS `onSessionHeaders` already `push(null)` when `END_STREAM`
is set. DATA-frame `END_STREAM` is unchanged.

This is distinct from #35947 / #35959 (`'data'` before `'response'` when there
*is* a body). That path is not modified.

## Test

Adds a regression in `tests/unit_node/http2_test.ts`: h2c upstream replies 204
(`END_STREAM` on HEADERS). The client awaits `'response'`, then attaches
`on('data')` / `on('end')`, and must receive `'end'` within 3s.

## AI Disclosure

This PR was drafted and filed by an AI assistant (Grok). I reviewed and edited
it myself.

title: fix(ext/websocket): flush the transport after writing a frame
body:
*Written by AI (Claude Fable 5.1); reviewed by Gideon Wald before submission.*

Fixes #36862.

`ServerWebSocket::write_frame` awaited `fastwebsockets`' `write_frame` and returned. That
function ends with `write_all` on the underlying stream and never flushes. For a `wss:` client
the stream is `tokio_rustls::client::TlsStream`, whose `poll_write` returns `Ready(Ok(n))` with
ciphertext still in rustls' buffer when the socket would block, and whose `poll_read` does not
drain pending writes. After the send task resolved nothing polled the write half again, so up to
64 KiB of a message could sit in user space until the next `send()`, while `bufferedAmount` had
already been decremented. The issue has a 25-line reproduction.

This PR awaits `flush()` in `ServerWebSocket::write_frame`, and makes the automatic Pong/Close
reply callback in `op_ws_next_event` go through that same helper instead of writing to the
write half directly. Every frame `ext/websocket` writes (the send ops, `close()`, server
shutdown, and now the automatic replies) goes through that one function, and a send completes
only once the transport has taken all of its bytes, or errors. On a plain TCP stream the flush
is a no-op.

fastwebsockets is bumped from 0.8.1 to 0.10.0 for the public `flush()` on `WebSocketWrite`;
0.10.0 was already in the lockfile for `dcore`, so this removes the duplicate. Besides
`flush()`, the only behavioural change between the two versions is in `write_frame`: a `Close`
written after a `Close` has already been sent is now written instead of silently dropped.
`ServerWebSocket::write_frame` skips the write when the write half is closed, which is what
fastwebsockets' own doc comment on obligated sends asks for, so routing the auto-replies through
it keeps the old behaviour: a peer acknowledging our `Close` does not get a second `Close`. One
small change follows from the same skip: a Ping arriving after we have sent our `Close` no longer
fails the connection with `ConnectionClosed`; its Pong is dropped and reading continues until the
peer's `Close`.

## Tests

- `websocket_write_flushes_buffered_transport`: a real HTTP upgrade over an in-memory buffered
  transport; after `write_frame` resolves, the peer must be able to read the whole frame with
  `now_or_never()`. Fails on `main`, passes with this change.
- `websocket_pong_flushes_buffered_transport`: the same for the automatic Pong that
  `op_ws_next_event` writes. Fails on `main`, passes with this change.

No timers, sockets, or sleeps.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p deno_websocket --features deno_core/v8` on `main` (685eb3b) with this change:
  all pass. With the `flush()` removed and the reply callback writing to the write half directly
  as before, but the version bump and tests kept: both new tests fail.
- A separate set of tests over a real tokio-rustls connection with controlled write readiness
  (Binary, Text, Ping and Close writes through `ServerWebSocket::write_frame`, plus a check that
  no second `Close` is written after the peer acknowledges ours) passes with this change and
  fails without it. They need `tokio-rustls` and `rustls-pemfile` as dev-dependencies and a
  fixture certificate; I can add them to this PR if wanted.
- The reproduction from the issue, ten rotating rounds on this machine: stock `main` stalled
  in 6 of 10 runs (official canary) and 4 of 10 (local debug build), 2.9.6 release in 4 of 10;
  a debug build of `main` from this branch, 0 of 5.
- `tests/unit/websocket_test.ts` against the repo's test server, with the binary built from this
  branch: 47 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (macOS aarch64).
- The reproduction also stalls on Linux aarch64 (`denoland/deno:2.9.6` and the Linux canary,
  two containers on a Docker bridge network) and completes there with plain `ws:`; not run on
  Linux with this branch.
- Not run: the CLI integration test suite, Windows, throughput measurements.

title: fix(serde_v8): return an error instead of panicking on unsupported value types
body:
`Deserializer::deserialize_any` calls `panic!` in `ValueType::from_v8` for any value type it does not classify (e.g. a `Symbol`). A serde `Deserializer` should report unsupported input as an `Err`, not panic, so this returns `Err(Error::UnsupportedType)` instead, as #36021 did for exceptions during conversion.

`BigInt` is folded into the same path since its `deserialize_any` arm already returned `UnsupportedType`; deserializing a BigInt into a numeric type is unaffected.

title: fix(ci): bump libuv-sys-lite to 1.48.4, pin rolldown minifier to 1.2.7
body:
Fixes the two independent breakages currently keeping main's CI red; they
have to land together for a green run.

First, the windows-11-arm64 runner image update (20260830.155 ->
20260906.161, rolled out starting Sep 8) bumped LLVM 20.1.6 to 22.1.8.
libuv-sys-lite 1.48.3 has no pregenerated bindings for windows-aarch64, so
it runs bindgen at build time there, and bindgen 0.70.1 (via clang-sys
1.8.1, which predates LLVM 22) silently generates unusable bindings against
the new libclang: opaque size-1 structs and missing
`sockaddr_in`/`sockaddr_in6`. Any cold build of the crate on those runners
fails, which is why the windows-aarch64 integration jobs (building
test_napi) went red - intermittently during the image rollout, consistently
since. Bump to libuv-sys-lite 1.48.4, which ships pregenerated
windows-aarch64 bindings (nathanwhit/libuv-sys-lite#5), so bindgen no
longer runs on CI at all - matching how the crate already works on every
other platform.

Second, the release snapshot minifier runs `npm:rolldown/experimental`
unpinned, and rolldown 1.2.8 (published Sep 9) started mangling private
class members with no opt-out, turning stack frames like
`Worker.#pollControl` into `Worker.#s` and breaking 12 worker spec tests in
the `test specs release` jobs. Pin the minifier to 1.2.7 (same commit as
#36844; whichever lands first dedupes).

Closes #36836

title: fix(runtime): pin rolldown minifier to 1.2.7 in snapshot builds
body:
The release snapshot minifier runs `npm:rolldown/experimental` unpinned, so
every release build silently picks up the latest rolldown. rolldown 1.2.8
(published Sep 9) started mangling private class members even with
`mangle.keepNames: true`, and its `MangleOptions` offer no way to opt out.
That turned stack frames like `Worker.#pollControl` into `Worker.#s` in
release builds, which is why 12 worker spec tests asserting on those frames
(`specs::worker::*`, `specs::run::worker_drop_handle_race`) are red in the
`test specs release` jobs on main and on every open PR.

Verified locally: minifying a class with a `#pollControl` member through the
exact options used in `runtime/transpile.rs` preserves the name on rolldown
1.2.7 and mangles it on 1.2.8. Pin the minifier to 1.2.7 and document why;
pinning also makes release snapshots reproducible instead of depending on
whatever rolldown version npm serves at build time.

title: fix(ext/http): extract traceparent from Deno.serve regardless of header name case
body:
Header names on the HTTP/1 fast path in `Deno.serve` reach the propagator carrier verbatim from the wire, so a request with `Traceparent:` (or any non-lowercase spelling) was silently ignored and the server span started a fresh trace instead of joining the caller's. HTTP/2 was unaffected because hyper already normalises header names there.

The fix just lowercases the names when building the carrier array. The new spec test sends a raw HTTP/1.1 request over TCP, since `fetch` lowercases header names itself and can't reproduce this.

title: fix(ext/node): return an error instead of aborting on a too-small prime size
body:
Fixes the abort described in #36838.

`crypto.generatePrimeSync(1)` panicked inside `num_bigint_dig` and, because release builds set `panic = "abort"`, took the whole process down. The caller had no way to recover: `try`/`catch` never ran. Node returns an OpenSSL error for the same input.

## AI usage disclosure

I found this bug while testing Deno's Node compatibility layer against Node, and located the cause by attaching a debugger to a locally built `deno`. I used an AI coding assistant to help write this patch and the tests. All code in this PR has been reviewed by me, and I built Deno from source and ran the reproduction and the tests below myself.


## Why it panicked

`validateRandomPrimeJob` calls `validateInt32(size, "size", 1)`, so it only guarantees `size >= 1`. The value is then handed to `num_bigint_dig`'s `RandPrime::gen_prime`, which hard-panics for `bit_size < 2`:

```rust
// num-bigint-dig-0.8.6/src/bigrand.rs
fn gen_prime(&mut self, bit_size: usize) -> BigUint {
  if bit_size < 2 {
  panic!("prime size must be at least 2-bit");
  }
```

`1` satisfies the first check and violates the second, so it passed validation and then killed the process.

In `ext/node_crypto/lib.rs`, the two branches of `gen_prime` are not symmetric — the `generate_with_options` branch propagates errors with `?`, while the `Prime::generate` branch (the one `size = 1` takes) calls straight through with no guard.

## Change

Reject `size < 2` in the JS layer, before the op is called, and match Node's error shape.

- `generatePrimeSync` throws `ERR_OSSL_BN_BITS_TOO_SMALL`
- `generatePrime` reports the same error through its callback rather than throwing, which is what Node does — worth calling out, since the two entry points are not symmetric here

```js
// generatePrimeSync
if (size < 2) {
  throw new NodeError(
  "ERR_OSSL_BN_BITS_TOO_SMALL",
  "error:01800076:bignum routines::bits too small",
  );
}
```

The message mirrors Node's, and the code matches what `checkPrimeSync` already uses for the sibling upper-bound check in the same file (`ERR_OSSL_BN_BIGNUM_TOO_LONG`), so this stays consistent with the existing style.

## Tests

Added two regression tests to `tests/unit_node/crypto/crypto_misc_test.ts`:

- `generatePrimeSync(1)` throws instead of aborting
- `generatePrime(1, cb)` calls back with the error and does not throw

## Verification

Built from source and ran against the built binary.

```
$ ./target/debug/deno run -A repro.js
caught: ERR_OSSL_BN_BITS_TOO_SMALL | error:01800076:bignum routines::bits too small
SURVIVED
deno exit=0
```

`node:test-crypto-prime.js` still passes:

```
test node_compat::parallel::test-crypto-prime.js ... ok (477ms)
```

Full `crypto_misc_test.ts`:

```
ok | 8 passed | 0 failed
```

I also ran the whole `crypto` filter of the node compat suite before and after the change. Both report `36 failed of 190`, with the same list of failures, so this change does not move that number. Those failures are pre-existing on this machine and unrelated to `generatePrime` — most are webcrypto/keyobject tests, and one of them (`test-crypto-negative-zero.js`) is a *different* call path hitting the same underlying panic (`keys.rs:3465`, via `generateKeyPairSync('dh', { primeLength: 0 })`). I left that one alone and will send it separately, since it needs a change in a different file.

Behaviour is unchanged for `size >= 2`; only the previously-aborting inputs are affected.

## Checklist

- [x] `./x fmt` passes without changing files
- [x] `./x lint` passes
- [x] Tests cover the change

title: fix(cli): preserve double dash before the entrypoint
body:
Deno 2.9.6 regressed handling of `--` before the first positional:
`deno run -- script.ts`, `deno eval -- code`, and bare `deno -- script.ts`
put the entrypoint into trailing args instead of accepting it as the script
path, because the parser entered trailing mode on the first `--`.

For entrypoint-style commands (a single-value positional followed by
trailing var args: run/watch/serve/eval/task/compile), a `--` seen before
any positional now switches the parser into a positional-only mode: the
remaining args fill the positionals literally, so the entrypoint may start
with a hyphen, and then the command's normal trailing-argument handling
resumes. A second `--` is forwarded literally, matching clap where only the
first separator is special. Commands that used clap's `.last(true)`
(test/bench/install/create), where args after `--` are script args that
bypass the positionals, keep their current behavior, as do commands with a
`.trailing()` positional (init/create/x).

Supersedes #36794 with the `.last(true)` commands excluded.

Fixes #36792

Co-authored-by: Tiancheng Xu <<email>>

title: fix(npm): tolerate lifecycle failures in optional dependency trees
body:
Packages used only through optionalDependencies can fail their install scripts without preventing the main program from starting. This covers optional dependencies of registry packages, and those declared in a root or workspace member package.json where Deno installs them (`deno add --save-optional`, or `deno install` seeding `deno.lock` from `package-lock.json`), including required dependencies beneath them. Packages that are also required elsewhere still fail installation. An `npm:` requirement identical to an `optionalDependencies` entry (e.g. importing `npm:<email>` with `"foo": "1.0.0"`) can't be told apart from it and is treated as optional.

Optional failures retain their script output as warnings. This changes failure handling only; failed packages remain installed. Optional peer references remain conservatively required because their metadata can overlap ordinary dependencies.

Fixes #36239.

title: fix(ext/web): pace identity pipeThrough bypass on the destination writable
body:
Fixes #36790

## Root cause

The identity `pipeThrough` writable bypass (#35799) paced its pump on the destination TransformStream's `[[backpressure]]` flag. `initializeTransformStream` sets every TransformStream's initial backpressure to `true`, and it only clears on the first pull of the readable side (readable-strategy HWM defaults to 0). So for `a.readable.pipeThrough(b)`:

1. The pump sees `b`'s initial backpressure and waits for `b.readable` to be consumed — never arming a read on `a.readable`.
2. `writer.write(1)` on `a` blocks on `a`'s own initial backpressure, which only that missing read would release — deadlock until someone reads `b.readable`.

The generic pipeTo loop paces on the destination *writable* (`writer[_readyPromise]`, HWM 1 by default), which guarantees the first read — that's why `pipeTo(new WritableStream(...))` and Deno ≤ 2.9.1 (no bypass) work.

## Fix

Reproduce the generic path's writable-side pacing inside the bypass with a slot count, keeping the bypass itself (no per-chunk writable ceremony) intact: count pending bypass writes against the destination writable's strategy HWM, stall when the slots are full, and resume when backpressure clears (a clear completes all queued transforms, since they captured the same change promise). Chunk-count parity with the generic path was traced for HWM combos (0/1, 1/1, 3/1, 0/3); memory stays bounded, and writable HWM 0 stalls in both paths identically (spec-conforming). One accepted approximation: custom writable `sizeAlgorithm`s are counted as size 1 per chunk — it can't hang.

## Tests

Added `pipeThroughWriteResolvesBeforeOutputConsumed` to `tests/unit/streams_test.ts`: the exact issue repro (write before consuming piped output must resolve), then asserts the chunk flows through and close propagates. Verified locally: the issue repro now prints `after write`; full `streams_test.ts`: 68 passed, 0 failed. (WPT was not runnable locally — it requires Python 3.11 — but the pump changes are exercised by the unit suite and CI's WPT run.)

---
